RXLIB initialization-failure caller trace (EK10910 strengthened; 2026-11-06; no Exec file/body/LOC credit): traced `init()` failure returns from missing `FindPort("REXX")`, failed `CreatePort()`, or failed `CreateRexxMsg()` (`workbench/rexxc/RXLIB.c:29-48`) to `main()`, which ignores the Boolean and dereferences static `msg` in the argument-count 2–5 branches (`:63-70,92-108`). Compared the adjacent `RX.c` caller, which handles failure and cleans up (`:97-101`), and verified that `RXLIB` is explicitly buildable while the aggregate Workbench dependency is commented (`workbench/rexxc/mmakefile.src:5-12`; `workbench/mmakefile.src:28`). <a id="gpt-backup-entry-array-byte-lba-mismatch-ek10353"></a>GPT backup entry-array byte/LBA unit pass (EK10353 added; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): traced `tablesize` from `EntrySize * NumEntries` rounded to bytes (`rom/partition/partitiongpt.c:512-514`) through the backup call's `backup - tablesize` argument (`:567-574`). Confirmed `GPTWriteTable()` stores that value in header `StartBlock` and forwards it as `StartBlock` to `WritePartitionDataQ()` (`:481-505`), whose contract and offset calculation treat it as an LBA (`rom/partition/writepartitiondata.c:28-35,53-62`). At 128 × 128-byte entries and 512-byte sectors, the code subtracts 16,384 LBAs instead of 32; the array can intrude into the GPT usable range and overwrite a partition tail. Traced the explicit HDToolBox Save Changes caller (`workbench/tools/HDToolBox/gui.c:341`) and both module manifests. Added EK10353 to the detailed report and index. The relevant implementation and caller already have full-body/path credit, so totals do not change. No GPT disk, write, or build was used; source-only.

<a id="console-handler-per-handle-signal-ownership-ek10350-recheck"></a>EK10350 candidate recheck and withdrawal (2026-11-01; no body/LOC credit): re-read all `open_con()` callers and the `CONMain()` task/packet lifecycle (`rom/filesys/console_handler/con_handler.c:461,720-755,1219-1291`). `open_con()` has one caller, during handler startup, and records that task as `fh->contask`. CON: leaves `dn_Task` unpublished, so each console handler task owns one filehandle; device-backed mode publishes `dn_Task`, and subsequent file handles are routed to the same existing handler/filehandle instead of calling `open_con()` again. On final close the handler clears the published device port, frees the filehandle resources, and returns from `CONMain()`. `AllocSignal()` changes only that task's `tc_SigAlloc` mask (`rom/exec/allocsignal.c:79-103,121-124`); the retained bits therefore cannot accumulate across later handler tasks, and the active ports legitimately need their signals until teardown. No caller-supported signal-exhaustion consequence remains. Withdraw EK10350 from the detailed report and master index; no source-body or coverage numerator changes. Source-only; no handler or signal operation was run.

PC metadata with height 1–13 yields zero text rows and a `UINT_MAX` scroll bound on the first debug character. AArch64 initially substitutes 1024×768 for a zero query, but accepts a later nonzero firmware-echoed height below 14 and publishes the callback; that specific firmware response remains unverified. Existing source and path accounting remain unchanged; no boot, framebuffer, or firmware response was exercised.

Review correction (2026-10-24): EK8827 is restored as a m68k-Amiga-only candidate after confirming `atomic_inc_b()` is an explicit byte-sized `addq.b` and the selected interrupt-exit scheduler gate treats the wrapped signed value as switch-enabled. EK799 `FindTask()` false-negative schedule recheck (2026-10-23): reread the complete named lookup plus ExecSMP `Signal()` wake and its selected ARM32/AArch64 and PC state-transition helpers. Confirmed a specific non-snapshot ordering: the lookup can miss a task on Wait in its earlier Ready scan, then a wake can move it to Ready before the lookup acquires Wait; because the lookup proceeds to Running/Spinning without revisiting Ready, it can return NULL while the task remains live on Ready. Signal's task spinlock does not serialize the lookup, which uses only separate list locks. The report's RTL driver free consequence still requires a later worker wait/wake transition during teardown; the direct Signal in DeleteUnit returns before its poll and was not used as the transition. No task transition, device teardown or schedule was run. Source-only.

Review correction (2026-11-02; supersedes the 2026-10-26 EK8800 withdrawal): EK8800 is restored. The withdrawal incorrectly applied proposed C23 wording to this checkout's configured C standards, which are probed through C17 (`config/features.in:90-145`). The C17 ballot says a positive signed left shift is defined only when its result is representable in the signed result type; `1 << 31` on 32-bit `int` is therefore undefined ([WG14 C17 ballot N2176 §6.5.7p4](https://www.open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg14/www/docs/n2176.pdf); N1570 §6.5.7p4 has the same wording). The source and coverage ledger already establish that bit 31 is allocatable after bits 16–30 are occupied and that selected signal consumers form masks with signed shifts. The observable mask consequence remains compiler-dependent; no generated compiler output or runtime result was established. EK9149 and EK9118 remain withdrawn for their separate implementation-defined address-conversion cases.

Permit/Forbid caller-path recheck for USB Audio OD3229 (2026-10-23; no separate EK): reread the selected `usbForceInterfaceBinding()` allocation-failure branch and Poseidon's ordinary `psdClassScan()` callback boundary (`rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:243-322`; `rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:6287-6294,6377-6390`) against task initialization and the generic plus selected ExecSMP nesting-counter implementations (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:230-237`; `rom/exec/permit.c:79-103`; `rom/exec/reschedule.c:58-65`; `arch/all-pc/exec/exec_platform.h:88-99,149-160`; ARM32/AArch64/RISC-V overrides cited by OD3229). The callback's ordinary allocation-failure return reaches Permit before Poseidon executes its following Forbid/Permit bookkeeping pair. The worker cleanup then publishes a null task pointer before reading the waiter fields, while the release method frees the same record after observing that pointer clear (`hub.class.c:1084-1098,147-175`; equivalent SuperSpeed path). This confirms the selected caller and the conditional stale-record window already detailed as Other Drivers OD3229; it is not an Exec implementation defect or a new report item. Existing full-body credit for `permit.c` stands; broader Permit/Forbid caller census remains open. No allocation failure or schedule was run. Source-only.

ARM32 SuperState/UserState privileged-mode caller recheck (EK9052 expanded, 2026-10-18): confirmed ARM32 `SuperState()` has no prior-mode check and always returns the post-SWI stack pointer (`arch/arm-native/exec/superstate.c:16-29`); `SC_SUPERSTATE` unconditionally selects System mode (`kernel/syscall.c:194-200`), while `KrnIsSuper()` treats non-User/non-System exception modes as privileged (`kernel/issuper.c:21-25`). A non-NULL `UserState` token always selects User mode (`exec/userstate.c:17-26`), violating the documented NULL-on-already-supervisor contract (`rom/exec/superstate.c:22-33`). Searched all ARM-native SuperState call sites: Processor_Init performs the processor probes and spawns SMP probe tasks (`arch/arm-native/processor/processor_init.c:19-25,28-83`); the other direct caller is in the VC4 diagnostic block (`vc4_drm_aros.c:2857-2860`). Kernel startup enters its user-mode continuation before ordinary initialization (`kernel_startup.c:329-352`); no privileged exception-handler call site was found. Added/restored a detailed EK9052 section and repaired the index anchor; retained the finding as conditional on external/future privileged-mode use. No transition was run; source-only.

EK8832 partial-allocation consequence recheck (2026-10-17; restored to the detailed report/index 2026-10-24): traced both low-memory `Allocate()` loops and the raw/aligned pointer handling in `core_BSPReconfigure` (`arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/kernel_startup.c:837-875`). If exactly one replacement succeeds, `newAlloc` is reset before the next search and the function has no branch that frees the successful partial block; this leak accompanies the CPU-count/TSS-capacity desynchronization trigger. The selected MADT count setter runs once during APIC-private setup (`arch/all-pc/kernel/acpi_apic.c:34-73`), so repeated-expansion leakage was not claimed. No allocation failure or AP startup was induced.

CPU-count/ID platform cross-check (2026-10-18): compared all four maintained `KrnGetCPUCount()` bodies and associated startup semantics. AArch64 native returns the population of registered CPU bits and BCM27xx can continue to a later CPU after an earlier PSCI failure (EK541); ARM32 native also returns a population count, but BCM2708 starts IDs sequentially and waits for each before advancing, so the sparse-ID trigger was not established there. PC returns the ACPI-discovered `apic_count`; failed AP boot leaves it unchanged and is already covered by EK9400. RISC-V OpenSBI returns DT CPU-node count but currently parks non-boot harts and does not enable Exec SMP in the selected configuration, so its count does not establish the same runnable affinity failure. The FDT kernel parser increments for every `cpu@` node without inspecting `status` (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_fdt.c:114-122`); selected `processor.resource` uses the same count for `GCIT_NumberOfProcessors` and walks the first count `cpu` nodes without status filtering (`rom/processor/init.c:25-44`; `arch/riscv64-all/processor/processor_init.c:441-452`). This leaves a conditional advertised-inventory question if a selected DTB has disabled CPU nodes; I have not promoted it to a finding because the intended `KrnGetCPUCount()` contract and a maintained DTB with such nodes are not established by this source pass. Future HSM/SMP support remains open. No boot or CPU start was run. Source-only.

RISC-V `status = fail` inventory finding recheck (EK9070 retained and qualified, 2026-10-22): matched selected manifests: `arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/mmakefile.src` includes `kernel_fdt`, `platform_init` and `getcpucount`; `arch/riscv64-all/processor/mmakefile.src` selects `processor_init`. The early parser counts every direct `cpu@` node and stores its `reg` hart ID by logical index (`kernel_fdt.c:110-124,176-188`); post-Exec `Platform_Init()` publishes that count and record array (`platform_init.c:23-48`); the selected resource snapshots the count and enumerates `cpu` nodes with `reg` without filtering `status` (`rom/processor/init.c:25-44`; `processor_init.c:441-469`). Thus `status = "fail"` creates a consistently indexed but publicly advertised non-operational CPU record; EK9070 remains a public inventory-contract finding, not a current runnable-affinity or scheduler failure. A checkout-wide tracked-file suffix search found no `.dts`, `.dtsi` or `.dtb` fixture, so no maintained firmware tree establishes that trigger on a current board image. `status = "disabled"` remains excluded from the claim because it may represent a physically present, quiescent CPU. No new finding or line credit; no firmware boot or CPU query was run. Source-only.

EK9400 affinity/scheduler recheck (2026-10-18; no new finding): further traced `SetTaskAffinity()`'s failed-CPU reschedule request (`rom/task/SetTaskAffinity.c:130-141`), `NewAddTask()`'s affinity-targeted schedule request (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:45-109`), and the online PC scheduler's affinity filters (`arch/all-pc/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:117-121,308-314`). A ready task retargeted to an AP that never started receives no kick because SetTaskAffinity only kicks TS_RUN tasks; online schedulers then skip it. For a running task, the remote kick goes only to the failed AP, so no immediate local reschedule is requested. These are consequences of the existing EK9400 startup-count/affinity mismatch, not a separate bug. No AP startup or affinity operation was run. Source-only.

EK9064 cross-platform mask-helper pass (2026-10-18): inspected all three checked-in `KrnGetCPUMask()` implementations: AArch64 native, ARM native and PC/APIC. Each adds the requested bit rather than replacing the destination; the PC wrapper delegates to `core_APIC_GetMask()`, which ORs the bit (`arch/{aarch64-native,arm-native}/kernel/getcpumask.c:21-22`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/getcpumask.c:20`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/apic.c:115-132`). The stale-output consequence therefore applies across selected SMP targets using these helpers. No additional per-architecture variation was found. Source-only.

EK9064 caller/output-buffer contract pass (2026-10-18): compared task.resource's `TaskTag_CPUAffinity` output contract and additive implementation (`rom/task/QueryTaskTagList.c:50-52,141-151`) with the selected AArch64 set-bit and clear-mask semantics (`arch/aarch64-native/kernel/{getcpumask,clearcpumask}.c`). The task.resource function never clears caller storage, so repeated queries into a reused mask can retain bits absent from the current task mask; the selected `smpaffinity.c` helper clears its fresh mask before each query (`:59-75,94-108`). Added EK9064 as a conditional caller-buffer reuse defect. No query was run. Source-only.

TaskTag_CPUAffinity query concurrency recheck (EK9064 retained; EK714 boundary, 2026-10-18): re-read `QueryTaskTagList`'s affinity loop and `SetTaskAffinity`'s in-place clear/refill under `tc_SpinLock` (`rom/task/QueryTaskTagList.c:141-151`; `rom/task/SetTaskAffinity.c:98-142`). The query does not take that spinlock, so concurrent setter/query calls can observe an intermediate or mixed mask; however, the API does not promise an atomic snapshot, and the only direct in-tree affinity-query caller is the SMP test, which queries after its setter/concurrency phase and clears a fresh output buffer (`developer/debug/test/smp/smpaffinity.c:59-75,94-108,193-250`). The other checked `QueryTaskTagList` callers request CPU number, CPU time/usage, or register values. Retain EK9064 for the deterministic reused-output stale-bit case; do not promote the weaker concurrent snapshot concern without a snapshot contract or selected caller requiring one. The earlier dense-ID bound issue remains EK541. No task query or concurrent affinity update was run. Source-only.

EK541 sparse CPU-ID query and signal-routing follow-up (rechecked 2026-10-28): traced `Signal()`'s affinity-mismatch IPI target selection and AArch64 restricted-context `signal_hook` (`rom/exec/signal.c:24-83,165-213`). With online IDs `{0,2}` and population count 2, a CPU-2-only task mask has no match in the dense ID loop, so initial signal routing defaults to CPU 0. Correction: the selected restricted-context hook does not call `Signal()` again; it atomically sets `tc_SigRecvd` and wakes a waiting task through `krnSysCallReschedTask()`. No lost-signal or recursive-requeue finding is established. Such a CPU-2-only mask is not accepted by `SetTaskAffinity` under this count, though task creation or another caller may supply one. The separate `TaskTag_CPUAffinity` query loop (`rom/task/QueryTaskTagList.c:141-150`; tag contract at `rom/task/task.h:22-24`) still omits CPU 2 from returned masks. These remain conditional dense-ID consequences; no task, signal, IPI or scheduling was run. Source-only.


EK862 managed allocator callback census recheck (2026-10-18; no new EK): searched every C assignment to `mhe_Alloc`/`mhe_AllocVec` and re-read all four definitions/copy sites (`rom/kernel/tlsf.c:1472-1473`; `rom/exec/memory.c:938-943`; `workbench/hidds/radeon/bitmap.c:343-346,421-425`; `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/vcgfx/vcgfx_memory.c:36-40,237-241`). TLSF supplies both callbacks; `AllocMemHeader` copies them independently; Radeon and VideoCore omit `mhe_AllocVec`, but their `mhe_Alloc` implementations return NULL. This confirms no selected in-tree pool header reaches the null-vector-callback branch; EK862 remains scoped to a custom managed pool header. No allocation or pool was created.
PC SMP failed-stack allocation unwind check (EK9400 expanded, 2026-10-17): followed `smp_Wake`'s per-CPU preparation order through the immediate stack-allocation failure return (`arch/all-pc/kernel/smp.c:247-264`) and checked the selected `KernelPost` caller for rollback (`platform_post.c:201-205`). GDT, TLS, optional Exec scheduler data, and IDT have already been stored in `CPUData`; neither the return branch nor caller frees them. The GDT/TLS/IDT allocators align an `AllocMem` result after requesting extra bytes but retain only the aligned pointer (`platform_post.c:52-82`), so an unwind must retain the raw bases. Expanded EK9400's report to include this resource leak alongside the false online-count consequence. This is the same failed AP startup path, not a separate finding. No allocation failure or boot was induced.

Prism2 last-close caller cross-check for EK8880 (2026-10-17; no new EK): `UnitTask` drains `GENERAL_QUEUE`, obtains `unit->access_lock`, and calls `ServiceRequest`, which releases the semaphore after handling the request (`workbench/devs/networks/prism2/unit.c:3879-3887`; `request.c:182-281`). Concurrent `DevBeginIO` uses `AttemptSemaphore` and queues requests when another caller owns the lock (`device.c:420-432`). Last-opener `CloseUnit` calls `DeletePCIUnit`/`DeletePCCardUnit`, then `DeleteUnit` calls `RemTask(unit->task)` without coordinating with the worker's semaphore wait (`device.c:538-574`; `pci.c:340-358`; `pccard.c:330-343`; `unit.c:385-403`). This could exercise EK8880's stack-resident `SemaphoreRequest` lifetime if the unit task is blocked in `ObtainSemaphore` when the final close removes it. The checked caller evidence does not establish a supported client closing its last open while I/O remains queued/in flight, and the normal worker loop waits on signals when it owns no request; retain this as a conditional cross-subsystem route, not an ordinary selected-workload trigger. No request, close, or semaphore was run. Source-only.

AddDosEntry/AssignLock cross-check (2026-10-17; no new finding): rechecked `rom/dos/adddosentry.c:81-120` against selected `AssignLock`, `AssignPath`, and `AssignLate` callers. `AddDosEntry(NULL)` returns success without insertion; for `AssignLock(name, BNULL)` this is the documented cancel operation, and an absent assign is documented as a successful no-op by the selected `workbench/c/Assign.c:690-701` caller. The nested DosList locks in the assignment helpers match AddDosEntry's documented lock design. This narrow check found no separate defect; broader DOS-list callers remain open. Source-only.
AllocSignal selected ASL AbortAslRequest caller follow-up (EK8800 cross-reference, 2026-10-17): traced the non-MorphOS `AbortAslRequest` branch through its temporary stack reply port, close-message send, and `WaitPort` (`workbench/libs/asl/abortaslrequest.c:65-99`; Exec `PutMsg`/`WaitPort`). A valid automatic allocation of bit 31 reaches the existing signed-int `WaitPort`/`PutMsg` masks covered by EK8800; `SetSignal(0, 1L << sig)` is additionally undefined on targets where C `long` is 32-bit. On allocation failure it uses `SIGB_SINGLE`; its port message is enqueued before WaitPort, whose list check makes this one-shot wait return without consuming a semaphore wait. No separate AllocSignal defect established; no requester or signal exhaustion was exercised. Source-only.
x86-64 PC MMU protection and split-pool pass (EK9023-EK9024, 2026-10-17): traced identity-map creation, `KrnMapGlobal`, `KrnSetProtection`, page splitting, both BSP and AP EFER setup, and selected `KrnAllocPages`/`KrnFreePages` callers. Confirmed BSP sets only `_EFER_LME` (`bootstrap/cpu.c:224-230`) and AP ORs only `0x100` into EFER (`kernel/smpbootstrap.s:114-119`); no selected EFER write enables NXE. Added EK9023 because all selected initial/dynamic entries keep NX clear and `core_ProtPage` never sets it; `MAP_Executable` therefore has no execute-permission effect. Added EK9024 because only 32 PDE splits are available and the 33rd distinct-region protection request logs and returns without changing permissions; the public call returns no status, and `KrnFreePages` proceeds to free pages after the unapplied revoke. Both findings are indexed. Page-table allocation/teardown and hardware behavior remain open; no protection change or allocation was run. Source-only.

x86-64 PC platform-init caller reconciliation (2026-10-17; no new EK): traced `Platform_Init` from `ADD2INITLIB` through `Kernel_Init`'s stop-on-false INITLIB dispatch and post-`AddResource` publication, then checked all local IDT gate and exception-registration results. The allocation-failure/partial-publication path remains EK8965; ignored required syscall/APIC exception registrations remain within EK8877. `core_SetIDTGate` validates vector occupancy and writes the gate; `core_SetExGates` panics on a failed gate setup, so neither adds a separate local defect. Updated the file row; later APIC/controller startup and hardware behavior remain open. No boot or allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

x86-64 StackSwap assembly call-alignment pass (EK9022, 2026-10-17): traced the selected assembly vector from its entry stack through its `Disable`, `FindTask`, stack exchange, and `Enable` calls; confirmed the first two calls use one pushed register after the saved RBX, leaving pre-call RSP 8 mod 16 and callee-entry RSP 0 mod 16. Compared with the x86-64 16-byte stack-alignment constant, `PrepareContext`'s ABI comments, `FindTask`'s C entry, and the selected Disable preservation stub. Added EK9022 for the unconditional internal call-alignment mismatch. The replacement-stack `Enable` call assumes its supplied `stk_Pointer` alignment; caller validity remains a separate public contract. No stack swap was run. Source-only.

x86-64 task-exit stub and context-frame caller pass (2026-10-17; no new EK): verified the `arch/x86_64-all/exec/mmakefile.src` AFILES selection, then traced the full `TaskExitStub` (`taskexit.S:12-15`) through x86-64 `PrepareContext`, `NewAddTask`/`NewCreateTaskA`, and the default `Exec_TaskFinaliser` (`preparecontext.c:15-109`; `rom/exec/newaddtask.c:296-307`; `rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:52-57`). The five pushed words give the entry point the required SysV stack alignment; on return the stub skips exactly the two stack-passed arguments and returns into the configured finalizer with call-entry alignment. The default finalizer removes the task and does not return. The local caller setup initializes the two stack argument slots to zero and `TASKTAG_ARG7/8` overwrite them when present. No independent frame/return-path mismatch established. Malformed externally supplied stack bounds, alternate-ABI callers, and other architecture exit stubs remain open; no task was launched. Source-only.

genmodule inline-header writer pass (2026-10-17; no new EK): reread the complete `tools/genmodule/writeincinline.c` body, including register, stack-call, alias and three variadic wrapper emitters; traced `INCLUDES` dispatch in `genmodule.c` and the generated `inline/%s.h` target dependency in `writemakefile.c`. Checked argument-register group construction and selected `va_list`/`RAWARG` declarations in Exec, DOS, Utility and Log configuration files. The inspected selected `va_list` and RAWARG variadic declarations have non-void result types, so the unconditional generated `retval` declaration in the va_list wrapper did not yield a selected void-return defect. No independent source-level defect established. Generated-header compilation across selected configurations, output-write failures and external config inputs remain open; no generator or build was run. Source-only.

VMM AddMemList block-backed size path reconciliation (2026-10-17; no separate EK): traced `PartSize` from `OpenPageFileAsPartition`'s DOS-environment cylinder geometry (`workbench/system/VMM/pageio.c:192-195`) and pseudo-partition block ranges (`:343-347,398-400`) through page alignment and the `PartSize - NeededForTables` cap (`pagehandler.c:151`; `VM_Manager_Init.c:742-766`). The source does not enforce a minimum remaining region after table overhead for arbitrary block-backed metadata, so that size condition remains unverified. The MUI standard-starter path supplies non-null CxParams and reaches EK9906's unset `VirtAddrStart`; after page-handler initialization it passes the null base to AddMemList. The vmm.library path is earlier blocked by EK428's null-CxParams diagnostic at VM_Manager_Init.c:680. Do not treat the block-size question as resolved or as an independent reachable defect without a valid-range caller. No VMM or partition was run. Source-only.

AddMemList expansion-board minimum-size caller follow-up (2026-10-17; no new EK): re-traced `ConfigChain`/`detectexpram` through `ReadExpansionRom`, Zorro sizing, optional `autosize`, `MemoryTest`, and `addmergedchunks` (`arch/m68k-amiga/expansion/{readexpansionrom.c:62-84,configchain.c:39-58,228-319,322-358,393-450,memorytest.S:35-38,81-86,153-164}`). Every registered ROM-sized Z2/Z3 board chunk is at least 64 KiB; the subsize table's minimum is 64 KiB, and auto-sized chunks require a positive result from a 512 KiB-block probe. Probe-detected expansion regions use 1 MiB blocks. These selected callers therefore do not trigger AddMemList's `size - MEMHEADER_TOTAL` underflow through a short region. Existing zero-size EK872 is the separately qualified Sam440 caller. Board address decoding and real hardware ranges remain unverified; no hardware or memory probe was run. Source-only.

POSIXC opendir temporary-assign cleanup pass (EK8997, 2026-10-17): traced the `DupLock`/`AssignLock` temporary mapping against dos.library ownership rules. `AssignLock` explicitly leaves the supplied lock owned by the caller on failure; the MakeDosEntry allocation failure returns without releasing it, while `opendir` only logs the failure and loses the duplicate pointer. The AROS source does not define `ExNext_IS_WORKING_WITHOUT_ASSIGN`, so this branch is selected. Added EK8997. No low-memory event or directory operation was induced. Source-only.

POSIXC descriptor-table growth errno follow-up (EK8996, 2026-10-17): compared `__getfdslot`'s local `AllocPooled` growth failure with its fd.library reservation error path, then traced both selected error callers. The allocation path returns -1 without `__set_errno`; `open()` preserves stale errno and `dup2()` returns under a comment that assumes the helper set errno. Added EK8996. No allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

POSIXC `pipe()`/`opendir()` descriptor allocation failure and concurrency pass (EK8994/EK8995, 2026-10-17): traced the slot callers through `__getfirstfd`, `__getfdslot`, `__setfdesc`, and owner-table routing in `__init_fd`. Confirmed both APIs fail to check the allocation result before descriptor publication, and pthread workers share the creator's descriptor array while free-slot search/reservation/publication is not atomic. EK8994 covers both APIs returning -1 into `__setfdesc`'s unchecked index; EK8995 covers concurrent slot collisions in both. The existing open/close threaded-use notes do not appear in either API's source documentation. No allocation failure, pipe, directory or thread was exercised. Source-only.

Exec internal Signal caller recheck (EK277/EK8845 retained, 2026-10-17; no additional finding): followed `Exec_CleanupETask` through parent/child list transfer and its post-unlock child-notification Signal (`rom/exec/exec_util.c:271-329`). The cached-parent lifetime and wrong-list-lock effects are already covered by EK277 and EK8845; Signal is a consequence of the same cached parent use, not an independent fault. Pthread stale-task cancellation test-caller recheck (EK8956, 2026-10-16): repository-wide search found one direct caller outside the library: `developer/debug/test/misc/pthreadtest.c` repeatedly cancels `thread1` inside a finite main loop but never joins it, while `thread_func1` itself has a finite loop. If that worker exits before the main loop’s first cancellation call, that call can reach the retained finished slot; a prior successful cancellation sets `canceled`, so subsequent calls return `ESRCH`. This provides a conditional checked-in trigger without claiming the schedule was run.
Pthread post-exit cancellation lifetime recheck (EK8956 expanded, 2026-10-16): traced joinable `ThreadInfo` publication and retention through `StarterFunc` return, DOS `CreateNewProc` task-memory registration, Exec self-RemTask and service cleanup, then `pthread_cancel` into `Signal`. Confirmed `Signal` dereferences task affinity/state/signal fields before terminal-state handling (`rom/exec/signal.c:170-196,262-280`), so the terminal-state check does not protect a reclaimed record. The still-joinable ID remains in its slot until `pthread_join` clears it. No thread was run. Source-only.
i386 non-SMP processor-resource skipped-core follow-up (EK8975, 2026-10-16): traced the selected i386 package and configure gate through APIC count, `smp_Initialize`, AP bootstrap halt path, the initializer’s `cpuNo > 0` skip, and GetCoreInfo/GetCPUInfo dispatch. Confirmed a successful APIC setup can publish the full discovered count while secondary processor records remain zeroed. Restored as a detailed conditional API finding; no boot/query was run.

All-native kernel TagItem walker selected caller and producer pass (2026-10-25; no new EK): re-read `arch/all-native/kernel/tags.c` and searched all direct `krnNextTagItem()`, `krnFindTagItem()` and `krnGetTagData()` call expressions. The only caller of this exact common implementation is `RelocateBootMsg()`'s two walks in `arch/all-native/kernel/boot_utils.c:28-55`; the `arch/all-native/kernel/mmakefile.src` selects the implementation for native PC kernel targets, and i386/x86_64 startup invokes the relocation helper. Traced the checked-in producer to `arch/all-pc/bootstrap/bootstrap.c`: the static `km[32]` receives a finite flat set of tags and a `TAG_DONE`, with no `TAG_MORE` or `TAG_SKIP` emission. The parser's standard control semantics match the selected producer/consumer path; malformed/cyclic or external bootloader lists remain outside this evidence. No independent caller-triggered defect was established. No boot or malformed list was run; source-only. This closes only the exact implementation's checked in-tree direct-caller slice, not the other architecture overrides or external boot handoffs.

PC processor API caller follow-up (2026-10-16; no new EK): traced `GetCoreInfo`/`GetCPUInfo` per-core selection and the PC `X86_AnswerTag` paths against selected ShowConfig, SysExplorer and AHI callers. The APIs correctly clamp legacy `GCIT_SelectedProcessor` to CPU 0 and the direct `GetCoreInfo` validates its index; AHI reads processor 0 and selects AVX2 routines only when compiled with AVX2 and its separate `AHIHasAVX2()` check succeeds. PC topology synchronization recheck (EK8974, 2026-10-16): traced each query task’s five per-entry stores, the CPU-local `Forbid` around aggregate recomputation, and both public read APIs. No boot or interleaving was run; source-only.

ARM processor-resource rollback cross-check (EK796, 2026-10-16): independently traced `common_Init` topology ownership, ARM `Processor_Init` array/record allocations and the generated `_set_libinit` failure rollback. `common_Init` returns success even if optional topology allocation fails; when a later ARM init step returns false, `_set_libinit` invokes only registered expunge hooks before generated code frees the resource base. The selected common and ARM sources register no exit/expunge cleanup, so topology and partial ARM records remain allocated; a failure after a secondary launch also skips its pending signal wait/free loop. This confirms EK796 without broadening it. No allocation failure or boot was run; source-only.

ARM SMP probe partial-launch follow-up (EK279, 2026-10-16): verified `NewCreateTask` can return NULL and `Processor_Init` continues without checking it. When one probe starts and another does not, the first signal releases the one-shot any-bit `Wait`; topology then reads the failed CPU's cleared record. If all launches with allocated signals fail, the init task remains in Wait. Expanded EK279 to cover both outcomes. No probe or allocation failure was run; source-only.

SoftIntDispatch in-flight callback review (2026-10-15; EK8935 added): the generic `Enable`/`SC_CAUSE` caller path confirms another ExecSMP CPU can dispatch the shared queue while a previous callback is active. Traced the concrete optional HDAudio producer through `HDA_IntCode` and the shared playback/record buffer state. This is distinct from EK8875's two pre-lock enqueuers and OD2898's teardown overlap; added the re-caused callback concurrency finding with its optional build and timing conditions. No interrupt or audio was run. Historical checkpoint before later restorations: 372 unique numbered EK headings. Source-only.

SoftIntDispatch in-flight callback trace (EK8935 clarified, 2026-10-15): distinguished EK8875’s concurrent pre-lock double-insertion and OD2898’s teardown overlap. `SoftIntDispatch` unlinks a node, restores `ln_Type = NT_INTERRUPT`, releases the queue lock and invokes its callback (`rom/exec/cause.c:164-188`). A later `Cause` can enqueue that same node while the first invocation remains active. On ExecSMP, any CPU’s outermost interrupt exit checks the shared `SFF_SoftInt` flag and calls `core_Cause` (`rom/kernel/kernel_intr.c:30-34,62-67`), so an unrelated interrupt on another CPU can dispatch the requeued callback before the first returns. The selected HDAudio producer re-causes stream callbacks; the AHI handlers update shared flip/current-buffer state and invoke shared audio hooks without a callback lock (`workbench/hidds/hdaudio/hdaclass.c:166-189`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/HDAudio/interrupt.c:46-115,122-169`). CPU-overlap timing and external expectations for callback serialization remain untested; the detailed report limits the finding to this conditional configuration and overlap. No callback or interrupt was run. Source-only.

EK640/KrnInitMemory reachability recheck (2026-10-09): repeated the tree-wide `KrnInitMemory`/`kb_PageSize` identifier search across C, headers, assembly and build/config files. Results remain limited to the API declaration/implementation, reads of `kb_PageSize`, and the unselected `developer/debug/test/kernel/allocator.c` caller; no assignment to `kb_PageSize` or selected production `KrnInitMemory` call appears. Withdraw EK640 from the active list: `AllocKernelBase` uses `MEMF_CLEAR`, there is no checked-in page-size assignment, and the only direct caller is unselected, so the current implementation returns before `mm_Init`. The missing semaphore initialization remains a latent implementation concern only if private kernel state is changed out of tree; no allocator runtime was exercised.
EK284 withdrawal: kernel_fdt counts direct `/cpus/cpu@*` children irrespective of `reg`, while processor.resource compacts only nodes with `reg`; a mismatch requires an incomplete CPU node, and no successful selected-boot case was established. EK286 is withdrawn as an orphaned ID: no standalone trigger, source location, or consequence exists in the current ledger or checkout, so it is not counted as a finding.
EK123/EK124/EK632 task-storage recheck: reread the setter's full first-allocation and growth paths with `TaskGetStorageSlot`, the parent getter and generated per-task-base caller. Growth copies the old array, publishes the replacement, then immediately frees the prior allocation without a cross-CPU lock; the comment's atomic pointer replacement does not serialize readers. `GetParentTaskStorageSlot` uses only local `Forbid`, confirming the documented SMP reader window for EK124. The separate parent-task lifetime path remains EK632. Slot rounding is correct at the 16-entry boundary for valid positive allocated IDs; no extra off-by-one claim was found. No task-storage API was run.

EK756 remote-variable ordering recheck: the `Process` layout requires alphabetic `pr_LocalVars`, `FindVar` exits early on that ordering, and `SetVar` inserts at its sorted point. Security `SetHomeVar` instead inserts `Home` and then `User` each at the head for a remote target, leaving `User` before `Home`; a following `FindVar("Home")` therefore stops at `User` and misses the node. Shell `GetVar` then tries `ENV:` and `ENVARC:` because variable expansion passes only `LV_VAR`, not `GVF_LOCAL_ONLY` (`rom/dos/getvar.c:171-190`; `workbench/c/Shell/convertVar.c:66-75`). If no global Home exists, conversion preserves the original `$Home` text; if one exists, it expands to that unrelated value. The current Security-Startup process gets its own Home through the same-task path and is unaffected; the broken value is in the parent target selected by `Login PARENT`, for subsequent commands. A full direct `secLoginA` caller census found only the selected `Login` command, whose PARENT option is the sole checked remote target path; external callers remain possible. This is a deterministic public variable-propagation defect, separate from EK755's conditional SMP race. No login was run.

EK755 remote `pr_LocalVars` caller audit: re-read all of `security_login.c`'s tag validation, owner application and SetHomeVar path, plus the selected `Login PARENT` caller and DOS `SetVar`/`FindVar`. `secT_Task` permits an authorized remote process; the security helper removes/frees/relinks that process's local-variable list under `Forbid`, which Exec documents as processor-local on SMP. The target's DOS readers/writers take no shared list lock. A direct caller census found only `C:Login` in-tree, and its PARENT concurrency with target access was not established; retain EK755 only for authorized external `secLoginA` callers targeting an active task while it accesses local variables. No interleaving was run.

EK423 withdrawn after rechecking AROS VMM reachability: `AllocAddressRange()` returns success without assigning `VirtAddrStart`/`VirtAddrEnd`, so the manager reaches its later memory-header initialization with an unset base before the proposed MemList race (`mmu_table.c:908-928`; `VM_Manager_Init.c:606-607,742-779`). The generic MemList-lock race was source-plausible only after that point, but no functioning AROS trigger was established. EK9906 now details the earlier startup blocker. No VMM was run.

EK799 named-task lookup follow-up: reread the `FindTask` list scan with PC/Raspberry Pi SMP switch-out and dispatch list handoffs, then traced WiFi worker `StopSupplicant` through `RunConnect()` and its asynchronous replacement start. A false-negative lookup after Ctrl-C can be accepted as completed shutdown, allowing another same-name supplicant launch while the old process remains live. Network Preferences `StopWireless`/`StopMobile` and `RestartStack` were also checked; their false-miss paths can request replacement launches, but no independent completed-stack or duplicate-manager outcome was established, so they are not reported as a concrete consequence. No scheduler interleaving was run.

Wait/scheduler handoff recheck (2026-10-11): traced generic `Wait`'s signal-mask/state/list publication through `KrnSwitch` and the selected x86-64 and native ARM SMP `cpu_Switch` paths. Both store the outgoing task context before releasing its carried `tc_SpinLock`; `Signal` takes the same lock before publishing signals and waking a `TS_WAIT` task, closing the examined early-dispatch/lost-wakeup window. The m68k build selects its assembly `Wait` override and dedicated voluntary switch; it checks `tc_SigRecvd & signalSet` after frame construction and before linking the task into `TaskWait`. RISC-V's `Wait(0)` in the FPU test task is an intentional permanent park after publishing the verdict. No additional defect found in these selected paths; nonselected platform handoffs, other callers and runtime scheduling remain open. No task switch was run.

OOP_GetMethodID lifetime recheck (2026-10-15; EK8784 retained, no new finding): re-read the unlocked `iidtable->Lookup`/`idb->methodbase` access against `release_idbucket` removal/free under `ob_IIDTableLock`. A full checkout `.c`/`.h` search reproduces the ledger census of 514 text matches; the 18 OOP-source matches are internal initialization, fixed Root/Meta dispatch IDs, class-owned method-base discovery, or documentation. No selected in-tree path was found that performs an unpinned lookup concurrently with a class releasing the final interface reference. EK8784 remains conditional on a public client using an IID while its last class/interface reference is released. No concurrent call was run. Source-only.

ExecSMP managed-allocation wait-under-MemList-lock caller census (2026-10-23; no new EK): re-read `nommu_AllocMem()` and its selected managed-header producers. `MEM_LOCK_SHARED` enters `Forbid()` and holds `MemListSpinLock` shared while invoking `mhe_Alloc()`; it avoids the per-header spinlock for `MEMF_SEM_PROTECTED` headers, whose callbacks may wait. TLSF's global MemHeader is initialized with `mh_First = NULL` and `krnCreateTLSFMemHeader()` explicitly does not add it to the list; `MEMF_SEM_PROTECTED` is applied later to managed pool-private headers in `CreatePool()`, after backing allocation has stripped that flag. The other selected managed system headers (Radeon and VideoCore) are not marked semaphore-protected. Therefore no selected global-list callback supplies the potential blocking trigger; the concern remains only for external/custom managed-header providers. No allocation or wait was run; source-only.

# exec-kernel file-by-file audit tracker

Hosted root-directory caller follow-up (2026-10-17; no new EK): traced `SetRootDirectory` through the sole bootstrap caller and the default-config open (`arch/all-hosted/bootstrap/bootstrap.c:181-185,224-235`). Its intended invocation assumption is documented by the MinGW and Darwin run instructions: start from the AROS installation root and run `boot/AROSBootstrap[.exe]` (`arch/all-mingw32/README.txt:29-35`; `arch/all-darwin/README.txt:49-57`). When invoked from the `boot` directory, the executable-presence check then climbs to `AROS.boot`; when invoked from the documented root, it leaves the working directory unchanged. Running from an arbitrary unrelated directory remains unsupported/undocumented and the later default config open fails; I did not promote this as an implementation defect. Custom `-c` behavior remains covered by EK9472. No bootstrap was run.

Generic IRQ callback lock-contract review (EK8933, 2026-10-15): traced the generic SMP dispatcher read lock through callback invocation and the public add/remove write-lock paths. An add/remove attempted by a callback waits forever on the lock held by that same dispatch; public vector docs omit the restriction, while an internal comment states it. No selected in-tree generic IRQ callback self-mutates the chain. The candidate is limited to external/future callers and does not apply to the separate PC/Efika implementations. No interrupt was run. Source-only.

Current report reconciliation (2026-10-15): exact heading recount finds 377 unique numbered EK IDs with no duplicates; updated the linked index to match. Earlier dated totals below are historical checkpoints. Coverage and caller review remain in progress. Source-only.

Genmodule reader error-path follow-up (EK850-EK851): re-read `readline` allocation, growth, initial-read and EOF paths plus `fileopen`/`fileclose` and both selected `readconfig` callers. A persistent initial-read stream error with EOF clear can make primary or override parsing loop on false empty lines (EK850). During a continued long-line read, failed `realloc` or a continuation stream error returns NULL that the section parser mistakes for EOF; either can continue from partial state, and a later override can reuse the freed static buffer (EK851). Existing EK8772 remains distinct: it concerns the incremental `fgets` size when a physical line exceeds the first buffer. No read or allocation failure was induced.

Exec bootstrap allocation follow-up (EK513): rechecked `Allocate`’s NULL return for insufficient MemHeader capacity against both startup base constructors. `PrepareAROSSupportBase` immediately writes through the returned pointer; the SMP-only `ExecLock__PrepareBase` derives a base pointer from a failed allocation, calls `MakeFunctions`, and stores resource fields before the kernel can reach its null-result panic. Detailed finding added to AROS-exec-kernel.md. `__AROSEXEC_SMP__` gates the second path; no low-memory boot was run.


EK671 withdrawn: partial KickMem reservations remain after a later reservation failure, but releasing them could let the running system overwrite preserved reset-proof module images; KickTag activation is deliberately all-or-none. No independent failure from the conservative reservation was established.


EK752 exact-wrap recheck: on 32-bit standard allocation, let `F` be the first free chunk address and request `AllocAbs(0xfffff000, F + 0x1000)` with MungWall disabled. Endpoint arithmetic wraps to F, within the MemHeader bounds; size alignment leaves it unchanged, so p4 also wraps to F. The PC memory-map builder derives its first free chunk from aligned `mh_First` before resetting and relinking the header (`arch/all-pc/kernel/kernel_mmap.c:48-67`). If that chunk contains the requested location, the carve branch sees `p4 == p2`, writes the remainder node at F and sets `p2->mc_Next = p4`, yielding a self-link; it also subtracts the oversized request from `mh_Free` (`rom/exec/memory_nommu.c:88-103,134-153,200-224`). The 32-bit example applies to standard MemHeader builds including i386-PC `notlsf`, m68k Amiga, PPC Sam440, and PPC-CHRP/Efika (`arch/i386-pc/kernel/kernel_startup.c:320-321`; `arch/m68k-amiga/boot/start.c:344-365`; `arch/ppc-sam440/kernel/kernel_startup.c:188-216`; `arch/ppc-chrp/exec/exec_init.c:233-237`; `arch/ppc-chrp/efika/kernel/kernel_init.c:580-590`). x86-64 `notlsf` selects standard headers, but this example does not establish a 64-bit trigger. ARM-native and SiFive-U `notlsf` header creation is disabled inside `#if (0)` (`arch/arm-native/kernel/kernel_startup.c:279-293`; `arch/riscv-native/sifive_u/kernel/kernel_startup.c:188-202`). No selected in-tree caller supplies this near-address-space-sized request. No allocation was attempted; source-only.

EK274 task-reference lifetime recheck: reread the complete SMP `Signal` wake branch, `RemTask` remote-removal path, and architecture-specific reschedule helpers. Signal drops `tc_SpinLock` before passing the raw task pointer to `krnSysCallReschedTask` (`rom/exec/signal.c:350-385,429-440`); selected PC consumes it in `X86_HandleReschedTask` and reads task state before the list lock (`arch/all-pc/exec/platform_init.c:259-295`), while ARM32/AArch64 helpers reacquire `tc_SpinLock` but cannot make a pointer safe if `RemTask` won first and freed the task before the helper's initial lock (`arch/arm-native/exec/platform_init.c:129-164`; `arch/aarch64-native/exec/platform_init.c:114-137`; `rom/exec/remtask.c:97-128,165-181`). The shared lock serializes state/list changes only while the task memory exists; it is not a lifetime reference. Selected `secKill` remains a direct remover (`rom/security/secKill.c:50-58`), and selected PC/Raspberry Pi SMP build gates remain confirmed. This supports the existing EK274 scope; no new finding or runtime interleaving was added.

EK67 co-option reachability recheck: `PrepareExecBase` obtains `args` from the boot `KRN_CmdLine` tag and tests for both options in its early generic initialization (`rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:322-355`). The native ARM tag helper preserves a supplied command line as a `KRN_CmdLine` value (`arch/all-native/kernel/boot_utils.c:59-77`), and the Raspberry Pi boot path also publishes its firmware command-line text under that tag (`arch/arm-raspi/boot/boot.c:684-698`). A repository text search found no checked-in default command line containing both `mungwall` and `stacksnoop`; the finding therefore remains conditional on the boot configuration requesting both, not on the ordinary shipped defaults. The bits are independent (`exec_intern.h:138-142`): allocation/free paths test MungWall and `NewAddTask` tests StackSnoop (`allocmem.c:105,freemem.c:70,newaddtask.c:261-265`). PPC-CHRP has its own `PrepareExecBase` override and compile-time MungWall setup, so EK67 remains scoped to targets using the generic initializer. No boot configuration was run.

EK783 plain-pool arithmetic recheck (consolidated into the detailed allocation-overflow finding): selected i386 and x86-64 CPUs define `AROS_WORSTALIGN` as 16 (`arch/i386-all/include/aros/cpu.h:52`; `arch/x86_64-all/include/aros/cpu.h:50`), so `MEMPOOL_WORSTALIGN` is 16. The requests `AllocPooled(plainPool, 0xfffffff0)` on 32-bit and `AllocPooled(plainPool, 0xfffffffffffffff0)` on 64-bit wrap `InternalAllocPooled`'s adjusted size to zero. With MungWall disabled, `stdAlloc` accepts a nonempty free chunk at rounded size zero; the returned address remains linked as free, and `InternalAllocPooled` overwrites its first word with the MemHeader pointer (`memory.c:1054,565-566,612-673,1217-1224`). Selected i386/x86-64 PC `notlsf` configurations choose standard allocation (`i386-pc/kernel_startup.c:320-321`; `x86_64-pc/kernel_startup.c:374-375`; `kernel_mmap.c:201-205,261-269`). This makes the existing API-boundary finding's immediate metadata consequence explicit; no large request was made.

CreatePool puddle-size overflow recheck (no additional finding): `CreatePool` adds header/context/alignment overhead and then rounds to the runtime page size (`createpool.c:100-108`). If the stored default wraps to zero, the managed branch calls `AllocMemHeader(0)`; its `nommu_AllocMem` reaches the selected allocator callback with size zero. TLSF explicitly returns NULL for a zero rounded size (`rom/kernel/tlsf.c:489-498`), while the checked VideoCore and Radeon managed allocation callbacks are stubs returning NULL (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/vcgfx/vcgfx_memory.c:36-43`; `workbench/hidds/radeon/bitmap.c:343-345`). Thus the managed pool creation returns NULL before `AllocMemHeader` writes a header. In the plain branch, the returned pool handle stores the zero default, but first-allocation growth compares the request against the underflowed limit and then raises its local puddle size to at least `neededSize` (`memory.c:1070-1147`). This can make managed pool creation fail or alter plain-pool default growth sizing, but the checked selected paths did not establish an undersized header or memory corruption. No extreme size was passed.

Genmodule `cdef` terminator boundary recheck (no new candidate): `readsectioncdef` advances five bytes after matching the four-byte `cdef` marker (`tools/genmodule/config.c:1536-1544`). On an ordinary newline-terminated `##end cdef` line, `fgets` writes its terminator one byte after the newline and `readline` replaces the newline with another NUL (`tools/genmodule/fileread.c:57-61`); the extra byte therefore lands on a valid NUL and does not read stale data. This can skip one non-space trailing character in malformed input, or inspect a stale byte if a no-newline terminator is the final file line, but the checked-in selected `cdef` sections use newline-terminated lines and no ordinary failure consequence was established. No bug number is credited; supplied EOF edge and parser diagnostics remain open.

Genmodule handler-generation recheck (EK737 withdrawn): the selected CDVDFS definition has consecutive `Resident=` entries. The parser assigns descending values 0 and 255 (narrowed to signed priorities 0 and -1); generated code inserts them through `Enqueue`, which sorts by descending `ln_Pri` (`tools/genmodule/config.c:2530-2542`; `writestart.c:895-909,933-934`; `rom/exec/enqueue.c:27-76`). The order places `CDFileSystem` ahead of `cdrom-handler`, consistent with ordered resident declarations. AFS explicitly uses successive resident declarations under `.autodetect 127` (`rom/filesys/afs/afs.conf:9-30`), supporting that ordering interpretation. Checked DOS/partition consumers iterate the list but no selected failure from this priority sequence was established; no bug is retained. Other generated handler behavior and resource lifetimes remain open; no handler was initialized.

Resource publication caller follow-up (no new candidate): reread `AddResource`, `OpenResource` and `RemResource` with the selected usergroup credential-resource constructor and initialization gate (`rom/exec/{addresource,openresource,remresource}.c`; `workbench/libs/usergroup/{resource,usergroup,credential}.c`). `CredentialInit` allocates and initializes its embedded global process, credentials, name and resource header before calling `AddResource`; the selected usergroup initializer first checks `OpenResource` and wraps that check/create sequence in `Forbid` (`usergroup.c:226-235`; `resource.c:35-65`). On SMP, `Forbid` alone does not serialize unrelated CPUs, and `AddResource` does not enforce unique names, but a simultaneous selected invocation of this same library init hook has not been established from the generated library lifecycle. No duplicate credential-resource finding is counted. `RemResource` only unlinks a node; no direct in-tree remover for this credential resource was found, so its open-count-one persistence is consistent with its global fallback design. Generated init serialization, external callers and resource teardown remain open; no resource lifecycle was run.

Generic `OpenDevice` completion and ownership recheck: reread its complete lookup/open/result body with `CloseDevice`, the LDDemon wrapper, selected printer/RNDIS class expunges, and the existing console/timer and optional VMM failure callers (`rom/exec/opendevice.c:73-139`; `closedevice.c:51-87`; `rom/lddemon/lddemon.c:533-555`). It zeroes `io_Unit` before dispatch, judges a driver's Open success from `io_Error`, and clears `io_Device` after a failed Open; it does not close or free a unit that the driver's own failed Open allocated. That leaves such cleanup with the driver and supports the already recorded gameport failed-open unit finding, rather than an additional generic Exec leak. The device-list lock is dropped before the Open vector and class expunge can free the base on another CPU (EK9099). LDDemon serializes its own same-name load/open acquisition, but the generic early vector and direct class removal still need the separate lifetime check. Selected null-request callers remain caller-side failures because this API requires a valid I/O request. No runtime open/expunge overlap was run.

Exception-handler registration/removal follow-up: reread both complete generic bodies and checked the selected PC platform/APIC registrations, optional VMM page-fault registration/removal, and the dispatch snapshot. Registration appends without enforcing the SMP dispatch snapshot's eight-entry cap (EK11), while removal unlinks under the same list lock but cannot wait for a callback already copied out of the lock. The selected APIC heartbeat replacement retains its static callback and KernelBase data during reset; it does not establish freed callback state. EK275 is withdrawn: the only selected in-tree lifetime example was optional VMM, whose AROS startup has no assigned range under EK9906. Null removal handles are accepted by the generic remover, so failed registration followed by null cleanup is not a separate failure here. Wider modules using this preliminary kernel API and actual SMP timing remain open.

Exec message and housekeeper follow-up (no new candidate): reread the complete `PutMsg`/`InternalPutMsg`, `ReplyMsg` and `ServiceTask` bodies (`rom/exec/putmsg.c:1-132`; `replymsg.c:1-69`; `service.c:1-124`) against `WaitIO`'s reply removal (`waitio.c:55-82`), the self-removal publication path (`remtask.c:125-163`) and the selected housekeeper creation (`exec_init.c:308-335`). `PutMsg` sets `NT_MESSAGE`, whereas self-removal deliberately calls `InternalPutMsg` to preserve the task node type; the service switch therefore sees task states rather than a message-node type change. Port list insertion is locked on SMP, but `ReplyMsg` still publishes `NT_REPLYMSG` before insertion (EK8799), and `WaitIO` still removes without the port spinlock (EK8819). The self-removal sender still publishes `TS_INVALID` before its final dispatch while the any-CPU service task can reclaim it (EK807 (former EK659)). `ChildStatus` was reread against the selected POSIX `waitpid` caller (`rom/exec/childstatus.c:1-93`; `compiler/crt/posixc/waitpid.c:113-141`): the live-child scan remains protected only by local `Forbid`; a notified child exit moves its ETask from `et_Children` to `mp_MsgList` under the task-list lock (`rom/exec/exec_util.c:307-330`), while ChildStatus scans those lists separately without that lock. A read between unlink and enqueue can therefore return CHILD_NOTFOUND and make waitpid return ECHILD for the live notified child (EK812). The non-notified-child use-after-free remains outside ChildStatus's documented contract. This check found no independent new defect; other callers and actual SMP interleavings remain open.

M68K borrowed-object lookup shadow exhaustion (EK9275; incorporates prior PID lookup candidate EK418): generated `FindResident`, `FindTaskByPID`, `FindPort`, and `FindSemaphore` thunks pass successful borrowed native results to `shadow_create_by_name` (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:1849-1855,2060-2066,2237-2243,2475-2481`). The `FindResident` path returns an existing pointer from `SysBase->ResModules` (`rom/exec/findresident.c:53-64`); the other APIs return list-owned or task-owned objects. This allocates a new guest shadow without native-pointer deduplication or per-lookup release (`m68kemu_shadow.c:75-92,122-132`), consuming the fixed 256-slot map (`m68kemu_intern.h:92-93`; `m68kemu_thunks.c:444-458`). Once full, these lookup thunks return zero despite native success. Further callers are reconciled in the 2026-11-01 expansion below; object teardown invalidation and guest-client workload remain open. No lookup loop was run.

M68K message-shadow failure follow-up (EK416/EK418): the generated `FindPort` wrapper creates a fresh guest shadow for each successful borrowed lookup (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:2059-2067`); `shadow_register` stops at 256 entries (`m68kemu_intern.h:92-93`; `m68kemu_thunks.c:444-458`). A guest can retain an earlier valid port shadow, fill the table through repeated same-name lookups, then call the manual `GetMsg` thunk on that port. `GetMsg` dequeues natively before `shadow_create` attempts registration and returns zero on failure without requeue or reply (`m68kemu_thunks.c:621-641`; `m68kemu_shadow.c:75-92`). This supplies an in-tree API sequence for the failure condition, not a runtime reproduction. The bridge's actual guest clients and sender wait behavior remain open.

MinGW host IRQ interface follow-up (no new kernel candidate): reread `arch/all-mingw32/kernel/host_intr.c:29-120,140-245,379-428` against all checked-in `KrnCauseSystemIRQ`/`KrnGetSystemIRQObject` clients in WingDI, emul.handler and the hosted socket module. The exported `NonMaskableInt` starts at -1 and has no checked-in assignment after initialization, so the switcher's non-maskable exception to `Ints_Enabled` (`:165`) has no selected producer. `KrnCauseSystemIRQ` forwards a valid allocated slot to `SetEvent`; its Boolean return is handled only where a client needs it. The selected host event objects are auto-reset, while `PendingInts` remains a Boolean, consistent with EK672's repeated-timer-loss path. A failed emul.handler worker startup omits its allocated IRQ release (`arch/all-mingw32/filesys/emul_handler/emul_handler_native.c:70-86`), but that is a filesystem client cleanup issue rather than a defect in this kernel API. External DLL callers, Windows event delivery and shutdown synchronization remain open. No hosted process was run.

MinGW host IRQ release boundary recheck (EK823 / OD2277): `arch/all-mingw32/kernel/host_intr.c:264-294` reserves timer IRQs 0 and 1 before setting `Ints_Num=2`. Rechecking WINGDI `GDI_Init` failure labels found that failure of its second or third dynamic IRQ allocation still reaches an unconditional free of the static, untouched IRQ field zero (`arch/all-mingw32/hidd/wingdi/gdi_native.c:381-440`). This clears the reserved timer-0 allocation bit; a later `KrnAllocSystemIRQ` can hand out the existing waitable timer handle as a device IRQ, whose `KrnCauseSystemIRQ` uses `SetEvent` and cannot signal it (`host_intr.c:379-427`). EK823 records the kernel contract consequence; OD2277 records the selected caller path. The socket client's later-startup resolver IRQ leak remains network N12. No allocation failure or Windows host run was performed.

EK8909 follows the AArch64 BCM2837 heartbeat registration into its timer initializer: the selected probe installs the callback, common post-init invokes it, and a diagnostic poll has no timeout if SYSTIMER_CLO stops advancing. ARM32 has no corresponding poll; Pi 4/5 use other probes. Hardware timer failure remains untested.
EK8873 follows the selected ARM32/AArch64 BCM2708 timer initializer through platform post-init. A failed timer-node allocation prevents compare programming, handler insertion and IRQ enable; the initializer returns an indeterminate local pointer, which post-init ignores. SMP CNTP supplies scheduler quantum but no VBlank delivery; UP has no alternate platform heartbeat. The AArch64 Pi 4/5 generic-timer hooks avoid this allocation. Hardware delivery and actual low-memory boot remain untested.

AArch64 native context-size and allocation follow-up (no new candidate): reconciled selected `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/{cpu_init,createcontext,kernel_execsmp}.c` with `arch/aarch64-all/include/aros/cpucontext.h:12-22`, native `kernel_intern.h:92-125`, `rom/kernel/{kernel_objects.h:11,deletecontext.c:47-55}`, and the selected `arch/aarch64-native/exec/preparecontext.c:21-87`. The 280-byte `ExceptionContext`, 528-byte `VFPContext`, and eight-byte alignment allowance give `kb_ContextSize=816`; `KrnCreateContext` aligns the tail inside that allocation and the generic deleter frees the same size. PrepareContext preserves the FPU pointer and sets EL1t/PSTATE for a new task. A failed `Exec_InitETask` in the secondary bootstrap still omits `KrnDeleteContext` for its earlier successful allocation (EK48); no separate context-size or tail-overrun finding is credited. Secondary-core allocation failure, real vector save/restore, and runtime dispatch remain open.

Device/resource removal and usergroup port-lifetime follow-up (no new Exec candidate): reread `rom/exec/remdevice.c:57-85` and `closedevice.c:59-98` against the selected dynamic-device and pending-I/O caller summaries. `RemDevice` still holds only local `Forbid` around the expunge vector and does not close EK9099's SMP lookup/expunge gap; `CloseDevice` still requires the caller to finish outstanding I/O, as EK358's WaitForPort path documents. Input key-repeat caller reconciliation (OD9868 in other-driver report): ordinary input.device timer processing calls `GetMsg(keytimermp)` before `SendIO`, as the existing `getmsg.c` ledger row says. In a simultaneous command/timer wake, its earlier `IND_ADDEVENT` release branch can instead call `WaitIO` to consume that timer reply; the later branch still reads the saved timer signal and ignores `GetMsg`'s null result (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:49-52,262-277,344-368,459-480`). This is an input-worker sequencing error, not an additional Exec `GetMsg` or `WaitIO` finding. Sam440 DMA cache-pair caller check (no new candidate): reread the full selected `arch/ppc-sam440/exec/{cachepredma,cachepostdma}.c` bodies and the Sam440 Exec manifest against the generic DMA API contract and direct calls in the selected EMAC driver (`rom/exec/{cachepredma,cachepostdma}.c`; `arch/ppc-sam440/exec/mmakefile.src`; `workbench/devs/networks/emac/{emac_unit,mal}.c`). Sam440 PreDMA translates the starting address and clears its cache range; PostDMA invalidates after a device-to-RAM transfer. EMAC instead uses `CacheClearE` directly for receive/transmit buffers and descriptors, so it does not demonstrate a new paired-API defect in these wrappers. The repository has 40 C/header files containing a `CachePreDMA(` reference across mixed targets; other selected Sam440 DMA clients, buffer physical contiguity and cache-line ownership remain pending. No DMA was run.

Task-affinity direct-caller and mask-lifetime recheck (EK273/EK541; no new candidate): reread all of `rom/task/SetTaskAffinity.c` against its checked-in C call census, selected PC/AArch64 `KrnGetCPUCount` implementations, and the SMP affinity debug test. Only `developer/debug/test/smp/smpaffinity.c` directly calls the setter in maintained C; the production DOS/Exec references found are comments. The API allocates a cleared fresh mask before locking when it needs one, rewrites an existing task-owned mask in place under `tc_SpinLock`, frees an unused fresh mask after a concurrent setter wins, then can pass its borrowed `cur` to `KrnScheduleCPU` after unlock. EK273's setter arm is now explicitly qualified as public-API/debug-test reachability, while its `SetTaskPri` and `Signal` arms retain production callers. On AArch64 the count is a population count and the setter's `0..count-1` loop still has EK541's sparse-core issue. Generated dispatch, external clients and concurrent runtime timing remain pending.

PC interrupt-controller callback/failure follow-up (no new candidate): reread all bodies in `rom/kernel/kernel_interruptcontroller.c` with the paired identity/instance definitions (`kernel_irqtypes.h`, `kernel_interruptcontrollers.h`), selected PC `APICInt_Register` and `IOAPICInt_Register`, the MADT IO-APIC parser's registration branch, and final `ictl.c` initialization. First registration assigns an ID and calls the controller's `ic_Register` before publication; IO-APIC's callback returns the invalid ID on disabled state or failed ACPI `\\_PIC`, and its parser checks the combined invalid result before touching the new per-instance slot (`arch/all-pc/kernel/acpi_ioapic.c:121-155,980-1000`). Duplicate-name registrations skip that callback and increase the existing instance count; this matches the selected per-CPU local-APIC and multi-IO-APIC registration shape, while count truncation at the packed instance width lacks a checked-in ordinary machine trigger. `krnInitInterruptControllers` calls each published controller's init once with its count, and `ictl.c` panics if none reports success. EK110/EK111 cover separate IO-APIC initialization/routing paths. Exceptional late AP startup, failed-callback ID consumption, external controller producers and runtime firmware behavior remain pending.

SetTaskPri selected self-demotion caller follow-up (EK833; no new candidate): reread the full `SetTaskPri` ready/running/waiting-list and post-lock scheduler paths (`rom/exec/settaskpri.c:53-153`) against the direct in-tree C caller census, then traced ACPICA's `LockSpin` failure loop (`arch/all-native/acpica/acpios_aros.c:392-414`) and the animation datatype's player/buffer priority handoff (`workbench/classes/datatypes/animation/animationplayback.c:302-310`; `animationbuffer.c:349-356`). ACPICA repeatedly lowers its own priority without an immediate switch request; on a single CPU with a ready lock holder this can prolong contention until another scheduler event, so EK833 now names that conditional caller. Animation's player also lowers itself while asking the buffer worker to purge, but its asynchronous signal and buffer completion do not establish a separate priority defect; GD2103 covers the worker's independent exiting-task lifetime race. AHI's `128` call remains OD812. Other task states, generated/external callers and runtime scheduler timing remain pending.

OpenSBI global-map I²C caller follow-up (no new candidate): reread `KrnMapGlobal` and the complete `krnMMUMapPages` body (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/mapglobal.c:19-58`; `kernel_mmu.c:148-198`) against the selected DesignWare I²C discovery and `dwi2c_add` register mapping (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/dwi2c/dwi2c_init.c:119-225`). This caller obtains its register address and size from `FDT_GetReg`, rejects zero values, and tests the mapping result before initializing its lock or probing the controller; a reported mapping failure skips that controller. The cast from the FDT's 64-bit region size into the 32-bit public mapping length remains a conditional large-region issue, but no selected firmware node with a register span beyond 4 GiB or dependent probe was established. EK676 still owns the fixed page-table-pool exhaustion path, which cannot return failure to this caller. Other firmware maps, resource sizing and runtime MMU behavior remain pending.

Unix-hosted page mapping and release follow-up (no new candidate): reread the complete hosted `KrnAllocPages`, `KrnFreePages` and `KrnSetProtection` bodies (`arch/all-unix/kernel/{allocpages,freepages,setprotection}.c`) with the selected `LoadSeg` and `CreateSegList` callers. Allocation rounds the requested length to the host page size, tries `mmap` with requested permissions, optionally retries without `MAP_32BIT`, and then retries R/W if executable mapping failed; failure after those tries returns null. Free passes the caller's byte length to `munmap`, whose independent 32-bit parameter narrowing is already EK21; ignored protection-result behavior is constrained by the void kernel API and the executable-page paths already examined in EK516/EK712. The far-mapping retry is conditional on `MAP_32BIT` being defined and executable requests reaching this override; the source alone does not establish a selected host configuration with that combination, so no separate relocation finding is promoted. Host `mmap`/`mprotect` outcomes and external page-API clients remain pending.

Kernel memory-statistics query recheck (no new candidate): reread the complete `KrnStatMemoryA` and `mm_StatMemHeader` bodies (`rom/kernel/statmemory.c:16-128`; `mm_linear.c:449-575`) against the selected `AddResource` caller (`rom/exec/addresource.c:74-101`) and all maintained direct C-call matches. The only production in-tree query requests `KMS_PageSize`, so `KrnStatMemoryA` returns before traversing `SysBase->MemList` or entering the block-map statistics loop. Aggregate queries initialize output values, filter physical flags, then lock each block header while walking its page map, but the surrounding MemList traversal remains unprotected; no selected production caller of those aggregate tags was found. EK25's explicit-address free-count error and EK639's unset generic `kb_PageSize` remain separate roots. Direct external aggregate callers and architecture-specific MMU initialization remain pending.

Virtual-to-physical caller and platform recheck (EK8839): enumerated maintained direct C calls to `KrnVirtualToPhysical`, then reread generic identity fallback, ARM32 and m68k overrides (`rom/kernel/virtualtophysical.c`; `arch/arm-native/kernel/virtualtophysical.c`; `arch/m68k-all/kernel/virtualtophysical.c`). Kernel page API direct-caller and override check (no new candidate): searched maintained C sources for direct `KrnAllocPages`/`KrnFreePages` calls, then reread the generic pair (`rom/kernel/{allocpages,freepages}.c`), both direct allocation callers (`compiler/arossupport/createseglist.c:57-101`; `rom/dos/loadseg.c:55-108`), and the Unix-hosted override/selection (`arch/all-unix/kernel/{allocpages,freepages}.c`; `mmakefile.src:49`). Both direct allocations request a system-chosen address; neither exercises the generic allocator's explicit-address branch. LoadSeg pairs its executable-hunk allocation with a length-preserving FreeFunc, while CreateSegList records the byte size in its segment header and relies on UnLoadSeg's page/pool distinction. The Unix-hosted `KrnAllocPages` substitutes `mmap` for the generic `kb_PageSize`-gated implementation, so generic EK639 does not apply there. Existing EK516/EK712 cover the separate hosted executable-page transitions and fallback behavior. External API users, generated call sites and runtime mapping behavior remain pending.

Signal-release caller check (no new candidate): reread `rom/exec/allocsignal.c:57-143`, `freesignal.c:48-56`, `createmsgport.c:48-78`, and `deletemsgport.c:47-55` against the PPP worker's direct signal lifecycle (`workbench/devs/networks/ppp/init.c:52-114,257-277`) and printer worker's port/signal cleanup (`workbench/devs/printer/driver.c:405-484`). `CreateMsgPort` checks a failed bit allocation and frees its port allocation; `DeleteMsgPort` frees the bit in the caller's task, matching the selected same-task worker cleanup. PPP checks `AllocSignal(-1)` before installing its bit or shifting it into `Wait`, and its `if(signalbit)` teardown cannot miss a successful automatic allocation under the default `TaskSigAlloc=0xFFFF` mask (`rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:319`), which reserves bit zero. The valid bit-31 signed-shift case is EK8800; invalid signal numbers are excluded; these selected caller paths do not establish a separate finding. Wider caller and task-ownership checks remain pending.

Network timer-reply caller check (EK9072): read selected dwmac and bcmgenet worker timer branches and teardown (`workbench/devs/networks/{dwmac/dwmac_unit.c:830-895,bcmgenet/bcmgenet_unit.c:1055-1145}`). Each dequeues a timer reply with `GetMsg`, clears `timerpending`, and rearms only while running; shutdown calls AbortIO/WaitIO only when `timerpending` is true. The same completion is therefore not removed twice on the checked path, including a wake that carries Ctrl-C and the timer signal together. PPP's serial helper calls AbortIO/WaitIO *before* draining its timer or serial reply port (`workbench/devs/networks/ppp/serial.c:49-80,190-208`), also excluding a GetMsg-then-WaitIO sequence. FEC's timer branch drains the reply port before rearming, while its Ctrl-C branch waits without first dequeuing (`workbench/devs/networks/fec/fec_unit.c:285-339`); its separate queued-input semicolon is already OD238. Nouveau and VMwareSVGA timer-compatibility helpers already have normal reply ownership checked in the graphics ledger. No new EK9072 sibling is credited from these selected callers; hardware completion and other remaining same-file matches remain open. No driver was run.

Further EK9072 caller matching: `compiler/pthread/pthread.c:260-323` dequeues up to two messages on the timed mutex's stack reply port; `CloseTimerDevice` calls AbortIO/WaitIO only when `CheckIO` says the timer is still pending (`:173-194`). Once the timer reply was dequeued, that branch is skipped, so this path does not repeat Logger's immediate double removal. AHI-Handler's `GetMsg` calls consume DOS packets from `PktPort`, while its `WaitIO` calls use separate AHI audio requests (`workbench/devs/AHI/AHI-Handler/main.c:259-276,475-510,650-670,745-765`). Speech's control-message dequeue and separate playback-slot waits were already recorded in the other-driver ledger. PoPo GUI handles events with `GetMsg(po_MsgPort)` but its periodic timer uses `CheckIO`/`WaitIO` on a different reply port (`rom/usb/poseidon/popo.gui.c:277-290,829`); lan78xx likewise dequeues task or SANA requests, not its timer reply, before its checked timer waits (`rom/usb/classes/lan78xx/lan78xx.class.c:568,628-641,723`). These selected same-file matches do not add an EK9072 sibling. Other matched files, concurrency and device completion contracts remain open; no request was run.

Timer-reply double-consumption caller check (EK9072): searched C files containing both `GetMsg` and `WaitIO`, then read the selected PopupMenu timer loop and teardown (`workbench/libs/popupmenu/pm.c:593-618,743-763,1078-1090`) against Exec's dequeue and WaitIO paths. PopupMenu removes a completed timer reply with `GetMsg`, re-arms that same request with `SendIO` before leaving its event-loop branch, then aborts/waits for the currently rearmed request during cleanup. This does not repeat Logger's immediate `GetMsg`-then-`WaitIO` on the same completed reply. Sound datatype's `GetMsg` uses a separate ObjectMsg command handshake in its constructor/disposer (`workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/dispatch.c:858-895,1424-1447`); the nearby `WaitIO` calls operate on audio or cursor requests. BoingIconBar's FocusTimer exclusion is already recorded in the graphics ledger. Other files in the broad same-file search still require function-level matching; no new candidate is credited from these checked callers. No timer or UI session was run.

PC kernel/HPET row-inventory reconciliation: compared every top-level `.c` file in `arch/all-pc/kernel` (51), `arch/i386-pc/kernel` (5), `arch/x86_64-pc/kernel` (9) and `arch/all-pc/hpet` (5) against explicit ledger paths; all 70 have rows. EK75 boot-source follow-up (`rom/exec/{sumkickdata,initkicktags,prepareexecbase}.c`, `arch/m68k-amiga/boot/start.c`): expanded the `KickMemPtr` search from C assignments to all checked-in source references, including the boot include layout and generated m68k shadow offsets. The located writes zero the field or copy it from a previous ExecBase (`rom/exec/execstrap_init.c:142`; `prepareexecbase.c:179,366`; `arch/m68k-amiga/boot/start.c:756,881,1003`; `arch/m68k-amiga/exec/moveexecbase.c:50,113`; PPC startup clears it). `rom/kernel/kernel_romtags.c:168-172` describes the checksum contract but does not create a list. `InitKickTags` reserves all `ml_NumEntries`, while `SumKickData` includes only the fixed one-entry structure in its checksum (`initkicktags.c:247-264`; `sumkickdata.c:74-91`). EK75 now has a detailed conditional entry: `SumKickData` hashes only the fixed one-entry `MemList` size while `InitKickTags` consumes `ml_NumEntries`; later entries can change without invalidating the saved checksum. A source search found no checked-in multi-entry `SysBase->KickMemPtr` producer, and the selected m68k bootstrap uses a separate `BootStruct.mlist`, so ordinary selected reachability remains unproven. External reset-proof producers and architecture firmware state remain open. No boot was run.

Exec manifest-to-ledger reconciliation (`rom/exec/mmakefile.src`): parsed the selected module's `ALL_FUNCTIONS` (145 names), `INIT_FILES` (2) and `FILES` (19) lists at the fixed commit. All 166 named local `.c` paths exist under `rom/exec` and have explicit rows in this ledger; a separate top-level directory census found 169 `.c` files with ledger rows. This verifies local inventory coverage for this manifest, not full function/caller review or exact architecture override expansion.
