Architecture-specific override and boot-source mapping remain open.

Exec `RemHead` caller-lock follow-up (`rom/exec/{remhead,getmsg,cause}.c`): the helper performs only the list unlink and leaves synchronization to callers (`remhead.c:59-73`). `GetMsg` holds the port's write spinlock around that unlink on SMP (`getmsg.c:59-72`), while `SoftIntDispatch` holds the selected soft-interrupt queue's write spinlock around its unlink (`cause.c:159-177`). The dispatcher's later `ln_Type` reset occurs after unlocking (`cause.c:177-182`); its separate enqueue-side queued-state test also precedes the lock (`cause.c:84-108`), which remains the EK35 double-enqueue interleaving. This check does not establish an unlocked `RemHead` defect in those two callers. Other helper callers, port and interrupt owner lifetimes, and architecture delivery remain open.

Soft-interrupt port caller check (EK35, no new finding): `InternalPutMsg` drops a port's queue spinlock before `PA_SOFTINT` calls `Cause` (`rom/exec/putmsg.c:83-115`), so that lock does not generally serialize calls on its interrupt node. The platform-selected RISC-V dwmac driver's write port uses this action and its TX completion IRQ can also `Cause` the same node (`workbench/devs/networks/dwmac/dwmac_unit.c:518-543,1019-1038,1120`; `dwmac_handler.c:82-116`). Its normal request handler holds `dwu_Lock` through `PutMsg` and releases it at handler exit (`dwmac_handler.c:471-555`), so two task-side writes are serialized; an IRQ arriving on another CPU would be the possible overlap. The dwmac target is opt-in (`dwmac/mmakefile.src:5-21`), and this pass did not establish its IRQ affinity or an SMP configuration that builds it, so dwmac is not added as a confirmed EK35 trigger. The existing selected PCI USB completion/submission trace remains EK35's concrete caller. No interrupt timing was run.

Soft-interrupt dequeue transition recheck (EK35, no separate finding): `SoftIntDispatch` removes a node under its queue spinlock, unlocks, and only then restores `ln_Type = NT_INTERRUPT` before invoking the handler (`rom/exec/cause.c:160-188`). A concurrent `Cause` in the unlock-to-type-reset interval can see `NT_SOFTINT`, skip a fresh enqueue, and set the pending flag (`:84-116`). That second call is coalesced into the first invocation, which has not begun yet; for the checked PCI USB submission path, requests are appended to the controller queue before `SureCause` invokes `Cause` (`rom/usb/pciusb/uhwcmd.c:1082-1089`), and the OHCI completion callback checks that queue when invoked (`rom/usb/pciusb/ohci/ohci_hcd.c:1310-1339`). This interval alone does not prove a dropped work item or callback. A distinct finding would require a selected handler with one-request-per-invocation semantics or another state transition that the pending callback cannot observe. The earlier EK35 double-enqueue interleaving remains valid because both callers can pass the pre-lock type test while the node is still linked. No interleaving was run.

Apple Silicon executable-segment fallback cross-check: `compiler/arossupport/createseglist.c:57-100` was traced through the configure selector (`configure.in:1806-1811`), Darwin RAM-pool permissions (`arch/all-unix/bootstrap/memory.c:58-76,113-115`), hosted page allocation (`arch/all-unix/kernel/allocpages.c:60-140`), and selected DOS boot/Shell callers. EK712 records the conditional case where page allocation fails but `AllocMem` succeeds: `CreateSegList` returns a jump segment from the nonexecutable pool and skips the R/X transition. This is not an ordinary successful-page-allocation failure and is distinct from EK516's loaded ELF code hunks. Other generated callers, host memory pressure and runtime entry remain pending; no segment was executed.

IRQ registration caller cross-check: reread the MinGW32 handler registration and dispatcher (`arch/all-mingw32/kernel/addirqhandler.c`, `kernel_intr.c`) against generic removal (`rom/kernel/remirqhandler.c`). The MinGW32 handler list is shared and dispatch selects nodes by their saved IRQ number; the selected in-tree host IRQ range is 0–255, so this pass adds no distinct kernel candidate. Tracing a separate PCI ATA caller of interrupt registration exposed a DMA-buffer leak on failed bus construction, now recorded as DISK-316 in the disk report (`rom/hidds/ata_pci/ata_pci_busclass.c:104-189,217-240`; `probe.c:636-663`). The probe caller releases its bus record and device reference on that failure; those are not part of DISK-316. Other IRQ callers and dispatch interleavings remain pending. No IRQ was run.

Generic CLI/STI target census: all architecture kernel manifests with a local implementation found by exact source search name both `cli` and `sti`: PC, Unix, MinGW32, ARM, AArch64, RISC-V64, m68k Amiga and native PPC (`arch/{all-pc,all-unix,all-mingw32,arm-native,aarch64-native,riscv64-all,m68k-amiga,ppc-native}/kernel/mmakefile.src`). The architecture implementations, bootstrap dispatch and any platform outside this manifest census remain separate review work.

EK124 threshold and lifetime recheck: generated `pertaskbase` configs set both `OPTION_PERTASKBASE` and `OPTION_DUPBASE` (`tools/genmodule/config.c:1025-1032`); the task-slot allocator starts at ID 1, first storage allocation has 16 entries, and writing ID 16 grows and frees the prior array (`rom/task/task_init.c:66-75`; `AllocTaskStorageSlot.c:51-76`; `SetTaskStorageSlot.c:70-108`). `GetParentTaskStorageSlot` reaches the generated parent-base fallback (`rom/task/GetParentTaskStorageSlot.c:52-63`; `tools/genmodule/writestart.c:317-322,1320-1326`), and the generated writer uses `SetTaskStorageSlot` (`:1374-1386`). This confirms the stale-array interleaving if the parent grows during the child read; `Forbid` is local on SMP (`rom/exec/forbid.c:58-60`). Maintained configs include posixc, usergroup, png, z, lzma, tiff, jpeg, zstd and bz2, but their selected run-time load order and a concurrent parent/child open at the threshold remain unverified. Detailed conditional finding restored in the report; no schedule was run.

Procure/Vacate selected-caller census: an exact C/assembly call search found the selected pthread timed-lock helper as the only non-test direct pair (`compiler/pthread/pthread.c:249-323`), alongside developer semaphore tests and the generated m68k guest thunks. The helper first dequeues up to two messages from its one local port, then calls `Vacate` only when the timer reply was among them; `Vacate` either removes a still-queued semaphore request and replies it or releases an already granted count (`rom/exec/{procure,vacate}.c`). The helper's uncontended timed-lock bug is covered by EK567, while EK568 covers its pre-send timer cleanup; no independent Exec-side cancellation defect was established by this direct caller census. External users, simultaneous grant/timeout ordering and post-cancel reply-port ownership remain open; no semaphore wait was run.

LoadResource open-failure contract follow-up: reread the selected command's library/device branches (`workbench/c/LoadResource/main.c:45-133`) against Exec `OpenLibrary`, `OpenDevice`, `CloseDevice`, and `OpenResource` (`rom/exec/{openlibrary,opendevice,closedevice,openresource}.c`), then traced the loader's replaced `OpenDevice` through its per-name load semaphore and original Exec vector (`rom/lddemon/lddemon.c:311-453,533-564,885-904`). The command intentionally treats a failed device open as success if the named device was nevertheless published, since its purpose is loading. LDDemon passes the request to Exec's original vector after its load attempt; that vector clears `io_Device` on failed open, and the loader also clears both device and unit on early load failure. `CloseDevice` explicitly accepts a failed request. InitResident publishes a successfully initialized device through `AddDevice` (`rom/exec/initresident.c:105-158`), so the command's list lookup can distinguish that outcome from a missing device even when its unit zero open fails. Its optional SMP `execlock.resource` lookup is followed by a guarded device-list lookup or a `Forbid` fallback, so the inspected path does not introduce a separate unprotected list read. No new Exec candidate was credited. Device-init failures before publication, wider clients and actual loader timing remain open; no load was run.

AllocSignal caller check in Raspberry Pi dma.resource: traced the two automatic signal allocations in `DMAWaitChannel` through its IRQ waiter publication, timer safety pulse, bounded polling fallback, AbortIO/WaitIO and release (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/dma/dma_init.c:342-496`). Unlike unchecked-bit callers already listed below, it tests both allocation results before shifting them and frees each bit only after clearing the IRQ-visible waiter; a missing bit keeps the bounded polling path. The two direct wait clients are vcgfx and VC4Gallium; neither establishes an invalid explicit signal number at the Exec API. This does not establish an invalid-signal-number bug or add an allocator candidate. Concurrent same-channel waits, host timer/device response and actual IRQ timing remain open; no DMA request was run.

RemTask and SDL event-task lifecycle follow-up: reread the full self/remote removal branches (`rom/exec/remtask.c:52-191`) against the optional hosted SDL event task and its startup-failure cleanup (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/event.c:42-155`; `startup.c:272-301`). The SDL cleanup calls `RemTask` on its worker while the worker's stack-allocated VBlank server is still registered. That retained server and freed task-stack exposure is already graphics GD113; the generic remote-running-task danger remains EK473 on an SMP target, but the checked SDL target chain does not establish such an SMP configuration or a concurrent executing worker at this cleanup point. `RemTask` does not remove arbitrary interrupt servers registered by the target task, and its documented contract does not promise to do so, so no new generic Exec defect is credited. Optional SDL startup timing, host target SMP selection and other RemTask callers remain open; no task was run.

PC APIC IRQ allocation/release follow-up: reread the selected PC `KrnAllocIRQ` wrapper, complete `core_APIC_AllocMSI` body, generic `KrnFreeIRQ` fallback, PC kernel manifest, and both PCI MSI/MSI-X allocation branches (`arch/all-pc/kernel/{allocirq.c,apic_msi.c,mmakefile.src}`; `rom/kernel/freeirq.c`; `arch/all-pc/hidds/pcipc/pcipc_deviceclass.c:380-540`). The manifest selects the PC allocator but no PC release override. The allocator advances a shared cursor after enabling a run; this remains EK810 (former EK43) for unreclaimed reservations and EK325 for concurrent overlapping reservations. The PCI MSI-X caller clamps its count to at least one before allocation; the legacy MSI caller's zero-minimum countdown is already other-driver OD948, with selected direct clients requesting one or more. A failed legacy-MSI enable read-back returns FALSE after reserving vectors and does not release them (`pcipc_deviceclass.c:510-561`), extending EK810 to failed setup attempts as well as successful acquire/release cycles. A direct zero-count kernel request does not establish a further selected driver fault, and no additional distinct candidate is credited. External callers, controller initialization on specific machines, and runtime IRQ behavior remain open; no IRQ was run.

Exec allocation and port-owner follow-up: reread `NewAllocEntry`, its legacy `AllocEntry` wrapper and `FreeEntry`, comparing their bodies with the selected caller census already tracked in the rows below (`rom/exec/{newallocentry,allocentry,freeentry}.c`). The allocator's `UWORD` count cannot overflow its MemList header-size arithmetic on maintained 32/64-bit layouts, and failure after an allocated block frees earlier successful blocks; the existing task-allocation findings remain EK24/EK469/EK470. Reread `CreateMsgPort` and `DeleteMsgPort` against Zune Configdata's selected filesystem notification port (`rom/exec/{createmsgport,deletemsgport}.c`; `workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/configdata.c:601-620,796-804,1316-1345`). The Exec deleter documents that remaining messages are not replied; Configdata's normal reload callback neither dequeues nor replies to the RAM handler's messages (graphics GD2272), while its `EndNotify` disposal path drains them. No new helper-level defect is credited from these paths. External allocator clients, queued-port ownership and cross-task deletion remain open; no allocation failure or notification was run.

OpenSBI high-device-window/RAM collision check (EK678): compared FDT RAM tuple admission and MMU identity-map coverage with the selected GOP framebuffer and PCIDT high-BAR remap formulas (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_fdt.c:145-174`; `kernel_mmu.c:149-197,360-399`; `kernel_startup.c:313-321,695-703`; `hidd/pcidt/pcidt_driverclass.c:137-145,459-470`). A reported RAM bank can cover virtual 128 GiB or above; the fixed device window also begins at 128 GiB and remapping overwrites its leaf PTEs. The allocator later publishes the reported RAM bank without excluding those device-overwritten pages (`kernel_startup.c:781-782,890-895,979-993`). No checked firmware layout combines that RAM capacity with a high GOP framebuffer or PCI BAR, so EK678 is conditional. EK677 is the separate case where the remap itself crosses Sv39's lower canonical boundary. Actual firmware extents, page-table overlap and runtime allocation remain open; no boot was run.

OpenSBI EFI framebuffer virtual-window boundary (EK677): traced GOP's 64-bit framebuffer base/size capture (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/efi_stub.c:719-723`) through `krnFBAddr`, the startup remap, boot-tag publication and the selected EFI framebuffer HIDD clear path (`kernel_startup.c:313-321,424-432,695-703`; `rom/bootloader/bootloader_init.c:174-190`; `rom/hidds/efifbgfx/efifbgfx_support.c:19-86,146-150`). Both the 256 GiB identity limit and 128 GiB remap base are page-aligned, so the selected differing-address mapper call preserves virtual/physical page offsets and is not the earlier suspected offset-mismatch bug. The alias window reaches Sv39's 256 GiB lower-canonical limit at physical 384 GiB; neither a start at/above that boundary nor a span extending beyond it is rejected before `KRN_FBAddr` reaches the display driver. Firmware GOP placement, span-end cases and real display behavior remain open; no high-address framebuffer was run.

OpenSBI framebuffer/RAM alias follow-up (EK678): rechecked the framebuffer virtual-base formula at spans crossing the 256 GiB identity limit. When the base is below the limit but the span ends above it, unsigned `base - limit` places the mapping below the fixed 128 GiB window; `krnMMUMapPages` can split and replace identity RAM leaves there. The later additional-bank MemHeaders do not exclude the framebuffer virtual span, so a mapped usable-RAM overlap is also published for allocation. Added a detailed conditional finding to `AROS-exec-kernel.md`; no checked-in firmware map establishes the overlap, and no framebuffer or allocation was exercised.

OpenSBI boot-mapping and unmap boundary follow-up: checked `krnInitMMU`, `krnMMUMapRegion` and `krnMMUSetPerms` (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_mmu.c:264-455`) against FDT memory-region admission, later initrd/DTB/framebuffer mapping, package placement and the public unmap wrapper (`kernel_fdt.c:145-175`; `kernel_startup.c:650-715,805-835`; `unmapglobal.c:17-27`). FDT memory tuples with zero size are skipped, and the startup calls for an initrd and firmware framebuffer require a positive span, so this selected path does not establish a zero-length `krnMMUMapRegion` request. The module permission update is applied to the loader's identity-addressed `lo..hi` range; this caller does not demonstrate `krnMMUSetPerms` destroying a nonidentity mapping. The page-table pool is also used during firmware-region and image setup before later global mappings, reinforcing EK676's shared capacity while leaving the exact remaining page count configuration-dependent. Other malformed firmware extents, region overlap and hardware cache effects remain open. No boot was run.

OpenSBI page-table allocation check (EK676; separate from EK201): reread the fixed 128-page pool, `krnPTAlloc`, both creation walkers and `krnMMUMapPages` (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_mmu.c:31-197`) with public `KrnMapGlobal` and PCIDT's individual 64-bit BAR mapper (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/mapglobal.c:19-55`; `arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/pcidt/pcidt_driverclass.c:406-470`). A valid series of sparse small mappings can require a fresh L0 table in each 2 MiB region; after the fixed pool fills, allocation halts in `wfi` rather than returning a mapping failure. PCIDT is a selected conditional caller, but no real BAR layout exhausting 128 table pages was established. EK201 remains the distinct absent-range unmap route. Page-table reuse, startup pool occupancy, hardware topology and runtime mapping remain open. No MMU call was run.

OpenSBI global mapping offset/caller check: reread `arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/{mapglobal.c,kernel_mmu.c:140-197}`, the public kernel signature, generic stub and the selected direct mapping callers. `krnMMUMapPages` rounds virtual and physical addresses down independently, adding the physical page offset to length; differing input page offsets would map the requested virtual byte to the wrong physical byte and can omit a tail page. The checked-in OpenSBI drivers normally pass identical addresses. PCIDT's nonidentity 64-bit PCI window uses `PCIDT_HIGH_WINDOW + (cpu - PCIDT_SV39_IDENTITY_LIMIT)`, and both constants are page-aligned, so its virtual and physical offsets also match for every mapped BAR (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/pcidt/pcidt_driverclass.c:55-86,137-145,459-470`; `pcidt.h:222-223`). No selected caller with differing offsets was established, and the generic public stub does not document whether that input is supported; no numbered kernel candidate is credited from this check. Direct third-party calls, unusual firmware window arithmetic and runtime mapping remain open. No pages were mapped.

Checksum producer/registration recheck (EK468): reread `rom/exec/sumlibrary.c:53-106` with `MakeLibrary`'s cleared negative-size allocation and base advance (`makelibrary.c:95-153`), `InitResident`'s `LIBF_SUMUSED` assignment and type dispatch (`initresident.c:103-153`), `AddLibrary`, `AddDevice`, `AddResource`, and `SetFunction`. The vector table occupies the positive `lib_NegSize` bytes before the base, yet `SumLibrary` starts at base plus that size and therefore reads zero vector words. Resident libraries and devices take the automatic AddLibrary/AddDevice checksum path; resources receive the flag but AddResource does not call SumLibrary, so they require a separate explicit call. `SetFunction` marks changed then invokes SumLibrary after writing a replacement vector, leaving the stored sum zero. The dynamically allocated printer per-unit base from `MakeLibrary` is not a demonstrated EK468 instance because that direct constructor does not enable `LIBF_SUMUSED` before AddDevice; the MinGW bsdsocket task-base constructor likewise explicitly sets only `LIBF_CHANGED` before its own `SumLibrary` call (`arch/all-mingw32/bsdsocket/bsdsocket_open.c:74-88`). No separate checksum candidate was found; selected resource callers, alternate architecture vector formats and runtime checksum alerts remain open. No vector was modified.

OpenSBI PLIC context/source-count follow-up (EK197): reread `arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_plic.c:40-255` with both producers (`kernel_fdt.c:73-225`; `kernel_acpi.c:330-399`), `platform_init.c:25-50` and boot-hart-only startup (`kernel_startup.c:770-774`). Both firmware parsers cap the stored supervisor-context list at `KRN_MAX_PLIC_CONTEXTS` (16), and `krnPLICInit` copies only that count; it supplies its named-context fallback when the list is empty, so this pass found no separate zero-length-list access in normal initialization. The FDT producer can name a boot context after its first 16 collected contexts while omitting that context from the stored list; `krnPLICInit` then enables and polls the retained contexts only. The earlier qualification that the target's 16-entry hart-ID array precludes a selected >16-hart configuration was too strong: `Platform_Init` allocates from the uncapped parsed `ncpus`, assigns fallback IDs beyond the stored array, and marks the parsed boot index online (`platform_init.c:23-47`). Thus firmware with more than 16 CPU/context entries and a boot hart beyond the first 16 is accepted by this path, while PLIC setup still ignores that boot context when its context list is nonempty. EK784 remains conditional on such firmware topology; no actual platform topology was established. EK197 now has a detailed entry: FDT `riscv,ndev` and ACPI `nsources` are copied without a bound and drive the initialization loop; the loop can exceed both the IRQ table limit and mapped register extent for inconsistent firmware. Real PLIC register extent, ACPI/FDT topology and future multi-hart delivery remain open. No controller or hart was run.

Dynamic printer-device publication caller check (EK9099; other-driver OD1889): reread generic `AddDevice`, `OpenDevice`, `RemDevice`, `MakeLibrary`, `PutMsg` and `AddTail` against selected `printer.device` per-unit construction and worker startup (`rom/exec/{adddevice,opendevice,remdevice,makelibrary,putmsg,addtail}.c`; `workbench/devs/printer/driver.c:95-187,408-413,538-549,764-850`). Exec publishes the supplied device node under its list lock, and a direct name lookup can reach its open vector as soon as `AddDevice` returns; it does not synchronize a driver's later private port setup. Printer publishes its zeroed per-unit object before `pd_Unit` is initialized by the worker, giving the direct per-unit-name caller route recorded as OD1889. The selected parent printer opener holds its own unit lock and waits for the worker handshake before calling the unit vector, so it is excluded. This is a printer caller lifecycle issue, not a second generic AddDevice defect; EK9099 remains the separate concurrent removal/expunge gap. Other dynamically constructed device bases, external openers and task timing remain open; no device was opened.

OpenSBI MSI mapping boundary recheck (EK17/EK488; other-driver OD1411): reread the full `KrnModifyIRQA` tag extraction, four-slot table and source unmask (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/modifyirq.c:17-129`) with the PLIC claim/fanout (`intr.c:41-129`), `krnRunIRQHandlers`' indexed handler list (`rom/kernel/addirqhandler.c:120-143`), the FDT-supplied PLIC source count (`kernel_fdt.c:191-200`; `kernel_plic.c:40-45,80-87`) and PCIDT's reservation/publication sequence (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/pcidt/pcidt_driverclass.c:724-769`). The only checked-in direct OpenSBI modifier call is PCIDT's: it supplies the positive base/count returned by `KrnAllocIRQ` after halving small failed requests. Thus it does not establish EK488's invalid-range direct-call trigger. The modifier itself still accepts a nonzero base/count with no handler-array range check, and dispatch can index that unvalidated base on a matching pending vector; EK488 remains a public-API robustness candidate. Exhausting the four controller slots returns FALSE, which PCIDT ignores (OD1411); this is a separate selected path that does not require an invalid base/count. The FDT `riscv,ndev` property supplies the PLIC source count, but a selected oversized firmware value was not established as an ordinary trigger for EK17. External callers, firmware topology, concurrent reconfiguration and interrupt delivery remain open; no IRQ was run.

OpenSBI MSI allocator/modifier contract recheck (2026-11-05; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): read the full `allocirq.c` and `freeirq.c` entry/helper bodies against the public `KrnAllocIRQ` and `KrnFreeIRQ` descriptions, all source callsites, and the selected PCIDT registration path. The oversized count wrap remains EK8894 (legacy EK17 label); selected PCIDT requests are bounded and halve on allocation failure. `KrnFreeIRQ` is documented for ranges previously returned by `KrnAllocIRQ`; the repository-wide search found no RISC-V caller beyond the generic example, so malformed free ranges are excluded as caller misuse. The firmware source 0 question in `KrnModifyIRQA` likewise has no selected trigger: PLIC source 0 is reserved, allocation begins above the reported source count, and PCIDT checks `b->msiIrq` before registration. No IRQ was allocated, freed or delivered; source-only.

OpenSBI virtual-IRQ release caller census correction (2026-10-17): the prior EK539 malformed-release example used `KrnFreeIRQ((ULONG)-1, 2)`, which violates the API's stated requirement that the range was taken with `KrnAllocIRQ`; there is no selected caller violating that contract. Withdraw EK539 as out-of-contract caller misuse. EK8894 (oversized allocation request arithmetic) and EK146 (overlapping valid allocations) remain distinct candidates. No allocation or release was run.

OpenSBI IRQ registration/disposal follow-up: compared generic `KrnAddIRQHandler`, `krnRunIRQHandlers` and `KrnRemIRQHandler` (`rom/kernel/addirqhandler.c:79-115,120-143`; `remirqhandler.c:49-76`) with the selected RISC-V PLIC unmask/claim/dispatch path (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/intr.c:41-52,59-129`; `kernel_plic.c:145-175,182-206,248-255`) and the DesignWare UART unit constructor/disposer (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/dwuart/SerialUnitClass.c:167-234,237-255`). The generic add vector allocates and links a handler before calling the platform unmask hook; on allocation failure it returns null without that hook. The UART enables its local interrupt bits before registration and still returns a unit after a null result, preserving other-driver OD1562. Its disposer tests the token before `KrnRemIRQHandler`, so this caller does not add an EK09 null-removal route. Generic add/rem and walk pair the interrupt spin lock on ExecSMP; the selected OpenSBI startup currently uses one online hart, while wider cross-hart controller claims and source-count contracts remain open. No interrupt was run.

EFI boot-tag and client-contract follow-up: compared `arch/all-native/efi/efi_init.c:62-110` and `findconfigtable.c:62-81` with both checked-in boot-tag producers (`arch/all-pc/bootstrap/multiboot2.c:183-211`; `arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_startup.c:412-422`), the `EFI_SystemTable` layout, and selected ACPI/SMBIOS callers (`arch/all-native/acpica/acpios_aros.c:166-182`; `arch/all-native/smbios/smbioslib.c:77-96`). The producers publish a nonzero firmware system-table pointer; the EFI resource checks the system-table signature but dereferences its RuntimeServices pointer without a local null guard. No checked-in producer manufactures a table with a null RuntimeServices field, and the ACPI/SMBIOS clients only ask for GUID configuration tables; this pass does not establish an ordinary selected null-runtime trigger or a new candidate. `EFI_FindConfigTable` guards a null ConfigTable before traversal, but firmware entry-count and table-storage validity remain external contracts. The resource target is named by the i386-PC, x86-64-PC and RISC-V OpenSBI boot manifests. No firmware configuration was run.

WaitForPort/timer cancellation cross-check (EK358): re-read the selected command cleanup (`workbench/c/WaitForPort.c:99-110,152-167`) against `timer.conf`, `TR_ADDREQUEST` list insertion and VBlank completion (`rom/timer/lowlevel.c:187-218,343-381`), `AbortIO` removal/reply (`rom/timer/abortio.c:55-93`), and the immediate request/port frees (`rom/exec/deleteiorequest.c:45-49`; `deletemsgport.c:43-58`). `timer.conf` has no timer-specific close hook. Ctrl-C/D can exit with the request still linked; CloseDevice does not cancel it, then cleanup frees both request and reply port. A later timer pass reads and completes the freed list node and can reply through the freed port. This is the detailed use-after-free/stale-reply-port finding EK358, with high source confidence and no runtime reproduction. AbortIO plus completion consumption is available but unused. Other timer backends and actual timing remain untested.

MinGW host timer/IRQ lifecycle recheck: reread selected `arch/all-mingw32/kernel/host_intr.c:135-211,230-423`, `host_debug.c:9-43`, the MinGW kernel startup call and direct host-IRQ clients in WingDI, Winsock and emulated filesystem startup. `core_init` creates two waitable timers and starts the switcher; `StartClock`'s zero/non-divisor period and the one-byte pending-bit loss are detailed in EK8846 (invalid/one-shot VBlank), EK674 (valid non-divisor VBlank drift), and EK672 (coalesced pending timer signals), while an overlarge `Ints_Num` or failed wait remains EK101. `KrnFreeSystemIRQ` marks slots reusable and intentionally retains their event handles; `KrnAllocSystemIRQ` clears the pending byte on reuse. Early `core_init` timer/thread/clock failures return zero before a successful boot, so this check did not establish persistent in-system handle loss from those exits. WingDI frees IRQs before joining its UI thread, already graphics GD164; no duplicate kernel finding is credited. Host-thread concurrency, failed host calls during a live boot, and runtime timer delivery remain open. No Windows-hosted process was run.

`NewCreateTaskA` output-port caller recheck (EK06): reread its port publication and failed-`NewAddTask` cleanup (`rom/exec/newcreatetaska.c:202-276`) against selected log-resource, serial logger, input.device, ATA controller/bus, SCSI bus, SD-card bus, console.device, screen-notify, menu-handler, narrator.device and speech.device startup. Log-resource and serial logger can report initialization success without testing the returned task, as EK790 records; console, input, narrator, speech, screen-notify and menu paths check the returned task and fail startup. ATA checks its result; on failure it retains the shared DetectionSem acquisition, already recorded as DISK-097. SCSI has the same acquisition-before-create pattern, but the reviewed disk audit found its current usable-device path unreachable because controller setup omits the required PIO interface; this conditional path does not add a separate active finding. SD-card decrements its pending-start counter when task creation returns null, but its bus remains registered; its normal I/O route requires a discovered unit, and this check did not establish one after a failed worker startup (`rom/devs/sdcard/sdcard_init.c:40-48,60-96`; `sdcard_device.c:142-155,649-669`). VMM page-handler, pre-pager and statistics launchers check their NewCreateTask result; the optional write-buffer resize worker ignores its result, but the reviewed path only skips asynchronous cache allocation, with no stronger consequence established (`workbench/system/VMM/VM_Manager.c:575-583`; `VM_Manager_Init.c:100-201`). No separate stale-port dereference is credited. Wider caller failure and teardown behavior remains pending. No task failure was run.

Reset-callback task-creation failure follow-up (EK675; promoted): reread `rom/exec/doresetcallbacks.c:119-183` against `rom/exec/newcreatetaska.c:190-276`, generic `ShutdownA`, and selected PC reset-performer registrations. `NewCreateTask` can return NULL and the dispatcher skips that callback; on a single-action PC cold/warm reboot the matching -110 performer is skipped and the later -128 power-off handler runs. The detailed finding is EK675. Wider platform and caller checks remain open. No shutdown was run.

Reset-callback caller group recheck: read the `CreatePCIUnit` registration and `DeletePCIUnit` cleanup branches in the six selected Prometheus network drivers (`workbench/devs/networks/{atheros5000,broadcom4400,etherlink3,nvidianet,prism2,rhine}/pci.c`). All six attempt `AddResetCallback` after `AddPCIIntServer` even if IRQ registration has already set `success = FALSE`; ordinary teardown removes the registered callback, but failed initialization calls `DeleteUnit` and `FreeCard` directly. On AROS, `AddResetCallback` always returns TRUE, so the IRQ-failure route leaves the reset node registered in freed unit storage. This is already recorded per driver in the other-drivers report (OD255, OD1772, OD736, OD785, OD566, and OD418 respectively); no duplicate Exec finding was added. These callers also demonstrate a registration/removal window relevant to EK59's unlocked reset-list traversal, but no concurrent shutdown was run. Other reset-callback producers and platform teardown paths remain pending.

WaitPort return-contract recheck (EK276): reread `rom/exec/waitport.c:45-98` and its adjacent GetMsg/PutMsg autodocs. WaitPort drops the SMP read lock before returning `lh_Head`; GetMsg removes under the write lock. The selected API text advises waiting before GetMsg but does not state exclusive-consumer ownership, so the report keeps EK276 conditional and medium API-use confidence. No checked-in competing consumer was established in the caller slices recorded below; the 204-match census is only a search inventory, not a completed caller audit. No message port was used.

Message-port and signal-pair recheck: reread `rom/exec/putmsg.c`, `getmsg.c`, `replymsg.c`, `waitport.c`, `remport.c`, `addport.c`, and `findport.c` together with `createmsgport.c`, `deletemsgport.c`, `allocsignal.c` (including `AllocTaskSignal`), `freesignal.c`, and `signal.c`. Publication and dequeue use the port spinlock; public-port insertion, lookup, and removal use the public-port list spinlock. Caller-specific public-port lifetime cases are documented in GD4019, GD4286 and OD806; a generic Exec lifetime finding remains open. The unlocked wait-head, reply publication and SMP signal-transition concerns remain EK276, EK8799, EK273 and EK274. `CreateMsgPort` releases its allocation when signal allocation fails, and `AllocTaskSignal` clears the newly allocated bit from pending, wait, and exception masks. This pass found no distinct additional defect in those paired bodies; cross-task deletion would require a caller-specific ownership check.

Generic IRQ registration caller check (EK815 scope): reread generic `KrnAddIRQHandler`, `krnRunIRQHandlers` and `KrnRemIRQHandler` (`rom/kernel/addirqhandler.c:73-143`; `remirqhandler.c:49-78`) against selected Raspberry Pi ARM and AArch64 timer initialization/expunge (`arch/arm-raspi/timer/timer_init.c:105-110,163-169`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/timer/timer_init.c:114-121,190-197`). Both timer variants reject a null add result and test their stored handle before removal, so neither reaches EK09's null dereference on that failure. The BCM2711 PCIe bridge still ignores a null registration token but never calls the generic remover for that token in its checked body; its unhandled MSI output is tracked as other-driver OD1778 (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2711/pcie/pcie_init.c:705-745`). This checked set does not close all kernel IRQ callers, including other SoCs and external drivers. No IRQ or timer was run.

Child-task API direct-caller census: searched all checked-in C and header files for `ChildStatus`, `ChildWait` and `ChildFree` calls. The production C submitters are POSIX `wait` and `waitpid` (`compiler/crt/posixc/wait.c:92-100`; `waitpid.c:113-149`) plus generated m68k ABI thunks for external clients (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:2342-2369`); the remaining direct matches are debug tests or DOS's separately named `internal_ChildWait`/`internal_ChildFree`. Rereading all three Exec bodies against the POSIX call sequence preserved EK811's SMP missed wakeup, EK812's unlocked live-child scan and EK476's no-child wait behavior. `waitpid`'s unlocked exited-list length scan has only child-exit append as an ordinary concurrent writer; `ChildFree` removal runs in the parent task after a completed wait, so this check did not establish a separate list-lifetime candidate. The three ledger rows now mark checked-in direct production C callers inspected; external binaries, generated dispatch and platform scheduling remain open. No child task was run.

Task-publication client recheck (EK315): reread `NewAddTask` and `TaskLaunch` (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:25-124,178-334`), task.resource's wrapper and prelaunch hook (`rom/task/task_execfuncs.c:20-91`), and the selected security.library notification (`rom/security/security_task.c:280-323`). The wrapper sends `TNA_ADDED` before calling Exec's original `NewAddTask`, and security's callback installs its task-owner node synchronously then; its ownership initialization is therefore outside EK315's later ready-before-prelaunch interval. Task.resource's own `TaskListEntry` remains delayed until Exec invokes `TaskRes_PreLaunch` after SMP ready publication, preserving EK315 for enumeration and task hooks. `InitETask` allocates an ETask before that path, and failure returns before launch (`rom/exec/exec_util.c:101-124`; `newaddtask.c:268-272`); the no-ETask affinity arm is not a selected successful launch. External notification clients and actual remote scheduling timing remain open; no task was launched.

Low-memory handler lifetime recheck (EK34): reread `AddMemHandler`, `RemMemHandler`, `AllocMem` and `checkMemHandlers` (`rom/exec/addmemhandler.c:46-59`; `remmemhandler.c:43-55`; `allocmem.c:105-116`; `memory.c:1313-1359`) against selected diskfont registration/expunge (`workbench/libs/diskfont/diskfont_init.c:33-79`). The list semaphore serializes removal with the handler walk but not with `AllocMem`'s earlier saved cursor. Diskfont's expunge-side `Forbid` does not protect a cursor saved by an allocator task that was descheduled before the failed allocation, so EK34's initial-snapshot route also applies on a single CPU. The retry route remains conditional: the selected loader daemon can request a retry, but no checked in-tree path removes its handler during that interval. Wider public callers and scheduling timing remain open; no allocation failure was run.

Interrupt-server caller cross-check: reread `AddIntServer`, `RemIntServer`, generic `IntServer`, generic `KrnAddIRQHandler`/`KrnRemIRQHandler` and the selected PC add/walk override, then searched direct C callers of the Exec pair across `rom`, `arch` and `workbench`. The legacy path's unlocked SMP walk and PC kernel override's unlocked SMP walk are already EK629 and EK31 respectively; the kernel-route null registration token and removal fault are already EK09. The older OHCI HIDD installs an IRQ but never removes it in its destructor, already other-driver OD206 (`workbench/devs/USB/drivers/OHCI/ohciclass.c:97-104,289-300`), whereas its UHCI sibling does call `RemIntServer` in disposal (`workbench/devs/USB/drivers/UHCI/uhciclass.c:428,534`). No duplicate Exec finding was added. The direct-caller search is an inventory, not a completed lifecycle audit of every caller; generated, indirect and architecture-specific dispatch contracts remain open.

Direct C-file inventory checkpoint: compared the ledger's exact-path rows with every `.c` file directly under `rom/exec`, `rom/kernel`, `rom/task`, `arch/all-pc/kernel`, `arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel`, `arch/arm-native/kernel`, `arch/aarch64-native/kernel`, `arch/all-unix/kernel`, `arch/all-android/kernel`, `arch/x86_64-pc/kernel`, `arch/i386-pc/kernel`, `arch/ppc-chrp/efika/kernel` and `arch/ppc-sam440/kernel`. All **479** existing direct C files across those 13 directories have a row. The local Exec, PC, OpenSBI and ARM manifests were reread alongside the inventory, and the earlier generic-kernel manifest reconciliation remains recorded below; their known absent ARM prerequisites remain EK8902. This is a file-row reconciliation only: nested directories, assembly, generated objects, per-target overrides and the outstanding body/caller/platform checks are not settled by it.

OpenSBI load-accounting follow-up (EK665–EK666): the selected Exec idle task (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/exec/exec_idle.c:18-59`) remains runnable while it waits in `wfi`; the kernel's only `__cpu_sleeptime` addition is in its no-task dispatcher fallback (`kernel/kernel_cpu.c:165-185`). The normal one-second timer sample therefore sees zero recorded sleep for both idle and busy windows. Its full-scale `2^32` quotient then narrows to zero in `uint32_t` (`kernel/kernel_timer.c:309-330`), so `KrnGetCPUAttr` and RISC-V processor.resource expose zero boot-hart load. EK665 covers the missing idle-task accounting. EK666 covers the independent full-scale wrap (still wrong for a genuinely busy window after accounting is fixed) and the additional `uint64_t` intermediate overflow in both per-CPU and per-task fixed-point scaling when a delayed sample's active-cycle numerator exceeds `UINT32_MAX` (`kernel_timer.c:63-80,309-319`). Neither finding claims `wfi` fails to halt; a timer-service delay long enough to trigger the extended-window case, failed idle-task startup, timer hardware and runtime load remain untested.

Reset-callback owner follow-up: checked the selected Linux-hosted framebuffer driver against Exec's `AddResetCallback`/`RemResetCallback` pair (`arch/all-linux/hidd/linuxfb/linuxfbgfx_hiddclass.c:127-159`; `rom/exec/addresetcallback.c:53-61`; `remresetcallback.c:45-50`). The driver registers its embedded node only after display construction succeeds and removes it before normal superclass disposal. The failed-display path returns null without registering a node and does not call the disposer; its leaked graphics object is already GD134, but it does not create an unlinked-node removal or dangling reset callback. Separate EK59 trigger confirmed: ordinary last-display removal reaches `HW_RemoveDriver`, whose disposer unlinks the embedded reset node and frees the graphics object; if this node is the saved successor while the non-supervisor shutdown walker waits for an earlier callback, it can leave the walker with a stale `tmp` pointer (`graphics_display.c:245-273`; `hwclass.c:287-295`; `linuxfbgfx_hiddclass.c:149-158`). GD135 is the independent tty restoration defect on ordinary teardown. No reset or display removal was run.

SMP self-removal handoff follow-up (EK807 (former EK659)): `RemTask(NULL)` posts its task to `ServicePort`, then stores `TS_INVALID` before its final `KrnDispatch` (`rom/exec/remtask.c:130-157`). The any-CPU housekeeper requeues a remotely observed `TS_TOMBSTONED` request but frees registered memory for `TS_INVALID` (`rom/exec/exec_init.c:308-331`; `rom/exec/service.c:51-92`). Each selected PC, ARM32 and AArch64 dispatch path retains `GET_THIS_TASK` and dereferences its `tc_State` when no affinity-eligible ready task exists (`arch/all-pc/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:294-325`; `arch/arm-native/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:242-307`; `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:221-278`). A CPU-local idle task normally supplies that fallback, so EK807 (former EK659) depends on its creation having failed while startup continued and on no other task being eligible. This supports a conditional stale-TCB read on all three selected SMP targets. The earlier broader claim that the task stack is necessarily used during final dispatch remains removed; architecture exception entry and active stack use are not needed for the TCB consequence. No SMP schedule was run.

OpenSBI CPU-index consistency follow-up (EK657): the selected `arch/riscv64-all/kernel/getcpunumber.c` forwards to `GetCPUNumber`, which returns raw `__boot_hartid` in `arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_intern.h:230-238`. The FDT parser counts `/cpus/cpu@*` nodes and records the boot hart's position separately from its `reg` ID (`kernel_fdt.c:115-122,176-188`); `platform_init.c:29-50`, `getcpucount.c:14-24` and `getcpuattr.c:13-46` use the position/count as the CPU index, matching `KrnGetCPUAttr`'s documented `0 .. KrnGetCPUCount()-1` input (`rom/kernel/getcpuattr.c:30-44`). A valid one-node tree with physical boot hart ID 4 therefore yields `KrnGetCPUNumber()==4`, count 1, and a failed attribute lookup for CPU 4. A full direct C callsite search found common Exec affinity uses under `__AROSEXEC_SMP__`, the guarded RISC-V SMP-init path, debug-only uses, and no selected OpenSBI caller combining the public number with the attribute accessor. The `configure` OpenSBI branch sets `__AROSPLATFORM_SMP__` but not `__AROSEXEC_SMP__` (`configure:11362-11390`); startup also explicitly leaves secondary harts parked until HSM bring-up (`kernel_startup.c:41-42,770-774`). This limits EK657 to a public API contract mismatch on the current target, not an established in-tree affinity overrun or boot failure. Native RISC-V reads `mhartid` through a different helper and still needs separate logical-index validation. Firmware topology, actual boot and external clients remain open.

AHIRecord BUFFERS input follow-up (EK462): `AsyncBuffers` is a 32-bit `ULONG`, and the `BUFFERS` string is assigned through `atol` without a range check (`workbench/tools/AHIRecord/AHIRecord.c:15,484,1575-1576`; `compiler/include/exec/types.h:35-43`). Explicit `BUFFERS=0` directly supplies a zero size to the selected AIFF/WAVE `OpenAsync` calls; positive `BUFFERS=32768` also wraps `4 * BIGBUFFERSIZE * AsyncBuffers` from 2^32 to zero (`AHIRecord.c:2930,2938`). `AS_OpenAsyncFH` retains zero after block-size rounding and splits it into zero-capacity halves (`workbench/libs/asyncio/src/OpenAsyncFH.c:59-74,120-124`); the immediate nonempty header writes follow EK462's zero-capacity nonprogress loop. These are concrete command-line inputs for the existing finding, not separate findings. Other extreme values, UI argument paths and filesystem reply behavior remain open; no recording was run.

Generic kernel memory-helper reachability: reread `rom/kernel/kernel_mm.c`'s page-allocator selector, free walk and `mm_AllocExecHeader` against `KrnAllocPages`, `KrnInitMemory` and the selected hosted Unix overrides (`rom/kernel/allocpages.c:63-83`; `initmemory.c:42-54`; `arch/all-unix/kernel/allocpages.c:53-148`; `freepages.c:11-27`). A checked-in C-call search found no client of `mm_AllocExecHeader`; no small-size input is established for its `maxsize - MEMHEADER_TOTAL` computation. Bare-metal generic allocation remains gated by zero `kb_PageSize` on the checked startup paths (EK639), while hosted Unix supplies its own mmap-based page entry points. Existing absolute-address findings EK14/EK25 remain conditional on direct explicit-address clients, since located production callers pass null. The exhaustive checked-in identifier search found no page-size injection; generated callers, out-of-tree initialization and runtime memory maps remain open.

Generic kernel source-list reconciliation: parsed `rom/kernel/mmakefile.src`'s continued `FUNCS` and `FILES` assignments and the conditional `MMU_FILES`/`ALLOCATOR` assignments (`:44-81`). They name 63 function C inputs, 12 base C inputs and two more when `USE_MMU=1`. All 77 named local `.c` paths exist and each has a row in this ledger; the same 77 are the complete direct `.c` file set under `rom/kernel` at this snapshot. This confirms the local generic-kernel file inventory, not architecture override selection, body/caller completeness, generated code, or the absent architecture sources recorded by EK8902. No kernel target was built.

AArch64 global map/unmap failure reconciliation (EK8823): the selected `KrnMapGlobal` and `KrnUnmapGlobal` wrappers and both range walkers are now detailed in one finding. A later page-table allocation can fail after earlier descriptors were edited, causing a zero return before the global TLB commit. Direct C caller search found no `KrnUnmapGlobal` callers; RP1 frees DMA backing storage when mapping reports failure, but selected xHCI request sizes do not establish the multi-region allocation-failure trigger. No low-memory map/unmap sequence was run.

Reset-callback owner cross-check: reread generic `AddResetCallback`, `RemResetCallback`, `ColdReboot`, `ShutdownA` and the callback walker against four selected or explicit driver owners (`rom/exec/{addresetcallback,remresetcallback,coldreboot,shutdowna,doresetcallbacks}.c`). VMwareSVGA embeds its reset node in the gfx object, registers before display construction, and disposes that object without unlinking on display failure; this is already GD588 (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/vmwaresvga_hiddclass.c:265-311`). SM502 follows the same registration order but its disposer removes the node before superclass disposal (`workbench/hidds/sm502gfx/sm502gfx_hiddclass.c:132-162`), so that failure does not add a stale callback. Nouveau stores its callback in a static interrupt node and guards repeated registration with `is_Code`; its shutdown data points to class-owned card data, so ordinary object-free reuse is not established by this local path (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/nouveau_hiddclass.c:343-383,413-425`). Broadcom 4400 removes its per-unit node in normal deletion but skips removal on failed PCI interrupt registration before freeing the unit, already OD1772 (`workbench/devs/networks/broadcom4400/pci.c:248-271,301-320`). The list mutation/walker race remains EK59. These checked owner paths are not a complete audit of all reset callback producers; hardware shutdown and cross-CPU timing were not run.

Exec signal API platform recheck: reread the selected `AllocSignal`, `FreeSignal`, `Signal` and `Wait` bodies alongside m68k `wait.S` and `signal_fast.S`, `NewAddTask`'s signal-field initialization and the default `TaskSigAlloc=0xFFFF` mask (`rom/exec/{allocsignal,freesignal,signal,wait,newaddtask,prepareexecbase}.c`; `arch/m68k-all/exec/{wait,signal_fast}.S`). The m68k wait path keeps the requested mask in D2, rechecks received bits after its voluntary switch and clears only those bits before returning them. Its fast signal path validates received bits and `TS_WAIT` again under masked interrupts before editing the wait/ready lists; exception-bearing or changed-state cases go to the C slow path. This does not add a lost-bit candidate to EK8800's valid bit-31 shift or to the recorded SMP task-lifetime cases EK273–EK274. Hardware interrupt nesting, scheduler assembly and wider public API callers remain open; no signal sequence was run.

ARM affinity caller and bootstrap boundary (EK634): selected `Exec_ARMCPUInit` creates idle tasks with heap-allocated affinity masks (`arch/arm-native/exec/platform_init.c:53-85`) after `Exec_ARMCPUSMPInit` enables Exec affinity at lower init priority (`:248-258,288-291`), so these successful tasks also exercise the inherited-mask overwrite in ARM `PrepareContext`. ARM `cpu_InitBootStrap` directly overwrites an ETask affinity pointer (`arch/arm-native/kernel/kernel_execsmp.c:99-123`), but this earlier secondary path also hits the already recorded uninitialized task-list insertion (EK153) before ETask initialization; it is not counted as an additional ordinary startup leak. USB2OTG passes an embedded unit field as a task-affinity pointer (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/usb/usb2otg/usb2otg_device.c:278-293`), while ETask cleanup assumes an allocated mask; its worker loops forever and no selected normal task-removal path was found, so an invalid-free outcome there is conditional and remains outside EK634's normal trigger. Failure exits and external affinity-tag callers remain pending. No SMP task or device was run.

ARM32 affinity-mask ownership follow-up (EK634): traced selected ARM processor probe creation with `TASKTAG_AFFINITY` through `NewAddTask`'s `InitETask` then ARM `PrepareContext` (`arch/arm-native/processor/processor_init.c:53-73`; `rom/exec/newaddtask.c:268-308`; `rom/exec/exec_util.c:124-163`; `arch/arm-all/exec/preparecontext.c:35-46`). The context tag assignment replaces the first allocated mask without freeing it; eventual ETask cleanup sees only the replacement. ARM native SMP enables the affinity flag before normal probe resource startup, and the Raspberry Pi boot manifest selects the processor resource. x86-64 and AArch64 context preparers explicitly release the old mask, so this finding is kept to the selected ARM32 route; armeb and RISC-V analogous assignments need their own selected SMP reachability checks. No SMP task was created.

OpenSBI optional boot self-tests (EK633, EK8775): `krnSchedTest` and `krnFpuTest` each allocate a boot-task signal but return without freeing it if `NewCreateTaskA` fails (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_startup.c:138-151,189-210`), and all three signal-allocation sites shift the unchecked `-1` result on signal-pool exhaustion (`:104-108,141-143,202-203`). EK633 details the conditional leaked bit and invalid mask behavior. The bootarg dispatcher matches `testsched`/`testfpu` as substrings rather than whole words, unlike the local `krnArgMatch` helper (`:219-241,1093-1111`); EK8775 details unintended test execution and the extra sleeping task. Both tests are opt-in; no task or signal failure was run. Other OpenSBI boot tests and task-startup contracts remain pending.

RemTail partition/filesystem caller follow-up: inspected direct RDB, MBR, EBR, SFS cache and ISA PnP call sites (`rom/partition/partition{rdb,mbr,ebr}.c`; `rom/filesys/SFS/FS/cachebuffers.c:770-823`; `rom/isapnp/pnp.c:844-861`) against the complete `RemTail`/`Remove` bodies. MBR/EBR and PnP drain until null; RDB likewise drains its child, bad-block and filesystem lists. RDB's child free helper calls `Remove` again after `RemTail`, but `RemTail` leaves the detached node's old predecessor/successor links intact, and with no intervening mutation this second pointer splice repeats the already-established neighbor link; no ordinary single-owner corruption finding is credited. SFS uses its separate buffer count to bound removals, so count/list divergence and concurrent partition-table mutation still need caller-state review. No filesystem or partition teardown was run.

Task.resource manifest reconciliation: read `rom/task/mmakefile.src` in full and compared its 20 named C translation units with the file rows already in this ledger. All 20 were present; the manifest itself was missing and is now inventoried below. The manifest builds `kernel-task` as a resource, selects architecture Exec/kernel include paths, and leaves the optional `-DDEBUG=1` line commented (`:5-70`), preserving the debug-build qualifier on EK405. Architecture make-option includes can still affect target flags; generated build and image selection remain pending. No task.resource build was run.

Reset-callback launcher scheduling follow-up: reread `Exec_DoResetCallbacks`' launcher priority 120, handler priority 119, timer port/request setup, and wait branches against `SetTaskPri` and `Wait` (`rom/exec/doresetcallbacks.c:18-24,70-112,115-190`; `rom/exec/settaskpri.c:85-155`; `rom/exec/wait.c:70-115`). The launcher enters `Wait` after starting a handler; that call moves it to the wait list and schedules another task, so its one-step-higher priority does not itself prevent a handler from running on one CPU. No new priority-starvation candidate was credited. The shared late-completion signal remains EK873 and missing-timer fallback is EK8992; support-task scheduling on platform-specific kernels and shutdown-time timer availability remain open. No shutdown sequence was run.

Task-storage snapshot caller recheck: reread complete `SaveTaskStorage` and `RestoreTaskStorage` bodies (`rom/task/SaveTaskStorage.c:46-77`; `RestoreTaskStorage.c:45-74`) against their only direct in-tree C caller, task.resource's `NewStackSwap` wrapper (`rom/task/task_execfuncs.c:196-229`). The resource initializer keeps that wrapper's Exec vector installation under `#if (0)` (`rom/task/task_init.c:79-81`), so snapshot allocation failure and restore-with-null do not establish a selected in-tree stack-swap failure. Public direct callers and cross-task misuse remain open; EK405 remains a conditional debug-build compile finding. No snapshot or stack swap was run.

Parent task-storage lifetime follow-up (EK632; detailed in AROS-exec-kernel.md): confirmed the generated per-task-base OpenLib caller invokes the borrowed-parent getter without protecting the returned value through its subsequent duplicate-base dereferences. Parent cleanup detaches/reparents children and frees the ETask. Exec OpenLibrary holds Forbid around the generated Open vector, so no same-CPU task-switch trigger is claimed; on Exec SMP, the getter only uses local Forbid, which does not synchronize a parent running on another CPU. This is distinct from EK124's live-parent slot-array replacement. Selected posixc and usergroup configs enable `pertaskbase`; no concurrent parent exit/open was run. Parent notification/child-list races and external callers remain pending.

Task-storage slot lifecycle crosscheck (EK631): reread the complete allocation, free, get, parent-get and set bodies alongside the resource initializer and selected generated/posixc callers (`rom/task/{AllocTaskStorageSlot,FreeTaskStorageSlot,GetTaskStorageSlot,GetParentTaskStorageSlot,SetTaskStorageSlot,task_init}.c`; `tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1135-1151,1577-1583`; `compiler/crt/posixc/__threadhook.c:135-175`). The initializer installs a free-list sentinel starting at slot 1, allocation advances that sentinel when no returned node exists, and free drops the ID on node-allocation failure. Both selected expunge paths then erase their saved positive IDs, so their next initialization cannot recover the dropped ID. This supports EK631's low-impact growth consequence without assuming an invalid public slot argument. Setter allocation failure, stale duplicate-base publication, and the SMP free-list race remain separate EK307/EK308/EK9125 findings. No allocation failure or lifecycle was run.

Task-storage API boundary follow-up: reread `AllocTaskStorageSlot`, `FreeTaskStorageSlot`, `SetTaskStorageSlot`, and `TaskGetStorageSlot` together (`rom/task/{AllocTaskStorageSlot,FreeTaskStorageSlot,SetTaskStorageSlot,GetTaskStorageSlot}.c`). Positive IDs returned by the allocator are the documented input to Set/Get; Set rejects IDs below 1, and its 16-slot rounding/copy indices preserve valid IDs at ordinary chunk boundaries. Get does not validate a negative ID before indexing, but that call violates its documented returned-ID input contract and no selected caller supplies one, so it is not counted as a separate finding. Extremely large IDs can overflow the signed allocation arithmetic, but no selected producer can establish such an ID without first exhausting the global LONG slot space; no practical selected trigger was established. EK9125 remains the selected SMP defect; EK631 remains the allocation-failure lifecycle issue.  Checked the complete direct-call search: `developer/debug/test/taskres/taskstorage.c`, `compiler/startup/relbases.c`, `compiler/crt/posixc/__threadhook.c`, and generated clients emitted from `tools/genmodule/writestart.c` cover the in-tree APIs. The test frees and reallocates a slot ID but does not query it afterward; the per-task array is not cleared by `FreeTaskStorageSlot`, so a reused ID can still expose its former value. The API does not promise clearing values on free, and generated PERTASKBASE opens validate a cached duplicate against its task/library identity (`writestart.c:1320-1340`); the established stale-duplicate lifetime paths remain EK306/EK307, so no broader reuse finding is promoted. The direct in-tree callers guard allocation failure or are already tracked under EK307/EK406/EK407. No runtime slot-reuse sequence or allocation failure was run.


Task-storage getter correction (EK122 withdrawn): reread `TaskGetStorageSlot`'s count comparison against the declared integer types (`rom/task/GetTaskStorageSlot.c:58-77`; `compiler/include/exec/types.h:82-91`). The stored count is an unsigned `IPTR`, so any negative `LONG slotid` converts to a large unsigned value for `tsstorage[0] <= slotid` and returns null before indexing. The earlier paragraph incorrectly credited a direct negative-ID out-of-bounds read. Successful in-tree allocator clients also use positive IDs (`rom/task/AllocTaskStorageSlot.c:47-86`; `tools/genmodule/writestart.c:307-322,1135-1151`). Failure and rollback of generated slot registration remain EK307/EK308; parent-reader concurrency and lifetime remain EK124/EK632. Other direct clients and task lifetime remain pending; no storage API call was run.
AllocSignal Exec/kernel caller pass (EK8800 and EK633 rechecked, 2026-10-16; no new finding): exact-symbol search of Exec, Task and kernel sources found only `CreateMsgPort`, `Exec_DoResetCallbacks`, and the optional RISC-V OpenSBI scheduler/FPU self-tests beyond the public vector itself. `CreateMsgPort` frees its struct and returns NULL when `AllocSignal` fails (`rom/exec/createmsgport.c:51-75`); reset callbacks use an unsigned mask for the allocated bit and retain the explicit SIGF_SINGLE fallback, while the OpenSBI test helpers' unchecked allocation/child-failure paths are already EK633. The bit-31 signed-shift API condition remains EK8800; no distinct Exec-core caller defect was established. Wider public callers and reset-signal interaction remain open; no task or shutdown was run.

Managed MemHeader teardown follow-up: traced `FreeMemHeader`'s saved `mh_Upper - addr` size and destructor call through `DeletePool` and the selected TLSF callback (`rom/exec/memory.c:982-998`; `deletepool.c:60-111`; `rom/kernel/tlsf.c:1285-1316,1465-1475`). The only direct callback assignment found in this checkout is TLSF's `destroy_Pool`; its `tlsf_destroy` frees a separately allocated control block when marked `TLSFF_AUTODESTROY` and releases autogrown areas, while `FreeMemHeader` subsequently frees the original header block. This selected successful-teardown route does not establish a double free or wrong free size. EK871 still covers initialization failure before a valid managed pool exists; external managed allocator callbacks and concurrent pool users remain open. No pool teardown was run.

Internal MemHeader size-boundary follow-up: `AllocMemHeader` is implemented inside `rom/exec/memory.c:898-979`, with one direct in-tree caller in the managed `CreatePool` branch (`rom/exec/createpool.c:92-107,131-146`). For a nonoverflowing request, `CreatePool` adds header/context/alignment overhead and rounds its puddle to at least a page before passing it, so `AllocMemHeader`'s plain-header `size -= MEMHEADER_TOTAL` branch is not reached with a too-small size by this selected caller. The unchecked public `puddleSize` arithmetic was rechecked, but no smaller allocation or other memory-safety consequence was established; ignored managed `mhe_InitPool` failure remains EK871. External/internal caller additions and allocator-backend contracts remain open. No allocation failure was run.

PC scheduling-IPI mask follow-up: reread selected `KrnScheduleCPU` against `core_DoIPI` and the post-lock calls from `SetTaskPri`, `Signal`, `NewAddTask` and `SetTaskAffinity` (`arch/all-pc/kernel/schedulecpu.c:46-59`; `kernel_ipi.c:25-81`; `rom/exec/settaskpri.c:135-148`; `signal.c:316-338,350-377,427-440`; `newaddtask.c:89-103`; `rom/task/SetTaskAffinity.c:111-142`). For a non-sentinel mask, `core_DoIPI` iterates APIC CPU slots and reads each bit through `KrnCPUInMask`; this is the existing EK273 post-unlock lifetime consequence when another task frees the mask. `KrnScheduleCPU` itself does not store the pointer for a later asynchronous read or add a second allocation/ownership step, so no separate helper candidate is credited. The generic single-CPU implementation instead issues `SC_SCHEDULE` and ignores the mask (`rom/kernel/schedulecpu.c:51-61`), narrowing this borrowed-mask read to the selected SMP overrides. APIC startup order and other architecture dispatch remain pending; no concurrent task exit was run.

Interrupt-vector producer follow-up: enumerated the direct in-tree C `SetIntVector` callers and reread the generic and PPC CHRP bootstrap loops plus the m68k disk/audio and AmigaVideo registrations (`rom/exec/setintvector.c:38-68`; `rom/exec/exec_init.c:216-261`; `arch/ppc-chrp/exec/exec_init.c:249-298`; `arch/m68k-amiga/disk/disk_intern_init.c:145-165`; `arch/m68k-amiga/devs/audio/audio_hardware.c:210-220`; `arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_chipset.c:1924-1931`). Their passed IDs are loop-bounded or named legacy constants, so none supplies EK542's out-of-range trigger. PPC CHRP's interrupt-record allocations only log failure and then dereference the null result while initializing or publishing it; this is covered by EK8842, not a SetIntVector-specific finding. External/public vector callers and hardware ownership remain pending. No boot or interrupt was run.

EK8799 task-context caller exclusion: traced the selected CON: handler's `SendIO` read and close-time `AbortIO`/`WaitIO` against `console.device`'s worker reply and abort method (`rom/filesys/console_handler/con_handler.c:646-659,1238-1256`; `rom/devs/console/consoletask.c:457-492,573-587`; `rom/devs/console/console.c:432-460`). The worker holds `consoleTaskLock` through `ReplyMsg`; `AbortIO` must acquire the same lock before CON: can reach `WaitIO`. Preemption after the worker sets `NT_REPLYMSG` but before it links the reply cannot let that close path pass `AbortIO` on one CPU. This caller does not establish EK8799's previously unproven single-CPU task-context overlap; the selected timer-interrupt SMP routes remain. No concurrent run was performed.

EK8762 correction: `log.resource` creates a fresh broadcaster task with one message-port signal; the default 16 reserved bits still leave 15 free signals for its two retry allocations (`rom/log/log.c:189-209,304-312`; `rom/exec/newcreatetaska.c:205-232`; `rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:319`). The proposed exhaustion trigger was withdrawn. EK351/EK8768 readiness recheck: `logInitialise` can return NULL before the broadcaster sets `lrb_Task`, and the selected serial logger stores that result. `logAddEntry` rejects the null handle safely, while `logFinalise(NULL)` would dereference it on logger-task exit; however, a complete in-tree signal/teardown search found no selected path that exits this permanent resource task. The only established startup effect is loss of its own initial diagnostic. Withdraw the crash candidate pending external task-removal reachability; no runtime test was run.

Signal API follow-up: reread complete `AllocSignal`, `AllocTaskSignal`, `FreeSignal`, `SetSignal` and `Wait` bodies against `NewCreateTaskA`, `NewAddTask` and the log broadcaster startup (`rom/exec/allocsignal.c:57-143`; `freesignal.c:48-56`; `setsignal.c:55-79`; `wait.c:62-153`; `newcreatetaska.c:205-232`; `newaddtask.c:239-251`; `rom/log/log.c:189-209`). `AllocTaskSignal` returns -1 on a full mask; the new-task message-port allocation checks that result before publication. It clears the chosen bit from the task's received, wait and exception masks, and `NewAddTask` leaves a nonzero allocation mask in place. No separate signal-API defect follows from this selected startup trace. Wider public callers and cross-CPU allocation timing remain pending; no signal workload was run.

Signal-bit 31 caller boundary recheck (EK8800): repository-wide literal search found no direct in-tree `AllocSignal(31)` call. The API still accepts explicit bit 31, and automatic allocation can return it when lower allocatable bits are occupied; the report therefore keeps this as a conditional public-API finding rather than attributing it to a selected production caller. No bit-exhaustion path was exercised.

x86-64 global-map failure-path follow-up (EK322): traced `alloc_page_table` through both missing-parent branches of `map_global_2m` (`arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/mapglobal.c:20-29,109-140`). A PML4 child can be published before allocation of its PDP child fails, leaving an empty table after `KrnMapGlobal` returns failure; the helper retains only the aligned pointer, not the `AllocMem` address, and performs no rollback. The previously ledgered EK322 partial-map/table-ownership candidate is now restored as detailed finding EK8888 after a full source recheck. The selected PC PCI caller handles a nonzero result as failure but has no page-table cleanup path. Other caller/configuration and runtime behavior remain open; no allocation failure was run.

Global mapping API target/caller sweep: read generic `rom/kernel/{mapglobal,unmapglobal}.c` and the available ARM32, AArch64, x86-64 PC, m68k and OpenSBI RISC-V overrides for those vectors, checking their manifests. The x86-64 map wrapper returns zero on success and its selected PCIPC BAR caller tests `!= 0` for failure (`arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/mapglobal.c:143-171`; `arch/all-pc/hidds/pcipc/pcipc_driverclass.c:232-253`); OpenSBI returns one on success and its selected DWI2C and PCIDT callers test `!KrnMapGlobal` (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_mmu.c:144-197`; `hidd/dwi2c/dwi2c_init.c:176-184`; `hidd/pcidt/pcidt_driverclass.c:60-80`). The apparent cross-target return-value disagreement is therefore not a new bug in these checked caller paths. ARM32's selected mapglobal body is a zero-return no-op, but no selected ARM32 in-tree caller was established: the BCM2711/2712 PCI modules are selected by the AArch64 Raspberry Pi manifest, and the V3D target edge is disabled for ARM32. Treat this as an external-client/API-contract gap, not a retained numbered finding; OpenSBI's allocating unmap walk remains EK201. Other target selection, generated calls, physical-page alignment contracts and external clients remain open. No mapping was run.

Shared-semaphore grant-order follow-up (EK875): reread `ReleaseSemaphore`'s last-holder grant loop and both immediate-acquire branches against shared/exclusive DOS `LockDosList` dispatch and selected Wanderer writer/DiskInfo reader calls. The implementation admits readers past queued writers; because public docs do not promise writer fairness and no sustained in-tree reader stream was established, EK875 remains a medium-confidence candidate rather than a confirmed fairness-contract violation. No semaphore workload was run.

EK8819 input-device caller correction: reread the key-repeat timer port's allocation, request copy, abort-time `WaitIO`, periodic `GetMsg` and resubmission (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:37-52,159-181,459-478`). The private port carries one timer request, which is consumed before reuse. Its timer completion cannot supply the *different* simultaneous list mutation required for EK8819's `WaitIO`/`InternalPutMsg` race. The report now treats the selected input caller as evidence of `WaitIO` use only; a selected shared-port overlapping writer remains open. The code-level SMP lock mismatch remains; no interleaving was run.

Reset-callback network-caller reconciliation (EK59, driver findings): checked the selected `AddResetCallback`/`RemResetCallback` pair (`rom/exec/addresetcallback.c:53-61`; `remresetcallback.c:45-50`) against six PCI SANA-II unit constructors and destructors: Atheros5000, Broadcom4400, EtherLink3, Nvidianet, Prism2 and Rhine (`workbench/devs/networks/{atheros5000,broadcom4400,etherlink3,nvidianet,prism2,rhine}/pci.c`). Each normal destructor uses its `UNITF_RESETADDED` flag to remove the callback; each constructor's failed IRQ-registration branch can register the callback and then bypass that destructor while freeing its unit. Those caller defects already have driver owners OD255, OD1772, OD736, OD785, OD566 and OD418, respectively. The common Exec API always returns TRUE and does not establish a distinct failure mode for these callers. EMU10kx's apparent reset registration is under `__AMIGAOS4__` and is not an AROS caller (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/EMU10kx/emu10kx-misc.c:382-404`). Other reset-callback users and shutdown concurrency remain open; no reset or IRQ failure was run.

EK8799 selected-caller configuration recheck: reread `ReplyMsg`, `InternalPutMsg`, `CheckIO`, `WaitIO`, and the lan78xx and PoPo timer polling/resubmission loops (`rom/exec/replymsg.c:50-64`; `putmsg.c:71-105`; `checkio.c:45-59`; `waitio.c:57-76`; `rom/usb/classes/lan78xx/lan78xx.class.c:626-639`; `rom/usb/poseidon/popo.gui.c:277-291`; `rom/timer/lowlevel.c:252-258,321-327`). The completion type is still stored before queue insertion, but an interrupt-context timer reply can overlap these ordinary polling tasks only on another CPU; the report now states this selected-route condition. A task-context preemption route remains possible but lacks a selected producer/client pair. No concurrent I/O was run.

POSIXC CRT hook registry correction (EK624 withdrawn): reread the two `__get_threadhooks` lookups and insertion (`compiler/crt/posixc/__threadhook.c:100-154`) against LDDemon's per-name open semaphore (`rom/lddemon/lddemon.c:369-391,471-494,500-531`) and the generated per-task-base OpenLib hook dispatch (`tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1277-1405`). Ordinary selected POSIXC opens serialize their init hook through the same name's loader semaphore, so the proposed concurrent duplicate-registry trigger is not established. A direct initializer outside that path would need separate evidence. EK576's failed registry allocation remains active; no process or worker was run.

Named-semaphore namespace and caller recheck (EK876, EK607): reread complete generic `AddSemaphore`, `FindSemaphore` and `RemSemaphore` list operations (`rom/exec/addsemaphore.c:52-81`; `findsemaphore.c:53-78`; `remsemaphore.c:47-70`) against the selected pthread named-semaphore implementation (`compiler/pthread/semaphore.c:43-152`). Pthread `sem_open`/`sem_unlink` use their own static list under `sema_sem`; they do not call Exec `FindSemaphore` or register entries on `SysBase->SemaphoreList`, so they are not an EK876 caller. Their open-handle lifetime remains EK607: `sem_close` tracks nothing and unlink destroys/frees the same object returned by open. The selected Editor preferences `FindPort`/`PutMsg`/interruptible reply wait was rechecked (`workbench/prefs/Editor/PrefsPort.c:27-109`); its former GD1793 reference has no matching current detailed body, so sender ownership remains open rather than counted as covered. External named-semaphore users, public Exec semaphore callers and runtime timing remain pending; no IPC or semaphore operation was run.

Exception registration/removal caller recheck (EK11; EK275 later withdrawn): reread complete generic `KrnAddExceptionHandler`, `krnRunExceptionHandlers`, and `KrnRemExceptionHandler` bodies (`rom/kernel/addexceptionhandler.c:26-198`; `remexceptionhandler.c:25-79`) and searched direct selected PC and optional VMM callers. Add enforces only `EXCEPTIONS_COUNT`, while SMP dispatch snapshots eight callbacks. All checked-in C callers were censused: selected PC/APIC registrations use distinct IDs; optional trap-debug adds one per CPU vector, Hyper-V adds a second at 2, and VMM a second at 14. No checked-in combination reaches nine on one vector, so EK11 remains external/future integration only. Remove unlinks under the same lock but does not drain callbacks copied by another CPU; VMM cleanup removes its fault callback before dismantling page tables (`workbench/system/VMM/x86/traphandler_x86.c:98-115`; `pagehandler.c:181-205`), which initially appeared to support an optional dynamic-removal route; EK275 is withdrawn below after the VMM AROS startup check. The APIC reset replacement uses resident callback code and data, so that selected removal alone is insufficient for EK275's freed-lifetime consequence. Other external module registrations, cross-CPU dispatch timing and VMM shutdown order remain pending; no exception was run.

PC i8042 IRQ-lifetime correction (EK31): reread the complete selected mouse constructor/disposer with its setup task, generic `KrnRemIRQHandler`, PC `KrnAddIRQHandler`/walker and mouse proxy removal (`arch/all-pc/hidds/i8042/i8042_mouseclass.c:45-99`; `i8042_mouseps2.c:186-235`; `rom/kernel/remirqhandler.c:50-78`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/addirqhandler.c:70-137`; `rom/hidds/mouse/subsystem.c:123-170`). EK31's unsynchronized PC IRQ add/walk and remove/walk remains, but its prior assertion that public `HW_RemoveDriver` reaches i8042 mouse disposal was inconsistent with OD1773: the mouse adapter fails to match the returned proxy handle. EK31 now treats that mouse destructor as conditional and does not claim a selected successful hot-removal caller. Timer and other handler registration paths remain in the finding; target runtime interleavings and broader callers pending. No IRQ or removal was run.

Abort/wait request follow-up (EK8819, EK8800, EK8799): the complete Exec `AbortIO` dispatch wrapper and `WaitIO` wait/remove body were reread against `GetMsg`, `InternalPutMsg`, `DeleteIORequest` and selected USB mass-storage timer cleanup. `AbortIO` forwards a device result and leaves completion ownership to `WaitIO`; the storage worker uses `CheckIO`, optional `AbortIO`, then `WaitIO` before reusing or deleting its timer request (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/MassStorage/storage_task.c:211-220,316-351`). That selected sequence does not establish a missing-wait bug. `WaitIO` still removes a replied node without the SMP port lock (EK8819; the `Disable()` contract explicitly says it is CPU-local on EXECSMP and shared data also needs a spinlock, `rom/exec/disable.c:58-61`), can observe `NT_REPLYMSG` before queue insertion (EK8799), and builds a pending-request wait mask with signed `1 << mp_SigBit` (`rom/exec/waitio.c:57-78`), now included in EK8800; `CreateMsgPort` obtains any free bit from `AllocSignal(-1)`, including bit 31 if lower bits are occupied (`rom/exec/createmsgport.c:54-65`). The storage component is owned by the separate disk report; broader device-specific abort semantics and caller lifetimes remain pending. No I/O or allocation was run.

Signal exception and priority follow-up: complete `SetExcept` was reread against its direct C callers, `SetSignal`, `Signal` and deferred `Reschedule`. The setter changes the current task's exception mask while holding local `Disable` and the SMP task spinlock (`rom/exec/setexcept.c:60-91`); selected pthread calls are behind disabled `USE_ASYNC_CANCEL` (`compiler/pthread/pthread_create.c:121-132`; `pthread.c:40`), and the other direct calls found are developer tests or the generated m68k thunk. This pass does not add a lost-update or selected pthread exception-delivery finding. Rechecked the apparent SMP lock-order hazard: `Reschedule` only marks the scheduler pending while Disable is active (`rom/exec/reschedule.c:58-77`); `SetExcept` drops `tc_SpinLock` before `Enable`, and `Enable` calls `KrnSchedule` only after the drop (`rom/exec/setexcept.c:82-91`; `rom/exec/enable.c:114-125`). Thus this path does not enter the scheduler holding the same task lock. `SetTaskPri` was reread with the PC scheduler: a ready task whose remembered CPU differs from the caller still gets no scheduler kick (EK842), while its remote running-task affinity pointer is passed after the task lock is dropped (EK273); the selected `ChangeTaskPri` target-lifetime issue remains EK840. No new distinct Exec candidate was credited. Remaining architecture scheduler paths, external SetExcept users and broader priority callers remain pending; no schedule was run.

Core source inventory check: every C/header/assembly path in `rom/exec` (183), `rom/kernel` (94), `arch/all-pc/kernel` (73), `arch/aarch64-native/kernel` (52), `arch/m68k-amiga/kernel` (16), and `compiler/pthread` (39) has a ledger row. In the five Exec/kernel directories, all C/assembly rows without an explicit body-review status are marked unbuilt or replaced by an architecture override. This is path/status coverage, not proof that target variants, cross-file ownership or runtime behavior have been fully audited. `compiler/crt/posixc` is recorded only for selected Exec/thread dependencies here: 16 of its 404 local C/header/assembly paths have ledger rows; the rest are outside this core inventory and must not be counted as reviewed.
