EK8839/OD1960 cross-report recheck: selected Pi SDHOST `sdhost_dma_setup` passes its ordinary `AllocMem` control-block pointer directly to the legacy DMA bus-alias macro (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/sdcard/sdcard_sdhost_bus.c:153-159,204-222`), while its data-buffer path calls `KrnVirtualToPhysical` and then forms the first-gigabyte DMA alias without checking that the translated bounce-buffer address fits it (`:62-70`; `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/include/hardware/bcm2708_dma.h:150-158`). EK8839 means the current ARM32 high-address translator is also wrong, so simply adding that call to SDHOST would not repair high-mapping DMA. The distinct SDHOST control-block omission and unchecked bounce-buffer address remain OD1960; source-only, with high-address allocation and runtime DMA unverified.

SetPatch FindSemaphore wrapper recheck (no new candidate): the selected m68k `SetPatch_Init` installs `spFindSemaphore` as Exec vector 99 (`arch/m68k-amiga/setpatch/setpatch_init.c:41-58,93-103`). The wrapper compares the supplied name with its special SetPatch semaphore, optionally opens graphics.library to enable AGA, then searches the ordinary semaphore list. Generic `FindSemaphore` documents a name pointer and delegates to `FindName` (`rom/exec/findsemaphore.c:26-35,49-61`); `FindName` asserts a nonnull name and compares C strings (`rom/exec/findname.c:73-85`). A null-name call would fail both contracts, so the wrapper's `Strcmp(name, ...)` does not establish a new regression. The in-tree direct callers found by exact C-call search pass string literals, named buffers, or other defined names; no selected null-name producer was found. The m68k build is not an SMP target, so its direct list search does not create a selected SMP-lock bypass. External m68k callers and the old AmigaOS SetPatch behavior remain unverified.


EK746 withdrawal reachability check: repository-wide `kb_PageSize` search found only the field declaration, zero checks in `rom/kernel/initmemory.c:49-53` and `rom/kernel/allocpages.c:66-68`, and reads in `statmemory.c`/the Unix override; no checked-in assignment exists. Thus the otherwise-mismatched generic DOS free path cannot be reached from checked-in startup and EK746 is withdrawn.

EK745 lock-boundary recheck: reread `OpenLibrary`, `CloseLibrary`, `RemLibrary`, the `struct Library` SMP fields and genmodule's ordinary non-duplicate vectors. `OpenLibrary` holds `LibList` read arbitration only through `FindName`, calls `EXEC_UNLOCK_LIST` before invoking OpenLib, and keeps only `Forbid` until return (`rom/exec/openlibrary.c:73-113`). `CloseLibrary` and `RemLibrary` likewise use local `Forbid` around the generated vectors (`closelibrary.c:64-82`; `remlibrary.c:64-88`); on SMP this does not serialize another CPU. The generated count increments/decrements and `LIBF_DELEXP` update contain no `EXEC_SPINLOCK_LOCK` (`tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1295-1305,1463-1468`), while `lib_SpinLock` is explicitly documented to protect open count and flags (`compiler/include/exec/libraries.h:52-59`) and is used in other library-vector mutation paths. Selected ASL's config confirms it uses the ordinary generated path. Caller-side qualification (2026-10-21): searched checked-in `RemLibrary` uses and found no direct ASL expunge caller; ASL has multiple ordinary library clients, but the delayed-expunge lifetime consequence is therefore scoped to external/API `RemLibrary` use. Expanded EK745 into the detailed report with the concurrent increment/decrement interleavings and this trigger limitation. Cross-core interleavings were not run.
Alert requester lifetime follow-up to EK473: `Alert_AskSuspend` saves its task's ETask pointer and formats initial text from it, then blocks in `SafeEasyRequest`/`SysReqHandler` (`rom/exec/useralert.c:88-115`; `:32-56`). The selected `security.library/secKill` path can remotely remove the waiting task and `RemTask` cleans its ETask (`rom/security/secKill.c:46-60`; `rom/exec/remtask.c:100-128`). If the requester returns with “More”, the alert code reads the saved ETask's stack/type/data (`useralert.c:116-119`); recoverable alert cleanup also passes the saved pointer to `ResetETask` (`rom/exec/alert.c:147-158`). This is additional caller evidence for EK473, not a separate finding. No requester/removal interleaving was run.

Native ARM DMA-buffer placement follow-up (EK8839 caller qualification): traced Raspberry Pi boot's `KRN_MEMLower`/`KRN_MEMUpper` values from the device-tree physical range through kernel placement (`arch/arm-raspi/boot/boot.c:204-239,483-500,556-604`). Boot lowers `KRN_MEMUpper` to the physical start of the relocated kernel before handoff; ARM kernel startup then constructs its System Memory MemHeader over that low `[memlower, memupper)` range (`arch/arm-native/kernel/kernel_startup.c:195-215,269-299`). The selected RPiHDMI buffers and control blocks use ordinary `AllocVec(MEMF_PUBLIC)` (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/RPiHDMI/rpihdmi-main.c:185-217`), so those allocations use the identity-addressed low range in this startup path, not the separate `0xf8000000` image mapping. EK8839 remains a high-address public-API defect, but this caller does not establish the trigger from its allocator source. Other memory headers, direct high-address clients and allocator changes remain unverified; no board or DMA was run.


AllocMem MungWall overflow restoration (EK30): confirmed the same `origSize` flows into `MungWall_Build` after `byteSize += MUNGWALL_TOTAL_SIZE` wraps, and the post-wall `memset` is unconditional even for `MEMF_CLEAR`. Traced the selected generic initializer's `mungwall` argument and swept direct in-tree AllocMem calls for large explicit constants or unchecked external-sized values; no selected extreme caller emerged. Restored the detailed API-level finding with the diagnostic-config trigger and no runtime reproduction.



m68k Wait/ChildWait ordering cross-check (EK811; no new finding): reread `arch/m68k-all/exec/wait.S` and `switch.S` against `rom/exec/childwait.c`. The m68k voluntary switch rechecks `tc_SigRecvd & tc_SigWait` with interrupts masked after building the prospective frame, and returns to the Wait loop without queuing the task if a signal arrived in that interval (`switch.S:60-102`). The normal m68k path is uniprocessor and ChildWait's Forbid prevents the earlier list-check/clear interleave. Thus this assembly does not demonstrate EK811 on m68k or a separate Wait lost-wakeup defect. Hardware nesting behavior and wider direct Wait callers remain open.

Optional D-Bus target caller audit (EK753): `rom/dbus/mmakefile.src` directly defines `kernel-dbus` with `amiga_threads.c`, but exact repository-wide target-name search found no parent aggregate edge; `rom/mmakefile.src`'s kernel object/package aggregates omit it. The source remains tracked as an explicit optional target, not a default package component. On SMP, `_condvar_wait`'s `Forbid` is local CPU only, so after releasing the caller mutex a remote signaler can signal the already-published waiter before `SetSignal(0, SIGF_SINGLE)` clears that bit. This can leave a signaled condition waiter asleep. Build-selected production reachability depends on explicitly including `kernel-dbus`; no default-image claim is made and no interleaving was run.

Console WaitForChar concurrency follow-up (EK708 detailed): DOS `WaitForChar` forwards each invocation as its own `ACTION_WAIT_CHAR` packet (`rom/dos/waitforchar.c:55-63`). The selected AUX startup hands control to the resident console handler in the same process, and device-backed console opens share its published task port (`workbench/fs/aux_handler/aux_handler.c:89-181`; `rom/filesys/console_handler/con_handler.c:748-761`). Its timed-wait branch has one `waitingdp` variable and one `timerreq`; a later positive-timeout packet stores over the earlier packet pointer (`con_handler.c:1133-1159`). A timer or console-read completion then replies only to the last stored packet. EK708 records the earlier caller's lost reply; EK709 separately records the reused timer request's queued-message corruption. No concurrent DOS packet sequence was run.

Console timer request reuse follow-up (EK709 restored): traced timeout expiry through `TimerProcessMicroHZ` and `ReplyMsg`, confirmed the handler never `GetMsg`s the timer port, then followed its next `SendIO` through the PC `BeginIO` override into `common_BeginIO` and the timer queue. Exec resets message type but does not unlink a replied message; the next expiry's `InternalPutMsg` unconditionally `AddTail`s the same node into the port that still contains it. This supports queue corruption on sequential timed waits, separately from EK708 concurrent packet replacement. No timer or DOS wait was run.


EK06 caller-trace refinement: the published port is freed on late `NewAddTask` failure, but selected `log.resource` uses it only as an initialization-success test. The resource can therefore report successful init with no broadcaster task; `logAddEntryA` gates submission on `lrb_Task` and returns `NULL`, so this pass found logging unavailability, not a stale-port dereference (`rom/log/log.c:304-317`; `rom/log/log_event.c:211-275`). The serial logger also ignores task creation failure, but its port dereferences are inside the worker that failed to start. Narrowed EK06 accordingly. No runtime failure was run.


Log listener candidate restoration (EK863 and EK8765; former EK8764 path): a repository call census was matched to the complete listener allocation, enqueue, removal and entry-free paths. `logAddListener` does not reject a failed per-listener `CreatePool`; a later event passes NULL to `AllocVecPooled`, whose `IsManagedMem` macro dereferences the null handle before it can return. This faults the broadcaster before the caller-side unchecked write, establishing EK863. EK8765 is now detailed: the service task queues the same raw entry pointer to each matching listener; standalone Logger can remove/free the entry before the optional `test-log` listener consumes its queued add message and calls `logGetEntryAttrs`. The serial logger does not remove live entries; its debug/add mask matches the broadcaster, so it is not used to overstate this trigger. No allocation failure or two-listener run was induced.

EK8795 timed-wait seconds-arithmetic and caller-boundary verification: the selected `time_t` typedef is signed 32-bit, and the deadline subtraction operands/results are `timespec.tv_sec` (`compiler/crt/posixc/include/aros/types/timespec_s.h:13-17`; `compiler/crt/stdc/include/aros/types/time_t.h:11-16`; `pthread_cond_timedwait.c:52,83`). A far-past representable absolute deadline can make that subtraction exceed the signed range before the code tests `rel.tv_sec < 0`; no earlier validation rejects negative seconds. The repository C-call census found `sem_timedwait` as the only maintained direct caller; its zero-count loop uses the absolute deadline, while `pthread_cond_timedwait_relative_np` calls the helper with `relative=TRUE` and does not trigger this arithmetic. Other public absolute API callers are external. Equal-width `time_t`/`timeval.tv_secs` means no separate narrowing bug is claimed. No timed wait was run.

EK764 relative-base lifetime follow-up: checked both checked-in explicit relative-link users (llvmpipe and softpipe), the complete `relbases.c` init/program-entry hooks, posixc's OpenLib behavior, and task.resource's wrapped `RemTask`. The task-resource wrapper frees only the per-task storage array after original task removal; it does not visit slot payloads. `relbases.c` has no exit/close path, so a task that used a relative wrapper retains its allocated table and the posixc `OpenLibrary` reference. No runtime exit or leak measurement was performed.

EK765 relative-base open-failure follow-up: traced generated relative-base accessors from `writegetlibbase.c` against `__aros_getoffsettable`. The first call publishes a zeroed slot table before `OpenLibrary`; a failed open leaves it published, and subsequent calls return it without retry. The generated accessor dereferences the field in that table, so the failure is not propagated safely. No open failure was induced.

EK8965 kernel-resource failure-path recheck: traced `Kernel_Init` through the generic `set_call_libfuncs` stop-on-first-false contract (`compiler/libinit/libinit.c:24-47`) and `AddResource` publication (`rom/kernel/kernel_init.c:122-138`; `rom/exec/addresource.c:62-100`). The selected i386 platform hook supplies a third concrete failure after publication: `PlatformInit` stores a successful platform-data allocation, then returns false if its 64 KiB system-stack allocation fails (`arch/i386-pc/kernel/platform_init.c:49-63`). This extends EK8965's selected trigger/configuration matrix, not a duplicate; no failure was induced.

Utility VSNPrintf caller reconciliation (EK679): searched all tracked C/header call sites for `VSNPrintf` and `SNPrintf`, then resolved aliases and selected target conditions. Direct in-tree Utility `VSNPrintf` use is Mount's `ShowFault`; utility `SNPrintf` calls are the two font.datatype destinations already checked as `MEMF_CLEAR`. CAMD's `SNPrintf` macro is under `__amigaos4__`, while this AROS build uses its local `RawDoFmt` helper. DiskImage declares a private `SNPrintf`/`VSNPrintf` implementation and its module is outside the currently selected aggregate; those functions do not call Utility. The generated m68k thunk forwards the public vector to guest clients but has no maintained C caller. Thus failed temporary allocation leaves Mount `ShowFault`'s output untouched before its `strlen` path (EK679); other public clients remain external. No allocation failure or formatter call was run.

RawDoFmt quad-format caller recheck (EK692 scope retained): searched checked-in C/header format literals for `%ll`/`%L` integer conversions and separated the formatter families. The x86-64 optional trapdebug caller uses the PC kernel `_bug` path (`arch/all-pc/kernel/_bug.c` -> `__vcformat`), whose shared `fmtprintf.c` parser explicitly consumes the second `l`; it is not a RawDoFmt client. `rom/devs/virtio/virtio_hw.c` places its `%llu` inside `D(...)`, while that manifest leaves `DEBUG` disabled. GPT's `%llu` calls remain behind its disabled `DREAD`/`DWRITE` macros. The sampled stdio clients dispatch through `__vcformat`, which supports long-long conversions. Thus these matches do not establish a live caller of RawDoFmt's unsupported modifier, and EK692 remains an API/possible external-client finding rather than an asserted default-build output defect. This was a targeted callsite check, not a full audit of all 356 RawDoFmt references. No formatter was run.


EK574 detailed follow-up: confirmed from the full worker-exit loop that `StarterFunc` invokes application TLS destructors while holding `tls_sem` shared, and `pthread_key_delete` attempts exclusive acquisition of that same semaphore. Exec maps shared ownership to a null semaphore owner, so the current task is not recognized as recursively owning the exclusive lock; it queues and waits while still holding the shared lock. The POSIX pthread_key_delete interface states the function is callable from a destructor. No destructor workload was run.


EK306 loader-context follow-up: for the selected non-m68k LDDemon path, a failed library search sends the segment back to the original caller, which invokes `CallLDInit` (`rom/lddemon/lddemon.c:435-446`); `LDInit` invokes `InitResident` in that context (`:224-228`). Thus the relative-library bases opened by root `InitLib` can be owned by the requesting task, while later library expunge can occur in a different task. The AROS Workbench-complete aggregate includes the png, tiff, jpeg, z and related module targets (`workbench/mmakefile.src:9-25`; `workbench/libs/mmakefile:9-63`). The TIFF datatype target in `workbench-datatypes-complete` declares `rellib tiff` and its loader calls `TIFFOpen`/`TIFFClose` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/tiff/{mmakefile.src,tiff.conf}`; `tiffclass.c:631,737`), confirming a selected client path; no caller sequence proving the cross-task overlap was found. No dynamic load/expunge was performed.

ROMTag scan-range caller census (continued): traced the selected `krnPrepareExecBase` range arrays at i386/x86-64 PC, ARM, AArch64, RISC-V SiFive U/OpenSBI, PPC Sam440, hosted Unix/MinGW and m68k Amiga (`arch/{i386-pc,x86_64-pc,arm-native,aarch64-native,riscv-native/sifive_u,riscv64-opensbi,ppc-sam440,all-unix,all-mingw32}/kernel/*`; `arch/m68k-amiga/boot/start.c:823-844`). Each supplies the `-1` terminator; RISC-V OpenSBI optionally adds a module interval only when its upper boundary is nonzero, and m68k can include multiple ROM ranges. This pass did not establish an empty or inverted selected interval reaching `krnScanResidents`' do-while probe; malformed firmware/tag ranges and the m68k flat-allocation capacity condition remain pending as recorded on the file row. No new scanner finding is credited from the range census. No boot was run.

OpenSBI PLIC diagnostic and initialization boundary follow-up: reread `kernel_plic.c` alongside the sole selected external-interrupt dispatcher (`intr.c`) and searched all target-local callers of `krnPLICDumpState`. Initialization returns before touching controller registers when the DTB/ACPI producer has no usable base/context; both producers cap context-list writes to the shared 16-entry bound, and the initializer copies only the published count. `krnPLICDumpState` would index `plic_ctxlist[0]` even with no stored contexts, but this target has no caller beyond its declaration, so that unreferenced diagnostic helper is not recorded as a current defect. The single static remembered claim context is not shared by another online hart in the selected startup, which leaves secondary-hart delivery as a future platform concern. The advertised PLIC source count and physical register extent remain the existing EK197 firmware-boundary questions; no new finding was established. No controller or firmware was run.


UEFI ExitBootServices retry follow-up (EK8862, formerly tracked as EK774): re-read the final map collection and exit sequence against the UEFI 2.10 ExitBootServices contract and the later kernel memory-header publication. The first descriptor snapshot is converted into `__efi_regions` and `__efi_fwregions` before the first exit call; on failure, a fresh key/map is fetched but its status and contents are not used to refresh those arrays. The spec requires obtaining a fresh map after an invalid key and permits partial shutdown on the first attempt. A changed descriptor ownership can therefore leave startup's memory publication based on a pre-retry snapshot. This remains conditional on a valid firmware changing a relevant descriptor across that failed attempt; no firmware was run.


UEFI relocation instruction-cache recheck (EK775 withdrawn): `hart_mask_base = -1` is the SBI encoding for ignoring the mask and targeting all available harts, so the `hart_mask=0` RFENCE call is not an empty-target request. OpenSBI processes the current hart locally when it is included in that set. The stub’s all-harts RFENCE request therefore does not establish a missing local instruction fence. No bug is retained; no firmware was run.


OpenSBI SBI helper caller-contract recheck: read `kernel_sbi.h` against all selected OpenSBI C callers and the relocation stub's standalone SBI wrapper. The shared helper places arguments in the standard `a0`–`a5` registers and returns `a0/a1`; selected BASE extension probing, DBCN buffer/length ordering, timer deadline, reset type/reason, and remote FENCE.I mask/base order agree with their current SBI declarations. `hart_mask_base = -1` is the specified all-available-harts form, so the zero mask in `sbi_remote_fence_i()` is intentional and includes the current hart where it is available (EK775 withdrawn). Caller-specific DBCN short-write handling remains EK728; no new helper ABI mismatch was established. No SBI firmware was run.


UEFI firmware-map capacity follow-up (EK8863, formerly tracked as EK776): traced `efi_collect_firmware`'s 24-entry bound through the conditional MMU mapping loop and the selected ACPI table reader. After 24 nonadjacent matching descriptors, collection stops without a truncation flag; when an EFI RSDP is present, startup maps only retained ranges, while ACPI dereferences its root and table addresses directly. A qualifying descriptor layout can therefore leave later firmware/ACPI data unmapped. Actual firmware maps, ACPI table placement and fallback behavior on hardware remain unverified; no boot was run.


OpenSBI ACPI root-length boundary recheck (EK777): compared `krnDumpACPI` with `acpi_find` and the boot-argument dispatch. Normal `acpi_find` rejects root tables no longer than their header, but the optional diagnostic path omits that check and subtracts `sizeof(acpi_header)` from a 32-bit length before narrowing the divided count to `unsigned int`. A short XSDT length can therefore produce a huge walk bound and out-of-table reads before MMU initialization when `dumpacpi` is requested. Firmware tables and runtime behavior were not tested.

Exec vector-allocation follow-up (EK783): reread `AllocVec`, `AllocVecPooled`, and paired free paths. The aligned hidden-header addition in `AllocVec` and the unmanaged pool prefix addition in `AllocVecPooled` both lack overflow checks and can turn near-limit `IPTR` requests into tiny successful allocations; managed pools forward the original request. No selected in-tree near-limit caller was found, so the trigger remains at the public API boundary.

CloseAsync external error-path follow-up (EK626): confirmed its documented result is error-negative/success-nonnegative, then traced the ignored DOS `Close` return through `rom/dos/close.c` to RAM `CmdEnd`, which can return failure for a changed file on a write-protected volume. CloseAsync frees its wrapper after the failed close and still returns the earlier nonnegative wait/final-write result. Existing maintained direct callers ignore that result, so the finding remains a public library-contract issue with no selected client behavior claimed. No handler close failure was induced.

AArch64 native task-context caller follow-up: traced `PrepareContext` through `NewAddTask`, `Exec_CleanupETask`, `KrnCreateContext`, `cpu_InitContextSize`, the first `cpu_Dispatch`, and the exception restore macros (`arch/aarch64-native/exec/preparecontext.c:21-88`; `rom/exec/newaddtask.c:270-309`; `rom/exec/exec_util.c:238-258`; `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/{createcontext,cpu_init,kernel_cpu,kernel_intern}.c`). The frame is 280 bytes; the FP/NEON block begins at aligned offset 288 and spans 528 bytes, matching the 816-byte context allocation and 66-word restore copy. Initial `cpsr=0x04` agrees with `CPUMODE_EL1t`; SP is aligned to the AAPCS64 16-byte boundary. `PrepareContext` has no failure return after allocation, while the failed-allocation path stores a null frame and NewAddTask cleans up the ETask without freeing a nonexistent context. No separate defect established. Caller contracts beyond NewAddTask and runtime dispatch remain open; no task was launched.

AArch64 EK807 (former EK659) trigger qualification: rechecked `Exec_ARMCPUInit`'s preallocated affinity mask against `PrepareContext` and the native scheduler (`arch/aarch64-native/exec/platform_init.c:63-80`; `exec/preparecontext.c:44-51`; `kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:38-48`). If `KrnAllocCPUMask` returns NULL, `PrepareContext` replaces the inherited mask with NULL, and `core_AffinityMatch` explicitly treats NULL as unrestricted; this allocation failure does not itself remove the idle fallback. EK807 (former EK659) still requires `NewCreateTask` to return NULL so no per-CPU idle task is registered, followed by self-removal with no other eligible ready task. Initialization does continue after that task-creation failure. No SMP schedule or allocation failure was run.


Mount name-bound recheck (EK682 withdrawn): `Mount` calls `ReadArgs(..., NULL)` for its CLI path; DOS `ReadArgs` reads into `TEXT argbuff[256 + 1]` with `FGets(..., sizeof(argbuff))`, so each parsed `DEVICE/M` token is below the 512-byte `PATHSTR_MAX` used by `dirname`. The relevant `SearchTable` prefixes are fixed and at most 23 bytes, keeping the combined `slen + len - 1` index below the same capacity. The Workbench startup branch does not use these CLI indexes and reads `wa_Name` from `WBArg`, whose `fib_FileName` field is 108 bytes (`compiler/include/dos/dos.h:57,81`). Thus the original-length indexes after `Strlcpy` are in bounds on selected entry paths; no in-tree caller supplies a larger buffer to the static Mount logic. The earlier candidate is withdrawn, not an active finding. No command was run.

Mount zero-progress read follow-up (EK683): reread `readfile`'s complete size/rewind/read loop and DOS `Read`'s documented return contract (`workbench/c/Mount.c:1249-1279`; `rom/dos/read.c:27-42`). A zero result is EOF; with `rest > 0`, the loop subtracts zero, advances by zero, and never closes the handle or frees the allocation. A concurrent truncation after the size query is a concrete external-writer trigger. No file or handler was changed.

Mount failed-insertion cleanup follow-up (EK684): traced `CheckDevice`/mountfile duplicate checks through `mount`, `AddDosEntry`'s locked duplicate-name rejection, and both caller cleanup paths (`workbench/c/Mount.c:1055-1219,1748-1922`; `rom/dos/adddosentry.c:88-121`). The precheck and insertion are separate, so simultaneous Mount calls can race. With a nonresident handler string, the local failure branch frees `HandlerString` without clearing it; caller `FreeStuff` frees it again and no owner releases the unregistered `DeviceNode` storage. No concurrent mount was run.

Mount multi-entry required-key follow-up (EK685): traced the CLI's once-per-command flag clear and `DEVICE/M` loop through `readmountlist`/`InitParams`, `ReadMountArgs`, `checkmount` and `MyMakeDosNode` (`workbench/c/Mount.c:293-310,624-690,746-760,1006-1023,1507-1512,1555-1564,1748-1764`). Each parameter block and device-string pointer is reset, but the global `flagargs` array is only ever set true after its initial clear. A later definition can consequently satisfy the required-field check from flags left by an earlier entry; a missing `DEVICE` becomes an empty startup name. No mountlist was edited or mounted.

OpenSBI PLIC omitted-boot-context caller recheck (EK784; no new candidate): retraced `kernel_fdt.c` supervisor-cause filtering/cap and independent boot-context selection into `krnPLICInit` and the selected external trap path. When `plic_ncontexts` is already nonzero, `krnPLICInit` copies only the capped array and does not append the separately identified `plic_context`; `krnPLICEnable` and `krnPLICClaim` use only that copied array, and `krnHandleExternalIRQ` has no alternate dispatch path if the boot context is absent. The report consequence is limited to AROS not dispatching interrupts through that context; pending/retrap behavior depends on inherited controller state. The finding remains specific to an FDT whose boot hart’s supervisor context occurs after the first 16 accepted cause-9 entries. The same truncation is present in ACPI: its parser caps enabled RINTC contexts at 16 and chooses the first stored context without matching `hart_id` to `__boot_hartid` (`kernel_acpi.c:360-393`); the report entry now covers both firmware inputs. No firmware or controller was run.

Exec vector-allocation arithmetic recheck (EK783): independently verified the modular wrap for `byteSize + AROS_ALIGN(sizeof(IPTR))` in `AllocVec` and `memSize + sizeof(IPTR)` in unmanaged `AllocVecPooled`. For either hidden-header width H, `IPTR_MAX - H + 2` wraps the backing request to one byte; the wrapper then records that wrapped size and returns after the header. Paired frees trust the stored size. The managed-pool branch forwards the original request. No in-tree near-maximum caller was found; no memory was allocated. EK783 is now restored as a detailed report entry.

OpenSBI FDT zero-cell boot-hang recheck (EK769): confirmed the tuple-width loop’s zero increment and zero-size `continue` prevent exit for a present `/memory/reg`; `kernel_cstart` has not reached its EFI/fixed-memory fallback because `krnParseFDT` never returns. The malformed-DTB condition is explicit, and the detailed finding is restored in the report. No parser run was performed.

OpenSBI FDT cell-count overflow recheck (EK772): checked a concrete unsigned-wrap case: root counts `0x40000001` and `1` yield an eight-byte computed tuple width, while `read_cells` still iterates the original first count without a property bound. The parser reaches this read for an eight-byte memory `reg`; this is distinct from EK769’s zero-width infinite loop. No DTB was constructed or parsed.

OpenSBI nested PLIC cell-width recheck (EK773): verified a valid root 1/1, `/soc` 2/2 encoding reads the first (zero) cell of the PLIC address as its base; `kernel_startup` attempts ACPI fallback only for a zero FDT base, then `krnPLICInit` declines setup if ACPI has no PLIC. This confirms interrupt-controller unavailability without relying on the earlier noncanonical-mapping branch. No matching board DTB was found or run.

OpenSBI FDT memory-region consumer recheck (EK771): traced the parser’s `memory` prefix and lack of `device_type`/`status` filtering through the non-EFI region path, RWX identity mapping, and startup `MemHeader` publication. A false region must survive the eight-entry cap and leave at least 1 MiB after exclusions before it becomes allocatable. No matching in-tree node was found; no FDT or allocator path was run. EK771 is restored in the detailed report with this trigger qualification.

POSIX childless-wait result recheck (EK476): checked the selected POSIXC manifest and traced `wait`, `waitpid(-1)` and `ChildWait(0)`. The wait helper only scans the exited-child port; it does not distinguish no children from live-but-not-exited children. The WNOHANG wrapper returns zero on an empty exited list without first establishing that a child exists. EK476 is now restored as a detailed finding. No child task or wait call was run.

PC IRQ-chain synchronization recheck (EK31): confirmed the selected PC translation unit overrides both `KrnAddIRQHandler` and `krnRunIRQHandlers`; neither takes `kb_IntrSpinLock`, while selected generic `KrnRemIRQHandler` takes the write lock and frees the node. The generic add/dispatch bodies take write/read locks, but are replaced for the PC build. The selected PC AHCI path takes `AddIntServer(INTB_KERNEL + r->res_tag, ...)` for its nonzero interrupt-resource flags; Exec forwards that kernel-vector call to `KrnAddIRQHandler`. On legacy INTx, the tag is the PCI device `INTLine`; MSI uses an allocated vector. A shared INTx assignment is possible but no checked-in machine assignment or overlap schedule was found. Same-IRQ concurrent writers and writer/dispatch lifetimes remain conditional. EK31 is now restored with this corrected scope.

Console completion library-lifetime follow-up (no new finding): traced the lazy `GfxBase` open in `InitCompletion` and GadTools handle through normal `close_con` teardown and `open_con` failure cleanup (`rom/filesys/console_handler/completion.c:64-100`; `con_handler.c:415-459,511-546,635`). `close_con` conditionally closes both handles after the window and console-device cleanup; the earlier `open_con` validation failure occurs before completion can lazily open graphics.library. `InitCompletion` does not check the lazy graphics open result before a later chooser uses graphics calls, but the console has already opened intuition.library, which retains its required graphics dependency; no selected failure state demonstrating a null graphics base was established, so this remains a checked dependency rather than a candidate. No console was run.

ConClip caller recheck (EK9487 detailed): traced the console menu's `do_paste` request through the selected ConClip command's `CODE_PASTE` handler into clipboard IFF chunk reading (`rom/filesys/console_handler/con_handler.c:908-912`; `support.c:752-801`; `workbench/c/ConClip.c:321-419`). The console's 16 KiB work-buffer allocation is unchecked; a nonempty clipboard reaches `memmove` and `ReadChunkBytes` without validating that pointer. The caller waits for a reply, so if the invalid access prevents ConClip from reaching `ReplyMsg`, that handler remains blocked. The null-destination access is established; a crash or missing reply is platform-dependent and was not reproduced. ConClip's other IFF read-result, stream and message-lifetime findings remain in the graphics/desktop ledger; no clipboard was read.

Console CSI chunk-boundary recheck (EK706 detailed): the windowed cooked handler requests 256 bytes, the selected console device queues up to 512 converted input bytes, and its read reply copies the requested byte count without CSI awareness (`rom/filesys/console_handler/con_handler.c:644-659`; `rom/devs/console/{consoletask.c:65-81,300-402,529-570,console_gcc.h:194-208}`). An exact stream with a two-byte key sequence straddling byte 256 is sufficient: the handler consumes the trailing `0x9B` as unknown at the first chunk's NUL boundary, then inserts the sequence's suffix as text after the next read. The package manifests select `kernel-console` and `kernel-fs-con` on Raspberry Pi ARM/AArch64; no input sequence was run.

AppWindow drop path recheck (EK701 detailed): traced the selected console window promotion and `AppMessage` loop through `NameFromLock`, `namefrom_internal`, and `AddPart` (`rom/filesys/console_handler/con_handler.c:324-325,780-829`; `rom/dos/{namefromlock,namefrom,addpart}.c`). `namefrom_internal` returns on FIB allocation failure before writing to the caller's buffer, while the console ignores `NameFromLock`'s failure and immediately treats the local array as a C string. `AddPart` uses `strchr` and `strlen`, confirming the uninitialized/unterminated read and possible scan past the local path array. EK701 now records this conditional low-memory AppWindow path; no drop was made.

Console-handler timer setup caller recheck (EK702 detailed): `WaitForChar(file, timeout)` forwards every nonzero-file request and timeout directly as `ACTION_WAIT_CHAR` (`rom/dos/waitforchar.c:57-63`); the console handler issues `SendIO` for a positive timeout only after its input buffer is empty (`con_handler.c:1133-1159`). `open_con` ignores the results of `CreateMsgPort`, `CreateIORequest` and `OpenDevice` (`con_handler.c:549-551`). Allocation failures produce NULL and `OpenDevice` dereferences the request; a reported timer-device open failure clears `io_Device`, which the later `SendIO` uses without a guard (`rom/exec/{createiorequest,opendevice,sendio}.c`). The in-tree `WaitForChar` calls found are SSH password input (`workbench/network/sshd/ssh.c:181`) and shell-output polling (`sshd.c:358,373`); these establish maintained public-wrapper use, but not that either handle is backed by this console handler. The documented DOS API is the trigger boundary. No allocation/device failure or packet was induced.

Console pathname-conversion recheck (EK703 detailed): traced the selected handler's startup `BSTR2C` helper and its immediate `isdosdevicec` caller (`rom/filesys/console_handler/con_handler.c:140-163,553-557`). `BSTR2C` can return NULL on `AllocVec` failure; the caller does not check it, and the parser dereferences it in its first loop condition. EK703 records the direct low-memory crash path. No allocation failure was induced.

Console filename `WINDOW` parameter recheck (EK704, no candidate confirmed): verified `con_handler_intern.h:59` documents `WINDOW0xXXXXXXXX`, then followed `parse_filename`'s slash-delimited parameter length and `string2val`'s bounded hexadecimal conversion (`rom/filesys/console_handler/support.c:232-258,343-347`). A correctly formed hexadecimal address is parsed as intended and `MakeConWindow` deliberately reuses the supplied window pointer (`con_handler.c:230-247`). The prior “wrongly parsed window pointer” note does not establish a defect; malformed caller-supplied addresses are not counted as a parser bug here. No window parameter was exercised.

Console pending-read EOF recheck (EK710 detailed): traced `ACTION_READ` into `con_read`, which appends each blocked DOS packet to `pendingReads`, then followed cooked input through the `INP_EOF` branch (`rom/filesys/console_handler/con_handler.c:1072-1088`; `rom/filesys/console_handler/support.c:994-1045,1175-1191`). With two or more pending reads and no buffered input, EOF removes and replies to only the first request, clears `FHFLG_EOF`, and leaves the remaining queue flagged pending; later reads also queue without seeing EOF. No matching close/read sequence was run.

Console history-ring shortcut recheck (EK705 detailed): verified commands are stored at `historypos` with wrap at 32, making the cursor the oldest physical slot once full (`rom/filesys/console_handler/support.c:632-644`; `con_handler_intern.h:41,83-84`). Shift-Up and Shift-Down instead force slots zero and `historysize - 1` (`support.c:659-665`); after wrap these are not generally the oldest and newest commands. With 33 distinct commands, `historypos` becomes 1: oldest is slot 1 and newest slot 0, while Shift-Down selects slot 31. No console was run.

Console-window EOF producer recheck (EK710): traced Intuition's `IECLASS_CLOSEWINDOW` event through the selected console task, which maps it to byte 28 (`CTRL-\`) before buffering and replying to a pending device read (`rom/devs/console/consoletask.c:292-330,379-402`). The cooked console handler maps byte 28 to `INP_EOF` (`rom/filesys/console_handler/support.c:550-570`). With no buffered line, its EOF branch replies to one pending DOS read and clears the EOF bit even if more read packets remain; this confirms the window-close trigger behind EK710. No close event or concurrent reads were sent.

Console EOF multi-reader caller follow-up (EK710, 2026-10-11): found a selected POSIX stream-clone path that can put multiple reads on the same console handler state. `popen(..., "r")` passes `SYS_Input=SYS_DupStream` with `SYS_Asynch=TRUE` (`compiler/crt/posixc/popen.c:73-90`); the public tag contract says this duplicates `Input()` (`compiler/include/dos/dostags.h:158-168`), `SystemTagList` uses `DupLockFromFH`/`OpenFromLock` (`rom/dos/systemtaglist.c:213-220`), and console.handler `ACTION_FH_FROM_LOCK` maps the clone to the same internal `fh` and increments its usecount (`rom/dos/openfromlock.c:58-73`; `con_handler.c:1003-1025`). If both parent and asynchronous command block reading the same cooked CON: stream and the window then closes before line data arrives, the EOF branch replies only one packet and clears EOF while the other remains queued. The multi-read scheduling and window-close sequence were not run.

Console completion writer-lifetime recheck (EK699 detailed): traced a DOS `Write` through `dopacket`'s caller-owned reply port into `answer_write_request`, then through Tab completion into `InitCompletion` and `DoScan` (`rom/dos/{write,dopkt}.c`; `rom/filesys/console_handler/{support,completion}.c`). `lastwritetask` retains `mp_SigTask` with no ownership; `CreateNewProc` places its Process structure in its task memory list, and `RemTask` frees that list after termination. Thus, when another client keeps the console handler alive and a writer exits without a later write refreshing the field, subsequent completion dereferences a stale task pointer. The DOS caller-port, process allocation and Exec release paths establish the conditional lifetime error. No shared-handle exit/completion sequence was run.

Console single-match path-length failure recheck (EK698, no new candidate retained): `PreparePattern` derives `dirpart` from the user's current input word, whose total line is bounded by `INPUTBUFFER_SIZE` (256), and the completion `match` buffer is also 256 bytes (`completion.c:124-145`; `con_handler_intern.h:39-40,88-89`). The three ignored `AddPart` results leave the already copied drawer or directory text intact (`completion.c:242-243,715-720,777-782`), so a too-long combined path is completed as its directory prefix (often with a trailing slash) rather than silently overrunning memory. Because the combined pathname cannot fit in the same bounded command line, the examined cases do not establish a distinct material regression beyond the apparent truncation fallback; EK698 is not promoted to a detailed finding. Requester and input semantics for such maximum-length paths remain untested.

Console completion caller recheck (EK699; shared-state precondition established, final sequence conditional): the boot path opens `cis`, creates `cos` with `OpenFromLock(DupLockFromFH(cis))`, then gives both to the initial CLI (`rom/dos/boot.c:310-315,337-347`). `ACTION_FH_FROM_LOCK` binds the new DOS wrapper to the same internal console `filehandle` (`rom/dos/openfromlock.c:58-74`; `rom/filesys/console_handler/con_handler.c:1003-1025`), establishing that the ordinary CLI's input and output can update and consume the same completion state. POSIX `vfork()` passes the parent's output handle to the child (`compiler/crt/posixc/__vfork.c:467-485`); `C:Run` also duplicates inherited handles through `OpenFromLock` (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Run.c:127-165`; `run_handle.h:7-45`). Thus the source establishes shared-state child writes and a later input-side Tab path are possible. The exact checked-in client sequence with no parent write between child exit and Tab completion remains unestablished, so EK699 retains that trigger condition and is not claimed as a reproduced user sequence. No child-exit/completion sequence was run.

Console Utility-library reference recheck (EK707, no material candidate retained): `open_con` uses `TaggedOpenLibrary(TAGGEDOPEN_UTILITY)` and its validation-failure path closes the reference, while normal `close_con` omits it (`rom/filesys/console_handler/con_handler.c:514,539-545,449-450`). `TaggedOpenLibrary` delegates to `OpenLibrary`, so the reference count is incremented; however, the selected Utility resident declares `noexpunge` (`rom/utility/utility.conf:3-5`). Repeated console opens therefore leave a stale `lib_OpenCnt` count, but this recheck did not establish a reclamation or behavior consequence in the selected library. No candidate is retained.


NewCreateTaskA unnamed-task bounds follow-up (EK788): verified that the default allocation count is two, the name count is raised only by TASKTAG_NAME, and NewAllocEntry sizes the MemList from and initializes exactly the requested entries. The selected Raspberry Pi ARM SMP processor probe omits both optional tags. NewCreateTaskA therefore reads beyond its two-entry allocation; allocator rounding may place the address in readable padding, and a nonnull residue can bypass NewAddTask’s supported null-name fallback. Promoted earlier EK24 coverage note as EK788 in the detailed report; no task was launched.


RemTask direct-caller follow-up: rechecked the maintained direct-call census against task-teardown ownership. Mesa’s `abort()` deliberately calls `RemTask(NULL)` to terminate the current task (`workbench/libs/mesa/aros_drm_shim.c:96-116`); this is a self-removal path and does not add a second remover for EK830. Hosted SDL HIDD expunge calls `RemTask(eventtask)` while the event loop itself runs indefinitely (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/event.c:60-86,151-154`); target-specific expunge sequencing remains pending, so no new caller-side claim is promoted. Existing remote-running task and queued-PC-IPI cases remain EK473/EK832. No task or HIDD was run.

RISC-V ETask-affinity follow-up: checked both `GetIntETask(...)->iet_CpuAffinity` scheduler reads against build gates and task-ready producers. They are compiled only under `__AROSEXEC_SMP__`, absent from selected OpenSBI configuration; native SiFive U boot remains blocked before this scheduler (EK193/EK195). The ordinary `NewAddTask`/legacy `AddTask` route only makes a task ready after successful `InitETask`; allocation failure returns before launch. No new ETask-null finding is credited. EK9131 now details the latent invalid-saved-SP wrong-node path; alternate low-level construction and runtime remain open.

EK790 task-port failure follow-up: traced `NewCreateTaskA`'s early output publication through failed `NewAddTask` cleanup and selected `log.resource` libInit. A failed ETask/context setup frees the port allocation but leaves the output non-null; libInit ignores the task result and reports success. `logAddEntryA` subsequently returns NULL while `lrb_Task` is unset, establishing unavailable logging rather than a port dereference. Also traced seriallogger init: with `debug=serial`, it registers a provider before task creation, ignores the null task result and returns success; no listener starts and no serial output is produced. Its provider remains registered. The x86-64 PC manifest selects the resource, but activation is option-dependent. No task allocation failure was induced.

EK791 CPU feature-detection follow-up (rechecked 2026-10-10): `cpu_HasZicbom` scans the full FDT totalsize without decoding property boundaries (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/exec/cpu_init.c:152-193`). The selected kernel parser extracts `/chosen/bootargs` as a pointer into that same blob and republishes the blob under `KRN_FlattenedDeviceTree` (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_fdt.c:227-231`; `kernel_startup.c:398-399`), confirming an unrelated bootarg substring reaches the scan. A positive match replaces the Exec DMA vectors (`cpu_init.c:210-218`); selected NVMe, VirtIO and PCI xHCI call `CachePreDMA`, so a false positive can execute CBO instructions on a hart without Zicbom. No in-tree FDT image supplied this trigger, and no firmware or device I/O was run. The prior EK673 no-Zicbom DMA candidate has since been withdrawn from the active report: all selected DMA clients route through PCIDT, which documents its bus-master controllers as cache coherent; external-client coherence remains unverified.

EK673 selected-client coherence recheck (2026-10-17): reread the OpenSBI package manifest and the selected NVMe SGL, VirtIO queue, and PCI xHCI DMA hook callers. Confirmed all three packages are selected and use `CachePreDMA`/`CachePostDMA`; however, the selected PCIDT allocator explicitly describes its bus-master controllers as cache coherent (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/pcidt/pcidt_driverclass.c:992-1001`). The source pass did not establish that the selected VirtIO PCI path or another selected device is noncoherent on any supported no-Zicbom configuration. At that time EK673 was left as an unresolved platform-configuration candidate. A later caller reconciliation found no selected noncoherent device and withdrew it from the active report; the generic hook mismatch alone does not establish a selected hardware trigger. No target was run and no DMA was performed.

EK613 CMO block-size conformance recheck (2026-10-17): compared `CBO_BLOCK` and both range loops (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/exec/cpu_init.c:80-101`) with the ratified RISC-V CMO specification. It explicitly describes cache-block size as implementation-specific and requires the execution environment to provide discovery; the initial CMO extensions require one uniform size across the system, not a fixed 64-byte size (CMO §19.1.3, https://docs.riscv.org/reference/isa/v20260120/unpriv/cmo.html). The RISC-V CPU binding exposes `riscv,cbom-block-size`; `cpu_Init` only searches for `zicbom` and does not read this property (`cpu_init.c:152-193,210-218`). Thus a uniformly 32-byte Zicbom implementation remains within the documented architectural model and causes every other block to be skipped by the hardcoded 64-byte loop. EK613 retained as conditional; no selected boot tree or hardware run establishes that exact block size.

OpenSBI zero-length CBO range check (2026-10-17; no new EK): when `address` is unaligned and `length` is zero, the Zicbom helper's aligned start is less than its end (`cpu_init.c:83-89,98-104`), so it performs one CBO on the preceding block instead of doing nothing. The selected xHCI helper returns before the cache hook for zero length (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_schedule.c:49-52`), NVMe I/O rejects zero length before PRP/SGL setup (`rom/devs/nvme/nvme_io.c:68-72`), and VirtIO invokes the data hook only for positive payload length (`rom/devs/virtio/virtio_queue.c:187`). Descriptor/header calls pass positive `sizeof` lengths. No selected OpenSBI caller supplies a zero-length DMA span, so the public zero-length edge is not promoted to a selected-device finding. No hook was called at runtime.

EK791 trap-consequence follow-up (2026-10-17): traced illegal-instruction scause 2 through the OpenSBI dispatcher. It maps to Exec's instruction-error trap (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_traps.c:55-63,250-258`; `compiler/include/exec/alerts.h:32`). The selected default task trap handler marks the alert dead-end and redirects an ETask to `Exec_CrashHandler`; without a usable task handler the kernel's fallback logs the fault and halts that hart (`rom/exec/traphandler.c:63-120`; `kernel_traps.c:248-264,327-335`). Thus EK791's consequence is an instruction-trap/dead-end task alert or hart halt on the first selected DMA hook executed by a hart lacking Zicbom, rather than silent incorrect cache maintenance. No exception was induced.

AttemptSemaphore pre-init reachability recheck (EK8854, 2026-10-17): searched all maintained C/header `PREINITLIB` registrations and the selected Exec pre-init call ordering. The only registration is `Exec_X86PreInit` (`arch/all-pc/exec/platform_init.c:443`), which runs before the bootstrap task is published (`rom/exec/exec_init.c:118-148,198-201`) but only calls `AddResetCallback`; it does not call AttemptSemaphore. No other maintained PREINITLIB registration or indirect in-tree AttemptSemaphore call path was found. EK8854 remains an external/public-API candidate for a pre-init module, with no selected in-tree trigger. No init callback was run.

EK34 allocator retry lifetime recheck (2026-10-17): confirmed `AllocMem` stores the current first handler pointer before trying the allocation (`rom/exec/allocmem.c:105-116`), while `checkMemHandlers` only acquires `LowMemSem` after that failure and dereferences the saved node before calling any handler (`rom/exec/memory.c:1313-1335`). `RemMemHandler` acquires the same semaphore, unlinks the supplied node, then returns to generated Diskfont expunge, which frees the base containing that node (`rom/exec/remmemhandler.c:46-52`; `workbench/libs/diskfont/diskfont_init.c:61-77`; `tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1510-1547`). The lock therefore serializes active list walks with removal but cannot protect the allocator's earlier snapshot. EK34 remains unchanged; no allocation failure or expunge interleaving was induced.

Kernel manifest target-composition follow-up (x86-64 PC and OpenSBI): compared `rom/kernel/mmakefile.src` with the selected target makefiles. Generic kernel functions/resources and target-specific kernel image composition are separate edges; x86-64 PC adds `kernel_startup`, platform/MMU objects, architecture API replacements and SMP bootstrap (`arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/mmakefile.src:25-50,65-87`), while OpenSBI declares an explicit kernel/BSP C and assembly set and packages kernel/task resources plus exec.library (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/mmakefile.src:20-63,65-99`). No duplicate/omitted local source was established in these two manifests. This is a partial target reconciliation only; other maintained architecture manifests, conditional `USE_MMU` sets and generated clocksource headers remain unreviewed. No build was run.

OpenSBI package boundary follow-up (EK792): traced the selected FDT initrd range into `krnLoadPackage`, compared its member iteration with `tools/package/FORMAT` and the canonical writer, and followed loader failure into the startup warning path. Length-prefixed paths/payloads are not bounded by the supplied package end, and the declared package-size field is ignored. Malformed/truncated package handling is now detailed in AROS-exec-kernel.md; generated ELF table/relocation bounds and malformed firmware initrd extents remain open. No malformed package was constructed or loaded.

OpenSBI ELF-member bounds follow-up (EK793): the outer package parser has the exact member `datalen` at `kernel_elf.c:443`, but drops it at the `krnLoadModule` call (`:453`). The ELF loader checks magic/machine only, then indexes section headers and uses section, relocation, symbol and string offsets without a member-length bound (`:56-59,221-307`). Its bump allocator also tests `addr + size` against the pool end without overflow protection and stores the wrapped sum as the next allocation pointer (`kernel_elf.c:40-54`), so a huge allocatable section size can bypass the pool bound before the initialization/copy loop. EK793 records these internal ELF-member bounds and allocator-overflow paths as independent from EK792’s outer package-record bounds. This applies only to malformed/corrupted ELF members in the selected OpenSBI boot package; the package producer writes bytes but does not validate ELF structure. Generated ELF shape and actual boot behavior remain untested.

OpenSBI package-member alignment check (no finding credited): `%make_package` passes absolute device/library/resource paths to `tools/package/pkg` (`config/make.tmpl:3753-3768,3795-3797`); the writer stores basenames and pads path fields to multiples of four (`tools/package/pkg:105-109`). The selected OpenSBI package orders `console.device`, `input.device`, `gameport.device`, `keyboard.device`, `nvme.device`, `virtio.device` and `USBHardware/pcixhci.device` first (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/boot/mmakefile.src:103-120`). Member data therefore has no format-level eight-byte alignment guarantee. The exact generated module lengths/offsets are absent from this source-only checkout, so an actual selected unaligned ELF-header access is not established and no candidate is credited.

ARM processor-resource allocation-failure rollback recheck (EK796): traced the common topology allocation and ARM per-CPU array/record allocations through the selected RPi processor manifest and generated `set_libinit` failure path. A later record allocation failure returns directly, skips the post-loop probe wait and `FreeSignal` calls, and generated rollback frees only the resource base; no common or ARM expunge hook releases the external topology/record allocations. The no-memory path was not induced.

ARM SMP processor affinity-fallback recheck (EK797): verified that ARM PrepareContext overwrites the affinity with the supplied null mask, and the selected scheduler treats null as unrestricted. The signal-exhaustion fallback probes synchronously on the current CPU. Both paths feed the record array later used for indexed GetCPUInfo and MPIDR topology. No resource failure or CPU probe was run.

ARM SMP probe-batch synchronization recheck (EK279): traced the worker signal to the end of `ReadProcessorInformation` and Exec `Wait` to its any-requested-bit loop. The single Wait can return before other secondary records are complete; a failed `NewCreateTask` leaves an expected bit without a sender. The Raspberry Pi ARM SMP source selection was checked; no task failure or interleaving was run.

ARM processor per-core API cross-check (legacy ID reconciliation; 2026-10-25): reread `GetCPUInfo`, `ARM_AnswerTag`, public selection/default rules, processor init rollback and SysExplorer’s indexed query loop. The selected index is clamped before reading `sysprocs`; failed per-core allocation aborts resource init before public callers can query it. Old temporary IDs EK9037-EK9040 refer to processor-resource findings maintained in the Other Drivers report as OD3529, OD3536, OD3533 and OD3539. EK9041’s null BrandString candidate is withdrawn: ShowConfig/SysExplorer substitute Unknown, SysMon’s `__sprintf` path uses RawDoFmt `%s` handling that maps NULL to empty output, and the public tag contract does not guarantee a non-NULL string. EK797 remains the separate identity/affinity mismatch. No resource failure or UI query was run.

OpenSBI package alignment follow-up (EK800): traced the selected `%make_package` expansion and package member ordering. Its `classes=$(BSP_USBCLASSES)` list is the first `PKG_FILES` group, so the first member is `hub.class`; the writer stores its 9-byte basename in a 12-byte path field, placing payload 28 bytes after the 8-byte package header. EFI `AllocatePool` supplies the package buffer, while the loader directly reads the ELF64 payload through naturally aligned structures and directly casts package cursors to `ULONG *`. This selected first-member offset is 4 modulo 8 for an 8-byte-aligned allocation; later path-length words also inherit prior payload lengths modulo four because payloads have no trailing padding. The RISC-V trap handler halts on an unhandled load-misaligned exception. This makes the alignment trigger concrete for firmware/package combinations that trap these accesses, though no generated package, allocation address, or target EEI was available to establish actual boot failure. No artifact or target was run.

OpenSBI bump-allocator alignment recheck (EK801): traced all three `krnBumpAlloc` call sites, section eligibility, SHT_NOBITS clearing and PROGBITS copying. A zero `sh_addralign` is used in address arithmetic before the function substitutes its eight-byte minimum, producing a null address. Whether the checked-in build’s generated modules contain such a nonempty SHF_ALLOC section remains unknown; no ELF was built or loaded. Distinct from EK793, which concerns malformed section extents.

OpenSBI relocation/alignment pass (EK793/EK801; no new candidate): checked every krnBumpAlloc call and relocation store width in `krnRelocOne`. A zero section alignment yields a null allocator result before section copy/clear and aborts package loading (EK801); the earlier report text claiming a write through zero was corrected after tracing both caller checks. For nonzero requested alignments below eight, the allocator also fails to recompute after applying its minimum; however, no selected valid module relocation/data layout was established that produces an independent failure, so this possibility remains open rather than a separate finding. R_RISCV_RELAX/R_RISCV_ALIGN no-ops preserve the current unrelaxed instruction layout; generated module flags and relocation records remain unavailable. No object was built or loaded.

Exec Wait/Signal handshake recheck (no new finding): reread the full 462-line `rom/exec/signal.c` against `Wait`'s received-bit test, wait-mask publication, TS_WAIT/list transition and `KrnSwitch` handoff. On SMP both paths serialize signal fields and state with the same task lock; a signal before Wait's test is observed as pending, while a signal after TS_WAIT publication removes the task from the wait list through the reschedule helper. Supported SMP switch implementations release the carried lock only after saving the outgoing context; RISC-V SMP is not a selected configuration. `Wait` clears only the requested received bits after wake. Existing EK811 remains the caller-level ChildWait gap where it clears a completion bit after scanning the queue; no separate lost-wakeup defect is established in Wait/Signal. No task or signal timing was run.

PC selected-core frequency caller recheck (EK798): reread the whole SysExplorer processor-page query loop and the selected generic and PC `GetCPUInfo` path. The caller changes only `GCIT_SelectedProcessor` per iteration and does not set task affinity; the generic processor method forwards that index to the saved PC per-core record, while `GetCurrentProcessorFrequency` executes `rdmsr` locally with no target argument. Therefore a call scheduled on a different logical CPU combines that caller CPU's APERF/MPERF ratio with the requested core's maximum-frequency record. No affinity switch or MSR access was performed.

PC IRQ-chain selected caller recheck (EK31): traced the selected PC AHCI interrupt setup through `bus_alloc_resource_any`/`pci_alloc_1intr` and `bus_setup_intr`. Its resource flags take the `AddIntServer(INTB_KERNEL + r->res_tag, ...)` branch (`ahci_aros_bus.c:334-369`); Exec sends kernel vectors from `AddIntServer` to `KrnAddIRQHandler` (`rom/exec/addintserver.c:62-67`). On the legacy INTx path `res_tag` is the device `INTLine`; MSI receives a separately allocated vector. This confirms a selected PCI caller path to the unsynchronized chain, The `x86_64-pc` `smp` configure branch is selected-capable and its boot package includes AHCI (`configure.in:2195-2199`; `arch/x86_64-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:66-68`), but no checked-in machine assignment establishes that two devices share an INTx line, and no concurrent registration/dispatch timing was run. No IRQ was added or dispatched.


ARM SMP processor probe barrier recheck (EK279): confirmed the caller creates one distinct allocated signal bit per secondary CPU but waits once on their union; Exec Wait is explicitly “some signal” and clears the entire requested mask. Processor_FillTopology reads the MPIDR fields immediately after that wait, while an unfinished ProbeCPUAndSignal may still write the corresponding cleared record. NewCreateTaskA returns NULL on task allocation/context failure, and Processor_Init does not test it after adding the signal bit, so failure of every secondary launch strands the init task in Wait. The report trigger is limited to three-or-more logical CPUs for the staggered-success race; no runtime probe or allocation failure was induced.

EK808 selector/map-bound follow-up: `mm_AllocPages` selects a header for non-NULL `addr` with `addr >= mh->mh_Lower || addr + length <= mh->mh_Upper` (`rom/kernel/kernel_mm.c:46-56`). For an address beyond the header, the first term is true; `mm_AllocAbs` rounds it and reads `head->map[start]` without validating `start < head->size` (`rom/kernel/mm_linear.c:275-322`). The checked production calls pass NULL and the generic allocator also needs nonzero `kb_PageSize`; retain this as a conditional API candidate pending a selected initialized generic-MMU client of absolute allocation. No access was attempted.


ChildOrphan emulation-result follow-up (EK481/EK813): checked the public Exec vector signature and return contract against the generated thunk body, the emulator dispatch D0 assignment for both manual and generated tables, and the `rom/m68kemu/mmakefile.src` target gates. The thunk unconditionally returns zero after calling the native API, so emulated callers cannot distinguish success from `CHILD_NOTNEW`/`CHILD_NOTFOUND`; promoted to detailed EK813. No emulated caller was run.
GetMsg/WaitIO caller-pattern recheck (EK9072; no second concrete trigger): searched all checked-in C/header sources for request-queue drains near WaitIO, then traced the apparent matches in `workbench/c/Eject.c:151-163`, generic and m68k trackdisk workers (`rom/devs/trackdisk/trackdisk_device.c:661-720`; `arch/m68k-amiga/devs/trackdisk/trackdisk_device.c:402-413`), Bluetooth HCI timer teardown (`rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:2499-2539,3036-3041`), and PPP serial/timer cleanup (`workbench/devs/networks/ppp/serial.c:51-80,170-214`). Eject's Ctrl-C path does not dequeue the completed request before WaitIO; trackdisk and Bluetooth timers have distinct ports from their command queues; PPP waits on each request before draining its port. These do not add a same-completion double-consumption case to Logger's `GetMsg(timer reply)` then `WaitIO` sequence. This pattern search is not a full audit of all 959 API references; wider caller paths remain open. No I/O sequence was run.

Exec timed-lock cleanup recheck (EK568/EK803): reread `pthread_mutex_timedlock` and `_obtain_sema_timed` against timer.device OpenDevice, CheckIO, AbortIO, list insertion and elapsed-time comparisons (`compiler/pthread/pthread.c:129-196,249-354`; `rom/exec/{opendevice,checkio}.c`; `rom/timer/{abortio,lowlevel,timer_macros}.c`). Confirmed EK568's zero-remaining-time branch explicitly sets `io_Flags=0`, leaves the request `NT_MESSAGE`, and closes before SendIO; timer AbortIO then treats the unlinked request as queued and calls Remove. Failed OpenDevice similarly leaves the stack request's flags indeterminate after OpenTimerDevice has set its message type, so CloseTimerDevice can enter the same abort route. Confirmed EK803's arithmetic uses unsigned 32-bit `timeval.tv_sec` on selected targets, and the timer compares unsigned elapsed counters; a past-deadline age greater than timer uptime wraps the relative delay into a future timer target. These source traces support the existing findings and do not add another candidate. No I/O request or timer was run.


Generic MMU absolute-allocation recheck (EK808): traced the public `KrnInitMemory` vector through `mm_Init` and the allocator test's manual MemList insertion (`rom/kernel/kernel.conf:69`; `initmemory.c:17-54`; `developer/debug/test/kernel/allocator.c:150-168`). This establishes that callers can create individually page-managed MemHeaders, though the only checked caller is the excluded test. For a valid explicit request inside a later high-address header, an earlier compatible header with enough free bytes passes `addr >= mh_Lower` and is selected before the actual containing header; `mm_AllocAbs` derives an unchecked map index from that address. This strengthens the source trigger but does not establish an ordinary selected in-tree caller or default boot reachability; no allocator operation was run.

EK567 fast-path recheck (2026-10-09): reread `pthread_mutex_timedlock`, `pthread_mutex_trylock`, `_obtain_sema_timed`, Exec `Procure`/`ReleaseSemaphore`, and `pthread_mutex_unlock` (`compiler/pthread/pthread.c:249-353`; `pthread_mutex_trylock.c:22-42`; `rom/exec/procure.c:47-70`; `rom/exec/releasesemaphore.c:62-82`; `pthread_mutex_unlock.c:26-43`). A successful trylock leaves `result == 0`, but the function falls through to the helper; its exclusive Procure is granted to the same task and increments `ss_NestCount`. One unlock decrements only one level, so this is a retained lock, not just duplicate work. Added the missing detailed EK567 entry to `../AROS-exec-kernel.md`; timeout behavior, external clients and runtime scheduling were not tested.


EK834 separate-process reachability recheck (2026-10-09): confirmed the public `dup2` implementation has a threaded-application restriction (`compiler/crt/posixc/dup2.c:45-55`), so same-process concurrent `dup2` is outside its documented use. The collision itself needs no such race: `posixc.conf:6` selects `pertaskbase`, and `__posixc_intbase.h:71-83` distinguishes ordinary Process-owned descriptor tables from pthread workers borrowing their creator’s table. One process can already hold `newfd` globally while another process has that number empty locally; the second can then call dup2 sequentially. The global `fd.library` stores only owner class and one data pointer, and `__getfdslot` skips reservation for any `FD_OWNER_POSIXC`, so the overwrite remains reachable across processes. Existing EK834 remains; no runtime process or socket operation was performed.


EK832 PC remote-removal path recheck (2026-10-09): traced the x86-64 `EXEC_REMTASK_NEEDSSWITCH` branch into `krnSysCallReschedTask` and `X86_HandleReschedTask` (`arch/all-pc/exec/exec_platform.h:14-20`; `rom/exec/remtask.c:97-128`; `arch/all-pc/exec/platform_init.c:259-328`). For a waiting/ready task, the handler performs scheduler-list/state transitions; it does not inspect or drain `kb_BusyIPIHooks`. `core_DoCallIPI(..., async=1, ...)` has already stored the callback in that independent kernel queue (`arch/all-pc/kernel/kernel_ipi.c:92-105,149-209`), and the target drains it later (`:224-279`). PC does not define `KERNEL_IPI_CALL_CANCELABLE`, so the subsequent `CancelSignalIPIs` call in RemTask is compiled out. This confirms the distinction from EK473's already-running target case; selected root `secKill` can remove a waiting non-process task. The `krnSysCallReschedTask` instruction is synchronous only on the remover CPU, not a remote-CPU acknowledgment (`arch/all-pc/kernel/x86_syscalls.h:26-29`); it does not wait for a queued callback. No IPI timing or removal was run.


64-bit PC self-RemTask path recheck (EK839/EK807 scope correction, 2026-10-09): `__WORDSIZE==64` selects `EXEC_REMTASK_NEEDSSWITCH` (`arch/all-pc/exec/exec_platform.h:16-18`), so `RemTask(NULL)` executes the PC software switch at lines 82-90 before it reaches cancellation, context/ETask cleanup or ServicePort publication (`rom/exec/remtask.c:109-163`). The handler enters `cpu_Switch`; PC `core_Switch` removes TS_REMOVED from the running list and marks it TS_TOMBSTONED on SMP (`arch/all-pc/exec/platform_init.c:190-205`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:205-216`). The task is not made runnable or published to ServiceTask, so the cleanup code cannot resume. Promoted this distinct resource-leak path to EK839 and narrowed EK807: ARM32/AArch64 `Exec_SuicideSwitch` explicitly returns after detach/tombstone, permitting the common RemTask cleanup/message path; PC does not. The selected DOS init self-removal is one caller (`rom/dos/dos_init.c:268-275`). No task was removed or runtime behavior tested.

`RemTask(NULL)` caller census for EK807/EK839: searched maintained C sources for executable self-removal calls. The selected DOS startup caller invokes it after CLI initialization (`rom/dos/dos_init.c:268-275`); the hosted emergency filesystem boot handler calls it only after synchronous emergency-shell creation fails (`arch/all-hosted/filesys/emul_handler/boot.c:184-191`); and the optional Mesa abort shim calls it to terminate the current task (`workbench/libs/mesa/aros_drm_shim.c:101-115`). The latter two are platform/feature-specific, while DOS startup is the direct 64-bit-PC selected path establishing EK839. No additional call-site-specific consequence is credited. Source-only; no task termination was induced.

PC Exec override inventory reconciliation: compared every checked-in `.c`/`.h` file under `arch/all-pc/exec` (7 C/header files) and `arch/i386-pc/exec` (4 C/header plus 2 assembly files) with the file rows; all 13 source/header/assembly files have rows, and the two override manifests account for all 12 local C/assembly implementation bodies plus the shared platform header (`all-pc` six C bodies and header; `i386-pc` four C and two assembly bodies). `rom/exec/mmakefile.src` enables architecture-specific assembly and includes the selected target override make options; the `pc` shared manifest and `pc-i386` manifest are separate, with no `arch/x86_64-pc/exec` source directory. HPET unit-release synchronization recheck: reread `AllocCSUnit` and `FreeCSUnit` with the selected resource init and kernel clock-source registration. Allocation serializes scans and owner publication with the initialized semaphore; release clears one owner pointer without taking it. The kernel registers only after successful array allocation and lock initialization, checks the returned `(IPTR)-1`, and retains its static owner. A tree-wide C/header search finds no in-tree `FreeCSUnit` caller, so no separate in-tree lost-allocation or double-release path is established; external ownership discipline and SMP timing remain open. Exec/kernel EK832 source recheck: reread PC `core_DoCallIPI` publication and busy-list callback order with `Signal`/`RemTask`. The async path copies the raw task pointer into an `IPIHook`, publishes it under the busy-list lock, and invokes the saved hook before removing that entry (`arch/all-pc/kernel/kernel_ipi.c:149-209,234-279`). PC defines no `KERNEL_IPI_CALL_CANCELABLE` in `kernel_ipi.h`, so `Exec_CancelSignalIPIs` has no PC body; `RemTask` calls it before `CleanupETask` and freeing `tc_MemEntry` (`rom/exec/signal.c:93-107`; `remtask.c:109-128,165-181`). This reconfirms the conditional stale-task callback path already recorded in EK832; queue timing was not run.

Exec EK862 managed-pool implementation recheck: a repository-wide allocator-table search found TLSF as the selected managed pool backend and confirmed it initializes both `mhe_Alloc` and `mhe_AllocVec`. ReAction class readers do not hold a library open reference, and list locking protects lookup only; local `Forbid` does not pin the owner across CPUs. This establishes a conditional selected lifetime race. Actual overlap and class-loader teardown ordering remain unverified; source-only.

EK875 test-coverage recheck: the selected debug `smpsem` phase 3 (`developer/debug/test/smp/smpsem.c:459-555`; target in `developer/debug/test/smp/mmakefile.src:31`) runs three finite shared-reader loops alongside a finite exclusive-writer loop and checks that readers never observe torn/odd values. It does not measure or assert bounded writer wait, and all participants eventually terminate by exhausting fixed iteration counts. The explicit `semaphoretest` shared-bid producer is also selected only in the debug test target. These tests cover mutual exclusion and shared grant operation but do not resolve sustained-reader writer progress; EK875 remains a conditional medium-confidence fairness candidate because the public contract does not specify a policy. No test was executed.
EK9099 local-preemption boundary recheck: `OpenDevice` acquires `DeviceList` read lock together with `Forbid`, drops only the list lock before invoking the Open vector, and calls `Permit` only after that vector returns (`rom/exec/opendevice.c:92-114,130-135`). This excludes a single-CPU task-switch interleaving from lookup to Open dispatch; the documented stale-pointer route requires another CPU to expunge/free the device after the read lock is released, because `RemDevice`'s `Forbid` is processor-local (`rom/exec/remdevice.c:65-81`; `forbid.c:58-60`). The selected PL2303/Poseidon lifecycle remains the caller path on ExecSMP. No open/removal overlap was run.
