EK604. **A concurrent first use of a statically initialized condition variable can traverse its uninitialized waiter list (conditional null dereference; high source confidence).** Static `PTHREAD_COND_INITIALIZER` sets the embedded semaphore and waiter-list pointers to their null sentinels (`compiler/pthread/pthread.h:345-347`). Lazy initialization checks `SemaphoreIsInvalid`, then calls `pthread_cond_init` from both `_pthread_cond_timedwait` and `_pthread_cond_broadcast` (`pthread_cond_timedwait.c:44-45`; `pthread_cond_broadcast.c:35-37`). `pthread_cond_init` calls `InitSemaphore` before `NEWLIST(&cond->waiters)` (`pthread_cond_init.c:39-40`). Exec `InitSemaphore` writes `NT_SIGNALSEM` at the end of its initial wait-queue setup (`rom/exec/initsemaphore.c:49-55`), and `SemaphoreIsInvalid` treats that marker plus a null wait-queue tail as valid (`pthread.c:51-56`). Thus there is an interval after the semaphore becomes valid but before the condition's waiter list is initialized. A concurrent `pthread_cond_signal`/`broadcast` can skip lazy initialization and walk `cond->waiters`; `ForeachNode` immediately reads `node->ln_Succ` from the list head (`pthread_cond_broadcast.c:39-45`; `compiler/include/exec/lists.h:195-200`), which is null for the static initializer and can fault. Concurrent initializers can also overwrite each other's semaphore/list state. The trigger is concurrent first use of a statically initialized condition object; POSIX permits static initialization and does not require `pthread_cond_signal` to be called with the associated mutex held. Serialize lazy initialization with a state that is published only after both fields are ready. No concurrent first-use interleaving was run; source-only.


AArch64 affinity-mask ownership failure follow-up (EK8790): traced the caller-allocated idle-task mask through `Exec_ARMCPUInit`, `NewAddTask`, `PrepareContext`, and `CleanupETask`. Both `NewAllocEntry` failure and failed `KrnCreateContext` precede `TASKTAG_AFFINITY` adoption; task cleanup frees ETask-owned state only, while the selected callers lose the separate mask. Rechecked the same boundary in x86-64 `Processor_Init`, where a failed task creation frees the task parameter MemList but not the separate affinity mask. The coverage ledger previously referenced an absent EK304 heading; those references now point to the restored detailed EK8790 entry. No allocation failure was run.

EK8790 TASKTAG_AFFINITY producer census: source-wide search found allocated masks passed to NewCreateTask in the selected PC processor query/idle-task creators and Raspberry Pi ARM32/AArch64 processor/idle-task creators; those are enumerated in EK8790 and their file rows. The selected Exec housekeeper and ACPI button pass the `TASKAFFINITY_ANY` sentinel, not an allocated mask. USB2OTG passes an affinity pointer embedded in its pooled unit and its separate expunge/ownership failure remains OD2422. The remaining direct mask-tag callsites are developer SMP tests. `arch/riscv-native/exec/platform_init.c` contains a guarded affinity expression, but the OpenSBI configure branch does not define `__AROSEXEC_SMP__`; the SiFive U image also has the separate pre-handoff stall EK195, so that expression is not credited as a current selected caller. No other selected caller that allocates a caller-owned mask and can lose it before `PrepareContext` adoption was established.

Exec log.resource rollback recheck (EK8782; duplicate EK8797 withdrawn): distinguished `NewCreateTaskA` failure before its port-output assignment from the late `NewAddTask` failure covered by EK06. `rom/log/log.c` registers its embedded low-memory handler before task creation; early task-allocation or output-port signal-allocation failure leaves `lrb_ServicePort` zero, causing `libInit` to return FALSE, but does not unlink the handler. Generated `InitLib` frees the resource base after `_set_libinit` fails, while `checkMemHandlers` later traverses and calls embedded nodes. The x86-64 PC and OpenSBI boot aggregates select `kernel-log`. No failure was induced.


Pthread cancellation-disabled path reconciliation (2026-10-11): restored EK572 after tracing the exact Exec signal mask semantics. `pthread_cancel` sets the pending flag and signals CTRL-C even when disabled; direct `pthread_testcancel` then calls `SetSignal(SIGBREAKF_CTRL_C, 0)`, which is a no-op because `signalSet` is zero. If no Wait has consumed the wake first, a later Exec Wait including CTRL-C returns immediately. The selected condition-wait path consumes the signal in its own Wait, so repeated condition-wait spinning is not claimed. No matching in-tree mixed-API caller was found; no threads or waits were run.


Reply publication follow-through (2026-10-11): reread `ReplyMsg`, `InternalPutMsg`, `CheckIO`, `WaitIO`, `DoIO`, and `DeleteMsgPort` with the selected input.device and Intuition callers. Confirmed that `SetPrefs` uses `DoIO` then frees its temporary reply port, while the input worker completes the matching queued timing commands through `ReplyMsg`; the SMP type-to-link interval can therefore outlive the port after `WaitIO` returns (EK8799). Exact platform/component selection beyond the x86-64 PC SMP configuration remains to reconcile. No runtime test.

Signal-mask expression and compiler-branch census (EK8800): searched `rom/exec` and `compiler/pthread` for signal-bit shifts. The selected signed-`int` sites are `putmsg.c`, `waitport.c`, `waitio.c`, `freesignal.c`, `pthread_cond_timedwait.c` and `pthread_cond_broadcast.c`, already covered by EK8800. `doresetcallbacks.c` and `exec_util.c` use `1UL`, so their shifts do not add this signed-shift case. The additional `pthread.c:297` expression is inside `#if defined(__AMIGA__) && !defined(__MORPHOS__)`; the AROS Clang target patch explicitly leaves `__AMIGA__` undefined (`tools/crosstools/llvm/clang-23.1.0.src-aros.diff:97-106`, noting AROS GCC also does not define it), so that manual Procure branch is excluded from AROS. No signal bit exhaustion or wait was exercised.

Reset-callback removable-owner recheck (EK59): traced the RISC-V OpenSBI DesignWare unit owner through registration (`SerialUnitClass.c:204-208`) and final `serial.device` close (`workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:233-257`), which disposes the HIDD unit; its destructor calls `RemResetCallback` before superclass disposal (`SerialUnitClass.c:237-263`). This is another concrete removable callback owner while the non-supervisor reset launcher waits and other tasks can run. Qualification: OpenSBI's BSP package selects `dwuart` but does not list `serial.device` in `BSP_DEVS`; the serial.device path requires the optional Workbench device package, so this does not claim the default kickstart contains that caller. EK59 already covers the generic saved-next race; no separate Exec finding is added. No close/reset overlap was run.

Shared-semaphore writer-progress recheck (EK875): reread `InternalObtainSemaphore`, `InternalAttemptSemaphore`, `ReleaseSemaphore`, `Procure`, and the public `ObtainSemaphoreShared` contract. The implementation admits later readers while `ss_Owner == NULL` even with an exclusive waiter queued, and release grants every queued shared request when the first waiter is shared; the public contract still states no writer-preference/fairness guarantee. The selected `LockDosList` read/write callers remain possible readers/writer but no sustained selected reader stream or bounded-wait contract was established. Retire EK875 as an unsupported fairness concern; do not present it as a defect without an API progress guarantee or sustained caller evidence. No scheduling was run.

POSIX wait scope recheck (2026-10-11): traced `waitpid(pid, ...)` through the live/exited `ChildStatus` scans and its pre-wait rejection. A PID that does not name one of the caller’s children returns `ECHILD`; no specific-PID hang is included in EK476. The childless any-child `wait()` and `waitpid(-1)` behavior remains as reported. No child task or wait call was run.

Null IRQ-removal caller recheck (EK815 / OD2266): compared the two i8042 keyboard and mouse construction failure paths. The keyboard publishes its object without checking `data->irq` and its own Dispose forwards the null token to `KrnRemIRQHandler` (OD2266). The PS/2 mouse constructor does check `data->irq`; on failure it explicitly calls the superclass Dispose rather than its own null-unsafe disposer and returns NULL (`arch/all-pc/hidds/i8042/i8042_mouseclass.c:57-88`). No additional mouse candidate is established. This narrows the defect to the keyboard path; no allocation failure or HIDD construction was run.

SuperState/UserState selected-override reconciliation (2026-10-11): compared the paired bodies and available direct-caller traces across PC, ARM32, AArch64, PowerPC and RISC-V OpenSBI. PC's processor-frequency paths still call UserState without checking SuperState's documented NULL result (EK485); the ARM32 and AArch64 UserState overrides guard their stack-switch assembly with `if (superSP)`, so their matching processor probe callers do not inherit that null-stack consequence. Sam440/CHRP retain EK560: their UserState wrappers force the user bit after an already-supervisor public call. OpenSBI's override returns NULL because the selected target keeps execution in S-mode, with the common UserState fallback a no-op; no current transition defect is established. m68k assembly frame behavior is now source-traced in the follow-up below; external m68k callers and interrupt-stack headroom remain open, as do remaining platform overrides and future user-mode target models. No processor probe or privilege transition was run.


m68k SuperState/UserState frame-pair recheck (2026-10-11): verified the selected objects in `arch/m68k-all/exec/mmakefile.src:27`, the preserved A5 trampoline through `Supervisor`, the saved-SR origin test, and the complementary USP/supervisor-SP transfer and RTE. The m68k architecture-tree C-call census found no direct use; `Supervisor()` and the vector ABI remain public, so external clients and interrupt-depth limits are not closed by this pass. No additional candidate established; no target build or privilege transition was run.

OpenSBI `KrnGetCPUCount` caller census (EK657): rechecked every direct maintained C caller at the pinned tree. The API supplies a count/logical-index bound to processor.resource, NVMe queue/MSI sizing, Exec signal/affinity, task queries, and `KrnGetCPUAttr`; none feeds the raw boot-hart ID from `KrnGetCPUNumber` into those bounds. The FDT producer counts `cpu@` nodes and separately records the boot hart's logical position. EK657 is therefore retained as a public API contract mismatch with no direct checked-in consumer trigger established; external clients and firmware topology semantics remain open. No boot or CPU topology was exercised.

Low-memory handler callback/expunge recheck: followed selected LDDemon `LDFlush` through `RemLibrary` into diskfont expunge, which calls `RemMemHandler` while `checkMemHandlers` holds `LowMemSem`. This does not deadlock: `InternalObtainSemaphore` increments `ss_NestCount` when `ss_Owner == ThisTask` (`rom/exec/semaphores.c:91-98`), and `RemMemHandler` unlinks diskfont before releasing its nested acquisition. Because diskfont has higher priority and has already been visited when LDDemon removes it, the current LDDemon iteration does not retain a cursor to the removed node; a `MEM_TRY_AGAIN` return also leaves `cmhs_CurNode` at LDDemon for the retry. Diskfont's `MEM_ALL_DONE` handling remains unpromoted: the checked-in header does not say that this status requests another allocation attempt, and no separate Exec candidate is established. No expunge or allocation failure was run.


Console completion task-lifetime caller recheck (EK699): proved a supported CreateNewProc sequence instead of relying on C:Run: pass the same interactive console handle for NP_Input and NP_Output and set NP_CloseInput/NP_CloseOutput FALSE to preserve it after child exit (`rom/dos/createnewproc.c:126-130,334-352,434-462,913-925`). The child write stores its task pointer in the shared console filehandle; after that child exits, the surviving caller can invoke Tab/Shift-Tab on the same handle, reaching InitCompletion and the stale `lastwritetask` reads. C:Run remains explicitly unproven as the in-tree reproducer because its cloned output path does not establish that the parent input uses the identical filehandle. No process or completion interaction was run.


Pthread cleanup-push caller recheck (EK8805): a checkout-wide direct-call search found only `pthread_once` registering `OnceCleanup` (`compiler/pthread/pthread.c:999`). That callback unlocks the once spinlock; the selected in-tree `_Init_Semaphore` initializer only calls `InitSemaphore` and `NEWLIST`, then returns (`semaphore.c:49-55`), so it does not demonstrate an exit/cancellation while that registration is absent. The silent registration failure remains a public API defect for external pthread clients whose cleanup callback is required after cancellation/exit, but lock stranding is not claimed for the selected semaphore initialization route. No allocation failure or cancellation was run.


Pthread cleanup stack pairing recheck (EK8805): verified a nested-handler consequence in addition to the omitted inner callback. If an outer CleanupHandler is linked, `pthread_cleanup_push` returns on inner `malloc` failure without changing the list (`pthread.c:1160-1182`); the paired `pthread_cleanup_pop` unconditionally `RemTail`s and frees the current tail (`:1184-1199`), which is the outer record. `execute == FALSE` silently discards that outer cleanup; `execute == TRUE` invokes it at the inner pop point. This is a public-client trigger for cleanup-stack corruption under allocation failure. No nested cleanup sequence or allocation failure was run.


AArch64 DMA cache-line ownership recheck (EK8816): traced CachePreDMA/PostDMA through NVMe PRP setup, segment bookkeeping and completion into the AArch64 64-byte `dc civac` implementation; the device checks transfer offset/length alignment but not caller-buffer alignment. Raspberry Pi packaging selects NVMe and RP1 documents non-coherent DMA. A source census found no checked-in NVMe data-I/O client (InstallAROS has only a default device-name string), so the partial-edge plus concurrent neighboring-write corruption remains a conditional public-client finding, not an established in-tree workload. No transfer or concurrent write was run. Other callers and per-CPU cache-line geometry remain open.


Log-provider finalizer recheck (EK8817): followed the selected serial logger from successful `logInitialise` through `logAddListener` failure to `logFinalise`; the matching-provider branch is an empty TODO and retains its pool/record on the live resource. The no-op finalizer reference was corrected from the unrelated EK8766 processor finding to EK8817. No allocation failure or worker exit was run.

Low-memory-handler self-removal recheck (EK8818): verified the self-removal allowance in `checkMemHandlers`, recursive `LowMemSem` ownership (`rom/exec/semaphores.c:91-112`), the early `MEM_TRY_AGAIN` return before cursor advancement, and `AllocMem` reusing the unchanged state on another failed attempt. The selected diskfont, log.resource and LDDemon callbacks do not demonstrate the trigger, so the finding remains conditional for API clients; no allocation retry was run.

EK8798 caller-lifetime recheck: traced C:TaskList from NextTaskEntry through its immediate QueryTaskTagList and subsequent task-field reads. QueryTaskTagList obtains GetIntETask(task) before tag processing; GetIntETask dereferences the returned Task. Exec RemTask can free the task MemEntry chain while task.resource retains only the list node. This confirms the selected command has a direct stale-task dereference path; no task removal was run.

EK629 selected PC VBlank recheck: confirmed that `handleMicroHZ` calls the selected `INTB_VERTB` vector when the emulated VBlank request expires (`rom/timer/lowlevel.c:286-305`); the configured PC timer defines `USE_VBLANK_EMU` and drives `handleMicroHZ` from its IRQ 0 handler (`arch/all-pc/timer/make.opts:1-2`; `arch/all-pc/timer/timer_init.c:34-56`). `VBlankServer` chains to the generic unlocked `IntServer` (`arch/all-pc/exec/intserver_vblank.c:20-72`), whose `ForeachNode` reads the current node's successor after callback return (`rom/exec/intservers.c:29-45`; `compiler/include/exec/lists.h:195-200`). The realtime callback dereferences its base to fetch `rtb_PulseTask`, and the node is embedded in that base; expunge removes it but does not drain active callbacks before generated code frees the base (`workbench/libs/realtime/realtime_timer.c:22-30,65-83`; `workbench/libs/realtime/realtime_init.c:52-61`; `tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1558-1587`). `Forbid` is documented CPU-local on ExecSMP (`rom/exec/forbid.c:58-60`). This confirms EK629's selected path and lifetime premise; no new finding or runtime reproduction.
EK629 lifetime extension: the generated expunge sequence frees the library base immediately after the hook (`tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1558-1587`); realtime's hook only signals its worker (`realtime_timer.c:78-83`). The selected `Pulse` task can be executing outside `Wait` while dereferencing the base and traversing its conductor/player state (`pulse.c:36,46-57,67-78,119-159`), with no join/termination wait in the library. This is an additional owner-lifetime consequence within EK629, not counted as a separate ID. No task scheduling or expunge was run.
EK629 build-selection cross-check: `workbench/libs/mmakefile`'s aggregate library target includes `workbench-libs-realtime` (and its include target), while `workbench/libs/realtime/mmakefile.src` builds the base, timer, and Pulse sources into the library. Thus the concrete teardown owner is part of the selected Workbench library aggregate (`workbench/libs/mmakefile:52,111`; `workbench/libs/realtime/mmakefile.src:4-26`).

2026-10-11 report-detail integrity recheck: restored missing detailed entries EK117, EK144, EK462, EK665, EK666 and EK768 from their existing source-trace ledger evidence. EK144 is qualified to an empty/malformed boot resident range; EK768 remains dependent on a nonzero OpenSBI FDT timebase below 100 Hz, with no supported board input found. Revalidated generated BOOPSI defaulting for EK736 and updated its standalone report entry. This reconciles those named claims only; broad generated-output and caller coverage remains incomplete.

AArch64 sibling check for EK8808: compared both selected Raspberry Pi mailbox implementations and traced every AArch64 `vcmb_read` call. AArch64 returns `NULL` immediately on FIFO timeout and every direct caller checks it before dereference; framebuffer callers abort setup, memory setup skips that mapping, clock setup returns, and UART setup uses its fallback clock. No parallel AArch64 hang or unchecked-null finding was established. This does not change EK8808, which remains limited to the ARM32 implementation. No firmware or board was run.

Raspberry Pi BSS tracker recheck (EK8812, 2026-10-11): verified `MAX_BSS_SECTIONS == 256` against the producer and consumer. Each nonempty `SHT_NOBITS` load writes an entry, increments the global cursor, and immediately writes a zero sentinel (`arch/arm-raspi/boot/elf.c:191-203`); `initAllocator` resets only placement cursors (`:135-140`). The boot path loads the embedded core and then one ELF or every package member without resetting the tracker (`arch/arm-raspi/boot/boot.c:606-658`), and passes the array in `KRN_KernelBss` (`:663-667`). The native ARM startup clears entries until the sentinel with no table bound (`arch/arm-native/kernel/kernel_startup.c:91-129`). Thus the 256th cumulative nonempty NOBITS section places the sentinel at `tracker[256]`, outside the array. EK8812 remains conditional on that combined section count; selected image counts, build output and runtime behavior were not checked. No additional finding established.


Raspberry Pi ELF rejection/status recheck (EK8822, 2026-10-11): confirmed `checkHeader` returns false for unsupported/malformed ELF headers, but `getElfSize` and `loadElf` each return 1 regardless (`arch/arm-raspi/boot/elf.c:19-78,84-123,425-485`). The selected boot sizing/loading callers ignore both results for the embedded core, standalone ELF and package members (`arch/arm-raspi/boot/boot.c:494-535,606-656`). The RasPi package manifest includes boot-critical resources, devices, handlers and HIDDs (`arch/arm-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:95-190`), so a rejected required member is silently absent while boot proceeds. This is distinct from EK8813's unchecked member-internal offsets: EK8822 is the rejected-header/no-failure-propagation path. Conditional on a rejected header; no packaged ELF or board was tested.


Raspberry Pi ARM32 zero-alignment reconciliation (EK801, 2026-10-11): consolidated this sibling path into existing EK801 rather than creating a duplicate ID. The AArch64 Raspberry Pi loader normalizes `sh_addralign == 0` to one in both sizing and placement (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/elf.c:160-163,224-230`), while ARM32 sizing rounds section size/region to zero and `load_hunk` rounds the destination pointer to zero, then copies or clears the section there (`arch/arm-raspi/boot/elf.c:97-117,154-203`). OpenSBI's separate consequence remains a checked allocation failure and package abort. Triggering generated zero-alignment allocatable sections remain unverified; no object was built or loaded.


Latest Exec/kernel recheck: closed the ARM/ARMEB alert-frame caller pass without adding a candidate. The ARM prologue stores `{fp,lr}` and sets fp to the saved LR slot; `UnwindFrame` returns the previous frame from fp[-1] and caller LR from fp[0]. Selected `PrepareContext` initializes r11 to zero, while TrapHandler captures r11 in alert context and `FormatAlertExtra` stops after the chain returns null. The ARMEB copy is byte-identical and selected by its target manifest. Corrupt-frame bounds, hardware exception-frame provenance and runtime alert rendering remain open; no alert was run.

AArch64 MMU concurrency follow-up (EK8824): `mmu_map_range`/`mmu_unmap_range` and `mmu_next` do not serialize page-table walks. Two calls that split the same existing L2 block can publish separate L3 tables and lose one caller's leaf when the parent descriptor is overwritten. AArch64 Raspi supports ExecSMP; direct PCI BAR/DMA callers were checked, but no selected in-tree overlapping invocation was established. External concurrent callers remain a conditional trigger; no mapping ran.


Exec/kernel genmodule output-finalization pass (EK8825): enumerated every command branch used by `%build_module` and traced its writer closes. FILES, INCLUDES, LIBDEFS, MAKEFILE and WRITEFD output paths have writers that ignore `fclose` results; `writefd`, `writemakefile`, `writelinkentries` and `writeinclibdefs` check `ferror` before close only, which cannot report errors first surfaced during final flush. The separately dispatched `WRITEFUNCLIST` writer has the same close gap but was not found on the selected `%build_module` path and is not included in EK8825. Several remaining selected writers do not check stream errors at all, and `writeincclib` relies on process-exit stdio cleanup without observing failure. The `%build_module_core` FD rule is selected for ABI modules, including Exec and kernel (`config/make.tmpl:2484-2492`; `genmodule.c:70-75`). This extends EK8825 to incomplete public `_lib.fd` output without a new candidate because the unchecked finalization mechanism is the same. No filesystem error was induced and no module was built.

EK8825 report/index integrity reconciliation (2026-10-27): the intact ledger contained the source and caller trace for this finding, but the recovered detailed report and master index had no EK8825 entry. log.resource stale low-memory-handler recheck (2026-10-12; EK8782, consequence tightened): traced `ADD2INITLIB` failure through generated `set_libinit` rollback and the resource-base free (`compiler/autoinit/functions.c:46-59`; `tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1156-1180`). `log_LowMemHandler` only returns `MEM_DID_NOTHING` and does not dereference its base argument (`rom/log/log.c:180-188`); the direct defect is the registered node remaining linked in Exec's low-memory list after that node is freed, with a later eligible retry reading list/callback fields from freed storage (`rom/exec/memory.c:1313-1347`). pthread_mutex_trylock selected-caller census (2026-10-12; no new candidate): repository-wide search found four in-tree call sites (`compiler/pthread/pthread.c:343,456`; `semaphore.c:182,309`). `pthread_mutex_timedlock`'s successful-try fallthrough and extra same-owner semaphore acquisition remain EK567. `pthread_barrier_destroy` and `sem_destroy` release one successful try-lock before destroying their guarded objects; `sem_getvalue` releases on success and its contended fallback's stale/unlocked `waiters_count` read remains the distinct EK623. The recursive mutex branch was checked against Exec `AttemptSemaphore`, which increments nesting for the current owner (`rom/exec/semaphores.c:164-205`); it does not fail merely because the task already owns the recursive semaphore. No additional selected caller defect was established; external pthread clients remain outside this call-site census.

SCSI timed-wait signal check (not promoted): inspected `rom/devs/scsi/waitto.c:23-50`, its timer-port creation in `timer.c:24-40`, and both in-tree callers (`scsi.c:956`; `lowlevel.c:157`). `scsi_WaitTO` also computes `1 << mp_SigBit`, so a bit-31 timer port would share EK8800’s signed-shift condition. The device is defined as the `kernel-scsi` module in `rom/devs/scsi/mmakefile.src`, but a source-manifest search found no platform `mmakefile.src` selecting `kernel-scsi`; therefore I have not added it as a selected configuration or expanded EK8800’s affected-scope claim. Selected `FreeSignal` caller follow-up (no new Exec finding): checked ARM native processor probe cleanup (`arch/arm-native/processor/processor_init.c:53-93`) and PC i8042 LED-worker failure cleanup (`arch/all-pc/hidds/i8042/i8042_kbdclass.c:175-223`). The ARM probe frees each successfully allocated signal in the same parent task after its wait; its unchecked child-creation path can leave the parent waiting forever and is already EK279. The i8042 fallback uses bit number `SIGBREAKB_CTRL_E` when `AllocSignal` fails, and early probe-failure cleanup calls `FreeSignal` on that fallback in the worker task itself just before it signals the parent and returns. Since signal allocation masks belong to each task and the worker is exiting, this does not establish a lasting reservation leak or cross-task signal release. The fallback bit/mask misuse and missed LED updates are already OD2336. Source-only.


Reset-callback selected-driver caller check (no new Exec finding): checked framebuffer HIDD registration/removal (`arch/aarch64-raspi/hidd/fbgfx/fbgfx_hiddclass.c:77-103`), Rhine failure cleanup (`workbench/devs/networks/rhine/pci.c:248-280,311-329`), and NVMe/VirtIO controller registration and Dispose (`rom/devs/nvme/nvme_controllerclass.c:459-466,538-562,582-590`; `rom/devs/virtio/virtio_controllerclass.c:139-171`). The framebuffer HIDD pairs registration with `RemResetCallback`; Rhine sets `UNITF_RESETADDED` only after successful registration and removes it on unit cleanup. NVMe and VirtIO do not unlink their embedded reset-handler nodes in Dispose; generic `HW_RemoveDriver` disposes registered driver objects (`rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c:266-300`), matching the already recorded conditional stale-node finding OD2372. NVMe explicitly reports bus removal unsupported and no in-tree NVMe removal caller was found, so no stronger normal-configuration trigger is claimed here. The shared reset-list mutation/concurrency issue remains EK59. Source-only.
WaitIO SMP reply-queue synchronization recheck (EK8819 reaffirmed): reread `WaitIO`, `ReplyMsg`, `InternalPutMsg`, `GetMsg`, and `Remove`. `ReplyMsg` changes `ln_Type` to `NT_REPLYMSG` before taking the reply-port lock inside `InternalPutMsg` (`rom/exec/replymsg.c:52-64`); producers then serialize `AddTail` under `mp_SpinLock` (`putmsg.c:71-92`). `WaitIO` can observe that type and call `Remove` under only local `Disable()` (`waitio.c:57-77`), while `Remove` directly rewrites adjacent links without acquiring the port lock (`remove.c:51-65`). The documented `Disable` contract explicitly says it is CPU-local on ExecSMP and requires a spinlock for parallel shared data (`disable.c:58-61`). This confirms the missing same-port lock and also exposes the publication interval where the request is marked replied before its queue links are inserted. EK8819 remains supported for ExecSMP; no runtime interleaving was run. Caller focus in the report remains appropriate: this requires another producer concurrently using the request's reply port.
EK8819 maintained shared-port caller validation (2026-10-12): traced the non-m68k audio.device selected by `workbench/devs/audio/mmakefile.src:4-11`. Its slave creates a common AHI reply port and per-channel AHI requests (`audio_commands.c:789-805,980-999`), submits asynchronous requests per channel (`:315-355`), and `FlushUnit` aborts then WaitIOs one request while the AHI device task drains/completes requests on its own task (`:371-380,411-430,1926-1947`; `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/device.c:912-929`; `devcommands.c:256-292`). Multiple channels can be active on the same reply port; during a flush the AHI task can ReplyMsg another channel request while the audio slave's WaitIO removes its aborted request. This establishes a supported in-tree producer/consumer overlap for the unlocked removal finding on ExecSMP. Source-only; no task interleaving was induced.
Pthread EK8836 static-mutex race recheck (2026-10-12; confirmed with trigger boundary): reread both first-use entry points, validity predicate, initializer, Exec semaphore initialization and selected link-library manifest (`compiler/pthread/{pthread_mutex_lock.c:32-45,pthread_mutex_trylock.c:32-44,pthread_mutex_init.c:26-40,pthread.c:51-56,pthread.h:285-305,mmakefile.src:26-45}`; `rom/exec/initsemaphore.c:49-68`). The initializer's zero semaphore fails `SemaphoreIsInvalid`; either lock path calls `_pthread_mutex_init` without an atomic initialization state. Exec `InitSemaphore` rewrites wait-list links, owner, nesting and (on SMP) the spinlock. A thread paused after its invalidity test can therefore reset those fields after another first-use thread has initialized and acquired the mutex. The selected link-library vectors include both lock paths. The only checked-in `PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER` is Mesa's `g_memstream_lock`; a checkout-wide search found only the three lock calls inside its `u_memstream_*` definitions, no selected in-tree call to those functions. EK8836 remains valid for concurrent external pthread first-use; no in-tree concurrent trigger is claimed. No thread or mutex was run.
Pthread EK8836 detailed-report restoration (2026-10-25): restored the confirmed static-mutex first-use race to `AROS-exec-kernel.md` and its index. The report scopes callers to concurrent external use of the public static initializer; Mesa's in-tree mutex definition has no selected callers. No new trigger or runtime claim was added.
Pthread mutex ledger identifier reconciliation (2026-10-25): the mutex-init, mutex-trylock, unlock, and Mesa memstream rows contain legacy references to EK605 for the lazy static-mutex race; these references describe the same finding now reported as EK8836. EK605 remains only as the header-layout review label in the `pthread.h` row, not as a separate detailed finding. The detailed report and master index use EK8836 as the canonical finding ID.

PC syscall-handler AddTail startup-order follow-up (2026-10-12; no candidate promoted or withdrawn): traced the static handler insertions against syscall-gate installation and ACPI/Exec startup. The i386/x86-64 platform handlers are inserted before the syscall gate is installed; ACPI PM/APIC handlers are inserted by `kernel.post` during RTF_COLDSTART, after `acpi_Init` waits for `ACPICA_InitTask` to exit and before `smp_Initialize` starts APs (`arch/all-pc/kernel/platform_post.c:149-190`; `acpi.c:169-206`; `acpi_apic.c:247-260`; `acpi_pm.c:95-136`). This rules out an AP concurrent traversal during those registrations and narrows the remaining question to other runnable COLDSTART tasks on the BSP during the ACPI table-hook callbacks. The current source trace does not establish such a competing task, so the unlocked registration/dispatch remains an open lead rather than a numbered race. No syscall or interleaving was run.

KrnStatMemory aggregate caller census (2026-10-12; confirms existing qualification, no new race): repeated an exact C/header call search and read the complete selected `KrnStatMemoryA` implementation against `AddMemList`. The only production call is Exec startup's `KMS_PageSize` query, which returns before traversing `SysBase->MemList`; the only other checked-in C caller is the developer allocator test, also requesting only `KMS_PageSize` (`rom/exec/addresource.c:83-99`; `developer/debug/test/kernel/allocator.c:113`). Aggregate tags do traverse without `MemListSpinLock`/`MemListSem`, while `AddMemList` inserts under `MEM_LOCK`, but no checked-in selected aggregate-query producer exists. Do not promote this as a selected in-tree race absent such a caller; external API clients and simultaneous memory-header insertion remain open. EK639 remains the distinct startup condition where zero `kb_PageSize` causes FALSE without writing the output. Source-only; no query/mutation concurrency was run.

AddIntServer kernel-IRQ bridge recheck (2026-10-12; confirms EK795/EK815, no duplicate wrapper finding): read the complete selected kernel-vector branches of `AddIntServer`/`RemIntServer` and rechecked their central contract against `KrnAddIRQHandler`/`KrnRemIRQHandler` (`rom/exec/addintserver.c:62-75`; `remintserver.c:51-63`). AddIntServer is void and stores the potentially NULL kernel token in the interrupt node's `ln_Succ`; it provides no registration status to callers. The selected trackdisk IRQ-0 allocation-failure path is already the device-startup hang EK795 (`rom/devs/trackdisk/trackdisk_device.c:242-276`; `trackdisk_hw.c:141-159,234-244`). Null-token removal through RemIntServer is part of EK815, with xHCI and PC serial/timer examples already cross-linked to their driver findings. Ordinary Amiga hardware-vector calls take the separate IntrList path. No independent wrapper defect beyond those caller consequences established; other registered callers' local handling and external callers remain open. Source-only; no IRQ registration was induced.


KrnStatMemory aggregate caller/reachability recheck (2026-10-12; no candidate promoted): searched all maintained C call expressions and confirmed that selected production Exec asks only for `KMS_PageSize` (`rom/exec/addresource.c:89`), which returns before MemList traversal; the only other checked C call is in the excluded kernel allocator test. `AddMemList` initializes a new header before taking `MEM_LOCK` and inserting it with `Enqueue` (`rom/exec/addmemlist.c:78-101`); on SMP that lock is the MemList write spinlock, while `KrnStatMemoryA`'s aggregate traversal does not take the matching read lock (`rom/exec/memory.h:14-17`; `rom/kernel/statmemory.c:103-120`). Since no selected production aggregate-query caller or explicit snapshot-consistency guarantee was found, the possible concurrent approximate/inconsistent aggregate result remains a public external-caller question, not a promoted finding. No concurrent query or insertion was run.


Raspberry Pi CPU-load sample race caller recheck (2026-10-12; EK8843 retained with external-overlap qualification): traced both selected SysMon consumers. Gauge and graph updates iterate core indices and call `GetCoreInfo` synchronously (`workbench/system/SysMon/processor_gauge.c:120-149`; `processor_graph.c:267-301`); the processor page invokes that update from its normal information refresh (`processor.c:90-124`). No second selected call is launched asynchronously from either loop, so a single SysMon update does not itself establish overlapping same-core queries. The legacy kernel vector remains directly callable, and separate tasks on separate ExecSMP cores can still overlap its shared per-core baseline read/modify/write; the existing candidate is therefore retained only for that concurrent-client trigger. No concurrent caller was run.

AArch64 Raspberry Pi BSS-tracker contrast (EK8812 follow-up, 2026-10-12): checked `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/elf.c:257-267` against the shared 256-entry tracker and boot’s cumulative package loading. Before appending a nonempty NOBITS section, AArch64 rejects a cursor at index 255 or greater; this leaves index 255 available for the zero sentinel after at most 255 entries. This prevents the ARM32 sibling’s sentinel write beyond `tracker[255]`; no AArch64 duplicate finding is credited. Source-only; no package was loaded.

AArch64 Raspberry Pi package-writer contract follow-up (no new finding): compared the selected `kernel-package-raspi-aarch64` edge in `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:229` and `%make_package` expansion (`config/make.tmpl:3750-3800`) with `tools/package/pkg:78-96,175-231` and `tools/package/FORMAT`. The writer emits a big-endian total size followed by padded NUL-terminated path records and exact built module bytes; the boot cursor advance `len + 5` matches the writer's stored path-length convention. The unpacker checks declared package/member bounds, but the bootstrap does not call that unpacker and still omits equivalent checks against firmware `pkg_size` (EK723). The selected build package inputs are generated module outputs; no independent package-format mismatch was found. ELF member-internal offsets remain unchecked by the bootstrap and no malformed compiler output was established. No package or image was built or loaded.

Task.resource/SysMon lifetime reconciliation (2026-10-12): expanded EK8798 with SysMon's default-build selected-task detail window path. Refresh can destroy the row without clearing `tld_TaskSelected`, and the timer calls `TaskViewUpdate` after releasing the task-list lock. With the same unpinned task pointer root already covered by EK8798, Graphics candidate GD2975 was withdrawn as a duplicate; GD1218 is restored as the debug.library leak finding; GD1219 and GD2975 are consolidated into EK8798. AArch64 GIC-400 IPI consumer reconciliation (2026-10-12; no new finding): traced all selected ARMI_SendIPI callsites through the Pi 4/Pi 5 GIC SGI backend and shared handle_ipi (arch/aarch64-native/kernel/gic400.c:74-119; kernel_ipi.c:115-138,186-258,273-314; schedulecpu.c:22-39; kernel_cpu.h:74-88). The receiver atomically exchanges each per-(target,source) message bitmap and dispatches its bits. Scheduling consumes no payload; IPI_CALL_HOOK drains its own per-target queue, and the remaining selected message bits only set/log state. Thus a newer is_Data may accompany a coalesced/older bitmap, but no selected consumer uses that word for functional arguments. CPU IDs and masks come from the four-core AArch64 topology and the selected affinity sentinels; no selected out-of-range target path established. Hardware target-list behavior and GIC mapping remain pending; no interrupt was sent.

OpenSBI CPU-load recheck (EK665-EK666): traced `KrnGetCPUAttr(KATTR_CPULoad)` to the saved per-hart `hd_Load` or boot-hart `__cpu_load` (`getcpuattr.c:28-47`). With the selected permanent idle task, `cpu_Dispatch` does not accumulate its `wfi` interval, so `slept` remains zero in ordinary windows. The sampler computes `2^32` then narrows to zero; therefore utilization can read zero during both idle and busy periods. EK665 and EK666 remain distinct: counting idle-task sleep restores partial-load meaning, while the full-busy case still requires fixing the independent narrowing. No load was measured.

Genmodule autoinit branch-selection follow-up (EK8825, no new candidate): traced `FILES` dispatch through `genmodule.c:15-23` and `writeautoinit.c:15-71` against `rom/exec/exec.conf`, `rom/utility/utility.conf`, and `rom/oop/oop.conf` plus their selected `%build_module` rules. Exec uses its handwritten autoinit; selected utility and OOP libraries take default autoinit and `rellinklib`, selecting both normal and relative symbol-set outputs. The writer ignores the final `fclose` result, so a close-time flush failure is part of EK8825 and can leave generated library/forced-base imports incomplete while genmodule reports success. No separate finding: same unchecked output-finalization mechanism. Generated files were not built or faulted.
Alert subsystem table bounds follow-up (EK65, 2026-10-12): documented generic `Alert_GetString` indexing for 0x44–0x7f and the native m68k hook indexing for 0x43–0x7f, including the ineffective UBYTE `< 0x80` check. Checked public `AN_*` constants end at `AN_Hidd` 0x42; no ordinary in-tree out-of-range producer was established, so trigger remains conditional on malformed/custom/future alert data. Added detailed EK65; no runtime alert was generated.
Alert formatter caller follow-up (2026-10-12): direct C call graph confirmed `FormatAlert` is invoked by `Exec_UserAlert` and `Alert_DisplayKrnAlert`; the latter serves the supervisor/system path, including the double-fault route (`rom/exec/useralert.c:88-105`; `rom/exec/systemalert.c:14-30,39-75`). Both flow through `Alert_GetString`; no index validation is added at the wrapper. This confirms EK65 reaches both formatting paths, but the complete architecture-specific entrypoint and producer census remains open. No alert was generated.
Alert formatter selection follow-up (2026-10-12): generic `rom/kernel/fmtalertinfo.c` is in the default kernel function set (`rom/kernel/mmakefile.src:45-54`); `arch/all-pc/kernel/mmakefile.src:23-30` selects the PC override; native m68k Amiga boot links `kernel-alerthook-kobj` (`arch/m68k-amiga/boot/mmakefile.src:7-13`), whose module compiles `rom/alerthook/alerthook.c` (`rom/alerthook/mmakefile.src:6-10`). `FormatAlert` reaches `KrnFmtAlertInfo` through `FormatTask`, so EK65’s generic bounds affect generic and PC formatter paths, while the native hook has its separate smaller bounds. Other target alert presentation and exhaustive producers remain open; source selection only, no builds.
EK8796 recheck (2026-10-12): repository-wide `DBFF_DISASSEMBLE` setter search found only the i386 and RISC-V debug initializers (`arch/i386-all/debug/debug_platform.c:55-60`; `arch/riscv-all/debug/debug_platform.c:12-17`); OpenSBI selects the RISC-V `debug` library (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/boot/mmakefile.src:99`). Both direct `FormatAlertExtra` callers were traced: system display receives NULL after `Exec_ExtAlert` clears AT_NONE data (`rom/exec/alert.c:162-164`; `systemalert.c:19-30`), while the user More path passes the ETask alert-data union even for AT_NONE (`useralert.c:116-122`). Thus the existing EK8796 consequences are confirmed for the gated disassembly path; no alert was raised.

MinGW host IRQ wait-count follow-up (EK101, 2026-10-12): traced the `Ints_Num` high-water update from the 256-slot allocator into `WaitForMultipleObjects` and its unchecked result-to-`PendingInts` index. After the two reserved timers, 63 simultaneous dynamic allocations raise the wait count to 65, beyond the Windows API's 64-handle limit. The maintained direct clients allocate six dynamic IRQs in total, so the trigger is external or future integration scope rather than established default-image behavior. Added detailed EK101; no Windows run. Host concurrency and other Windows contracts remain open.

Hosted Unix `KrnCause`/software-signal recheck (2026-10-12; no new candidate): traced generic `KrnCause` through `SIGUSR2`, the selected `sigaction` setup and `core_IRQ` (`arch/all-unix/kernel/cause.c:12-21`; `kernel.c:298-324`; `kernel_intr.c:30-50`). `SIGUSR2` intentionally enters `core_IRQ`/`core_ExitInterrupt` to run pending Exec soft interrupts and scheduler work; `SIGUSR1` is separately registered to `core_SysCall`, which interprets task state for switch/schedule/dispatch (`kernel.c:322-324,346-357`; `kernel_intr.c:58-107`). The checked Unix direct IRQ users use `SIGALRM`/`SIGIO`; no in-tree `SIGUSR2` handler registration was found. Unix signal coalescing, external use of reserved signals and full trap-context behavior remain open. Source-only; no signal was raised.

ExecSMP child-orphan/exit race recheck (EK8845; 2026-10-12): traced the public `RemTask` teardown into `CleanupETask` (`rom/exec/remtask.c:115-128`) and the separate public `ChildOrphan` path (`rom/exec/childorphan.c:88-104`). `Exec_CleanupETask` reads `et_Parent` and resolves its ETask before taking the child's `iet_TaskLock` (`rom/exec/exec_util.c:271-278`), while `ChildOrphan` protects the parent's child list and detaches the child under the parent's distinct `iet_TaskLock`. ExecSMP `Forbid` is processor-local (`rom/exec/forbid.c:58-60`), so it does not serialize these two public operations across CPUs. The cleanup later uses the cached parent and unconditionally removes the ETask (`exec_util.c:302-323`); this confirms the previously reported stale-parent/double-detach interleaving. A whole-tree C-call search still found no in-tree `ChildOrphan` caller, so reachability remains conditional on an external/public-vector client; no candidate change or runtime task schedule.


Reset callback support-task allocation trace (2026-10-12; EK675 promoted): confirmed `NewCreateTask` can return NULL and `Exec_DoResetCallbacks` skips the current callback when that happens. Selected PC registration priorities establish the concrete single-action reboot consequence: skipped -110 cold/warm performer falls through to the -128 power-off handler. No failure or reboot was run.


Condition-wait cancellation/timeout recheck (2026-10-12; EK802 confirmed, no duplicate): reread `_pthread_cond_timedwait` signal collection and result branch (`compiler/pthread/pthread_cond_timedwait.c:140-165`), `pthread_cancel`'s deferred request publication (`pthread_cancel.c:34-55`), and Exec `Wait`'s returned signal mask (`rom/exec/wait.c:75-80,128-141`). When timer expiry and CTRL-C cancellation are both collected, the timeout test returns before `pthread_testcancel`; this is the existing EK802 condition and it remains distinct from EK625's cancellation cleanup path after cancellation is acted upon. POSIX's cancellation-point wording was rechecked at the Open Group condition-wait specification. No timed wait or race was run.


Condition signal/broadcast handoff recheck (2026-10-12; existing findings confirmed, no new candidate): reread `pthread_cond_signal`, `_pthread_cond_broadcast`, and the timed-wait list insertion/removal (`compiler/pthread/pthread_cond_signal.c:26-31`; `pthread_cond_broadcast.c:26-56`; `pthread_cond_timedwait.c:124-150`). Waiters publish and unlink their stack node under `cond->semaphore`, and broadcast traverses under the same semaphore, preventing a concurrent ordinary unlink during traversal. `pthread_cond_signal` selects only the first node, while `sem_post` retains `sem->lock` through repeated signals; the selected multi-post case is already EK628. The static-condition lazy-init interleaving remains EK604, and allocated bit-31 mask shifting remains EK8800. No condition call or concurrent signal was run.

Cause()/soft-interrupt delivery recheck (2026-10-12; no new Exec finding): reread the selected Cause implementation, Exec Enable path, generic kernel interrupt exit and representative m68k-Amiga, i386-PC, x86-64-PC and all-Unix delivery hooks. Valid documented priorities -32,-16,0,16,32 map to indices 0..4; the source explicitly documents invalid priorities as caller error, and the selected `-128` input-handler registration remains a caller defect already qualified in this ledger. Amiga Causes hardware `INTF_SOFTINT` (`rom/exec/chipset.h:43-48`); non-Amiga `CUSTOM_CAUSE` is a no-op, with `SFF_SoftInt` checked from `Enable` (`rom/exec/enable.c:89-115`), generic interrupt return (`rom/kernel/kernel_intr.c:30-51`) and idle dispatch loops (representative i386/x86-64 `kernel_cpu.c`). `core_Cause` calls the installed Exec interrupt vector (`rom/kernel/kernel_intr.h:29-36`); the kernel manifest selects the generic cause routine and target hooks. This bounded route check found no lost-wakeup edge in the inspected code; remaining architecture-specific interrupt-return and SMP delivery paths stay open. No interrupt was raised.

ChildWait/SetSignal lost-wakeup recheck (EK811; 2026-10-12, no separate Wait/SetSignal finding): followed `SetSignal`'s masked update under `tc_SpinLock` (`rom/exec/setsignal.c:60-78`), `Signal`'s corresponding publication lock, and `Wait`'s locked received-bit test plus transition to `TS_WAIT` (`rom/exec/wait.c:69-113,122-138`). These primitives prevent a signal racing the actual Wait transition from being lost, but they cannot restore the child signal if `ChildWait` clears it after the child has already appended its ETask and signaled (`childwait.c:92-113`; `exec_util.c:314-328`). Thus EK811 remains specifically the queue-scan/clear ordering race; no independent signal-state defect is credited. Source-only, no wait was run.

CachePostDMA ARM-native target-selection follow-up (2026-10-12; early census, superseded in part by EK9346): confirmed `arch/arm-native/exec/mmakefile.src` selects the ARM PreDMA override but does not select a CachePostDMA override, leaving `rom/exec/cachepostdma.c`'s no-op selected on ARM-native. The direct maintained ARM-native C-call census found only mailbox calls to `CachePreDMA(..., DMA_ReadFromRAM)` (`mbox_init.c:52,195`), with no paired `CachePostDMA` call or selected device-to-memory user of the public hook. This early census did not include packaged Workbench callers; EK9346 now records the selected 32-bit BCMGENET caller under the explicit noncoherent-DMA condition; the selected usb2otg cache maintenance is direct `CacheClearE` and does not demonstrate dependence on CachePostDMA. No platform-wide coherence proof or runtime DMA case was established; keep the finding conditional and the target/client review open.
PC IRQ destination recheck for EK821 (2026-10-12; no new candidate): `IOAPICInt_EnableIRQ` selects `intrMap->im_CPU` when a mapping exists, otherwise starts from `KrnGetCPUNumber()`, then stores the selected CPU into a newly materialized mapping (`arch/all-pc/kernel/acpi_ioapic.c:546-592`). MADT interrupt-source overrides create mappings during ACPI parsing and initialize their CPU from the parsing CPU (`:842-874`); initial IOAPIC routing likewise uses CPU0 for an unmapped route (`:408-438`). The generic PC PCI driver's selected `AddInterrupt` forwards the caller's `INTLine` directly to `KrnAddIRQHandler`, which enables the route (`rom/hidds/pci/pcidriverclass.c:279-288`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/addirqhandler.c:79-103`). This supports the source-level possibility that distinct unmapped device IRQ lines first enabled by tasks running on different CPUs retain different APIC destinations. It does not establish that selected device startup is actually distributed across CPUs or that two dispatches overlap; EK821 remains conditional, with no additional candidate.

Low-memory handler callback walk follow-up (2026-10-12; no new candidate): `checkMemHandlers` saves the current node's successor before invoking the callback and holds `LowMemSem` across the walk (`rom/exec/memory.c:1321-1339`). Self-removal through `RemMemHandler` re-obtains that semaphore in the same task; `InternalObtainSemaphore` increments `ss_NestCount` for its current owner (`rom/exec/semaphores.c:93-113`), and the saved successor lets the walk continue after unlinking the current node. A callback returning `MEM_TRY_AGAIN` releases the semaphore before `AllocMem` retries (`memory.c:1341-1348`; `allocmem.c:113-116`). The selected diskfont, log.resource and LDDemon callbacks were already traced in the table; their return paths do not establish an additional iterator or self-removal defect. External callback contracts and actual memory-pressure interleavings remain unverified. Source-only.

Signal-bit-31 allocator and teardown recheck (2026-10-12; EK8800 retained, no separate candidate): reread the explicit and automatic allocation paths, message-port lifecycle, and wait/signal consumers. `AllocSignal` narrows to signed `BYTE`, but valid explicit 31 remains 31; automatic allocation can choose the highest free bit from the unsigned 32-bit allocation mask (`rom/exec/allocsignal.c:61-111`). `CreateMsgPort` accepts every result except -1 and stores the bit in the port (`rom/exec/createmsgport.c:51-67`), while `DeleteMsgPort` passes it to `FreeSignal` (`rom/exec/deletemsgport.c:48-55`). The selected `FreeSignal`, `WaitPort`, `WaitIO`, `PutMsg`, and `AllocTaskSignal` expressions use signed `1 << signalNum`/`1L << signalNum` forms (`freesignal.c:49-54`; `waitport.c:74-80`; `waitio.c:57-78`; `putmsg.c:101-106`; `allocsignal.c:103-111`). On 32-bit-int targets bit 31 is an undefined signed shift; this confirms the valid-input trigger, but the exact downstream mask depends on compiler behavior. The review found no direct literal `AllocSignal(31)` call previously, so the report correctly keeps this API-level and conditional. No signal was allocated and no wait or port lifecycle was exercised.


VMM exception-handler lifetime reconciliation: restored EK9906 as a detailed finding. `AllocAddressRange()` returns success in its AROS stub without assigning the range; later VMM setup passes the null base into page-table/range setup and the `vmm.library` path uses a null `VirtMem` header. EK275 is withdrawn as an active in-tree finding because this optional AROS VMM path does not establish a functioning runtime teardown/free-target case; external consumers of the preliminary kernel handler API remain open. No VMM path was run.

Caller census found only one explicit in-tree `OOP_RemoveClass` outside OOP internals: xHCI controller shutdown (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_controllerclass.c:607-612`); `rg` found no caller of that static shutdown helper in the selected xHCI tree, so it does not establish ordinary overlap. OOP_ParseAttrs candidate recheck (EK8855): confirmed `parseattrs.c` is selected through `rom/oop/mmakefile.src:16-21`; the parser returns an error for `numattrs > 32`, returns normally on TAG_DONE/TAG_MORE NULL, and advances for unmatched attrs and TAG_SKIP. The selected gfx pixel-format caller supplies its declared table count (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_init.c:61-71`); no checked-in malformed producer or mismatched caller was found. KrnCause architecture-dispatch follow-up (2026-10-12; no new candidate): expanded the `rom/kernel/cause.c` caller trace across the selected syscall routes. PC's `core_SysCallHandler` enters `core_SysCall` only for user-mode system calls (`arch/all-pc/kernel/syscall.c:41-76`), and generic `SC_CAUSE` reaches `core_ExitInterrupt`/pending-softint processing (`rom/kernel/kernel_intr.c:30-53,61-67`). ARM and AArch64 syscall handlers likewise gate default syscall dispatch on user/system mode (`arch/arm-native/kernel/syscall.c:236-246`; `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/syscall.c:291-301`). OpenSBI RISC-V routes only the outermost classified syscall trap into `core_SysCall` (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_traps.c:160-178,224-235`). Unix calls `core_ExitInterrupt` after its signal-based syscall path (`arch/all-unix/kernel/kernel_intr.c:71-106`); MinGW's `SC_CAUSE` branch does the same (`arch/all-mingw32/kernel/kernel_intr.c:125-127`). Efika marks `SC_CAUSE` for the exit handler, which runs the softint producer on user return (`arch/ppc-chrp/efika/kernel/syscall.c:50-57,111-114`; `scheduler.c:285-327`); Sam440 routes the syscall through the generic handler and uses a user-mode guard at its interrupt exit (`arch/ppc-sam440/kernel/syscall.c:159-161`; `kernel_intern.h:104-111`). The m68k Amiga override/no-op and chipset interrupt route remain as recorded in the existing row. No additional delivery defect established. Remaining architecture-specific syscall entries, external KrnCause callers and runtime interrupt delivery remain open; no syscall or soft interrupt was run.

VMM signal-allocation recheck (2026-10-12; EK8865 withdrawn): traced all manager, page-handler and prepager `AllocSignal` calls through the selected AROS task-creation callers. The manager is a fresh process with a process-port signal, three explicit signals and two additional message-port signals; workers are fresh tasks with three explicit signals and one message port. Each stays below the documented 16 allocatable bits, and no selected preallocation path exhausts the pool. The allocations remain unchecked but the earlier report's trigger was not established in the selected build, so no active candidate is retained. No signals were exhausted or tasks started.


Task.resource SMP late-prelaunch recheck (2026-10-12; EK8866 added): traced TaskLaunch ready publication and local interrupt re-enable against PC, ARM32 and AArch64 `core_Dispatch` ready-list selection and affinity filters, the patched task.resource RemTask wrapper, self-removal to ServiceTask, MemEntry freeing, later prelaunch insertion and NextTaskEntry state dereference. Confirmed that when another CPU is affinity-eligible, it can dispatch and finish the task before the creator calls TaskRes_PreLaunch, leaving a task-list entry with a freed task pointer. The SMP scheduling interleaving was not run.

Interrupt-controller definition/caller follow-up (2026-10-12; no new candidate): completed the selected PC call-site check for `krnGetInterruptController` and the adjacent IRQ identity fields in `kernel_interruptcontrollers.h`. `ictl_enable_irq`/`ictl_disable_irq` guard the lookup result, check optional callbacks and bound IRQ before taking `kb_Interrupts[irq]`; `cpu_intr` bounds IRQ before lookup and guards the controller before Ack/Enable access. Full-width `ic_Id` comparison is consistent with the documented warning that Exec `ln_Type` carries only its low byte. The earlier `kernel_interruptcontroller.c` trace covers registration and list publication; non-PC architecture implementations and external producers remain pending. No IRQ or controller was run.

AArch64 Raspberry Pi SMP allocation recheck (EK8868): checked every shared trampoline and per-secondary stack/TLS allocation against its immediate consumer. All three allocation results can reach unchecked copy, pointer indexing, field stores or cache flushes before core release. Conditional boot fault under memory pressure; no failure or boot was induced.

ARM32 BCM2836 SMP allocation recheck (EK8869): traced each per-core normal-stack, FIQ-stack and TLS allocation to trampoline publication and startup-lock handoff. Allocation results are unchecked; a missing TLS faults immediately and invalid stack setup can prevent the secondary unlocking the boot CPU's unbounded startup wait. No failure or boot was induced.

AArch64 PSCI secondary-start cleanup recheck (EK8870; reconciles stale EK620 ledger label): traced successful per-core stack/TLS allocations through PSCI CPU_ON's nonzero-return branch. That branch releases startup_lock and continues without freeing either block; no later owner recovers them. This handled-failure leak is distinct from EK8868, where allocation failure faults before startup. Conditional memory leak on firmware start refusal; no firmware response was exercised.

Exec ReplyMsg/WaitIO publication recheck (2026-10-13; EK8799 strengthened): confirmed the observable ordering against primitive implementations. `ReplyMsg` stores `NT_REPLYMSG` before calling `InternalPutMsg` (`rom/exec/replymsg.c:60-63`); `CheckIO` reads `ln_Type` with no lock (`rom/exec/checkio.c:48-59`); `WaitIO` may therefore skip waiting and call `Remove` (`waitio.c:57-76`). On ExecSMP, `InternalPutMsg` does not take the reply port spinlock until after the type store, and it links only later with `AddTail` (`putmsg.c:71-92`). `Remove` unconditionally writes through `ln_Pred` and `ln_Succ` and has no linked-membership check (`remove.c:51-64`). This supports EK8799's premature completion if a concurrent observer reaches WaitIO in the publication interval. The selected lan78xx/PoPo polling callers require a remote-CPU overlap with the timer interrupt; synchronous input.device/Intuition SetPrefs does not provide an early observer, as clarified in the later caller correction. No concurrent I/O was run. Source-only.

Disable/Enable nesting-width recheck (2026-10-13): compared the public matching-call contract with generic ExecBase, task, PC per-CPU, ARM/AArch64/RISC-V TLS counters, selected byte atomic operations, and m68k Amiga Disable/Enable assembly. The `BYTE` counter starts at -1; 129 outstanding disables wrap to -128 but still unwind without early enable, while 130 wrap to -127 and the first Enable reaches -128, which generic Enable and the Amiga assembly override treat as permission to enable interrupts. EK9385 records the deep public-call-chain trigger; no in-tree 130-deep caller or runtime test was established. Broader Disable/Enable caller and architecture review remains open.

Forbid/Permit nesting-width recheck (2026-10-13): compared the documented matching-call contract and task initialization with selected m68k assembly, PC, ARM/AArch64/RISC-V task-disable counter layouts and generic interrupt-exit scheduling gates. Confirmed the existing EK8827 beyond m68k: selected byte-counter paths wrap -1 to -128 after 129 outstanding Forbid calls, and a pending interrupt-exit switch can treat that negative value as enabled. Merged the platform scope into EK8827 rather than creating a duplicate finding. The PC SMP secondary-start uninitialized counter is separately EK8829. No in-tree 129-deep caller or runtime trigger was established. Source-only; wider caller audit remains open.

PC Processor_Init affinity-allocation recheck (2026-10-13; EK8766/EK8790): reread `Processor_Init`, selected PC `KrnAllocCPUMask`/`KrnGetCPUMask`, `core_APIC_GetMask`, x86-64 `PrepareContext`, and the PC scheduler. A failed affinity allocation does not dereference NULL: `core_APIC_GetMask` explicitly skips the write. The NULL tag is still adopted by the query task; the selected scheduler then confines it to CPU 0, supporting EK8766's wrong-CPU-record consequence for a secondary probe. If task construction fails before tag adoption, the allocated mask leak remains EK8790. The i386 PC build does not select ExecSMP, so this specific secondary-query trigger is x86-64 PC ExecSMP. No allocation failure or task execution was induced.

PC cpu_PrepareExec mask-allocation failure recheck (2026-10-13): reread the whole function against `Exec_InitETask`, PC APIC mask helpers, and scheduler affinity predicates. `SystemCPUMask` and masks assigned to the current/ready/wait tasks are not checked for allocation failure; `KrnGetCPUMask`/`core_APIC_GetMask` tolerate NULL, and the PC membership predicate treats NULL as boot-CPU-only. The inspected path therefore degrades those task masks to CPU-0-only and leaves the boot CPU eligible; this pass did not establish a distinct crash or task-loss candidate. AP bootstrap affinity creation has its own checked failure path, while the idle-task mask-allocation consequence is already covered by EK8835. No allocation failure or SMP boot was induced; other scheduler and affinity paths remain open.

PC AP shared-trampoline timeout recheck (EK8878, 2026-10-13): traced the single shared low-memory `SMPBootstrap` block from `smp_Setup` into each `smp_Wake` iteration, the release-build 50-second ready-lock timeout, x86-64 `smpbootstrap.s` argument loads, and `smp_Entry`'s later ready-lock release. A timed-out but still executing AP is not cancelled before the BSP overwrites `SP`/`Arg1`/`Arg2`/`Arg4` for the next CPU; if it has not yet loaded the arguments, it can enter with the next CPU's launch data. Added EK8878 as a medium-confidence hardware-timing candidate, limited to that delayed trampoline state; normal startup and APs that already loaded their arguments are not affected. No AP startup was run. This also narrows the earlier late-wake/trampoline question in the `smp.c` row; other late-AP and hardware timing behavior remains open.

PC KernelPost/SMP wake result recheck (2026-10-13; EK9400 strengthened): traced the integer result from `core_APIC_Wake` through `smp_Wake` and `KernelPost`. A per-CPU nonzero wake result is logged but does not abort the loop or change `smp_Wake`'s final return of 1; `KernelPost` therefore emits the full discovered `apic_count` as “cores online” after partial wake failure. The separate stack-allocation return of 0 suppresses that log but still leaves the count unchanged. This adds a directly observed misleading status message to EK9400's existing offline-affinity-target consequence; no additional ID. No APIC wake or failed allocation was induced.

PC AP bootstrap failure-unwind recheck (2026-10-13; EK822/EK9400 strengthened): traced `cpu_InitBootStrap` after successful `Exec_InitETask`. If its second `KrnAllocCPUMask` fails, the branch deletes the context and frees the task allocation but omits `Exec_CleanupETask`; the separate ETask allocation leaks, and any mask allocated by `Exec_InitETask` is already lost when the affinity field was overwritten. The caller `smp_Entry` logs the null bootstrap task but unconditionally unlocks the AP-ready lock before halting; the BSP sees the unlocked lock and accepts the AP as started. EK822 now states the additional failure-unwind leak, and EK9400 includes this false-online path. No allocation failure or SMP boot was induced.

Exec ETask ownership/affinity cross-check (2026-10-13; EK8820/EK822): reread `Exec_InitETask`, `Exec_CleanupETask`, and `NewAddTask`'s `PrepareContext` failure cleanup against selected PC, ARM32 and AArch64 null-mask scheduler rules. The common initialization path stores a NULL result and still returns success, supporting EK8820's inheritance/creator-core consequence; ordinary `NewAddTask` context failure does call `CleanupETask` and expunges the linked child ETask, so no general leak is added there. The PC bootstrap manually frees task/context storage after its second mask failure without that cleanup, which remains the narrower EK822 leak. Broader creation and teardown caller census remains open; no task was launched or allocation failure induced.

EK473 detailed-body reconciliation (2026-10-13): restored the missing numbered finding body after verifying the recorded PC remote-removal path against `RemTask`, the `int $0xfe` reschedule handler, its `TS_TOMBSTONED` state update, and the CPU-local Forbid contract. The selected root-only `secKill` entry supplies a public in-tree route to call `RemTask` on a plain task, including one running on another CPU. This is a task lifetime/teardown defect, not the duplicate cleanup owner race EK830 or queued callback race EK832. The report count is now 267 unique detailed bodies; no task was removed or runtime interleaving exercised.

EK277 detailed-body reconciliation (2026-10-13): restored the missing parent/child teardown candidate after tracing task-parent assignment through `NewAddTask`/`Exec_InitETask` and both ETask cleanup branches. Child cleanup snapshots its parent ETask before locking; concurrent parent cleanup can reparent the child, unlock, and expunge the former parent before child cleanup's later lock/removal/notification path. The selected CPU-local Forbid contract permits this interleaving on ExecSMP. The finding is distinct from EK8845's `ChildOrphan` race. The report now contains 268 unique detailed bodies; no concurrent task exit was run.

SumKickData producer recheck (2026-10-13; EK75 remains externally conditional): searched maintained C, assembly, boot and Exec initialization references for writes to `KickMemPtr`, `KickTagPtr`, and `KickCheckSum`. The selected m68k AROSBootstrap constructs its `BootMemChunk` entries with `ml_NumEntries = 1` (`AROSBootstrap.c:309-340`), but passes its boot list through `BootStruct`, not the preserved ExecBase checksum fields (`:1350-1360`). The only selected `KickMemPtr` restoration paths copy pre-existing fields from a valid old ExecBase (`arch/m68k-amiga/boot/start.c:975-1005`; `rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:174-181,362-368`); no maintained in-tree multi-entry producer was found. EK75's checksum omission for MemList entries beyond the fixed header remains source-valid only for externally supplied legacy state. The debug trace's words beyond `MemList` are guarded by DEBUG and were not promoted. No boot or checksum was run.

EK75 MemList-layout recheck (2026-10-13): verified `struct MemList` uses the conventional counted trailing-entry layout (`compiler/include/exec/memory.h:61-66`) and `InitKickTags` consumes every `ml_NumEntries` entry (`rom/exec/initkicktags.c:250-270`), while `SumKickData` adds only `sizeof(struct MemList) / sizeof(ULONG)` words for each node (`rom/exec/sumkickdata.c:74-93`). Thus the checksum omission is real for any supplied node with more than one entry. The selected AROSBootstrap producer remains one-entry-per-node; the residual trigger is external state preserved from a valid legacy ExecBase on the m68k warm-boot path, not a demonstrated default project producer. No candidate status change; no boot was run.


ARM SMP affinity-mask cleanup recheck (EK8790 broadened, 2026-10-13): confirmed `KrnAllocCPUMask` allocates a four-byte public cleared mask (`arch/arm-native/kernel/alloccpumask.c:20-26`) and `KrnFreeCPUMask` releases it (`freecpumask.c:16-26`). `Processor_Init` allocates this mask before `AllocSignal`; on signal exhaustion it falls back to inline probing and leaves the unused mask unfreed (`processor_init.c:55-76`). This is separate from the later task/context-construction failure path already in EK8790, where the mask has not transferred to ARM `PrepareContext`. No signal or memory failure was induced; source-only.

RemTask duplicate-cleanup recheck (EK830, 2026-10-13): revalidated the terminal-state precheck against PC, ARM32 and AArch64 reschedule handlers. PC serializes list updates but accepts repeated TS_REMOVED requests and maps each to TS_TOMBSTONED; ARM32/AArch64 serialize task state under `tc_SpinLock` but likewise return no cleanup-owner result. The common RemTask caller then performs cleanup unconditionally. The source mechanism remains; selected caller review does not establish a pair targeting the same task concurrently, so the report now states that condition without a specific external trigger route. No task removal was run.

Exec IRQ-server API recheck (2026-10-13; EK31/EK815 reconfirmed): reread the complete `AddIntServer`/`RemIntServer` pair and generic `KrnAddIRQHandler`/`KrnRemIRQHandler` (`rom/exec/addintserver.c:62-78`; `remintserver.c:52-72`; `rom/kernel/addirqhandler.c:77-115`; `remirqhandler.c:49-78`). `INTB_KERNEL` is 16, so values below it index the 16-entry legacy vector table, while the kernel route subtracts the base and the generic add helper admits only `irq < HW_IRQ_COUNT`. `RemIntServer` forwards the stored token directly; failed-token cleanup remains EK815, and the PC override’s unlocked SMP walk/mutation remains EK31. No additional IRQ-number range or narrowing defect established; platform-specific overrides and caller lifetimes remain open. No IRQ was run.

The source-wide call census and selected bounded producer IDs remain as recorded in the `setintvector.c` row; no vector was changed or dispatched.


PCI interrupt-wrapper caller recheck (EK815, 2026-10-13; no new null-token caller): the generic PCI AddInterrupt method returns FALSE when `KrnAddIRQHandler` returns NULL (`rom/hidds/pci/pcidriverclass.c:279-287`). Both selected HDAudio HIDD variants record `irqAdded` only after that success and gate removal on the flag (`workbench/devs/AHI/Drivers/HDAudio/hda_hidd.c:178-199`; `NVHDMI/hda_hidd.c:178-199`).
