VirtIO checks the result too, but its normal selected controller constructor does not reach storage `AddBus`/`SetUpBus` because of OD2541 (`virtio_controllerclass.c:145`; `rom/hidds/base/storage/storage_controllerclass.c:74-120`). Thus this wrapper set adds no active EK815 null-removal caller; external and alternate PCI-driver overrides remain open. No registration failure was induced.


Kernel page-size initialization recheck (2026-10-13; EK639/`KrnInitMemory` scope refined, no new finding): repeated the whole-tree `kb_PageSize` and `KrnInitMemory` search including C, headers, assembly and build/config inputs. The only direct caller remains the excluded allocator test; `developer/debug/test/kernel/mmakefile.src:5-11` omits it. Generic `AllocKernelBase` obtains a `MEMF_CLEAR` block (`rom/kernel/allockernelbase.c:13-29`), and `Kernel_Init` runs selected platform INITLIB hooks without any checked-in page-size write (`rom/kernel/kernel_init.c:90-140`). The generic `KrnInitMemory` returns before `mm_Init` at zero page size; `USE_MMU=0` on m68k Amiga, while Unix uses its separate mmap allocator and a local 4096-byte fallback (`arch/all-unix/kernel/allocpages.c:63-68`). This confirms no selected production caller or in-tree field initializer; generated/indirect callers, out-of-tree platform setup and runtime memory maps remain open. EK640 stays withdrawn because its unprotected `mm_Init` path is unreachable with checked-in state. No allocation or boot was run.


`KrnScheduleCPU` generic-wrapper caller/manifest follow-up: its body issues only local `SC_SCHEDULE` and does not consume `cpu_mask` (`rom/kernel/schedulecpu.c:47-57`). The selected ExecSMP configurations with cross-CPU scheduling callers replace that generic body: all-PC (`arch/all-pc/kernel/mmakefile.src:43`), ARM native (`arch/arm-native/kernel/mmakefile.src:46`) and AArch64 native (`arch/aarch64-native/kernel/mmakefile.src:44`) provide architecture implementations. The selected m68k-all override also uses its architecture path (`arch/m68k-all/kernel/mmakefile.src:25`). No in-tree ExecSMP configuration selecting the generic body was found; no independent defect credited. Non-SMP generic callers and external private-API use remain outside this check.


Exec/kernel SumKickData caller reconciliation (2026-10-13; EK75): traced every checked-in assignment/copy of `KickMemPtr`, the `InitKickTags` checksum-and-reservation sequence, and the m68k warm-boot handoff. The checked-in AROSBootstrap builds local one-entry MemLists for its own BootStruct flow but does not publish them through the preserved ExecBase KickMem fields. No ordinary selected in-tree producer of a multi-entry `SysBase->KickMemPtr` was found. EK75 remains a conditional checksum coverage gap only if an external/legacy reset-proof producer supplies multiple entries; external producers are the remaining caller-scope gap. The debug-only trace's extra word reads remain unpromoted because selected DEBUG reachability and short-node shape are not established. No boot was run.

Exec `Signal`/semaphore-wait caller follow-up (2026-10-13; EK8880 rechecked): reread the complete wait insertion and task teardown paths. `InternalObtainSemaphore` links a stack-local `SemaphoreRequest`, drops the SMP semaphore spinlock, then waits (`rom/exec/semaphores.c:121-145`); non-current `RemTask` marks/removes the task, flushes signal IPIs on SMP, cleans its context and frees every `tc_MemEntry` allocation without visiting semaphore queues (`rom/exec/remtask.c:64-100,112-181`). `NewCreateTaskA` puts task and stack allocations in that ownership list (`rom/exec/newcreatetaska.c:174-188,250-252`). `ReleaseSemaphore` later removes a queued node, updates ownership, and signals its stored waiter (`rom/exec/releasesemaphore.c:136-178`). `secKill` routes plain tasks directly to `RemTask` without testing their state (`rom/security/secKill.c:38-60`). This reconfirms EK8880 as conditional; ExecSMP `Forbid` is local-CPU only (`rom/exec/forbid.c:54-60`), so it does not itself serialize the independent semaphore list. No in-tree workload was found that kills a task during the exact blocked interval, and no runtime was used. Broader public `Signal` caller census and external callers remain open.

Taskless AttemptSemaphore reachability recheck (EK8854, 2026-10-13): verified the symbol-set census and selected PC callback. The only maintained `PREINITLIB` registration is `Exec_X86PreInit`, which initializes/registers the shutdown callback and returns (`arch/all-pc/exec/platform_init.c:424-443`); repository-wide source search found no `PREINITLIB` callback that calls either attempt API. The null-owner state corruption remains proven if an external or future callback uses the API before `SET_THIS_TASK`, but no checked-in caller trigger is established. The finding stays conditional and is not presented as a default boot failure. No bootstrap was run.

EK8827 Sam440 exit-path follow-up (2026-10-13): traced `ExitInterrupt` in the selected PPC440 UIC/decrementer handlers through `arch/ppc-sam440/kernel/kernel_intern.h` to the shared `core_ExitInterrupt` gate in `rom/kernel/kernel_intr.c`. It tests `TDNESTCOUNT_GET < 0` before honoring `FLAG_SCHEDSWITCH`, same polarity as the previously mapped paths; with the signed-byte counter wrapped to -128, a pending switch is permitted. Added Sam440 to EK8827 configuration scope. No interrupt or nested-call sequence was run. Broader caller/depth reachability remains open.

InitResident bind-driver caller check (2026-10-13): re-read the selected `workbench/c/BindDrivers.c` dispatch with `rom/exec/initresident.c`, `adddevice.c`, `addlibrary.c`, and `addresource.c`. For a failed autoinit, `InitResident` returns NULL before publication and BindDrivers unloads the segment; on success, the type-specific Add* call publishes the completed base before returning non-NULL, and BindDrivers retains the segment. `AddLibrary`'s special debug.library open occurs after list insertion and no failure cleanup is attempted, but the selected debug resident is `noexpunge` and the cached base is null-checked by inspected consumers; this does not establish a new selected failure. This check does not close the separate open/expunge lifetime gap EK9099 or broader dynamic module admission review. No module was loaded.


AUX default-device BSTR follow-up (EK8881; 2026-10-13): traced the zero-Startup generated AUX mountlist through `buildDefaultStartup`, target BSTR macros, the console handler’s BSTR length/copy, and its `OpenDevice` call. The default builder always stores a length-prefixed string; `AROS_FAST_BSTR` treats the pointed-to byte as the first character, so the device name copied to `fh->devname` has the length byte prefixed. This defect is independent of EK867 once the tagged stack-structure pointer survives its bit-30 mask. No startup was run.

Shared-semaphore starvation caller recheck (EK875, 2026-10-13): verified the selected DOS examples against their lock durations. Wanderer’s volume enumeration takes `LDF_WRITE` and explicitly waits for shared locks to drain before scanning (`workbench/system/Wanderer/Classes/iconvolumelist.c:116-169`); DiskInfo takes `LDF_READ` only around `FindDosEntry` and immediately unlocks (`workbench/system/Wanderer/Tools/DiskInfo/diskinfo.c:293-296`). `GetDeviceProc` releases its `LDF_ALL|LDF_READ` lock before `RunHandler` and reacquires it afterward (`rom/dos/getdeviceproc.c:265-278`), so that path does not establish a reader lock held across handler startup. The public shared-obtain contract promises coexistence and exclusion against an exclusive owner, but no writer preference (`rom/exec/obtainsemaphoreshared.c:33-38`). EK875 remains a conditional reader-starvation candidate if shared acquisitions keep the holder count nonzero; these checked-in DOS examples do not demonstrate that sustained sequence. No lock workload was run.

Pthread public API/link-library census (EK617 detail, 2026-10-13): rechecked the installed-header copy, active `%build_linklib` source list, function list, `.conf` declarations and checkout-wide symbol references. Eighteen public pthread declarations have neither implementations nor active link exports: six thread-attribute scheduling/scope accessors, four barrier-attribute functions, two condition-attribute pshared functions, two concurrency functions, two mutex-attribute pshared functions, and two rwlock-attribute pshared functions. `pthread_sigmask` is implemented and was excluded. No client was compiled or linked.

PC processor-query affinity recheck (EK8766; former EK295 ledger candidate): a failed mask allocation is tolerated by `KrnGetCPUMask`; the task still receives a NULL `TASKTAG_AFFINITY`, and x86-64 `PrepareContext` replaces its inherited mask with NULL. The PC scheduler restricts NULL-mask tasks to CPU 0, while `Processor_QueryTask` attributes the live CPUID results to the requested `pqd_CPUNo`. This promotes the candidate to a detailed report finding. x86-64 PC ExecSMP is the affected selected configuration; i386 PC does not enable ExecSMP. No allocation failure or boot was run.

x86-64 EK8889 global-remap trigger sweep (2026-10-13): searched every direct C call to `KrnMapGlobal` and compared the x86-64-selected path. `PCIPC::MapPCI` is the selected PC path and only maps identity ranges beyond the initially mapped 128-GiB window (`arch/all-pc/hidds/pcipc/pcipc_driverclass.c:232-253`); it does not establish a changed physical mapping at an already-used VA. Other direct callers found are for separate architecture or optional backends. The generic public vector documentation contains no overlap/remap restriction (`rom/kernel/mapglobal.c:13-52`; `compiler/include/aros/kernel.h:28-39`), and x86-64 `map_global_2m` rewrites leaf descriptors while invalidating/reloading only the local CPU (`arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/mapglobal.c:109-145`). Retain EK8889 only as a conditional public-API remap defect; no selected x86-64 caller currently proves the trigger. No mapping or CPU interleaving was run.

Raspberry Pi EK8811 package-shape evidence check (2026-10-13): re-read `boot.c` sizing and load loops (`:500-548,603-665`) against the `getElfSize`/`loadElf` static global-count flow (`elf.c:84-115,425-451`). The last ELF member measured during package sizing leaves `int_shnum` for the subsequent embedded-core load; each load then resets it only after allocating the VLA. The current repository contains no checked-in `.pkg`, `.elf`, or `.bin` package/build artifact from which to compare real member section counts. EK8811 remains a source-confirmed bounds flaw with a conditional count/order trigger; generated package contents and board behavior remain unverified. No image was loaded.

EK8889 PCIPC threshold-overlap caller recheck (2026-10-13): confirmed core_SetupMMU installs writable/cacheable identity 2-MiB PDEs across the first 128 GiB (`arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/mmu.c:43-83,154-156`). The selected PCIPC MapPCI call is gated on BAR end >128 GiB but rounds BAR start down to 2 MiB and remaps through rounded end (`pcipc_driverclass.c:235-247`). This earlier note inferred a valid BAR would straddle the boundary; that inference was not established by the selected source and is superseded by the 2026-10-18 caller recheck below. EK8889 remains conditional on a real overlapping remap.


ARM32 Raspberry Pi bootstrap body completion (2026-10-13; no new finding): reread all 715 lines of `arch/arm-raspi/boot/boot.c`, the local MMU helper/header, allocator/cache helpers and tag definitions. Traced all local map/unmap callers plus package sizing/load loops, kernel placement/clear, DTB copy/reparse, allocator switch, cache flush and final tag handoff. Existing findings cover malformed package spans (EK8807), rejected ELF handling (EK8822), live-DTB overlap (EK10944), and DT property bounds/LED diagnostic cases (EK8882/EK8883). No separate mapping or handoff defect was established. Firmware layout, package contents and actual MMU behavior were not exercised.


OOP disposal selected-caller follow-up (2026-10-13): traced the bitmap allocation/free and mode-enumerator pixel-format release paths through `OOP_DisposeObject` to root disposal. The bitmap paths guard nullable objects; the shared pixel-format table removes its last-reference entry under `pfsema` before disposing it. No new issue established. The repository-wide source-call census remains incomplete and includes unselected/tests/generated contexts.

VMM manager initialization reconciliation (2026-10-13): reread `VM_Manager_Init.c` in bounded chunks and traced every initialization error return into the manager’s shared cleanup path (`VM_Manager.c:601-630`). Checked open-library rollback, message-port removal, signal release, conditional notification teardown, support-task stop/wait ordering, and final library close against Exec/DOS callers. The diagnostic `FilePart(CxParams->PrefsPath)` is unconditional after the optional preferences-task branch. The vmm.library caller passes null CxParams and reaches this member dereference before the page-handler launch or later EK9906 null-base AddMemList call; this is EK428's direct startup path, not a consequence masked by EK9906. Partial child-task startup/handshake ownership, target ABI/platform contracts, and real library-startup behavior remain open. No VMM runtime path was executed.

OOP disposal PCI/PCIPC caller follow-up (2026-10-13): traced selected common PCI removal, PCIPC host-bridge replacement and PCI/PCIPC/PCIDT temporary PCI-object disposal paths (`rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:66-100,482-515,663-690`; `arch/all-pc/hidds/pcipc/pcipc_deviceclass.c:31-128`; both driver/init pairs; `arch/riscv64-opensbi/hidd/pcidt/pcidt_deviceclass.c:20-110`). PCI removes device nodes before disposal under `dev_lock`; selected base/derived device classes have no dispose override, and the common PCI singleton's empty Root::Dispose makes its short-lived API wrappers non-owning. PCIPC and PCIDT class method tables confirm the traced overrides. PCIPC's replacement disposes an object still inside construction; the outer PCI scanner inserts only the final returned object, so no stale list link is left. No additional disposal defect established. This is a selected caller cluster only; the 203-line repository census and remaining callers are unclassified.


OOP disposal ATA constructor rollback follow-up (2026-10-13): the ATA PCI bus constructor's failed-New path computes Root::Dispose and calls `OOP_DoSuperMethod`; this is superclass cleanup and does not enter the class's `PCIATABus__Root__Dispose`. The caller therefore correctly frees the still-unowned probe record/reference. The skipped class cleanup does leak an already allocated DMA buffer when subsequent IRQ setup fails (OD2661 in Other Drivers); this selected caller is classified, while the global `OOP_DisposeObject` census remains incomplete.

OOP disposal generic-HW/mouse proxy follow-up (2026-10-13): traced generic `HW_AddDriver` setup-failure disposal and `HW_RemoveDriver` unlink/cleanup/dispose ordering against the mouse proxy's constructor and destructor (`rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c:170-207,264-298`; `rom/hidds/mouse/subsystem.c:92-170`; `driverdata.c:40-101,110-117`). A failed inner mouse-driver construction uses superclass cleanup while the proxy's inner-driver field remains null; successful proxy disposal owns and disposes its driver. Removal unlinks under the exclusive list semaphore, then performs cleanup and disposal after unlocking; enumeration holds a shared lock and its contract forbids mutation from the callback. No new invalid-disposal or list-lifetime defect established in these paths. Driver callback quiescence during platform teardown and remaining disposal callers remain open.

OOP disposal serial-mouse caller follow-up (2026-10-13): traced rejected-unit disposal, probe-failure resource release, and successful mouse teardown through the PC serial HIDD. Failed mouse construction uses superclass cleanup after `test_mouse_serial` already releases acquired resources, while successful construction later disposes the still-registered unit before freeing callback storage. No duplicate disposal established; cross-CPU interrupt quiescence and remaining serial callers are open.

OOP disposal VESA PCI-scan caller follow-up (2026-10-13): `Find_PCI_Card` disposes only the temporary `CLID_Hidd_PCI` singleton wrapper after enumeration and releases the obtained PCIDevice attribute base; PCI Root::Dispose is intentionally empty for the shared singleton (`rom/hidds/vesagfx/vesagfx_support.c:230-267`; `rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:663-690`). No device-object ownership is transferred by the enumeration hook. This selected caller is classified; the global OOP disposal census remains incomplete.

OOP disposal NVMe probe caller follow-up (2026-10-13): traced `NVME_Probe`'s temporary PCI singleton through PCI enumeration and subsequent registration of the separately owned PCI-device records (`rom/devs/nvme/nvme_init.c:276-338`). The singleton wrapper is disposed only after enumeration and its Root::Dispose is the intentional no-op; PCI device objects remain owned by the common PCI device list, with the driver's acquired device reference carried by each probe record into controller construction. A NULL PCI singleton is guarded. The later `HW_AddDriver` failure record/reference leak is already tracked as OD2365, not a second disposal bug. The global 203-line OOP disposal caller census remains incomplete.

OOP disposal Sam440 battclock caller follow-up (2026-10-13): traced both public read/write functions' per-operation I²C-device and bus lifetime (`arch/ppc-sam440/battclock/readbattclock.c:66-116`; `writebattclock.c:68-133`). Each nullable device object is disposed before the bus object; the HIDD_I2CDevice attribute base and opened libraries are released on the common function exit. The generic I²CDevice class owns no bus object and the selected AMCC440 bus requires no additional caller-side deinit. No disposal defect established in this cluster. The read and write result-handling issues are OD2663/OD2664 in Other Drivers; the global disposal census remains incomplete.


EK8891. **The PC ExecSMP dispatch-state query macro uses an undeclared scheduler pointer (conditional macro defect; high source confidence, no in-tree trigger found).** In the `__AROSEXEC_SMP__` branch of the selected PC Exec platform header, `FLAG_SCHEDDISPATCH_ISSET` fetches `tls_t *__tls = TLS_PTR_GET()` but then tests and dereferences `__schd` without declaring it, and never uses `__tls` (`arch/all-pc/exec/exec_platform.h:279-286). The PC `tls_t` contains a `ScheduleData` pointer, not `ScheduleFlags` (`arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/tls.h:12-18`); neighboring query macros correctly obtain `struct X86SchedulerPrivate *__schd = TLS_GET(ScheduleData)`. An ordinary expansion with no caller-scope `__schd` is ill-formed; if a caller has a visible `__schd`, the macro reads that object rather than the current CPU’s TLS `ScheduleData`. A repository-wide C/header search found no checked-in expansion, so this does not currently break the selected x86-64 PC ExecSMP build. It remains a source-level defect for external consumers or a future in-tree caller. Use the same `ScheduleData` lookup as `FLAG_SCHEDSWITCH_ISSET`. No compile was run; source-only.


RemTail cross-client caller recheck (2026-10-13): expanded the selected caller pass to MUI ZText destruction, DragNDrop cleanup and Prometheus board-list teardown. Their inspected drain loops use RemTail null termination; Prometheus expunge is gated by its library reference count, while DragNDrop same-task event/disposal ordering remains open. No independent generic Exec list defect established; broader SFS list consistency and external callers remain pending. Source-only.


PC IPI NULL-mask recheck (EK8892, 2026-10-13): traced `core_DoCallIPI` request-bit construction to `core_DoIPI` destination iteration and the selected APIC `KrnCPUInMask` implementation. NULL accounts for all CPUs but sends only to CPU 0, leaving multi-CPU requests incomplete. Current production call sites pass a real mask; the finding is conditional on external/future NULL-mask use. No IPI was run.


PC exception-handler registration follow-up (EK8877, 2026-10-13): widened the finding to include ignored syscall-handler allocation failures in both PC platform initializers. Confirmed `cpu_Trap` halts on the unhandled syscall vector but exempts unhandled spurious interrupts, so spurious registration failure is excluded from the impact claim. No allocation failure or trap was run.

Interrupt-exit direct-caller recheck (2026-10-13; no new candidate): followed every in-tree `core_ExitInterrupt` call returned by the source census at the pinned revision. Generic `SC_CAUSE` delegates to the generic softint/scheduler exit; hosted Unix invokes its signal IRQ exit only when `SupervisorCount == 1`; MinGW's host IRQ and `SC_CAUSE` routes both reach its idle-aware override; Efika distinguishes supervisor return from user return in its PPC exit frame and its IRQ/syscall paths; PC invokes exit only when `INTR_FROMUSERMODE`; OpenSBI RISC-V enters it only for the outermost trap classified for reschedule. Sam440's shared exit gate was already traced in the EK8827 follow-up. These checks found no new caller crossing the nested/supervisor boundary or contradicting the existing task-disable gate. This is a targeted call-site recheck, not closure of the architecture inventory: interrupt entry/exit implementations, external callers, and platform-specific scheduling behavior remain open. Source-only; no interrupt or syscall was run.


RISC-V fatal backtrace diagnostic follow-up (EK8893, 2026-10-13): confirmed the selected OpenSBI kernel links generic `KrnBacktraceFromFrame`, which returns zero unconditionally, and defines no platform override. The fatal path therefore prints only saved PC/ra and omits stack frames; the adjacent source comment claiming a stack scan is inaccurate. Added this bounded diagnostic finding. No trap was run.


OpenSBI virtual-IRQ count-bound follow-up (EK8894, 2026-10-13): the allocator checks `base + count` in 32-bit ULONG arithmetic before validating the capacity. An oversized public request can wrap that sum and make the search read past the fixed bitmap. The selected PCIDT bridge caller retries with smaller bounded counts, so this remains an exported-API condition; no IRQ was allocated.

EK8894 outer-loop and caller recheck (2026-10-13): confirmed the candidate-start test `(irq + count) <= HW_IRQ_COUNT` also wraps in 32-bit `ULONG` arithmetic (`allocirq.c:36,39`). The startup timer requests one source and PCIDT begins at `PCIDT_MSI_VECTORS == 32`, halving after failures (`kernel_timer.c:256`; `pcidt.h:76`; `pcidt_driverclass.c:744-750`), so no selected in-tree caller supplies the unsafe extent. The inner `n < count` scan itself has no remaining-capacity bound and indexes `__virq_used[(irq+n)-base]` until a used slot or success condition; a large external count can therefore cross the 1024-byte array before any rejection. The report now limits the claim to this definite out-of-bounds read and does not assert that a reservation write completes. No allocation was run.

Exec soft-interrupt delivery/caller recheck (2026-10-13; no new generic finding): traced Cause's `INTF_SOFTINT` request through `Enable`'s non-supervisor `KrnCause()` path and the selected PC kernel's `core_ExitInterrupt` and idle-CPU paths into `core_Cause`, which invokes the Exec vector installed during `exec_init.c`; interrupt-context requests are handled on exit, and x86-64's trap return explicitly disables interrupts because `SoftIntDispatch` can re-enable them. This reconciles the PC delivery portion for EK8875; other architecture delivery remains open. The queue-type reset window still has no generic lost-work attribution because no selected callback was shown to lose a discrete event when it drains its backing queue/condition; any narrower event-loss claim needs a specific caller whose callback ignores pending work. No interrupt was caused.

Soft-interrupt platform matrix follow-up (2026-10-13; no new finding): verified that Unix installs SIGUSR2 as `core_IRQ` and SIGUSR1 as `core_SysCall`; `KrnCause` raises SIGUSR2, whose outermost handler reaches `core_ExitInterrupt` and `core_Cause`. MinGW's `SC_CAUSE` exception branch also calls `core_ExitInterrupt`. On m68k Amiga, `Cause` writes the chipset soft-interrupt request directly and the Exec override of `Enable` re-enables chipset interrupts; its `KrnCause` stub is intentionally unused. The generic/SMP queue defect remains bounded to concurrent shared-node callers; interrupt delivery is no longer an open question for PC, Unix, MinGW or m68k Amiga. Other maintained architecture paths and actual delivery remain untested.

OpenSBI soft-interrupt path closure (2026-10-13; no new finding): traced generic `KrnCause` through the RISC-V `krnSysCall(SC_CAUSE)` ebreak (`kernel_cpu.h:56-67`), the outermost `SCAUSE_BREAKPOINT` syscall dispatch (`kernel_traps.c:165-178,205-226`), and `core_SysCall` to `core_ExitInterrupt`, which invokes the Exec softint vector when `SFF_SoftInt` is set (`rom/kernel/kernel_intr.c:30-75`). External PLIC interrupts also pass through outermost `core_ExitInterrupt` on trap return (`kernel_traps.c:166-179`). This resolves the OpenSBI delivery path; native RISC-V and other maintained ports remain unverified.
x86-64 task startup ABI follow-up (2026-10-13): rechecked `TASKTAG_ARG7/8` stack slots, entry alignment and the return-to-finalizer route as a unit (`arch/x86_64-all/exec/preparecontext.c:74-109`; `taskexit.S:12-14`). The argument push order matches the x86-64 ABI, and `TaskExitStub` removes the two reserved stack arguments before returning to `fallBack`. A source-wide search found no in-tree `TASKTAG_ARG7` or `TASKTAG_ARG8` caller; the selected direct callers pass at most four arguments, and their startup is handled by the same `NewCreateTaskA` → `NewAddTask` path (`rom/exec/newcreatetaska.c:254-270`; `newaddtask.c:268-308`). The x86-64 selected affinity producers and transferred-mask contract are separately traced under EK8790/EK8766; USB2OTG's embedded pointer is already qualified under OD2422. No context was dispatched.

PC idle syscall follow-up (no new candidate): traced `arch/all-pc/exec/exec_idle.c` through `krnSysCallChangePMState(0x90)`, syscall registration, and both generic and ACPI handler bodies. `platform_post.c` calls `acpi_Init` before registering defaults; when the FADT parser registered the custom handler, `krnAddSysCallHandler(..., force=FALSE)` rejects the later duplicate, preserving the ACPI sleep handler. Both selected handlers enable interrupts for `hlt`, return with interrupts disabled, and deliver pending soft interrupts before `IdleTask` calls `Reschedule`; the ACPI SMP branch accounts sleep time on the current APIC core. No local defect established. Hardware wake delivery, ACPI/APIC availability on specific SMP machines and runtime scheduling remain pending; no idle task was run.


SetIntVector dispatch-side recheck (EK542, 2026-10-13): enumerated direct `core_Cause` callers as well as SetIntVector writers. All selected cause IDs are `INTB_SOFTINT` or `INTB_VERTB`; the m68k Paula dispatcher passes its macro argument through only at those two selected invocations. This does not provide an in-tree trigger for EK542's out-of-range vector ID and does not alter the finding. No interrupt was delivered.

x86-64 task-context handoff recheck (EK8790/EK8766, 2026-10-13): traced `PrepareContext` through `NewAddTask` and `TaskExitStub`. The six register arguments match SysV x86-64 order; ARG7/ARG8 occupy the two reserved stack slots, and the stub removes those slots before returning through the selected finalizer. `NewAddTask` invokes `CleanupETask` when context creation or preparation fails. In `PrepareContext`, however, `KrnCreateContext` precedes tag iteration, and affinity ownership is replaced only when the TASKTAG_AFFINITY case is reached (`preparecontext.c:37-51`), so the pre-adoption mask leak recorded in EK8790 remains accurate. Null-affinity CPU0-only scheduling remains the separate EK8766 caller condition. No context was dispatched.

x86-64 failed-context cleanup follow-up: `PrepareContext` stores the result of `KrnCreateContext` (including NULL) in `et_RegFrame` before returning FALSE (`arch/x86_64-all/exec/preparecontext.c:37-40`). `NewAddTask` then calls `CleanupETask`; that cleanup frees owned affinity and ETask/list state but does not inspect or delete `et_RegFrame` (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:305-310`; `exec_util.c:238-281`). The separate `KrnDeleteContext` branch in `TaskLaunch` follows only a successfully prepared task, so this failed allocation does not pass NULL to the kernel context deleter (`newaddtask.c:85-115`). No new cleanup defect established. The TASKTAG_AFFINITY pre-adoption leak remains EK8790. No context allocation was induced.

AArch64 task-context ABI/caller recheck (EK8790, 2026-10-13): traced the selected native `PrepareContext` through `KrnCreateContext`, the exception-frame restore layout, and common `NewAddTask` failure cleanup. `TASKTAG_ARG1..8` map to x0..x7; SP is rounded down to 16-byte AAPCS64 alignment; LR receives the selected fall-back routine; CPSR/PSTATE is set to `0x04`, matching `CPUMODE_EL1t` in `KrnCreateContext` and the mode used by kernel startup. Affinity-mask ownership still transfers only upon reaching the tag case, after context allocation; a failed context creation therefore retains EK8790's caller-owned pre-adoption leak. No argument-register or PSTATE mismatch established. No task was dispatched.

ARM32 task-entry ABI follow-up (EK8896, 2026-10-13): traced common `NewAddTask` alignment into ARM32 `PrepareContext` and the public `NewCreateTaskA` argument contract. The 16-byte-aligned incoming SP loses one or three 4-byte words when ARG5 or ARG7 is the highest supplied stack argument, violating AAPCS32 public-interface 8-byte SP alignment. The report records the public/external trigger; source-wide search found no in-tree ARG5–ARG8 producer. No task was dispatched.

AArch64 Raspberry Pi IRQ callback follow-up (2026-10-13): traced `handle_irq`/`handle_fiq` into BCM2837 legacy dispatch, BCM2711/2712 GIC dispatch, timer callbacks, and GIC SGI handling. BCM2837 masks controller sources during early setup and enables its system timer only after registering the timer handler with `KernelBase`; the GIC paths EOI dispatched interrupts, direct-handle the timer PPI, and route SPIs to CPU0. No new source-level issue established. Hardware routing and behavior remain untested.


genmodule public prototype writer/dispatcher follow-up (2026-10-13; EK8825 scope confirmed): traced `writeincproto` and `writeincclib` through `INCLUDES` dispatch. The proto writer checks only `fopen` and ignores its final `fclose` result; the clib writer never explicitly closes its stream, but the dispatcher calls it once and the process exits immediately after the command branch, so no accumulating file-descriptor leak is established. A delayed flush/close failure can still be lost at process exit, already within EK8825. The clib row now records this distinction; no generated output or filesystem failure was induced. Source-only.


Exec genmodule suffix-boundary follow-up (EK733, 2026-10-13): traced both `writeincludes` suffix-detection branches through `functionhead` defaults, `rom/exec/exec.conf`'s four-character argument-taking `Wait`, the `INCLUDES` dispatcher and the Exec `%build_module` generated-include dependency. Both writers form `name + (strlen(name) - 7)` before `strcmp`; this is an out-of-object pointer in the selected Exec header-generation pass. The report records the host-tool consequence without claiming a deterministic crash or runtime Exec defect. No generator or build command was run.

PC syscall-handler registration/dispatch concurrency follow-up (2026-10-14; no candidate): revisited the unsynchronized `kb_SysCallHandlers` traversal and `AddTail` registration. On i386/x86-64, the syscall gate and initial handler list are installed during platform initialization before `RTF_COLDSTART` (`arch/i386-pc/kernel/platform_init.c:79-108`; `arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/platform_init.c:244-274`; `kernel_startup.c:423-433,619-635`). Exec's additional registrations run during `exec.library` INITLIB (`arch/all-pc/exec/platform_init.c:445-494`; `rom/exec/exec_init.c:266-280`), before `kernel.post` reaches `smp_Initialize` (`platform_post.c:201-205`); kernel.post is explicitly a later COLDSTART resident (`platform_post.c:97-104,117-129`). ACPI registration hooks run after `ACPICA_InitTask` exits and before AP startup (`arch/all-pc/kernel/acpi.c:198-235`; `platform_post.c:168-180,201-205`). The pre-AP registrations therefore have no other CPU traversing the list concurrently; the table-hook loop contains no scheduling yield after the ACPICA wait. The source reviewed does not establish a re-entrant syscall from inside the short list mutation or an interrupt-driven syscall path. This startup lead is not promoted. Runtime interleaving and other platform-specific registrations remain outside this check; no syscall was run.

NewCreateTaskA/NewAddTask construction-failure reconciliation (2026-10-14; no new candidate): reread tag traversal, task/stack/name/optional-port MemEntry sizing, and the failure handoff (`rom/exec/newcreatetaska.c:100-162,190-272`; `newaddtask.c:268-331`). `LibNextTagItem` owns TAG_MORE/TAG_SKIP traversal. A TASKTAG_TASKMSGPORT signal-allocation failure exits before `InitMsgPort` and before writing the caller's output pointer; after successful port setup the pointer is published before `NewAddTask`, so a later InitETask/context failure frees the backing MemList and leaves that output pointer stale (existing EK06). On PrepareContext failure NewAddTask calls `CleanupETask` before NewCreateTaskA frees the task/stack/port list; InitETask allocation failure has no ETask allocation to unwind. The name-slot count/initialization cases remain as separately scoped in EK788 and its caller rechecks. No independent task-port ownership leak or missing tag-list control case was established. No task or allocation failure was induced.

EK744 report reconciliation (2026-10-14): found the ledger had detailed references to EK744 but no standalone finding section in `AROS-exec-kernel.md`; added the full selected trigger and call chain. `C:CheckMem` is selected in `workbench/c/mmakefile.src:11` and calls `AvailMem(MEMF_CLEAR)`; MungWall must be enabled and the scan must discover a damaged tracked header. `MungWall_Scan` holds `AllocMemListSpinLock` through `CheckHeader`/`Exec_ExtAlert`; the ordinary no-nested-alert requester path allocates with `AllocMem`, whose successful `MungWall_Build` tries the same lock. No corruption or allocation was induced. Source-only.

EK744 platform-gate recheck (2026-10-14): verified `rom/exec/mmakefile.src` always includes `mungwall.c`; runtime wall tracking is enabled only when the parsed kernel command line contains `mungwall` (`prepareexecbase.c:322-340`). `AllocMemListSpinLock` is initialized and used only under `__AROSEXEC_SMP__` (`prepareexecbase.c:299-305`; `mungwall.c:275-300`). `configure.in` selects that macro for x86-64 PC and Raspberry Pi `smp` variants (`:1667-1671,2195-2199`). The selected CheckMem command is present in `workbench/c/mmakefile.src:11`. This confirms the report's platform/runtime conditions; no build or alert was run.

DoIO/WaitIO reply-publication recheck correction (EK8799; 2026-10-27): corrected the 2026-10-14 conclusion after re-reading `WaitIO()`'s wait loop. The selected Intuition `SetPrefs()` caller uses `DoIO()` for `IND_SETTHRESH`/`IND_SETPERIOD`; `DoIO()` enters `WaitIO()` immediately, which sees `NT_MESSAGE` and sleeps on its private reply port. `InternalPutMsg()` inserts the reply before signaling that port, so this path does not establish early return or reply-port deletion during publication. The selected `C:Wait` path is different: its independent Ctrl-C signal can wake the task, which calls `CheckIO()`, conditionally aborts, calls `WaitIO()`, then closes and frees the one-use request (`workbench/c/Wait.c:171-194`). If the VBlank timer interrupt on another ExecSMP CPU has stored `NT_REPLYMSG` but not yet enqueued it, `CheckIO()` can skip abort and `WaitIO()` can return before cleanup. This corroborates the reset-callback route in EK8799. No request, signal, reset, or interleaving was run; source-only.

Signal restricted-context migration follow-up (EK8905, 2026-10-14): traced remote routing in `rom/exec/signal.c:170-225` against the ARM32/AArch64 FIQ hook (`:42-78`) and both native SMP schedulers' shared ready-list migration and affinity-filtered dispatch (`arch/arm-native/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:168-204,269-288`; AArch64 `:159-197,247-261`). A target can move from the CPU selected before the task lock is acquired to another CPU before the hook drains; the restricted hook sets `TF_EXCEPT` but only sets its local scheduler flag, so an exception signal to a target now running elsewhere is deferred until that CPU later reschedules. This affects the exceptional signal path; ordinary signal bits are retained. The later task dispatch checks `TF_EXCEPT` in `kernel_cpu.c:498-499` on ARM32 and `:426-427` on AArch64. Added EK8905 with ARM32/AArch64 gates and source locations; the existing `rom/exec/signal.c` table row records the broader Signal and caller work, while this supplement captures the additional migration trace. Public caller and migration timing checks remain open. No signal or migration was run. Source-only.

EK8905 reschedule bound recheck (2026-10-14): qualified the report's original “indefinitely” wording. `core_Schedule` forces a switch when the current task has `TF_EXCEPT` (`arch/arm-native/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:96-104`; AArch64 `:84-92`), and selected supported native CPUs arm per-core scheduler heartbeat timers during CPU registration (`kernel_cpu.c:193-201` on ARM32, `:174-180` on AArch64; platform timer callbacks in `platform_bcm2708.c:291-320` and `platform_bcm2711.c:200-215`). The checked sources support delayed exception dispatch until the destination CPU's next scheduling event, not permanent signal loss. No timer or signal was run.

Exec/kernel inventory count update (2026-10-14): the coverage ledger now names 900 unique EK identifiers; 304 have detailed report sections and 596 do not. Counts are computed from the current coverage references and report headings, not as a completion percentage; file-by-file review remains open.


Public-port duplicate-name recheck (GD4390, 2026-10-14): followed the AmigaGuide datatype's documented per-object ARexx names from its worker task to `FindPort`/`AddPort`, then checked Exec's selected SMP locking. `Forbid` is processor-local, FindPort drops PortListSpinLock before returning, and AddPort locks only publication while allowing duplicate names. Two concurrent AmigaGuide object workers can therefore publish the same supposedly unique suffix. The caller-specific user-visible result is detailed in Graphics/Desktop GD4390; the shared check-then-publish mechanism is also exercised by GD4020's ConClip singleton startup. No objects or ports were created. Source-only.
Late-secondary startup follow-up: EK8903 covers the AArch64 BCM27xx timeout interleaving in `platform_bcm27xx.c`. The one-second wait releases the global startup lock and the loop reuses shared trampoline stack/TLS/CPU slots; whether firmware can delay a secondary beyond the wait remains unverified. The existing platform source row records full body and caller review; this race was traced through `kernel_cpu.c` as a focused follow-up. Source-only.
Bootstrap failure follow-up: added EK8904 after tracing all `cpu_InitBootStrap` NULL-return cleanup branches into ARM32 and AArch64 `cpu_Register`. The nominal fatal label releases the startup lock but does not stop; both variants then dereference `__tls->ThisTask->tc_SPUpper`. Existing per-file kernel_cpu and kernel_execsmp rows now have this caller/error-path follow-up; successful-path findings EK153/EK726 remain separate. No allocation failure or boot was induced. Source-only.
EK8904 scope clarification: the optional bootstrap task-name `AllocVec` may fail without aborting bootstrap; the finding applies only to the checked MemList/Task/stack allocations, context creation, or ETask initialization that cause `cpu_InitBootStrap` to return NULL.

Signal/Wait/priority handoff cross-check (2026-10-14; no new candidate): reread the generic and selected SMP `Signal` paths alongside the full `Wait` transition and `SetTaskPri` post-lock reschedule. In `Wait`, the task lock covers the pending-bit check, wait-mask publication, TS_WAIT list insertion and carried-lock switch; after wake it reacquires the lock and checks pending signals again (`rom/exec/wait.c:66-120`). `Signal` publishes bits while holding the same task lock; the ordinary TS_WAIT path and restricted-IPI FIQ hook both release it before handing the raw task pointer to the scheduler (`signal.c:293-384`, restricted hook `:35-80`), matching existing lifetime/race candidates EK273/EK274. The missed immediate preemption when a running caller demotes itself in `SetTaskPri` is already EK833; the current code compares the updated priority with the same task's priority and therefore does not request a switch on that self-demotion path (`rom/exec/settaskpri.c:99-105,129-153`). No separate lost-wakeup or priority candidate was established. No signal, wait or scheduling event was run.

`log.resource` initializer recheck (2026-10-14; existing findings retained): reread all of `rom/log/log.c`'s resource setup and broadcaster startup against its Exec task-creation and pool-growth callers. `logInitialise`'s unchecked first pooled handle allocation remains EK8763; the partial-init low-memory-handler cleanup and task-publication branches remain separately covered by EK8782 and EK790. Provider finalization is still a TODO, already covered by EK8817 and selected provider-lifetime findings. The DOS/timer signal allocation returns before `lrb_Task` publication, so that task does not enter the service loop; no distinct externally visible failure beyond the tracked startup/readiness cases was established. No allocation failure or logger was run.

`SetTaskPri`/pthread yield follow-up (EK833, 2026-10-14): re-read the complete `pthread_once` and named semaphore path after checking the self-demotion behavior. The apparent first-call `pthread_once` omission is not a defect: `PTHREAD_ONCE_INIT` sets `started=-1`, so `__sync_val_compare_and_swap(&started, FALSE, TRUE)` returns nonzero and the first call enters the lock and invokes the initializer; later callers also enter the lock and are gated by `done` (`compiler/pthread/pthread.h:257-266`; `pthread.c:987-1008`). The non-SMP `sched_yield` call still lowers and restores its own task priority through `SetTaskPri`; the single-CPU contended named-semaphore once lock remains the only selected direct caller route found (`sched.c:46-68`; `pthread.c:758-779,987-1008`; `semaphore.c:43-59,117-124`). No once call or contention was run.

EK8800 pthread waiter caller recheck (2026-10-14; no new candidate): followed the bit-31 allocation case through selected `pthread_barrier_wait` and `sem_wait`/`sem_timedwait`. Barrier waiters loop on the barrier generation predicate around `pthread_cond_wait`, and the completing thread broadcasts; a missed bit-31 wake can therefore leave a barrier generation blocked. Semaphore waiters likewise loop on `sem->value` around `pthread_cond_timedwait`, while `sem_post` increments the value before signaling, so this path does not claim consumption of a nonexistent count but can fail to wake a blocked waiter. The undefined shift in signal-mask construction remains conditional on allocation of bit 31; no signal exhaustion or wait was run.
HPET name-attribute report reconciliation (EK760, 2026-10-14): restored the detailed finding after the coverage row's ID was found to have no report heading. Re-read both string cases against the public clock-source tag comments and all in-tree `GetCSAttrsA` references. The getter's one-byte pointer-address store is incompatible with either a pointer-sized string result or a complete caller-buffer string; the tag contract omits a buffer length, supporting pointer-output semantics. HPET init passes `TAG_DONE`, and no in-tree query reaches the defect, so the report limits impact to external clients. The main-index count is updated; no external call was made.

ARM bootstrap-affinity follow-up (EK8907, 2026-10-14): traced both native `cpu_InitBootStrap` mask allocations through `KrnAllocCPUMask`, each selected scheduler's explicit NULL-means-anywhere rule, the RUN-to-READY shared-list transition, and the bootstrap task's post-registration WFI loop. The code documents this context as CPU-only but does not handle affinity allocation failure. Qualified the consequence as conditional migration/per-core scheduling inconsistency; no specific crash is established. Current earlier list-head findings EK153/EK726 prevent the normal path until corrected. Source-only; no allocation failure, migration, or boot.

BCM27xx timed-out secondary ownership follow-up (EK8908, 2026-10-14): traced each stack/TLS allocation to the one-second `bcm27xx_wait_core` timeout branch. The branch unlocks and continues without reclaiming or recording the buffers; if the core never starts they remain allocated, while freeing at timeout is unsafe for a late starter (EK8903). Added a conditional memory-leak candidate and qualified the firmware-dependent trigger. No timeout or boot was induced.

EK8905 exception-mask caller census (2026-10-14): searched all maintained C/header/assembly sources for `SetExcept`, `tc_SigExcept`, and `tc_ExceptCode`. The only production `SetExcept` caller is pthread's async-cancel setup/teardown; `USE_ASYNC_CANCEL` has no active definition in this checkout (`compiler/pthread/pthread.c:40`). EK8800 selected-caller cross-check (optional BTHID GUI): `bGUITask` allocates `nhb_TrackingSignal` only after its MUI app/window is constructed and forms `sigmask` with signed `1 <<` before its event loop; the HID worker later forms the same mask while signaling the GUI (`rom/bluetooth/classes/bthid/bthid.gui.c:1604-1617`; `bthid.class.c:973-976`). JanoEditor signal-mask caller cross-check (EK8800, 2026-10-14): traced `create_port()`'s `CreateMsgPort` allocation and returned `(ULONG)(1 << port->mp_SigBit)` through both duplicate-instance forwarding and Preferences IPC waits (`workbench/tools/Edit/Events.c:437-474,480-491`; callers `Jed.c:67` and `Prefs.c:529`). UP public-port lookup cross-check (EK8913, 2026-10-14): traced `FindPort` through `FindName` on non-ExecSMP, `RemPort` and `DeleteMsgPort`, then verified the selected WaitForPort poll caller. `FindPort`'s list lock is SMP-only; only the writer enters Forbid, so an already-running search can be preempted between node access and `GetSucc`, then resume after the owner unlinks/frees the current MsgPort. This is traversal lifetime, distinct from EK29's returned-pointer use after lookup. No schedule or port removal was run.

Pthread mutex attribute getter signature recheck (EK8916, 2026-10-14): compared `pthread_mutexattr_gettype`'s public declaration and selected body (`compiler/pthread/pthread.h:474`; `pthread.c:232-242`) with the POSIX interface. Both AROS declarations use a mutable attribute pointer while the function only reads `kind`; POSIX declares the attribute pointer const. The source-compatibility consequence is limited to const-qualified callers under diagnostics-as-errors. The selected manifest copies the header and links `pthread.c` (`compiler/pthread/mmakefile.src:7-15,17-45`). This is distinct from EK617's declarations with no implementation. No client was compiled; broader attribute clients remain open.

ahi.device CMD_RESET caller cross-check (OD2858; no new Exec finding): followed the driver’s two TermIO calls through Exec `ReplyMsg`, `InternalPutMsg`, and `AddTail`. ReplyMsg sets NT_REPLYMSG and unconditionally appends the node; AddTail overwrites the node links without checking prior membership. A second reply while the first remains queued therefore self-links or otherwise damages the message-port list, while an earlier WaitIO can consume the first completion before reset returns. This confirms OD2858 as an ahi.device caller/lifecycle defect; no additional generic Exec defect was added. No reply-port operation was run.
Pthread semaphore count and timeout-argument recheck (2026-10-14; no new finding): reread `sem_init`, `sem_post`, `sem_timedwait` and `pthread_cond_timedwait`. `sem_init` rejects initial values above `SEM_VALUE_MAX`; `sem_post` checks the upper bound while holding `sem->lock` and returns `EOVERFLOW` before increment; timed waits validate `tv_nsec` in the selected condition-wait helper. `sem_wait` intentionally passes a null deadline, and the helper skips timer setup for that path. Existing findings EK607, EK623, EK625, EK628 and EK8910 remain the concrete semaphore cases; no additional overflow or invalid-nanoseconds candidate was established. No semaphore operation was run.
Genmodule output-finalization inventory recheck (EK8825, 2026-10-14; no separate finding): enumerated the `fclose` sites across `tools/genmodule/*.c` and traced each command arm in `genmodule.c:14-83`. The normal successful path ignores close-time failure in the generated-output writers, including stack/register stubs, link entries, interface/inline/prototype headers, function lists, skeletons, thunks, start/end sources and library-base helpers; writers that test `ferror` do so before close and still ignore a later flush error. `writeincclib` leaves its one output stream for process exit, which likewise does not propagate the delayed flush status. The selected `%build_module` generation commands invoke the affected outputs, so these cases remain within EK8825. No additional failure mode beyond unchecked output completion was established; no disk fault or generator run was induced.

M68K AbortIO result/shadow follow-up (EK482, 2026-10-15): compared Exec's vector-dispatch return and timer.device's success/error mutations with the generated M68K thunk and A-line dispatcher. The thunk returns literal zero and omits `io_sync_back`, unlike neighboring DoIO/CheckIO/WaitIO; dispatcher copies the thunk result to guest D0. Timer.device returns -1 for a request already marked NT_REPLYMSG and sets IOERR_ABORTED on successful cancellation. Restored EK482 in the report for false success and stale guest IOStdReq fields. Optional m68kemu target only; no guest binary/device operation was run.

M68K ChildOrphan return follow-up (EK481, 2026-10-15): matched the Exec FD declaration to native ChildOrphan's success/error returns and the generated thunk; it drops the result and returns literal zero. The M68K dispatcher copies that value to guest D0. Restored EK481 for an invalid/non-child task ID being reported as successfully orphaned. No guest task operation was run.

M68K Intuition zero-return wrapper recheck (EK483, 2026-10-15): enumerated all 71 zero-only generated Intuition wrappers and compared them with `intuition.conf` and native implementations. Eight declare scalar results (`AddGadget`, `ModifyIDCMP`, `RemoveGadget`, `SetMenuStrip`, `AddGList`, `RemoveGList`, `ActivateGadget`, `SetAttrsA`); two declare pointers (`LockPubScreenList`, `GetDefaultPubScreen`). The thunks return zero for all ten. Confirmed LockPubScreenList obtains PubScrListLock before returning the list, so a guest checking the null result and skipping unlock can retain the semaphore. Restored EK483; pointer returns require shadow translation. No emulated GUI call was run.

M68K Commodities return follow-up (EK484, 2026-10-15): compared all 17 zero-only Commodities wrappers against `commodities.conf`; only ActivateCxObj and SetCxObjPri are declared non-void. Their native implementations return the active state and priority from before the change, respectively, while both generated thunks return literal zero. In-tree commodities tools ignore these results, so scope the effect to guest clients that query the prior state. Restored EK484; no guest call was run.

M68K graphics thunk return recheck and report/index reconciliation (EK386; 2026-10-15, detailed entry restored 2026-10-24): compared all 93 zero-only generated graphics wrappers against `rom/graphics/graphics.conf`; nine declare non-void returns: `BltBitMap`, `MrgCop`, `MakeVPort`, `OrRectRegion`, `ClearRectRegion`, `XorRectRegion`, `WritePixelLine8`, `WritePixelArray8`, and `SetWriteMask`. Their native implementations return plane counts, operation/status values, plotted-pixel counts, or `-1`, while each generated wrapper discards the result and returns zero; Moira writes that value to guest D0. Restored the detailed EK386 entry and master-index link, and consolidated historical GD1759 into this shared m68kemu ABI finding. No maintained guest caller consuming these returns was established; no emulated vector was invoked.
PC APIC heartbeat-finalizer return recheck (EK562, 2026-10-15): verified the reset path replaces the registered heartbeat with `APICHeartbeatFinalizer`, an `int` function with no return, before APIC timer shutdown (`arch/all-pc/kernel/apic_ia32.c:740-747,758-789`). `krnRunExceptionHandlers` ORs its result and the selected `cpu_Trap` path halts on a zero aggregate for non-spurious vectors (`rom/kernel/addexceptionhandler.c:184-185`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/cpu_traps.c:90-115`). Kept the trigger conditional on heartbeat delivery during the replacement-to-disable window and the consequence conditional on the undefined return value. Restored detailed EK562; no reset or interrupt was run.
InitKickTags duplicate-resident recheck (EK08, 2026-10-15): re-read `CopyResidents`, priority sorting and the selected `InitCode` loop (`rom/exec/initkicktags.c:54-82,105-120,160-178`; `rom/exec/initcode.c:57-96`). The rejection predicate rejects any equal-version candidate even if its priority is higher, and `CopyResidents` appends a rejected candidate; `InitCode` later visits every entry, so same-name valid preserved KickTags are not deduplicated before initialization. The selected m68k Amiga boot preserves KickTag pointers from a valid previous SysBase (`arch/m68k-amiga/boot/start.c:751-758,881-883`); no checked-in KickTag producer was found, so this remains a conditional external/custom boot-data candidate. Restored detailed EK08; no module or reset was run.

ARM processor-probe affinity ownership recheck (EK8918, 2026-10-15): traced `Processor_Init`'s per-secondary `KrnAllocCPUMask`/`TASKTAG_AFFINITY` through `NewAddTask` → `InitETask` → ARM `PrepareContext` and `CleanupETask` (`arch/arm-native/processor/processor_init.c:55-70`; `rom/exec/newaddtask.c:270-272,305-309`; `rom/exec/exec_util.c:133-163,245-256`; `arch/arm-all/exec/preparecontext.c:37-46`). Confirmed successful tag handling overwrites the mask allocated by `InitETask`, and cleanup frees only the replacement pointer. Kept separate from EK8790's caller-owned mask leak when context creation fails before the affinity tag is adopted. No task or allocation was run; source-only.

ARM32/ARMEB per-CPU idle-task affinity ownership follow-up (EK8918 broadened, 2026-10-16): checked `Exec_ARMCPUInit`'s `KrnAllocCPUMask`/`TASKTAG_AFFINITY` caller against common ETask initialization and both ARM/ARMEB `PrepareContext` implementations (`arch/arm-native/exec/platform_init.c:37-90`; `arch/arm-all/exec/preparecontext.c:37-46`; `arch/armeb-all/exec/preparecontext.c:37-46`). INITLIB sections are emitted in numeric priority order by `gensets`, and Exec traverses the set forward; the priority -127 SMP hook therefore pins the boot task before the priority-0 CPU initializer creates idle tasks (`tools/collect-aros/gensets.c:41-63`; `rom/exec/exec_init.c:278`; `platform_init.c:248-288`). These children also inherit a concrete affinity and lose the mask allocated by `InitETask` when PrepareContext adopts the caller mask. Broadened EK8918 to include successful per-CPU idle-task creation as well as processor probes; no additional ID. No task or allocation was run; source-only.

BCM2712 interrupt-table bound follow-up (EK8919, 2026-10-15): traced the GIC IAR mask and spurious threshold through `krnRunIRQHandlers` into the fixed `kb_Interrupts[384]` table. `KrnAddIRQHandler` rejects >=384 but the platform dispatch path does not. Narrowed the trigger to valid SPI IDs 384–1019; 1020–1023 are special interrupt numbers, not SPIs. The platform init disables the distributor but does not clear the per-INTID enable registers; retained the finding conditionally on an enabled unsupported SPI being delivered. No hardware state or interrupt was run.

ARM processor-probe affinity cross-check (2026-10-15; EK797/EK8918): re-read the mask-allocation-failure route. `KrnAllocCPUMask` returns NULL, `PrepareContext` still adopts the present `TASKTAG_AFFINITY` tag and stores NULL, and the ARM scheduler defines NULL as run-anywhere; `ReadProcessorInformation` captures the executing core MPIDR and `Processor_FillTopology` assigns it to the requested index. PC boot-pitch scope recheck (EK8920): compared the parallel Multiboot1 producer and selected i386 GRUB entries against the Multiboot2 GOP path. Multiboot1 copies its framebuffer pitch into the same 16-bit VBE fields, but the shared v1 header sets `mode_type=1` (text preference), the i386 GRUB2 default requests the `multiboot` v1 entry, and the explicit listed VESA entries call `vesa_setup`/BIOS mode selection; no checked-in ordinary i386 producer path establishes a >65,535-byte framebuffer pitch. Kept EK8920 scoped to x86-64 Multiboot2 GOP, where the header requests an unconstrained best 32-bpp mode and the UEFI default path is selected. No bootloader or video mode was run. Source-only.

Exec SMP Signal/RemTask recheck (2026-10-15; EK832 retained, no duplicate): re-read the full queued-signal route from `Signal`'s `task->tc_State`/affinity branch through PC `core_DoCallIPI`, the hook-list drain, `signal_hook`, and `RemTask` cleanup (`rom/exec/signal.c:24-34,90-107,170-247`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/kernel_ipi.c:92-105,195-221,224-285`; `rom/exec/remtask.c:97-128,165-181`). PC does not define `KERNEL_IPI_CALL_CANCELABLE`, so `Exec_CancelSignalIPIs` compiles to an empty body there; the asynchronous IPI retains a raw `Task *` and the hook later dereferences it. The selected PC boot aggregate includes `security.library`; its root-only `secKill` can reach `RemTask` for an ordinary task. A direct C-call census found no maintained `SetTaskAffinity` production caller beyond selected affinity setup paths and tests, so EK832 remains conditional on an external privileged caller configuring affinity and removing the target during the queued-hook window. This is distinct from EK473's already-running remote task lifetime and EK830's concurrent double removal. No signal, IPI, or task teardown was run. Source-only.


Current Exec/Kernel report reconciliation (2026-10-15): the detailed report has 338 unique numbered EK headings and no duplicate IDs. The 337-finding checkpoint above predates the latest restorations; inventory and file-by-file review remain in progress. Source-only.


PC APIC descriptor-allocation order recheck (2026-10-15; no new finding): read the full `arch/all-pc/kernel/apic.c` body against ACPI MADT registration and `platform_post`. The APIC-support hook counts each Local APIC entry before the parser allocates `APICData` as header plus `acpi_apicCnt` CPU records; the parse hook starts `apic_count` at one for the BSP and appends only enabled non-BSP entries. `ictl_Initialize` reaches `core_APIC_Probe` only when ACPI did not provide `kb_APIC`. Therefore the suspected probe-allocation-one-then-ACPI-appends-many overflow does not follow the selected initialization order. `core_APIC_GetNumberFromLocal` searches only the populated count, and mask paths remain covered by EK9149. No MADT, APIC hardware or affinity operation was run. Source-only.

PC CPU-mask invalid-ID candidate check (2026-10-15; no new finding): reviewed `core_APIC_CPUInMask`'s `TASKAFFINITY_ANY` branch, which returns TRUE without validating `cpuNo`, against the public `KrnCPUInMask` input contract (`rom/kernel/cpuinmask.c:24-33`) and every selected callsite in Exec, task.resource, kernel IPI, and PC boot/SMP setup. Maintained callers supply a current CPU number or iterate `0..KrnGetCPUCount()-1`; none submit an arbitrary out-of-range ID. Keep the invalid-ID behavior as an external caller-contract lead rather than adding it to EK9149. The signed shift for logical CPU numbers 31 modulo 32 remains the separate in-range issue. No mask operation was run. Source-only.

MinGW ExecBase failure cleanup resolution (2026-10-15; no finding): traced the MinGW kernel entry return through shared `kick`, which displays a modal error and returns the kernel status, then through `bootstrap` and the hosted `main` (`arch/all-mingw32/kernel/kernel_startup.c:147-149`; `arch/all-hosted/bootstrap/kickstart.c:15-20`; `bootstrap.c:415`; `arch/all-hosted/bootstrap/main.c:6-8`). pthread condition-wait caller recheck (2026-10-15; no new finding): followed `pthread_cond_wait` and `_pthread_cond_timedwait` into every maintained direct caller. `pthread_barrier_wait` uses the unbounded wait in two phase loops (`pthread.c:487-519`); barriers initialize their condition and lock before publication (`:421-433`), and the repository has no barrier wait caller outside the implementation/declarations. The only direct timed-wait caller is `sem_timedwait` (`semaphore.c:226-254`), whose semaphore count is rechecked in a loop for successful/spurious condition returns; EK8910 remains the distinct simultaneous condition-plus-timeout path that returns before rechecking. Partition FileSystem.resource caller/locking follow-up (2026-10-15; EK8925): traced Mount `PatchDosNode` into `GetFileSysEntry`, the partition library `AddBootFileSystem` wrapper and `AddFS`, the selected PFS3 `AddToFSResource` call in handler initialization, ExecSMP `Forbid` semantics, optional CDFS unlinking, and DISK-078. `AddBootFileSystem` releases `bootSem` before `AddFS`; both `AddFS` and PFS3 use processor-local `Forbid` around their duplicate scan and insertion, so concurrent same-DOS-type registration can publish duplicate nodes and loaded segments. The sole in-tree direct AddBootFileSystem caller is sequential boot scanning; PFS3 initialization is an in-tree producer but no overlapping same-type trigger was established. The separate failed-load FileSysEntry leak is already DISK-078 and was not duplicated. No registration was run. Source-only.


Mount EK8921 caller/ownership recheck (2026-10-15): traced both selected `readmountlist` and `readmountfile` callers through `mount`'s no-handler return and their `FreeStuff` cleanup. `PatchDosNode` explicitly leaves the node unchanged when `GetFileSysEntry` finds no match (`workbench/c/Mount.c:1428-1448`); `FreeStuff` only frees parsed global strings; the local unregistered `DeviceNode` and its name, startup-message, and environment allocations are not passed back to either caller and remain unreleased. EK8921 is confirmed; no mount was run. Source-only.


PFS3 FileSystem.resource producer follow-up (2026-10-15; EK8925 scope refined): confirmed `AddToFSResource` is compiled for AROS and called from each selected PFS3 `Initialize` path (`rom/filesys/pfs3/fs/init.c:305-311`; PFS3 manifest includes `fsresource.c`). Its same-DOS-type search, allocation, and AddHead are inside local `Forbid` only (`fsresource.c:26-72`). Thus same-type PFS3 initializations can race one another as well as with partition `AddFS` on ExecSMP; this is the cross-CPU list race captured by EK8925. No concurrent handler initialization was run. Source-only.

FileSystem.resource public-caller recheck (2026-10-15; EK8925 trigger qualification): a repository-wide search found one checked-in `AddBootFileSystem` call, from DOSBoot `checkbootpartition` (`rom/dosboot/bootscan.c:242`). WaitPort unlocked-return candidate restoration (EK276, 2026-10-15): restored the ledger-tracked candidate after rechecking `WaitPort` and `GetMsg` under the same message-list lock. Log provider-list concurrency recheck (2026-10-15; EK490/EK496 not promoted): traced every maintained `lrh_Entries`/`lrb_Providers` access in `rom/log`. Per-producer `lrh_Entries` is initialized and modified by `logAddEntryA`/`logRemEntry`, but there is no active traversal of that list; `logNextEntry` traverses only the built-in global provider list. `logFinalise` walks `lrb_Providers` but its match body is still `TODO` and performs no mutation or resource release. LDDemon-to-RemDevice caller lifetime follow-up (2026-10-15): confirmed the selected `LDFlush` device path holds `Forbid` around `RemDevice` (`rom/lddemon/lddemon.c:697-700,745-755`); the Exec vector nests `Forbid`/`Permit` around the expunge callback (`rom/exec/remdevice.c:65-83`). Exec `AllocSignal` caller spot-check (2026-10-15; no new finding): repository search found 98 C/header references, including documentation/declarations; this is an inventory count, not a completed caller census. Traced selected `input.device` startup: `NewCreateTask` seeds the input task's `tc_SigAlloc` from `TaskSigAlloc` (`rom/exec/newcreatetaska.c:220`; initialized to `0xFFFF` in `prepareexecbase.c:319`), first allocates the command MsgPort signal, then `processevents.c` allocates `ResetSig` (`rom/devs/input/input.c:68-76`; `processevents.c:198`). Thus this path obtains low signal bits 16 and 17 and does not reach AllocSignal exhaustion or the bit-31 shift boundary; related signed shifts in its wait mask remain within range. This caller does not establish a separate failure-path defect. Other AllocSignal/Signal clients, including optional drivers and GUI paths, remain caller-review work. No task was started; source-only.

Exec `AllocSignal` failure-path caller follow-up (2026-10-15; SD-card bus lead not promoted): `BusTask` does not check failure of its media or command signal allocations before forming `Wait` masks and later shifting those fields (`rom/devs/sdcard/sdcard_bus.c:1695-1712,1738`; same-file command waiters at `:1019,1285,1299,1303,1567,1662`). Traced selected construction: `NewCreateTask` reserves one bit for `sdcb_MsgPort` (`sdcard_init.c:80-88`; `rom/exec/newcreatetaska.c:216-233`), then `sdcard_OpenTimer` creates one task-owned reply port (`timer.c:20-58`), and BusTask requests exactly three more bits. A fresh task starts with the normal 16 allocatable high signal bits; five allocations do not exhaust that pool, and no additional signal allocation occurs on this selected entry path before those requests. Thus the negative-shift branch is not established for the in-tree SD-card bus task; behavior under external task mutation or a changed caller remains outside this call-path check. No driver task or device was started. Source-only.

AArch64 Raspberry Pi EK8929 caller recheck (2026-10-15; no new finding): reread `getElfSize`, `loadElf`, and the two boot passes. On rejected core headers, `getElfSize` explicitly stores zero for both sizes but still returns 1; boot ignores that status, reserves/maps from those sizes, assigns `entry = kernel_virt`, ignores `loadElf` failure, and still reaches the handoff when `/memory` exists. The package pass likewise logs “ELF loaded OK” after ignoring a rejected member result. Corrected the detailed trigger wording to “package-member ELF” so it does not imply a length-bound contract that EK8931 separately says is absent. No image was loaded; generated package validity remains unverified. Source-only.

EK799 native-scheduler source recheck (2026-10-15; no new finding): verified both `arch/arm-native` and `arch/aarch64-native` select their scheduler bodies for Raspberry Pi targets. Each switch-out removes a running node through `exec_TaskRemoveRunning` and later enqueues it through `exec_TaskEnqueueReady`; these helpers take the list locks separately. The scheduler holds `tc_SpinLock` during the task transition, but `FindTask` does not acquire it, so a lookup can observe neither list during the handoff. This confirms the report’s Raspberry Pi SMP condition; caller consequences and exact race windows remain source-derived, with no interleaving run. Source-only.


Exec/Kernel m68k Amiga resident-table follow-up (2026-10-15): added EK8932 after tracing `ROMLoad` allocations through `scanMemLists` into `scanResidents(..., FALSE)`. The loadseg-only path is bounded to one match, but the KICKMEM scan appends all matches without checking the remaining fixed-table capacity. Whether a supported ROM image reaches the overflow threshold remains unverified. No boot was run. Source-only.


Exec/Kernel m68k Amiga resident-list consumer follow-up (2026-10-15; EK8932): traced `BootS->reslist` through `CollectKickResidents` at `arch/m68k-amiga/boot/start.c:450-491,1017-1024`. `countres` and `copyres` consume the zero-terminated/tagged list without a separate capacity parameter, so they rely on the bootstrap table terminator; an EK8932 overrun can therefore also invalidate this downstream traversal. On an intact list, allocation uses the counted old+new upper bound, duplicate replacement reduces rather than increases output length, and priority sorting covers the resulting count. No independent consumer defect established. `start.c` remains open for earlier saved-alert production, boot-input variants, and broader platform contracts. No boot was run. Source-only.


Exec/Kernel m68k Amiga resident scan boundary recheck (2026-10-15; EK8932 only): re-read `scanResidents` for both `LoadSegment` callers. The file-local segment scan uses `end - 26`; for a segment shorter than the Resident header size, the loop condition is false on ordinary non-wrapping addresses, so this check did not establish a short-segment overread. The KICKMEM append remains independently unchecked when the number of matches exceeds remaining table capacity. No malformed segment was supplied. Source-only.

Exec/Kernel pthread condition initialization caller census (2026-10-15; EK604 retained with external trigger): searched maintained C/header/assembly and found `pthread_barrier_init`, `sem_init`, `_pthread_cond_broadcast`, and `_pthread_cond_timedwait` as the only direct calls. Barrier and semaphore construction are sequential within their init functions; the two lazy guards are the only concurrent-first-use route for a `PTHREAD_COND_INITIALIZER` object. No in-tree static initializer use was found, and explicit concurrent reinitialization remains outside this finding. No thread interleaving was run. Source-only.


Exec SetSignal selected input-device timer caller follow-up (2026-10-15; no new finding): `rom/devs/input/processevents.c` builds the key-repeat mask from the dedicated key-timer reply port and includes it in the worker wait mask (`:260-266,459-470`). Its abort macro waits for `WaitIO` completion before `SetSignal(0, keytimersig)` clears any residual notification (`:47-52`), so this selected timer cleanup does not clear a completion signal before the I/O has completed. The signal mask update itself remains protected by the per-task SMP spinlock in `setsignal.c`; no input device or timer was run. The broader maintained SetSignal caller set remains open. Source-only.


Exec/Kernel ServiceTask tombstone-requeue recheck (2026-10-15; no new finding): traced the `TS_TOMBSTONED` retry against the selected SMP state transitions. The service task requeues when CPU-affinity routing is enabled and it is not running on the tombstoned task's saved CPU (`rom/exec/service.c:48-63`); the selected PC/ARM32/AArch64 setup enables `EXECF_CPUAffinity` before secondary CPUs start (`arch/all-pc/kernel/smp_exec.c:60`; `arch/arm-native/exec/platform_init.c:258`; `arch/aarch64-native/exec/platform_init.c:207`). When the remover and service task share the target CPU, the service task cannot run until the self-removing task reaches its dispatch. If the service task runs elsewhere, the target CPU continues independently through `RemTask`'s `TS_INVALID` store and dispatch (`rom/exec/remtask.c:135-163`), after which the queued request can be reclaimed. The retry can briefly redrain the same message while the remote CPU completes those instructions, but no selected-path evidence establishes a persistent spin or starvation defect. Existing EK807 remains the separate premature-reclamation race when the remote service frees the TCB before local dispatch is safe. No SMP interleaving was run. Source-only.

Exec SetTaskPri full-body/caller recheck (2026-10-15; EK273/EK833/EK842 retained, no new ID): reread all of `rom/exec/settaskpri.c` and the maintained direct C caller set. Its SMP order is task spinlock then the state-selected list lock; ready tasks are removed/re-enqueued under the ready-list write lock, wait tasks only have their priority field changed, and remote running tasks capture `iet_CpuAffinity` before releasing locks and call `KrnScheduleCPU` afterward. The captured affinity is an owned cpumask freed by `CleanupETask`, so this remains EK273's borrowed-mask teardown race; no independent lock-order, list-reorder, or scheduler defect was established. Selected self-demotion and delayed-yield consequences remain EK833; ready-task CPU-routing latency remains the qualified EK842 candidate. Direct callers include pthread scheduling/create, Bluetooth and USB worker setup, ChangeTaskPri, Intuition freeze handling, animation playback, SysMon, reset callbacks, ACPICA, PC spinlock handling, AHI, and AROSTCP; existing caller-specific issues remain attributed to EK833/OD812 or their subsystem reports. Platform scheduler and external-client review remains open. No task or scheduler event was run. Source-only.

Kernel BootMsg/restart caller follow-up (2026-10-15; no new finding): traced the Efika `SC_REBOOT` call through the initial Open Firmware entry contract and startup label. `bootstrap.c` stores `KERNEL_PHYS_BASE` in `KRN_KernelBase` (`:108,392-393`) and invokes that address as the kernel image entry; `kernel_init.c` places global `start` in `.aros.init`, where it preserves the incoming tag pointer and dispatches through `target_address` to `kernel_cstart` (`:28,31-34,128-138,165-177`). The selected reboot handler reads the same tag as the restart entry and calls it with `BootMsg` (`arch/ppc-chrp/efika/kernel/syscall.c:89-106`); `kernel_cstart` recognizes `msg == BootMsg` and skips copying the tag list again (`kernel_init.c:193-195`). Although `KRN_KernelBase` is named like a data address, the selected Efika image deliberately uses its base as the entry point, so this cast/call is not an invalid function pointer. PC warm restart separately passes retained `BootMsg` to `core_Kick`/`kernel_cstart` (`arch/all-pc/kernel/syscall.c:230-255`). The `rom/kernel/getbootinfo.c` accessor simply returns the global pointer. Other target restart and tag-payload lifetime paths remain open; no reboot was invoked. Source-only.


ARM native scheduling IPI caller follow-up (EK273 rechecked; no new finding): traced both ARM32 and AArch64 `KrnScheduleCPU` overrides through selected `Signal`, `SetTaskPri` and `NewAddTask` callers into the IPI receiver. Each override synchronously copies the caller's one-word affinity mask into a scalar before the mailbox call and does not retain the pointer. This does not close EK273: concurrent `Exec_CleanupETask` can free that mask after the caller unlocks but before the synchronous read. Updated both per-file rows to separate the helper's immediate-copy behavior from the existing caller/teardown lifetime race. No IPI or task-removal interleaving was run. Source-only.

Exec reset callback / PCIUSB caller cross-check (2026-10-15; no new EK candidate): verified `AddResetCallback` calls `Enqueue` without checking or unlinking the supplied node (`rom/exec/addresetcallback.c:56-61`; `enqueue.c:67-98`). Exec Signal/RemTask cancellation ordering recheck (2026-10-15; no new finding): audited the suspected queue-sweep/dequeue race in both selected ARM32 and AArch64 `kernel_ipi.c` implementations. `Exec_CancelSignalIPIs` takes and releases `tc_SpinLock` before sweeping; `Signal` checks task state and commits under that lock. The sweep and FIQ drain use the same per-CPU queue lock, and the drain publishes its executing callback before releasing it. Thus callbacks committed before the barrier are either removed while queued or observed as executing; none can be newly committed after the sweep. PC EK832 remains distinct because its selected header disables this cancellation path. No SMP interleaving was run. Source-only.
