SetSignal exception-mask dispatch follow-up (EK8940 retained conditionally, 2026-10-15): rechecked the exception scheduler gate and all selected direct `SetExcept`/nonzero `SetSignal` call sites. `core_Schedule` gives `TF_EXCEPT` precedence but does not infer it from the signal masks (`rom/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:35-43`); `Exception` consumes the intersection only after dispatch (`rom/exec/exception.c:58-75`). The sole selected `SetExcept` production caller is pthread creation (`compiler/pthread/pthread_create.c:129,176`); its selected worker path has no matching `SetSignal` of the exception bit. Other positive-mask direct `SetSignal` calls are Bluetooth’s dynamic self-signal restoration and a Bluetooth task’s Ctrl-C bit; no selected task-exception mask is set on those tasks. Thus no in-tree reproducer was established; retain EK8940 only for external/direct clients that enable a task exception and then set that same received bit with SetSignal. No task or exception was run. Source-only.


TLSF autogrow callback lock-boundary trace (EK172/EK871 recheck, 2026-10-15; no new finding): compared `nommu_AllocMem`'s per-header SMP spinlock around non-`MEMF_SEM_PROTECTED` managed callbacks with TLSF's autogrow callback (`memory_nommu.c:35-54`; `tlsf.c:489-543,1401-1416`). Global MemHeaders created or converted by the kernel use fixed TLSF areas and leave `autogrow_get_fn` unset. Autogrow is configured only by private pool `init_Pool`; the pool allocator calls `tlsf_malloc` through `AllocPooled` on that private header, not by walking it in `SysBase->MemList`, and its callback obtains backing via global `AllocMem`. Thus the apparent recursive same-header spinlock is not reached by the selected TLSF setup. Existing EK871 covers ignored private-pool initialization and the AArch64 additional-range header publication after failed TLSF initialization; EK172 remains the unchecked growth-size addition; no recursive-lock finding added. No pool exhaustion or allocation was induced. Source-only.

SetSignal selected USB MassStorage media-reinsert caller trace (2026-10-15; no new finding): checked `StorageTask`'s direct `SetSignal(0xffffffff, timer_reply_bit)` against its wait loop and timer request lifecycle (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/MassStorage/storage_task.c:172-180,209-218,232-267,334-351`). Removal aborts and waits for the old timer request before marking the device absent; reinsertion sets the timer signal bit to force the next wait iteration through media sensing, then the common tail submits the next two-second request. This is intentional self-wakeup and does not establish overlap with an outstanding timer. No USB device or timer was run. Other SetSignal callers remain pending.

SetSignal console CharMap/ConClip reply handshake trace (2026-10-15; no new finding): traced `charmapcon_copy`'s stack reply port and clear-before-`PutMsg` sequence through the selected ConClip receiver and Exec `WaitPort` (`rom/devs/console/charmapconclass.c:1345-1370`; `workbench/c/ConClip.c:395-419`; `rom/exec/waitport.c:62-89`; `rom/exec/putmsg.c:71-106`). The receiver replies after processing the synchronous copy, and `WaitPort` rechecks the queued message after each wake, so the clear does not erase an early reply. The caller does not `GetMsg` the returned reply, leaving its node linked only in the stack-local reply port as the function exits; ConClip no longer accesses the message after `ReplyMsg`, and no retained reference or later list operation on that port was found, so no independent lifetime consequence is established. No copy interaction was run. Other SetSignal callers remain pending.

Classic Amiga pthread timed semaphore request cleanup trace (EK8950 added, 2026-10-15): followed `_obtain_sema_timed` through the `__AMIGA__ && !__MORPHOS__` queue insertion and timeout return, then through `ReleaseSemaphore` dequeue/ownership signaling. The timer-winning path leaves its stack-local `SemaphoreRequest` linked; later release can consume the stale request. Contrasted with the non-Amiga `Vacate` cleanup. Pthread timer-signal fallback timed-condition trace (EK8951 added, 2026-10-15): checked `OpenTimerDevice` fallback selection/SetSignal argument order against Exec SetSignal and the `_pthread_cond_timedwait` SendIO/Wait/timeout-result path. Unlike `_obtain_sema_timed`'s classic branch, the condition wait does not clear its timer-bit mask before waiting; pending CTRL-D therefore yields an immediate `ETIMEDOUT`. `sem_timedwait` retries this path while its count is zero. No signal exhaustion or timer operation was induced. Source-only.
Cause priority and PA_SOFTINT caller follow-up (2026-10-15; no new EK): corrected the input.device reachability note: its priority -128 reset handler is called directly by the keyboard reset-list walk, not submitted to `Cause` (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:200-208`; `rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:503-509`). Sampled selected PA_SOFTINT callers: PCIUSB/xHCI NAK timeout uses -16, OHCI/UHCI hub timers are zero-initialized and stay at priority 0, and USB Audio initializes its player callback priority to 0; each is within Cause’s documented -32..32 range (`rom/usb/pciusb/uhwcmd.c:249-269`; `workbench/devs/USB/drivers/{OHCI/ohciclass.c:76-82,UHCI/uhciclass.c:322-329}`; `rom/usb/classes/audio/usbaudio.class.c:3299-3302,3436-3442`). Cause architecture reentrancy boundary (2026-10-15; no new EK): traced the selected m68k-Amiga route from `Cause` through `CUSTOM_CAUSE(INTF_SOFTINT)`, Paula level-1 dispatch, `core_Cause(INTB_SOFTINT)`, and `SoftIntDispatch` (`rom/exec/cause.c:84-126,164-212`; `rom/exec/chipset.h:43-48`; `arch/m68k-amiga/kernel/amiga_irq.c:126-154,190-208`; `arch/m68k-amiga/kernel/sti.c:14-21`; selected in `arch/m68k-amiga/kernel/mmakefile.src:20-35`). During the softint callback, `KrnSti` enables Paula sources but does not lower the 68000 CPU interrupt mask set on level-1 exception entry; a newly requested level-1 softint therefore cannot nest before the current handler returns. The dispatcher can then consume the requeued node on its loop, and the retained Paula request can cause a later empty pass. This does not establish simultaneous callback execution on the selected single-CPU m68k path; EK8935 remains limited to ExecSMP shared-queue delivery. A checkout-wide lexical inventory found 61 `PA_SOFTINT` occurrences across 31 C/header/assembly files, including the definition, comments, and repeated flag transitions; that is a locator count, not a completed review of all 61 caller contexts. The remaining callers, target selection and callback lifetimes are still pending. No interrupt was run. Source-only.

PC APIC destination/command serialization recheck (EK8953, 2026-10-16): verified the per-CPU explicit-destination sender writes ICRH then ICRL without local interrupt masking, against the public interrupt-callable Signal contract, PC Signal-to-core_DoCallIPI route, selected NVMe completion Signal caller, target-mask handler scan, and hook recycling. PA_SOFTINT caller follow-through (2026-10-16; RTL8139 path checked, no new EK): inspected the selected RTL8139 port setup and all three relevant producers/consumers (`workbench/devs/networks/rtl8139/unit.c:321-470,478-501,512-638,1052-1078`; `handler.c:100-209`). The write-port action is enabled at unit initialization and re-enabled by `RTL8139_TX_IntF` after draining; `InternalPutMsg` can call `Cause` for each queued write. When the TX ring fills, the callback switches the action to `PA_IGNORE`, and the NIC completion interrupt or timeout callback directly calls `Cause` to restart it. Thus an interrupt-side direct `Cause` can race the task-side `InternalPutMsg`/`Cause` path on an ExecSMP build, subject to driver selection and execution overlap. This is another concrete caller shape consistent with EK8875's pre-lock queued-state race, not a separate generic defect; whether the RTL8139 build supports ExecSMP and the relevant IRQ concurrency is not yet established, so it is not counted as an additional confirmed trigger. The handler serializes task requests with `rtl8139u_unit_lock`, but does not serialize the IRQ/timeout paths against `Cause`. No interrupt was run. The lexical census remains incomplete for the other listed call sites.

PA_SOFTINT network callback follow-through (2026-10-16; e1000 caller path checked): `e1000` initializes the write port with `PA_SOFTINT` and its TX interrupt node (`workbench/devs/networks/e1000/unit.c:998-1022`); task-side `CmdWrite` queues requests through `PutMsg` (`handler.c:240-277`), and the single unit worker serializes `handle_request` with `e1ku_unit_lock` (`unit.c:598-605`; `handler.c:101-189`). The TX callback removes requests and updates shared `tx_ring` state without a callback-level lock (`unit.c:146-300`). While it runs, `SoftIntDispatch` has reset the node type and released the queue lock, so a later worker `PutMsg` can requeue the same node; ExecSMP delivery could overlap a second TX callback on another CPU, matching the generic EK8935 dispatch window and exposing unsynchronized ring/queue consumption. The e1000 x86 targets are declared in its module makefile, but their metatarget edges are commented (`workbench/devs/networks/e1000/mmakefile.src:3-5,18-24`); no checked-in boot/package route selecting e1000 alongside ExecSMP was established in this pass. Therefore this is recorded as a conditional caller/configuration trace, not as an additional confirmed finding or affected shipped configuration. The watchdog's direct `Cause` is commented out (`unit.c:330`); no interrupt or overlap was run.

PC IRQ walker/removal synchronization reconciliation (EK31/EK821; 2026-10-16): reread the complete selected `arch/all-pc/kernel/addirqhandler.c` plus generic `rom/kernel/remirqhandler.c`. PC `KrnAddIRQHandler` disables only the local CPU and mutates the chain without `kb_IntrSpinLock`; PC `krnRunIRQHandlers` traverses the same chain without the generic dispatcher's read lock. The selected generic remover takes the shared write lock, removes the node, and frees it, so that lock cannot exclude the PC dispatch walk or PC add path. Kept this under EK31's existing cross-CPU chain mutation/lifetime finding. Separately, PC `ForeachNodeSafe` passes shared `PlatformData.kb_LastIntr` as its cursor (`kernel_arch.h:82`; `addirqhandler.c:116-132`), while generic dispatch uses stack-local cursors; this remains EK821, a distinct simultaneous-dispatch cursor race. The selected `cpu_intr` path calls this PC walker (`cpu_intr.c:511-519`). No chain mutation or interrupt was run. Source-only.

PCNet32 PA_SOFTINT callback caller follow-up (EK8875/EK8935, 2026-10-16; no new finding): traced selected source definitions in `workbench/devs/networks/pcnet32/{handler.c,unit.c}`. `S2CmdWrite` queues on `WRITE_QUEUE` with `PutMsg` and, when the ring-full counter is 1..5, retries with direct `Cause(&pcnu_tx_int)` after `Delay` (`handler.c:237-261`). The port routes `PutMsg` to the same TX callback via `PA_SOFTINT`/`mp_SigTask`, configured at unit initialization (`unit.c:1131-1156`). `PCN32_TX_Int` reads the shared request head, copies into the selected TX buffer, advances `next_tx`, removes/replies the request and toggles PA_SOFTINT/PA_IGNORE without a cross-CPU lock (`unit.c:459-610`); the PCI ISR independently causes RX and TX-completion nodes (`:797-803`). This callback body is non-reentrant over its request queue and ring state if the same softint can be dispatched concurrently, matching EK8935's generic callback-overlap mechanism. The driver has an x86 module target, but its dependency is commented out of `workbench/devs/networks/mmakefile.src:10-11`; no checked-in default boot/package edge selecting PCNet32 together with ExecSMP was established. Treat as a conditional source caller trace, not an additional selected in-tree trigger. No network device, request or interrupt was run. Source-only.

Pthread CRT-hook expunge overlap recheck (2026-10-16; no new finding): re-read `compiler/pthread/pthread_create.c:63-91,134` and `compiler/crt/posixc/__threadhook.c:132-179`, plus the selected `compiler/crt/posixc/mmakefile.src` and `posixc.conf` build entries. The pthread worker snapshots callback addresses under the registry semaphore, releases it, then invokes them; posixc removes the hook and frees its task-storage slot under that semaphore during expunge. This leaves a mechanical snapshot-to-call lifetime window. However, the checked selected source/build paths establish no supported in-tree sequence that drops the last posixc open reference while another worker is paused in that window; the posixc configuration is expungeable, but routine CloseLibrary alone does not prove expunge while open references remain. Keep the overlap as an unresolved external lifecycle boundary, not a confirmed project bug. No task, expunge or hook was run. Source-only.

Pthread condition-variable shared-waiter caller recheck (2026-10-16; no new finding): traced the selected `pthread_cond_wait`/`pthread_cond_signal` wrappers through `_pthread_cond_timedwait` and `_pthread_cond_broadcast`, then through the barrier and unnamed/named semaphore callers. Waiter insertion and removal both hold `cond->semaphore`, as does the broadcast traversal, so the stack-local waiter is not removed while the signaler traverses it. The wait core reacquires the caller mutex, decrements `incond`, removes the waiter under the condition semaphore, and frees its signal before `pthread_testcancel`; cancellation therefore does not leave an ordinary condition waiter linked. Signal-mask shifting remains EK8800, unsynchronized lazy initialization of static condition variables remains EK604, and the selected semaphore's post/wait ordering remains EK628/EK625. `pthread_cond_destroy` concurrent with arbitrary waiters remains governed by caller synchronization; no in-tree concurrent destroy/use path was found. No condition wait, signal, barrier or semaphore was run. Source-only.

i386 kernel.resource failed-init publication caller follow-up (EK8965; 2026-10-16): traced the 64 KiB system-stack allocation failure through `PlatformInit` and the ordered INITLIB dispatcher. `Kernel_Init` has already called `AddResource`; that function enqueues the resource and publishes Exec’s global `KernelBase` before the platform hook (`rom/exec/addresource.c:62-100`). The false return stops `set_call_libfuncs`, and `Kernel_Init` returns NULL without reversing those effects (`compiler/libinit/libinit.c:24-47`; `rom/kernel/kernel_init.c:122-138`). `InitResident` only adds an AUTOINIT resource after a non-NULL initializer return, but the kernel’s self-publication has already occurred. This corroborates the existing generic finding with the i386 selected failure branch; no allocation failure or boot was induced. Source-only.

x86-64 interrupt-entry XMM-save alignment lead (2026-10-16; no finding): recalculated the fixed same-ring frame and found that `FXSData` follows the interrupted RSP modulo 16, while the handler uses `movaps`. Initially the selected `SoftIntDispatch` → `KrnSti` path looked like a concrete 8-mod-16 trigger, but the x86 STI interrupt shadow defers maskable interrupts through the following `ret`; after return, the caller resumes at its ABI-aligned call site. Thus that path does not establish a timer-triggered misaligned save. The selected x86-64 `KrnMapGlobal` and `KrnSetProtection` callers check for a NULL `SuperState` result and invoke `UserState` after the privileged operation. No defect established in this handoff. x86-64 CPL helper caller recheck (2026-10-16; no new finding): read `arch/all-pc/kernel/issuper.s` and traced its direct x86-64 PC users in `spinlock.c` and `spintrylock.c`, plus `KrnMapGlobal` and `KrnSetProtection`. The CS low-two-bit test returns true only at CPL 0; `and`/`xor` write EAX and clear any stale upper RAX bits. The spinlock callers use it to avoid task ownership for supervisor-mode acquisition, and the mapping callers use it to decide whether to enter `SuperState`. No defect established in the helper. PC spin try-lock atomic/caller recheck (2026-10-16; no new finding): reread the full `KrnSpinTryLock` body, its `spinlock_t` union/bit definitions and x86-64 `compare_and_exchange_byte/long` implementations. The read-side updater bit protects the plain 24-bit reader-count increment; locked operations serialize its acquisition/release with writer acquisition. The only maintained caller is the PC SMP AP-readiness loop: BSP holds each lock in write mode until that AP releases it, so try-read observes the write flag and returns NULL; a successful reader acquisition is released once. Although the read branch can spin while another reader owns the updater bit and the caller checks its deadline only after return, that internal branch is not reached by the selected write-held handshake. No additional selected defect established. External API callers, interrupt use and nonblocking expectations remain pending; no lock or CPU wake was exercised. Source-only.

PC spinlock owner-publication ordering recheck (2026-10-16; no new finding): compared `KrnSpinLock`, `KrnSpinTryLock`, `KrnSpinUnLock` and the selected caller classes. The lock word becomes held before task-owner publication, while unlock clears `s_Owner` before the lock word is released; a concurrent writer can briefly observe NULL and skip the existing priority-demotion path. This is a source-level timing window, but the checked selected PC clients that can contend either disable local interrupts around task-context critical sections (NVMe and interrupt-handler-list mutation), run under IRQ/trap context (scheduler/heartbeat/list readers), or use the AP readiness lock with no competing task writer. The synchronous IPI lock's completion release is in the target interrupt handler. No selected preemptible task-task reproducer was established; no finding is added. Public external callers and any documented interrupt/preemption contract remain unresolved. Source-only.

ARM32 scheduler/housekeeper EK807 recheck (2026-10-16; retained with narrower ordering): traced `Exec_SuicideSwitch` → `RemTask` → `core_Dispatch` against `ServiceTask` and ARM `cpu_Dispatch` (`arch/arm-native/exec/platform_init.c:225-245`; `rom/exec/remtask.c:135-163`; `arch/arm-native/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:242-307`; `rom/exec/service.c:48-91`; `arch/arm-native/kernel/kernel_cpu.c:502`). The service task's current CPU number is refreshed when it is dispatched. While the request is `TS_TOMBSTONED`, a service task on another CPU requeues it; once `RemTask` stores `TS_INVALID`, the common service branch frees the TCB without checking CPU affinity. Thus EK807 requires the requeued request to be dequeued again in the interval after that store and before local dispatch has finished reading the saved current-task pointer. This confirms the race's narrower timing rather than an immediate free from the first remote dequeue. No scheduling interleaving was run; source-only.

ARM CacheClearE/CachePreDMA caller recheck (2026-10-16; no new EK): compared the ARM Exec wrapper register operands with `SC_CACHECLEARE` extraction and the full `cache_clear_e` line-rounding/edge/sentinel loop (`arch/arm-native/exec/cachecleare.c:18-33`; `arch/arm-native/kernel/syscall.c:49-124,224-233`). The syscall receives the same r0-r2 values and issues DSB after maintenance. Traced ARM `CachePreDMA` through `KrnVirtualToPhysical`; it returns an affine translation within each low identity or high kernel-mapping region and leaves the requested length unchanged. Its only direct `arch/arm-native` caller is BCM2708 mailbox; that protocol documents 64-byte line ownership and checks caller start alignment. No selected local caller crossing the mapping boundary or wrapper/syscall mismatch established. Generic DMA clients packaged on ARM, cache hardware behavior and external inputs remain open; no DMA or cache operation was run. Source-only.

If the interface is absent, the second shutdown return reaches the null interface call instead. No Android startup or pipe failure was induced. Source-only.

Exec/Kernel EK8932 table-layout threshold recheck (2026-10-16): verified `BootMemHeader.res[256]` is followed immediately by `FakeBase`, and the pool is allocated with `MEMF_CLEAR` (`AROSBootstrap.c:53-65,432-446`). `scanResidents` searches for a free start only in indices 0..254 but appends every match without a bound. The 256th accumulated match consumes `res[255]` as data; the 257th writes `resptr[256]` into `FakeBase`'s first word (`ExecBase.LibNode.Node.ln_Succ`). The boot `countres` consumer has no capacity parameter and stops only on NULL (`arch/m68k-amiga/boot/start.c:394-405,456-470`), so the 257th pointer extends its traversal into the overwritten adjacent field. Refined EK8932's exact threshold/consequence; supported ROM resident-count feasibility remains open. No boot or resident scan was run. Source-only.

i386 processor.resource skipped-core API-contract recheck (EK8975; 2026-10-16; expanded): compared the per-core result contract in `rom/processor/getcoreinfo.c:26-62` with the i386 dispatch. i386 processor.resource affinity-mask ownership follow-up (EK8976; 2026-10-16): traced the successful CPU-0 query-task path. With APIC data, `KrnAllocCPUMask` allocates memory; i386 non-ExecSMP `PrepareContext` has no compiled-in affinity-tag consumer, and ETask cleanup also omits mask freeing. The processor initializer does not release the allocation after successful NewCreateTask. Secondary CPU indexes skip task creation before this allocation. This leaves one mask-sized leak per successful initialization (typically one ULONG); no boot or task creation was run. Source-only.


i386 processor.resource affinity-mask failure-path follow-up (EK8976 expanded; 2026-10-16): traced both NewCreateTask outcomes. The non-SMP i386 `PrepareContext` does not consume TASKTAG_AFFINITY; task cleanup omits mask freeing outside ExecSMP. On creation failure, `NewAddTask` calls `CleanupETask` and `NewCreateTask` frees only its MemList (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:305-309`; `newcreatetaska.c:257-263`), which does not own `taskAffinity`; on success, task exit also has no owner for it. Expanded EK8976 to cover either outcome after a non-NULL APIC mask allocation. No boot, task creation, or allocation failure was run. Source-only.

Generic linear allocator zero-length caller-scope refinement (EK16 review, 2026-10-16): `KrnAllocPages(NULL, 0, flags)` also reaches the faulty zero-page transition when the generic MMU page allocator is initialized: `mm_Allocate` rounds zero to `pages == 0`, accepts the first free block because `free >= pages`, and calls `SetBlockState(head, candidate, 0, P_ALLOC)`; at the first block, the helper decrements page index zero before storing (`rom/kernel/mm_linear.c:129-261,43-101`). This is the same zero-length root cause already represented in the allocator notes, not a separate finding. A full direct-call census still shows selected production callers passing positive loader lengths; no in-tree zero-length caller or checked-in generic `kb_PageSize` initializer establishes the trigger on current startup (EK639). Do not infer runtime reachability from the public vector alone. No allocation was made.

PC SMP online-count/startup confirmation recheck (EK9400; no new finding, 2026-10-16): reread the AP startup and affinity chain (`arch/all-pc/kernel/smp.c:118-147,217-318`; `smp_exec.c:28-60,158-190`; `acpi_apic.c:231-260`; `getcpucount.c:12-23`; `rom/exec/SetTaskAffinity.c:41-95`). ACPI publishes enabled APIC entries into `apic_count` before wake. A stack-allocation failure returns from `smp_Wake` without reducing that count; per-CPU wake failure/readiness timeout instead continues and reaches the unconditional success return. If bootstrap-task creation fails, `smp_Entry` still unlocks the AP-ready lock before halting, so the wake loop classifies the failed AP as ready. The unchanged discovered count is later exposed to affinity validation, which can accept a mask naming only a failed AP; active dispatchers then reject the task on all CPUs. This is already covered by EK9400. No AP startup or affinity request was run. Source-only.

EK8835 AP idle-task fallback recheck (no new finding, 2026-10-16): re-read the complete selected failure chain (`arch/all-pc/kernel/smp_exec.c:118-147,220-231`; `arch/all-pc/exec/platform_init.c:350-418`; `rom/exec/remtask.c:82-90,130-163`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:166-198,324-405`). `Exec_X86CreateIdleTask` may return NULL on task/name allocation failure, and an affinity-mask allocation failure can instead publish a NULL-affinity task that the PC predicate treats as CPU-0-only. The AP bootstrap then self-removes. The PC dispatch fallback selects the current non-WAIT tombstoned task, `core_Switch` refuses to switch it, and `core_Dispatch` recursively re-enters itself; no AP-local idle fallback or halt path intervenes in that condition. EK8835 remains source-supported and limited to x86-64 ExecSMP AP startup with no other eligible ready task. No AP startup or recursion was run. Source-only.

KrnRemIRQHandler null-token recheck (EK815, 2026-10-16; existing finding confirmed): read the complete generic body and paired generic add/run paths. `KrnAddIRQHandler` initializes the return token to NULL, leaves it NULL when `krnAllocIntrNode()` fails, and only publishes a populated `IntrNode` after successful allocation (`rom/kernel/addirqhandler.c:75-109`). `KrnRemIRQHandler` still evaluates `h->in_nr` before testing `h` (`rom/kernel/remirqhandler.c:52-56`), so the allocation-failure token deterministically reaches an invalid dereference when a selected caller forwards it. The generic ExecSMP add/remove path uses the write side of `kb_IntrSpinLock`, and callback traversal uses the read side (`addirqhandler.c:95-109,125-142`; `remirqhandler.c:59-73`); no separate generic list-lifetime race was established. This confirms EK815 and its caller-specific OD cross-references; no IRQ was registered or removed. Source-only.

SAD and alert task-lifetime recheck (EK480/EK8978, 2026-10-16): traced generic `Exec_CheckTask`'s list-by-list read locks through the selected `TI`/`RI` dereferences, `FormatTask`, and the x86-64 PC `RemTask` unlink/free path. NewCreateTaskA optional-name and task-port branch recheck (2026-10-16; no new finding): reread tag parsing, MemList sizing, task-port publication and `NewAllocEntry` zero-length behavior (`rom/exec/newcreatetaska.c:115-156,190-263`; `newallocentry.c:75-95,107-145`). CloseDevice wrapper synchronization follow-up (2026-10-16; no new EK): Exec `CloseDevice` and the selected LDDemon replacement both use only local `Forbid` around the device Close vector (`rom/exec/closedevice.c:67-82`; `rom/lddemon/lddemon.c:598-623`). Unlike LDDemon OpenDevice, the close wrapper does not acquire the per-device `LDObjectNode` semaphore. This leaves valid concurrent close operations, and open-versus-close overlap, unsynchronized across ExecSMP CPUs; it supports the keyboard list mutation trigger already detailed in OD2303. Console handler CSI table and edit-consumer pass (2026-10-16; no new EK): reread the complete `scan_input` special-byte/CSI parser, the full match table, `process_input` command dispatch, and the console.device's selected raw-key/paste production. Console cooked-input CSI split candidate restoration (EK706 detailed and indexed; 2026-10-27): re-read `startread()`, the device-read completion path, `scan_input()`, the full match table, and the `process_input()` switch (`rom/filesys/console_handler/con_handler.c:644-659,951-982`; `support.c:499-595,805-1090`). Confirmed device-backed cooked mode requests one byte per read and restarts the read after each response, while the parser consumes `0x9B`, returns `INP_UNKNOWN` if its suffix is incomplete, and stores no cross-read parser state. Thus a multi-byte AROS CSI key sequence on a cooked device-backed stream is split on every byte response: the CSI prefix is discarded and suffix characters are handled as ordinary input. Also retained the distinct windowed-console case where the 256-byte con-handler buffer boundary splits a sequence; selected `console.device` stores up to 512 converted bytes and fulfills up to the read length (`rom/devs/console/console_gcc.h:194-208`; `consoletask.c:529-561`). Selected con-handler boot manifests include Raspberry Pi ARM/AArch64 and RISC-V OpenSBI. No device, key sequence, or console was run; source-only.

EK699 Process/ETask reclamation timing pass (existing finding refined; 2026-10-27; no new ID or file/LOC credit): traced the selected `system_sh()` wait through `waitpid()` to `ChildWait()`/`ChildFree()` (`compiler/crt/posixc/system.c:111-121`; `waitpid.c:141-149`). `ChildFree()` expunges the ETask but not the Process allocation. A self-terminating child reaches `RemTask(NULL)`, which queues its Task/Process memory to the Exec service task; `service.c` later frees its `tc_MemEntry` list (`rom/exec/remtask.c:115-181`; `rom/exec/service.c:63-90`). Thus the report now distinguishes ETask reaping from asynchronous Process-storage reclamation and makes a later completion after that cleanup the trigger. The repository has a selected `system()` caller in WPA CLI, but no checked-in caller proves the same output handle later receives cooked Tab completion; that client sequence and memory reuse remain conditional. No child or console was run.

pthread timed-mutex grant and timeout recheck (EK567 retained; no new EK, 2026-10-16): reread `pthread_mutex_timedlock`, `_obtain_sema_timed`, mutex trylock/unlock, Exec `Procure`, `Vacate`, `ReleaseSemaphore`, and timer close. A successful trylock falls through to exclusive Procure; Procure recognizes the same owner and increments `ss_NestCount`, while one pthread unlock releases only one level, confirming EK567. If the timeout reply wins or races with a grant, Vacate removes the still-pending request or releases the already-granted ownership; timer cleanup aborts and waits for an unfinished request. No separate timer/grant issue was established. No pthread call or timer was run. Source-only.

DynModule EK8850 public-load serialization recheck (2026-10-16): followed the exported `dynmoduleLoadModule` wrapper through `_InternalLoadModule`, existing-port lookup, free-slot choice, reply wait, and slot publication (`compiler/dynmodule/dynmodule_loadmodule.c:22-36,69-145`; `dynmodule_modules.c:32-49,68-80`). The slot-table operations have no shared semaphore, lock, or Forbid region in the selected implementation; `DYNMODULE_Init` is only declared in the checked tree and does not wrap the subsequent operations. `dynmodule.h:49-50` declares public load/free without a caller-serialization condition. The two callers can therefore both reserve the same still-null slot and both return distinct client handles after separate successful Open replies, while the second publication replaces the first pointer and resets the single open count; the earlier handle is no longer found by `dynmoduleFreeModule`. Retain EK8850 as a conditional concurrent external-client race in the optional DynModule link library; no maintained in-tree client or concurrent load was found. Source-only.

Pthread timed-wait cancellation-vs-timeout ordering check (EK8980, 2026-10-16): traced deferred `pthread_cancel` flag/signal publication (`compiler/pthread/pthread_cancel.c:26-50`) through the timed condition wait's two-bit Wait mask, mutex reacquisition, cleanup and result selection (`pthread_cond_timedwait.c:104-169`). When timer and CTRL-C are both in the returned mask, timer-first branching returns `ETIMEDOUT` without `pthread_testcancel`, leaving the enabled cancellation pending. Cross-checked the Open Group condition-wait contract: the function is a cancellation point and acts on a pending/concurrent cancellation instead of returning ([specification](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/009604599/functions/pthread_cond_timedwait.html)). Added EK8980, distinct from EK8910's permit-consumption consequence of the same timer-first branch. The direct public condition-wait callers are external; the selected `sem_timedwait` implementation also delegates to this path. No wait, cancellation or race was run; source-only.

SetSignal/SetExcept complete direct-reference census (EK8940 recheck, 2026-10-16; no new finding): exact repository search found 284 lexical `SetSignal` references and 11 `SetExcept` references; these include exec.conf prototypes, comments and the m68k assembly vector. Among selected direct `SetExcept` calls, the only production pair enables/disables SIGBREAKF_CTRL_C in the pthread worker; its own `SetSignal(SIGBREAKF_CTRL_C, 0)` changes no received bits. The two optional exception tests use `Signal` to deliver the enabled bit, while their handler's `SetSignal(0, 0)` has an empty mask. No other selected path both enables an exception bit and sets that same current-task bit through `SetSignal`; EK8940 remains a public API sequence candidate with no established in-tree trigger. No task or exception was run. Source-only.

genmodule generated DEVICE registration recheck (2026-10-16; no new EK): the source generator's `case DEVICE` emits `AddDevice(LIBBASE)` without a `break`, followed by `AddLibrary(LIBBASE)` (`tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1186-1201`), which would link the same node into both device and library lists if emitted. The registration switch is gated on neither `OPTION_RESAUTOINIT` nor `OPTION_SELFINIT`; configuration postprocessing assigns `OPTION_RESAUTOINIT` to every non-resource/handler module unless self-init is requested (`config.c:825-830`). A repository-wide `.conf` search found `selfinit` only in `rom/dosboot/dosboot.conf` and `rom/expansion/expansion.conf`; neither is a device. Thus selected generated devices skip this fallthrough block, and no generated-device list corruption is established. No module was generated or loaded; source-only.

Pthread timed-lock shared-helper caller reconciliation (2026-10-16; no new EK): re-read the mutex and rwlock timed acquisition paths against `_obtain_sema_timed` and Exec `Procure`. `pthread_mutex_timedlock` falls through after a successful trylock and is the distinct double-acquire in EK567. Both `pthread_rwlock_timedrdlock` and `pthread_rwlock_timedwrlock` return immediately for any result other than `EBUSY`, so their uncontended paths do not duplicate the Procure acquisition. The contended paths reach the shared timer/semaphore handoff already traced in the pthread body and Exec `Procure`/`Vacate` rows. No lock or timeout was exercised; source-only.
OOP attribute-base failed-acquisition caller recheck (2026-10-16; no new EK finding): traced the known `OOP_ObtainAttrBases` cleanup-loop defect (GD1214, OD2399) through selected Radeon HIDD startup. `ATI_Init` supplies twelve attribute-base descriptors and immediately returns false when acquisition fails (`workbench/hidds/radeon/ati_init.c:221-236,258-279`); `OOP_ObtainAttrBases` then enters its non-advancing clear loop when any non-final interface acquisition fails (`rom/oop/obtainattrbases.c:56-64`), so Radeon initialization does not return to library rollback. The helper defect is already reported in the Graphics/Desktop and Other Drivers reports; this confirms an additional selected caller and does not create a duplicate EK finding. No attribute-base failure or initialization was induced. Source-only.
CreateMsgPort/DeleteMsgPort signal-owner caller recheck (2026-10-16; no new EK): followed the port's `mp_SigTask` assignment in `CreateMsgPort` and `FreeSignal`'s use of `GET_THIS_TASK` through selected USB HID and OHCI timer paths. The USB keyboard/mouse worker ports are created and deleted in the same worker task (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/HID/{kbdclass,mouseclass}.c`); OHCI's helper frees the creator's original signal before opening the timer, sets `mp_SigTask` to the current task for each synchronous delay, then allocates a signal in the deleting task immediately before `DeleteMsgPort` (`workbench/devs/USB/drivers/OHCI/ohcidriverclass.c:49-104`). Intuition's decorator reply port is also created and deleted inside the same input-device action (`rom/intuition/decoration.c:103-126`). These selected callers do not establish a cross-task signal-release defect. The general Exec behavior remains an API ownership question because `DeleteMsgPort` frees the bit from the caller's task allocation mask, while `mp_SigTask` can identify a different owner; no selected cross-task deletion sequence was established in this bounded pass. No message port or signal was created; source-only.
Long-lived message-port task-context caller census (2026-10-16; no new EK): checked stored ports in selected long-lived controller/task paths against `CreateMsgPort`'s `mp_SigTask` assignment and `DeleteMsgPort`/`FreeSignal`'s caller-task behavior. USB HID ports remain worker-local as recorded above. This sample does not establish a selected cross-task `DeleteMsgPort` path; the broader 578-call inventory has not been exhaustively task-context classified. i386 processor.resource skipped-core contract recheck (EK8975, 2026-10-16; retained): verified `GCIT_NumberOfProcessors` and the public topology contract define logical processors as hardware threads, while `GetCoreInfo` promises TRUE for each present logical index and leaves tags untouched only for absent indices (`compiler/include/resources/processor.h:69-74`; `rom/processor/getcoreinfo.c:26-62`). Reset callback signal-allocation fallback and completion-wait caller audit (EK8991, 2026-10-16): traced `Exec_DoResetCallbacks` from signal allocation through clearing and waiting to `ResetCallbackHandler` completion delivery. When no private bit is available, it uses shared `SIGF_SINGLE`; `Wait` accepts any event on that bit, so an unrelated delivery can advance the chain while the callback remains active. The selected RISC-V OpenSBI signal exhaustion paths remain EK633; selected PC memory-raw-I/O code confirms `SIGF_SINGLE` is also used as a public task event (`memoryrawio.c:150,232`), though an active delivery to a reset caller during the callback window was not established. Reset callback timer setup failure-path pass (EK8992, 2026-10-16): traced `CreateMsgPort`, `CreateIORequest`, timer.device `OpenDevice`, and per-handler waits. Each setup failure leaves `treq == NULL`; successfully created callback tasks then use the unbounded `Wait(ResetCallbackSignal)` branch. A non-completing callback therefore blocks later callbacks/reset performer. This is distinct from task creation failure EK675 and timer-fired races EK873/EK8946. Added EK8992. No allocation failure, timer open or shutdown was run.
Reset callback SIGF_SINGLE fallback caller qualification (EK8991 rechecked, 2026-10-16; trigger narrowed, no new finding): traced `ResetCallbackHandler` completion (`doresetcallbacks.c:31-43`) and all in-tree `ShutdownA` callers, then exact direct task-signal sends using `SIGF_SINGLE`. The bit is used broadly as a public task event, but the checked sources do not prove one of those senders targets a task that is simultaneously the generic reset launcher, exhausted its allocatable signals, and is waiting on a handler. The early-advance consequence remains valid if that public signal reaches the launcher during the wait; EK8991 remains explicitly conditional and no selected in-tree reproduction is claimed. The keyboard-device reset-handler completion path is separate from Exec's `ResetCallbackSignal` chain. No reset or signal was sent.

Exec interrupt-server wrapper to generic-kernel IRQ path recheck (EK09/EK31/EK629; 2026-10-16; no new finding): reread `AddIntServer`, `RemIntServer`, `KrnAddIRQHandler`, `KrnRemIRQHandler` and `krnRunIRQHandlers` as one path (`rom/exec/addintserver.c:53-67`; `remintserver.c:50-67`; `rom/kernel/addirqhandler.c:75-143`; `remirqhandler.c:49-78`). Generic MMU absolute-allocation reachability refinement (EK808/EK8801, 2026-10-16): rechecked `allocpages.c`, `initmemory.c`, `allockernelbase.c`, all maintained `kb_PageSize` references and `KrnInitMemory` callers. The base is allocated with MEMF_CLEAR; there is no checked-in assignment to the private page-size field; and the only `KrnInitMemory` call is in the excluded allocator test. Therefore the public `KrnAllocPages` vector alone cannot reach either linear-map defect in checked-in bare-metal startup; both candidates now require target initialization of page size and MemHeaders before the external/direct request. Unix has its separate mmap allocator and does not exercise `mm_linear.c`. No allocator or boot was run. Source-only.

Exec Allocate managed-header callback pass (2026-10-16; no new finding): reread the full `rom/exec/allocate.c` dispatch and directly selected callback assignments/callers. The TLSF managed allocator accepts a NULL flags pointer, rounds zero to zero and returns NULL; the selected Radeon and VideoCore GPU managed callbacks intentionally return NULL for legacy `Allocate`, with the drivers’ graphics allocation paths using their separate APIs. Selected Efika supervisor pools use the ordinary allocator path; PC low-memory headers can be TLSF-managed when that allocator is selected, and `tlsf_malloc` accepts the NULL flags pointer passed by legacy `Allocate`. The documented hand-built-header zeroing requirement is already covered by EK809 and checked selected construction sites initialize headers with `MEMF_CLEAR` or zeroed storage. No independent Allocate defect established. Other private MemHeader producers, external callers and runtime allocation remain open. Source-only.

Exec Deallocate managed-header/free-size pass (2026-10-16; no new finding): read the complete dispatch and traced the selected TLSF, Radeon and VideoCore callbacks plus V3D’s rounded allocation/free pair. TLSF recovers allocation extent from its block header and ignores the caller size; its free callback tolerates NULL. The selected Radeon/VideoCore managed callbacks are no-ops paired with their unsupported legacy allocation stubs. V3D rounds to page size on both allocation and free and rejects handle zero before Deallocate. The plain path deliberately ignores NULL/zero-size releases and routes valid blocks to `stdDealloc`; no selected size/ownership mismatch was established. Wider managed-header producers and external callers remain open. No allocator was run. Source-only.


PC Exec/kernel target-composition pass (2026-10-16; no new EK): re-read the generic kernel source/function set, `arch/all-pc/kernel/mmakefile.src`, and i386-PC/x86-64-PC overlays. Traced the shared PC manifest's selected APIC/ACPI/SMP groups against each target's platform-priority startup, interrupt assembly and bootstrap object rules; x86-64's early-trap/trap-debug sources are disabled by empty default switches. Existing EK810 and PC mask/IRQ findings remain associated with the selected common function set. This closes manifest-level source composition for these two PC targets only; generated objects, firmware delivery and hardware behavior remain unverified. Source-only.

Generic page allocator MemList/SMP publication recheck (2026-10-16; no new EK): revisited `mm_AllocPages`' unprotected forward `MemList` walk against selected `AddMemList` publication and the per-header allocator locks (`rom/kernel/kernel_mm.c:22-68`; `rom/exec/addmemlist.c:91-101`; `rom/exec/memory.h:14-17`; `rom/kernel/mm_linear.c:184-270`). `AddMemList` fully initializes the new header before `Enqueue` links it; the allocator consumes forward `ln_Succ` pointers and each allocator-map mutation is separately serialized by that header's semaphore. A concurrent insertion may be skipped or observed, but this pass did not establish an invalid node dereference or map race from the forward traversal itself, so no SMP candidate is credited. The generic `KrnAllocPages` path is selected in the generic kernel manifest and the `USE_MMU=1` allocator adds `kernel_mm`/`mm_linear`; however, the complete checked-in source search still finds no assignment to `kb_PageSize`, so the wrapper exits before this walk on checked startup (`rom/kernel/allocpages.c:63-83`). Unix uses its mmap override. EK14/EK25/EK16/EK489/EK639/EK722/EK8801 retain their distinct documented conditions; no allocation or concurrent insertion was run. Source-only.

Unix-hosted `KrnAllocPages` explicit-address contract follow-up (EK8993, 2026-10-16): compared the public vector's required-region language and generic absolute allocator with the selected Unix override (`rom/kernel/allocpages.c:27-46`; `kernel_mm.c:43-53`; `arch/all-unix/kernel/allocpages.c:50-57,106-145`). The override passes a non-NULL address to host `mmap` as a hint, omits fixed-placement semantics, and returns any non-`MAP_FAILED` result without checking that it includes the requested page. Thus it can report success at a different location when the hint is unavailable; added a conditional exported-API finding. A direct maintained C-call search found only DOS LoadSeg and CreateSegList, both passing NULL; selected current callers do not establish the trigger. No map was requested. Source-only.
AllocSignal public-caller cross-check (OD3344 and trackdisk rechecked, 2026-10-16; no new Exec finding): the AHIRecord main-task uses of `AllocSignal(-1)` do not test the `-1` exhaustion result before shifting it into masks; this caller-side defect is OD3344 in the Other Drivers report. The trackdisk worker passes through `NewAddTask` with the default 0xFFFF system-reserved mask, leaving signals 16-31 available for its two direct allocations and timer reply port, so no signal-exhaustion defect follows from that worker startup. Other public callers from the source-wide `AllocSignal` search remain pending; this note does not close the caller census. Source-only.

Pthread condition-wait timeout, waiter ownership and selected semaphore caller recheck (EK603 restored to detailed report/index; EK802/EK8910 retained; 2026-10-19): reread the full `_pthread_cond_timedwait` path and its only maintained direct in-tree timed caller, `sem_timedwait` (`compiler/pthread/pthread_cond_timedwait.c:35-180`; `semaphore.c:226-254`). The stack waiter is linked and unlinked under `cond->semaphore`, and `_pthread_cond_broadcast` traverses under the same semaphore; the waiter signal remains allocated until after mutex reacquisition and list removal. `sem_timedwait` loops only while the condition return is zero, so a timed-out call with a concurrently posted permit returns ETIMEDOUT without consuming the positive count (EK8910), while the timer-first result can also bypass deferred cancellation (EK802). `pthread_cond_destroy`/concurrent arbitrary waiters remain caller-synchronized; no selected in-tree timed condition caller exists beyond `sem_timedwait`, which uses a NULL deadline in its only direct call (`pthread_cond_wait` path). The fallback Ctrl-E consumption (EK603), fallback timer-bit pending state (EK8951), signed bit-31 shifts (EK8800), and signal/list races were rechecked against their existing entries; no separate waiter lifetime defect established. No condition wait, cancellation, timer, or semaphore was run. Source-only.

DeleteMsgPort port-signal owner check (2026-10-16; no new EK): traced two selected worker-owned resource groups as explicit creator/deleter task pairs. AmigaGuide's `asyncmethodfunc` creates `ag_ProcPort` and `ag_RexxPort`, consumes them in that worker, and deletes both before returning (`workbench/classes/datatypes/amigaguide/process.c:203-240,350-392`). The Bluetooth BNEP worker creates `ncp_TaskMsgPort` inside `bAllocEth` called from its task, then `bFreeEth` executes at the end of that same event-loop task and deletes the port (`rom/bluetooth/classes/btpan/btpan.class.c:930-951,1000-1030,1044-1090`). Thus these object-owned ports do not expose the known `DeleteMsgPort` behavior of freeing `mp_SigBit` from the deleting task's signal mask when that differs from the creator's. This is a focused caller sample, not closure of the remaining public Create/DeleteMsgPort census. No process, port or signal was run. Source-only.

Exec task-creation affinity failure recheck (EK8820): followed `NewCreateTaskA` through `NewAddTask` into `Exec_InitETask` and checked allocation-failure handling. When a parent has a concrete affinity, `KrnAllocCPUMask()` failure leaves the child ETask affinity NULL; `KrnGetCPUMask` tolerates the NULL destination, and selected ARM/AArch64 schedulers treat NULL as unrestricted while PC treats NULL as CPU-0-only. This confirms EK8820's incorrect-inheritance behavior and platform-dependent consequence; no separate candidate. `NewCreateTaskA` frees its MemList on task setup failure, and `Exec_InitETask` returns immediately if the ETask allocation itself fails before later resources are acquired. No allocation failure or scheduling was induced. Source-only.

EK06 serial-logger caller follow-up: selected seriallogger INITLIB stores `NewCreateTask`'s return in `selrb_Task` but returns TRUE unconditionally after attempting worker creation. On the same post-port-publication task setup failure covered by EK06, its worker never starts, so the published port is not consumed, serial logging is unavailable, and the provider registered immediately before task creation never reaches the worker-only `logFinalise` call. This extends EK06's selected false-success impact to serial debugging and its provider lifetime; no distinct Exec mechanism or report item. No task-creation failure or serial-debug boot was induced. Source-only.

| `compiler/crt/posixc/seekdir.c`, `telldir.c`, `readdir.c`, `readdir64.c` | Read complete implementations and traced counter/iterator state in both `doupath` modes; audited all exposed dirent output fields and related constructors | EK8998: `readdir()` and `readdir64()` increment the logical position after returning an entry, but decrement it on every failed `ExNext()` including EOF; `telldir()` exposes that drift. `seekdir()` resets DOS enumeration and advances inclusively, so a saved location repeats or skips entries depending on path mode. EK9015: both read functions leave the exposed XSI `d_ino` field untouched; `opendir()` and `fdopendir()` allocate the shared DIR buffer from non-clearing `malloc`, and `scandir*` copies the unset value. The direct d_ino caller census found no checked-in consumer; public XSI/dirent64 users remain affected. No runtime directory test was run. |

| `compiler/crt/posixc/scandir.c`, `scandir64.c` | Full implementations read; traced `readdir()`/`readdir64()` error signaling, manifest entries, and caller configuration | EK8999: both scan loops treat any NULL result as EOF and return a partial count without checking the errno set for non-EOF `ExNext()` errors. The WPS `wps_get_dev_pwd_e_file_name()` caller treats a partial nonnegative result as complete (`workbench/network/WirelessManager/src/wps/wps_ufd.c:58-79`), but it is conditional on `CONFIG_WPS_UFD`, which is absent from the checked-in default `.config` and guards its Makefile object. EK9000: common failure cleanup passes NULL `dirp` to `closedir()` after `opendir()` failure, replacing the original errno with EFAULT. Both are detailed in the Exec/Kernel report. Allocation, media, enumeration, or open failure was not induced. |

| `compiler/crt/posixc/alphasort.c`, `alphasort64.c`, `dirfd.c`, `rewinddir.c`, `closedir.c` | Full short implementations and public configuration/manifest entries checked; callers, shared descriptor table, and resource teardown traced | `alphasort*` delegate to `strcoll` with qsort-compatible signatures. `dirfd()` returns the backing descriptor documented as belonging to a live DIR stream. `rewinddir()` delegates to `seekdir(dir, 0)`; no separate issue beyond EK8998. `closedir()` rejects a null stream with EFAULT; this confirms the errno overwrite in EK9000 when scandir cleanup calls it after failed opendir. For an ordinary live stream it decrements the shared FCB open count under its semaphore, unlocks/frees the FCB only at zero, releases the fdesc slot, then frees the DOS FIB and DIR object; no additional local teardown defect established. Use of a DIR after close or externally closing its `dirfd` is caller misuse and not promoted. |

| `rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c` | Full 691-line body and selected backend, enumeration, removal, and singleton callers reviewed; firmware/controller behavior and external clients pending | Full PCI scan, bridge/IRQ routing, device enumeration, driver add/remove, singleton New and empty Dispose bodies read against HW superclass removal. OD3563 covers the cross-driver device-disposal loop; OD3522 covers duplicate ACPI host-bridge scans; OD2884 covers the void registration API losing `HW_AddDriver` failure. The direct legacy Add caller includes Raspberry Pi RP1 initialization (`rp1_pci.c:280`, selected by `PKG_HIDDS=...pcirp1`). Caller-path correction (OD3563 recheck, 2026-10-19): `arch/all-pc/hidds/pcipc/pcipc_init.c:54-78` calls deprecated `HIDD_PCI_RemHardwareDriver` during PCIPC expunge; `rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:626-658` enumerates same-class instances and calls `HW_RemoveDriver`. PCIPC can create multiple instances from ACPI host-bridge nodes (`pcipc_driverclass.c:589-637`). This corrects the prior wrong `pcipc_driverclass.c:645-660` citation and withdraws the unrelated AArch64 example; no checked-in caller establishes the specific owner distribution required for OD3563. Setup-traversal concurrency recheck (2026-10-21; no EK/OD): `HW__HW__AddDriver()` invokes `HW_SetUpDriver()` before taking `driver_lock` to publish the new driver (`rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c:173-199`); PCI `InsertDevice()` protects each append with `dev_lock` (`pciclass.c:86-92`), but `PCI__HW__SetUpDriver()`'s IRQ-routing/diagnostic list walks and `FindBridge()` do not hold it (`pciclass.c:172-205,243-296`). PCI removal does take the exclusive device lock (`pciclass.c:451-490,508-514`), so concurrent setup/removal could overlap the unprotected walks. The selected PCIPC init processes host-bridge instances synchronously in one loop (`arch/all-pc/hidds/pcipc/pcipc_driverclass.c:606-635`), and its expunge invokes removal separately (`pcipc_init.c:54-78`); no selected in-tree overlapping trigger was established, so no race finding is promoted. Concurrency under external clients/hotplug remains open. Firmware bridge topology and external clients also remain open. No PCI operation or concurrent add/remove was run; source-only. |

AllocSignal selected UnixIO waiter follow-up (2026-10-17; no new EK): traced `UXIO__Hidd_UnixIO__Wait` through `AllocSignal`, `AddInterrupt`, `Wait`, removal, and `FreeSignal` (`arch/all-unix/hidd/unixio/unixio_class.c:381-411,828-875`). It returns ENOMEM when allocation fails before shifting the bit; on successful registration it frees the bit after wake, and on non-Darwin registration failure `AddInterrupt` removes the stack waiter before returning. Darwin retains the waiter and reports success so its periodic SIGALRM polling can wake it. The poll/register lost-wakeup candidate remains OD115 in the Other Drivers report and is independent of signal allocation. No signal exhaustion or host descriptor was induced. Other public AllocSignal callers remain pending.

KrnRemIRQHandler direct-C caller census follow-up (EK815, 2026-10-17): re-enumerated all checked-in C references. Rechecked the optional `developer/debug/windebug/windebug.c` path: failed `KrnAddIRQHandler` exits before cleanup reaches removal; successful registration is removed after the event/console-hook path. Rechecked `rom/hidds/ata_pci/ata_pci_busclass.c`: legacy construction calls its own Dispose only after a non-NULL raw IRQ token; failed raw registration invokes the superclass disposer directly, while native PCI removal uses `HIDD_PCIDevice_RemoveInterrupt`. Neither adds a new null-token caller. Existing i8042, timer rollback and other handler paths remain as cross-referenced; non-C callers and remaining platform-specific controller behavior remain open. No IRQ allocation, event, or PCI device was exercised. Source-only.

PC unchecked exception-registration consequence recheck (EK8877, 2026-10-17): confirmed the existing registrations are not replaced by another handler path. Both PC platform hooks install the shared syscall IDT gate and then rely on the `APIC_EXCEPT_SYSCALL` exception-list entry for `core_SysCallHandler`; the normal syscall wrappers execute `int $0xfe` (`arch/all-pc/kernel/x86_syscalls.h:16-28`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/syscall.c:41-70`). `cpu_Trap` dispatches only through `krnRunExceptionHandlers` before its non-spurious halt path (`arch/all-pc/kernel/cpu_traps.c:88-124`). BSP APIC setup likewise installs error/IPI gates before its unchecked list registrations and enables the APIC afterward (`arch/all-pc/kernel/apic_ia32.c:1050-1128`). Thus allocation failure leaves a gate without the required list handler; no equivalent fallback was found. EK8877 remains supported. No boot, allocation failure or interrupt was induced. Source-only.

SAD task-list traversal entry-path recheck (EK8977, 2026-10-17): followed public `Debug()` into `InternalDebug()` and checked the selected PC kernel input-acquisition hook. `InternalDebug` calls `KrnObtainInput`, then `RawIOInit` and enters the prompt without `Forbid`/`Disable`; the PC `KrnObtainInput` implementation simply returns TRUE (`arch/all-pc/kernel/obtaininput.c:14-23`). SAD's `FO`/`DI` commands only modify nesting if separately entered later, so they do not protect the initial `ST` traversal. The selected x86-64 ExecSMP task-list writers continue to use per-list spinlocks while this read remains unlocked. EK8977 remains supported; no SAD command or concurrent task transition was run. Source-only.

Debug-library registration publication recheck (2026-10-17; prior EK520 label withdrawn): followed `RegisterModule_ELF`/`RegisterModule_Hunk` insertion through `HandleModuleSegments` and symbol-table population against `Debug_SymResolver` and `EnumerateSymbolsA`. The resolver range fields remain zero until the segment index is filled and the bounds are published; the selected resolver therefore does not binary-search a not-yet-built index for ordinary nonzero code addresses. `EnumerateSymbolsA` may observe a transient prefix because the insertion lock is released before symbol population, but no selected caller contract promises a registration snapshot and this is not retained as a correctness finding. The independently confirmed allocation and unload defects are EK9003-EK9005. Source-only.


PC x86-64 global-map selected-caller reconciliation (EK8887-EK8889 retained; no new EK, 2026-10-17): corrected the prior narrow C-call census by following the OOP `HIDD_PCIDriver_MapPCI` dispatch into selected PCIPC and x86-64 consumers. The x86-64 package selects PCIPC, ATA PCI, NVMe, and VESAGfx (`arch/x86_64-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:66-68`). ATA PCI and NVMe check a failed mapping before MMIO access; VESAGfx reaches the map method only for its PCI fallback when firmware reports no framebuffer, then `HwInit` rejects a NULL result (`rom/hidds/ata_pci/probe.c:220-230`; `nvme_controllerclass.c:261-277`; `vesagfx_support.c:68-78,189-225`). No PCI hardware or mapping was exercised. Source-only.

Logger finding reconciliation (EK9009-EK9012, 2026-10-17): restored the tracked exit-status issue, proved the shell wrapper returns it, then rechecked the missing buffer releases and DOS flush results. `log.resource` listener allocation failure refinement (EK863 expanded, 2026-10-17): traced both nullable allocation edges in `logEventBroadcast`. Failure to create the listener's private pool publishes a listener that later passes NULL into `AllocVecPooled`; with a valid pool, a per-event allocation can also return NULL and the caller writes through that message pointer without checking. Both are the same unchecked broadcast-message ownership path already tracked by EK863. Selected Logger, serial logger and optional test listener registrations were rechecked; no separate caller issue was added. No low-memory event was run. Source-only.


`logRemEntry` caller reconciliation (EK8927/EK8765/EK8767 rechecked, 2026-10-17): the only checked-in C caller is standalone Logger, in its startup spool and after receiving an add broadcast. The initial walk is under the write lock; live removal follows the worker's publication and broadcast. These callers do not create EK8927's immediate public-API add/remove trigger. The later source recheck established that the failure is the still-unlinked `lep_Node` before publication, not an ExecSMP-only dequeue window. Logger's removal can still free an entry while a second listener has an earlier add notification queued, as EK8765 records, and producer-list name ownership remains EK8767. No log entry or listener schedule was run. Source-only.

OOP public-class lifetime detailed restoration (GD4254, 2026-10-17): reconciled `findclass.c`, `newobject.c`, `removeclass.c`, `basemetaclass.c`, and generated class shutdown. `OOP_FindClass` releases the class-list lock before return; `OOP_NewObject` increments `objectcount` only after return; generated shutdown unlinks then disposes, while BaseMeta disposal frees name/dispatch data without waiting on the count. `BaseMeta::New` additionally resolves public `superid` via unlocked `FindName`. Added the detailed conditional candidate to Exec/Kernel, explicitly noting no in-tree concurrent lookup/unload path was established (the xHCI shutdown helper is static and has no checked-in caller). No schedule/object was run. Source-only.


OOP bootstrap failure recheck (GD1221-GD1222, 2026-10-17): reread `NewHash`, `OOPInit`, `GetIDs`, `OOP_ObtainAttrBase`, and the generated INITLIB unwind. Confirmed `NewHash` tests the already-non-NULL header after `AllocVec` rather than testing `ht->Table`, so built-in ID lookup reaches `HashLookupStr` with NULL buckets. Confirmed later `OOPInit` failure reaches `OOPExpunge`, which closes only Utility and never frees the separately allocated IID table or releases acquired IDs. Detailed both existing candidates in the Exec/Kernel report. GD4253 partial IFMeta cleanup remains separately qualified; no failure was induced. Source-only.


OOP method-base exhaustion trace (EK9013, 2026-10-17): checked `ULONG` width, the 10-bit method-offset layout, counter initialization/use sites, and class disposal. `init_mi_methodbase` has no capacity check before shifting a 32-bit counter left by 10; after 2^22 unique reservations, values repeat, while disposing dynamic classes releases IID buckets but leaves the counter advanced. IFMeta dispatch selects by that numeric ID alone. Added EK9013 as an extreme-volume, generic `CLID_MIMeta` candidate; the only checked-in example is developer/debug, and no production caller nearing wrap was found. No class construction or method dispatch was run. Source-only.


OOP attribute-base exhaustion trace (EK9014, 2026-10-17): followed new-IID assignment in `OOP_ObtainAttrBase`, the 32-bit `ob_CurrentAttrBase`, 10-bit method-offset layout and startup Root/Meta base acquisition. At counter value 2^22 the shifted return is zero (failure) although the IID bucket remains in the table; an existing method-bucket reference may remain, while a newly created bucket gains no attribute reference. The next new IID returns a base aliasing an earlier live ID. Added EK9014 separately from EK9013's method-base collision because attr-base aliasing affects public attribute IDs. No in-tree production caller approaching the cumulative threshold was found; no ID was allocated. Source-only.


OOP IFMeta trigger qualification (EK8954, 2026-10-17): rechecked the public Timer example against the actual `OOP_OCLASS(super)` dispatch. Root uses BaseMeta, whose `basemeta_getifinfo` safely returns NULL for a missing interface; the unchecked IFMeta function is reached only when the superclass is an IFMeta-created class. Narrowed the report trigger and removed the Timer example as evidence of the fault. No dynamic class was created. Source-only.


Exec self-removal/ServiceTask tombstone branch recheck (EK807 scope confirmed, 2026-10-17; no new finding): reread the self-removal handoff and the complete `ServiceTask` state switch (`rom/exec/remtask.c:130-164`; `rom/exec/service.c:37-90`) against selected ARM32/AArch64 `Exec_SuicideSwitch` and `core_Dispatch` (`arch/arm-native/exec/platform_init.c:225-246`; `arch/aarch64-native/exec/platform_init.c:183-201`; `arch/{arm,aarch64}-native/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c`). On SMP, RemTask caches the dying CPU in `tc_UserData`; ServiceTask requeues a `TS_TOMBSTONED` request when CPU affinity is active and the housekeeper CPU differs, and falls through to free it when they match. The source-level stale-current-task consequence remains limited to a failed per-CPU idle-task fallback plus no other ready task eligible on the dying CPU, allowing another CPU's housekeeper to reclaim the TCB before local dispatch finishes. This recheck does not establish a general early free on normal paths, and it does not resolve platform startup/firmware timing. No allocation failure or scheduling interleaving was run. Source-only.

POSIX directory-entry inode-field audit (EK9015, 2026-10-17): compared all fields written by `readdir`/`readdir64` with the selected public `dirent.h` layout and XSI d_ino definition. Confirmed neither function assigns d_ino; both opendir constructors allocate DIR with non-clearing malloc, and scandir copies the whole entry. No checked-in d_ino consumer was found. Added EK9015. Source-only.


x86-64 KrnMapGlobal selected PCI failure-propagation reconciliation (EK8887-EK8889 retained, 2026-10-17; no new EK): retraced `PCIPC__Hidd_PCIDriver__MapPCI`'s zero-success/nonzero-failure convention into the selected ATA PCI, NVMe, and VESAGfx consumers (`arch/all-pc/hidds/pcipc/pcipc_driverclass.c:230-253`; `rom/hidds/ata_pci/probe.c:220-230`; `rom/devs/nvme/nvme_controllerclass.c:261-277`; `rom/hidds/vesagfx/vesagfx_support.c:68-78,189-225`). PCIPC returns NULL after any nonzero `KrnMapGlobal` result; ATA and NVMe stop controller setup on a null map, and VESAGfx's initialization rejects a still-null framebuffer. This confirms allocation-failure propagation and does not add an independent caller defect. The selected x86-64 boot manifest and generic PCIPC override are established in the file row; BAR placement at high physical addresses, runtime concurrency, optional PCI modules, and page-table reclamation remain open. No BAR or map operation was used. Source-only.

ChildWait lost-wakeup atomicity recheck (EK811 retained, 2026-10-17): verified the signal-clear ordering against the selected Exec primitives. `SetSignal(0, SIGF_CHILD)` takes the caller task spinlock and clears the received bit (`rom/exec/setsignal.c:68-93`); `Wait` later takes that same lock and returns immediately only if the bit remains set (`rom/exec/wait.c:68-83`). Child completion publishes its ETask node under the parent message-port spinlock, unlocks, then calls `Signal` (`exec_util.c:314-330`). Thus publication and Signal can both finish between ChildWait's empty scan and SetSignal; the clear is internally atomic but still erases that already-delivered wakeup, and Wait correctly sleeps because the bit is now zero. The POSIX wait/waitpid wrappers consume ChildWait's returned ETask and free it, and selected __vfork requests NP_NotifyOnDeath (`compiler/crt/posixc/wait.c:92-100`; `waitpid.c:140-149`; `__vfork.c:476-502`). EK811 stands as an ExecSMP lost wake; no task scheduling or wait was run. Source-only.

Exec child API recheck (EK811, EK812, EK476 retained; no additional candidate, 2026-10-18): reread `ChildStatus`, `ChildWait`, `ChildFree`, `ChildOrphan`, `Exec_CleanupETask`, and the selected POSIX wrappers. Confirmed EK812's live-child scan lacks the parent `iet_TaskLock`, while `ChildOrphan`, `ChildFree`, creation and exit mutation use it; the notified-exit transition releases that lock before acquiring the completion-port lock, leaving the already-recorded false-absence window. Confirmed EK811 separately at the message-port-to-signal handoff. Checked `waitpid(-1, WNOHANG)`'s direct `ListLength` traversal against the exit append and `ChildFree` removal: new nodes are initialized before publication, and no checked-in concurrent ChildFree call for the same parent task was established, so a racing empty count is an allowed WNOHANG snapshot; no separate list-count issue added. EK476 already covers the childless any-child wait returning/ blocking behavior. No child lifecycle or wait call was run.

Child completion double-claim recheck (2026-10-17; no new EK): inspected whether concurrent ChildWait callers can both return the same queued ETask and race its ChildFree reclamation. Each ChildWait obtains the current task's own ETask and scans that ETask's private completion port (`rom/exec/childwait.c:77-113`; `exec_util.c:170-177`); one task cannot execute two synchronous ChildWait calls concurrently, while other tasks have distinct ETask completion lists. The public ChildWait contract also requires ChildFree on a returned child before the next call (`childwait.c:27-39`). ChildFree removes a selected entry under the live-list or completion-port writer lock before ExpungeETask (`childfree.c:59-96`). No selected route to two claimers of one parent's completion node was established. EK811 lost wakeup and EK812 ChildStatus live-list race remain; no task was run. Source-only.

POSIX directory-entry field follow-up (EK9015 retained, 2026-10-17): checked the selected `dirent.h`, `readdir`, `readdir64`, `opendir`, `fdopendir`, and `scandir*` paths against the XSI contract. The Open Group defines XSI `d_ino` as the file serial number, supporting EK9015's missing-field result. Checked a possible `readdir64.d_name` termination defect and did not promote it: `max` is at most `MAXFILENAMELENGTH` (108), and the DOS FileInfoBlock contract states `fib_FileName` is converted to NUL-terminated C text (`compiler/include/dos/dos.h:57,81-85`), so `strncpy(..., max)` receives its terminator within the copied bound. `readdir` explicitly adds a terminator at `d_name[max]`; `dirent64.d_name` is 256 bytes. The POSIX layer does not expose the 108-byte DOS source as an unterminated string in this path. No directory was enumerated. Source-only.

genmodule override diagnostic recheck (EK9017 retained, 2026-10-17): verified the counter across the actual sequential `readconfig` calls. `readline` increments global `lineno`; `fileclose` sets `file` and `filename` to NULL without resetting it; `fileopen` resets only when it itself sees a non-NULL open stream. `readconfig` closes the primary config before opening the permitted `-o` override, so that `fileopen` sees NULL and preserves the primary line count. Subsequent `filewarning`/`exitfileerror` print the override filename with this accumulated counter. The `-o` option is documented and parsed in `tools/genmodule/config.c:57,107,163-164`; no runtime generator invocation was made. Source-only.

`scandir` error-result caller recheck (EK8999/EK9000 retained, 2026-10-17; WPS scope qualified 2026-10-21): traced both scan loops, `readdir`/`readdir64`, `closedir`, and the WPS caller. The scan functions initialize `errno`, preserve it around selector callbacks and comparators, and the readers set it on non-EOF `ExNext` failures; however, both loops terminate on NULL without branching on the saved read error, then publish and return the partial count. The WPS `wps_get_dev_pwd_e_file_name` caller treats every nonnegative count as complete and chooses `namelist[0]` after sorting (`workbench/network/WirelessManager/src/wps/wps_ufd.c:58-79`), but the caller is conditional on `CONFIG_WPS_UFD`, absent from the checked-in default `.config`; no default in-tree selected caller is claimed. EK9000 remains distinct: on `opendir` failure the common cleanup calls `closedir(NULL)`, replacing the original errno. No directory or DOS read error was induced. Source-only.

EK8999/EK9000 report restoration and shared cleanup recheck (2026-10-29; no path/LOC credit): re-read `scandir()` and `scandir64()` through their success/error exits, both selected directory readers, and `closedir()`. Confirmed a non-EOF `ExNext()` error sets errno then returns NULL; both scan loops treat it as end-of-directory, publish the partial list and return its count. Reconfirmed `opendir()` failure reaches shared cleanup with `dirp == NULL`, and `closedir(NULL)` replaces the original errno with EFAULT. Preserved the optional `CONFIG_WPS_UFD` caller qualification and kept the errno overwrite separate from partial-result success. Replaced both stale recovery placeholders; existing index anchors remain. No directory enumeration or open failure was induced; source-only.

BCM2837 timer-route diagnostic recheck (EK8909/EK8873 retained, 2026-10-17): traced the ARMPLATFORMS probe loop from `kernel_startup.c` through `platform_Init` and the exact `ARMI_Platform == 0xc43` BCM2837 match. The initializer's diagnostic loop is unconditional after successful timer-node allocation and timer-3 programming; it waits on unsigned `SYSTIMER_CLO` delta for two VBlank periods with no timeout, before returning to `KrnAddSysTimerHandler`/`platform_PostInit`. A nonadvancing mapped counter therefore holds platform post-init indefinitely (EK8909). The separate allocation-failure path skips timer setup and returns an indeterminate local pointer, which `platform_PostInit` ignores (EK8873); the loop is not reached in that case. No Pi hardware or timer was used. Source-only.

## Exec Signal dispatch branch recheck (2026-10-17)

Re-read the selected `rom/exec/signal.c:158-462` path alongside `RemTask` and the existing signal findings. The PC SMP cancelable path claims an IPI slot before locking the target, rechecks terminal state under `tc_SpinLock`, commits before releasing that lock, and aborts the slot on terminal targets; this remains the EK832 lifetime boundary and does not establish a second defect. The local SMP path checks terminal states under the task lock, atomically records the signal, sets exception state, and releases the task lock before scheduler calls. The remote running-task exception path caches the affinity pointer before unlock, and the waiting/ready paths pass the raw task to rescheduling after unlock; those remain the specific EK273/EK274 lifetime concerns already recorded. The legacy non-SMP list mutation remains protected by `Disable`. No additional branch-local defect established. `PutMsg`'s signed `1 << mp_SigBit` is already included in EK8800. This was source reconciliation only; no scheduler timing was run. Public `Signal` caller lifetime and architecture-specific scheduler helper completion remain open.


PC SMP task-reschedule list-lock pass (EK9018, 2026-10-17): traced `Signal`'s TS_WAIT wake branch through `krnSysCallReschedTask`, `X86_HandleReschedTask`, `X86_SetTaskState`, and the selected PC SMP/CPU-affinity setup (`rom/exec/signal.c:353-372`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/x86_syscalls.h:26-29`; `arch/all-pc/exec/platform_init.c:207-255,259-338,472-479`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/smp_exec.c:52-60`; `configure.in:1647-1671`). The handler selects a list lock from state before locking, but does not reselect/revalidate the list after lock acquisition. Two Signal callers can both pass through Signal's task-lock section before either local scheduler syscall changes TS_WAIT; each caller invokes the local syscall, while affinity only controls the subsequent KrnScheduleCPU request. The second helper can then mutate TaskReady links while holding TaskWaitSpinLock and with `X86_SetTaskState` target locking disabled for an already-READY task; the waiting task need not be eligible on both caller CPUs. Added EK9018 as distinct from EK274's task-object lifetime issue. The 32-bit PC branch is excluded because it does not define `EXEC_REMTASK_NEEDSSWITCH`. No concurrent calls or schedule were run; source-only.


PC reschedule syscall concurrency validation (EK9018 reaffirmed, 2026-10-17): checked the x86-64 PC `int $0xfe` call path, registered exception handler snapshot, syscall callback dispatch, and APIC affinity predicate (`arch/all-pc/kernel/x86_syscalls.h:26-29`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/syscall.c:41-80`; `rom/kernel/addexceptionhandler.c:144-185`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/apic.c:137-155`). The exception-handler list is snapshotted under its lock and callbacks execute after unlocking; this protects handler registration, not concurrent CPU invocations. `TASKAFFINITY_ANY` is accepted by `core_APIC_CPUInMask` on every CPU, confirming a normal unrestricted-affinity waiting task can be signaled locally from two CPUs. EK9018 remains supported and distinct from EK274 task lifetime. No system-call or scheduler interleaving was run. Source-only.


PC exception-callback dispatch pass (EK9019, 2026-10-17): re-read the i386 and x86-64 `cpu_Dispatch` exception branches against selected `Signal`, `SetExcept`, `Exception`, and shared PC scheduling (`arch/i386-pc/kernel/kernel_cpu.c:25-50`; `arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/kernel_cpu.c:76-80,168-176`; `rom/exec/signal.c:305-342`; `rom/exec/setexcept.c:69-87`; `rom/exec/exception.c:54-80`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:65-101`). Both PC dispatchers omit the only selected function that clears `TF_EXCEPT` and calls `tc_ExceptCode`: i386 has the TODO call commented, and x86-64 has it under `#if (0)` with a diagnostic in the alternative branch. A source-wide C/assembly call search found no alternate PC caller. Added EK9019. The affected conditions require a configured exception callback and matching signal; no callback or switch was run. Source-only.
PC ExecSMP AP scheduler-state initialization recheck (EK8829 retained, 2026-10-17): traced the selected AP allocation and initializer through first bootstrap `Permit()`/`Enable()`, initial dispatch, heartbeat, and IPI paths (`arch/all-pc/kernel/smp.c:247-253`; `kernel_scheduler.c:56-61,294-357`; `smp_exec.c:193-229`; `rom/exec/{permit,enable}.c`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/{apic_heartbeat,kernel_ipi}.c`). The AP `X86SchedulerPrivate` allocation is not MEMF_CLEAR, and the initializer only assigns granularity and quantum; no later per-CPU nesting initialization occurs before Permit/Enable. Confirmed the separate failed-allocation NULL dereference is already EK8828. No boot or memory-pattern case was run. Source-only.

Pthread mutex-attribute field and caller pass (2026-10-17; no new finding): traced mutexattr init/destroy/settype/gettype with the public struct, `_pthread_mutex_init`, and lock/unlock consumers. Init sets `kind` but not `pshared`; selected mutex construction reads only `kind`, and no maintained direct attribute caller was found.
