CreatePool size-overflow cross-check (2026-10-17; no new finding): followed unchecked initial puddle overhead/page-rounding in `rom/exec/createpool.c:96-113` into `InternalAllocPooled` (`rom/exec/memory.c:1054-1058,1090-1138`). A wrapped default `pool->PuddleSize` does not alone establish undersized user memory: an oversized allocation computes an enlarged puddle from the adjusted request, while requests whose adjustments also wrap are covered by EK783's direct `InternalAllocPooled` size-wrap consequence. The separate initial handle block remains sized from fixed pool-structure overhead and is checked before pool-header setup. Existing EK783 retained; no additional `CreatePool` arithmetic finding. Public extreme-size request only; no allocation executed. Source-only.

Cause caller qualification: ARM USB2OTG shared work nodes (2026-10-17; no new EK8875 trigger): traced the selected device's `FNAME_DEV(Cause)` wrapper and both `hu_PendingInt`/`hu_NakTimeoutInt` initializers (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/usb/usb2otg/usb2otg_device.c:260-279,760-797`). On ExecSMP the wrapper recognizes these exact nodes, serializes work-flag updates with `hu_Lock`, signals the dedicated worker, and returns without calling Exec `Cause`; on non-SMP the concurrent-CPU race is absent. The `Cause` calls found in core/scheduler code target `hu_PendingInt` and use the same wrapper (`usb2otg_core.c:338,688,735,787`; `usb2otg_schedule.c:292`). This selected ARM device path therefore does not add a second reproduction of EK8875. Source-only; no device or interrupt was run.

VMM paging bitmap/sentinel and cache caller audit (EK9020 added, 2026-10-17): traced `InitMap`/`NumContiguousSlots`/`AllocMultipleSlots` into initial and replacement cache setup, then through cache flush to partition-backed `WriteMultiplePages`. When PartSize has a multiple of 32 pages, the final real bitmap word has no occupied tail bits; contiguous counting can therefore pass `BitMapEnd` and count the zero sentinel as up to 32 extra slots. The resulting cache span can include invalid paging slots, and a slot exactly at PartSize passes the `>`-only offset check before a full-page transfer. Added EK9020, qualified for optional VMM and blocked AROS startup (EK9906); no runtime path was exercised. Source-only.
i386 PrepareContext stack-entry ABI recheck (EK8963 retained, 2026-10-17): recomputed the direct task-entry stack from `AROS_STACKALIGN == 16` (`arch/i386-all/include/aros/cpu.h:53`), NewAddTask's align-down (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:274-284`), and PrepareContext's argument/return pushes (`arch/i386-all/exec/preparecontext.c:71-89`). The selected PC dispatcher restores that ESP and EIP through IRET without a call/trampoline (`arch/i386-pc/kernel/kernel_cpu.c:25-52`; `core_interrupts.s:128-156`); selected `ServiceTask` and `SupervisorAlertTask` use one stack argument (`rom/exec/exec_init.c:321-329,342-349`). Confirmed the i386 build makefiles contain no stack-boundary override; GCC's i386 options document a default preferred boundary of 16 bytes and say the incoming boundary defaults to the preferred boundary ([GCC i386 options](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc-4.8.3/gcc/i386-and-x86-64-Options.html#i386-and-x86-64-Options)). EK8963 remains conditional on the selected cross-compiler retaining that incoming-boundary default; its code path and in-tree one-argument callers are confirmed. The toolchain invocation is generated outside this source snapshot. No task or build was run. Source-only.

VMM small-MaxTransfer loop candidate qualification (2026-10-21; no new EK): traced `de_MaxTransfer` from the DOS environment into `PagingDevParams.MaxTransfer` and the partition-backed `WriteMultiplePages` chunk expression (`compiler/include/dos/filehandler.h:47`; `workbench/system/VMM/find_dev_params.c:25-39`; `pageio.c:602-661`). A mounted partition can be configured with a byte limit below one page (`workbench/c/Mount.c:662,926`), for which `ALIGN_DOWN(MaxTransfer + 1, PAGESIZE)` is zero and the `BytesToWrite` loop makes no progress. The ordinary Mount and partition/device producers inspected use defaults of at least 2 MiB, but Mount accepts an explicit smaller value. This remains a downstream VMM candidate rather than a numbered finding: selected AROS VMM startup reaches EK9906’s unset `VirtAddrStart`/no-op address-range setup before a functioning paging range or this write path is established; no separate current AROS impact is shown. Keep the trigger qualified to a valid VMM paging path with a mounted backing partition whose configured MaxTransfer is below `PAGESIZE - 1`. No device or VMM path was run. Source-only.

VMM swap-slot capacity equation follow-up (2026-10-17; no new reachable AROS bitmap finding): traced the sole `InitMap(PartSize/PAGESIZE)` caller, page-file sizing/alignment, virtual-range calculation and cache reservation (`workbench/system/VMM/cache.c:30-51`; `pagehandler.c:151,153-160`; `VM_Manager_Init.c:742-753`; `pageio.c:88-130,191-195,336-345,398-400`). For normal nonzero backing sizes, `AddedMemSize` is capped at `PartSize - ALIGN_UP(PartSize/(PAGESIZE/sizeof(ULONG)),PAGESIZE)`, and the first page is resident; so the number of pageable virtual slots is below `PartSize/PAGESIZE`, the bitmap slot count. Cache slots are reserved from that same bitmap and later freed with their owning page slots. `AllocSlotNextTo`'s exhausted-map slot-zero fallback is therefore not reachable from the configured virtual-page capacity alone. A very small block partition can make table reserve equal/exceed `PartSize` before the subtraction; no minimum partition-size check was found, but the selected AROS path fails earlier at the tracked unset `VirtAddrStart` (EK9906), so downstream bitmap corruption is not credited as an active AROS issue. External device geometry and alternate target startup remain unverified. Source-only.


Exec reset callback API/caller recheck (2026-10-17; no additional finding): reread `AddResetCallback`/`RemResetCallback` and the non-supervisor callback traversal (`rom/exec/addresetcallback.c:53-63`; `rom/exec/remresetcallback.c:45-50`; `rom/exec/doresetcallbacks.c:65-120,185-207`). Registration is an unconditional `Enqueue` and returns TRUE; removal is a direct `Remove`. The shutdown path traverses with `ForeachNodeSafe`, launches callbacks serially in tasks outside supervisor mode, and preserves the waiter/signal after timeout. The existing EK59 covers the saved-next-node hazard if a callback removes that node during traversal; no independent defect in the thin add/remove wrappers was established. Selected additional callers include timer.device, whose reset node is added at init and removed at expunge (`arch/all-pc/timer/timer_init.c:182,224`), and network PCI units already covered by their own failure-path findings. The direct-call search is not a full caller lifecycle audit: 42 C/header files matched, including platform-specific and macro-replaced cases. Broader producers and callback interleavings remain pending. Source-only.

Exec AddDevice selected registration recheck (2026-10-17; no new Exec candidate): reread the complete `AddDevice` body and representative resident, USB MassStorage, printer, and `RemDevice` paths (`rom/exec/adddevice.c:53-69`; `rom/exec/initresident.c:122-155`; `workbench/devs/USB/classes/MassStorage/storage_device.c:784-812`; `rom/exec/remdevice.c:65-85`). `AddDevice` computes the vector checksum before acquiring the public device-list write lock, then publishes under that lock and `Forbid`; InitResident only publishes after its init returns non-NULL. The selected MassStorage constructor's unchecked `AllocPooled` remains its existing disk-report candidate, not a separate list-publication defect. Printer's pre-worker rollback and its post-spawn reply-port failure remain covered by EK9099/OD1028. This pass found no new generic AddDevice issue; generated registrations, ownership after publication, and duplicate-name policy remain open as recorded in its file row. Source-only.


Exec low-memory registration and retry recheck (2026-10-17; EK34, EK8782, EK8818 retained, no scope change): re-followed all three checked-in C producers and both allocator retry levels. Diskfont's embedded handler is removed during expunge, confirming EK34's saved-head-before-lock window (`workbench/libs/diskfont/diskfont_init.c:52-55,65-77`; `rom/exec/allocmem.c:108-116`; `rom/exec/memory.c:1313-1349`). `log.resource` registers before `NewCreateTask` and returns failure based on the output service port, but init rollback does not unregister the embedded handler, preserving EK8782 (`rom/log/log.c:298-317`; generated rollback `tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1156-1180`). `RemMemHandler` permits recursive removal while `checkMemHandlers` owns `LowMemSem`; retry returns before cursor advancement, and `Remove` leaves detached node links intact, preserving EK8818's conditional callback self-removal/successor-removal cases (`rom/exec/remmemhandler.c:46-52`; `rom/exec/memory.c:1324-1349`; `rom/exec/remove.c:55-63`). The three built-in handlers still do not establish EK8818's exact sequence; external callback behavior is not verified. No allocation failure, init rollback, or callback interleaving was run. Source-only.


Exec public semaphore caller recheck (2026-10-17; EK9025 added): traced optional CDFS's first-use `FindSemaphore`/`AddSemaphore` publication through device startup and failure cleanup (`rom/filesys/cdfs/cdfs.c:222-248,291-305,611-624`; Exec API `rom/exec/addsemaphore.c:51-65`; `remsemaphore.c:47-58`). A first CDFS handler start can publish the singleton, then return failure if device allocation or `BCache_Create` fails before any device is linked; that path bypasses the only cleanup that removes the public semaphore and closes `utility.library`. Added EK9025 as a selected caller lifecycle defect, conditional on builds including the optional `kernel-fs-cdfs` target. The generic AddSemaphore/RemSemaphore list locking remains unchanged; platform-specific CDFS success and teardown interleavings are still open. No failure was induced. Source-only.

PCI device-list semaphore caller follow-up (EK8854, 2026-10-17; no new finding): traced `dev_lock` initialization before PCI root/driver publication (`rom/hidds/pci/pci_init.c:59-65`), shared enumeration and exclusive `PCI__HW__RemoveDriver` (`pciclass.c:414-449,451-516`), plus the public remove wrappers and PCI expunge caller (`rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c:266-288`; `pciclass.c:626-660`; `pci_init.c:71-103`). The selected removal path reaches `AttemptSemaphore` only after library initialization and performs `ReleaseSemaphore` on both post-acquisition exits; if it cannot acquire, it returns without mutation. The legacy class-removal wrapper enumerates, drops the shared lock before attempting exclusive removal, as its comment requires. This selected PCI caller does not instantiate EK8854's taskless PREINITLIB condition. Broader direct clients and other attempt-API callers remain covered by the existing census/open scope. No PCI operation was run. Source-only.

PCI class setup/enumeration source pass (2026-10-17; no new EK): read `PCI__HW__SetUpDriver`, `AssignIRQ`, `FindBridge`, and `PCI__Hidd_PCI__EnumDevices` end-to-end (`rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:104-449`), following root `HW_AddDriver` setup/publication and removal cleanup (`rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c:173-223,266-300`). Bus scanning extends `highBus` only from successfully constructed bridge objects; ordinary and multifunction function iteration stays within PCI's 32-device/8-function limits. Enumeration balances its shared list lock after all callbacks. The setup IRQ-routing and optional warning passes traverse the global device list without `dev_lock`; the source comment only establishes that the *new driver* is not public, while root setup runs before publication and has no setup-wide serialization. A concurrent PCI driver setup/removal could therefore overlap those traversals with list edits/disposal, but this pass did not establish a selected in-tree concurrent trigger or hotplug contract, so it is left as an open caller/concurrency question rather than promoted. No bus scan or concurrent method was run. Source-only.

WaitForPort EK8913 owner-side trigger follow-up (2026-10-17): traced the selected AROSTCP `S/startnet` script from `Run >NIL: QUIET AROSTCP` to `WaitForPort AROSTCP` (`workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/S/startnet:3-5`) and the selected AROSTCP Rexx owner. `rexx_show()` publishes `AROSTCP` with `AddPort`; shutdown calls `rexx_deinit()`, which invokes `rexx_hide()`/`RemPort`, drains queued messages, and `DeleteMsgPort`s the same object (`workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/kern/amiga_rexx.c:43-48,109-127`). This supplies a concrete selected producer/remover whose service lifetime can overlap the command's repeated Boolean `FindPort` polling; the traversal race is already EK8913, not a new finding. The script's `If NOT Warn` only reports whether the wait command timed out; it does not hold or dereference the returned port. No stack startup/shutdown was run. Source-only.

WaitIO premature-completion caller follow-up (EK8799, 2026-10-17): traced `Exec_DoResetCallbacks`' shared VBlank timer request from setup through each handler's `SendIO`, `Wait` on callback/timer signals, `CheckIO`/`WaitIO`, next-handler reuse, and final close/free (`rom/exec/doresetcallbacks.c:79-115,143-164,190-205`). Timer VBlank expiry removes the request from the timer wait-list and calls `ReplyMsg` (`rom/timer/lowlevel.c:343-381`); `ReplyMsg` publishes NT_REPLYMSG before `InternalPutMsg` links it, as already established for EK8799. If the separate callback-completion signal wakes the launcher during this interval on ExecSMP, it may `WaitIO`-remove before the port insertion, then reuse the same timer request for the next callback. This adds a selected Exec-owned timeout caller to EK8799; no new finding is counted. No reset or timer race was run. Source-only.


Signal task-reference handoff recheck (EK274 detailed report restored, 2026-10-17): compared the `TS_WAIT` and remote `TS_READY` handoffs in `Signal` with `RemTask` cleanup and the first dereference in PC, ARM32 and AArch64 scheduler helpers. The selected `security.library` `secKill` caller directly removes plain tasks. Added the detailed EK274 entry and index summary. x86-64 Multiboot2 memory-map conversion follow-up (2026-10-17; no new EK): traced the selected bootstrap `MB2_TAG_MMAP` path from `mb2_parse` through its in-place `mmap_convert` and into x86-64 kernel startup (`arch/all-pc/bootstrap/multiboot2.c:80-97,143-150,365`; `compiler/include/aros/multiboot2.h:180-208`; `arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/kernel_startup.c:259-297,435-454,520`). For spec-shaped entries, the source and destination record strides are both 24 bytes on the selected x86-64 ABI; the first converted `mb_mmap.size` occupies the tag's `entry_version` word, and subsequent size fields occupy the preceding entry's reserved pad, preserving address/length/type fields. The startup's largest-address and MemHeader consumers are the existing tracked `kernel_mmap.c` paths. This pass did not establish a defect for valid entries. The conversion still assumes bootloader-provided tag and entry sizes are valid; malformed/truncated Multiboot2 tags and firmware contracts remain open. No boot image or firmware was run. Source-only.

ChildWait EK811 recheck (2026-10-17; finding retained): compared the current `Exec_CleanupETask` publisher, `ChildWait`, `SetSignal`, `Wait`, and configured variants. The producer links the completion ETask before signaling; ChildWait unlocks its port scan before clearing the same signal; `SetSignal` and `Wait` serialize the received bit under the task spinlock but do not cover the earlier list predicate. Exec documents `Forbid` as CPU-local on EXECSMP, and configure.in enables EXECSMP for x86-64 PC and Raspberry Pi `smp` variants. Uniprocessor Forbid closes this interleave. No separate SetSignal/Wait finding and no reproduction. Detailed EK811 remains in the main report. Source-only.

CreatePool EK809 target-configuration refinement (2026-10-17): rechecked the EXECSMP build gate against both PC startup allocator selectors. `configure.in` defines `__AROSEXEC_SMP__` for the x86_64 PC `smp` variant only (`:1647-1669`); i386 sets platform SMP support but not Exec SMP in its target block (`:1624-1646`). Both i386 and x86_64 startup code accept `notlsf` (`arch/i386-pc/kernel/kernel_startup.c:320-321`; `arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/kernel_startup.c:374-375`), so only x86_64 PC `smp` plus `notlsf` reaches the nonmanaged hand-built MemHeader lock acquisition described by EK809. Tightened the detailed report's affected configuration accordingly; no new finding. No build or boot was run. Wider pool callers and non-PC allocator configurations remain open; source-only.


AVL API semantic recheck (2026-10-17; no new EK): independently traced `AVL_FindNode`, predecessor/successor-by-key, address traversal, and delete rebalancing against the documented comparator sign and node-membership contracts (`rom/exec/avl.c:651-700,706-1080`; `compiler/include/exec/avl.h:16-34`). Floor/ceiling searches retain the nearest candidate on the correct side; left/right traversal follows the parent links as expected; root removal with one child resets that child's parent. The selected `avltest.c` checks stored balance factors after batches of insert/delete operations, but does not assert parent pointers or sorted order after each mutation (`developer/debug/test/exec/avltest.c:72-99,257-306`). No separate native AVL defect established; external callers and runtime/test execution remain outside this source pass.

ARM32 virtual-to-physical HIDD caller reconciliation (EK8839 requalified; 2026-10-17): traced the remaining selected VC/GPU direct calls. VCGFX's control block, bounce buffer and fill pixel are allocated from `MEMF_PUBLIC`; VC4Gallium's DMA control block uses `AllocMem(MEMF_PUBLIC)` (`vcgfx_dma.c:71-108`; `vc4_galliumclass.c:170-181`), so the checked buffers stay in the low public heap after the Pi boot lowers `KRN_MEMUpper` to the relocated kernel's physical base. VCGFX `PutImage` passes `msg->pixels` into `vc4_dma_put`, which translates it but returns FALSE when the resulting range is not bus-addressable; `PutImage` then falls back to NEON copying (`vcgfx_bitmapclass.c:94-96`; `vcgfx_dma.c:350-382`). This does not prove erroneous DMA output; caller-buffer origin and any valid high-map pointer remain open. No DMA or translation was run. Source-only.
Task-notification hook removal guarantee recheck (2026-10-17; no new EK): traced the semaphore mode and lifetime from `RemTaskNotifyHook` through `taskres_NotifyTasks` and Security teardown (`rom/task/RemTaskNotifyHook.c:43-48`; `task_support.c:130-145`; `security_task.c:371-389`). Dispatch holds the shared registry semaphore while invoking each callback; removal obtains it exclusively, so returning from removal drains any in-flight callback before Security frees callback state and prevents later dispatch. The selected Security callback does not add/remove hooks. `AddTaskNotifyHook` does not reject a repeated registration of the same linked Hook node, but no checked-in C caller repeats registration; this caller-precondition case is not promoted. Existing external callback self-removal deadlock EK8787 remains conditional. No hook registration or task event was run. Source-only.

NewCreateTaskA optional-name caller census (2026-10-17; EK788 retained, scope unchanged): rechecked the source-tree C callsites omitting both `TASKTAG_NAME` and `TASKTAG_TASKMSGPORT`. The two Intuition PPC calls are guarded by `__MORPHOS__` (`windowclasses.c:414-422`) or disabled `PROPHACK` (`inputhandler.h:18-19`, `propgclass.c:586-595`); they are not selected AROS callers. The hosted hostdisk call includes `TASKTAG_NAME` (`hostdisk_device.c:139-142`). RawPutChar/krnPutC selected-target slice (2026-10-17; no new EK): rechecked `RawPutChar`'s KernelBase gate against its direct callers and selected `krnPutC` implementations. RawPutChar deliberately emits only when `KernelBase` is non-NULL; early kernel diagnostics call `krnPutC` directly, and the generic `KrnPutChar` contract explicitly permits a NULL base. The selected Unix and MinGW implementations use `HostIFace->KPutC` independently of the base; MinGW brackets the call with Forbid/Permit only when the base exists. PC implementations preserve interrupt flags around boot-console output; native ARM/AArch64/RISC-V and m68k/PPC implementations also tolerate a NULL base, with hardware-specific output paths. No generic early-boot null dereference or selected direct-caller misuse was established. Remaining target routes include m68k-emulation thunk behavior, host-interface setup ordering, hardware UART/firmware readiness and debug-output serialization; source-only, no output path was run.

Exec_ExtAlert context-type producer census (EK61/EK426 recheck, 2026-10-17; no new candidate): enumerated every maintained direct call: plain `Alert` supplies `AT_NONE`/NULL; semaphore and Supervisor helpers supply type zero/NULL; the trap handler supplies `AT_CPU` plus `ExceptionContext`; MungWall supplies `AT_MUNGWALL` plus `MungwallContext`; and the two memory-alert branches supply `AT_MEMORY` plus `MMContext` (`rom/exec/{alert.c:58,semaphores.c:28,41,supervisor.c:76,traphandler.c:129,mungwall.c:158,memory.c:466,509}`). These are the only non-NULL context types and match `contextSizes[0..3]` (`alert.c:63-69`); no selected private caller passes an out-of-range type or mismatched data structure. Public `Alert` caller execution contexts, task teardown races, external private callers, and architecture-specific alert behavior remain open. No alert was raised. Source-only.

PC bootstrap long-long diagnostic caller follow-up (EK692 boundary recheck, 2026-10-17; no new finding): traced the bootstrap `kprintf` wrapper to `compiler/fmtprintf` rather than Exec `RawDoFmt` (`arch/all-pc/bootstrap/support.c:106-113`). The selected multiboot v1/v2 call sites using `%llX` report 64-bit framebuffer addresses in hexadecimal (`multiboot1.c:147,158,218,230,252`; `multiboot2.c:185,232,276,319,331,361`), and the formatter handles hexadecimal long-long values without the unavailable decimal division helpers (`compiler/fmtprintf/fmtprintf.c:84-90,164-214`; `fmtprintf_pre.c:102-140`). The bootstrap formatter’s documented `%llu`/`%lld` limitation therefore does not establish a defect in those selected diagnostics. This is distinct from EK692, which concerns the built-in Exec RawDoFmt parser and its documented `ll`/`L` contract. Other bootstrap formatting conversions and callers remain pending; no bootstrap was run. Source-only.

PC bootstrap archive-record boundary pass (EK9031 added, 2026-10-17): traced `AddModule` archive iteration through `ar_name` and `ar_next`. The loops only test `file < mod_end`; the helpers read fixed header fields and the BSD name length without receiving or checking the module end. A short trailing record can therefore be read beyond the module extent. Added EK9031 for truncated/inconsistent ar-format Multiboot modules; distinct from EK347's failed-iteration behavior, EK349's BSD extended-name `ar_size` double-counting, and EK350's workspace-allocation failure. The selected in-tree package writer does not emit ar archives; no malformed archive was parsed. Source-only.

Efika idle-task creation failure caller recheck (2026-10-17; no new EK): traced the `NewAddTask` result in `Kernel_Init` through Efika dispatch and all `idle_task` references (`arch/ppc-chrp/efika/kernel/kernel_init.c:647-696`; `kernel/scheduler.c:82-154,238-326`; `kernel/intr.c:337-380`). Superseded by EK9074: the caller unconditionally assigns `idle_task = t` even when `NewAddTask()` returns NULL; the unregistered allocation remains retained, and `core_Dispatch` waits with interrupts enabled when `TaskReady` is empty. The potentially unsafe allocation-failure branch raises `AT_DeadEnd` before dereferencing allocations; Exec's `Alert` then calls `ShutdownA(SD_ACTION_REBOOT)`, whose documented contract allows a zero return if reboot fails (`rom/exec/alert.c:183-185`; `rom/exec/shutdowna.c:34-39`). Falling through after a failed reboot would proceed into null dereferences, but the machine is already in the fatal alert path and this does not establish a distinct recoverable task-creation bug. The prior EK225/EK226 shorthand was not a standalone report/index entry; EK225 is now restored as a detailed finding, and EK226 remains unsubstantiated. Efika build viability remains unverified. No allocation failure or boot was induced. Source-only.


Debug-library KRN_DebugInfo producer lifetime follow-up (2026-10-17; no new EK): traced `Debug_Init` and `RegisterModule_ELF` against each maintained boot producer (`rom/debug/debug_init.c:33-58`; `rom/debug/registermodule.c:350-442`). The shared PC/hosted/ARM bootstrap ELF loader copies module descriptors, ELF headers, section tables and names into the persistent kernel read-only image before returning `KRN_DebugInfo` (`bootstrap/elfloader.c:540-549,701-733`). Efika and Sam440 copy Parthenope module metadata into their reserved kernel memory during boot-tag processing (`arch/ppc-chrp/efika/kernel/kernel_init.c:239-296`; `arch/ppc-sam440/kernel/kernel_startup.c:275-343`). OpenSBI builds descriptors from its resident package image; the comment says that image remains resident, and the bump-allocated descriptor chain lies below the final free-memory boundary (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_elf.c:467-500`; `kernel_startup.c:824-840,890-893`). `RegisterModule_ELF` copies the module name, section string tables and symbol records into its own nodes before returning, while section addresses refer to loaded module memory. Thus no dangling `KRN_DebugInfo` producer storage was established for these selected paths. Startup callback overlap and remaining generated target variants remain pending; no debug library was initialized. Source-only.

Exec reset-callback timeout-boundary follow-up (EK8946 rechecked, 2026-10-17): inspected the exact task-priority and task-removal synchronization rather than relying only on their API contracts. `SetTaskPri` reads `task->tc_SpinLock` before acquiring it, then reads/updates task and ETask state under that lock (`rom/exec/settaskpri.c:67-101`); `RemTask` marks the handler removed, deletes its context and cleans up its ETask without acquiring that task spinlock (`rom/exec/remtask.c:64-132`). The timeout branch's local `Forbid()` does not serialize a remote CPU (`rom/exec/forbid.c:58-64`). This supports EK8946's conditional stale-pointer race: after the launcher has observed the nonnull callback pointer, the handler can enter removal on another CPU before `SetTaskPri` takes the task lock. The stale pointer is not made safe by `SetTaskPri`'s internal lock because obtaining that lock itself dereferences the task. EK873 (late completion after a successor starts) and EK59 (saved reset-list successor removed during a wait) remain separate interleavings. No task teardown or reset timing was run. Source-only.

Efika context allocation recheck (EK225, 2026-10-17): verified `KrnCreateContext`'s `Allocate` result is passed to `memset` before the null check and public-memory fallback (`arch/ppc-chrp/efika/kernel/kernel_init.c:392-408`); the selected context producer is `arch/ppc-chrp/exec/preparecontext.c:70`. Restored the missing formal finding. Efika build viability remains unverified; no allocation failure or boot was run. Source-only.

Efika MMU mapping recheck (EK224, 2026-10-17): traced the public byte-count `MapPCI` contract through the selected Efika PCI override into `KrnMapGlobal` and `mmu_map_area`. Non-page-multiple lengths underflow the unsigned countdown, install successive mappings until the hash has no free PTE, and leave a partial mapping on failure. No in-tree Efika client with a nonmultiple length or live MMU was established. Also found EK223 is only a historical row reference: no formal numbered finding or retained build log substantiates its claimed build break. `kernel_intern.h` defines `goUser()` with an empty parameter list; GNU C accepts the three `goUser(msr)` calls as non-prototype calls, so their arity alone does not prove a compile failure. The helper ignores the saved MSR, but no selected supervisor-mode caller was established. Efika build viability remains unverified rather than treated as established. Source-only.

Efika saved-MSR restoration recheck (2026-10-17; no numbered finding): followed `goSuper` through `SC_SUPERSTATE` in the syscall handler, compared `goUser` with `KrnMapGlobal`'s direct `wrmsr(msr)` restore, and traced all three `goUser(msr)` callers. The helper ignores the extra argument under GNU C and sets `MSR_PR` unconditionally. Repository caller search did not establish a selected supervisor-mode entry; retain this only as an open caller question, not a numbered finding. This also explains why the earlier EK223 build-break claim is not substantiated by call arity. No target build or privilege transition was run. Source-only.

Task CPU-time rounding findings restored (EK316/EK318, 2026-10-17): traced `iet_CpuTime` producer normalization, `QueryTaskTagList` nanosecond-to-microsecond rounding, and the selected `C:TaskList` formatter. EK316 is the API value crossing 1,000,000 microseconds without a seconds carry; EK318 is the independent display rounding of valid 995,000–999,999-microsecond values to `.100`. Counter boundary and display behavior were not run. Source-only.


CreatePool EK809 lock-construction recheck (2026-10-17): compared the nonmanaged handle path with `AllocMemHeader`. `CreatePool` passes `requirements & ~MEMF_SEM_PROTECTED` to `nommu_AllocMem`, then writes the MemHeader fields directly and calls `Allocate` without `EXEC_SPINLOCK_INIT`; `AllocMemHeader` initializes the lock immediately after `nommu_AllocMem` (`rom/exec/createpool.c:126-175`; `rom/exec/memory.c:902-915`). Thus even a protected-pool caller reaches the initial unprotected standard allocation, and the flag is applied later to the pool structure. Clarified EK809. The x86_64 PC SMP plus `notlsf` scope and stale-lock trigger remain as previously qualified; no pool was instantiated. Source-only.
ARM32 secondary-online publication recheck (EK8904 strengthened, 2026-10-17): traced `cpu_Register` → `cpu_Init` → `cpu_InitBootStrap` failure into BCM2708's startup-lock handshake and `KrnGetCPUCount`. `cpu_Init` ORs the CPU bit before bootstrap task creation (`arch/arm-native/kernel/kernel_cpu.c:358-365`); bootstrap failure jumps to the fatal label, releases `startup_lock`, and does not clear the bit (`:185-186,207-225`). BCM2708 then accepts the unlock and continues its ordered startup loop (`platform_bcm2708.c:115-160`), while `getcpucount.c` popcounts the stale bit. Expanded EK8904's ARM32 consequence and corrected the `getcpucount.c` coverage wording; no bootstrap failure or boot was induced. Source-only.


ChildStatus/waitpid API-contract recheck (EK812 refined, 2026-10-17): confirmed the selected `waitpid(pid, ...)` caller calls `ChildStatus(tid)` and returns `ECHILD` immediately for `CHILD_NOTFOUND` (`compiler/crt/posixc/waitpid.c:113-117`); notified-child exit removes from `et_Children` under `iet_TaskLock`, then appends under the port lock after releasing the first lock (`rom/exec/exec_util.c:307-330`), while `ChildStatus` scans the live list under only local `Forbid` before taking the port read lock (`rom/exec/childstatus.c:61-87`). The ChildStatus API note limits supported queries to `NP_NotifyOnDeath` children (`:31-36`); EK812’s live-list traversal UAF remains possible during such a valid query if it visits a different unnotified sibling that exits concurrently, whereas the transient `CHILD_NOTFOUND` requires handoff of the queried notified child. This narrows the trigger; the existing handoff finding and recommended parent-task-lock/port-lock ordering stand. No task or wait call was run. Source-only.


Exec child-status paired API pass (EK812/EK811 boundary recheck, 2026-10-17; no additional candidate): reread complete `ChildWait`, `ChildFree`, and `ChildOrphan` paths against `Exec_CleanupETask` and the POSIX wait wrappers (`rom/exec/childwait.c:54-105`; `childfree.c:52-108`; `childorphan.c:61-125`; `exec_util.c:302-330`; `compiler/crt/posixc/waitpid.c:113-147`). Completed-child removal from `mp_MsgList` uses the same port spinlock as `ChildStatus` and `ChildWait`, then expunges only after unlink, so no separate completed-record free race was found. `ChildOrphan` changes `et_Children` under `iet_TaskLock`, corroborating EK812’s missing reader lock. `ChildWait` releases the message-port read lock before clearing `SIGF_CHILD` and waiting, leaving the already documented EK811 publish/signal interval intact; no duplicate finding added. The live-child `ChildFree` branch concerns the API-documented invalid operation on a running child and is not promoted as a supported-call finding. No child lifecycle or wait call was run. Source-only.

AllocPooled selected HyperLayers caller/error-path recheck (2026-10-17; no new EK): traced `rom/hyperlayers/layers_init.c:26-37`, which checks `CreatePool` failure and returns FALSE before publishing `lb_ClipRectPool` or installing the layer manager. The selected `_AllocClipRect` and `_CreateClipRectsFromRegion` direct pooled allocations can fail later without consistently handling NULL; the concrete layer-operation consequences are already tracked as GD4261/GD4262 in the Graphics/Desktop report (`rom/hyperlayers/basicfuncs.c:332,1147-1155`). Semaphore writer-progress contract recheck (EK875, 2026-10-17): reread `ObtainSemaphoreShared`'s public function contract and the implementation's shared admission and release scan (`rom/exec/obtainsemaphoreshared.c:33-38`; `semaphores.c:91-113,124-150,164-201`; `releasesemaphore.c:118-185`). The public text defines multiple simultaneous shared owners and says an exclusive owner prevents shared acquisition, but does not specify writer preference or bounded wait. The implementation permits arriving readers to join an active shared group despite an older queued writer, and release grants queued shared requests beyond intervening writers. This confirms the behavior in EK875 but does not establish a contract violation or starvation under a maintained workload; retain its conditional/medium-confidence wording pending an explicit fairness contract or selected sustained-reader caller. No contention was run. Source-only.

PC `krnSysCallReschedTask` additional caller-state pass (2026-10-17; no additional EK): enumerated the checked direct Exec callers beyond `Signal`: `NewAddTask` publishes a new task from `TS_INVALID` to `TS_READY` (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:33-43`), the AddTask `TS_REMOVED` fallback is reached only if the CPU-affinity flag changes between its repeated checks; with stable flags, the earlier branches cover both values (`:51-54,90-115`), `RemTask` requests terminal removal before canceling queued signal IPIs (`rom/exec/remtask.c:68-123`), and `ServiceTask` can request `TS_READY` from its unexpected-service-state recovery branch (`rom/exec/service.c:93-112`). The new-task invalid-state path is distinct and does not rely on stale list selection; the teardown and service-recovery callers have their own lifetime/state preconditions and were not shown to produce an independent instance beyond EK9018's concurrent stale-state/list-lock mechanism. No task transition or signal was run. Source-only.

AUX fast-BPTR handover duplicate reconciliation (2026-10-17; no new EK): cross-checked the producer, con-handler consumer and architecture BPTR definitions (aux_handler.c:42,131-147; con_handler.c:124,480-499; compiler/include/dos/bptr.h:17-22,47-50). The bit-30 pointer corruption is the same defect already detailed as EK867, so removed duplicate EK9036 from the detailed report. The default startup is stack-backed and mountlist startup uses the same encoding. No target/runtime was used.

POSIXC descriptor lookup/close lifetime contract follow-up (2026-10-17; not promoted): traced `__getfdesc`'s owner-table lock and returned `fdesc *` (`compiler/crt/posixc/__fdesc.c:116-144`) through selected `read` and `close` (`read.c:53-81`; `close.c:53-80,111-118`). The lock ends before the caller uses the pointer, while close can free both the FCB and descriptor after its FCB lock; therefore concurrent close after lookup can invalidate the returned object before use. `__dos64_read` takes the FCB lock only after reading its fields (`__dos64.c:136-153`). However, this `close()` implementation explicitly documents threaded application use as unsupported (`close.c:36-38`), so this interleaving is retained as an open API/thread-safety contract gap, not added as a finding. The same shared-table pthread setup and separate publication races remain tracked in EK8995. No thread or descriptor was used. Source-only.

Console input compaction CopyMem architecture census (2026-10-17; no new EK): closed the cross-architecture gap noted on `support.c:1122-1132`. `answer_read_request` moves the unread suffix from a higher source address down to the beginning of the same buffer; forward traversal preserves this overlap direction. The selected generic implementation traverses forward (`rom/exec/copymem.c:74-77,99-100`); x86-64's implementation also copies forward (`arch/x86_64-all/exec/copymem.c:122-165,210-214`); m68k baseline and CPU-specialized paths use post-increment forward moves (`arch/m68k-all/exec/copymem_.S:21-50`; `_020.S:35-103`; `_040.S:37-56`; `_060.S:37-57`, selected by `exec_platform.c:34-52`). The i386 SSE vector routes copies below 4096 bytes to the generic implementation, and its large-copy routine includes a backward path (`arch/i386-all/exec/copymem_SSE.S:47-61,91-97,161-218`); this console buffer compaction is bounded below that threshold. Thus the examined target implementations preserve this specific overlap direction despite the public no-overlap contract; no candidate is credited. No copy was executed. Source-only.

Condition-variable lazy-init publication follow-up (EK604 expanded, 2026-10-17): re-read `pthread_cond_signal`, `_pthread_cond_broadcast`, lazy condition initialization and Exec semaphore initialization (`compiler/pthread/pthread_cond_signal.c:26-31`; `pthread_cond_broadcast.c:35-45`; `pthread_cond_init.c:35-41`; `rom/exec/initsemaphore.c:49-67`). `InitSemaphore` writes `NT_SIGNALSEM` before its count/owner fields and SMP spinlock; `SemaphoreIsInvalid` therefore may report valid before `InitSemaphore` completes. On ExecSMP a concurrent condition operation can reach `ObtainSemaphore` while its lock is uninitialized. Once that returns, the separate window before `NEWLIST(&cond->waiters)` still lets broadcast traverse a null static-initializer list head, as already documented in EK604. Same root cause; no new finding ID. Direct `pthread_cond_signal` callers in this tree are `sem_post` and wrapper-level uses; sem/barrier objects shown in the selected callers explicitly initialize their condition variables, so the concurrent static-first-use trigger remains an external public API case. No concurrent call or SMP run was performed. Source-only.
Signal restricted-IPI and teardown reconciliation (2026-10-17; no new EK): re-read the full `Signal` body, affinity route, selected ARM/AArch64 FIQ hook, PC IPI hook queue, `RemTask` cancellation and m68k `ExitIntr` gate. On ARM/AArch64, the stale target-CPU route where a task migrates between Signal's snapshot and FIQ delivery is already EK8905; the hook's local `FLAG_SCHEDSWITCH_SET` does not kick the task's new CPU. PC's raw queued-hook lifetime without a cancelable interface is EK832. The selected native cancellation path commits under `tc_SpinLock` and drains/waits before cleanup; no additional queue lifetime issue was established. m68k's `ExitIntr` assembly skips scheduler exit when the saved SR returns to supervisor mode, then calls `core_ExitIntr` only on user-mode return (`arch/m68k-all/exec/exitintr.S:23-42`); this matches `core_ExitIntr`'s deferred-schedule contract and adds no nested-kernel scheduling defect. The broad public `Signal` caller census and remaining architecture IPI contracts stay open. No IPI, migration or interrupt was run; source-only.


USB HID NewAddTask caller failure trace (cross-report OD3564, 2026-10-17): traced the keyboard/mouse `NewAddTask` calls against the complete Exec failure contract. `Exec_InitETask` returns FALSE when its ETask allocation fails, and architecture `PrepareContext` can also fail; `NewAddTask` returns NULL without publishing the task in either case (`rom/exec/exec_util.c:111-123`; `newaddtask.c:270-309`). The two selected USB HID callers ignore the result, retain their caller-built `tc_MemEntry` chains and publish the task pointer; Exec normally frees those entries only on task removal (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/HID/kbdclass.c:206-234`; `mouseclass.c:191-219`; `rom/exec/remtask.c:168-181`). The failure consequence belongs to Other Drivers OD3564 rather than a duplicate EK issue in the generic API. No allocation failure or task creation was run. Source-only.

KrnStatMemory selected-caller recheck (2026-10-17; no new EK): reread `KrnStatMemoryA` and `mm_StatMemHeader` against `AddMemList`, `MEM_LOCK` and all checked-in direct C/header calls (`rom/kernel/statmemory.c:23-125`; `mm_linear.c:468-573`; `rom/exec/addmemlist.c:78-101`). The only selected production caller, `Exec_AddResource`, requests `KMS_PageSize` and takes the early return before traversing `SysBase->MemList`; the allocator test also asks only for page size and is excluded by its manifest. Aggregate queries initialize result values then traverse the list without taking `MEM_LOCK`, while AddMemList publishes initialized headers under that lock. The source states headers are only added and never removed; any concurrent snapshot concern therefore remains conditional on external clients requesting aggregate tags, with no selected caller or established invalid state transition. No separate finding is credited. No memory query or concurrent header addition was run. Source-only.

Intuition startup-task removal caller pass (EK task-removal review; 2026-10-17; no new finding): re-read `InitDefaultScreennotifyHandler` and `InitDefaultMenuHandler` against their worker entrypoints (`rom/intuition/screennotifytask.c:24-66,75-112`; `rom/intuition/menutask.c:105-175,225-260`). Each parent clears its signal bit before `NewCreateTask`, then waits for the worker's initialization signal. On failure, each worker signals only after publishing its success flag and then blocks in `Wait(0)`; the parent calls `RemTask` only on that failed-start path. Successful workers continue using their reply port, so the parent does not remove them there. The stack parameter pointer remains live until the signal wait returns, and no post-signal worker access to that stack record is established on the failure path. No separate task-removal lifetime bug found in these callers. No task or allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

PC secondary-CPU bootstrap RemTask caller pass (2026-10-17; no new finding): traced `smp_Entry`'s AP bootstrap task from `cpu_InitBootStrap` through `cpu_BootStrap`, idle-task creation, ready-lock release and `RemTask` (`arch/all-pc/kernel/smp.c:39-145`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/smp_exec.c:94-191,193-231`; `arch/all-pc/exec/platform_init.c:350-414`). The AP bootstrap is made current before Exec scheduling is enabled; after idle-task creation returns, the entry path releases the ready lock, removes the bootstrap task, and halts. The source does not establish an ordinary scheduler handoff that would let this bootstrap task resume later and run the post-`RemTask` halt path as a freed task. Allocation failure in idle-task construction can leave the CPU without its idle task, but the selected dispatcher and that failure route are already covered by EK8835/EK8790; no duplicate finding was added. The hook-pool mask allocations in `smp_Initialize` remain covered by the existing IPI allocation candidates. No SMP boot or allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

Signal restricted-context IPI wake caller recheck for EK274 (2026-10-17; no additional race): traced the ARM32/AArch64 `signal_hook` TS_WAIT path from off-affinity Signal routing through `krnSysCallReschedTask` (`rom/exec/signal.c:42-72,164-180,198-225`). Although the hook drops `tc_SpinLock` before that call, both selected native `core_CancelCallIPIs` implementations wait until any matching in-flight hook has finished (`arch/arm-native/kernel/kernel_ipi.c:178-215`; `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/kernel_ipi.c:145-181`), and `RemTask` invokes cancellation before freeing the task (`rom/exec/remtask.c:112-130`). Thus this queued-hook route does not establish EK274's concurrent-free window; EK274 remains limited to the direct local `Signal` wake path, which has no queued callback for cancellation to drain. No IPI or task removal was run. Source-only.

OpenSBI PLIC alternating-claim candidate withdrawal (EK9029 withdrawn, 2026-10-17): revisited `krnHandleExternalIRQ`'s consecutive-source guard against `krnPLICEnable`'s fixed priority-1 writes (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/intr.c:112-127`; `kernel_plic.c:150-174`). The ratified PLIC priority rule resolves equal priorities by interrupt ID, with the lowest ID winning ([RISC-V PLIC priority specification](https://docs.riscv.org/reference/plic/plic-priority.html)); the claimed lower-ID level source therefore repeats until the code masks it, preventing the proposed alternating sequence under compliant selected hardware. Removed EK9029 from the detailed report and its coverage note. No hardware or IRQ was exercised. Source-only.

Exec signal-mask bit-31 caller recheck (EK8800 confirmed, 2026-10-17): traced `CreateMsgPort` through `AllocSignal(-1)` to `AllocTaskSignal`'s full 32-bit allocation mask and bit-number extraction (`rom/exec/createmsgport.c:50-68`; `rom/exec/allocsignal.c:70-123`), then verified `WaitPort` and `WaitIO` form masks with signed `1 << mp_SigBit` (`rom/exec/waitport.c:75-80`; `rom/exec/waitio.c:57-64`) while `Wait` consumes a `ULONG` mask (`rom/exec/wait.c:65-79`). Thus automatic allocation may return bit 31, which reaches the signed-shift case; the candidate's API-level scope and conditional consequence remain correctly stated. No signal exhaustion or wait was exercised. Source-only.

Native RISC-V invalid-stack recovery cross-architecture recheck (EK9027 retained, 2026-10-17): compared native RISC-V `core_Dispatch`'s invalid saved-SP branch with selected ARM and AArch64 scheduler implementations (`arch/riscv-native/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:198-250`; `arch/arm-native/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:328-359`; `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:293-326`). The native branch changes the selected `newtask` to `TS_WAIT`, but enqueues the function-entry `task` pointer; both ARM and AArch64 enqueue the rejected `newtask`. When a different selected task has invalid SP and the prior current task remains on TaskReady, the native branch inserts that node into TaskWait without unlinking it from its existing list. EK9027 is retained as a source-confirmed latent scheduler bug; native SiFive U boot's pre-scheduler stall remains an explicit reachability limitation. No task or scheduler was run. Source-only.

Console-handler support caller/state trace (2026-10-17; no new EK): followed `answer_read_request`, `HandlePendingReads`, `con_read`, and raw-input pumping through the selected handler's ACTION_READ, ACTION_WRITE, mode-switch, timer/close and device-completion branches (`rom/filesys/console_handler/support.c:1095-1192`; `con_handler.c:662-681,930-975,1060-1120`). Console reads request at most `CONSOLEBUFFER_SIZE` (256 bytes) in cooked mode and one byte in device mode (`con_handler.c:656-657`); `io_Actual` is therefore stored in signed-WORD `conbuffersize` within range, and the input/console buffers provide 258 bytes including terminators. Pending request packets are removed before reply, and `stopread` drains the pending list when a WAIT read is abandoned (`con_handler.c:694-713`). No state-bound or reply-ownership defect established in this caller slice. Device behavior beyond the requested I/O length and external handler clients remain outside this check. No console I/O was run. Source-only.

Console-handler stream-name allocation failure trace (EK9044 added, 2026-10-17): traced `BSTR2C`'s `AllocVec(len + 1)` failure return through `open_con` and `isdosdevicec`, then through the caller's open-packet reply path (`rom/filesys/console_handler/con_handler.c:140-163,554-559,743-760`). Console-handler open-constructor failure-path reconciliation (EK9044 distinct from EK702; 2026-10-17): rechecked the `open_con` setup and common cleanup around the stream-name conversion (`rom/filesys/console_handler/con_handler.c:140-163,535-640`). `BSTR2C` failure reaches the immediate `isdosdevicec(NULL)` dereference before the existing `close_con`/`FreeVec(filename)` unwind, so it is separate from EK702's unchecked timer port/request/device setup failures later in the same constructor (`:549-551`, detailed at Exec report EK702). `CONMain` replies to open only after `open_con` returns (`:743-760`), confirming the packet remains outstanding if the task faults. EK8800 WaitIO signal-mask recheck (2026-10-17): confirmed that `CreateMsgPort` accepts any successful `AllocSignal(-1)` result and stores it in `UBYTE mp_SigBit`; `AllocTaskSignal` can return bit 31 from its 32-bit free-mask scan (`rom/exec/createmsgport.c:54-65`; `allocsignal.c:70-103`). `WaitIO` passes signed-int `1 << mp_SigBit` to `Wait`, whose argument is `ULONG` (`rom/exec/waitio.c:57-64`; `exec.conf:126`). AArch64 CachePreDMA selected xHCI caller follow-up (EK8902 scope, 2026-10-17; no new EK): re-read the native AArch64 override and trace the selected `rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_schedule.c` caller into `xhciQueueData_IO` (`cachepredma.c:20-38`; `xhci_schedule.c:47-99,327-352`). `CachePreDMA` returns `KrnVirtualToPhysical(address)` without modifying `*length`; xHCI ignores the returned address and uses the original pointer and unchanged requested length for TRB construction; on 64-bit builds it only substitutes a `MEMF_31BIT` bounce buffer when a non-AC64 controller cannot address the original virtual range. This caller would require an identity/bus-address-compatible DMA mapping or explicit use of the translated address; however the selected AArch64 kernel source set has unresolved missing files (EK8902), and the current generic translator is identity, so the reviewed source does not establish a selected non-identity translation or an actual non-contiguous allocator result. debug.library ELF module unload cleanup recheck (EK9046 added, 2026-10-17): confirmed `RegisterModule_ELF` obtains separately allocated `.shstrtab` and `.strtab` copies via `getstrtab`, while the final-record path in `RemoveSegmentRange` frees `m_str` twice under distinct `if` guards and never frees `m_shstr` (`rom/debug/registermodule.c:184-194,378-393`; `rom/debug/unregistermodule.c:154-172`). `InternalUnLoadSeg` is the only checked DOS unload entry and calls `UnregisterModule` before releasing the segment chain (`rom/dos/internalunloadseg.c:57-63`); Exec `FreeVec` sends the allocation header to `FreeMem` and only treats NULL as a no-op (`rom/exec/freevec.c:53-66`). AArch64 HPET allocator/releaser ownership recheck (EK8761 retained, 2026-10-17; no new EK): read the complete `AllocCSUnit`, `FreeCSUnit`, and `GetCSUnitAttrsA` bodies and searched all maintained C call sites. `rom/kernel/registerclocksource.c:65` is the only in-tree allocator caller and no in-tree FreeCSUnit caller exists. External resource-client ownership and concurrency remain open. No resource call or allocation failure was induced. Source-only.
debug.library ELF registration and unload ownership follow-up (EK9046 added, 2026-10-17): re-read `RegisterModule_ELF`, `HandleModuleSegments`, and the selected DOS `InternalUnLoadSeg` call chain. debug.library ELF symbol-name bounds pass (EK9047 added, 2026-10-17): compared `RegisterModule_ELF`/`addsymbol`'s `st_name` use with the DOS ELF table-loading and relocation caller (`rom/debug/registermodule.c:199-205,450-478`; `rom/dos/internalloadseg_elf.c:1629-1652,478-540`). EK8799 detailed report/index reconciliation (2026-10-17): restored the detailed entry after re-reading `ReplyMsg`, `InternalPutMsg`, `CheckIO`, `WaitIO`, and `Remove`. WaitIO publication and shared-port removal findings independently rechecked (EK8799/EK8819 retained, 2026-10-17): reread the complete WaitIO/CheckIO/ReplyMsg/InternalPutMsg/GetMsg/Remove paths. EK8799 remains the state-before-enqueue window: ReplyMsg stores `NT_REPLYMSG` before the producer acquires the port spinlock and links the node; a consumer can observe this state and remove using retained pre-reply links. EK8819 is separate: after a reply node is linked, WaitIO's Remove still holds only local Disable while GetMsg/InternalPutMsg use the port spinlock, so its neighbor writes can race another message insertion/removal on the same shared reply port. The selected reset-callback timer path confirms EK8799 reachability, and the non-m68k audio.device four-channel AHI reply-port path confirms EK8819 reachability. No additional WaitIO state-transition defect established; no I/O or schedule was run. Source-only.

PC Signal queued-hook/task-removal caller recheck (EK832 retained with narrow caller qualification, 2026-10-17): re-read the selected affinity branch and removal path (`rom/exec/signal.c:170-247`; `remtask.c:97-128,165-181`) against the PC busy-IPI publication/drain (`arch/all-pc/kernel/kernel_ipi.c:92-105,149-160,195-209,230-279`). The queued hook contains the raw `Task *`; `RemTask` calls `CancelSignalIPIs` after marking the task terminal and before freeing its memory, but a repository search confirms `KERNEL_IPI_CALL_CANCELABLE` is not defined by the selected PC kernel, so the helper's conditional body is absent and cannot drain the queued hook. `SetTaskAffinity` permits an online CPU mask and selected PC SMP enables affinity, but a source census still finds no maintained production caller creating the exact affinity-pinned Signal plus concurrent privileged RemTask sequence. Retain the finding as a conditional public-API/direct privileged-caller case, not an ordinary workload claim. No IPI or task removal was run. Source-only.

Repository-wide search found no maintained caller of these pthread scheduling setters beyond their own definitions; the finding remains a public API contract issue. No pthread operation was run. Sam440/Efika direct `SuperState` contract recheck (EK9050 added, 2026-10-17): searched selected source for public `SuperState()` call pairs and read both PPC syscall handlers and privilege wrappers (`arch/ppc-sam440/kernel/syscall.c:87-90`; `arch/ppc-chrp/efika/kernel/syscall.c:38-41`; `arch/ppc-sam440/exec/superstate.c:17-30`; `arch/ppc-chrp/exec/superstate.c:17-30`). The kernel records the entering MSR in the syscall result before clearing `MSR_PR`; both C wrappers then ignore the result and return NULL. This conflicts with the generic public contract (`rom/exec/superstate.c:31-33,62-75`), which assigns NULL only to already-supervisor entry and tells the caller not to restore user mode for NULL. A direct client using the documented conditional restore can therefore remain privileged after the transition. In addition to the two EMAC pairs, PPC CHRP `PrepareContext` calls `SuperState()` then unconditional `UserState(NULL)` (`arch/ppc-chrp/exec/preparecontext.c:77,137`); it intentionally restores user mode while building a task context and does not establish the conditional-restore trigger. No selected in-tree caller following the documented conditional pattern was found; existing EK560 separately covers `Supervisor()`'s unconditional restore on already-privileged entry. Added EK9050 for the direct-API contract mismatch; trigger remains external. No mode transition was run. Source-only.

A direct client using the documented conditional restore can therefore remain privileged after the transition. In addition to the two EMAC pairs, PPC CHRP `PrepareContext` calls `SuperState()` then unconditional `UserState(NULL)` (`arch/ppc-chrp/exec/preparecontext.c:77,137`); it intentionally restores user mode while building a task context and does not establish the conditional-restore trigger. Exec public `RemTask` caller census continuation (2026-10-18): repeated a source-wide call search and reviewed all eight maintained network `DeleteUnit` call sites against their task construction and the common non-current teardown path. These workers are created with `AddUnitTask`/`NewAddTask`; on unit deletion each selected caller invokes `RemTask` only when `UNITF_TASKADDED` is set, then frees the externally allocated task stack and record. Constructor failure can leave an allocated but unpublished task when stack allocation or task initialization fails; the checked callers route this through their respective `DeleteUnit` cleanup. `FreeMem(NULL, STACK_SIZE)` is a defined no-op in selected Exec (`rom/exec/freemem.c:69-72`), so the unconditional stack-free form in Intel Pro/100 and Rhine does not add a NULL-free finding. This reconfirms the existing conditional EK473 remote-running-task lifetime concern for the caller family, but no independent caller defect was established. The source census found 39 textual matches across `rom`, `arch`, `compiler` and `workbench`, including comments, declarations and debug/test references; semantic filtering and caller-by-caller coverage outside the reviewed groups remain open. The worker has no library open reference and may already be in its tick body when the final caller closes. Cross-architecture `SuperState`/`UserState` override matrix (2026-10-18): re-read generic, m68k, ARM32, AArch64, PowerPC, and both RISC-V implementations and compared their return-token semantics with the public Exec contract. ARM32 always enters System mode and returns a non-NULL stack token, even when `KrnIsSuper()` would classify the caller's original exception mode as privileged; a paired `UserState` switches to User mode. Added conditional EK9052. Existing PPC EK9050 (public `SuperState` always returns NULL after a user-to-supervisor transition) and EK560 (`Supervisor` unconditionally restores an already-privileged caller to user mode) remain distinct consequences. AArch64's syscall and wrapper were checked for the same token/mode question: it returns the saved supervisor stack token and `UserState` restores the task mode; no additional mismatch was established for the selected task-mode entry. m68k checks the saved SR before returning a token and gives NULL for supervisor entry. RISC-V OpenSBI intentionally returns NULL and its common UserState is a no-op while all selected execution remains S-mode; riscv-native's zero token likewise has a no-op UserState. Full caller inventories, nested transitions, and runtime behavior remain open. Source-only.

EK799 FindTask snapshot-semantics and RTL8139 trigger recheck (2026-10-18; existing finding strengthened): verified that the defect does not depend solely on an unlocked no-list interval. `FindTask` scans Ready before Wait and does not rescan Ready; a concurrent task migration between those scans can leave the task absent from both observations even if it is already on the destination list (`rom/exec/findtask.c:64-99`). ARM32/AArch64 `Exec_ReschedTask` explicitly removes under the source lock, releases it, then sets state/enqueues under the destination lock (`arch/arm-native/exec/platform_init.c:189-203`; `arch/aarch64-native/exec/platform_init.c:157-170`). On x86, `X86_HandleReschedTask` holds the source-list lock while `X86_SetTaskState` enqueues on the destination, but this still cannot make `FindTask`'s earlier Ready scan part of the same snapshot; the ordinary switch-out path also uses separate running/ready list operations (`arch/all-pc/exec/platform_init.c:259-324`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:205-260`). Qualified the selected RTL8139 story: DeleteUnit synchronously calls Signal before entering its FindTask poll, so its initial Wait-to-Ready wake syscall has returned; the relevant direct consequence requires a later scheduler transition while the worker is still live in deinitialization/timer cleanup, not the wake call's own list mutation (`signal.c:353-385`; `unit.c:852-874,1153-1167`). This remains possible from the worker's live task state and the non-snapshot lookup, but no transition or teardown was run. Corrected the EK799 mechanism in the detailed report. Source-only.

Permit/Forbid selected caller follow-through (2026-10-18; no new EK): reviewed the full `rom/exec/permit.c` and paired `forbid.c` counter operations against two maintained direct caller paths. `aux_handler` enters a forbidden section before probing the startup message, balances `Permit` on its successful handoff before launching the handler, and balances it on the common failure return (`workbench/fs/aux_handler/aux_handler.c:115-175`); the success path intentionally does not fall through. `Avail` brackets the multi-pool availability snapshot with one `Forbid`/`Permit` pair (`workbench/c/Avail.c:195-220`). Exec PutMsg action-dispatch and callback-caller census (2026-10-18; no additional EK): reread the complete `PutMsg`/`InternalPutMsg`, `ReplyMsg`, `WaitPort`, and `FindPort` bodies. Message-list publication uses the port spinlock on SMP; PA_SIGNAL/PA_SOFTINT/PA_CALL action dispatch follows unlock. CreateMsgPort/DeleteMsgPort task-affinity disposition (2026-10-18; no EK): resolved the cross-task signal-release question by comparing the local contracts and implementations. `AllocSignal` explicitly allocates from the current task’s signal pool (`allocsignal.c:32-54,57-64`); `CreateMsgPort` calls it in the current task and stores that task in `mp_SigTask` (`createmsgport.c:54-65`); `FreeSignal` explicitly clears the current task’s allocation (`freesignal.c:32-39,50-58`). Therefore `DeleteMsgPort`’s same-task requirement follows from its paired task-owned signal resource, even though the DeleteMsgPort text does not repeat it. The selected create/delete paths inspected follow this ownership. Cross-task deletion is not counted as an Exec defect. Source-only.


AttemptSemaphore taskless-context boundary check (2026-10-18; no additional EK): compared `InternalAttemptSemaphore` with the explicit no-current-task returns in `InternalObtainSemaphore` and `ReleaseSemaphore` (`semaphores.c:50-72,164-184`; `releasesemaphore.c:59-70`). The public Attempt wrappers pass `GET_THIS_TASK` without an equivalent guard (`attemptsemaphore.c:53-56`; `attemptsemaphoreshared.c:52-55`). A taskless pre-init call could therefore reach `CheckSemaphore`/the counter update path, unlike the paired APIs. The direct in-tree caller census found no maintained pre-scheduler caller; ACPI and the other selected sites use runtime resource/device operations. Because normal semaphore use is task-context work and no supported selected pre-init trigger was established, this remains an external/initialization contract question, not a finding. No semaphore call was run without a current task.

Semaphore waiter/forced-removal caller recheck (EK8880, 2026-10-18): verified the public RemTask contract explicitly frees all memory in the removed task's `tc_MemEntry` list (`rom/exec/remtask.c:30-39,165-181`) and does not remove a pending `SemaphoreRequest` from another semaphore's wait list; the waiter node is stack-local (`rom/exec/semaphores.c:121-150`). A later ReleaseSemaphore traverses that list and reads the request before signaling its waiter (`rom/exec/releasesemaphore.c:136-178`). The selected root-only `security.library` `secKill` route directly calls RemTask for plain tasks (`rom/security/secKill.c:38-59`), but no in-tree caller of `secKill` was found, so the exact blocked-task trigger still requires an external root caller. EK8880 remains conditional; no new finding or runtime claim.

ObtainSemaphoreList forced-removal follow-up (EK8880 expanded, 2026-10-18): traced its distinct waiter representation: each contended semaphore queues its embedded `ss_MultipleLink` and stores the waiting task in `sr_Waiter` (`rom/exec/obtainsemaphorelist.c:87-100`). `RemTask` frees the task without walking semaphore wait queues; unlike ordinary ObtainSemaphore, this leaves the queue node allocated with the semaphore but retains a stale task pointer. `ReleaseSemaphore` later removes that node and signals its `sr_Waiter` (`rom/exec/releasesemaphore.c:136-178`). The same external forced-removal precondition and secKill caller limitation as the stack-node path apply. Expanded EK8880 to cover both wait APIs; no separate finding or runtime claim.

ExecSMP x86-64 Cause-to-ExitInterrupt delivery recheck (EK8935 retained, 2026-10-18): traced the selected PC interrupt-return gate in `arch/all-pc/kernel/cpu_intr.c` (`:532-541`) into `core_ExitInterrupt`, which tests the shared ExecBase `SFF_SoftInt` and invokes `core_Cause` (`rom/kernel/kernel_intr.c:30-34`). The Exec interrupt vector is called with interrupts enabled; `SoftIntDispatch` marks the dequeued node NT_INTERRUPT and releases the per-priority queue lock before executing it (`rom/exec/cause.c:164-188`). On non-Amiga PC `CUSTOM_CAUSE` is a no-op (`rom/exec/chipset.h:42-57`), and `Enable` routes pending softints through `KrnCause` when running outside supervisor mode (`rom/exec/enable.c:99-116`); the callback's own dispatcher also loops back after return. This does not serialize with another CPU returning from an unrelated user-mode interrupt and observing the same shared pending flag, so the existing EK8935 sequence remains viable. The x86-64 kernel selects shared `all-pc/kernel/cpu_intr.c` (`mmakefile.src:68`) and the platform uses the ExecSMP code paths; the report correctly leaves the HDAudio producer optional and conditional. No interrupt or callback was run. No new EK ID; other architecture delivery variants and runtime overlap remain untested.

The conditional trigger and recommendation to propagate initializer failure remain; no allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

PC APIC MSI allocator and selected PCI vector-API caller recheck (2026-10-18; no new EK): reread the complete `core_APIC_AllocMSI` reservation loop, PC `KrnAllocIRQ` dispatch, generic no-op `KrnFreeIRQ`, PC kernel manifest and both legacy MSI/MSI-X paths in `PCIPCDev__Hidd_PCIDevice__ObtainVectors` (`arch/all-pc/kernel/apic_msi.c:20-91`; `allocirq.c:14-33`; `rom/kernel/freeirq.c:48-66`; `arch/all-pc/hidds/pcipc/pcipc_deviceclass.c:369-562,564-644`). x86-64 early exception register-dump caller/stack-layout pass (EK9062 added, 2026-10-18): read all of `arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/kernel_early.c` and traced the only `core_InitEarlyIDT` call from `core_Kick` (`kernel_startup.c:194-212`) under `KERNEL_USE_EARLYTRAP` (`arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/mmakefile.src:26-30`). The interrupt/error/RIP/RFLAGS offsets themselves match the normalized no-error/error-code stub frames; the framebuffer formatting remains source-only and untested. No boot or exception was induced.

RISC-V task-context and scheduler-width selection pass (2026-10-18; no new EK): re-read the complete selected 64-bit `PrepareContext` body and traced its only direct Exec caller through `NewAddTask`/`NewCreateTaskA`: all eight LP64 argument registers are populated, failed `KrnCreateContext` is cleaned up through `CleanupETask`, and successful context frames are dispatched/freed by the OpenSBI 64-bit path (`arch/riscv64-all/exec/preparecontext.c:21-78`; `rom/exec/newaddtask.c:301-311`; `arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_cpu.c`; `rom/exec/remtask.c:112-124`). RISC-V64 OpenSBI trap-frame/scheduler offset reconciliation (2026-10-18; no new EK): compared the complete 272-byte frame emitted by `traps.S` with `struct ExceptionContext`, `RISCV_REGSAVE_CNT`, `copyContext`, and `cpu_Switch`/`cpu_Dispatch` (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/traps.S:28-81,91-168`; `arch/riscv64-all/include/aros/cpucontext.h:13-91`; `kernel_cpu.c:36-44,107-140,185-222`). The 29 saved x-register slots occur in the same order and at offsets 0..224; interrupted SP is reconstructed as frame+272 at offset 8; PC/status/flags/FPU/vector metadata align at 232/240/248/256/264. `copyContext` deliberately copies only x/PC/status so task-owned flags and extension-state pointers remain intact. The frame alignment and SIE/SPIE restore sequence were also checked; no additional GP-register or scalar frame-offset mismatch established. RISC-V64 OpenSBI boot-tag payload lifetime follow-up (2026-10-18; no new EK): traced `krnPrepareBootTags()`'s static `BootTags[16]` and `VBEModeInfo` storage through its `BootMsg` publication (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_startup.c:83,296,379-437,655-656`). The maximum set is 12 entries plus `TAG_DONE`, within the 16-item array. `KRN_FlattenedDeviceTree` and optional `KRN_CmdLine` borrow the firmware DTB; startup maps the DTB's 2 MiB region before the selected CPU and device consumers use it (`:688-705`; `arch/riscv64-opensbi/exec/cpu_init.c:162-176`; selected DWI2C, PCI-DT, DWUART and battclock initializers). `KRN_VBEModeInfo` points to static kernel storage, `KRN_EFISystemTable` to the UEFI-provided table, and `KRN_DebugInfo` is filled after package loading before Exec heap/header setup (`:826-843`). AArch64 KrnSpinInit caller and owner-field pass (2026-10-18; no new EK): read `KrnSpinInit`, `KrnSpinLock`, `KrnSpinTryLock`, `KrnSpinUnLock`, and `KrnSpinIsLocked`, then searched all AArch64-selected direct calls and the `EXEC_SPINLOCK_INIT` macro callsites. The initializer clears the lock word, which is the complete state used by the selected IsLocked and acquisition tests; the AArch64 code does not read `s_Owner` before a write acquisition, which sets it, and a write unlock clears it. The direct kernel caller initializes the BCM27xx startup lock before secondary release; the Exec macro invocations initialize task, base-list, port, memory-header, semaphore, and interrupt locks in their constructors before those objects are published to other CPUs. No uninitialized owner-field effect established. EK8900 is the distinct mismatch between `SPINLOCK_INIT_WRITE_LOCKED` and native ARM writer encoding, and no checked-in use of that initializer was found. External lock clients and lifetime of locks retained across object reset remain open. No lock or SMP startup was run. Source-only.

Raspberry Pi ARM32/AArch64 `KrnGetBootInfo` producer lifetime pass (2026-10-18; no new EK): traced boot-tag placement, payload relocation, and generic accessor use for both selected Raspberry Pi boot paths (`arch/arm-raspi/boot/boot.c:96,226-231,248,562-573,665-710`; `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/include/hardware/bcm2708_boot.h:12-36`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/boot.c:63,190-220,305-318,926-936,1024-1088`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/include/bcm2708_boot.h:14-53`; startup `arch/arm-native/kernel/kernel_startup.c:58-93,132-160,269-297`; `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/kernel_startup.c:61-88,142-183,333-362`). Linux processor HostLib caller and partial-load failure pass (2026-10-18; no new EK): followed the selected `arch/all-linux/processor/mmakefile.src` pair through `linuxcpu_hostlib_init`/`linuxcpu_hostlib_expunge` and `linuxcpu_hostlib_load_so` (`processor_hostlib.c:42-94`). A missing resource or failed library/symbol load leaves `linuxcpu_handle` NULL; the frequency wrapper checks that handle before calling `linuxcpu_getproccpufreq`, and the expunge hook closes only a successfully returned handle. A partial symbol table after a failed lookup is therefore not reached through that wrapper. Processor resource common-init and generated rollback caller trace (EK796 confirmed, 2026-10-18): compared `rom/processor/mmakefile.src`/`processor.conf` with the selected architecture-specific module manifests, generic `common_Init`, `GetCPUTopology`, and autoinit rollback (`init.c:17-55`; `gettopology.c:17-65`; `compiler/autoinit/functions.c:40-70`; `tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1156-1180`). If optional topology allocation itself fails, common init still succeeds with NULL; the API explicitly returns NULL and generic CPU info paths use topology-independent fallback values, as already recorded in the topology failure recheck. Pegasos PPC `BootMsg` relocation/lifetime recheck (2026-10-18): the selected `arch/ppc-chrp/pegasos/kernel/mmakefile.src` builds `kernel_startup.c` into the Pegasos kernel. On first entry, the code places `BootData` and a copied, explicitly terminated tag list immediately after the `KRN_KernelHighest` address, stores the copied list in global `BootMsg`, and sets the boot allocator cursor after that list (`kernel_startup.c:131-177`). The idle task executes `wfi` with task interrupt state enabled, then calls `Reschedule()` after normal trap return; the pending-switch flag is therefore serviced by the scheduler path rather than relying on the target's no-op `CUSTOM_CAUSE`. EFI32-to-x86-64 system-table ABI pass (EK9069 added, 2026-10-18): traced the PC Multiboot2 EFI tag parser and x86-64 resource selection into `efi_Init` and `EFI_FindConfigTable` (`arch/all-pc/bootstrap/multiboot2.c:113-117,183-211`; `arch/all-pc/bootstrap/mmakefile.src:4-12`; `arch/x86_64-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:60-72`; `arch/all-native/efi/efi_init.c:62-110`; `findconfigtable.c:62-84`; `compiler/include/hardware/efi/efi.h:18-34`; `compiler/include/aros/multiboot2.h:303-315`). The 64-bit parser accepts EFI32 when EFI64 is absent and publishes that pointer unchanged. The resource interprets it with native 8-byte pointers/IPTR; after the shared 24-byte table header, RuntimeServices is at offset 88 rather than EFI32 offset 56, and later count/config-table fields likewise shift. Added EK9069: the resource can dereference the wrong service pointer during initialization and ACPI/SMBIOS lookup can read the wrong table fields. This is conditional on an EFI32-only Multiboot2 handoff to the x86-64 build; no such firmware/bootloader run was performed. EFI64 takes precedence when both tags are present. Source-only.

EK600 report/index restoration and OpenLib rollback recheck (2026-10-18): the ledger previously said EK600 was detailed, but exact searches found no EK600 entry in the current detailed report or top-level index.
