`CopyMemQuick()` 64-bit size contract against TLSF realloc caller (2026-10-18; no new EK): checked the sole direct kernel allocator caller, `tlsf_realloc()`'s move path (`rom/kernel/tlsf.c:869-978`), against the generic implementation's `ULONG high` block counter (`rom/exec/copymemquick.c:48-82`) and TLSF mapping range (`tlsf.c:30-45,155-180,215-216`). On 64-bit TLSF, `MAX_FLI` limits a block below 2^37 bytes; the quick-copy loop can represent up to 2^37-4 bytes, and TLSF block alignment leaves its largest usable block below that limit. The selected allocator caller therefore does not exceed the helper's documented size limit. This was a targeted allocator-caller check, not a complete repository-wide `CopyMemQuick()` caller audit; the remaining direct-call contracts stay open. No large allocation or copy was run. Source-only.

`CopyMemQuick()` x86 scheduler-context callers (2026-10-22; no new EK): traced all direct calls in the i386 PC and x86-64 PC kernel scheduler context paths (`arch/i386-pc/kernel/kernel_cpu.c:48-68,74-99`; `arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/kernel_cpu.c:289-303`) against the API preconditions and `arch/i386-all/exec/cpu_init.c:29-36` SSE vector replacement. The copy sizes are field-offset/`offsetof` expressions ending before separately saved FPU/SSE state; each transfers between the live interrupt-stack frame and the task's ETask context, so the selected source/destination objects are distinct and the ULONG-multiple extents preserve their structure alignment. The x86-64 caller computes its extent from `regs->gs` and `sizeof(regs->gs)`, likewise an integral field extent. The SSE replacement retains the same public contract; scheduler ordering saves/restores the floating-point state outside the copied range. This closes only these two target caller paths; the generic repository-wide caller audit, other architecture callers and external callers remain open. No scheduler execution or target build was run; source-only.

Exec `Enqueue`/`AddBootNode` asynchronous caller timing recheck (2026-10-22; no new EK): searched every direct in-tree `AddBootNode()` caller, then traced the asynchronous USB mass-storage path from its spawned `nMSTask` (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/massstorage.class.c:656-663,1145-1174`) through media-change processing and `CheckPartitions()` (`:4032-4058`) to `AddBootNode()` (`partitions.c:273`). This establishes a real task-context writer that can be scheduled independently of DOSBoot, whose initialization counts `MountList` and opens its menu at `dosboot_init.c:218-235`; menu selection iterates under `Forbid()` only (`menu.c:668-681`), while `AddBootNode()`'s serialization includes `BootSemaphore` and `Forbid()` (`rom/expansion/addbootnode.c`). However, this source trace does not establish that the optional Poseidon mass-storage class is initialized early enough for its worker to overlap DOSBoot's one-time startup menu, nor that DOSBoot's menu is re-entered after startup. Therefore this remains a conditional timing question, not a confirmed corruption finding. The direct NVMe AddBootNode caller is reached from the module's one-time `NVME_Probe` (`nvme_init.c:272-334`) through storage bus setup; its scheduler context and relative module-init order were not established in this pass. No device, menu, or list was used; source-only.

TLSF realloc shrink boundary recheck (EK9080 added, 2026-10-18): corrected the earlier conclusion that the selected ROM-tag scanner's bounded shrink is safe merely because TLSF returns the same pointer. `tlsf_realloc()` creates a remainder header even when the old/new payload difference is exactly one rounded header, yielding a zero-sized free block. For a whole-block allocation ending at `area->end`, that remainder is the sentinel; `INSERT_FREE_BLOCK()` rejects it through `tlsf_block_in_area()` and enters the non-returning corruption path. `krnRomTagScanner()` supplies a selected `mhe_ReAlloc` caller and can request a shrink from the allocated size to the resident-array size. The exact size and final-block combination is conditional; no boot was run. The prior `rom/kernel/tlsf.c` row's statement that the scanner shrink is safe is superseded by EK9080. Source-only.

TLSF free-count consistency and Exec allocation prefilter pass (EK9081 added, 2026-10-18): compared every `mh_Free` write in `rom/kernel/tlsf.c` with TLSF's private `free_size` changes and the selected Exec managed allocation path. `tlsf_malloc()` copies the private count into `mh_Free`, but `tlsf_freevec()` and realloc shrink increase only the private count. `nommu_AllocMem()` rejects a header on `mh_Free < byteSize` before invoking the managed allocator; `nommu_AvailMem()` instead queries `mhe_Avail`, so it can expose the differing counts. The default PC boot selects TLSF unless `notlsf` is requested. This yields conditional allocation failure for requests larger than stale `mh_Free` but no larger than available free memory. The Radeon managed callbacks return NULL and VideoCore's allocator is separately tracked; neither is this TLSF path. No allocation was run. Source-only.

TLSF accounting caller-boundary check (2026-10-18): traced the other observed `mh_Free` size prefilter in `rom/kernel/kernel_mm.c` through `mm_Allocate()` to `GetBlockHeader()` (`rom/kernel/mm_linear.c:106-127`). TLSF headers keep `mh_First` NULL, so the page allocator rejects them as outside the page-bitmap allocator; it does not consume TLSF free space through that route. This keeps EK9081's demonstrated false-negative consequence on Exec's managed `nommu_AllocMem()` path. Rechecked `mhe_ReAlloc` providers: TLSF is the only implementation that changes an allocation in place; Radeon and VideoCore return NULL and are not reachable for the boot scanner's selected system-memory header. No additional caller defect established. Source-only.

Exec allocator filter follow-up (EK9081, 2026-10-18): traced the central `nommu_AllocMem()` rejection test from the MemList walk to the managed callback and checked the paired free route. Kernel IRQ identity/layout and removal-caller pass (2026-10-18; EK09 rechecked, no new EK): checked `kernel_irqtypes.h` widths against `KernelBase.kb_Interrupts`, generic `KrnAddIRQHandler`/`KrnRemIRQHandler`, kernel initialization and the PC `HW_IRQ_COUNT` variants. CopyMemQuick 64-bit counter-limit correction and report restoration (EK8990, 2026-10-18): corrected the earlier 16-GiB threshold to 128 GiB after recalculating the actual loop: `size` is divided by four, then `high = size / 8` is stored in 32-bit `ULONG`; the unrolled loop copies eight ULONGs per iteration (`rom/exec/copymemquick.c:53-88`). At exactly 2^37 bytes, `high` truncates from 2^32 to zero and `low` is zero, so nothing is copied; sizes beyond that wrap to the modulo-128-GiB remainder. Added the missing detailed EK8990 section and repaired the index anchor. Rechecked that selected 64-bit TLSF's maximum block is below 2^37; no selected allocator call reaches this trigger. The broader direct-caller size audit remains open. No large buffer or copy was used. Source-only.

Exec WaitPort SMP signal/list recheck (2026-10-18; no new EK): reread the full implementation and enumerated direct C callsites (`rom/exec/waitport.c:52-104`; repository search across `rom`, `workbench`, and `arch`). On ExecSMP it checks list emptiness under the port read spinlock with local interrupts disabled, releases both before `Wait()`, and reacquires/rechecks after every wake, so a message arriving between the empty check and `Wait()` leaves a pending signal and does not establish a lost wake. The returned message pointer is read after releasing the lock; no selected shared-port competing consumer was established in the sampled request/reply and process ports, so no race finding is promoted without such a caller. Multiple consumers sharing one port and caller/port destruction overlap remain open contracts. No port or task was run; source-only.

Exec single-semaphore queue-count boundary trace (EK9071 added, 2026-10-18): traced the signed `WORD ss_QueueCount` from InitSemaphore’s -1 sentinel through the owner and 32,769 exclusive `InternalObtainSemaphore()` callers (`compiler/include/exec/semaphores.h:50-58`; `rom/exec/initsemaphore.c:56-64`; `semaphores.c:87-97,114-150`). The 16-bit value is -32767 after those waiters; owner release decrements it to -32768, fails `ss_QueueCount >= 0`, and resets owner/count without unlinking or signalling any `ss_WaitQueue` node (`rom/exec/releasesemaphore.c:83-113,186-196`). Added EK9071, separate from EK8781’s `ObtainSemaphoreList.failedObtain` narrowing and list-wide return-without-wait defect. No task fan-out or contention was run; source-only.

POSIX flock lookup/removal lifetime pass (EK9075 added, 2026-10-18): rechecked `FindSemaphore()` pointer return under its list spinlock against `RemSemaphore()` unlink semantics and the selected path-named semaphore lifecycle in `compiler/crt/posixc/flock.c`. `LOCK_UN` may release and free an unowned, unqueued named semaphore while a remote task retains a lookup result but has not yet called `ObtainSemaphore`; Exec documents that `Forbid` is CPU-local on ExecSMP. Reset callback walker race recheck (EK59, 2026-10-18): re-read `Exec_DoResetCallbacks`, `ForeachNodeSafe`, `AddResetCallback` and `RemResetCallback` together (`rom/exec/doresetcallbacks.c:115-183`; `compiler/include/exec/lists.h:203-208`; `addresetcallback.c:56-61`; `remresetcallback.c:46-49`). The loop captures `tmp = current->ln_Succ` before running each handler; in the non-supervisor path it waits for a support task or timer while callback-list mutation remains enabled, and `RemResetCallback` unlinks that node without a shared lock. If an ordinary teardown removes and frees the saved successor during the wait, the loop advances through stale `tmp`. The selected Linux framebuffer last-display removal is one in-tree disposer that unlinks and frees a callback object (see `../AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`, row for arch/all-linux/hidd/linuxfb/linuxfbgfx_hiddclass.c; implementation at `linuxfbgfx_hiddclass.c:149-158`); generic removal `rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c:287-295`. x86-64 `KrnMapGlobal` caller/selection recheck (EK8887–EK8889, 2026-10-18; no new finding): confirmed the kernel target includes `mapglobal` (`arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/mmakefile.src:48-50`) and the x86-64 boot package selects `pcipc`, ATA PCI, AHCI, NVMe and VESAGfx (`arch/x86_64-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:66-68`). VMM paging-priority caller recheck (EK9076 added, 2026-10-18): traced `adjust_priority()` from its sole startup call after PageHandler and PrePager launch. It is skipped for PD_FILE and uses the named paging-device task for partition-backed modes. The active Workbench:System edges select the VMM app and handler (`workbench/system/VMM/MUI/mmakefile.src:18-21`; `workbench/system/VMM/mmakefile.src:47-52`); keep the candidate conditional on running VMM with the stated paging mode and caller priority. Standard allocator large-size index recheck (EK9077 added, 2026-10-18): reread all 1,408 lines of `rom/exec/memory.c` in full, including allocator-context creation, index maintenance, plain allocation/free, managed-header dispatch, pool growth, pool free and memory-handler iteration. Traced `nommu_AllocMem` through `mhac_GetSysCtx` into `stdAlloc`; a sufficiently large plain header gets an index context, and requests from 2 GiB through below 4 GiB narrow to negative signed `LONG` in `mhac_CalcIndex`. On AROS GCC the signed shift loop can remain at -1 while `mh_SpinLock` (ExecSMP) and the shared MemList lock are held. x86-64 PC has an explicit `notlsf` standard allocator option and an 8-GiB high-memory region, although actual RAM and a near-limit caller are not established. Added EK9077 with those conditions; existing EK783 covers the separate size-addition wrap. No large allocation or runtime path was exercised. Source-only.

Standard allocator large-size candidate recheck (EK9077 retained, 2026-10-22): re-read `mhac_CalcIndex`, its only standard-allocation call path, and the context setup invariant (`rom/exec/memory.c:197-217,232-288,354-378,527-590`; `memory_nommu.c:20-83`). `stdAlloc` receives pointer-width `IPTR size`; it checks total free bytes and then calls `mhac_GetBetterPrevMemChunk`, whose signed `LONG` parameter remains the narrowing point. A context can only be allocated from a sufficiently large header; the index-sizing calculation therefore yields a nonzero index count on that path, so the separate zero-index concern is not established. x86-64 `notlsf` still selects standard headers, and GCC's sign-preserving right shift of negative `LONG` leaves -1 fixed, so the loop is nonterminating for 2–4 GiB requests. The plain path holds the MemHeader spinlock on ExecSMP, while the selected `nommu_AllocMem` path retains the shared MemList lock around the call. The public `AllocMem`/`AllocVec` interface can receive such a request, but this recheck did not identify a maintained in-tree caller issuing a near-limit allocation or establish that firmware supplies enough contiguous free bytes in the affected header. EK9077 remains conditional with those occurrence limits; no memory was allocated and no runtime behavior was induced. Source-only.

TLSF free-accounting/pre-filter recheck (EK9081 retained, 2026-10-22): reconciled every assignment to `mh_Free` in `rom/kernel/tlsf.c` with the free, realloc-shrink, and ordinary Exec allocation paths (`tlsf.c:590-603,810-914,1318-1355`; `rom/exec/memory_nommu.c:23-83`). Successful `tlsf_malloc()` is the only post-initialization operation that copies `tlsf->free_size` back to `mh_Free`; both `tlsf_freevec()` and the shrink branch of `tlsf_realloc()` increase only the private count. The Exec prefilter runs before the serialized `mhe_Alloc` callback and skips a header whose stale `mh_Free` is smaller than the request. Thus a failed prefilter cannot self-refresh; it persists until some smaller successful allocation reaches TLSF. `AvailMem()` reads `mhe_Avail()` and can report the larger private count meanwhile. The existing EK9081 consequence and trigger remain accurate; default PC TLSF selection was rechecked in both i386/x86-64 startup paths. No allocation or free was run; no new line credit. Source-only.

Both GetCPUInfo paths clamp an invalid selected logical index to zero, and the platform getters independently validate the index against APIC CPU count or FDT hart count (`arch/all-pc/processor/getcpuinfo.c:34-38`; `arch/riscv64-all/processor/getcpuinfo.c:30-34`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/getcpuattr.c:58-64`; `arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/getcpuattr.c:20-24,37-39`). The generic `rom/kernel/getcpuattr.c` returns the documented unsupported value `-1`. No distinct defect was established in this API/caller slice; EK9083 remains the producer-side PC fixed-baseline/sample-interval mismatch, and EK597 remains the zero-performance-ratio frequency case. ARM/AArch64 legacy CPU-load long-gap recheck (EK9085 added, 2026-10-18): traced the `ULONG` casts and modulo subtractions in both `KrnGetSystemAttr` overrides to their microsecond clock and idle-accounting producers. The 100-ms minimum-window check uses the wrapped elapsed value and does not detect a gap beyond `2^32` microseconds. A `2^32+500,000`-us sample with `2^32+250,000` us idle therefore calculates 50% load for about 0.006% actual busy time. ARM exposes the path through `processor.resource`/SysMon; no checked-in AArch64 CPU-load caller was found, so the latter remains public-API conditional. Distinct from EK8843's concurrent baseline race. No timer, query, or hardware behavior was induced. Source-only.

PC APIC MSI selected-caller serialization boundary (EK325 follow-up, 2026-10-18): rechecked direct PC `ObtainVectors` callers and the PCI enumeration lock after including the xHCI package variants in the caller search. The PC-specific direct consumers are AHCI (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci_aros.c:115-123`) and NVMe (`rom/devs/nvme/nvme_busclass.c:324-344`); pcixhci is selected by Raspberry Pi/OpenSBI packages, not the checked PC boot manifests (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:217`; `arch/riscv64-opensbi/boot/mmakefile.src:104`). The PCI enumerator uses `ObtainSemaphoreShared` around callback traversal, so concurrent enumerations are not mutually exclusive (`rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:422-448`). NVMe surrounds its own ObtainVectors call with `Disable()`, which does not serialize a second CPU's call; AHCI has no matching allocator lock (`nvme_busclass.c:329-344`; `ahci_aros.c:115-123`). These paths do not establish a concrete overlapping selected boot schedule, so EK325 remains conditional on concurrent API requests on PC ExecSMP; its shared-cursor race and affected-call mechanism are confirmed, but runtime reachability remains unverified. No IRQ or PCI device was exercised; source-only.

OpenSBI RISC-V software-interrupt delivery trace (2026-10-18; no new finding): followed `Cause()` from `rom/exec/cause.c` through `Enable()` and `KrnCause()` into the selected OpenSBI syscall mechanism. OpenSBI's `kernel_cpu.h` uses `ebreak` because S-mode `ecall` enters SBI; `kernel_traps.c` recognizes the scheduler syscall, steps over the breakpoint, and calls `core_SysCall(SC_CAUSE)`. `core_ExitInterrupt()` checks `SFF_SoftInt` and `core_Cause()` invokes the Exec `IntVector`; `exec_init.c` installs `SoftIntDispatch` at `INTB_SOFTINT`. Timer and external interrupt exits also pass through `core_ExitInterrupt()`. The explicit idle path checks the pending flag after `wfi`. No mismatch was established for these paths. OpenSBI SSI/IPI behavior, nested-trap races, other RISC-V configurations, and other architecture-specific delivery paths remain open. No build, trap, or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only.

POSIXC descriptor growth and owner-table race reconciliation (2026-10-19; EK8994-EK8996/EK8995 retained, no new EK): reread the complete `__fdesc.c` slot/owner path and checked fd.library `FD_Reserve()` implementation against the pipe/opendir callers (`compiler/crt/posixc/__fdesc.c:116-301,378-391,692-776`; `compiler/crt/posixc/pipe.c:96-123`; `compiler/crt/posixc/opendir.c`; `workbench/libs/fd/fd_alloc.c:125-195`). `FD_LOCK` protects local table growth and `FD_Reserve` serializes global reservations, but `__getfirstfd`, reservation, and `__setfdesc` do not share one critical section. For pthread workers, `fd_owner` routes both local tables to the creator’s descriptor array; the separate same-owner skip intended for vfork inheritance does not close the interleaving. This reconfirms EK8995 for pipe/opendir and EK8994/EK8996 for failure paths; no duplicate entry added. `open()` and `close()` still document threaded use as unsupported, so their analogous callers are not used to widen the finding. No allocation failure, descriptor operation, or thread was run. Source-only.

RemDevice direct-call census and Bluetooth class expunge caller recheck (2026-10-19; EK9099 retained, no new Exec ID): reran an exact C/header/assembly search for `RemDevice(` and excluded the API comment/declaration matches, yielding 21 direct executable call sites: 17 USB class expunges, two Bluetooth class expunges, the selected per-unit `printer.device` rollback, and LDDemon's memory-handler sweep. Read both Bluetooth expunge paths (`rom/bluetooth/classes/btserial/btserial.class.c:79-112`; `btpan/btpan.class.c:74-116`) and traced btserial's selected device open/expunge vectors (`rom/bluetooth/classes/btserial/dev.c:43-137,180-210`). The class expunge can reduce its reserved device-base open count to zero and call `RemDevice`; `OpenDevice` releases DeviceList's read lock before entering `devOpen`, and `devOpen` first dereferences/increments that base's `lib_OpenCnt`, while `RemDevice` protects the expunge only with local `Forbid`. On SMP another CPU can therefore expunge/free the base in the lookup-to-open-vector gap, preserving EK9099's conditional stale-base race. No separate Bluetooth issue is promoted. The direct-call census does not cover generated vectors, indirect callbacks or external device clients; all 17 USB class callers are not individually re-audited in this pass. No overlap was run; source-only.

ExecSMP dynamic USB-device open/expunge caller audit (EK9099 added, 2026-10-19): individually enumerated all 17 USB-class C `RemDevice()` call sites and paired each with that class's `dev.c` open-count and final-expunge logic: asixeth, bluetooth, cdcacm, cdceth, davicometh, ethwrap, lan78xx, massstorage, moschipeth, palmpda, pegasuseth, printer, rawwrap, rndis, serialcp210x, serialpl2303 and stir4200. Each class expunge calls `RemDevice()` after reducing the reserved device-base count; each paired `devOpen()` increments `lib_OpenCnt` only after entry, while `devExpunge()` removes and frees the base at zero. Cross-checked the generic `OpenDevice()` list-read-lock release before vector dispatch with `RemDevice()`'s Forbid-only wrapper and `forbid.c`'s processor-local ExecSMP contract (`rom/exec/opendevice.c:92-114,130-135`; `remdevice.c:65-81`; `forbid.c:52-61`). The race is therefore retained as EK9099, conditional on overlapping open and expunge on separate CPUs. The same property is present in both direct Bluetooth class expunges and was separately traced through the btserial open vector. Historical provisional references in this ledger had no matching current report/index entry; they have been reconciled to the detailed EK9099. These checks cover the direct in-tree USB/Bluetooth callers, not generated registrations or external device users. No overlap was run; source-only.

PC concurrent Signal reschedule/list-lock finding reconciliation (EK9018, 2026-10-19): promoted the existing candidate to the detailed report and top-level index after rechecking `Signal`'s task-lock release and syscall handoff (`rom/exec/signal.c:350-372`), state-based list-lock selection and stale-state path (`arch/all-pc/exec/platform_init.c:269-326`), `X86_SetTaskState`'s optional destination-list lock (`:207-253`), and unrestricted affinity acceptance (`arch/all-pc/kernel/apic.c:137-155`). Two handlers can select `TaskWaitSpinLock` while the task is `TS_WAIT`; after one moves the task to `TaskReady`, the other can remove/re-enqueue its node with `dolock == FALSE`, mutating the ready list under the wrong lock. Scope remains x86-64 PC ExecSMP; no concurrent scheduling was run. This reconciles a report/index omission and does not claim a fresh whole-file line credit.
VMM page-file request-order caller trace (2026-10-19; no new EK): followed `ReadPage`/`WritePage` into `ReadSinglePage`/`WriteSinglePage`, `HandleReturn`, and the sole `PageHandler` caller (`workbench/system/VMM/cache.c:72-123`; `workbench/system/VMM/fault.c:845-879`; `pagehandler.c:581-610`). Although multiple page faults can have I/O outstanding, the single PageHandler task emits each seek followed immediately by its matching transfer to the same `DeviceProc` port, and each request pair carries a `TrapInfo` backpointer until the transfer reply is consumed; `WriteMultiplePages` uses one synchronous request at a time. For the AROS build, `InitPrePager()` does not install `PktWaitPatch` because that patch is under `#if !defined(__AROS__)` (`workbench/system/VMM/prepager.c:343-348`), so the non-AROS path that diverts a file transfer after its seek is not selected. The AROS `PageHandler` is the sole in-tree sender to this page-file `DeviceProc`; its sequential seek/transfer sends therefore do not establish an AROS file-offset interleaving, and no EK is added. For a system reset, PageHandler separately waits for `PageFaultsInProgress == 0` before allowing reset; ordinary shutdown ordering is not established by this trace. This closes the selected PageHandler ordering question only; DOS handler failure semantics, other packet producers, filesystem-specific completion behavior, failed-OpenDevice ownership and remaining cleanup branches stay open. No paging I/O or fault was run. Source-only.

WaitPort raw-dequeue caller census (EK276 rechecked; no new EK, 2026-10-19): searched all 224 C/header `WaitPort(` matches in `rom`, `workbench`, `arch` and `compiler`, then traced the selected callers that remove `WaitPort()`'s returned node directly or compare the returned head with a specific message. The NList, NListtree, TextEditor and BetterString clipboard RPCs serialize each static reply-port transaction with their shared `serverLock`; each server processes and replies to one request at a time, while startup/shutdown use the port only in their init/expunge handshakes. `workbench/libs/asyncio/src/WaitPacket.c` documents and maintains one packet outstanding on its private port before raw `Remove`. The FKey and `rexxc` clients each use a private port for one submitted RexxMsg, wait until that message is the head, then immediately free the message and delete the port; no selected second producer/consumer on those ports was found. These checked patterns do not establish the concurrent-consumer trigger for EK276; its public shared-port borrowed-head interval remains conditional. The 224 matches are an inventory, not a full caller audit; all other WaitPort clients and external multi-consumer contracts remain open. No port or message was used. Source-only.

OpenDevice/RemDevice cross-side lifetime recheck (EK9099 retained, 2026-10-19): reread the full generic lookup/dispatch and expunge wrappers (`rom/exec/opendevice.c:92-135`; `rom/exec/remdevice.c:65-81`) and the Bluetooth serial and PAN expunge/open paths (`rom/bluetooth/classes/btserial/btserial.class.c:79-112`; `btserial/dev.c:43-137,180-210`; `btpan.class.c:81-104`; `btpan/dev.c:60-63,226-244`). Both class variants drop the reserved device-base reference before `RemDevice`; their `devOpen` increments the count only after OpenDevice dispatch begins, and `devExpunge` frees the base at zero. The Bluetooth class parent build edges are optional (`rom/bluetooth/classes/mmakefile.src:10-13`; `btpan/mmakefile.src:8-12`). `OpenDevice` releases the `DeviceList` read lock before entering `devOpen`; the selected `devOpen` increments `lib_OpenCnt` only after entry. `RemDevice` invokes expunge under `Forbid`, which is local-processor-only on ExecSMP, and the class expunge can drop its reserved reference before the zero-open device expunge removes/frees the base. The interleaving and lifetime consequence are therefore as stated in EK9099; this pass adds the optional Bluetooth PAN class path to the exact caller evidence, without adding a separate Exec finding or claiming a concurrency reproduction. Source-only.

Permit nesting follow-up for USB Audio caller OD3229 (2026-10-19): reread `Permit`, `Reschedule`, `Wait`, and task initialization (`rom/exec/permit.c:80-100`; `reschedule.c:74-90`; `wait.c:83-127`; `newaddtask.c:234-236`). `Permit` decrements the signed task-disable count; the selected Poseidon class scan reaches its Forbid/Permit pair only after the USB class callback, so the unmatched call leaves a one-count offset. `Wait` stores that value in `tc_TDNestCnt`, sets the live counter to -1 during the blocked interval, and restores the saved value on wake, so it does not correct the caller imbalance. Ordinary balanced Forbid/Permit pairs preserve it. After 128 accumulated unmatched decrements, the byte wraps to a positive value and blocks task switching for that task until a subsequent offset-changing call. This sharpens the Exec-side cross-subsystem account in Other Drivers OD3229; it does not add an Exec vector finding. EK8827 remains the opposite-direction nested-Forbid overflow. Wider direct-caller sequencing remains open; no nesting or scheduler behavior was run. Source-only.


Exec semaphore counter-wrap trigger refinement (EK9071, 2026-10-19): recalculated `ss_QueueCount` and `ss_NestCount` from `InitSemaphore()` through recursive `InternalObtainSemaphore()` calls and the competing-owner/release branches (`rom/exec/initsemaphore.c:56-64`; `semaphores.c:87-112`; `releasesemaphore.c:80-113,186-196`). 65,536 acquisitions by one exclusive owner produce `ss_QueueCount == -1` and `ss_NestCount == 0` while retaining that owner pointer; a competing obtain increments the queue count to zero and unconditionally replaces the owner. This needs two tasks but no large fan-out. Retained the separate 32,769-waiter branch, where the release-side signed count test bypasses all queued requests. Added the lower-resource trigger and its ownership consequence to EK9071 and synchronized the index. Narrowing to signed WORD is target-dependent per C, so the finding explicitly scopes the wrap to two's-complement targets. No source code was changed and no semaphore call or contention was run; source-only.


Exec Procure/Vacate cross-check for EK9071 (2026-10-19): traced the same signed semaphore counters through `Procure` immediate grants, queued-message publication, and `Vacate` cancellation or post-grant release (`rom/exec/procure.c:61-109`; `vacate.c:54-94`). Same-owner Procure increments the nesting and queue counters and immediately replies, so 65,536 recursive bids reproduce the false-free sentinel collision without using `ObtainSemaphore`. When another owner holds the lock, one bidding task can queue 32,769 retained message structs; the later `ReleaseSemaphore` branch can fail its signed nonnegative test and leave them unreplied. `Vacate` only decrements the counter when it removes a still-queued message; after grant, its `ReleaseSemaphore` call does not repair a wrapped count. Updated EK9071 and the Procure/Vacate coverage rows. No message, semaphore, or concurrency was run; source-only.

Native RISC-V Exec platform override full-body and selected scheduler check (2026-10-19; EK9027 retained, no new finding): re-read all 229 physical lines of `arch/riscv-native/exec/exec_platform.h` (208 code lines by `cloc 2.06`) against the complete `tls_t` layout/access macros (`arch/riscv-native/kernel/tls.h:4-48`) and scheduler consumers. POSIX descriptor-table large-target arithmetic pass (EK9120 added, 2026-10-19; no new line credit): traced `dup2(newfd)` through `__getfdslot()` and the later descriptor lookup (`compiler/crt/posixc/dup2.c:116-131`; `__fdesc.c:116-144,239-298,611-688`). On a 32-bit target, `newfd = 0x40000000` wraps `(wanted_fd + 1) * sizeof(fdesc *)` to four bytes, while the table already contains three standard-stream entries; `FD_SLOTS` is then set to over one billion before the global descriptor reservation is attempted. A failed `FD_Reserve()` returns without restoring the old array or slot count, and a later lookup trusts that count before the fd.library ownership check. Added EK9120 with allocator-rounding qualification for immediate copy overrun; logical allocation/count mismatch is source-proven. No call, allocation, or build was run. Source-only.

Console-handler pending-read completion cross-check (2026-10-19; no new EK): traced `con_read()` through `HandlePendingReads()` and `answer_read_request()` (`rom/filesys/console_handler/support.c:1095-1191`) against the selected handler's input-event/EOF dispatch (`con_handler.c:1040-1091`). Copy lengths are bounded by both available input and the request length; a completed request is removed before reply, and EOF is consumed one waiting read at a time. No independent queue-removal, copy-size, or EOF defect was established in this slice. Existing EK710 covers the selected EOF behavior with multiple queued reads; broader DOS stream semantics, external packet callers, and handler shutdown races remain open. No read request or console event was sent. Source-only.


realtime.library final-close/worker ordering cross-check (EK9051 retained; 2026-10-19): re-read `AllocTimer()`/`FreeTimer()` alongside `Pulse()` and generated library expunge output. `CreateNewProc()` publishes the worker before `AddIntServer()` installs the VBlank signaler; final expunge removes the interrupt and signals CTRL-C, but `Pulse()` checks CTRL-C only after its blocking `Wait()` returns. If the task is already processing a tick, it continues accessing `RealTimeBase` and executing library code while generated expunge proceeds to `__freebase()` and returns the segment list (`tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1569-1587`). This confirms the existing EK9051 worker/base lifetime candidate; it does not establish that every close interleaves with an active tick. `FreeTimer()` has no completion wait or task join, and no separate partial-init defect was found in the reviewed timer setup path. No close, interrupt, or task interleaving was run; source-only.

Realtime Pulse worker/expunge lifetime recheck (EK9051 formalized; 2026-10-19): followed the task's `tc_UserData` base pointer through its tick loop and CTRL-C check, then traced `FreeTimer` and generated library expunge. The stop check occurs only after `Wait`; `FreeTimer` signals without joining; the hook returns and generated code frees the base and returns the library segment. Exec AddHead selected-caller audit (2026-10-19; no new EK): searched maintained C callers under `rom/exec` and traced each `AddHead` invocation. Bootstrap-task memory-list insertion occurs before multitasking setup (`exec_init.c:196`); NewCreateTask builds its private memory list before NewAddTask publishes the task (`newcreatetaska.c:251`); MungWall's allocation-list insertion is protected by its SMP spinlock (`mungwall.c:65-75`); ETask child-list insertion is protected by the parent ETask spinlock on ExecSMP (`exec_util.c:215-231`). M68k Amiga KrnGetBootInfo warm-reset and NULL-consumer recheck (2026-10-19; no new EK): traced ColdReboot through the ROM reset vector to the next exec_boot publication, then checked the selected MMU and Exec tag-list consumers against LibGetTagData/LibFindTagItem/LibNextTagItem. Normal startup publishes a copied public tag array after the temporary stack is abandoned; AROSBootstrap supplies tags and command-line storage in its retained BootMemHeader. On tag-array allocation failure, BootMsg becomes NULL, LibNextTagItem returns NULL safely, and the alert formatter also tests the accessor result. Optional x86-64 trapdebug caller/context recheck (EK8923 retained; stale EK251 reference removed, 2026-10-19): re-read `kernel_trapdebug.c` in full (345 lines), the `KERNEL_USE_TRAPDEBUG` conditional target selection (`arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/mmakefile.src:7,42-45`), and its only installer (`platform_init.c:247`). Checked all 18 `KrnAddExceptionHandler` registrations against `krnAddExceptionHandler()` allocation/return behavior (`rom/kernel/addexceptionhandler.c:97-127`); registration failure can omit optional diagnostic handlers, but no core operation depends on them, so no separate finding was added. Traced the handler’s FPU dump conditions through `ExceptionContext` (`arch/x86_64-all/include/aros/cpucontext.h:47-86`) and x86-64 exception-entry assembly (`core_interrupts.s:139-151`): exception frames carry `ECF_SEGMENTS`, not the saved-FPU flags, so the FPU diagnostic takes its safe “no FPU/SSE context” path rather than dereferencing those union pointers. EK8923 remains the concrete #UD diagnostic fault. Repository-wide report/index check found no current EK251 entry, so removed the stale reference from both file inventories. No optional build or trap was run; source-only.
PC SMP ready-lock allocation alignment recheck (EK8831 retained; 2026-10-19): re-evaluated `smp_Initialize()`'s post-`AllocMem` alignment expression (`arch/all-pc/kernel/smp.c:342-360`). On NULL, `(0 + 127) & ~127` remains NULL, so the alignment step does not convert allocation failure into a non-NULL low pointer; the logged failure branch is reachable. This does not weaken EK8831: `smp_Wake()` independently allocates `apicReadyLocks` and uses its result without alignment or a NULL check (`smp.c:228-245`). The ready-lock failure still reaches `KrnSpinLock()` before AP launch (`:266-280`). No allocation failure or boot was induced; no line credit.

OOP hash constructor/selected class-creation recheck (GD1221 cross-ledger, no new EK, 2026-10-19): repeated a fixed-string search for every in-tree `NewHash()` call, excluding the unselected `rom/oop/unused` prototypes, and traced both live callsites (`rom/oop/oop_init.c:60`; `rom/oop/metaclass.c:162-180`). `OOPInit` uses `HT_STRING` for the global IID map; the selected `IFMeta::allocdisptabs()` uses `HT_INTEGER`, but `calc_ht_entries()` includes the superclass interface count before adding only new interfaces (`metaclass.c:601-652`), and the selected BaseMeta parent supplies at least root and meta interfaces (`basemetaclass.c:738-746`). Thus the `CalcHashULONG()` zero divisor at `HashMask==0` is not reached by these checked class constructors. Confirmed the distinct GD1221 path remains: `NewHash()` tests the table-structure pointer rather than `ht->Table` after bucket-array allocation (`hash.c:70-103`), and OOP initialization can subsequently pass that non-NULL table object into ID insertion/lookup (`oop_init.c:60-80`). No additional OOP hash finding established; class-construction caller census remains bounded to selected in-tree callsites, with external private-header use and allocation failure untested. No line credit.


ARM/AArch64 idle-task name allocation recheck (EK805 detailed, 2026-10-19): compared both native `Exec_ARMCPUInit` bodies, their `ADD2INITLIB` priority-0 registration, and the common `Exec_Init` INITLIB invocation. In the ExecSMP branch, every reported CPU enters the loop; `AllocVec(15)` is immediately passed to `sprintf` with no null check. The Raspberry Pi `smp` configure branch defines `__AROSEXEC_SMP__`. Restored EK805 as a detailed finding and indexed it. No allocation failure or boot was induced; source lines were already body-reviewed, so no line credit added.


ARM/AArch64 idle-task name ownership pass (EK806 detailed, 2026-10-19): traced the allocated name through `NewCreateTaskA` success and failure. It copies into the name slot in the task `MemList`; later `NewAddTask` failure causes `FreeEntry(ml)` to release only that task-owned copy, and neither architecture caller releases the original `AllocVec` allocation. The leak is therefore present whenever the 15-byte allocation succeeds, regardless of task-creation outcome. Added detailed EK806 and its master-index entry. No task creation or memory accounting was run; no line credit because the source bodies were already reviewed.


Realtime player constructor/setter caller census (2026-10-19; existing findings retained): searched all C/assembly sources for `CreatePlayerA`, `CreatePlayer(` and `SetPlayerAttrsA`. Direct maintained callers are `DT_InitPlayer()` in Animation, the internal `CreatePlayerA()` -> `SetPlayerAttrsA()` call, and `developer/demos/realtdemo.c`; the demo checks the player result before use (`:52-61`). CheckIO state predicate and caller-family pass (2026-10-19; no new finding or line credit): reread `CheckIO` and `WaitIO` (`rom/exec/checkio.c:48-60`; `waitio.c:50-80`) against Exec `SendIO`/`AbortIO` contracts and inventoried maintained C call sites with repository-wide `rg`. Checked representative selected teardown/reuse callers: NVMe timer cleanup aborts only when still pending then always WaitIOs (`rom/devs/nvme/nvme_timer.c:63-82`); the sound datatype removes completed audio requests and aborts-plus-waits pending ones (`workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/dispatch.c:2958-2966`), and its double-buffer path only reuses requests for which CheckIO reports complete (`:3318-3329`). PC boot-console UART readiness/ownership gap recheck (EK9127 added, 2026-10-19): traced the selected all-PC `con_CanGetc()` then `con_Getc()` call through all-native serial boot-console helpers and the i386 PC serial HIDD. `debug=serial` defaults to COM1; serial.device unit 0 constructs the same COM1 HIDD unit, enables receive-data interrupts, and its handler drains UART_RX before delivering bytes. This establishes a conditional TOCTOU path where a ready byte is consumed after the boot-console test and before its unbounded receive loop, violating the no-wait KrnMayGetChar contract. Added EK9127 to the detailed report and index. No serial device or input race was run; source-only. No line credit: this was a focused caller/ownership gap review, not a complete new-file review.


16450 boot-console full-body and baud-option boundary pass (EK9128 added, 2026-10-19): read all 144 physical lines of `arch/all-native/bootconsole/serial_16450.c` (101 `cloc 2.06` C code lines), traced `debug=serial` suffix handling through `con_InitSerial()` and the selected Multiboot, Multiboot2 and tag-list initializers, and checked the bootconsole manifest selection. `strtoul("0", ...)` stores zero because the only validation is an upper bound; the next divisor calculation divides `SER_MAXBAUD` by that zero. Added EK9128 to the detailed report, index and source row. This credits the 101 code lines to the incremental Exec/Kernel line-read tally; it does not imply whole-platform or runtime validation. No boot or invalid baud option was exercised; source-only.


PPC boot-console serial mapping/build-selection pass (2026-10-19; no new finding or line credit): followed `arch/all-native/bootconsole/serial_16450.c` into selected PPC paths. The Pegasos kernel links `bootconsole` (`arch/ppc-chrp/pegasos/kernel/make.opts`), sets `IO_Base=0xFE000000` and `Serial_Base=0x02F8`, then calls `serial_Init()` (`kernel_startup.c:111-123`), matching the backend’s `__ppc__` address calculation and the source comment identifying Serial2/IRQ3. Sam440 does not link `bootconsole`; its kernel has separate `krnPutC` and nonblocking `KrnMayGetChar` UART0 implementations. No additional PPC mapping defect established. Other PPC target selection and shared-UART ownership remain unreviewed; no UART was accessed. Source-only.

Bootconsole tag-list caller provenance pass (2026-10-19; no new finding): rechecked `con_InitTagList()` and traced its direct calls from i386 and x86-64 `kernel_startup.c`; traced VBE/GOP tag construction through Multiboot 1/2 and the bootstrap VESA setup. In the selected shared manifest, the tag-list initializer is compiled into the all-native bootconsole. The examined producers populate VBE mode/controller pointers together where the initializer dereferences both, and the 64-bit framebuffer address is carried separately for high-address GOP framebuffers. Broader boot protocols and external callers remain open. No new line credit or finding; source-only.

btserial device final-close/class-expunge lifetime pass (EK9129 added, 2026-10-20): traced the class's retained device-base open-count reservation, `devClose()` decrement and remaining base accesses, the class `libExpunge()` gate and reservation drop, `RemDevice()` dispatch, and device-base free (`rom/bluetooth/classes/btserial/{dev.c:160-210,btserial.class.c:82-106}`). Exec documents `Forbid()` as processor-local on ExecSMP; its `CloseDevice()` and `RemDevice()` wrappers therefore do not serialize the close vector against class expunge on another CPU. Added EK9129 for the conditional final-close overlap; the LDDemon `RemDevice` replacement also unloads the segment returned by device expunge before returning. No close/expunge race was run. Source-only.


SysMon Gauge class caller and ownership reconciliation (2026-10-19; no new finding): traced the CPU usage context-menu hook registration in `main.c` to `processorgaugehookfunc`, which creates the Gauge class with the existing processor count, swaps it into the live group, then disposes the previous class instance. Rechecked the complete Gauge custom-class constructor, update and dispose methods. The class body’s unchecked pointer-array allocation is GD2966 and its unchecked GaugeObject child insertion is GD2985; the distinction from SysMon’s separate CPU frequency arrays is maintained. The pointer vector is allocated independently of MUI child ownership and has no matching `FreeMem` in the class dispose method; promoted as the distinct Graphics/Desktop finding GD5537. No GUI or allocation failure was exercised; no line credit. Source-only.


SysMon Graph source-handle and disposal trace (2026-10-19; no new finding): followed the selected Graph constructor’s `GetSourceHandle`/`SetSourceAttrib` pairs through Graph’s source-array growth helper. SysMon immediately configures each returned handle; growth copies existing source records, so no stale handle is retained by this caller. Multi-graph children are Group-owned, and `OM_DISPOSE` keeps the read-hook array alive through superclass child disposal before freeing it. Existing GD2953, GD2967 and GD2985 cover the selected Graph failure paths. External source-handle clients and target GUI behavior remain open. No new issue or line credit; source-only.


`KrnCause` direct-caller and architecture-entry census (2026-10-20; no new EK): searched the pinned tree for `KrnCause()` and `SC_CAUSE`. The only direct selected Exec call is `rom/exec/enable.c:114`, guarded by the final `Disable()` nesting release, user-mode check, and pending `SFF_SoftInt` test (`:88-116`). Generic `rom/kernel/cause.c` issues `SC_CAUSE`; the already-traced PC, ARM, AArch64, OpenSBI, Unix, MinGW, Sam440 and Efika routes reach their exit-softint handling under their recorded user-mode/outermost-trap conditions. Unix and Efika provide platform `KrnCause` definitions; Amiga's override remains the documented no-op paired with chipset delivery. The tree search found no additional direct `KrnCause()` caller or generic-wrapper defect. Intel x2APIC handoff audit (EK9130 added, 2026-10-20): traced the x86-64 PC `Platform_Init()` APIC sequence, shared xAPIC register helpers, and later controller probe. `core_APIC_GetBase()` masks the base from IA32_APIC_BASE but never checks EXTD; `core_APIC_Config/Enable` then use MMIO, and x86-64 `core_APIC_Probe()` skips the i386 APIC-presence check. A repository-wide search found no x2APIC transition or register-MSR path. Intel’s SDM identifies MSR access as the x2APIC interface and says its MMIO interface is unavailable; Intel documents firmware handoff in x2APIC mode on current Core Ultra/Xeon generations. Added conditional EK9130 for x86-64 PC firmware handoffs in that mode. No hardware or boot was tested.

x86-64 task-exit stub caller and stack-layout reconciliation (2026-10-20; no new EK): traced `PrepareContext()` stack construction, NewAddTask finalPC selection, the default Exec finalizer, and a repository-wide C caller census for `AddTask()`/`NewAddTask()`. The stub’s two-word discard matches the two unconditional stack-argument slots and the fallback entry alignment; the default finalizer removes the current task. All maintained C creation callers use a NULL finalizer, while `TASKTAG_FINALPC` has no checked-in caller and is not documented as returning or non-returning. No local defect established; external custom-finalizer contract remains open. No task was run to return. Source-only.


Raspberry Pi ARM32 BootMsg producer-to-startup lifetime pass (2026-10-20; no new EK): verified `arch/arm-native/kernel/mmakefile.src` selects `kernel_startup.c` for `raspi-arm`/`raspi-armeb`, and `arch/arm-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src` passes the tag list to the generated core entry. The producer places the 64-entry TagItem array at the fixed low-memory boot layout (`boot.c:248,702-710`; `boot.h:13-14`; `bcm2708_boot.h:11-30`), while `query_memory()` raises the first usable RAM bound past the entire `bcm2708bootmem` reservation (`boot.c:218-236`). The maximum locally appended tag set is under that capacity. Followed pointer-bearing tags: `KRN_BootLoader` and optional `KRN_FuncPutC` remain within the bootstrap interval advertised by `KRN_ProtAreaStart/End`; the kernel reserves that interval before publishing managed memory (`kernel_startup.c:208-214,284-298`). The flattened tree and its `bootargs` string are copied/parsed in the mapped kernel image (`boot.c:564-575,674-700`), and `KRN_KernelBss` points to the bootstrap's static tracker, which also lies in the protected bootstrap range (`elf.c:142-143,194-203`). `kernel_cstart()` sets global `BootMsg` from this retained list before startup and later passes it into `krnPrepareExecBase` (`kernel_startup.c:137,301-307`). This closes only the selected Raspberry Pi ARM32 producer/lifetime path; CE boot and alternate firmware producers remain open. No boot was run; source-only.


Native RISC-V invalid-stack wrong-node candidate promoted (EK9131, 2026-10-20): reread `core_Dispatch()` against `cpu_Switch()`/`core_Switch()` and the selected kernel manifests. A rejected `newtask` is removed from `TaskReady` and changed to `TS_WAIT`, but the wait branch enqueues the function-entry `task` pointer (`arch/riscv-native/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:161-250`). In the normal switch path the prior task may still be linked in `TaskReady`, so dispatch can insert that same node in `TaskWait` and leave the rejected task unqueued. Added EK9131 to the report and master index. The native-RISC-V scheduler object is selected, but SiFive U's current boot function spins in `wfi` and its startup handoff is under `#if (0)` (`boot/boot.c:38-44`; `kernel_startup.c:50-68`); no current runtime reachability is claimed. No line credit changed and no task was run.


Pthread custom-stack ABI alignment cross-architecture caller pass (EK8962 restored and expanded, 2026-10-20): traced `pthread_attr_setstack()` through `pthread_create()` into selected i386 and PowerPC `NewStackSwap` implementations and the PPC `StackSwap` vector (`pthread.c:854-864`; `pthread_create.c:154-165`; `arch/i386-all/exec/newstackswap.c:30-38,63-74`; `arch/ppc-all/exec/newstackswap.c:30-47`; `arch/ppc-all/exec/stackswap.S:43-51`). With an aligned base and a size such as `PTHREAD_STACK_MIN + 1` (40,961), the accepted upper bound is misaligned. i386 subtracts 32 bytes for its eight argument slots; PPC subtracts `SP_OFFSET` and a frame-copy span that is a multiple of 16, so both retain the misaligned boundary. The selected `AROS_STACKALIGN` is 16 on both targets. Restored EK8962 to the detailed report and master index, extending the earlier i386-only coverage note to PPC. Traced DOS `RunCommand` as a non-triggering selected caller: it clamps to `AROS_STACKSIZE` 40,960. `cloc 2.06` reports 43 C code lines for PPC `newstackswap.c` and 41 assembly code lines for `stackswap.S`; both bodies and selected caller paths are now recorded as full reads. Custom stack execution and generated code were not tested. Source-only.


Pthread custom-stack alignment cross-architecture caller pass (EK8962 expanded, 2026-10-20): traced `pthread_attr_setstack()` and `pthread_create()` through each selected `NewStackSwap` implementation and architecture makefile: i386, PPC, ARM/ARMeb, m68k, AArch64, RV32 and RV64. Confirmed the non-aligned `stk_Upper/stk_Pointer` is preserved through argument pushes, frame copying or direct SP installation on all seven families; their selected CPU headers specify 16-byte alignment except m68k, which requires 8-byte alignment. Checked the two control paths: x86-64 rounds its new pointer down to `AROS_STACKALIGN`, while hosted Unix uses `makecontext()` with the supplied stack region, so neither is added to this finding. `config/specs.in:26` selects `__AROS__` but not `__AMIGA__`, so pthread_create uses the `NewStackSwap` branch on AROS. Expanded EK8962's report and index scope. No stack switch or build was run. Source-only.


Android all-unix NewStackSwap host-path caller and alignment recheck (2026-10-20; superseded by EK9378 recheck): confirmed `arch/all-linux/android/exec/make.opts:5-6` is the only source selection for this override and that it defines `HAVE_SWAPCONTEXT` despite its comment that Android lacks the context APIs. The earlier pass left the initializer and host-symbol outcome conditional; the 2026-10-23 recheck traced HostLib's unresolved-entry behavior, interface release, ignored INITLIB-set return and DOS `RunCommand()` use, establishing the stale-interface candidate now detailed as EK9378. The function supplies `uc_stack.ss_sp/ss_size` from caller bounds and delegates initial SP/alignment to external `makecontext`; source alone does not establish the platform's alignment contract, so EK8962 is not extended to this path. Checked the generic pthread and DOS RunCommand callers: each passes a non-NULL `StackSwapArgs`; the public vector contract still permits NULL and untracked/guest callers remain open. No runtime behavior was claimed and no build was run. Source-only.


i386 PrepareContext stack-entry ABI arithmetic recheck (EK8963 detailed report added, 2026-10-20): recomputed the full modulo-16 sequence from `NewAddTask()`'s align-down through `PrepareContext()`'s argument and fallback pushes. For one argument, aligned top 0 -> argument push 12 -> fallback push 8, while the usual incoming state after a 16-byte-aligned call site is 12. The x86-PC dispatch restores this context through the interrupt frame/IRET path, with no call shim. Confirmed selected one-argument C entries in Exec initialization. Kept the finding conditional on the compiler's incoming-boundary assumption: the source build files contain no override, but generated toolchain options and generated code were not checked. Added the detailed entry and master-index link; no build or task was run. No additional whole-file line credit. Source-only.


i386 PC CPU-context macro and trap-dump caller pass (EK9132 added, 2026-10-20): read the full 27-code-line `arch/i386-pc/kernel/kernel_cpu.h`, traced every macro use through the selected generic kernel/PC sources, and followed the raw interrupt frame through `core_EnterInterrupt` into `cpu_Trap()`/`PrintContext()`. `CPUSSEContxtSize` matches the selected i386 `kb_ContextSize` for the configured FXSAVE context; no separate AVX-state defect was established because this source path does not enlarge the context for AVX. `krnSysCall` callers use the selected software-interrupt path, `SP(regs)` maps to the pre-entry ESP in the same-ring frame, and no other macro mismatch was found. Added EK9132: the same-ring hardware frame has no saved SS, so the dump's `regs->ss` slot reads stack data. Credited 27 cloc 2.06 header lines; strict recorded aggregate updates from 456,093/804,558 to 456,120/804,558 = 56.7%. Caller audit beyond selected in-tree macro uses remains open; no trap or build was run. Source-only.


i386 PC private-kernel header and selected caller pass (2026-10-20; no new EK): read all 59 `cloc 2.06` code lines in `arch/i386-pc/kernel/kernel_intern.h`; traced the boot-private fields into startup/platform consumers, `__save_flags`/`__restore_flags` into debug paths, and all selected `krnLeaveSupervisorRing()` callers. Startup enters the user selector after platform post-init; ACPI power-off enters user mode for ACPICA as its comment requires; the AP bootstrap re-enters supervisor mode inside `core_APIC_Init()` before editing IDT/APIC state. No separate source defect established. The IOPL policy and non-tree callers are not established by this snapshot. Credited 59 header code lines; strict recorded aggregate updates from 456,120/804,558 to 456,179/804,558 = 56.7%. No mode transition or build was run. Source-only.


i386 bootmem no-bound finding recheck (EK8948 detailed entry restored, 2026-10-20): traced `krnAllocBootMemAligned()` into the i386 first-boot path and selected PC bootstrap reservation. The bootstrap guarantees at least `ro_size + rw_size + PAGE_SIZE - 1 + 0x80000` for placement, while `KRN_KernelHighest` is the actual loaded image end; this gives a 512-KiB minimum tail, so simple absence of any reserve is not the trigger. The reserve is not computed from copied `KRN_MMAPLength`, tag count or string/BSS payload sizes, and i386 compiles out the allocator's only limit check. The finding is therefore conditional on those early requests exceeding the minimum tail when the chosen RAM region has no additional usable extent. `mmap_InitMemory()` consumes the cursor as `khi` and excludes only the intersection with RAM chunks. Added the exact limitation and trigger to the report/index; no boot metadata or runtime was used. Source-only.


Exec Permit pthread caller slice (2026-10-20; no new EK): traced the pthread timed-mutex Forbid/Wait/Permit sequence through _obtain_sema_timed and the paired sched_yield call (`compiler/pthread/pthread.c:294-304`; `compiler/pthread/sched.c:46-57`). The AROS timed path brackets waiter publication and Wait with one pair; Wait's documented nesting save/restore allows task switching while blocked and restores the caller's nesting after wake. sched_yield sets the pending-reschedule flag between its matched calls. No unmatched Permit or Exec defect was established in these callers. Repository-wide textual hits are not a completed caller census (they include comments and non-call references); the Permit row remains pending wider caller sequencing. No pthread operation was run; source-only.


TaskRes recycled-slot SMP list race recheck (EK9125 expanded; 2026-10-20): traced both AllocTaskStorageSlot() branches and FreeTaskStorageSlot() against the exact Exec AddHead()/Remove() list-link stores and the TaskRes initializer (rom/task/AllocTaskStorageSlot.c:51-76; FreeTaskStorageSlot.c:47-64; task_init.c:66-75; rom/exec/addhead.c:51-61; remove.c:49-57). The original EK9125 sentinel duplicate-ID case remains. A freed non-tail node is removed and immediately freed by allocation; concurrent allocators can retain the same head pointer and race its removal/free. Concurrent frees race AddHead publication, and free versus allocation can race the same head links. The single-CPU Forbid critical sections do not serialize these mutations across CPUs; no SMP lock protects the list. Expanded EK9125 rather than adding a duplicate, and updated its short AROS index description. Generated task slots from module InitLib/expunge and POSIX C thread hooks are selected callers. No concurrent list operation or library lifecycle was run; source-only.


PPC generic PrepareContext valid-tag and NewAddTask failure-path pass (2026-10-20; no new EK): re-read `arch/ppc-all/exec/preparecontext.c` and traced its only common caller through `NewAddTask()` (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:301-309`). `KrnCreateContext()` allocates a cleared frame (`rom/kernel/kernel_objects.h:11`); the NULL branch returns FALSE and NewAddTask cleans the ETask. For a valid tag list, argument tags populate r3-r10, TAG_MORE/TAG_SKIP/TAG_DONE navigation is consistent with tag semantics, and the frame receives `finalPC`, aligned `tc_SPReg`, and `initialPC`. No defect was established in this path. The generic PPC object’s selection against CHRP/Sam440 overrides and its selected dispatch pairing remain open; malformed/cyclic tag-list bounds are not promoted without a caller contract violation. No task, allocation failure or target build was run; source-only.

Efika PPC interrupt-disable mask report restoration and caller qualification (EK816, 2026-10-20): restored the detailed report/index entry referenced by the existing `ictl.c` coverage row. Rechecked `ictl_enable_irq()` against `ictl_disable_irq()` and traced final-handler removal through `KrnRemIRQHandler()` (`arch/ppc-chrp/efika/kernel/intr.c:152-164`). For main IRQs 4–19, the disable comparison yields 1 instead of the corresponding mask bit; `ictl_handler()` has no main-orphan masking branch (`ictl.c:134-153`). IRQ 20 happens to use bit zero and is not affected by this expression; peripheral IDs 21–44 share the typo, but the peripheral orphan branch masks a delivered source at `:173-177`. `RemIntServer()` exposes the kernel IRQ removal route (`rom/exec/remintserver.c:53-55`; `compiler/include/exec/interrupts.h:82-87`). The only direct Efika timer cleanup call is guarded by a `noexpunge` library option (`timer_init.c:153-159`; `rom/timer/timer.conf:3`), so no ordinary in-tree last-main-IRQ removal trigger was established. Added EK816 detail to the report and index; no IRQ, controller or hardware was exercised. Source-only.

Efika interrupt-controller recheck (2026-10-20; EK817/EK818 restored with qualifications): compared `ictl_handler()`'s PIS scan and orphan-mask bit with the PER source numbering in `arch/ppc-chrp/efika/include/asm/mpc5200b.h`; traced the optional built-in OHCI IRQ assignment/registration and controller interrupt enable. The scan tests bits 21..0 while USB source 6 is bit 25 and requests IRQ 27, so the selected handler cannot be reached for that source. The orphan path masks a counter-derived bit rather than the tested PIS bit. Restored EK817 with the optional package/aggregate-target caveat and source-only impact wording. For EK818, confirmed the calculated `ictl_ee` value is discarded by the subsequent constant write; no local evidence identifies firmware field values or external-line consumers, so the report states register-state loss and leaves hardware consequence conditional. These findings refine the existing row and do not earn full-file line credit. No build, controller, or hardware was run.


Efika kernel debug resolver full-body/caller pass (2026-10-20; no new EK): read all 289 cloc 2.06 C code lines in `arch/ppc-chrp/efika/kernel/debug.c`; traced `findNames()`'s two selected callers through `mmu_handler()` and the `KRN_DebugInfo` boot-tag producer/copy into the static module list. Confirmed the serial output helper polls its debug UART status before/after each byte. Efika OpenFirmware-tree error-propagation and consumer recheck (EK647/EK648 restored, 2026-10-20): re-read `ofw_get_properties`, recursive `ofw_build_tree`, `ofw_scan_tree`, the bootstrap publication of `KRN_OpenFirmwareTree`, Efika `krnCopyOFWTree`, and the selected `builtin`/`reg` consumer. The builder ignores property/child allocation failures and returns a partial root; bootstrap publishes it. If `builtin` or `reg` is absent, `ForeachNode` ends on a non-NULL sentinel and the consumer tests the pointer as a match before reading fields. Separately, property construction ignores `ofw_get_prop` status and retains the declared length; the Efika consumer reads four MBAR bytes without validating either result or length. TLSF MemHeader conversion/init-failure path distinction (2026-10-20; EK871 scope refinement): traced `krnConvertMemHeaderToTLSF()` from its PC, hosted Unix and RISC-V OpenSBI callers through the first-chunk selection into `krnCreateTLSFMemHeader()` and `tlsf_init()`. Conversion chooses a chunk only when its byte count is at least `ROUNDUP(sizeof(tlsf_t)) + 3 * ROUNDUP(sizeof(bhdr_t))`, exactly the threshold checked by `tlsf_init()` for embedding the control structure; therefore this converted-header path does not need the separately allocated TLSF control block whose failure underlies EK871. Direct `krnCreateTLSFMemHeader()` callers, including the cited AArch64 additional-memory-header path, remain subject to that conditional failure. `krnConvertMemHeaderToTLSF()` can return NULL when no chunk meets the threshold; checked callers either retain the original header, drop the unconvertible PC region, or are covered by their existing startup branches, with no independent selected failure consequence established in this pass. This narrows EK871's conversion-path scope and adds no finding or line credit; no boot or allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

TLSF conversion caller-result nuance (2026-10-20 correction): the preceding EK871 path-scope note's phrase that checked callers either retain or drop a NULL conversion result was too broad. The PC builder omits an undersized region and RISC-V OpenSBI retains the original header on a NULL result, but hosted Unix assigns the conversion result directly for its first chip header and does not test it before `bootmh = chipmh` (`arch/all-unix/kernel/kernel_startup.c:201-212`). The selected hosted bootstrap supplies its low-memory map to this path; this pass did not establish a valid boot map that both allows startup to reach conversion and has no chunk meeting TLSF's embedded-control threshold. Treat that as an unresolved low-memory boundary, not as proved safe or as a confirmed failure. The prior note's embedded-control conclusion still holds when conversion succeeds. Source-only.

PC TLSF conversion multi-chunk ownership pass (EK9137 added, 2026-10-20): followed the selected PC builder's pre-/post-kernel `krnAddMemChunk()` appends into `krnConvertMemHeaderToTLSF()`. Conversion scans past chunks below its embedded-control threshold, places the new managed MemHeader in the first qualifying chunk, then adds only that chunk and its successors; any earlier nonempty free chunks are dropped with the old MemHeader. Added EK9137 for the conditional loss of usable memory. The code establishes the omission, but this pass did not establish a selected firmware map whose first retained chunk falls below the threshold while a later chunk meets it. No new line credit because the converter and PC map builder already have full-body coverage; no boot or allocation was run. Source-only.

Realtime alarm publication-order recheck (EK9138 added, 2026-10-20): traced `PLAYER_AlarmTime` through `SetPlayerAttrsA()` and compared its flag/time store order with Pulse's locked player walk and alarm read (`workbench/libs/realtime/setplayerattrsa.c:195-198`; `pulse.c:76-78,126-150`). The setter does not acquire `RT_CONDUCTORS`, so on ExecSMP Pulse may observe `PLAYERF_ALARMSET` with the previous deadline before the requested `pl_AlarmTime` is stored. Rechecked `CreatePlayerA()`'s cleared allocation and READY default, and confirmed a conductor plus signal destination can be established before a later alarm-time tag; the zero prior deadline can therefore produce an early signal for a future deadline. Search of maintained C sources found no direct `PLAYER_AlarmTime` or alarm-signal setter caller; record as a conditional public API race with that caveat. This does not add whole-file line credit: these function bodies already have credit. No alarm or interleaving was run; source-only.

POSIXC close-on-exec report/index restoration and foreign-socket flag path (EK8969 restored; EK9139 added, 2026-10-20): rechecked regular `execve()`/`execv()` through `__exec_do_regular()`, `RunCommand()`, target `__init_fd()`/`__copy_fdarray()`, and the isolated pretend-child close pass. Separately traced the foreign-owner branch of `fcntl()` through AROSTCP's fd.library registration: `F_SETFD` returns success without storing flags, `F_GETFD` always returns zero, and the socket hook table has no fcntl hook. Existing function bodies were already credited; no line credit added. No process or socket operation was run; source-only.

POSIXC/AROSTCP descriptor-flag contract recheck for EK9139 (2026-10-20; no new EK): matched the public fcntl documentation in `compiler/crt/posixc/fcntl.c:28-50,67-75` with the local descriptor implementation and the fd.library hook ABI. Local `F_SETFD` stores the supplied flag and `F_GETFD` returns it (`fcntl.c:168-181`); the documented `FD_CLOEXEC` bit is acted on by `__close_on_exec_fdescs()` (`__fdesc.c:799-818`). The foreign-socket branch precedes that local storage path and hard-codes `F_GETFD=0`/`F_SETFD=0` (`fcntl.c:94-110`). The public `struct fd_hooks` includes `fdh_fcntl` (`workbench/libs/fd/include/fd.h:40-45`), but AROSTCP explicitly registers it NULL while handling only O_NONBLOCK through its ioctl hook (`amiga_fdhooks.c:191-234`). This confirms the documented API mismatch and keeps the later exec-close consequence independently qualified by EK8969. No socket/fcntl operation was run and no new line credit was added.

AArch64 DOS Shell stack-size caller pass (EK8962 expanded, 2026-10-20): traced the selected `Stack` command in `workbench/c/shellcommands/mmakefile.src` through its pointer-sized `CLI_DEFAULTSTACK_UNIT` rounding, Shell's conversion back to bytes, `RunCommand()`'s minimum-only clamp and exact `stk_Upper` calculation, and AArch64 `NewStackSwap()`'s direct SP installation. For `Stack 40961`, the command stores 5,121 8-byte units; Shell passes 40,968 bytes, which leaves the stack top 8 modulo the AArch64 16-byte ABI alignment. `AllocMem()` rounds allocation size, but `RunCommand()` derives the top from the original requested size, so this does not repair alignment. Extended EK8962 to include this selected ordinary Shell trigger; no whole-file line credit because these source bodies were not in the current Exec-only line denominator and the finding pass did not claim them reviewed. Stack switching/build/runtime not exercised; source-only.

Exec DoIO body and completion handoff review (2026-10-20; EK8799 retained, OD2140/OD1539 caller errors distinguished): read the complete 25 `cloc 2.06` code lines, checked null request/device exits, IOF_QUICK initialization, BeginIO vector dispatch, conditional WaitIO, and returned `io_Error`. The synchronous wrapper reports failure correctly when an earlier OpenDevice failure leaves `io_Device` NULL; LPe32002 and BCM2708 USB OTG callers that ignore this return are device-side findings, not a DoIO defect. Re-traced selected Intuition SetPrefs -> input.device IND_SETTHRESH/IND_SETPERIOD -> ProcessEvents -> ReplyMsg. Although ReplyMsg publishes NT_REPLYMSG before linking, DoIO immediately enters WaitIO while the request is still NT_MESSAGE; WaitIO then sleeps until InternalPutMsg links the reply and signals the private port. SetPrefs therefore does not expose EK8799's publication interval, and its caller-side port deletion is not evidence of an early-return race. PFS3 named device-unit semaphore publication cross-check (EK9140 added, 2026-10-20): traced the two-stage `FindSemaphore`/`AddSemaphore` path during handler initialization through Exec's per-operation list spinlocks and processor-local Forbid, then through the stored pointer to `lock_device_unit()` and `UpdateDisk()` (`rom/filesys/pfs3/fs/init.c:573-626`; `rom/exec/{forbid,findsemaphore,addsemaphore}.c`; `rom/filesys/pfs3/fs/update.c:197-204`). OpenSBI DWMAC null IRQ-token failure-path recheck (EK09 / OD2923 retained; coverage alias EK815, 2026-10-20): traced `DWMAC_CreateUnit()` through `AddIntServer()` and the worker readiness handshake into `DWMAC_DeleteUnit()` (`workbench/devs/networks/dwmac/dwmac_unit.c:1105-1118,1126-1177,1184-1205`). The service task can initialize and make unit creation return success even when `KrnAddIRQHandler()` has failed, because `AddIntServer()` is void and DWMAC unconditionally sets `dwu_IRQAdded`; a later task/allocation startup failure follows `DWMAC_DeleteUnit()` and calls `RemIntServer()` with the null `is_Node.ln_Succ`. The `RemIntServer()` kernel branch forwards that token to `KrnRemIRQHandler()`, whose `h->in_nr` read precedes its null check (`rom/exec/addintserver.c:64-67`; `remintserver.c:53-55`; `remirqhandler.c:52-56`). This verifies the failed-registration rollback trigger in OD2923 and does not add a separate kernel defect. DWMAC remains opt-in; no allocation failure or hardware was induced. No line credit; source-only.

m68k voluntary Wait/switch signal-race recheck (2026-10-20; EK811 retained, no new EK): traced the selected assembly Wait override into `m68k_VoluntarySwitch`, the frame rollback path and the Amiga level-1/2 IRQ wrappers plus `Signal()`. The `0x4000` write to INTENA clears master enable because `INTF_SETCLR` is bit 15 and `INTF_INTEN` bit 14; the switch path performs this before its second `tc_SigRecvd & tc_SigWait` check and keeps Paula masked through `TS_WAIT` and TaskWait publication, then writes `0xC000` to reopen it. A signal arriving during frame construction is caught by the second check; later ordinary Paula signal delivery sees the published wait state and can wake it. This supports the existing Wait/Signal handshake qualification and does not reproduce a lost wakeup. The m68k assembly Wait does not call the C `KrnSwitch` wrapper; it calls the voluntary entry directly. No task or interrupt was run. Updated this source row; no line credit. Source-only.

m68k ROM-support remap-table allocation failure recheck (EK8944 restored/qualified, 2026-10-20): reread the complete 198-line `arch/m68k-amiga/kernel/romsupport.c` and checked the selected 68030 translation helper, `CopyMem` implementation and boot ordering. With `i > 0`, `AllocMem((i + 2) * sizeof(ULONG), MEMF_ANY)` is followed by a positive-length `CopyMem` and two sentinel stores without a NULL check; an allocation failure therefore faults at the destination access. The code path requires a recorded nonidentity 030 ROM-window mapping. The normal AROSBootstrap handoff clears inherited 030 MMU state before restart (`arch/m68k-amiga/c/AROSBootstrap.c:1014-1048`), so the report now limits the candidate to an alternate/legacy 030 startup that retains such a mapping; the source establishes the failure consequence but not that this configuration is currently shipped. Big-endian InitStruct macro follow-up (EK9145, 2026-10-20): completed the decoder/public-header comparison and searched all tracked C/header/assembly source for `INITSTRUCT` uses. FreePooled complete-body and paired-release pass (2026-10-20; no new finding): read all 75 physical lines (29 `cloc 2.06` C lines) of `rom/exec/freepooled.c`; traced its ordinary path through `InternalFreePooled`, `stdDealloc` and `FreeMemHeader`, plus the managed callback setup in `CreatePool` and TLSF's `mhe_Free = tlsf_freemem` pair (`rom/kernel/tlsf.c:863-866,1476`). For managed TLSF pools, the public `MEMF_SEM_PROTECTED` bit is set on the callback header and TLSF takes/releases the associated semaphore in its free path; unprotected callback use is not promised concurrent safety. EK9124 remains the distinct plain-pool allocation adjustment overflow. Wider mutable-string callers, managed callbacks and external users remain pending. ### PC Utility SetMem build-selection and dispatch recheck (candidate withdrawn, 2026-10-20)

Compared the all-PC Utility object and `-mavx` flag (`arch/all-pc/utility/mmakefile.src`) with the SSE2 intrinsic body (`setmem_sse.c`, `setmem_pc.h`), x86 runtime dispatch and kernel flags, and selected graphics text caller (`rom/graphics/text.c:154-166`). The earlier i386 candidate is withdrawn: the i386 Utility initializer is a separate architecture-specific object compiled under the configured `-march=i486` ISA baseline (`configure.in:1381`), which does not define `__SSE__`; therefore the `#ifdef __SSE__` branch that installs `SetMem_SSE` is absent in that build. Although the i386 kernel sets `ECF_FPFXS` for SSE-only CPUs, that flag cannot reach the compiled-out setter. The all-PC `-mavx` option is attached to the PC Utility target and compiles `setmem_sse`; on x86-64, `make.opts` enables `USE_SSE_COPYMEM`, so this object aliases `SetMem` to the SSE-named implementation, while the x86-64 initializer separately patches AVX only when its `__AVX__` branch is compiled and context support is present. Whether the compiler emits AVX instructions in the x86-64 default alias cannot be established from source alone and is not promoted as a finding. Credited full bodies for `setmem_sse.c` (129 physical lines; cloc 2.06: 73 C code lines) and `arch/i386-all/utility/utility_archinit.c` (57 physical lines; cloc: 44 C code lines). The PC Utility manifest, scalar helper, selected graphics caller, and existing i386 kernel CPU feature body were read/rechecked; individual API caller audit, x86-64 generated instruction selection, and runtime behavior remain open. Source-only.


### m68k Utility arithmetic override body and caller pass (EK9147-EK9148 added, 2026-10-20)

Read the complete `arch/m68k-all/utility` manifest, initializer, and six selected assembly files, then traced same-basename object exclusion through `rom/utility/mmakefile.src` and `config/make.tmpl:2106-2109,2142-2143`. Added EK9147 for the `UMult64` operand-half mapping, including the statically traced `2*3 -> 9` result and the public API contract; added EK9148 for `SMult64` selecting sign correction from D0 rather than the saved sign accumulator, with `SMult64(-1,1) -> +1`. The initializer patches native 020 operations on 68020/030/040, but leaves the software 64-bit routines selected on 68000/68010 and skips those replacements for 68060. Read the four 32-bit division/multiplication routines; no additional defect established in their ordinary quotient, remainder, low-product, or carry paths. Credited six assembly bodies (187 `cloc 2.06` code lines) and `utility_archinit.c` (29 C code lines). `ieeedpmul.c` was read fully as a candidate caller, then excluded from the selected runtime trigger because `mathieeedoubbas_init` unconditionally patches LVO 13 to `FPU_IEEEDPMul`; its rounding and exceptional-value behavior remain outside this Utility pass. Other public UMult64 clients, exact target boot/package selection, generated assembly include, and runtime arithmetic remain open. Source-only; no arithmetic was executed.

PC APIC descriptor-width and SMP loop-bound pass (EK9150 added, 2026-10-20): completed the 114-line `apic.h` review (83 `cloc 2.06` code lines) and traced `apic_count` from the MADT count/parse hooks into the allocated `CPUData` flexible array and `smp_Wake()`.
