Taskless AttemptSemaphore inconsistency (EK9152 promoted from former coverage-only EK8854, 2026-10-20): rechecked both public wrappers, `InternalAttemptSemaphore`, `ReleaseSemaphore`, Exec PREINITLIB order and the complete maintained PREINITLIB registration/caller search. The attempt wrappers pass NULL as the owner before task publication; on a free initialized semaphore the helper records a zero owner and positive nesting/count, while ReleaseSemaphore immediately returns for NULL `ThisTask`. The balanced pre-init sequence can therefore leave a phantom-held semaphore whose later exclusive users wait indefinitely. `exec_init.c` runs PREINITLIB before creating/publishing the bootstrap task, but the sole maintained registration is PC `Exec_X86PreInit`, which only adds the shutdown callback; no checked-in callback calls either attempt API. Promoted the mechanism to EK9152 with the external/future callback condition explicit; not a default selected-path claim. No startup or semaphore operation was run. Source-only.

CHRP resident-scan allocation failure caller recheck (2026-10-20; no new EK): re-read `exec_RomTagScanner()` final-array conversion and its direct caller in `exec_main()` (`arch/ppc-chrp/exec/exec_init.c:444-549,245-249`), then traced the NULL result into `InitCode()` (`rom/exec/initcode.c:69-100`). Failure to allocate the final `(i+1)` pointer array returns NULL without draining the temporary `rtList`; the caller publishes NULL and both single-task and cold-start `InitCode()` calls then skip their resident loops without an error result. Failure to allocate an individual `rt_node` instead silently omits that resident. This confirms the leak/omission behavior under allocation failure, but the required-resident set for the selected CHRP images and whether a later checked startup path necessarily fails were not established, so no separate finding is promoted here. The manifest selects this CHRP Exec override (`arch/ppc-chrp/exec/mmakefile.src:12-40`); the Efika variant substitutes its kernel implementation and must be checked separately. No allocation failure or boot was induced. Source-only.

CHRP resident-scan allocation consequence established (EK9153 added, 2026-10-20): enumerated the selected Efika link and cold-start RTAS resident instead of leaving the earlier required-resident impact open. Confirmed genmodule enforces NOAUTOINIT for resources and generated resource initialization calls AddResource only after successful init (`tools/genmodule/config.c:825-830`; `tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1080-1099,1186-1192`; `rom/exec/initresident.c:159-166`); this closes the registration-mechanism link in EK9153. The Efika kernel links `rtas_resource.o` (`arch/ppc-chrp/efika/kernel/mmakefile.src:13-15`); `rtas.conf` priority 99 is mapped to `RTF_COLDSTART` by the generator (`rtas.conf:1-6`; `tools/genmodule/writeinclibdefs.c:31-48`), and `rtas_init` is the resident init callback. An `rt_node` allocation failure skips the resident; final array failure returns NULL, leaks the local nodes, and causes `InitCode()` to skip all residents (`exec_init.c:490-506,526-549,245-249,409-410`; `rom/exec/initcode.c:69-100`). Traced missing `rtas.resource` to selected `ShutdownA()` (`arch/ppc-chrp/exec/shutdowna.c:27-44`), which returns without RTAS calls when `OpenResource` returns NULL. Added EK9153 to the report and index; the prior unproven-required-resident note is superseded for this concrete shutdown consequence. No allocation failure, boot or firmware call was induced. Source-only.

DOS-list semaphore nesting/caller trace (2026-10-20; no new EK): rechecked `LockDosList`, `AttemptLockDosList`, `UnLockDosList`, and `AddDosEntry` against the selected NTFS volume-add path (`workbench/fs/ntfs/packet.c:620-624`; optional `workbench-fs-ntfs` target in `workbench/fs/ntfs/mmakefile.src:3-12`). `LDF_VOLUMES|LDF_WRITE` obtains the shared `di_DevLock` exclusively; nested `AddDosEntry` obtains that same lock as a read request, which the current owner may nest, then obtains `di_EntryLock` in the established Dev-before-Entry order. Its inner `UnLockDosList` drops only that nested DevLock count, and the caller drops the outer count afterward. The checked path does not create a lock inversion or release the caller's ownership prematurely. This trace adds no fairness/count-wrap trigger beyond the existing semaphore findings. No handler or contention was run; source-only.

EK9155 PCIe MSI firmware-range caller follow-up (2026-10-20; no new finding): traced BCM2712 PCIe bridge OF `msi-ranges` and optional `brcm,msi-offset` parsing through `msi_first_intid`, vector allocation and `GetVectorAttribs`, then followed the selected RP1 setup's USB-host MSI vector requests. The software path adds the GIC SPI base and publishes the resulting INTID without checking against AArch64 `HW_IRQ_COUNT=384`; RP1 configures its USB interrupt messages using those returned IDs. This establishes an in-tree path by which firmware-provided IDs above 383 can reach BCM2712 IRQ dispatch, conditional on the actual node range and an interrupt being delivered. The checked-in tree does not establish the Pi 5 board's effective OF range or prove a live enabled source above 383. Expanded EK9155's source trigger/scope and confidence accordingly. Read the relevant full functions and surrounding OF, allocation, and RP1 setup code; no device tree or hardware was queried. Source-only.

GenModule long-proto-name filesystem-reachability qualification (EK9032 rechecked, 2026-10-20): followed `writeincproto()` from path construction and `fopen()` to the local `define[256]` copy (`tools/genmodule/writeincproto.c:14-23,132-155`). Since the file path ends in `<includename>.h`, the 256-byte name needed for the unterminated `strncpy` requires the host filesystem to allow a filename component of at least 258 bytes. On filesystems enforcing a 255-byte component limit, `fopen()` fails before the stack-buffer read. Narrowed EK9032's practical trigger to custom inputs on a supporting host filesystem; the source-level unterminated copy remains confirmed. No generator or filesystem boundary was exercised.

GenModule long-proto-name finding restoration and source recheck (EK9032; 2026-10-29; no body/path/LOC credit): re-read the full `writeincproto()` body and the `includename` parser/normalization and `writeincludes` dispatch (`tools/genmodule/writeincproto.c:15-23,132-159`; `tools/genmodule/config.c:1300-1305,1422-1426`; `tools/genmodule/genmodule.c:39-46`). Confirmed the nondigit-leading 256+-byte path uses `strncpy()` without a terminator then passes the stack array to `%s`; digit-leading names use bounded `snprintf()` and are excluded. Qualified reachability because the writer first opens `<includename>.h`, so an ordinary 255-byte component limit blocks a single long component; path-like names require usable directories or a host filesystem allowing longer components. Restored the detailed finding text in `AROS-exec-kernel.md`; the writer body was already credited and this adds no coverage. No custom config, generator, filesystem boundary or build was run. Source-only.

POSIXC relative-library partial-open rollback pass (EK600 expanded, 2026-10-20): traced the per-task generated `OpenLib` ordering (`set_open_rellibraries()` before OPENLIB hooks) against `_set_open_rellibraries_list()` and the per-task failure branch (`compiler/autoinit/libraries.c:77-106`; `tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1386-1400`). The helper returns immediately if a mandatory later library open fails and does not close already opened entries; the per-task branch restores the previous task base and frees the duplicate without calling `set_close_rellibraries()`. POSIXC has two required rellib entries, `StdCBase` and `StdCIOBase` (`__posixc_init.c:17-22`), so one can remain opened if the other fails. Expanded EK600 as another trigger of the same rollback gap and added its missing short index entry. No library was opened or forced to fail; source-only.

POSIXC relative-library rollback classification correction (EK8934 separated from EK600, 2026-10-20): compared generated duplicate-base OpenLib (`tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1386-1400`) with `_set_open_rellibraries_list()` and the ordinary `_set_libinit()` rollback (`compiler/autoinit/libraries.c:77-127`; `compiler/autoinit/functions.c:40-84`). The dependency-open failure is distinct: the helper can return after a later required dependency fails without closing earlier successful entries, and duplicate-base OpenLib frees the copy without the close helper. Restored/added EK8934 as this generated dependency-open finding. EK600 remains limited to later module OPENLIB-hook failures after dependencies opened successfully; its POSIXC pool, descriptor-copy and stdio partial-state consequences remain separate. The earlier pass incorrectly folded EK8934's trigger into EK600; the report and index now keep them distinct. No dependency was opened or failed; source-only.

M68k RunHunk/RunFile full cleanup recheck (2026-10-20; existing EK9161/EK9162 retained, no new finding): re-read the complete 235-line `m68kemu_run.c` body. RunHunk destroys the containment context after both load failure and setup/execute return; RunFile closes its file and frees its file buffer at each checked read/context failure and after loading, then destroys the context after setup/execute. The child path duplicates the current directory, passes it to `CreateNewProc` with `NP_Synchronous`, and unlocks it on process-creation failure; the successful synchronous return reads `ctx->exit_code` only after child completion. Direct selected DOS callers pass through `RunCommand` and `NewCreateProc`, already tracked for stack and argument semantics. The ignored `M68KEmu_SetupLibBase` DOS result was checked against the fresh-context region/capacity path; no reachable allocation failure was established there. No load, process, or allocation failure was induced; source-only.

BCM2708 SMP timer-FIQ return-to-scheduler trace (EK151/EK152/EK156/EK157 and EK8873 rechecked; no new EK): traced the per-core CNTP setup and tick from `ARMI_InitTimerCore` through the BCM2836 FIQ-pending handler, ARM FIQ vector and `core_ExitInterrupt` into the ARM scheduler (`arch/arm-native/kernel/platform_bcm2708.c:207-319,455-483`; `arch/arm-native/kernel/kernel_cpu.c:194-204`; `arch/arm-native/kernel/intr.c:169-196`; `rom/kernel/kernel_intr.c:30-50`; `arch/arm-native/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:88-145,257-412`; `arch/arm-native/exec/exec_platform.h:92-114,216-227`). The tick rearms CNTP, decrements only the owning core's TLS elapsed quantum, and raises that core's TLS switch/quantum flags; a task-context FIQ return calls `core_ExitInterrupt`, which checks the same switch flag and enters scheduling. Exec-disabled or nested FIQ returns defer rescheduling to the normal exit path. This confirms the per-core timer accounting and rules out a lost tick-to-scheduler handoff in the inspected selected path. BCM2708 GPU/system-timer VBlank remains the separate CPU-usage/VBlank delivery path; IRQ routing and physical timing were not exercised. No whole-file or code-line credit; source-only.
Exec GetMsg message-port primitive and PutMsg/WaitPort handoff pass (2026-10-20; no new EK): reread the full `GetMsg()` body and traced its list removal against `InternalPutMsg()` and `WaitPort()` (`rom/exec/getmsg.c:52-79`; `putmsg.c:71-105`; `waitport.c:53-96`; `remhead.c:48-70`). In the selected ExecSMP build, enqueue, dequeue and the waiter's emptiness check each use local interrupt exclusion plus the port spinlock; the waiter releases both before sleeping and rechecks after every signal, as required because signals may arrive without messages. The reviewed lock ordering has no nested port locks and does not establish a message lost-wakeup or duplicate-removal path. The direct `GetMsg()` caller census is not complete (repository search finds 779 references including declarations/comments and non-C sources), so this closes the primitive/handoff slice only; message-port lifetime and caller-specific ownership remain open. No task, port, or message was exercised; no whole-file line credit. Source-only.
Exec Allocate managed/unmanaged dispatch and direct selected caller pass (2026-10-20; no new EK): read the complete `Allocate()` body and traced its managed callback branch, ordinary `stdAlloc` branch, zero-size handling and selected managed-header implementations/callers (`rom/exec/allocate.c:92-143`; `rom/kernel/tlsf.c:489-570`; Radeon `bitmap.c:343-359`; VideoCore `vcgfx_memory.c:191-212`; `rom/exec/memory.c:246-285`; selected callsites in `rom/exec/createpool.c:170`, `kernel_memory.c:82`, `arch/ppc-chrp/efika/kernel/intr.c:47,116`). The public function requires a valid MemHeader pointer; its ASSERT follows an initial header dereference, so NULL is outside the documented input contract and is not counted as a finding. For valid headers, zero-size requests return NULL in the ordinary branch and selected TLSF callback; Radeon/VideoCore managed alloc callbacks also return NULL. Selected caller sizes are nonzero structure or allocation extents. On SMP, ordinary header mutation dispatches through `stdAlloc` and the per-header locking already tracked in the allocator rows; TLSF callbacks own their allocation lock. No additional dispatch or size-bound defect established. Wider external MemHeader construction and managed callback clients remain pending. No allocation was issued; no whole-file line credit. Source-only.
ObtainSemaphoreList duplicate-member candidate recheck (rejected; no new EK, 2026-10-20): tested whether a repeated semaphore member could enqueue the same `ss_MultipleLink` twice when contended (`rom/exec/obtainsemaphorelist.c:76-115`). The input is an intrusive List of `SignalSemaphore` objects linked through each object's sole `ss_Link` (`compiler/include/exec/semaphores.h:50-58`); a valid list cannot contain the same object twice without first corrupting its own link topology. The public function documents external list protection and does not define a non-intrusive wrapper-entry format. Thus the proposed duplicate waiter-node corruption has no well-formed input trigger and is not promoted. Existing EK8781 remains the distinct signed `failedObtain` overflow candidate; no source or list was mutated and no semaphore operation was run.

SysMon startup rollback and shared OOP helper recheck (EK9122/GD6078/GD1214 retained; 2026-10-20): re-read `main()`/`InitModules()`/`CreateApplication()` control flow and the full selected `timer.c`, `video.c`, and shared `rom/oop/obtainattrbases.c` failure paths. Confirmed `InitModules()` deinitializes only prior successful modules, so the failing module owns its own partial-init unwind; `InitVideo()` does not close `oop.library` when attribute-base acquisition fails, and when an earlier-than-final descriptor fails the shared helper loops on the same remaining descriptor forever (GD1214), preventing `main()` from reaching rollback. The final-descriptor case returns and leaks the OOP open reference (existing Graphics/Desktop finding); if application construction later fails, successful timer/video modules are retained because `main()` returns before `DeInitModules()` (EK9122/GD6078). These are already indexed candidates, so no new ID or line credit. Other SysMon startup failure points remain open. Source-only; no allocation or lookup failure was induced.

SysMon startup module caller closure follow-up (2026-10-24; EK9122 and GD6078/GD2969 reconciled): re-read the four module initializers/teardowns against `InitModules()`, `DeInitModules()`, `CreateApplication()` and both `main()` exits. Successful prior modules are unwound in reverse order if a later module initializer fails; a module returning FALSE must undo its own partial initialization. The memory module owns no resource, the processor module obtains a processor resource with no matching close interface, and timer/video own resources released only by their DeInit methods. The two reportable failure boundaries remain: video's final attribute-base failure leaks its `oop.library` open reference (GD2969), while successful initialization followed by failed MUI construction skips all module teardown (EK9122/GD6078). Earlier attribute-base failure hangs in the shared helper (GD1214). No additional module-init defect established; unrelated SysMon lifecycle/caller work remains open. No failure or application was induced; source-only.

Pthread self-ID caller and slot-lifetime pass (2026-10-20; no new EK): read the complete `pthread_self.c` and traced `GetThreadId()` against pthread construction, join, detached cleanup, and every direct selected caller (`pthread_exit`, cancellation state/type, TLS access, and cleanup handlers). Pthread detach-after-completion lifecycle recheck (EK569 restored, 2026-10-20): traced `pthread_detach()` against both `StarterFunc()` exit branches, `pthread_join()`, and `__pthread_Exit_Func()`. The completed joinable branch has already skipped record clearing; detach then marks that record detached, join rejects it, and the exit hook waits on its still-non-NULL `task` forever. Confirmed this call order is permitted for a terminated but unjoined POSIX thread. Restored the full candidate to the Exec/kernel report; the master index already links that report. No line credit; no thread or process exit was run. Source-only.

Exec child lifecycle report reconciliation (EK277/EK8845 restored, 2026-10-20): compared all current report headings with the child teardown coverage cross-references and found these two IDs had narrative rechecks but no standalone finding entries. Re-read `Exec_CleanupETask()` against both parent cleanup/reparenting and `ChildOrphan()` single/bulk detachment. Restored EK277 for ordinary concurrent parent/child cleanup and EK8845 for explicit orphan-versus-child-exit, keeping their distinct triggers, list-lock/lifetime consequences, ExecSMP condition, and lack of a maintained `ChildOrphan` C caller explicit. The master `AROS.md` links the Exec/kernel report. No line credit; no concurrent task operation was run. Source-only.


Pthread creation-failure slot interleaving report reconciliation (EK609, 2026-10-20): the existing candidate was promoted to the detailed report after tracing the two relevant orders from `CreateNewProcTags()` failure through the unlocked cleanup and a second `GetThreadId(NULL)` slot search. The second creator can have its `parent` cleared before publication, or the first caller can signal/return the second worker's record as its own successful creation. The per-file row retains the wider startup/CRT and thread-lifetime gaps; no failure or overlap was induced. Source-only.


Pthread join-cancellation report reconciliation (EK608, 2026-10-20): promoted the existing candidate after checking Exec `Wait()`'s selected signal-mask loop against `pthread_cancel()`'s CTRL-C signal and the joiner's parent-only wait. A worker-completion signal can release the join loop without a second cancellation test; the pending request is then left for a later cancellation point. No join/cancel interleaving was run. Source-only.

Pthread cancel-after-exit finding/report reconciliation (EK8956, 2026-10-20): reread the complete `pthread_cancel`, `pthread_create` completion, `pthread_join`, Exec `Signal`, `RemTask`, and service-cleanup paths at commit `282a0454356dc2b9554ab023997d7f7ca24fc03e`; rechecked the selected `developer/debug/test/misc/pthreadtest.c` caller. Joinable completion retains the Task pointer, cancel does not reject the finished slot, and normal self-exit cleanup reclaims the Task storage before a later cancel can pass that pointer to `Signal`, which reads Task/ETask fields before its terminal-state test. Added EK8956 as a standalone detailed finding. The test provides a conditional checked-in caller, but no schedule or runtime behavior was reproduced. No new line credit; broader pthread lifecycle and external callers remain open. Source-only.

Task-notification callback registry-mutation recheck (EK8787 detail restored, 2026-10-20): traced `taskres_NotifyTasks()`'s shared `trb_NotifySem` hold across synchronous callback invocation against the exclusive acquisition in both `AddTaskNotifyHook()` and `RemTaskNotifyHook()`, then verified `InternalObtainSemaphore()` queues/waits when the current shared holder requests exclusive mode. The public callback contract permits semaphore acquisition and prohibits waiting for other tasks, but does not explicitly prohibit these registry mutators; no selected in-tree callback mutates the registry (Security's does not). Restored EK8787 as a standalone conditional API finding, qualified to callback-driven registration change; no callback or task event was run. Existing body/path credit unchanged. Source-only.

Task-hook queued-registration report reconciliation (EK8803/EK9183, 2026-10-20): re-read AddTaskHook, RunTaskHooks, InitTaskHooks, task hook node layouts, the public Hook layout, and selected startup registration/dispatch (`rom/task/{AddTaskHook,RunTaskHooks,InitTaskHooks}.c`; `rom/task/task_intern.h:77-80`; `compiler/include/utility/hooks.h:20-26`; `compiler/startup/startup.c:94-96,121-124,133-135`). Confirmed queued registration links `Hook.h_MinNode` while traversal casts that node to a wrapper whose first field should be `Hook *`; the dispatcher therefore receives the successor pointer, reaching the tail sentinel at the end, and the allocated wrapper is unlinked. Split the independent unchecked `AllocMem` dereference into EK9183. Queued mode is selected by `THF_IAR`/default flags; `THF_ROA` dispatches immediately. The public functions are in selected task.resource, but no in-tree AddTaskHook caller exists; both findings require an external queued-hook registration. Added standalone report entries; no hook or allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

PC syscall selector and argument-register/caller pass (2026-10-20; no new EK): reread the full `arch/all-pc/kernel/syscall.c` and `x86_syscalls.h` syscall table/macros, then matched the ABI to `CPUEXCTX_REGA/B` on x86-32 and x86-64 (`arch/all-pc/kernel/cpu_x86.h`), the selected per-platform registration paths, and maintained syscall callers in Exec, ACPI/APIC and kernel power management. The selector uses EAX/RAX's low `ULONG` as documented; pointer/state operands use EBX/RBX in both callers and handlers. The private IDs `0xFA`-`0xFF` and x86-64 BSP-update `0xF0` are distinct from the generic `SC_*` IDs; forced replacement is used only by the Exec scheduler handlers, while the non-forced PM registration preserves an earlier ACPI implementation. Traced failed KBC cold-reset return to the subsequent warm-reset handler in the selected shutdown chain; no separate reset-fallback defect established. `core_SysCallHandler()`'s matching-handler dispatch and user-return generic scheduler branch were checked against the registered custom/system types; no new mismatch found. Other syscall trap-frame/privilege and architecture context-save contracts remain open. No syscall, power transition or hardware behavior was exercised; source-only.

EK824 entry/return-frame and handler-route recheck, promoted from the prior coverage-only candidate (2026-10-20): compared `BUILD_IRQ`/`BUILD_IRQ_ERR` use in both selected PC assembly tables with the CPU-pushed error-code slots and the shared `core_EnterInterrupt`/`core_LeaveInterrupt` frame layout. Vectors 21, 29 and 30 use the no-error wrapper in both variants, so the CPU error value occupies the saved RIP slot; verified that `krnRunExceptionHandlers()` can report a registered exception handled and `cpu_Trap()` then returns to the common restore path. No selected handler for those vectors or feature-enablement path was found. Added EK824 to the detailed report and AROS index, qualifying runtime reachability. No exception or return was induced; source-only.


EK9190 x86-64 interrupted-stack alignment and selected softint caller recheck (2026-10-20): derived `FXSData` placement for a same-ring IRQ from CPU, stub, register-save and XMM-area stack deltas: 24 + 16 + 160 + 72 = 272 bytes, so its modulo-16 alignment equals the interrupted RSP. Traced the maintained `core_ExitInterrupt()` → `core_Cause()` → `SoftIntDispatch()` route; `SoftIntDispatch()` calls `KrnSti()` before its ordinary C callback call. Under the target's 16-byte x86-64 call-site alignment, a callback entry has RSP mod 16 = 8; an IRQ at that entry preserves the same-ring stack and reaches `movaps` with an unaligned destination. The first store raises #GP and the selected unhandled trap path halts. Replaced the prior no-trigger conclusion in the x86-64 assembly row and added EK9190 to the report and index. No interrupt was induced or runtime path exercised; source-only.

x86-64 asynchronous callback XMM-preservation pass (EK9191, 2026-10-20): re-read the complete x86-64 `core_EnterInterrupt`/`core_IRQHandle`/`core_LeaveInterrupt` XMM save path, raw `KrnAddIRQHandler` callback type and documentation, Exec `Interrupt` callback declarations, `AddIntServer` wrapper, and selected x86-64 kernel/Exec compiler flags. Only XMM0-3 are saved/restored on the no-task-switch path; `cpu_intr.c` internally requires handlers to preserve XMM5-15 but leaves XMM4 unaccounted for, while the public APIs describe ordinary C callbacks and do not publish a vector-register preservation rule. General-register-only compilation is applied to kernel and Exec objects, not globally to callback clients. Added EK9191 as a conditional public-contract/state-preservation candidate; no selected in-tree callback was specifically established to clobber XMM4-15, and no callback or interrupt was run. Source-only.

AllocSignal bit-31 and Shell caller reconciliation (EK8800 withdrawn; correction 2026-10-26): a direct-call scan identified the Shell repair loop after synchronous RunCommand as a selected route that can call AllocSignal(31). The expression 1L << 31 is not undefined solely because the signed result is not representable: for 32-bit long, the positive result fits the corresponding unsigned type and conversion to signed is implementation-defined. The generic allocator and selected callers therefore do not establish incorrect mask behavior for supported compilers; EK8800 remains withdrawn and is absent from the detailed report and master index. Invalid signal numbers above 31 remain outside the API contract. No signal, shell command or exhaustion path was run.

SetSignal/SetExcept interaction disposition (former coverage-only EK8940 candidate, rechecked 2026-10-20): the generic `SetSignal` autodoc describes reading/changing the current task's received mask; `SetExcept` separately documents which signals cause task exceptions. `Signal()` explicitly checks the intersection and sets `TF_EXCEPT`/scheduling state, whereas `SetSignal()` only changes the current task's mask. No API text found promises that manually changing the received mask invokes an exception callback, and the selected `SetExcept` callers have no matching nonzero `SetSignal` use. Therefore the absent automatic callback is not established as a defect; retain this only as an API-semantics question, not a finding. No signal or exception was run. Source-only.

WaitPort borrowed-head disposition (former coverage-only EK276 candidate, rechecked 2026-10-20): the API returns a pointer to the current first queued message and explicitly leaves it on the port; `GetMsg()` is the separate dequeue operation. On ExecSMP, WaitPort releases its read lock before returning, so an independently synchronized consumer can remove the message immediately afterward. The checked-in clients inspected use private ports or serialize shared RPC ports, and the API does not promise a stable message reference across concurrent consumers. Without a selected conflicting caller or a contract requiring such lifetime stability, this is caller synchronization rather than an established Exec defect; retain it as an external shared-port contract question, not a finding. No port or message was used. Source-only.

m68kemu keymap-thunk ABI and selected-consumer pass (EK9192 added, 2026-10-20): traced the four selected keymap.library wrappers against `KeyMap` and `KeyMapPacked`, the m68kemu shadow registry, and native `MapRawKey`/console consumers. `SetKeyMapDefault`, `MapRawKey` and `MapANSI` pass guest-layout map fields through `THUNK_PTR` without conversion; `AskKeyMapDefault` returns a native pointer without guest-address mapping. On the selected 64-bit m68kemu hosts, guest `KeyMap` storage is 32 bytes while native storage is 64 bytes, and the shadow table has no `KeyMap` entry. Added EK9192 to the detailed report and index. No guest program, keymap change or keyboard operation was run. Source-only.

m68k ASL requester allocation/use/free thunk lifecycle pass (EK9193 added, 2026-10-20): traced AllocFileRequest/AllocAslRequest through native ASL allocation and the guest D0 return conversion, then followed RequestFile/AslRequest/FreeFileRequest/FreeAslRequest/AbortAslRequest/ActivateAslRequest back through THUNK_PTR. The allocator thunks return native requester pointers without registering guest shadows or handles; paired calls resolve only guest memory or registered shadows. NULL/unrecognized RequestFile fails through AslRequest, and FreeAslRequest returns without freeing when passed NULL. Added EK9193 to detailed report and index. The FileRequester layout descriptor exists but the allocation thunk does not register it; generic requester types require a mapped handle as well. No requester was allocated or opened. Source-only.

m68k Commodities object-handle and pointer-argument pass (EK9194/EK9195 added, 2026-10-20): traced the registered CreateCxObj thunk through m68k D0 return narrowing, then followed CxObj use/delete calls through THUNK_PTR and confirmed the shadow table has no CxObj descriptor or per-object registration. Native DeleteCxObj(NULL) is a no-op and CxObjType(NULL) returns CX_INVALID. Separately compared CreateCxObj's public pointer-bearing macros with its type dispatch: the thunk passes raw guest arg1/arg2 values, while native CX_FILTER/SEND/SIGNAL/TRANSLATE/CUSTOM stores or dereferences them as host pointers (CX_CUSTOM later invokes the callback). Added separate EK9194 (returned-object handle mapping) and EK9195 (pointer arguments/callback ABI) entries. No guest program, object or input event was run. Source-only.

CxBroker NewBroker ABI follow-up (2026-10-20; later filed under EK9893): traced the generated CxBroker thunk through `THUNK_PTR` into native `CxBroker`/`BrokerFunc`. The shadow descriptor records m68k NewBroker size 26 and native size 56 with pointer fields at different offsets, but the thunk does not create/use that shadow or marshal its nested strings and port; native broker creation reads them at host offsets. This was initially grouped under EK9195, then split into the dedicated EK9893 finding to keep it distinct from EK9195's `CreateCxObj()` typed-pointer arguments. No broker was created. Source-only.

Utility TagItem thunk lifecycle pass (EK9196 added, 2026-10-20): traced the generated AllocateTagItems/CloneTagItems/FreeTagItems thunks through the 32-bit m68k return path, guest TagItem conversion, and native utility allocator ownership. The two allocator thunks return native pointers without guest shadow/address mapping; FreeTagItems converts its input to a temporary, native FreeTagItems frees that temporary, and the thunk then frees it again. The public API documents those allocation results as the valid inputs to FreeTagItems. Added EK9196 with the selected 64-bit host configuration and conditional guest-client trigger. No guest program or allocator call was run; source-only.

m68k utility FindTagItem result lifetime pass (EK9197 added, 2026-10-20): followed the generated thunk's converted TagItem temporary through native FindTagItem, FreeVec, and shadow_create_by_name. A successful match returns an element pointer inside the temporary; the thunk frees that backing array before shadow_create copies the TagItem fields. Confirmed the selected 64-bit TagItem layout reads native-width ti_Data. Added the conditional matching-tag UAF/stale-result finding. No guest call or allocator reuse was exercised; source-only.

m68k utility TagItem mutator write-back pass (EK9198 added, 2026-10-20): traced MapTags, FilterTagChanges and FilterTagItems from generated thunks through m68k_to_native_taglist to native in-place modifications and temporary cleanup. Confirmed each modified native list is discarded without guest write-back; FilterTagChanges also updates originalList when requested. Added the shared marshalling finding. Guest arrays and utility calls were not run; source-only.

m68k utility NextTagItem vector/generator pass (EK9199 added, 2026-10-20): compared Utility vector offset 48 with the checked-in generated table and manual thunk tables. The generator rejects pointer-to-pointer arguments, no offset-48 thunk is registered, and Moira dispatch returns zero for unimplemented library LVOs without guest cursor write-back. Cross-checked the public function contract for tag traversal. Added the unconditional NULL/unchanged-cursor finding for emulated m68k clients. No guest call was run; source-only.

m68k utility TagItem mutator-family expansion for EK9198 (2026-10-20): rechecked adjacent generated wrappers and added RefreshTagItemClones and ApplyTagChanges after confirming each mutates a converted list and the thunk frees it without guest write-back. Their native contracts copy original tags into a clone and apply changelist ti_Data values into a target list, respectively. EK9198 now names five affected APIs; no guest list or utility API was run. Source-only.

m68k utility Tag[] ABI boundary recheck (2026-10-20; no new EK): checked whether TagInArray/FilterTagItems pass a 32-bit guest tag array to a wider native element type. `utility/tagitem.h` defines `Tag` as ULONG, which remains 32-bit in this ABI, and both thunks resolve the guest array pointer through THUNK_PTR; the suspected element-width mismatch is rejected. Separately expanded EK9197: TagItem shadow serialization treats ti_Data as SF_PTR, so a scalar-valued tag cannot round-trip as a scalar even if its temporary lifetime is fixed. No tag array was processed; source-only.

m68k utility NamedObject lookup/release lifecycle pass (EK9200 added, 2026-10-20): traced AllocNamedObjectA shadow creation, AddNamedObject input resolution, FindNamedObject result, and ReleaseNamedObject input resolution. The generated FindNamedObject thunk returns the native pointer directly; successful named lookup increments no_UseCount, while ReleaseNamedObject accepts only THUNK_PTR-resolved guest addresses. Added the conditional guest-handle/reference-leak finding. No namespace operation was run; source-only.

m68k NamedObjectName string return follow-up to EK9200 (2026-10-20): traced the generated wrapper and native implementation; NamedObjectName returns the native NamedObject node name pointer, which is returned directly through D0 without guest string translation. Expanded EK9200 to include inability to dereference the returned name in guest code. No object name was queried; source-only.

m68k NamedObject shadow destruction pass (EK9201 added, 2026-10-20): paired the generated AllocNamedObjectA shadow_create_by_name path with FreeNamedObject. The free thunk resolves and frees the native object but never removes the guest mapping or returns the shadow allocation to the emulated heap; native FreeNamedObject deallocates the object itself. Added the normal allocation/free lifecycle stale-shadow and guest-heap leak finding. No NamedObject was allocated or freed; source-only.

m68k RemNamedObject message-ABI pass (EK9202 added, 2026-10-20): followed the generated message argument through THUNK_PTR into RemNamedObject and its deferred/immediate ReplyMsg paths. Compared the 20-byte guest Message layout and field offsets with the selected 48-byte native layout; native ln_Name and mn_ReplyPort access uses differing offsets. Added the conditional guest-resident message marshalling finding. No message or object operation was run; source-only.

m68k UnpackStructureTags output-width pass (EK9203 added, 2026-10-20): traced the generated taglist converter into native UnpackStructureTags and its supported pack-type stores. Guest output pointers become direct host pointers, and native code stores IPTR (eight bytes on selected 64-bit hosts) into guest m68k four-byte IPTR slots. Added the conditional adjacent-word overwrite finding. No pack operation or guest buffer was run; source-only.

m68k Pack/UnpackStructureTags paired-output boundary check (2026-10-20; EK9203 retained, no new finding): confirmed PackStructureTags reads converted TagItem data and writes the caller-provided pack buffer at pack-table byte offsets; it does not mutate the TagItem array, so it is not an additional EK9198 write-back case. UnpackStructureTags writes through ti_Data as native IPTR and remains EK9203. Provenance/compatibility of every m68k pack-table encoding and full pack-buffer layout semantics remain open; no packing operation was run. Source-only.

m68k formatted-output caller expansion for EK9173 (2026-10-20): traced generated Utility VSNPrintf through the native VSNPrintf implementation into RawDoFmt, confirming that it shares m68k_to_native_fmt_stream and the untranslated `%b` BSTR branch already found on DOS VPrintf/VFPrintf. Expanded report and index trigger/API scope. No format call was run; source-only.

m68k manual RawDoFmt callback-contract pass (EK9204 added, 2026-10-20): compared thunk A2/A3 handling with the public RAWFMTFUNC_COUNT/STRING/SERIAL contract and native PutCh dispatch. The thunk ignores A2 and unconditionally memcpy-copies its rendered buffer to non-NULL A3; count mode therefore overwrites its ULONG counter for output of four or more bytes, while serial/custom callbacks are not invoked. Added the conditional guest-memory corruption and missing-callback finding. No formatting or callback was run; source-only.

m68k manual RawDoFmt output-boundary pass (EK9205 added, 2026-10-20): reviewed the 1024-byte local buffer and each snprintf call. The thunk advances its output pointer by snprintf return values (required length), not the bounded bytes stored, then writes a terminator and uses the pointer difference for a later copy. A field/output exceeding remaining capacity therefore leaves the buffer and drives out-of-bounds pointer use. Added the conditional formatter size bug. No format was run; source-only.

m68k formatted-output `%i` width pass (EK9206 added, 2026-10-20): compared the shared converter parser with native RawDoFmt size-modifier handling. The converter parses `l` but not `i`, and its fallback copies a guest ULONG (four bytes); native `%i` fetches IPTR/SIPTR (eight bytes on selected 64-bit hosts). This sign-extends incorrectly for negative `%id` values and misaligns subsequent mixed-width arguments. The converter is used by DOS formatted-output and Utility VSNPrintf thunks. Added the conditional format ABI finding; no output was run. Source-only.

m68k locale FormatString return-cursor and Hook ABI pass (EK9207/EK9208 added, 2026-10-20): traced the generated locale thunk through converted argument stream, native InternalFormatString result, temporary cleanup and D0 narrowing. No-argument templates convert to NULL and return NULL; argument-bearing templates return a pointer into the freed temporary rather than the guest stream cursor. Compared the guest 20-byte and native 40-byte Hook layouts and followed native h_Entry invocation; added separate cursor-lifetime and Hook/callback ABI findings. Checked the selected locale API contract and checked-in tests; no guest call or callback was run. Source-only.

m68k locale positional-format argument-mapping pass (EK9209 added, 2026-10-20): compared the sequential m68k_to_native_fmt_stream parser with native locale FormatString indexStream/ARG lookup and GetDataStreamFromFormat positional parsing. The thunk ignores `%n$`, consumes arguments in textual occurrence order, and does not convert `%s` pointers in the fallback path; checked-in locale tests include reordered positional strings/numbers. Added the conditional wrong-argument/pointer finding. No format was run; source-only.

m68k locale Hook caller expansion for EK9208 (2026-10-20): checked the adjacent generated FormatDate thunk and native `_WriteChar` path. It also passes the guest Hook address via THUNK_PTR and invokes `hook->h_Entry` for emitted characters, so the 20-byte/40-byte offset mismatch and lack of guest-call trampoline apply to both FormatDate and FormatString. Expanded report/index trigger and caller scope. No date formatting or hook was run; source-only.

m68k locale object and string pointer lifecycle pass (EK9210/EK9211 added, 2026-10-20): traced OpenLocale/OpenCatalogA return paths to CloseLocale/CloseCatalog and locale-operation THUNK_PTR resolvers; confirmed no shadow creation despite generated Locale/Catalog layouts. Separately traced GetLocaleStr/GetCatalogStr native string returns through D0 narrowing, including GetCatalogStr(NULL, ..., guest default) after input string translation. Added object-handle/lifetime and string-result mapping findings. No locale object or string lookup was run; source-only.

m68k ParseDate Hook caller expansion for EK9208 (2026-10-20): traced the generated ParseDate thunk and native GetChar macro/call sites. It resolves the guest Hook as raw bytes and invokes its h_Entry for input characters, so the same Hook field offset mismatch and missing m68k callback trampoline apply. Expanded EK9208 to FormatDate, FormatString and ParseDate. No input stream or callback was run; source-only.

m68k locale generated-vector slice recheck (2026-10-20; EK9207-EK9211 retained): read the complete locale.library generated thunk block and its 25-entry dispatch table in `rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:6553-6770,7956-7984`. Classified each wrapper's register arguments and conversions, then rechecked native pointers, returned pointers, Hook arguments, DateStamp layout, string/buffer arguments, and temporary cleanup against the referenced API bodies and shadow layouts. The existing findings remain specific to FormatString's converted cursor/arguments, raw Hooks, OpenLocale/OpenCatalog handles, and GetLocaleStr/GetCatalogStr results. The remaining wrappers examined here mostly pass scalar values or fixed-layout DateStamp/buffer pointers; this does not establish correctness of their native APIs or of external m68k callers. The block comment says “34 thunks” while its generated count and dispatch table contain 25; treated as stale generated commentary with no runtime consequence. This is a partial-file slice, not full-body credit for the 8,000-line generated unit. No m68k call was run; source-only.

m68k TagItem bridge control-tag caller pass (EK9212/EK9213 added, 2026-10-20): rechecked `m68k_to_native_taglist()` against the public TAG_MORE/TAG_SKIP definitions and `LibNextTagItem()` traversal, then traced the generated Utility `FindTagItem()` vector through `LibFindTagItem()` to the shared iterator. The bridge translates TAG_MORE's data to a host pointer but leaves the continued array in guest 8-byte layout, while native 64-bit iteration advances through 16-byte TagItems; its contiguous sizing pass also ignores TAG_MORE termination. Separately, the pointer-range heuristic translates TAG_SKIP's numeric count when it is at least 0x100 and less than guest memory size, after which the native iterator uses that translated value as a count. Added EK9212 and EK9213 to the detailed report/index. Reconfirmed EK9197's FindTagItem free-before-shadow-copy issue during the same trace; no guest tag list was executed. Source-only.

m68k Utility TagItem ownership findings recheck (EK9196-EK9199 retained, 2026-10-20): matched generated vector offsets against `rom/utility/utility.conf` and traced allocation, clone, free, find, mutation, and iterator wrappers to the native utility implementations. Confirmed AllocateTagItems/CloneTagItems return native allocations without guest mappings, FreeTagItems frees the converted temporary in the native routine and then frees it again in the wrapper, FindTagItem frees the array before shadow-copying its returned element, five mutator wrappers discard native-side changes, and NextTagItem has no generated vector entry despite its declared vector. These are already covered by EK9196-EK9199; this pass made no duplicate finding. No utility API or allocation was run; source-only.

m68k scalar TagItem consumer trace for EK9213 (2026-10-20): traced the same pointer-range conversion through the generated `NewCreateTaskA()` wrapper and native `TASKTAG_STACKSIZE` handling. The thunk's converted `ti_Data` reaches native `NewCreateTaskA()` as a host pointer; the callee casts it to ULONG, aligns it, applies the platform minimum, and uses the resulting length in `NewAllocEntry()`. Expanded EK9213 beyond the long-count TAG_SKIP case to include this selected scalar-tag consumer; the actual size depends on the host address's low 32 bits and allocation limits. No task was created; source-only.

m68k NewCreateTaskA guest-entry and return-handle trace (EK8899 detailed; EK9215 added, 2026-10-21): followed the generated `NewCreateTaskA()` thunk through tag conversion, native `NewCreateTaskA()`/`NewAddTask()`, and selected x86-64 `PrepareContext()`. `TASKTAG_PC` becomes a pointer into guest arena memory and is installed directly into the native context's `rip`; the Moira execution loop is used only by `M68KEmu_Execute()` and is not entered by this task path. Separately, the thunk returns the native Task pointer without creating the Task shadow used by `FindTaskByPID`; the dispatcher narrows it to guest D0 and paired `Signal()` resolves only shadows or guest-arena addresses. Added the detailed EK8899 entry and EK9215 return-handle finding. No task was created or dispatched; source-only.

Parthenope fixed-buffer/no-capacity report reconciliation (EK532 detailed report/index restored, 2026-10-21): rechecked the `boot_dev_t.load_file` signature against the selected CD, DOS and ext2 full-file copy paths and Parthenope kernel/menu/initrd/module call buffers. Parthenope SUSP iterator read-error cleanup pass (EK9221, 2026-10-21): traced the initial SUA allocation/read and CE replacement allocation/read exits through `get_entry()` and the constructor caller. Both failed-read returns leak their currently allocated buffer; `get_entry()` discards the error result and returns NULL, so the constructor proceeds. Parthenope CD lookup allocation-failure pass (EK9225, 2026-10-21): traced the requested-path copy and per-directory-entry name allocation through `fs_cdrom_find_file()`, `fs_cdrom_load_file()`, and the selected kernel/menu/initrd/module callers. DOS InternalFlush flag serialization/caller recheck (EK9226, 2026-10-21): read the complete flush loop alongside `Write`, `Flush`, `Seek`, `FWriteChars`, ExecSMP semantics, and `CreateNewProc` output-handle setup (`rom/dos/internalflush.c:25-82`; `write.c:59-73`; `flush.c:56-86`; `seek.c:71-91`; `fwrite.c:94-178`; `createnewproc.c:344-352,434-437`). `FHF_FLUSHING` is checked and then set with no atomic primitive or handle lock. Two tasks sharing a write-mode FileHandle can both observe it clear before either sets it, snapshot the same `fh_Pos`, and issue duplicate `ACTION_WRITE` payloads. If one call resets `fh_Pos` first, the other can take its concurrent-data branch, subtract its old positive snapshot from zero, and leave a negative (32-bit) or wrapped (64-bit) cursor used by `FWriteChars` as a buffer index (`internalflush.c:57-78`; `fwrite.c:150-164`; `dosextens.h:293-335`). The output BPTR supplied via NP_Output is assigned directly, and the selected animation datatype gives Output() to two asynchronous child processes, although no overlapping flush from those children is established. Added conditional EK9226. Existing zero-progress EK8841 and failed-flush propagation EK8840/EK8884 are separate. No shared handle, handler write, or task interleaving was run; source-only.

Parthenope CD scan/block-size contract follow-up (2026-10-21; no new EK): traced `get_dev()` through the `context.c` wrappers and `context.h`; `start_unit_scan`, `next_unit_scan`, `end_unit_scan`, and `end_global_scan` are supplied callbacks, and their implementations are not present in the checked-in Parthenope subtree. The same start/advance/end pattern is used by `rdb.c`, but that does not prove callback lifecycle semantics. `get_dev()` receives a scan `blocksize` and the descriptor carries `blksz`, while `cdrom_read()` uses fixed 2048-byte ISO blocks; no selected producer or supported non-2048 CD descriptor was found in this subtree, so no block-size defect is promoted. m68k Hunk premature-EOF caller pass (EK9229, 2026-10-21): traced the full-record loop in `M68KEmu_LoadHunksFromMemory()` through its success return to the selected disk `RunFile()` entry check and `setup_and_execute()` call. EOF before all declared hunks reach `HUNK_END` exits the loop without taking the parser failure label, so a nonzero first-hunk address is returned and executed. Added EK9229, distinct from EK9157 payload/header-size mismatch and EK9164 unsupported relocation records. No Hunk file or guest program was loaded; other malformed-record arithmetic and the linked-SegList loader remain open. Source-only.

m68k Hunk resident-name length arithmetic pass (EK9230 later withdrawn; historical note, 2026-10-21): checked the 32-bit `ULONG` width and the resident-name skip loop, then traced `M68KEmu_LoadHunksFromMemory()` from both `RunFile()` and disk `OpenLibrary()` fallback callers. The contemporaneous interpretation was that a nonzero `n` of `0x40000000` made `n * 4` wrap to zero and stall on the same field; this was later withdrawn after accounting for `rd32(&p)` advancing before the multiplication. No malformed file or guest program was loaded; other Hunk arithmetic and record-validation paths remain open. Source-only.

m68k runner argument-size arithmetic pass (EK9231, 2026-10-21): traced the public RunHunk/RunFile `ULONG argSize` inputs and DOS command-line callers through `setup_and_execute()` into the guest allocator and `m68k_to_host()`. Added EK9231, qualified because checked DOS callers do not establish such a large source buffer; no buffer or runner call was used. Synchronous process and external caller contracts remain open. Source-only.

m68k containment-accessor wrap and thunk caller pass (EK9232, 2026-10-21): traced `m68k_read32()`'s `addr + 3` check against the 32-bit `ULONG` type and fixed 32 MiB guest arena, then followed selected generated tag-list thunks into `m68k_to_native_taglist()` and its first read. PC bootstrap kick ABI and first-start consumer cross-check (2026-10-21; no new EK): traced `bootstrap.c`'s `LoadKernel()` result into `kick(kentry, km)` against both selected PC bootstrap overrides and the x86-64 startup consumer. The i386 `kick()` directly calls the loaded entry with `(km, AROS_BOOT_MAGIC)` (`arch/i386-pc/bootstrap/cpu.c:10-15`); the selected x86-64 version enables long mode and far-jumps with `km` in RDI and the magic in RSI, matching `start64(struct TagItem *, ULONG)` (`arch/x86_64-pc/bootstrap/cpu.c:202-236`; `arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/kernel_startup.c:94-101`). `start64()` gates the magic before `core_Kick()` and `boot_start()` forwards the tag list into `kernel_cstart()` (`kernel_startup.c:94-134,194-223`). No signature, argument-register or first-call mismatch was established. The x86-64 path's unsupported-CPU return reaches the bootstrap's subsequent panic/halt. Bootloader-provided tag extents, memory-map validation, and all later tag-data relocation remain separate open checks. No boot or CPU transition was run; source-only.


FindTask false-negative target matrix and EK799 scope qualification (2026-10-21): compared all `ENABLE_EXECSMP` assignments in `configure.in` with selected PC and Raspberry Pi scheduler transitions and network package edges. ExecSMP is enabled for x86-64 PC and Raspberry Pi `smp` variants only; PC and ARM32/AArch64 Pi schedulers use independently acquired source/destination list locks. The RTL816x/PCNet32/RTL8139 teardown callers belong to the PC plug-in-card aggregate, which the Raspberry Pi package excludes in favor of SoC/USB drivers. No target was built and no task transition was run; source-only.


PC KrnExitInterrupt caller and context-exit pass (2026-10-21; no new EK): followed the public wrapper into both selected x86 assembly `core_LeaveInterrupt` exits, the common exception dispatcher, and every checked direct caller. The sole direct caller is optional `HVExceptionHandler`, which registers for exception 2 and passes the original context received from `krnRunExceptionHandlers` to `KrnExitInterrupt` when the debug prompt exits (`arch/all-pc/debug/hyperv/hyperv-debug.c:17,185-250`; `rom/kernel/addexceptionhandler.c:131-189`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/cpu_traps.c:94-99`). Assembly consumes the frame and IRETs, so it does not return to `core_IRQHandle`'s normal `PLATFORMF_INEXCPT` clear (`cpu_intr.c:416,485`; x86-64 `core_interrupts.s:146-197`; i386 `core_interrupts.s:159-165`). The stale exception bit is copied into `kb_LastState` on the next entry, but the only checked reader `KrnFmtAlertInfo` branches on `PLATFORMF_INIRQ`, not the exception bit (`fmtalertinfo.c:54-59`); no current concrete behavioral consequence is established. Recorded the context/lifecycle detail in the file row, with no new finding. No exception or debug prompt was run. Source-only.
FindCliProc/Status semaphore-release scheduling recheck (EK840 retained, caller trace strengthened, 2026-10-21): checked the Status command's outer exclusive `rn_RootLock`, local `Forbid`, nested `FindCliProc()` shared acquire, and release order (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Status.c:154-166`; `rom/dos/findcliproc.c:52-68`). Exec's `InternalObtainSemaphore()` explicitly treats reacquisition by the same owner as nesting (`rom/exec/semaphores.c:109-112`), so the shared lookup does not deadlock under the outer exclusive lock. After Status executes `Permit()` and then releases the outer root lock, a process already waiting in `removefromrootnode()` can be signaled by `ReleaseSemaphore()`; its final `Permit()` may schedule the waiter (`rom/exec/releasesemaphore.c:164-177,207-212`; `rom/exec/permit.c:81-103`). That process removes/frees its CLIInfo under the root lock and then `RemTask()` reclaims task storage (`rom/dos/rootnode.c:121-135`; `rom/exec/remtask.c:115-128,165-181`) before Status dereferences the borrowed pointer in `printProcess()` (`Status.c:199-224`). This confirms the selected single-CPU lifetime window in EK840; no separate finding or wider `FindCliProc` caller was established. No command, task exit or scheduler interleaving was run. Source-only.

PC bootstrap memory-backed ELF callbacks and module extent pass (EK343 retained, no new finding): read all 41 physical lines (23 `cloc 2.06` C code lines) of `arch/all-pc/bootstrap/memory_io.c`, verified its all-PC bootstrap manifest selection, and enumerated every callback reference in the shared `bootstrap/elfloader.c`. `GetKernelSize()` consumes the callbacks to read the ELF header and section table; `LoadKernel()` reads allocated section data and relocation tables. `AddModule()` receives the Multiboot start/end pair for raw ELF modules but saves only the starting pointer in `ELFNode.eh`; package member discovery performs range checks within the package, then stores the resulting data pointer without its member extent. RISC-V OpenSBI syscall-ID/exception fallthrough pass (EK9238 added, 2026-10-21): followed the `ebreak` classifier through the active `kernel_traps.c` target, saved `a7` register slot, shared `core_SysCall()` dispatcher, and ordinary breakpoint exception fallback (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_traps.c:27-32,170-177,224-258`; `kernel_cpu.h:49-61`; `rom/kernel/kernel_intr.c:61-81`; shared ID table `rom/kernel/kernel_syscall.h:15-30`). `SC_MAX=0x100` admits reserved syscall numbers, while the generic dispatcher handles only IDs 0-3. An ordinary breakpoint with `a7=SC_CLI` (4) is therefore stepped over without exception dispatch. Added EK9238 and its AROS index entry. No trap was executed; no ordinary in-tree `ebreak` caller was found. Source-only.


RISC-V OpenSBI fatal-trap diagnostic guard pass (2026-10-21; EK9238 retained, no new EK): traced the instruction-fetch classification macro through `krnTrapDispatch()`'s exception reporting and code-byte dump (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_traps.c:94-121,152-188,190-314`). The code dump reads `sepc` surroundings without an address probe, but it is explicitly skipped for instruction-address misaligned/access/page faults (`SCAUSE_IS_IFETCH`: causes 0, 1, 12; `:94-95,306-308`), where `sepc` may be unreadable. Data-fault diagnostics can still fail if surrounding instruction bytes are inaccessible, but the reviewed source does not establish a routine selected path or a separate functional consequence beyond an already-fatal trap, so no new finding was added. The nested handler halts on an unhandled secondary fault rather than returning to the failed read (`:255-312`). No trap or diagnostic was run. Source-only.

Architecture syscall-ID/dispatcher cross-check (EK9238 retained, no additional finding; 2026-10-21): enumerated generic `SC_*` definitions and every selected `case SC_*` dispatcher found in the architecture source (`rom/kernel/kernel_syscall.h:15-30`; `rom/kernel/kernel_intr.c:61-81`; `arch/arm-native/kernel/syscall.c:169-241`; `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/syscall.c:180-280`; `arch/ppc-sam440/kernel/kernel_cpu.h:27-28` and `syscall.c:60-120`; `arch/ppc-chrp/efika/kernel/syscall.h:4-14` and `syscall.c:30-95`; `arch/all-mingw32/kernel/kernel_intr.c:114-128`; `arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_traps.c:32,224-258`). The platform handlers have distinct supported subsets and the reviewed callers use their corresponding architectural helpers; no extra missing-case consequence was established in these selected paths. The OpenSBI breakpoint gate remains the concrete mismatch: it admits every a7 value through `SC_MAX` (0x100), advances PC and returns `TRAP_SYSCALL`, while generic `core_SysCall()` handles only IDs 0-3, so an in-range unsupported code such as `SC_CLI` is consumed without executing its service or reaching the normal breakpoint exception route (EK9238). This cross-check does not establish that ordinary non-scheduler syscall IDs are called on OpenSBI, nor does it cover indirect binary callers or all architecture builds. No syscall, trap or target was run; source-only.

DOS `Flush()` direct-caller result-handling slice (EK9239 added, 2026-10-21): traced the standard C `ftell()` caller through `Flush()`, `InternalFlush()`, the current-position query, and the selected RAM handler (`compiler/crt/stdc/ftell.c:54-66`; `compiler/crt/stdc/__stdcio_dos64.c:65-72`; `rom/dos/flush.c:53-71`; `rom/dos/internalflush.c:38-51`; `rom/filesys/ram/handler.c:188-190; rom/filesys/ram/commands.c:703-774`). `ftell()` ignores a failed Flush, then a successful Seek/current-position query can return the underlying position; the failed `InternalFlush()` has also cleared `FHF_WRITE`, so buffered output is not retried by Close. Added EK9239 for the standard C implementation, conditional on handler write failure. The POSIXC `ftell()` implementation has the same unchecked Flush-then-query behavior; the 2026-10-21 caller pass extends EK9239 to both implementations. `fflush()` and `fsync()` callers checked in this slice propagate DOS Flush failure; `fseeko()`'s hole-filling path was subsequently audited; see the candidate-withdrawal entry below. No I/O failure was induced; source-only.

POSIXC file-position caller continuation (EK9239 extended; no additional finding, 2026-10-21): traced both standard C and POSIXC `ftell()` through their unchecked `Flush()` and position-query helpers (`compiler/crt/stdc/ftell.c:54-66`; `compiler/crt/posixc/ftell.c:61-78`; `compiler/crt/stdc/__stdcio_dos64.c:65-72`; `compiler/crt/posixc/__dos64.c:70-87`). Both can report a successful underlying position after `InternalFlush()` has failed and cleared `FHF_WRITE`; EK9239 now covers both. Continued into `__fseeko64()` and its `fseek`, `fseeko`, `fseeko64` and `fsetpos64` wrappers (`compiler/crt/posixc/__fseeko.c:26-152`; `fseek.c:62-65`; `fseeko.c:63`; `fseeko64.c:58`; `fsetpos64.c:53-60`). The hole-fill loop ignores `FWrite()` counts and final `Flush()`, but selected-handler checks show the final seek fails when the extension remains incomplete; no finding added. `fflush()` and `fsync()` remain correctly propagating in the checked slice. Broader filesystem short-write contracts and other POSIXC file-position callers remain open. No I/O was run; source-only.

POSIXC fseeko hole-fill error candidate withdrawn (2026-10-21): the shared engine does ignore `FWrite()`/`Flush()` results while extending a file (`compiler/crt/posixc/__fseeko.c:98-119`), but the selected RAM, SFS and NTFS handlers reject the final seek when the failed/short zero-fill leaves the target beyond EOF (`rom/filesys/ram/commands.c:728-739`; `rom/filesys/SFS/FS/filesystemmain.c:2034-2044`; `workbench/fs/ntfs/packet.c:338-353`). Their caller therefore receives a failed final seek, not the successful return asserted by the provisional EK9240. A write error can be replaced by the final seek error and a partial extension may remain, but the reviewed source does not establish that partial side effect as a distinct contract violation. Removed EK9240 from the detailed report and index; no finding retained. Source-only.

POSIXC ftruncate shared-offset concurrency pass (EK9241 added, 2026-10-21): read both `ftruncate()` variants and traced their save-size-change-restore calls through the individually locked 64-bit helpers (`compiler/crt/posixc/ftruncate.c:62-117`; `ftruncate64.c:62-117`; `__dos64.c:56-172`). Confirmed `dup2()` shares the same FCB across descriptors and `lseek()` uses the same per-operation FCB lock (`dup2.c:108-131`; `lseek.c:64-100`; `__fdesc.h:37-38`). Because the wrappers release that lock between the saved-position read, size operations and final restore, an overlapping seek can return Q and then have its shared position overwritten by ftruncate's earlier P. Added EK9241. Filesystem resizing and lock/unlock behavior beyond the offset contract remain open; no concurrent call was run. Source-only.

EK9242 RAMFS request-boundary recheck (2026-10-21; no new finding): confirmed the trigger crosses distinct handler transactions rather than an assumed mid-packet race. Each `__dos64_setfilesize()` call locks the FCB only for its `SetFileSize64`/`SetFileSize` request, then releases it before ftruncate's seek and buffered zero writes (`compiler/crt/posixc/__dos64.c:116-137`; `ftruncate.c:81-114`). RAMFS `CmdSetProtect()` resolves the object and changes `protection` without consulting its live opening list (`rom/filesys/ram/commands.c:1731-1761`); the later `CmdWrite()` tests that property and returns `ERROR_WRITE_PROTECTED` (`:637-670`). `InternalFlush()` clears `FHF_WRITE` on negative Write and returns FALSE (`rom/dos/internalflush.c:35-54`), which ftruncate ignores. This confirms the conditional sequence and false-success consequence; the protection change must still occur between extension and flush. No DOS operation or interleaving was run. Source-only.


POSIXC ftruncate RAMFS position-preservation caller pass (EK9244 added, 2026-10-21): traced the pre-resize `__dos64_getpos()` and unchecked post-resize `__dos64_seek(oldpos)` in both wrappers (`compiler/crt/posixc/ftruncate.c:78-79,110-114`; identical `ftruncate64.c`). RAMFS `ChangeFileSize()` iterates every opening and clamps positions greater than the new file length (`rom/filesys/ram/filesystem.c:747-756`); RAMFS `CmdSeek()` rejects positions beyond EOF (`rom/filesys/ram/commands.c:725-739`). Thus a 100-byte file positioned at 80 and truncated to 50 leaves the position at 50 after the attempted restore to 80 fails, while the wrapper returns success. Added EK9244 and index entry. No file operation was run. Source-only.

AArch64 Raspberry Pi bootstrap MMU caller and TLSF range follow-through (EK9245 added, 2026-10-21): read the full selected `mmu_map_section()` and `mmu_unmap_section()` paths against every boot caller in `boot.c` and `vc_fb.c`. `mmu_map_section()` chooses the low PMD path when the tuple begins below 4 GiB; `mmu_slot()` then returns NULL for blocks at/above 4 GiB, silently skipping the upper portion. `query_memory()` still emits the original tuple bounds, and AArch64 `kernel_cstart()` passes that full range to `krnCreateTLSFMemHeader()`; `tlsf_add_memory()` writes a terminal boundary header near the range end. This supports a conditional boot-failure candidate for a single `/memory/reg` tuple crossing 4 GiB. Separate firmware tuples starting at/above 4 GiB take the high PUD path; the checked source comment says Pi 4 firmware emits separate ranges above its first GiB, but no checked-in DTB proves Pi 5 or other supplied firmware uses a crossing tuple. Added EK9245 with that platform-data qualification. No FDT was loaded or booted. Source-only.

Shell source scope expansion and `readLine()` boundary/caller pass (EK9247 added, 2026-10-21): reconciled `workbench/c/Shell/mmakefile.src`'s `FILES` with the Exec/Kernel source inventory. Read the complete `buffer.c` and `readLine.c` bodies and the selected `interact()` call path (`Shell.c:73-197`; `readLine.c:52-138`; `state.h:11-12`). `interact()` reserves `LINE_MAX+1` bytes before `readLine()`, so the latter's direct input writes and ignored `bufferAppend()` return are safe for ordinary bounded lines; no allocation-failure defect was established there. At `i == LINE_MAX`, however, `readLine()` returns before draining the physical line or setting `moreLeft`. `interact()` leaves its previous value intact and uses it to select continue versus end-of-input handling, yielding suffix-as-command after a prior successful read or premature stream completion when false. Added EK9247 and its index entry. `buffer.h`, `Shell.h`, and `state.h` definitions were also read. The manifest's other selected source files remain explicitly unreviewed in the supplemental inventory below; `shell_init.c` is selected by the `kernel-shell` module target.

Shell alias argument splice in backtick commands (EK9250, 2026-10-21): read all of `convertLine.c` and traced `checkLine()`/`convertBackTicks()` input into the selected alias path. `convertBackTicks()` builds its embedded command by copying bytes between backticks and does not append a newline before calling `checkLine()` (`workbench/c/Shell/convertBackTicks.c:36-49,88-92`). `readCommandR()` parses the command token with `ReadItem()`; its documented separator behavior leaves the cursor at the first argument, then alias expansion copies `in->len - in->cur - 1` bytes on the assumption the last byte is a newline (`convertLine.c:131-139,149-165,202-206`; `rom/dos/readitem.c:55-64,112-123`). The newline is only appended later in `convertLine()` after alias expansion (`convertLine.c:321-332`). Thus an embedded alias with an argument drops the argument's last character; e.g. alias `say` = `Echo []` invoked as `` `say hello` `` splices `hell` into the alias command. Copy the full remaining range when the source has no newline, or normalize embedded input before alias expansion. **Affected configuration and trigger:** selected Shell targets using a local alias with `[]` argument substitution in a backtick command that supplies a final argument byte. No alias or command was run. **Confidence:** high for the no-newline embedded input, `ReadItem()` cursor, unconditional one-byte subtraction, and later newline append; consequence depends on alias invocation with trailing arguments. Source-only.

`WaitPort()` caller recheck (2026-10-21): traced the e1000 `e1ksm_SyncPort` handshake in `workbench/devs/networks/e1000/unit.c:512-560,1032-1048`. Exec Enqueue PC ACPI caller pass (2026-10-21; no new EK): traced `ACPI_APIC_SUPPORT()` and `ACPI_IOAPIC_SUPPORT()` hook registration into `acpi.c`'s live `ForeachNode()` traversal and each count hook's insertion of lower-priority parse hooks (`arch/all-pc/kernel/acpi_apic.c:270-340`; `acpi_ioapic.c:1088-1202`; `acpi.c:187-236`; `compiler/include/exec/lists.h:195-202`; `rom/exec/enqueue.c:67-97`). The count hooks insert only after the current node because each new priority is lower; `ForeachNode` reads the current node's successor after the callback, so it sees the new hooks and processes them in order. The `acpi_apicCnt`/`acpi_ioapicCnt` guards limit each count callback to one parser-hook registration pass. No duplicate-node insertion or list skip/corruption established in these selected PC callers. This is a caller-specific pass, not whole-callsite credit; the broad Enqueue caller review remains pending. No ACPI table or list was processed. Source-only.
Exec Enqueue Expansion AddBootNode and DOSBoot MountList reader pass (2026-10-21; no new EK): re-read the complete `Enqueue()` implementation and `AddBootNode()` caller, then traced DOSBoot's MountList readers, bootstrap mutations and DOS initialization flag transition (`rom/exec/enqueue.c:67-97`; `rom/expansion/addbootnode.c:126-220`; `rom/dosboot/dosboot_init.c:97-126,200-278`; `rom/dosboot/bootstrap.c:311-345`; `rom/dos/cliinit.c:449-535`). `AddBootNode()` serializes duplicate scans and pre-DOS insertions with `BootSemaphore`, and its `Forbid()` protects the actual Enqueue; DOSBoot initialization/reordering also holds the semaphore. Selected DOSBoot menu and bootstrap reads include `Forbid()` or occur in the boot task, but some `ListLength()`/menu enumeration regions do not take `BootSemaphore`. On ExecSMP, `Forbid()` is CPU-local, so an asynchronous driver calling AddBootNode during those reads could race. The in-tree DOSBoot `bootscan` caller runs synchronously before menu setup, and NVME's selected AddBootNode call is reached through `StorageController::SetUpBus`; this pass did not establish whether another maintained asynchronous SetUpBus can run during the uncovered readers. Therefore no race is promoted; async caller timing and wider AddBootNode callsite classification remain open. No list operation or device setup was run. Source-only.

AddBootNode caller-context census for DOSBoot MountList readers (2026-10-21; no new EK): repeated a repository-wide direct-call search across C/header/assembly source and traced the storage-controller bus setup path (`rom/hidds/base/storage/storage_controllerclass.c:75-112,281-293`) into selected NVMe, VirtIO, ATA, AHCI/SCSI and SD-card boot-node creation. NVMe's `NVME_Probe` is an `ADD2INITLIB` routine at priority 30 (`rom/devs/nvme/nvme_init.c:73-78,332-336`); these sources establish initialization-time calls but not an asynchronous overlap with DOSBoot. The selected USB mass-storage volume paths also call `AddBootNode` (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/partitions.c:273-274`; `workbench/devs/USB/classes/MassStorage/storage_volumes.c:274-275,510`) and can be reached through device-volume discovery, but this source check did not establish whether those tasks can run during `dosboot_init.c`'s unprotected `ListLength()`/menu enumeration or `bootstrap.c`'s initial list count. The list read paths remain unlocked while `AddBootNode()` uses `BootSemaphore`; selected DOSBoot boot-scan/reordering paths do hold the semaphore, and `Forbid()` alone is CPU-local on ExecSMP. Retain the existing conditional race note; no selected overlapping schedule is proven, so no EK finding is added or weakened. No device enumeration or boot was run; source-only.

Exec Amiga chipset-helper and selected-caller pass (2026-10-21; no new EK): re-read `rom/exec/chipset.h` against its complete in-tree callsite census: `AddIntServer`, `RemIntServer`, `Cause`, and `Reschedule`. `AddIntServer`/`RemIntServer` call enable/disable under the Exec interrupt-list write lock with local interrupts disabled, and disable occurs after list removal; the header's sentinel check matches the standard empty-list representation. The hardware limit `INTB_INTEN == 14` bounds both shift expressions to bits 0–13. Cause/Reschedule only acknowledge or cause the software interrupt bit 2. Updated the header row to replace the open caller note with this finite caller pass. No hardware register was accessed; external clients and target hardware behavior remain open. Source-only.


Exec signal-semaphore shared-state access pass (2026-10-21; no new EK): searched every occurrence of `ss_QueueCount`, `ss_NestCount`, `ss_Owner`, `ss_WaitQueue`, and `SEM_LOCK` in `rom/exec`, then checked initialization, exclusive/shared obtain and attempt, release, Procure/Vacate, and ObtainSemaphoreList paths. Each mutation is under the same per-semaphore SMP spinlock, including Procure's message-to-request queue publication and Vacate's cancellation/delegated release. The ObtainSemaphoreList owner read is locked; its debug-only final check runs only after this task owns each semaphore. `CheckSemaphore`'s unlocked `mlh_Tail` validation compares the invariant NULL tail field of the MinList, not its concurrently mutable head/tail-predecessor links. Updated the semaphore definitions row; this closes only Exec-internal state-access reconciliation, not public callers or ownership contracts. No semaphore contention was run. Source-only.


SC_SCHEDULE backend and configuration recheck (no new EK, 2026-10-21): traced the generic `core_SysCall()` branch and selected Unix, MinGW and Efika handlers (`rom/kernel/kernel_intr.c:69-80`; `arch/all-unix/kernel/kernel_intr.c:41-87`; `arch/all-mingw32/kernel/kernel_intr.c:105-123`; `arch/ppc-chrp/efika/kernel/syscall.c:67`). PC IRQ callback/removal caller census recheck (EK31/EK9263 retained; no new EK, 2026-10-21): searched all selected PC and maintained C/header IRQ-removal call sites, then separated callbacks from ordinary teardown/reset callbacks (`arch/all-pc/timer/timer_init.c:34-103,164-166,221-224`; i8042 callers at `i8042_mouseps2.c:219-224`, `i8042_mouseclass.c:94-102`, and `i8042_kbdclass.c:335-345`). Sashimi duplicate-resource ordering and target-edge recheck (EK846 retained, 2026-10-21): re-read `AddSashimiResource()` and `OpenSashimiResource()` alongside Exec `AddResource()`, `OpenResource()`, `Enqueue()` and the `workbench-complete` virtual-target chain (`developer/debug/sashimi/sashimi.c:427-493,506-535`; `rom/exec/{addresource,openresource,enqueue}.c`; `workbench/mmakefile.src:9-25`; `developer/debug/mmakefile.src:6`; `developer/debug/sashimi/mmakefile.src:5-11`; MetaMake virtual dependency handling `tools/MetaMake/dirnode.c:175-197,272-279`). The `Forbid()` around Sashimi's lookup/add is local on ExecSMP; Exec's writer lock serializes each `Enqueue()` but `AddResource()` performs no duplicate-name check. The zero-initialized Sashimi node has equal priority to an existing instance, so `Enqueue()` places the later node after equal-priority entries and `FindName()` continues to return the first duplicate until it is removed. This confirms the source-level duplicate publication and lookup-switch consequence already documented in EK846; no new issue or line credit. Sashimi is selected by the active `workbench-complete` virtual dependency, while running two instances is the required trigger. No tool or concurrent start was run; source-only.

m68k Exec AllocEntry/NewAllocEntry structure and return pass (EK9270-EK9271 added, 2026-10-22): compared both generated wrappers with the selected native implementations and the generated MemList layout (`m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:1898-1902,2500-2505`; `newallocentry.c:82-118,145`; `allocentry.c:66-80`; `m68kemu_shadow_layouts.h:2609-2617,4579`; `compiler/include/exec/memory.h:61-66`). m68k Exec AllocAbs guest-address path (EK9272 added, 2026-10-22): traced guest A1 through the generated wrapper and pointer mapper into native `AllocAbs` (`m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:1891-1895`; `m68kemu_thunks.h:37`; `m68kemu_intern.h:115-125`; `allocabs.c:68-83`). The m68k context reserves a 32 MiB arena with one host `AllocMem` call, then allocates guest heap space within it (`m68kemu_memory.c:19-42,62-103`). Exec's native absolute allocator searches free host MemHeader chunks or TLSF free blocks (`memory_nommu.c:88-130`; `tlsf.c:987-1027`); the translated address lies within the already reserved arena, so native allocation cannot claim an otherwise free guest address. Added EK9272 for the exposed guest API's failed absolute-allocation path. Outside-arena addresses map to NULL. No maintained guest caller was found; no allocation was attempted. Source-only.
