AllocMem/MungWall platform-enable configuration recheck for EK30 (2026-10-22): verified `IPTR` is unsigned pointer-width (`compiler/include/exec/types.h:85-91`), and `mh_Free`/request sizing remains pointer-width (`compiler/include/exec/memory.h:28-31`). Rechecked both 32-bit and 64-bit wrap algebra: `IPTR_MAX - MUNGWALL_TOTAL_SIZE + 2` plus the overhead wraps to 1, which can pass the free-byte precheck and be rounded only to the allocator's minimum chunk; `MungWall_Build()` then writes its fixed pre-wall/header before applying the original size (`allocmem.c:105-118`, `memory_nommu.c:30-47`, `mungwall.c:28-61`). `MEMF_CLEAR` still reaches the unconditional pre-wall/header write. Expanded EK30's affected-configuration text: MungWall can be enabled by generic boot command line, m68k-amiga debug bootstrap default, or PPC-CHRP `AROS_MUNGWALL_DEBUG` configuration. No caller supplying the extreme request was found in the selected sweep; no allocation was attempted. Candidate remains conditional and source-only.


<a id="mungwall-one-byte-allocation-size-abi-recheck-ek30"></a>EK30 pointer-width API and minimum-allocation write-extent recheck (2026-10-31; finding upheld; no path/LOC credit): confirmed the public `AllocMem` and `AllocAbs` vectors both declare `byteSize` as `IPTR` (`rom/exec/exec.conf:106-107`), so the wrap value is not lost to a `ULONG` parameter conversion on either target width. Followed the `AllocMem()` wrapped size of one through `nommu_AllocMem()` into `stdAlloc()`'s `AROS_ROUNDUP2(size, MEMCHUNK_TOTAL)` request (`rom/exec/allocmem.c:92-118`; `memory_nommu.c:20-77`; `memory.c:527-585`). For `AllocAbs()`, the shifted address must still land in a memory header and the one-byte adjusted range must be allocatable; the out-of-extent MungWall writes are otherwise the same. `MungWall_Build()` unconditionally clears `MUNGWALL_BLOCK_SHIFT` and writes its header before it places the post-wall at the original size; `MEMF_CLEAR` only suppresses the user-region fill (`mungwall.c:28-67`; `debug.h:224-235`). The fixed minimum writes are larger than the one-chunk request. This confirms the conditional EK30 mechanism; no maintained near-maximum caller was found, and no allocation/build/runtime operation was performed.

EK30 selected AllocAbs caller-boundary follow-up (2026-10-31; no new finding or LOC credit): searched direct C call sites and traced representative checked-in callers. The developer Exec allocator test uses a fixed 4,096-byte request (`developer/debug/test/exec/allocmem.c:31-59`); DevTest uses its fixed `PERF_BUF_SIZE` of 512 KiB for benchmark allocations despite accepting a memory-type/address selector (`devtest.c:1906,2197-2200`); VMM's aligned allocator rejects a candidate header when `mh_Free < size` before it calls `AllocAbs()` (`workbench/system/VMM/globals.c:350-381`). The m68k boot/MMU callers derive ordinary image/page sizes, and debug-buffer callers use `sizeof`-based requests. This is a scoped caller sample and direct-call inventory, not proof about external clients or all runtime values; it supports the report's conditional trigger and does not establish a maintained near-maximum request. No allocation or caller was run; source-only.

Low-memory callback cursor edge recheck for EK8818 (2026-10-22): re-read the `for` initialization, condition, callback, and increment separately (`rom/exec/memory.c:1329-1348`). Confirmed two distinct cases: (1) the cursor points at the current node during callback; self-removal plus `MEM_TRY_AGAIN` returns before cursor advancement, so a further allocation failure revisits that detached node; (2) the successor is loaded into local `tmp` before callback, so removing/freeing that successor and returning normally makes the increment save a freed cursor, which the next condition dereferences. A successor freed by a callback that returns `MEM_TRY_AGAIN` is not this second case because the function returns before the increment. Recursive `LowMemSem` acquisition permits callback-driven RemMemHandler (`semaphores.c:91-112`; `remmemhandler.c:46-52`), and the source comment explicitly expects self-removal; the public remover accepts the registered Interrupt record without restricting removal to self. The three checked-in callback producers still establish neither sequence, so EK8818 remains conditional on an external/custom handler. No callback or allocation retry was run. Source-only.


Exec vector-allocation boundary audit (EK9278 added, 2026-10-22): reread the complete `AllocVec`, `FreeVec`, `AllocVecPooled`, and `FreeVecPooled` bodies and checked the 32-/64-bit `IPTR` definitions and 16-byte i386/x86-64 worst alignment. `AllocVec` adds aligned header width `H` without a range check; `IPTR_MAX-H+2` wraps the backing request to one byte, while success stores that one-byte total and returns after the header. The unmanaged `AllocVecPooled` branch has the same issue with `sizeof(IPTR)`; its managed branch forwards the original request. Paired vector frees trust the stored total. The wrapper header does not itself prove an out-of-bounds write because the allocator may grant a minimum chunk; the established defect is success with backing extent far smaller than the requested payload. Existing whole-tree caller census found no selected near-maximum caller. Added EK9278 to the detailed report and index. No allocation or payload access was performed; source-only.

Low-memory retry callback-contract recheck (EK8818 retained and qualified, 2026-10-22): checked `MEM_TRY_AGAIN`/`MEMHF_RECYCLE` declarations against the complete AllocMem retry loop and `checkMemHandlers()` callback/for-loop ordering. The public header supplies status constants but no lifetime rule requiring a callback record to remain registered/alive after `MEM_TRY_AGAIN`; the implementation comment explicitly anticipates self-removal. Confirmed Diskfont's selected callback returns `MEM_ALL_DONE`, LDDemon returns retry only after removing libraries/devices while its own handler remains registered, and log.resource always returns `MEM_DID_NOTHING`. Thus neither recorded selected registration owner establishes the dangerous self-removal/retry or cached-successor-free sequence; retain EK8818 only as a conditional public-API composition candidate. No allocation failure or handler mutation was induced; source-only.

Exec `Enqueue` sentinel and `AddPort` node-contract recheck (no new EK, 2026-10-22): reread `Enqueue()` and `ForeachNode` (`rom/exec/enqueue.c:62-99`; `compiler/include/exec/lists.h:195-201`) against the public insertion contract. Sam440 Parthenope DOS read-status and failure-propagation pass (EK9301 added, 2026-10-22): re-read all 362 physical lines of `arch/ppc-sam440/boot/parthenope/src/dos.c` (C body previously credited) and traced `dos_loadsector()` through all its call sites. Sam440 Parthenope OFS file-progress bounds pass (EK9302 added, 2026-10-22): traced the selected `dos_loadfile()` loop against `DosDataBlock.data_size`, the file header byte count, and the boot device's returned length. In OFS mode, `tocopy` is capped only by the remaining file size and untrusted `data_size`; zero leaves `size` unchanged and the positive-size loop cannot terminate. The same value can exceed the `blocksize - sizeof(struct DosDataBlock)` payload allocation, so a sufficiently large remaining file makes `memcpy()` read beyond the scratch block. Expanded EK9302 to record both exact malformed-block conditions and their distinct consequences. No partition or file was read; source-only.

i386 optional Multiboot command-line startup trace (EK9303, 2026-10-22): re-read the full `arch/i386-pc/exec/debug_init.c` body and its Exec manifest, then traced Multiboot 1/2 command-line discovery through `ParseCmdLine()` and `KRN_CmdLine` construction (`arch/all-pc/bootstrap/multiboot1.c:68-89`; `multiboot2.c:102-109,141-146`; `bootstrap.c:469-481`). Native bootconsole option-boundary recheck (EK9304 added; EK97 relocation candidate qualified, 2026-10-22): traced `con_InitSerial()` from the selected i386/x86-64 Multiboot 1/2 bootconsole setup and the PC kernel's `con_InitTagList()` (`init_multiboot.c:11-18`; `init_multiboot2.c:22-35`; `kernel_startup.c:86-99,125-133`). AArch64 sparse-ID processor.resource consequence (EK541 expanded, 2026-10-22): traced the selected Raspberry Pi package resource list (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:216`) to common processor initialization. The generic `rom/processor/init.c` sizes topology from `KrnGetCPUCount()` and assigns entry IDs `0..count-1`; the public topology contract says entries describe logical processors and their IDs are usable with `GetCoreInfo()`/`GCIT_SelectedProcessor` (`gettopology.c:35-41`). Source-only.

`rom/exec/addsemaphore.c` full-body and list-lock pass (no new EK, 2026-10-22): read the complete 69-line body (21 `cloc 2.06` C lines), including initialization-before-publication, priority insertion and the SMP list-lock boundary. `rom/exec/allocpooled.c` full-body pass (no new EK, 2026-10-22): read all 99 physical lines (43 `cloc 2.06` C code lines), including size-zero behavior, managed-header dispatch and the plain-pool `InternalAllocPooled()` route. `AllocPooled()` small-size behavior in the Poseidon/Pencam path (2026-10-24; existing OD9435 confirmed, no new EK): traced `AllocPooled()`'s nonzero request dispatch (`rom/exec/allocpooled.c:70-94`) into `InternalAllocPooled()`'s alignment overhead and plain-pool allocation (`rom/exec/memory.c:1038-1060,1128-1185,1220-1228`), then compared it with `psdAllocVec()`'s unchecked `ULONG` header/alignment addition and PencamTool's 64-byte initial bulk read (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:331-368`; `rom/usb/shellapps/PencamTool.c:627-648`). `InternalAllocPooled()` pool-growth arithmetic/caller recheck (2026-10-24; no new EK): reread the complete function (`rom/exec/memory.c:1038-1228`) and traced the nonempty-puddle fit test, enlarged-puddle and gradual-growth calculations, `AllocMemHeader()` failure exit, allocator callback dispatch, semaphore release, MungWall wrapper, and returned MemHeader prefix. Exec DeviceList FindName caller census and PFS3 SMP recheck (EK9305 added, 2026-10-22): enumerated direct `FindName(&SysBase->DeviceList, ...)` callers. The selected ATA/SCSI/SDCard boot waits, console handler, LoadResource, and OpenDevice use the ExecLock read path on SMP (or their documented single-CPU Forbid fallback); PFS3's `GetDriveGeometry()` is the relevant selected exception. Both PFS3 and PFS3DS module manifests define `LIMIT_MAXTRANSFER`, and the branch runs for an opened `scsi.device` unit. It protects the traversal only with `Forbid()`, which is processor-local on ExecSMP; dynamic device add/expunge can therefore mutate the list while `FindName()` follows links. SetTaskPri ready-task remote-reschedule candidate qualification (EK842 retained as latency-only, 2026-10-22): rechecked `SetTaskPri()` against both selected ExecSMP scheduler backends (`rom/exec/settaskpri.c:105-145`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:65-131`; `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:78-132`). When a ready task's remembered CPU differs from the caller, `SetTaskPri()` reorders the ready list but sends no IPI; its remote IPI path is limited to a target already in `TS_RUN`. A higher-priority ready task is selected when the affected CPU next runs its scheduler. PC reevaluates through its APIC heartbeat (1,000 ticks/s, `arch/all-pc/kernel/apic_heartbeat.c:46-55,145-157`). Raspberry Pi AArch64 arms per-core CNTP at 50 Hz and uses a four-tick quantum (`platform_bcm27xx.c:114-138,140-155`; `exec_platform.h:12`), so a continuously running lower-priority task can retain the CPU until that quantum boundary absent another schedule event. Neither the SetTaskPri autodoc nor selected callers promise immediate preemption on a remote priority change; the bounded delay is therefore not promoted as a correctness bug. Keep EK842 only as a qualified responsiveness observation; no scheduler timing was run. Source-only.

On 32-bit builds, a caller-provided near-`ULONG_MAX` `stackSize` survives the minimum check and reaches `AllocMem()`, establishing an in-tree route to the existing MungWall addition overflow when that debug mode is enabled. `pr_StackSize` is `ULONG`, so this caller does not prove a near-`IPTR_MAX` request on 64-bit builds; `AllocMem()` remains pointer-width public API. Updated EK30 affected-trigger wording. No allocation was attempted; source-only.

The unmanaged pool path independently adds an `IPTR` header without overflow checking, matching EK783; managed pools delegate the vector callback with the original size. The paired unmanaged free trusts the stored total size. The new `CreateProc()` route uses `AllocMem()` directly and does not establish a near-maximum `AllocVec`/`AllocVecPooled` caller. Existing EK783 remains public-API conditional; no new finding or runtime allocation. Source-only.


Exec MungWall free-path follow-up (2026-10-22): reread `FreeMem()` and the complete relevant `MungWall_Check()`/`CheckHeader()` path (`rom/exec/freemem.c:64-73`; `rom/exec/mungwall.c:126-169,180-257`). `FreeMem()` passes the caller size into header validation before adding total overhead for `InternalFreeMem`; the checker removes the MungWall list entry before alerting and returns the raw header on a valid managed block. This confirms EK30’s wrapped allocation cannot be rehabilitated by free-side sizing; its header stores the original near-limit request, while its backing reservation is tiny. The fallback for a block without a recognized header rounds an unaligned pointer down before returning it; however the documented ordinary startup enables MungWall before public allocations, the m68k MoveExecBase exception explicitly clears the flag while freeing the pre-MungWall SysBase block, and no selected unaligned pre-enable `AllocAbs` allocation/free pair was established. No separate finding credited on that conditional fallback. No free or allocation was executed. Source-only.

### Pthread rwlock try-call self-owner contract recheck (EK9306 corrected, 2026-11-01)

Pthread rwlock try-call self-owner contract recheck (EK9306, claim corrected 2026-11-01): re-read both try APIs and the exact Exec attempt wrappers. `pthread_rwlock_trywrlock()` calls `AttemptSemaphore()`, whose same-task owner branch increments the semaphore nesting count and returns success; POSIX requires `EBUSY` when any writer holds the lock, including the caller ([POSIX `pthread_rwlock_trywrlock`](https://manpages.ubuntu.com/manpages/jammy/man3/pthread_rwlock_trywrlock.3posix.html)). `pthread_rwlock_tryrdlock()` instead calls `AttemptSemaphoreShared()` with a NULL owner, so it fails while a task owns the exclusive lock; the prior 2026-10-22 statement that both succeed was incorrect and is withdrawn. The rwlock unlock path releases one nesting level. `compiler/pthread/mmakefile.src` selects `pthread.c` through `linklibs-pthread`; repository-wide search found no maintained direct callers, leaving external/future clients as the trigger. No source-line credit changed because the implementation body already has full-file credit. No lock call was run; source-only.

Exec semaphore-attempt implementation recheck for EK9306 (2026-11-04; no source/body credit): reread `InternalAttemptSemaphore()` alongside `AttemptSemaphoreShared()` and `ReleaseSemaphore()`. The exclusive attempt passes the current task as owner, so its same-owner branch intentionally nests; the shared attempt passes NULL and cannot match a non-NULL exclusive owner. This confirms that EK9306 is specifically the POSIX wrapper's incorrect try-write return mapping, not a generic shared-attempt defect. The implementation's semaphore-spinlock/list protection remains separate from the pthread rwlock static-initialization race tracked by EK606. No semaphore operation or contention was run.

Exec `Disable()` cross-driver caller check for OD11375 (2026-11-04; no EK or source/body credit): reread `Disable()`'s documented EXECSMP scope and generic implementation (`rom/exec/disable.c:58-61,83-89`) against PPP `abortio()` (`workbench/devs/networks/ppp/init.c:503-526`) and its service-task queue locks (`handler.c:150-164,209-218,246-254,281-284`). Disable masks/excludes only the calling processor; it is not mutual exclusion against the task on another CPU. This confirms the caller-specific lock mismatch already reported as OD11375. No additional Exec implementation defect is established; wider Disable callers remain pending.

Sam440 MMU-handler caller-registration recheck (EK9300 retained, 2026-10-22): confirmed `intr.c` is selected by `arch/ppc-sam440/kernel/mmakefile.src` and `intr_init()` runs before `exec_main()` (`arch/ppc-sam440/kernel/kernel_startup.c:358-363`). The selected vector table maps exceptions 13/14 to `mmu_handler()` (`intr.c:74-90`); `krnRunExceptionHandlers()` returns zero when no handler matches, including a NULL KernelBase (`rom/kernel/addexceptionhandler.c:131-142`). A repository-wide `KrnAddExceptionHandler`/`krnAddExceptionHandler` search found no Sam440-specific registration for either vector; the only checked architecture registrations are PC/APIC, optional x86 debug, and an x86 VMM page-fault handler. The generic PPC exception path treats zero as unhandled and halts, while Sam440's MMU routine returns without `ExitInterrupt` or modifying saved SRR0 (`intr.c:340-357,395-402`); the trampoline restores SRR0 and executes `rfi` (`:268-278`). This confirms EK9300's selected default-fault trigger and retry consequence; no additional finding or line credit. No exception or target was run; source-only.

 i386 PC 4-GiB map-end overflow follow-up (EK9307 added, 2026-10-22): re-read the full selected `mmap_InitMemory()` traversal and the Multiboot map record layout (`arch/all-pc/kernel/kernel_mmap.c:128-165`; `compiler/include/aros/multiboot.h:132-143`), then matched the i386 `PC_Memory` regions and startup consumer (`arch/i386-pc/kernel/kernel_startup.c:39-53,350-353`). With a valid record starting at `0x01000000` and length `0xff000000` (zero high halves; exclusive end 4 GiB), `IPTR end = mmap->addr + mmap->len` wraps to zero; the intersection condition rejects the whole entry, so neither the low 16-MiB ISA interval nor the high-memory interval receives its usable RAM. Added EK9307 to the detailed report and AROS index. The effect remains conditional on that map shape; no bootloader record or startup was exercised. `kernel_mmap.c` already has full-body credit; this adds caller/input-boundary evidence, not additional line credit. Source-only.

Exec `FreePooled()` selected FTManager construct/destruct caller pass (no new EK, 2026-10-22): traced the optional `workbench-system-ftmanager` target's List construct and destruct hooks (`workbench/system/ftmanager/mmakefile.src:5-11`; `fontlist_class.c:43-89,133-147`) plus `flAddEntry()` ownership (`:371-376`). The construct hook allocates one block sized as `sizeof(entry)` plus all three NUL-terminated strings and copies those exact lengths; the destruct hook recomputes those lengths from the stored strings and frees the same total. No selected mutation of the copied filename/family/style fields was found after insertion. If the pooled allocation fails, the List insertion can omit that item and `flAddEntry()` frees its temporary `AllocVec` source; no separate pool mismatch or ownership defect was established. This is one caller slice only; the broader FreePooled direct-call census remains pending. No font list or allocation failure was run. Source-only.
Exec DOSBoot MountList snapshot versus late USB partition insertion (EK9308 added, 2026-10-22): supersedes the earlier unresolved timing note at the `AddBootNode()` caller recheck. Confirmed the selected Raspberry Pi boot packages include both `dosboot` and Poseidon mass storage; USB ROM startup resident priority 10 precedes DOSBoot's −50 and starts class/hardware enumeration before a fixed maximum wait. The mass-storage worker signals its parent before configured startup delay and partition scanning, so a configured delay can keep it active into DOSBoot initialization. `dosboot_Init()` snapshots `ListLength`, initializes only the first half of a `2 * count` zeroed state array, and later drains/rebuilds MountList using unbounded `index++`; with no boot menu, the second half remains zero and a late-inserted node at index `count` is not re-added. `AddBootNode()` holds `BootSemaphore`, but DOSBoot's snapshot and final reorder do not hold it continuously, so the writer can interleave between these phases. Added EK9308 to the report and index. Trigger requires a nonempty initial MountList, successful state allocation, no menu, and a USB partition insertion between the count and final reorder before DOS sets EBF_DOSFLAG. No target build, USB device or boot run was used; source-only.

DOSBoot `initWindow()` failure cleanup qualification (2026-10-22; EK9311 retained, no new finding): checked selected GadTools failure contracts and the `OpenWindow()` result path. `FreeVisualInfo(NULL)` is explicitly safe (`workbench/libs/gadtools/freevisualinfo.c:44-49`), and `CloseWindow(NULL)` returns immediately (`rom/intuition/closewindow.c:111-117`), so those calls do not add independent faults. `FreeGadgets(gadlist)` also runs after a failed OpenWindow and owns only the gadget/context objects; it does not release the separately allocated Boot Options label lists. Thus the leak remains specifically the skipped `freeGadgets_PageBoot()` path. No allocation/window failure was induced; source-only.

DOSBoot device-row selection index pass (EK9312 added, 2026-10-22): followed skipped startup-less MountList entries and compact row insertion (`rom/dosboot/menu.c:260-277,312-318`) into the toggle's direct `devicesEnabled[msg->Code]` access (`:685-701`), then verified final list reconstruction consumes the array by full MountList order (`rom/dosboot/dosboot_init.c:254-273`). With a skipped entry before a displayed row, its compact position differs from its MountList state index, so the click changes a different node's state and the final reorder acts on that wrong node. Added EK9312 and its index entry. No menu or boot was run; source-only. This remains a partial function/caller pass with no whole-file line credit.

DOSBoot capacity-format arithmetic width pass (EK9313 added, 2026-10-22): checked `DosEnvec` field types (`compiler/include/dos/filehandler.h:29-44`) against the capacity expression and subsequent scaling (`rom/dosboot/menu.c:357-372`). On 32-bit builds all multiplicands are 32-bit `IPTR`, so assignment to `UQUAD` occurs only after the sector-count product can wrap; a 2^32-sector product becomes zero before scaling. Added EK9313, limiting impact to the displayed Boot Options capacity on 32-bit systems. The selected menu/device/environment path is required; no device or menu was run. Partial code/caller pass only; no whole-file line credit.

A 15-index environment passes the page gate but does not include DosType; with media present the formatting path reads beyond the environment. Added EK9314 and the index entry. No short environment/device/menu was run; no whole-file credit.

Exec `WaitPort` selected Intuition failure-caller cross-check (GD5066, 2026-10-22): traced the `rom/intuition/menutask.c` call `WaitPort(port)` after `CreateMsgPort()` can return NULL and the child incorrectly marks startup successful (`menutask.c:109-140`). RISC-V alert unwind candidate EK9371 recheck (2026-10-23; retained, no new ID): matched the trap frame definition to the alert producer: `ExceptionContext.fp` is saved register x8/s0 (`arch/riscv64-all/include/aros/cpucontext.h:20-29`), and `Exec_TrapHandler()` passes that saved register as `iet_AlertStack` (`rom/exec/traphandler.c:100-112,129`). The RISC-V alert `UnwindFrame()` treats it as a CFA and reads `frame[-1]`/`frame[-2]` (`arch/riscv64-all/exec/alert_cpu.c:40-49`), while the selected architecture diagnostic scanner explicitly says `-fomit-frame-pointer` removes the frame chain and scans stack words instead (`arch/riscv64-all/kernel/backtracefromframe.c:15-22`). `FormatAlertExtra()` checks only `TypeOfMem(fp)` before those reads (`rom/exec/alertextra.c:157-168`), which confirms allocation membership but not that the value is a frame CFA or that the preceding two words remain within the allocation. EK9371 is retained with high confidence for invalid trace interpretation and conditional out-of-allocation reads; an actual secondary fault depends on the saved s0 value. No trap or alert was induced; source-only.

EK715 i386 instruction-padding bound recheck (2026-10-23; existing finding confirmed): re-read the complete `FormatAlertExtra()` disassembly loop and traced `DCIT_Instruction_HexStr` to the selected i386 `GetCtxInstructionA()` implementation and imported udis86 decoder. `__WORDSIZE` is 32 on i386; the formatter subtracts unsigned `ULONG inslen` from a 16-character padding width, while udis86 permits a 15-byte instruction and returns its hex bytes into a 64-byte buffer. Thus any decoded instruction longer than eight bytes makes the subtraction wrap before writes into the 17-byte `insPad` array. Confirmed the i386 debug initializer enables `DBFF_DISASSEMBLE`; the candidate is now detailed in the report and master index. The distinct RISC-V alert-type confusion and frame-unwind findings remain separate. No build, alert, or disassembly was run; source-only.

Exec interrupt-exit vector and m68k caller pass (2026-10-23; no new EK): re-read the generic `ExitIntr()` stub and reconciled its selected m68k replacement, vector installation, interrupt wrapper, and deferred scheduler path (`rom/exec/exitintr.c`; `arch/m68k-all/exec/{exec_platform.c,exitintr.S,schedule.S}`; `arch/m68k-amiga/kernel/amiga_irq.c:156-176`; `arch/m68k-all/kernel/kernel_intr.c:21-42`). The trap wrapper saves the same six registers expected by the vector, whose SR offset is 24 bytes; `ExitIntr` skips scheduling on supervisor-mode return, calls `core_ExitIntr()` for user-mode return, and tail-jumps to the common scheduler only when `TDNestCnt < 0` and `ARF_AttnSwitch` is set. The selected m68k `Signal()` fast path sets that switch flag when it wakes a higher-priority task and explicitly defers switching to `ExitIntr()` (`arch/m68k-all/exec/signal_fast.S:69-80`). Exact source search found no other checked-in caller of the private vector; non-m68k kernel paths use their CPU-specific interrupt-exit routines. No frame/restore or scheduling defect established in this selected path; external/private vector users and hardware exception-frame behavior remain open. No interrupt or task switch was run; source-only.

`KrnIsSuper()` implementation and direct-caller matrix recheck (2026-10-23; no new EK): inspected every checked-in implementation and the architecture manifests selecting them, then ran a repository-wide C/assembly callsite census. Confirmed x86 CPL, m68k SR, PPC assembly, ARM CPSR, hosted Unix/Mingw, and RISC-V trap-depth implementations; AArch64 native's manifest names a missing local `issuper` source and remains the separate EK8902 build-selection candidate. Traced direct call families in PC interrupt-controller setup/teardown and spinlocks, hosted Unix I/O/packet host-library locking, RISC-V trap entry/exit, and Exec Permit/Enable, reset, SuperState, DOS cleanup and debug readers. These selected uses do not establish an additional mismatch. OpenSBI startup currently runs AROS on only the boot hart, so its global trap-depth counter is not concurrently changed by another hart before SMP bring-up. The native field offsets therefore do not match the guest structure and its later offset writes extend beyond that guest object. Native `EndScreenNotify(NULL)` returns success without unregistering the live notification. Added EK9377 for the unusable guest handle and qualified possible retained registration/object state. M68K DrawInfo borrowed-shadow caller reconciliation (EK9275 expanded; 2026-10-23): traced the generated GetScreenDrawInfo/FreeScreenDrawInfo pair against the native Intuition implementations and the shadow allocator. Each successful Get call returns the screen's same embedded DInfo pointer and unconditionally creates a new guest shadow; native FreeScreenDrawInfo is a no-op, and its generated thunk never removes that mapping. Repeated get/free cycles therefore consume the fixed 256-entry table and guest heap, then make valid later GetScreenDrawInfo calls return zero. Folded this same duplicate-borrowed-shadow mechanism into EK9275; no new ID and no emulated screen call. Generated wrapper body credit already existed; this is caller/lifetime reconciliation only. `krnRunIRQHandlers()` architecture-dispatch caller census (EK9155 retained; no additional finding, 2026-10-23): searched every checked-in call to the shared dispatcher and matched caller ranges to each selected kernel's `HW_IRQ_COUNT`. PC dispatch rejects `irq_number >= HW_IRQ_COUNT`; Sam440 UIC iteration is bounded to 0–127 under its 256-entry table; BCM2708's three banks stay within 0–71 (ARM's table has 72 entries). OpenSBI PLIC source IDs are bounded by the spec to 1–1023 for its 1,024-entry table, timer IRQs come from bounded virtual allocation, and MSI vectors are range-checked by the allocator. Both AArch64 BCM2711 and BCM2712 accept GIC IDs below 1023 without checking the shared 384-entry table; retained EK9155 is directly grounded for BCM2712 by the selected PCIe MSI ID propagation, while this pass did not establish a BCM2711 in-tree source that delivers IDs 384–1022, so it does not expand the finding to Pi 4. Realtime `PLAYER_ExtSync` conflict-result and constructor rollback recheck (EK9056 expanded; 2026-10-23): reread the complete `PLAYER_ExtSync` tag branch in `SetPlayerAttrsA()` and traced it through `CreatePlayerA()` (`workbench/libs/realtime/setplayerattrsa.c:76,263-294`; `createplayera.c:97-158`) against the public failure/error-output contract (`createplayera.c:97-108`; `setplayerattrsa.c:47-57`). Realtime alarm destination publication recheck (EK9138 expanded; 2026-10-23): compared `PLAYER_AlarmSigTask`/`PLAYER_AlarmSigBit` setters with Pulse's complete alarm delivery branch (`workbench/libs/realtime/setplayerattrsa.c:212-229`; `pulse.c:126-151`). Exec signal-bit 31 body/caller reconciliation (EK8800 withdrawal correction, 2026-10-26): the source and caller census is retained as evidence, but its dated conclusion was wrong. On 32-bit targets the positive shift into bit 31 is representable in the corresponding unsigned type; conversion back to signed is implementation-defined, not undefined. No selected compiler behavior was found that produces an incorrect ULONG signal mask, so EK8800 is withdrawn and no detailed finding or master-index entry is warranted. The selected Shell, ASL and Exec paths remain useful caller coverage, but do not establish a defect from this expression alone. No signal exhaustion, shell operation, or wait was run; source-only.

PC exception saved-SS target-boundary recheck (EK9132 retained i386-only; 2026-10-23): compared the C diagnostic field reads with both selected PC entry stubs and context layouts (`arch/{i386-pc,x86_64-pc}/kernel/core_interrupts.s`; `arch/{i386-all,x86_64-all}/include/aros/cpucontext.h`). The i386 same-ring hardware frame contains only EIP/CS/EFLAGS, so its `ExceptionContext.ss` slot aliases unrelated pre-entry stack data; the common page-fault log and unhandled `PrintContext()` both print that field, as covered by EK9132. x86-64 differs: the 64-bit entry frame includes SS:RSP even without a CPL change, so the same-ring invalid-SS report is not extended to x86-64. This distinction is specified by Intel's 64-bit interrupt-frame description ([Intel SDM, Vol. 3A, §6.14.2](https://www.intel.com/content/dam/public/us/en/documents/manuals/64-ia-32-architectures-software-developer-vol-3a-part-1-manual.pdf)). EK9375 SAD RA/RC count-boundary recheck (2026-10-23; retained and trigger narrowed, no new EK): reread the exact `RA` and `RC` loops and `GetL()` parser (`rom/exec/debug_internal.c:361-391,461-479`). The counter begins at one, but the pointer is dereferenced before each increment, so for any count below `ULONG_MAX` the code reads exactly `cnt` bytes; no ordinary one-past read is established. `GetL()` accepts eight hexadecimal digits and `ULONG` is 32-bit, so `FFFFFFFF` is the sole count that makes `t++` wrap after the last requested byte. The next loop iteration then dereferences the first byte beyond the requested range. The already reported nontermination/out-of-range continuation is therefore restricted to that maximum count and a readable region long enough to reach the wrap; no lower count or near-wrap variant was established. No SAD command or memory range was read; source-only.


Realtime Pulse expunge/Forbid scope recheck (EK9051 narrowed to ExecSMP; 2026-10-23): re-read `FreeTimer()` and the complete Pulse wait/tick loop (`workbench/libs/realtime/realtime_timer.c:78-84`; `pulse.c:25-160`) against realtime `Expunge()` (`realtime_init.c:52-61`), generated module expunge (`tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1558-1587`), and Exec callers. Realtime Pulse/LDDemon segment-unload path correction (EK9051 UP scope restored; 2026-10-23): followed LDDemon initialization installing its Exec `RemLibrary` vector (`rom/lddemon/lddemon.c:890-898`) through its library-removal wrapper and flush scan (`:632-650,682-724`). `RemLibrary()` calls the target expunge vector, then `UnLoadSeg(seglist)`, and only afterward releases `Forbid()`; the base ROM package selects LDDemon (`rom/mmakefile.src:151`). `realtime.library` is a regular loadable library (`workbench/libs/realtime/mmakefile.src:24-26`) whose expunge signals Pulse but does not join it. EK8795 arithmetic candidate recheck and report restoration (2026-10-23): verified the old coverage-only candidate against `timespec_s.h`, `time_t.h`, and the absolute-deadline branch. Despite the source comment claiming 64-bit subtraction, `time_t` is signed `AROS_32BIT_TYPE`, and both operands at `pthread_cond_timedwait.c:83` are therefore signed 32-bit. A representable far-past deadline can overflow before the `rel.tv_sec < 0` clamp (`:102-106`). AArch64 memory-range consumer-capacity recheck (EK9390 added, 2026-10-23): followed each selected `/memory/reg` tuple through `query_memory()` and the `KRN_MEMLower`/`KRN_MEMUpper` tag consumer (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/boot.c:246-322`; `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/kernel_startup.c:151,229-235,331-395`; `compiler/include/aros/kernel.h:80-85`). MinGW x86 hosted CPU-context allocation/save/restore contract pass (no new EK; 2026-10-23): reconciled both `arch/all-mingw32/kernel/cpu_i386.h` and `cpu_x86_64.h` context layouts/macros with the architecture-specific `cpu_init.c` and `createcontext.c`, generic `krnAllocCPUContext()`/`KrnDeleteContext()`, `kernel_cpu.c` switch/dispatch/exception trampoline, and the host's `GetThreadContext()`/`SetThreadContext()` flags (`arch/all-mingw32/kernel/host_intr.c:151-194`). AArch64 BCM27xx secondary startup and per-core timer caller recheck (EK541, EK8868, EK8870, EK8903, EK8904 retained; no new EK; 2026-10-23): re-read the active `__AROSEXEC_SMP__` path in `platform_bcm27xx.c`, the trampoline/TLS handoff and `cpu_Register()`, with the existing report entries and direct callers. Confirmed that the boot CPU initializes IPI reception before launch; each secondary is given stack/TLS state before wake, registers its CPU bit before bootstrap task creation, initializes the per-core timer heartbeat only after `cpu_BootStrap()`, then releases `startup_lock`. `bcm27xx_wait_core()` observes that release and proceeds sequentially to the next CPU ID. Existing findings cover unchecked shared/per-core allocations (EK8868), PSCI refusal leaks (EK8870), timeout ownership/reused shared trampoline state (EK8903), bootstrap failure after publishing the online bit (EK8904), and sparse online IDs after a refused earlier CPU (EK541). The shared CNTP interval is initialized by the first successful secondary while launches are serialized by `startup_lock`; later secondaries reuse it, so no separate interval-initialization race was established. The AArch64 timer-device issues OD9393-OD9395 are tracked in Other Drivers; the standard Raspberry Pi package includes `kernel-timer` through an active `#MM` edge and `PKG_DEVS_ARCH := timer` (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:97-118,217-232`). No allocation failure, PSCI response, timeout, CPU startup, timer interrupt, or SMP schedule was induced; source-only.

PC KrnGetCPUNumber selected wrapper and caller-mapping recheck (EK657 distinguished; no new EK, 2026-10-23): re-read the selected all-PC wrapper and APIC logical-ID mapping (`arch/all-pc/kernel/getcpunumber.c:12-19`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/apic.c:71-113`) against CPU discovery/count and per-CPU attribute bounds (`getcpucount.c:12-25`; `getcpuattr.c:57-84`). The PC path maps the executing local APIC ID through the compact `cores[]` table; the discovered count is the same table bound, and per-CPU attribute access rejects out-of-range IDs before indexing. With no APIC data, the wrapper returns logical CPU 0 for the uniprocessor case. A local APIC ID absent from the discovered table yields `(apicid_t)-1`, exposed through the public unsigned return type; this requires inconsistent/failed topology or an execution context outside the registered CPU set. No selected ordinary caller was found that supplies such an invalid result as a normal index, and no distinct consequence beyond the existing API/topology contract leads was established. This narrows the PC implementation only; it does not close the broad direct-caller/platform census or change generic body-line credit. No CPU query or boot was run; source-only.

These objects are outside AROS's `MemoryMap` allocations, so no allocator reuse of the list or tag payloads is established. `KrnGetBootInfo()` may therefore return the same long-lived bootstrap list on these paths. Pegasos CHRP startup full-body and boot-caller recheck (EK8859 qualified; 2026-10-23): read all 159 `cloc 2.06` C code lines of `arch/ppc-chrp/pegasos/kernel/kernel_startup.c`, traced `kernel_entry()`/`core_kick()` and first-start tag/payload relocation through `kernel_start()`, and followed the selected OpenFirmware bootstrap call at `arch/ppc-chrp/boot/openfirmware/src/bootstrap.c:415`. The unconditional loop at `kernel_startup.c:224-225` is outside the first-start conditional and prevents any later kernel-resource/Exec handoff if this entry is used. The architecture makefile defines the direct `kernel-kernel-chrp-ppc-pegasos` target with native-PPC and bootconsole prerequisites, but repository-wide search found no other checked-in image/package/aggregate edge selecting it; EK8859 is therefore retained as a conditional target-only candidate and does not assert default packaged reachability. Firmware memory reservation, external image integration and runtime behavior remain open. No build or boot was run; source-only.

Pegasos CHRP boot-memory allocator caller-bound recheck (EK8859 retained; no new finding; 2026-10-25): reread both selected allocator bodies (`kernel_bootmem.c`, 20 `cloc 2.06` C lines) and all call sites in `kernel_startup.c`, then traced the OpenFirmware bootstrap claim/release of `[0x07000000, 0x08000000)` and the producer’s `KRN_KernelHighest` handoff. The bump allocator has no upper-bound check and `kernel_start()` copies the tag list, then relocates BSS, OF tree, VBE records and strings into that arena; the startup eventually parks in the already-recorded unconditional loop, so this target does not reach Exec. The bootstrap keeps the 16 MiB claim on the successful kernel-entry path, but the source does not establish a maximum serialized payload or prove the post-kernel arena’s exact remaining capacity for all firmware trees. Therefore the allocator-bound question remains open and no independent out-of-range-write finding is asserted. Existing body credit is unchanged. No boot, memory write or firmware tree was exercised; source-only.

Pegasos CHRP boot-memory allocator and caller pass (2026-10-23): read the full 14-code-line `kernel_bootmem.c` body and both declarations in `kernel_bootmem.h`; traced every allocator call to first-start tag/BSS/OF-tree/VBE/cmdline/bootloader relocation in `kernel_startup.c`. The bump allocator has no end check and advances before clearing. The bootstrap claims a 16-MiB region at `0x07000000`, with the kernel loaded at `KERNEL_PHYS_BASE` `0x07800000`, and releases that region only after `kernel_phys_entry()` returns (`bootstrap.c:198-199,415,420-422`). Pegasos `kernel_startup()` never returns because of its unconditional terminal loop (`kernel_startup.c:224-225`), so the selected path retains the reservation; this rules out reuse through the bootstrap's ordinary release path. The in-tree producer does not provide a bounded boot-memory end or a maximum OF-tree size, so allocator exhaustion remains an integration/input-boundary question; no maintained input exceeding the reservation was established and no second overflow candidate is promoted. `KRN_MMAPLength` is read but unused in startup, while the selected producer does not publish those tags; no independent consequence was established. No boot, memory map, or firmware tree was used; source-only.
x86-64 boot-memory map producer/caller pass (2026-10-23; no new EK): traced the selected Multiboot v1 and v2 parsers through `bootstrap.c`'s `KRN_MMAPAddress`/`KRN_MMAPLength` tags and `kernel_cstart()`'s first-start relocation, `mmap_FindRegion()`, allocator initialization, and later MMU sizing (`arch/all-pc/bootstrap/multiboot1.c:91-110,256-257`; `multiboot2.c:80-100,148-150,213-217`; `bootstrap.c:610-620,650-655,692-740`; `arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/kernel_startup.c:257-322,433-455,477-520`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/kernel_mmap.c:102-220,276-349`). Shell overlong-line caller and parameter-type recheck (EK9247 retained; 2026-10-23): re-read `readLine()`'s bound/return and `interact()`'s `moreLeft` loop (`workbench/c/Shell/readLine.c:52-138`; `Shell.c:73-150`). For lines exceeding `LINE_MAX`, `readLine()` exits before consuming the newline or updating `moreLeft`; a later overlong line can therefore leave the previous newline's TRUE value set and cause the unread suffix to be parsed as another command, while an initial overlong line follows the end-of-input path. Checked the header/definition pointer types: `BOOL` and `WORD` are both signed 16-bit typedefs in `compiler/include/exec/types.h:58-62,179-182`, so their spelling difference is not an ABI defect. EK9247 remains; no additional finding. No Shell input was run; source-only.

Shell resident initialization failure-path follow-up (EK9251 expanded; 2026-10-23): traced `CreateSegList()`'s BNULL allocation result and both `AddSegment()` return/ownership paths through selected `shell_init` (`workbench/c/Shell/shell_init.c:58-83`; `compiler/arossupport/createseglist.c:38-41,80-85`; `rom/dos/addsegment.c:64-100`). Expanded EK9251 and its index label. No allocation failure or resident-list change was induced; source-only.

VMM x86 page-fault handler lifecycle recheck (2026-10-23; no new EK): reread the full `workbench/system/VMM/x86/traphandler_x86.c` body (90 C code lines per `cloc 2.06`) against PageHandler startup/cleanup, VMM exit checks, and PC exception dispatch. Both failed PageHandler initialization and normal loop exit reach `Cleanup_PageHandler()`, which calls `VMMRemoveTrapHandler()` before restoring page tables, freeing the cache, or deleting the paging port (`pagehandler.c:181-244,625-632`). Normal exit first runs `ExitPossible()`: it disables new VMM allocation, verifies that remaining virtual allocations can fit, and synchronously locks every allocated page before `NoMoreVM()` and support-task shutdown (`VM_Manager.c:44-77,91-165,169-183`; `VM_Manager_Init.c:1040-1059`). The withdrawn EK9394 signal-fallback candidate remains only a source-level conditional; kernel exception-handler removal does not join callbacks already snapshotted on ExecSMP, but no reachable selected VMM caller/callback overlap was established beyond the blocked VMM startup. No VMM, page fault, or shutdown was run; source-only.

Security `FillUserInfo()` group-copy allocation/caller pass (EK9416 revalidated, 2026-10-31): traced the complete `secGetUserInfo.c` vector and its synchronous request into `GetUserInfo()`, alongside `FillUserInfo()`'s group-array replacement (`security_server.c:83-108,255-358`). Login converts it into an owner with only the primary group (`security_login.c:307-328,633-649`; `secUserInfo2ExtOwner.c:43-63`); `usergroup.library`'s group-member collector silently omits the secondary membership (`usergroup_security.c:355-380`). PCI IRQ routing attribute semantics reconciliation (2026-10-23; no new EK): rechecked `AssignIRQ()` against the PCI device class storage/accessors and the selected PCIPC `_PRT` parser (`rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:219-286`; `pcideviceclass.c:644-650,768-769`; `arch/all-pc/hidds/pcipc/pcipc_driverclass.c:265-289`). The field named `IRQLine` in `DeviceData` is populated from PCI config `INT_PIN` (the 1-based A-D pin); `INTLine` is separately populated from `PCICS_INT_LINE`. `AssignIRQ()` intentionally matches the former against `_PRT.Pin + 1`, swizzles that pin while walking parent bridges, and writes the routed GSI/IRQ into the latter. The similar field names are not evidence of a pin-versus-line mix-up. Existing PCI removal and setup-concurrency findings remain as previously qualified; no new IRQ routing defect established. No firmware table or hardware routing was exercised; source-only.

Exec `FindPort()` targeted direct-caller census (2026-10-24; no new EK): searched `rom/exec`, `rom/kernel`, and `arch` C/assembly sources; the only direct architecture caller in that slice is m68k SetPatch's `p5stuff()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/c/SetPatch.c:123-150`). It performs an unprotected lookup of the external `BOOT-MMU-Port`, then interprets offset `0x26` as a list and walks it while applying memory protection. PC/RISC-V scheduler spin-state and invalid-stack dispatch cross-check (EK9131 retained; no new EK; 2026-10-24): compared the selected PC, RISC-V, AArch64 and generic scheduler dispatch paths around `TS_SPIN` fallback and invalid saved-stack handling (`arch/all-pc/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:294-406`; `arch/riscv-native/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:190-252`; `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:78-145`; `rom/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:114-173`). PC `core_Dispatch()` queues the rejected ready task itself onto `TaskWait`; its later `TS_SPIN` fallback would reclassify the current task without removing it from `TaskSpinning`, but the corresponding producer hook is not reached by a maintained in-tree caller: the PC `Exec_PlatformData.SpinLockCall` has no caller, normal PC `EXEC_SPINLOCK_LOCK` passes a NULL failure hook, and the RISC-V `EXECTASK_SPINLOCK_LOCK` macro has no in-tree use (`arch/all-pc/exec/exec_platform.h:40-66`; `platform_init.c:43-74,172-186,479-485`; `arch/riscv-native/exec/exec_platform.h:21-28`). The native RISC-V invalid-stack path still enqueues the wrong task node (EK9131); PC's corresponding invalid-stack branch enqueues `newtask`, and generic/AArch64 paths use their own caller context. This is caller/build reachability evidence only; architecture context-save behavior and the native RISC-V boot limitation remain open. No scheduler state, task stack or spinlock contention was induced; source-only.

AArch64 native boot-tag iterator producer/capacity closure (2026-10-24; no new EK): rechecked the standard-control-tag iterator and its only direct native-kernel consumer (`krnGetTagData()` in `kernel_startup.c:88,366-367`), then searched all selected AArch64 native/Raspberry Pi boot sources for boot-list writes and all kernel callers. `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/boot.c` is the only checked-in producer for this target and emits no `TAG_MORE`/`TAG_SKIP`; its 23 conditional/unconditional append operations plus the `TAG_DONE` terminator cap the list at 24 entries. `BOOT_TAGS_SIZE` reserves 1,024 bytes, or 64 AArch64 TagItems (`boot/include/boot.h:16-17`), so this producer stays within the reservation without relying on firmware-supplied list length. # PC local-APIC controller startup and AP handoff reconciliation (2026-10-24; no new EK)

Traced the selected x86-64 PC local-APIC path from `core_APIC_Probe()` through BSP `core_APIC_Init()`, `APICInt_IntrController` registration, `APICInt_Init()` and AP `cpu_BootStrap()` initialization (`arch/all-pc/kernel/apic.c:16-62`; `apic_ia32.c:69-130,1066-1141`; `smp_exec.c:195-215`; `platform_post.c:166-205`; `ictl.c:87-134`). The target selects these common PC bodies through its architecture manifest. The interrupt-controller list is initialized before SMP wake; AP initialization later finds the already-registered local APIC and increments its instance count, but `krnInitInterruptControllers()` is not rerun and the selected AP local-vector setup does not consume that updated count. Concurrent AP increments could lose the diagnostic/instance count, but no operational consequence was established. BSP/AP exception-handler allocation failures remain EK8877/EK9264; x2APIC-to-xAPIC MMIO handoff remains EK9130. Exec `ExitIntr` selected producer/restore pass (2026-10-24; no new EK): reread the generic vector-6 stub, m68k override, vector installation, and every checked-in producer (`rom/exec/exitintr.c`; `arch/m68k-all/exec/exitintr.S`; `arch/m68k-all/exec/exec_platform.c:27-32`; `arch/m68k-amiga/kernel/amiga_irq.c:126-176`; `arch/m68k-all/kernel/kernel_intr.c:21-42`). All seven native Amiga trap wrappers share one save/restore sequence: they drop the software vector ID, save the same six registers that `ExitIntr` restores, and branch there only when the interrupt handler returns TRUE; the assembly tests the saved supervisor bit before calling `core_ExitIntr`, which requests `__Schedule_this` only when needed. No frame-offset mismatch or local producer/restore defect established. This closes the selected native-Amiga wrapper slice, not external uses of the private vector or other m68k exception frames; no interrupt or context switch was run.
AArch64 native exception diagnostics and cache-helper caller pass (EK9417 added; 2026-10-24): reread the complete 398-line `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/intr.c` in source order and reconciled ESR-class dispatch, vector callers, exception-handler/core_Trap returns, fault-code dump bounds, saved-SP dump bounds, and the local cache helpers. Re-traced every selected `aarch64_flush_cache()` call in `platform_bcm27xx.c`: TLS and release-slot addresses are explicitly 64-byte aligned; the trampoline is an `AllocMem()` result with only `sizeof(struct MemChunk)` alignment documented, but its assembly-defined span is 240 bytes (47 instructions, four alignment bytes and six 64-bit data slots), so the helper's 512-byte walk covers its lines for every 64-byte starting offset. The possible unaligned tail omission therefore does not affect the current trampoline content. The stack dump's `sp + 8` and page-end additions can wrap for the exact aligned top address `0xfffffffffffffff8`, admitting an invalid read; added EK9417 for the conditional secondary Data Abort during exception diagnostics. No extra cache-helper finding established in the selected call paths. No cache op, exception, or board was used; source-only.
AArch64 vector saved-SP provenance recheck for EK9417 (2026-10-24): reread the complete 332-line `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/vectors.S` and matched `save_context` to the ExceptionContext layout. For EL0-origin exceptions, it explicitly loads `sp_el0` and stores that value at `FRAME_SP`; for EL1t-origin exceptions, it stores the pre-frame kernel SP (`vectors.S:49-77`; frame `:6-20`). Thus an arbitrary invalid user SP is passed unchanged to `dump_code_around()` by the undefined/data-abort handlers; the wrap trigger is not an assumption that `regs->sp` points into the diagnostic kernel frame. EK9417 remains conditional on this invalid top-page value and a translation fault on the diagnostic read. This confirms the saved-SP path only; no additional vector defect or line credit. No exception or target was run; source-only.


Forbid wrap target-semantics reconciliation (EK8827 restored; 2026-10-24): rechecked the old 129-deep nesting candidate against selected C and architecture atomic implementations. The m68k path is definite: `TDNESTCOUNT_INC` maps to `AROS_ATOMIC_INC`, and `atomic_inc_b()` emits `addq.b #1`; after 129 outstanding calls from -1, the stored byte is 0x80 and `core_ExitInterrupt()`'s `< 0` gate may schedule on a pending switch. Restored EK8827 with m68k-Amiga-only scope. Earlier cross-target notes treated all signed-byte increments as guaranteed wrap; for paths using signed C increment/conversion, that result is implementation-defined and no selected compiler result was established, so those scopes are withdrawn from this finding. OD3229 remains independently grounded in its one-level unmatched-Permit caller: the later Forbid/Permit pair operates on an offset count that stays negative, so it cannot suppress task switching; no overflow is needed for that consequence. Earlier historical wording about 128 unmatched decrements wrapping the signed byte is superseded and is not a separate credited trigger. No nested call or interrupt was run; source-only.


CEBoot boot-information arena caller pass (EK9418 added; 2026-10-24): read all 39 `cloc 2.06` code lines of `arch/arm-native/ceboot/bootmem.c` and traced every `AllocBootMem()` call through `AddTag()` and `main()` (`bootstrap.c:69-83,145-153,174,192,200-202`). `InitBootMem()` allocates a fixed 4,096-byte arena; a request that exceeds its remaining aligned capacity prints an error and calls `exit(0)`, bypassing the `-1` failure returns used by surrounding startup. CEBoot ELF file-I/O adapter full-body pass (EK504 expanded; 2026-10-24): read all 89 `cloc 2.06` C code lines of `arch/arm-native/ceboot/elf_io.c`; traced `open_file()`, `read_block()`, `load_block()` and their shared-loader call sites in `bootstrap/elfloader.c:507-525,623-682`. Exec managed-header AvailMem callback lock-order recheck (EK744 retained; no new EK; 2026-10-24): reread the full `nommu_AvailMem()` callback dispatch (`rom/exec/memory_nommu.c:318-439`) against TLSF, Radeon and VideoCore `mhe_Avail` implementations and selected lock holders. On ExecSMP, `MEM_LOCK_SHARED` retains the global MemList read spinlock while invoking the callback. Radeon `mh_Avail()` can wait on `CardMemLock`; the checked Radeon owners are only `AllocBitmapArea()` and `FreeBitmapArea()`, which take `HWLock` then `CardMemLock` and perform bitmap operations without calling Exec allocation, so this pass establishes blocking while holding the shared MemList lock but no concrete lock cycle. m68kemu Hunk-loader checked-in caller reconciliation (2026-10-24; no new EK): searched direct C/C++ references and traced all three Hunk-loader call sites. `M68KEmu_LoadHunks()` is called only by `RunHunk()` (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_run.c:175`), whose caller supplies a `LoadSeg()` BPTR and whose context is destroyed after the run (`:171-181`). `M68KEmu_LoadHunksFromMemory()` is called by `RunFile()` (`:224-231`) and `M68KEmu_LoadM68KLibrary()` (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_m68klib.c:66-68`); the first frees the file buffer after parser return and destroys its context on either parser result, while the disk-library caller frees the input buffer but retains successful guest hunks through subsequent Resident/AUTOINIT admission, including the already reported EK553 post-parse rejection leak. The runtime path is selected through `thunk_exec_OpenLibrary()` only after generated/native fake-base lookup fails (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks.c:37-85`); top-level `RunFile()` reaches the same parser directly. No file, library or guest code was loaded; source-only.

Partition root geometry and USB mass-storage capacity caller pass (EK9423 added; 2026-10-24): re-read `OpenRootPartition()` and generic root `GetPartitionAttrs()` handling, then traced the selected USB MassStorage `TD_GETGEOMETRY` producer and HDToolBox/DOSBoot root-handle callers (`rom/partition/openrootpartition.c:54-86`; `rom/partition/getpartitionattrs.c:105-109,184-190`; `workbench/devs/USB/classes/MassStorage/storage_device.c:104-123`; `workbench/devs/USB/classes/MassStorage/storageclass.c:614-634`; `workbench/devs/USB/classes/MassStorage/storage_task.c:134-138`; `workbench/tools/HDToolBox/harddisks.c:127-137`; `rom/dosboot/bootscan.c:299-305`). USB MassStorage sets cylinders to `msu_blockCount / 16065`, so a present unit with `msu_blockCount` below 16,065 can return zero; `OpenRootPartition()` subtracts one into unsigned `de_HighCyl` without validation. The root `PT_ENDBLOCK` default then promotes the wrapped high cylinder and computes a multi-trillion-block extent. Added EK9423 for this selected small-media root-geometry mismatch. Existing HDToolBox reads the root geometry/environment and DOSBoot scans tables from the root handle; no particular downstream out-of-range operation was established. Other block-device geometry producers and external root-handle consumers remain open. No device, media, table, or build was exercised; source-only.

EK9423 selected HDToolBox behavior recheck (no scope expansion; 2026-10-24): traced the root geometry copied by `harddisks.c` into `ptclass.c`'s partition drawing, pointer-to-block conversion and edit validation (`workbench/tools/HDToolBox/harddisks.c:127-137`; `ptclass.c:449-541,568-588,794-815`; `partitions.c:229-270`). With zero cylinders, `getBlock()` multiplies by `dg_Cylinders-1` (unsigned wrap) and `validValue()` sees a zero-sector extent, so the reported root geometry also makes the partition editor's coordinate/validity calculations unusable for an otherwise recognized small-media partition table. This corroborates the consumer-visible consequence of EK9423 but is not recorded as a separate finding. No disk or GUI operation was run; source-only.

EK8832 caller-to-consumer confirmation and report/index restoration (2026-10-24): traced the ACPI MADT count mismatch through `acpi_APIC_AllocPrivate()`, `krnSysCallBSPUpdate()`, and `X86_HandleBSPUpdateSC()` into `core_BSPReconfigure()` (`arch/all-pc/kernel/acpi_apic.c:60-71`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/syscall.c:112-120`; `arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/kernel_startup.c:837-879`). The handler discards the result; the function raises `kbp_APIC_Max` before replacement allocations and leaves `newGDT`/`newTSS` indeterminate when their respective `Allocate()` calls fail. Confirmed the earlier boot allocation creates a one-entry TSS array while setting the initial maximum to one (`kernel_startup.c:384-397`); AP setup later sizes each private GDT and iterates TSS descriptors using the updated maximum, with `core_CPUSetup()` resolving and writing the chosen TSS (`arch/all-pc/kernel/platform_post.c:52-69`; `arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/kernel_startup.c:681-781`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/smp.c:247-250`). This supports EK8832's conditional TSS-array overrun path and partial-allocation leak. The reference existed in coverage notes but had no finding heading or master-index link; restored the detailed section and active index entry, bringing the Exec/Kernel active index count to 504. No allocation failure or AP start was induced; source-only.

ARM native `kernel_debug.c` selected callback/caller recheck (2026-10-24; no new EK): read all 18 `cloc 2.06` C code lines and reconciled `ARMI_PutChar`/`ARMI_SerPutChar` setup in `platform_bcm2708.c` with the direct `KrnPutChar`, `bug()` and alert-output routes. PPC CHRP/Efika, Sam440, and m68k virtual-to-physical override/caller reconciliation (2026-10-24; no new EK): rechecked the per-target implementations and selected direct consumers. Efika's `virt2phys()` searches the current hash table, preserves page offset on a hit, and returns `0xffffffff` on a miss (`arch/ppc-chrp/efika/kernel/mmu.c:455-466`); `KrnVirtualToPhysical()` temporarily enters supervisor mode around that lookup (`:469-487`). Its selected `CachePreDMA()` returns the translation without checking a miss (`arch/ppc-chrp/exec/cachepredma.c:20-35`), while RTAS passes its resident argument block and return-array addresses through the same API (`arch/ppc-chrp/rtas/rtas_init.c:96-114`). Those callers supply valid mapped buffers by contract; no selected invalid/unmapped address path was established, and the API's miss sentinel is not documented here, so no separate candidate is promoted. Sam440 subtracts the `0xff000000` high alias and leaves identity-mapped addresses unchanged (`arch/ppc-sam440/kernel/virtualtophysical.c:20-26`), matching the local map (`mmu.c:292-299`); selected CachePreDMA/ATA callers and address constraints are covered in the existing row at 1615. m68k checks the platform's ROM virtual/physical pairs and otherwise returns the original address (`arch/m68k-all/kernel/virtualtophysical.c:28-41`); the ROM support/config-chain callers are covered by its inventory row. The earlier generic-row qualifier is updated: these three implementation families and their selected direct callers have now been reconciled, while AArch64/RISC-V translation selection details, wider DMA-buffer provenance, external callers, and hardware mapping behavior remain open. No DMA, RTAS call, mapping operation, or hardware was run; source-only.

Efika PTE0 API-field suspected omission recheck (2026-10-24; no new EK): rejected the initial suspicion that `mmu_map_page()` omits the abbreviated page index. Its PTE0 construction sets valid, segment-derived VSID, the H selector from the primary/secondary placement, and the six API bits from `(virt >> 22) & 0x3f` (`arch/ppc-chrp/efika/kernel/mmu.c:154-157`). `find_pte()` constructs the same complete word for lookup, including API and H (`:34-38,49,63-70`). This matches the MPC603e hardware PTE format and search comparison, which require V/VSID/H/API and compare API to the effective-address page index ([MPC603e User's Manual, section 5.5.2](https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/reference-manual/MPC603EUM.pdf)). The code therefore does not have the suspected missing-API defect; no PTE candidate was added. No MMU access was run; source/spec-only.

AArch64/RISC-V virtual-to-physical manifest and caller closure (2026-10-24; no new EK): reconciled the final native RISC-V and OpenSBI selections. `arch/riscv-native/sifive_u/kernel/mmakefile.src` adds only `intr`, `kernel_cpu`, `kernel_scheduler`, and `tags` to the generic kernel module, so `rom/kernel/virtualtophysical.c` supplies identity translation; its selected native `CachePreDMA()` calls it directly (`arch/riscv-native/exec/mmakefile.src:12-17,42-44`; `cachepredma.c:20-35`). The SiFive U startup builds its managed RAM directly from boot tag addresses and does not enable a virtual remapping in the checked local path (`arch/riscv-native/sifive_u/kernel/kernel_startup.c:175-215`); no nonidentity RAM translation caller was established. OpenSBI likewise uses the generic identity body; its Sv39 boot mapper explicitly maps RAM at `VA == PA` (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_mmu.c:127-137,223-240,350-416`). Its Zicbom runtime vector override operates directly on the passed address and returns it unchanged (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/exec/cpu_init.c:93-102,104-124,210-218`); no direct maintained caller of `KrnVirtualToPhysical()` on a nonidentity `KrnMapGlobal()` mapping was found. That possibility remains an external API/caller question, not a source-backed in-tree defect. AArch64 native's `mmakefile.src` does list `virtualtophysical` among local `CFILES`, but no corresponding source file exists (`:20-62`; `rg --files arch/aarch64-native/kernel`); EK8902 already records the manifest's missing C prerequisites, so no AArch64 runtime mapping behavior is credited. No build, DMA, mapping operation, or hardware was exercised; source-only.

OpenSBI `KrnMapGlobal()` physical/virtual page-offset caller audit (2026-10-24; no new EK): inspected `krnMMUMapPages()` page rounding and all checked-in direct `KrnMapGlobal()` callers. The OpenSBI PCI HIDD is the only selected caller in that target passing distinct VA and PA: `PCIDT_MapAt()` maps 64-bit PCI windows at a high VA (`pcidt_driverclass.c:60-77,139-146,461-468`). Its VA is derived from the CPU-address window by adding a constant aligned displacement (`PCIDT_HIGH_WINDOW - PCIDT_SV39_IDENTITY_LIMIT`, both page aligned; `pcidt.h:222-223`), so the within-page offsets of its VA and PA match. Other checked OpenSBI callers use identity VA/PA (`dwi2c_init.c:176`, `dwuart_init.c:149`), while the distinct allocation mapping callers in ARM PCI paths pass page-aligned allocator addresses and physical translations. `krnMMUMapPages()` accounts for the physical page offset when rounding the extent and independently aligns both bases; no maintained call with incongruent page offsets was established. The public header gives no explicit congruent-offset precondition, so arbitrary external callers remain an API-contract gap; this pass does not promote a concrete bug. No mapping was performed; source-only.

EK629 cross-architecture VBlank dispatch recheck (2026-10-24): compared the PC-only confirmation with the selected AArch64 Raspberry Pi Exec/kernel manifests and timer path. AArch64 `exec/mmakefile.src` supplies no `intserver_vblank` override, so it uses `rom/exec/intserver_vblank.c`; `bcm2711_gentimer_tick()` explicitly routes the VBlank call to CPU 0 under `__AROSEXEC_SMP__` and invokes `core_Cause(INTB_VERTB)` (`arch/aarch64-native/exec/mmakefile.src:20-27`; `rom/exec/mmakefile.src:39`; `platform_bcm2711.c:184-194`). The generic VBlank wrapper calls `IntServer()` without acquiring `IntrList` read protection; Add/Rem retain only the writer lock and local interrupt disable. A mutation on another CPU can therefore overlap the CPU-0 walk on this selected configuration as well as the already documented PC `USE_VBLANK_EMU` path. The ARM-native bcm2708 platform also calls `core_Cause(INTB_VERTB)`, but exact SMP IRQ routing was not established, so it remains out of the confirmed affected scope. Expanded EK629; no body credit change and no runtime IRQ/interleaving was exercised.


RemTask remote-running caller recheck (EK473 retained; no new EK, 2026-10-24): reread the complete `rom/exec/remtask.c` removal branch (`:58-184`) and the selected PC SMP `X86_HandleReschedTask()` transition (`arch/all-pc/exec/platform_init.c:240-321`) against `secKill()` (`rom/security/secKill.c:41-60`) and its x86-64 PC aggregate selection (`arch/x86_64-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:57-64`; `configure.in:1667-1672`). `secKill()` can pass a non-process task to `RemTask()` without checking that it is parked. On the PC SMP path, the reschedule syscall on the remover CPU removes the task from its state list and marks it `TS_TOMBSTONED`; it does not rendezvous with the task's running CPU before `RemTask()` deletes its context/ETask and frees its MemEntries. This reaffirms EK473's conditional remote-running-task lifetime issue; it is distinct from EK832's queued callback and EK830's duplicate cleanup ownership. The broader direct-caller census and per-caller serialization checks remain incomplete; this recheck adds no whole-file or whole-subsystem completion credit. No task was removed and no schedule was run; source-only.

PC `KrnDisplayAlert()` full-body and dead-end caller check (no new EK, 2026-10-24): read all 22 `cloc 2.06` C code lines in `arch/all-pc/kernel/displayalert.c`, then traced its only checked public C caller through `Exec_SystemAlert()` into `Alert()` (`rom/exec/systemalert.c:30,84-100`; `rom/exec/alert.c:179-192`). AArch64 Raspberry Pi early-diagnostic UART caller pass (EK9425 added, 2026-10-24): traced the selected exception vectors and OOM logger into `kprintf()`/`putByte()`, then compared `UART_BASE` against the boot-time ordering of SoC ID, peripheral-base, RP1-window and `serInit()` initialization. AArch64 Raspberry Pi initrd endpoint-width and package-size caller pass (EK9426 added, 2026-10-24): traced both 32/64-bit device-tree endpoint reads into the static `uint32_t pkg_size`, then through both the package-sizing scan and ELF/package loading gates (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/boot.c:67,774-800,828,974`). The endpoint difference is pointer-width before assignment; a nonempty range exactly divisible by `2^32` stores zero and is skipped by both gates. Added EK9426, explicitly conditional on an unusually large valid initrd and a usable target. For nonzero narrowed lengths, the existing EK723 covers the separate lack of bounds against the package's own record lengths; no claim is made that the 32-bit PKG length can represent a >4-GiB archive. Also confirmed the same `kprintf` sweep's `%p` sites use the AROS formatter's pointer-sized `%lx` path; integer-valued `%p` inputs remain C type mismatches, but the selected AArch64 ABI does not establish a separate wrong-value effect here. No image or boot was used; source-only.


AArch64 Raspberry Pi early diagnostic recheck (EK9425 retained; `kprintf.c` full-body count reconciled; 2026-10-24): reread all 31 physical lines / 19 `cloc 2.06` C code lines of `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/kprintf.c`, its `putBytes()` serial sink, `serialdebug.c`'s `UART_BASE` macro and `putByte()`, and the selected vector/boot initialization order. RISC-V stack-swap selected-caller reconciliation (2026-10-24; no new EK): read both `NewStackSwap` bodies and both legacy `StackSwap` assembly bodies in full, reconciled their RISC-V Exec manifests, and traced selected `pthread_create()` and DOS `RunCommand()` callers. `pthread_attr_setstack()` accepts arbitrary positive stack sizes and `pthread_create()` computes `stk_Pointer = base + size` without alignment; EK8962 already covers the resulting RISC-V 16-byte ABI misalignment. The only checked in-tree C legacy `StackSwap()` caller is `text.datatype` (`textclass.c:3553-3587`): its 12,288-byte alternate stack has an aligned extent and swaps back before freeing; it does not extend EK8962. Its deprecated-API declaration/build selection was not verified. `NewStackSwap(args == NULL)` is permitted by the public contract; the RISC-V body loads argument registers from the fallback stack address, but the selected C callers supply non-NULL arguments and no incorrect result was established for a zero-argument entry. No target or stack switch was run; source-only.

VMM usage-query allocation-failure candidate recheck and withdrawal (2026-10-28; no source-path/LOC credit): confirmed `HandleVMMsg()` sets `NoReply = TRUE` after `VMUsageInfo()` even when its list-header allocation fails and returns before signaling (`VM_Manager.c:348-354`; `mem_tracking.c:280-314`; `VM_Manager.c:373-385`). VMM page-lock request/reply caller pass (2026-10-24; no new EK): traced `VM_Manager.c:9-23,44-85,147-160` through page-handler `HandleVMMsg`, its LockPage/UnlockAllPages branches, lock-task completion in `fault.c:61-87`, and the dispatch reply/free rule (`pagehandler.c:490-529`). A failed manager message allocation returns before queueing; a queued LockPage request sets the shared result before signaling the manager, and its zero ReplySignal causes the page handler to free the request. If a partial page-lock sequence fails, `ExitPossible()` queues a stack-backed UnlockAllPages message with the manager signal bit and waits before returning; `TryToQuit()` then re-enables VM. No stale acknowledgment, unfreed request, or failed-state transition was established in these checked paths. DOS asynchronous command ownership and broader manager/page-handler lifecycle remain open. No page lock or quit path was run; source-only.

VMM token-parser bounds and caller pass (EK9428 detail restored, 2026-10-28): traced `GetNthString()` in `globals.c:397-417` and all selected VMM callers. It copies each token through the destination until whitespace/NUL and writes a terminator without receiving a destination capacity. In `mmu_table.c:343-366`, `FGets(...,79)` accepts a line up to 78 characters while fields are copied to `buffer[20]`; a config token longer than 19 bytes writes beyond that local array. The `rexx.c` caller similarly uses `cmd[30]`, `buffer[50]`, `task_name[50]`, `param[30]` and `filename[100]` with external ARexx argument strings. The MMU config path runs in `SetupMMUTable()` before `AllocAddressRange()` (`VM_Manager_Init.c:560-607`), so it is not hidden behind EK9906; the Rexx message loop is conditional on successfully completing later startup. Restored EK9428 in the detailed report/index; no malformed config or long ARexx request was supplied. Source-only.

VMM Rexx memory-type dispatch and cache caller pass (EK427 restored, 2026-10-24): traced the `REXX_MEMTYPE` switch arm in `HandleRexxMsg()` through `RexxMemType()`, the missing `break`, `RexxWriteBuffer()`, `AllocNewCache()` and page-handler `NewCache()`. A valid small memory-flag argument is parsed and stored as `CurrentConfig.MemFlags`, then reused as `DesiredWriteBufferSize`; `AllocNewCache()` rounds it down to zero pages and submits a zero-sized replacement. `NewCache()` flushes the old cache, frees it, and installs a null/zero cache, so the unintended command disables write caching. Restored EK427 in the detailed report and master index. The VMM handler is optional, and the checked AROS startup has EK9906 before the normal Rexx message loop; this report records source behavior without claiming current runtime reachability. No Rexx command or cache resize was run. Source-only.

VMM cache-resize task and allocation failure caller pass (EK9429 added; 2026-10-24): traced the manager's changed-WriteBuffer branch and ARexx `WRITEBUFFER` command through `AllocNewCache()` into the page-handler message dispatch and `NewCache()` (`VM_Manager.c:484-495,567-580`; `rexx.c:318-328`; `cache.c:238-309`; `pagehandler.c:518-528`). `NewCreateTaskA()` returns NULL after task/memlist setup failure (`rom/exec/newcreatetaska.c:253-272`), but the manager ignores it; the worker likewise returns without notification on message or backing-buffer allocation failure. The setting remains committed while the previous cache stays active, and the Rexx branch reports success. Added EK9429 with optional-handler and EK9906 reachability qualifications. Successful replacement messages are serialized by the page-handler loop; `NewCache()` flushes the old cache before releasing it, so this pass found no independent replacement-buffer ownership defect. VMM remains an optional target and default AROS startup is blocked earlier by EK9906. No task/allocation failure or cache resize was induced; source-only.

m68k `FindToolType` guest-array ABI pass (EK9433 added; 2026-10-24): traced generated `icon.library` vector 96 through `THUNK_PTR(0)` and native `FindToolType`'s `CONST STRPTR *` loop (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:4485-4490`; `workbench/libs/icon/findtooltype.c:47-60`). x86-64 PC `kernel_cpu.h` macro and context caller pass (2026-10-24; no new EK): read all 47 physical lines / 29 `cloc 2.06` code lines and traced the exact macro users. `krnSysCall(num)` emits `int $0xfe`; the selected IDT setup maps `APIC_EXCEPT_SYSCALL` to vector 0xfe and registers `core_SysCallHandler`, whose frame is the header's native `ExceptionContext`. m68k emulator containment-heap helper/direct-caller recheck (2026-10-24; no new EK): reread `M68KEmu_CreateContext()`, `M68KEmu_DestroyContext()`, `M68KEmu_HeapAlloc()` and `M68KEmu_HeapFree()` (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_memory.c:16-151`) and enumerated their direct guest/native callers in `m68kemu_run.c`, `m68kemu_thunks.c`, `m68kemu_shadow.c` and `m68kemu_m68klib.c`. Context creation clears the 32 MiB arena, frees it if context allocation fails, and initializes one in-range free block below the fixed stack; split, whole-block removal, address-ordered reinsertion and adjacent coalescing preserve the free-list shape for valid allocated addresses. `FreeVec` intentionally supplies size zero and the allocator recovers the block extent from its header. `AllocMem` forwards but the heap ignores requirement flags, and `AllocVec` drops them; the already-recorded MEMF_CLEAR and AvailMem candidates (EK9160/EK9387) remain the caller-visible consequences. Rounding/header arithmetic is already EK9159. `CreatePool` returns one documented fake handle and the pool thunks intentionally share the containment heap, so lack of native per-pool ownership is not treated as a new finding. The checked-in direct callers either propagate allocation failure or retain the separately recorded argument, shadow and library-load consequences; no additional local heap defect was established. This recheck narrows the previously open guest allocation-callsite scope but does not close all helpers, external guest binaries, Moira behavior, or target execution. No allocation, free, or emulator run was performed; source-only.


m68k CyberGraphX scalar tag-consumer trace (EK9213 expanded; 2026-10-24): corrected the earlier limited exclusion in the `m68kemu_shadow.c` inventory. The CGFX wrapper forwards these values into BestModeIDA's UWORD dimension fields; common dimensions in the guest-address interval are consequently replaced by a narrowed host pointer. ExecSMP Forbid caller cross-check: traced DOS `GetDeviceProc()` late-assign promotion under `LockDosList(LDF_ALL | LDF_READ)` into the shared semaphore acquisition and Exec `Forbid()` contract (`rom/dos/getdeviceproc.c:191-259`; `rom/dos/lockdoslist.c:60-65`; `rom/exec/forbid.c:58-60`). The shared read lock allows readers on separate CPUs, while Forbid only blocks local task switches on ExecSMP. Two simultaneous first-use promotions can both observe a late entry with no primary lock, publish separate successful target Locks, and overwrite one stored pointer; the overwritten lock is not released. Recorded the caller defect as DOS D33 rather than an Exec implementation defect. Other Forbid/Permit call families and platform interrupt-exit contracts remain open; no concurrent lookup was run. Source-only.

Timer AbortIO list-lock/reply callback follow-up (2026-10-24; no new EK): read `rom/timer/abortio.c:57-91` against the complete `ReplyMsg()`/`InternalPutMsg()` dispatch (`rom/exec/replymsg.c:49-70`; `putmsg.c:72-130`) and the timer expiry paths (`rom/timer/lowlevel.c:277-339,363-401`). AbortIO removes and marks a request while holding the timer-list write lock, then replies before releasing it. The reply-port action runs only after the reply-port spinlock is released, but still synchronously inside the caller's timer-list critical section; a callback that re-enters the same timer-list API could therefore self-deadlock. Checked the only selected `PA_CALLBACK` setup in Poseidon: it is installed on hardware-task/device ports, and its two callbacks drain/forward USB requests rather than establish a timer-list re-entry (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:9072-9115,9246-9256`). The public `PA_CALL` action is marked never-used in the selected port header (`compiler/include/exec/ports.h:50`), and no maintained timer AbortIO caller with a reentrant callback port was established. Keep lock-order/reentrant-callback behavior open for external callback clients; do not promote this conditional API composition to an Exec finding from the selected caller set. No timer request or callback was run; source-only.


m68k Intuition `NextPubScreen()` guest-buffer return follow-up (EK9432 expanded; 2026-10-24): traced generated vector -534 from `rom/intuition/intuition.conf:143` through `thunk_intuition_NextPubScreen()` (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:5609-5615`) into the native implementation (`rom/intuition/nextpubscreen.c:22-43,84-95`).
