m68k generated graphics pointer-return and structure-marshalling follow-up (EK9432 expanded; 2026-10-24): checked the selected graphics return wrappers `InitTmpRas`, `UCopperListInit`, `GfxNew`, `GfxLookUp`, `OpenMonitor`, `AllocDBufInfo`, and `AllocSpriteDataA` against their native result and paired input APIs. The guest `TmpRas` is passed directly despite its 8-byte guest/16-byte native layout, so the native pointer write plus `Size` store overruns it by four bytes; its returned arena pointer also needs host-to-guest offset conversion. Guest `UCopList` is likewise passed directly at 12 bytes for a 24-byte native layout, and native initialization writes four bytes beyond it; its returned internal `CopList` pointer is unconverted. Native-allocated or internal `CopList`, `ExtendedNode`, `MonitorSpec`, `DBufInfo`, and `ExtSprite` results have no corresponding guest shadow, and paired GfxFree/CloseMonitor/FreeDBufInfo/FreeSpriteData thunks resolve guest arena/shadow pointers rather than the returned native addresses. ROMTag zero-resident sort recheck (EK144 detail/index restored; 2026-10-24): reread the allocation, population, terminator write and bubble-sort sequence in source order (`rom/kernel/kernel_romtags.c:303-341`) and its sole generic startup caller (`rom/kernel/prepareexecbase.c:21-36`). CreateMsgPort DOS RunHandler failure-order caller trace (2026-10-24; no new EK): checked `rom/dos/runhandler.c:131-168` against the direct Exec creator/deleter contract. `RunHandler()` starts the new process with `CreateNewProcTags()` before calling `CreateMsgPort()` for its startup reply; if port allocation fails, it frees only the boot path and returns (`:142-146`), leaving the already-started handler without its startup packet at `:163-166`. DOS report D28 already records the caller-side failure path, including the separate unchecked process result; this is not promoted as an Exec `CreateMsgPort()` defect. Packet-allocation failure after process start takes a similar early return after deleting the reply port (`:149-153`). No handler start or allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

KrnModifyIRQHandler finding-detail and selected SMP configuration recheck (EK8774 expanded; 2026-10-24): checked its generic manifest entry and public vector declaration (`rom/kernel/mmakefile.src:46`; `kernel.conf:75`) against the setter (`modifyirqhandler.c:57-73`), generic callback dispatch (`addirqhandler.c:125-141`) and PC replacement (`arch/all-pc/kernel/addirqhandler.c:115-131`). The generic SMP walker uses `kb_IntrSpinLock` in READ mode, which the setter never takes; the PC override has no cross-CPU lock at all. `Disable()` is local to the calling CPU. x86-64 PC config enables ExecSMP for the `smp` target variant (`configure.in:1647-1671`); target-independent generic SMP configs select the generic dispatcher unless an architecture override replaces it. No direct C/header/assembly API caller was found, so the external-client trigger and old-state lifetime consequence remain qualified. Replaced the previous reconstruction-only report block with a detailed finding. No IRQ or concurrent update was run; source-only.

EK8774 ExecSMP architecture-selection closure (2026-10-24): confirmed the available configured ExecSMP variants and their dispatcher selection. `configure.in:1647-1671` enables `__AROSEXEC_SMP__` for x86-64 PC `smp`, whose `arch/all-pc/kernel/mmakefile.src:20-26` selects the unlocked architecture `addirqhandler.c`. The Raspberry Pi branch enables `__AROSEXEC_SMP__` for its `smp` target variants (`configure.in:2110-2199`); `arch/all-native/kernel/mmakefile.src:20-28` supplies no `addirqhandler.c` replacement, so the generic `rom/kernel/addirqhandler.c` read-lock path is selected. This narrows EK8774 to the two checked configured SMP families rather than an unspecified generic set; no direct in-tree modifier caller was found. No build or IRQ operation was run; source-only.

Console completion DOS-list BSTR candidate disposition (EK8973 not promoted; 2026-10-24): rechecked `ScanVol()` against the BSTR representation and selected public DOS-list constructors (`rom/filesys/console_handler/completion.c:381-397`; `compiler/include/dos/bptr.h:66-86`; `compiler/include/dos/dosextens.h:371-379`; `rom/dos/makedosentry.c:51-88`; `rom/expansion/makedosnode.c:131-176`). Standard BSTR storage does not guarantee a C terminator, but `struct DosList` is explicitly private, and both selected constructors allocate/initialize the name storage with a trailing NUL before publication; `AROS_FAST_BSTR` uses C strings by definition. The earlier conditional mention of external “valid DOS-list producers” did not establish a supported producer that publishes unterminated names. EK8973 is therefore not treated as an active candidate; no entry was found in the detailed report or master index to remove. The remaining `ScanVol()` source slice was not otherwise re-audited by this disposition. No DOS list or completion operation was run; source-only.

Console completion signed match-count overflow pass (EK9441 added; 2026-10-24): re-read `completioninfo`, `AddMatchNode()`, `Completion()` and the selected TAB dispatch, then checked the `WORD` typedef and selected FAT directory-index limit (`rom/filesys/console_handler/completion.c:45-57,317-344,350-377,773-788`; `compiler/include/exec/types.h:58-62`; `rom/filesys/fat/direntry.c:84-99,122-172`; ARM/AArch64 package manifests `:129-133`). Confirmed the signed 16-bit counter increments once for every unique sorted match with no cap, while the caller opens the chooser only for `nummatchnodes > 1` and autoinserts only for exactly one. On low-16-bit narrowing, 32,768 matches produce a negative count and suppress both paths; narrowed the candidate to chooser loss and dropped the prior unsupported 65,537-match false-unique scenario, which is beyond the selected FAT backend's 65,536 raw-entry limit. Added EK9441 to the detailed Exec/Kernel report and master index. The wrap result is implementation-defined and therefore explicitly conditional on target/compiler behavior; no directory, chooser, allocation condition, or build was run. Source-only.

Console completion ExNext error-propagation pass (EK9442 added; 2026-10-24): traced `ScanDir()` through `ExNext()`, `dopacket2()`, `IoErr()` and the selected FAT `ACTION_EXAMINE_NEXT` handler (`rom/filesys/console_handler/completion.c:350-377,773-788`; `rom/dos/exnext.c:34-53,73-81`; `rom/dos/dopkt.c:138-149`; `rom/dos/ioerr.c:45-51`; `rom/filesys/fat/packet.c:166-210`). The public ExNext contract says false can mean either end-of-directory or a real error and directs callers to check IoErr; FAT propagates non-end failures from lock validation, directory-handle setup/iteration, file locking and FIB construction through `dp_Res2` into the caller process. ScanDir discards that distinction, then Completion may auto-insert its sole accumulated match as if enumeration were complete. Added EK9442 and replaced the older ledger-only EK8794 references. The false-unique consequence is conditional on an error after one match and another matching entry beyond the failure; no error or completion was induced. Source-only.

ExecSMP ChildStatus two-list transfer recheck (EK812 detailed and indexed; 2026-10-24): re-read the complete `ChildStatus()` scans, selected SMP child-exit transfer, `Forbid()` semantics, POSIX `waitpid()` early child check and POSIXC notified-child creation (`rom/exec/childstatus.c:53-88`; `exec_util.c:307-329`; `rom/exec/forbid.c:55-60`; `compiler/crt/posixc/waitpid.c:110-118`; `compiler/crt/posixc/__vfork.c:479-485`). The exit path holds `iet_TaskLock` across the remove from `et_Children` and later append under the port lock, but `ChildStatus()` takes neither that task lock nor a common lock spanning both lists; its local `Forbid()` does not exclude another CPU. A scan during the gap returns `CHILD_NOTFOUND`, which the selected waitpid caller converts directly to ECHILD. Restored EK812 to the detailed report and index from its prior ledger-only state. The report is limited to ExecSMP and the exact conditional schedule; no task, wait, or SMP execution was run. Source-only.

ExecSMP ChildStatus live-list lifetime consequence reconciliation (EK812 expanded; 2026-10-27; no new finding or LOC credit): rechecked the full `ChildStatus()` live-list loop (`rom/exec/childstatus.c:53-72`) against `Exec_CleanupETask()`'s non-notifying exit path (`rom/exec/exec_util.c:310-330,361-369`). A valid query for a notified child still traverses all sibling nodes; an unnotified sibling can be removed from `et_Children` and freed on another CPU because ChildStatus does not take `iet_TaskLock`. Expanded EK812's detailed report and both master-index summaries to include this conditional stale-node access alongside the already-reported false `CHILD_NOTFOUND` during notified-child list transfer. Scope remains ExecSMP and conditional cross-CPU overlap; no task exit or schedule was run.

VMM x86 trap/free-queue SMP withdrawal recheck (EK638 remains withdrawn; 2026-10-27; source confirmation only): reread all `Free` and `PageReq` list producer/consumer sites and the x86 Trap-14 caller. `TrapPageFault()` removes from `Free` and appends to `PageReq` under `Forbid()` (`workbench/system/VMM/x86/traphandler_x86.c:55-85`); `AddFree()`/`AddPageReq()` and `HandlePageFault()` use the same local-only protection (`fault.c:10-27,848-887`), and the page-handler returns structures through `InformTask()`/`AddFree()`. Exec documents that `Forbid()` does not serialize another CPU on ExecSMP (`rom/exec/forbid.c:45-60`), so a working multi-CPU x86 VMM would need shared-list synchronization. Kept this out of active findings because the selected AROS VMM startup does not establish the virtual range needed for `ShouldHandleFault()` to accept a page fault (EK9906; `mmu_table.c:908-928`); no current reachable fault-path defect is established. This is a revalidation of the withdrawn EK638 condition, not a new finding or runtime claim; no VMM or SMP schedule was run.


Unix ColdReboot selected-caller census (2026-10-24; no new EK): searched direct call sites and traced the maintained command path (`workbench/c/Reboot.c:59-75`), selected generic debug `RE` dispatch (`rom/exec/debug_internal.c:108-111`), optional Poseidon boot keyboard and HID reset paths (`rom/usb/classes/bootkeyboard/bootkeyboard.class.c:578`; `rom/usb/classes/hid/hid.class.c:6601`), and bootstrap status consumer (`arch/all-unix/bootstrap/kickstart.c:150-163`). EK22 Unix startup consequence caller trace (2026-10-24): followed failure beyond `Kernel_Init()` through the selected single-task Resident scan. The resident's failed non-autoinit initializer returns NULL through `InitResident()`; `InitCode()` ignores that return and `kernel_startup()` unconditionally calls `core_Start(hostlib)`. `core_Start()` dereferences `getKernelBase()->kb_PlatformData` before any NULL check. Since `setKernelBase()` is reached only after successful `PlatformData` allocation, the second-allocation failure leaves the global unset and the selected startup reaches a NULL dereference (`rom/exec/initresident.c:155-169`; `rom/exec/initcode.c:86-96`; `arch/all-unix/kernel/kernel_startup.c:298-300`; `kernel.c:218-221`; `allockernelbase.c:35-43`). Expanded EK22's consequence to include this source-level startup failure; host signal/fault handling remains untested. No failure or boot was induced; source-only.


Unix `core_Start()` failure-return caller recheck (EK9444 added; 2026-10-24): traced `HostLib_GetInterface()` allocation/missing-symbol semantics through all `core_Start()` early returns and its selected startup caller. On hosted builds `krnPanic()` returns, as the adjacent startup failure branch documents (`kernel_startup.c:261-264`); nevertheless `kernel_startup()` discards `core_Start()`'s FALSE result and enters `InitCode(RTF_COLDSTART, 0)` (`:297-300`). Those returns precede signal mask and trap/IRQ/syscall handler setup (`kernel.c:236-247,260-330`). The non-NULL unresolved-symbol result remains allocated; HostLib documents that even incomplete interfaces must be passed to `HostLib_DropInterface()` (`getinterface.c:41-49`). Added EK9444 for continuing cold-start after failed signal subsystem initialization and the separate partial-interface leak. Host allocation/symbol failure and later boot behavior were not induced; source-only.
Exec m68k ExitIntr saved-frame and return-path pass (2026-10-24; no new EK): traced every selected Amiga Level 1-7 normal/direct trap wrapper through the installed vector-6 stub, `core_ExitIntr()` and `__Schedule_this` (`arch/m68k-amiga/kernel/amiga_irq.c:155-176,306-336`; `arch/m68k-all/exec/exitintr.S:18-42`; `arch/m68k-all/kernel/kernel_intr.c:21-41`; `arch/m68k-all/exec/schedule.S:19-28`). The wrapper's six saved 32-bit registers place SR at the assembly's `SP+24` test offset; the supervisor return bypasses task scheduling, while user return enters the common scheduler label with the original register frame intact. The generic C vector is explicitly an unimplemented private architecture entry, and other maintained kernel interrupt paths select architecture-specific schedulers. No supported in-tree mismatch found; arbitrary external private-vector calls remain outside scope. No interrupt or context switch was run; source-only.


Pthread stack-size minimum contract pass (EK8837 added to detailed report and index; 2026-10-24): re-read both `pthread_attr_setstack()` and `pthread_attr_setstacksize()` implementations, the public `PTHREAD_STACK_MIN` definition (40,960 bytes), the selected pthread link-library manifest, and `pthread_create()`'s ordinary and custom-stack paths. Both setters accept an undersized value because the shared setter checks only null attributes and the non-null-address/zero-size combination. `pthread_create()` forwards a positive value as `NP_StackSize`/`NP_PPCStackSize` when it allocates the stack, or uses it to calculate the custom stack upper bound before switching. POSIX requires `EINVAL` below `PTHREAD_STACK_MIN`; recorded the API mismatch and conditional downstream consequence without asserting a runtime stack fault. No thread was created; source-only.

Pthread stack-address preservation follow-up (EK9450 added; 2026-10-24): traced `pthread_attr_setstacksize()`'s `pthread_attr_setstack(attr, NULL, size)` call through the shared setter's unconditional assignments, `pthread_attr_getstack()` readback, and `pthread_create()`'s custom-stack versus Exec-allocated-stack branches. A valid custom stack set earlier is therefore discarded when the caller changes only its size; the subsequent thread uses an Exec-created stack. This is distinct from EK8837's missing minimum-size validation. No thread was created; source-only.

Pthread attribute-initialization platform stack-size follow-up (2026-10-24; no new finding): compared `pthread_attr_init()`'s inherited `tc_SPUpper - tc_SPLower` / MorphOS task-attribute values with the public 40,960-byte `PTHREAD_STACK_MIN`, platform `AROS_STACKSIZE` values, task stack floors and `pthread_create()` propagation. The m68k generic default macro is 16,384 bytes, MorphOS is 32,768, and m68k task creation may floor at 4,096; these are below the pthread minimum and can become the inherited requested child stack size. The POSIX `pthread_attr_init()` contract initializes each attribute to the implementation's default value ([Open Group Issue 7](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/pthread_attr_init.html)); its minimum-size error is specified for explicit `pthread_attr_setstacksize()` calls. The inherited values therefore do not independently establish a conformance defect. MorphOS is a configured target (`configure.in:2017-2018`), but `NewGetTaskAttrs()` has no implementation in this source tree, so its task-size results and client adequacy remain unverified. No task/thread was created; source-only.

PC SMP IPI per-hook mask failure pass (EK8834 added to detailed report and index; 2026-10-24): re-read `smp_Initialize()`, `KrnAllocCPUMask()`, `core_DoCallIPI()`, the remote completion handler, and the selected Exec `Signal()` caller. An IPI-hook array can be successfully allocated while either mask allocation for an individual hook fails; the hook is nevertheless placed on the free list with a NULL mask. Its first use performs nonzero-length clear/copy operations on the mask, and the remote handler later reads/writes both masks. Confirmed the remote Signal route is selected when ExecSMP affinity is enabled and the target task runs on another CPU or is outside the caller's affinity. This is distinct from EK8833's hook-array allocation failure and empty-list wait. No allocation failure or IPI was induced; source-only.

PC SMP IPI hook-pool allocation failure pass (EK8833 added to detailed report and index; 2026-10-24): traced the failed aligned hook-array allocation through `smp_Initialize()`'s log-only branch, successful SMP setup/wake path, all free-list insertion/removal sites, `core_DoCallIPI()`'s retry loop, and the selected remote `Signal()` caller. No initial hook means the free list is permanently empty: the only re-add path requires completion of a hook that was first removed from this list. A later cross-CPU signal therefore spins indefinitely while trying to allocate a hook. Separately tracked from EK8834's checked-out hook containing a NULL CPU mask. No allocation failure or signal was induced; source-only.

PC x86-64 ExecSMP AP idle-task failure/dispatch pass (EK8835 added to detailed report and index; 2026-10-24): traced `cpu_BootStrap()` through `Exec_X86CreateIdleTask()`, `smp_Entry()`'s bootstrap-task `RemTask()`, and the scheduler's no-eligible-task fallback. Idle-task creation can return NULL on metadata/name/task allocation failure, but the bootstrap code ignores the result and continues. Once the bootstrap task is tombstoned, if no other task is eligible for that AP, `core_Dispatch()` chooses it again; the tombstone branch cannot launch, `core_Switch()` refuses the switch, and the dispatcher recurses. This is separate from EK839's resource leak and EK8790's pre-adoption affinity-mask ownership. No AP startup or allocation failure was induced; source-only.

Exec/Kernel candidate-to-report crosswalk (2026-10-24): reconciled every unique EK ID in the coverage finding table against report headings and master-index links. Promoted EK8833 (empty IPI hook pool), EK8834 (unchecked per-hook CPU masks), and EK8835 (AP idle-task failure/dispatcher recursion) to detailed report sections with matching index links. Marked EK8770 as a cross-reference to canonical EK9402 and EK8815 as a cross-reference to canonical EK9237; no duplicate report entries are needed. All remaining differences are those two explicitly mapped aliases.

MUIScreen `AddTask()` caller closure (2026-10-24; no new Exec finding): reread the full selected `workbench/libs/muiscreen/muiscreen_init.c` path against `rom/exec/addtask.c` and `rom/exec/newaddtask.c`. The caller allocates the Task and separate 4 KiB stack, then returns FALSE on AddTask failure without freeing either allocation; this is already documented as GD490. On success, the worker remains active until the break signal; expunge returns without joining it (GD4535), and normal worker exit does not free either allocation because the task has an empty `tc_MemEntry` list (GD4536). These are caller-owned allocations/lifecycle defects, not duplicate Exec implementation findings. Failure semantics and teardown consequences are source-traced only; no allocation failure or expunge interleaving was run. This closes the MUIScreen direct-caller slice only; trackdisk, network-driver and other caller/platform audits remain open.


Exec `NewAddTask()` network-driver caller follow-up (2026-10-24; OD3260 expanded, no new Exec finding): compared legacy `AddUnitTask` wrappers and allocation/cleanup paths in Intel Pro/100, Broadcom4400, NvidiaNet, Realtek8180, Atheros5000, Prism2, VIA Rhine and EtherLink III, plus the direct AddTask service workers in BCM GENET and DWMAC. On AROS the legacy wrappers call `NewAddTask`; three callers leak their separately allocated 4-KiB stack when ETask setup fails after stack allocation (OD3260: Realtek8180, Atheros5000 and Prism2). The other five legacy callers free an allocated stack even when task insertion fails. BCM GENET and DWMAC attach task/stack ownership to `tc_MemEntry` and their AddTask-failure cleanup explicitly releases those allocations. The report scope was expanded only for the three verified leak sites. This closes the worker-stack allocation/failure-cleanup slice for these callers, not their full driver lifecycle or the entire direct `NewAddTask` call graph; trackdisk and the remaining caller/platform audits stay open. No allocation failure or task was induced; source-only.


EK9099 Raspberry Pi AArch64 ExecSMP configuration verification (2026-10-24; existing finding strengthened): checked `configure.in`'s `r*pi` AArch64 branch and variant handling (`:2113-2139,2195-2199`): the platform advertises SMP support, and the explicit `smp` target variant defines `__AROSEXEC_SMP__`. The AArch64 Raspberry Pi package selects `USB/massstorage` (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:227`). Combined with the already-traced MassStorage `libExpunge` → `RemDevice` → `devExpunge` path and generic OpenDevice lookup gap, this establishes a concrete selected ExecSMP configuration for EK9099. Other Raspberry Pi variants are not claimed as ExecSMP. No configure, package build, device open, or expunge was run; source-only.


Exec OpenLibrary/RemLibrary race current source recheck (EK8981 entry expanded, 2026-10-24): reconciled the lock macros and ordinary-library generator branch precisely. `OpenLibrary()` releases the `LibList` read lock before checking the version and calling the Open vector; on ExecSMP its local `Forbid` does not stop a remover on another CPU. The ordinary library generator invokes `OPENLIB` hooks before incrementing `lib_OpenCnt` (`tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1285-1302`), while `RemLibrary()` invokes ExpungeLib under only local `Forbid`; a zero-count generated expunger removes/frees the base. Rechecked the VMM `VMLib` ExpungeLib hook returns success and its optional-target `ExitPossible()` calls RemLibrary after FindName; the default aggregate still excludes VMM. Replaced EK8981's reconstructed formal report entry with the explicit trigger, sequence, consequence and scope. LDDemon remains excluded from this interleaving because it holds the LibList write lock through its sweep. No open/expunge or SMP schedule was run; source-only.


AArch64 BCM27xx late-secondary timeout candidate restoration and caller recheck (EK8903 restored; 2026-10-24): re-read the assembly trampoline loads (`arch/aarch64-native/kernel/kernel_cpu.c:101-110`), the shared stack/TLS slot writes and cache publication (`platform_bcm27xx.c:362-388`), the one-second lock wait and timeout unlock/continue (`:282-298,391-428`), and the secondary's completion unlock (`kernel_cpu.c:184-192`). Confirmed that an earlier core delayed beyond the timeout can observe a later iteration's stack/TLS, while a core that already loaded its values can release a later attempt's reused lock. Restored the surviving EK8903 coverage candidate as a detailed report and index entry; actual firmware delay beyond one second remains unverified. Live heading/link reconciliation now finds 538 unique active Exec/Kernel entries; the previous 503/504 snapshots were stale. No boot or CPU start was performed; source-only.

`KrnGetCPUNumber()` architecture-selection and caller-boundary reconciliation (2026-10-24; no new finding): re-read the generic fallback and all five maintained overrides (`rom/kernel/getcpunumber.c`; `arch/{all-pc,arm-native,aarch64-native,riscv-all,riscv64-all}/kernel/getcpunumber.c`) and matched each replacement to its local kernel manifest. Searched `configure.in`: the only `__AROSEXEC_SMP__` definitions are x86-64 PC `smp` and Raspberry Pi `smp`; their manifests select the all-PC and AArch64-native overrides. Exec's affinity and CPU-index callers are guarded by that macro, while OpenSBI's standalone branch does not enable it and its current startup runs only the boot hart. No additional generic-fallback defect was established. The coverage row now narrows the remaining question to non-SMP platform bootstrap/interrupt ordering and external clients rather than unspecified override selection. No CPU query or startup path was run; source-only.

`KrnSwitch()` selected entry/caller matrix pass (2026-10-24; no new finding): searched all C/assembly call expressions and found the sole checked-in direct call in `rom/exec/wait.c:113`, after the task is moved to `TS_WAIT` and its wait list (`:92-104`). Searched every `KrnSwitch` definition: generic `rom/kernel/switch.c`, m68k `arch/m68k-all/kernel/switch.c` (`Supervisor(m68k_VoluntarySwitch)`), and PPC CHRP/Efika `arch/ppc-chrp/efika/kernel/scheduler.c` (`SC_SWITCH`). Confirmed the manifests select the m68k override and PPC local scheduler; Unix/MinGW instead replace `core_SysCall` and decode the wait state, while PC/ARM/AArch64/RISC-V route through the generic syscall wrapper and platform-specific `cpu_Switch`/dispatch. The ledger row now records that matrix. This does not close per-architecture trap-frame or scheduler handoffs; no task switch was run. Source-only.

`Wait()`/`cpu_Switch()` task-lock release and scheduler-handoff recheck (EK9451 added; 2026-10-24): traced `Wait()`'s TS_WAIT/list publication and carried task lock through the selected x86-64 PC, ARM32 and AArch64 `cpu_Switch()` paths (`rom/exec/wait.c:92-113`; `arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/kernel_cpu.c:362-375`; `arch/arm-native/kernel/kernel_cpu.c:389-447`; `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/kernel_cpu.c:354-391`). The switch paths release `tc_SpinLock` immediately after context save, before the old CPU enters `core_Switch()`; ARM32/AArch64 also continue task CPU-accounting writes after unlocking. Traced the matching Signal wake (`rom/exec/signal.c:269-302,350-385`), AArch64 `Exec_ReschedTask()` from TS_WAIT to TaskReady (`arch/aarch64-native/exec/platform_init.c:114-180`), remote dispatch to TS_RUN/TaskRunning, and the original CPU's core_Switch() RUN branch that removes/requeues a task now observed as TS_RUN. This establishes the conditional duplicate-running/ready-list interleaving for configured x86-64 PC and Raspberry Pi ARM32/AArch64 ExecSMP variants. It is distinct from EK9018's stale list-lock selection between concurrent PC signal helpers and EK274's task lifetime after signal unlock. Replaced the prior Wait ledger conclusion that no separate Wait finding was established. No signal, task switch or SMP schedule was run; source-only.

AArch64 spinlock encoding versus shared public initializer pass (EK9452 added; 2026-10-24): compared `spinlock_t`'s shared bit-field/macro layout and `SPINLOCK_INIT_WRITE_LOCKED` (`compiler/include/aros/types/spinlock_s.h:31-60`) with the selected AArch64 lock, try-lock and unlock implementations (`arch/aarch64-native/kernel/{spinlock,spintrylock,spinunlock}.c`). The header and PC implementation use `SPINLOCKF_WRITE` at bit 27; AArch64 writes/tests bit 31 and its unlock path therefore treats a bit-27 prelocked initializer as a reader count, decrements it, and leaves a nonzero word that prevents later write acquisition. The shared header's `slock.write` field is also declared at bit 27, unlike the AArch64 writer marker. A repository-wide C/header/assembly search found no in-tree `SPINLOCK_INIT_WRITE_LOCKED` use or direct `slock.write` consumer; the trigger is a public shared-header/client integration path on selected Raspberry Pi AArch64 ExecSMP. No lock operation or target was run; source-only.

AArch64 BCM27xx startup-lock initialization and timeout caller recheck (EK8903 confirmed; no new EK; 2026-10-24): read the complete selected AArch64 `KrnSpinInit()` override (`arch/aarch64-native/kernel/spininit.c`) and traced its only boot-time shared-lock initialization in `bcm27xx_init()` to the serialized CPU-launch loop (`platform_bcm27xx.c:307,362-428`). The one-second deadline is `CNTFRQ_EL0` added to `CNTPCT_EL0` (`:282-298`). On timeout the boot CPU explicitly unlocks `startup_lock` and advances; subsequent iterations overwrite the common trampoline's stack/TLS slots (`:373-382`), while `mpcore_trampoline` reads those slots only after execution begins (`kernel_cpu.c:101-110`). A core that has entered the C startup path unlocks the same global lock only after bootstrap and per-core initialization (`kernel_cpu.c:168-192`). This reconfirms EK8903's two distinct late-start interleavings: stale shared trampoline values and completion of the wrong launch attempt. The checked source establishes the one-second timeout/reuse window, but does not establish that shipped firmware can exceed it. No spinlock, CPU startup or timeout was induced; source-only.
ARM32/AArch64 boot-task affinity failure recheck (EK8867 restored to detailed report/index; 2026-10-24): reconciled both selected kernel `platform_PostInit()` implementations with their Exec `Exec_ARMCPUSMPInit()` retries. Each kernel path silently ignores a failed CPU-mask allocation before `ARMI_Init()` releases secondaries; the later Exec hook retries and also ignores failure. Both selected SMP schedulers treat NULL task affinity as eligible on any CPU. Traced `Exec_InitServices()`'s priority-127 housekeeper launch to the boot task's ready-list transition and the secondaries' timer scheduling; both platform sources explicitly say coldstart work is not migration-safe. Restored EK8867 as a conditional cross-CPU coldstart migration candidate, requiring both mask allocations to fail and qualifying the ordinary secondary path behind the earlier EK153/EK726 bootstrap list-head defects. No allocation, CPU startup, or scheduling interleaving was run; source-only.
EK8867 build-gate and mask-allocation contract follow-up (2026-10-24): verified the Raspberry Pi `smp` configure branch defines `__AROSEXEC_SMP__` (`configure.in:2195-2199`) and both selected kernel mask allocators return the nullable `AllocMem()` result for their 4-byte mask (`arch/arm-native/kernel/alloccpumask.c:18-25`; `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/alloccpumask.c:14-22`). Rechecked each kernel `platform_PostInit()` allocation before `ARMI_Init()` and the subsequent Exec retry; platform comments explicitly place the Exec retry after secondary release. This supports EK8867's two-failure trigger and selected target scope. No memory failure, CPU startup, or migration was run; source-only.

Coverage checkpoint (2026-10-24; reproducible tracked-path `cloc 2.06` recount, updated for SysMon module caller pass): deduplicated ledger table paths that resolve to tracked local C, C++, header, assembly, or include files; unqualified basenames were resolved only when unique in the checkout. Counted a file as body-reviewed only when a table's status cell explicitly begins with `Full`, `Read all`, `All <line-count> ... lines`, or `Complete body/file`; excluded paths explicitly marked excluded/unbuilt/not-selected. Result: 1,108/1,622 paths and 232,349/362,506 code lines (64.1%). This is coverage of the files represented in this ledger, not proof that every build-selected file is inventoried, and it measures body reads rather than caller/platform/end-to-end review completion. Rows with targeted checks or unresolved statuses do not receive full-body credit.

x86-64 PC interrupt-entry full assembly pass (EK9190/EK824 rechecked; 2026-10-24): read all 222 physical lines / 189 `cloc 2.06` assembly code lines in `arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/core_interrupts.s`, selected by the x86-64 PC kernel manifest. Compared every exception stub's error-code convention and generated hardware IRQ stub with the shared frame offsets, then traced `FXSData` creation into `core_IRQHandle()`'s aligned `movaps` stores and `cpu_Trap()`/exception-handler return behavior. Recomputed the selected ring-0 soft-interrupt callback stack case for EK9190: a pending IRQ at ordinary callback entry produces an unaligned 64-byte save area, so the first `movaps` faults. Reconfirmed EK824's error-code mismatch for vectors 21, 29 and 30 and the lack of a selected handler or feature-enabling path; retained it as a conditional frame-ABI defect, not a claimed default runtime failure. Read the FS selector/base restore and `core_Supervisor` stack handoff against the selected syscall ABI; no additional issue established. No assembly was built and no interrupt, trap, or supervisor transition was run; source-only. Caller timing beyond the traced SoftIntDispatch route and actual CPU/firmware feature state remain open.

x86-64 PC AP trampoline source-order and timeout-caller pass (EK9454 added; 2026-10-24): read all 137 physical lines / 98 `cloc 2.06` assembly code lines of the selected `smpbootstrap.s`. Reconciled each assembly data offset with the C `SMPBootstrap` structure, then traced the BSP's `smp_Setup()` copy and PML4/IP initialization, per-AP stack/argument writes, IPI wake and 50-second ready-lock wait, and `boot64`'s sequential argument loads into `smp_Entry()`. Confirmed that timeout does not cancel/wait for the AP before the next loop iteration overwrites the shared argument block; added EK9454 with the at-least-two-AP and delayed-consumption conditions. Checked the 32-bit PML4 load against the selected x86-64 PC boot-memory setup and retained the documented external/high-memory loader limitation without promoting another finding. AllocMem's selected x86-64 worst-case alignment is 16 bytes, matching the initial AP stack's C-call alignment; no stack-alignment candidate was added. No assembly was built and no AP, timeout, or mode transition was run; source-only.

x86-64 PC AP stack alignment and call-ABI follow-up (2026-10-24; no new EK): traced `_APICStackBase` allocation (`arch/all-pc/kernel/smp.c:261-272`) through `AllocMem()`'s documented `sizeof(struct MemChunk)` alignment (`rom/exec/allocmem.c:60-62`) and the x86-64 `AROS_WORSTALIGN`/`AROS_STACKALIGN` definitions (both 16; `arch/x86_64-all/include/aros/cpu.h:50-51`). The three-stack allocation size is a multiple of 16, so the initial stack pointer remains 16-byte aligned. `boot64` loads that pointer directly and performs a normal `call`, giving the callee the x86-64 ABI entry alignment (RSP mod 16 = 8). When MungWall is enabled, its user-pointer offset is `MUNGWALL_BLOCK_SHIFT`: `MUNGWALLHEADER_SIZE` is rounded to `MEMCHUNK_TOTAL`, and `MUNGWALL_SIZE` is 32, a multiple of x86-64's 16-byte `MEMCHUNK_TOTAL` (`rom/exec/mungwall.h:22-27`; `compiler/arossupport/include/debug.h:224-235`). Thus the wrapper preserves the alignment. This confirms the stack-alignment assumption recorded in the EK9454 pass; it does not address the separate SMP allocation-failure findings EK8828/EK8830/EK8831 or late-AP timeout window. No allocation or CPU startup was run; source-only.

AArch64 Raspberry Pi `BootMsg` storage/caller lifetime pass (2026-10-24; no new finding): traced the selected bootstrap tag-buffer placement (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/boot.c:421,1088`) to `bm_boottags` within `struct bcm2708bootmem` (`boot/include/boot.h:12-17`; `boot/include/bcm2708_boot.h:36-44`). The kernel memory producer clamps the first allocatable `KRN_MEMLower` to at least `sizeof(struct bcm2708bootmem)` (`boot.c:302-307`), keeping the tag array below the region handed to the kernel TLSF allocator. The bootstrap/stack/tag area is also within the protected bootstrap interval supplied through `KRN_ProtAreaStart/End` (`boot.c:761-767`), which kernel startup reserves with `mhe_AllocAbs` before normal allocations (`arch/aarch64-native/kernel/kernel_startup.c:350-360`). The selected startup keeps the pointer as global `BootMsg`, and generic `KrnGetBootInfo()` returns it (`rom/kernel/getbootinfo.c:44-49`); the shared ARM `KrnVirtualToPhysical()` later reads kernel base tags from the same retained list. The OpenFirmware tree and command-line string are rebuilt into kernel memory before their tags are emitted (`boot.c:1047-1063`), while the bootstrap callback/name reside in the protected bootstrap image. Thus this target's tag-list storage and observed retained tag values remain backed for their use; no dangling-tag candidate established. This closes only the AArch64 Raspberry Pi producer/lifetime slice, not the other `BootMsg` producers or external tag-data consumers. No boot or allocator operation was run; source-only.

m68k Amiga `BootMsg` relocation allocation-failure pass (EK9453 added; 2026-10-24): traced the tag list's stack-residency check and copy in `arch/m68k-amiga/boot/start.c:212-232` through the platform `KrnGetBootInfo()` override and selected command-line consumer in `boot/mmu.c:192-205`. If the relocation `AllocMem()` fails, `newbootmsg` remains NULL but is still published to `PlatformData.BootMsg`; the reset continues, silently removing all boot tags. Added EK9453, scoped the consequence to lost boot metadata and possible omission of command-line MMU selection, and explicitly did not claim a null-list crash or certain boot failure. No allocation failure or reset was induced; source-only.

RISC-V OpenSBI `BootMsg` storage, bounds, and warm-restart pass (2026-10-24; no new finding): traced `krnPrepareBootTags()`'s static `BootTags[BOOTTAG_MAX]` through its caller, `BootMsg`, `krnPrepareExecBase()`, later `KRN_DebugInfo` update and generic `KrnGetBootInfo()` consumers. It emits eight fixed tags and at most four optional entries (one each for `CmdLine` and EFI system table, plus two framebuffer tags), followed by `TAG_DONE`: at most 13 entries fit the 16-entry array (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_startup.c:82-83,379-437,655-656,836-845`). `BootTags` is kernel BSS and lies below `__kernel_end`, while the primary heap begins at aligned `__kernel_end` (`:779-783`); the warm-kick path reruns `_start_kernel`, clears BSS and rebuilds the list before Exec initialization (`startup.S:129-165`; `kernel_startup.c:655-656`). Thus the static tag-list storage remains reserved during normal use and is reinitialized before warm-restart publication; no capacity or lifetime candidate established. The FDT/EFI payload-address and extent contracts remain separate open checks already tracked under EK8860/EK9042 and other boot findings. No boot, warm restart, or tag consumer was run; source-only.

RISC-V OpenSBI MMU body and mapping-offset caller pass (2026-10-24; no new finding): reread all 278 `cloc 2.06` code lines in `kernel_mmu.c`, including Sv39 walks, 1-GiB/2-MiB splitting, 4-KiB mappings, permissions, unmapping, initial RAM/firmware maps and the fixed page-table pool. Traced `krnMMUMapPages()` through the public `KrnMapGlobal` wrapper, PLIC, EFI framebuffer and every in-tree PCIDT `MapAt` call. Startup, PLIC, UART/I2C register maps, and identity-window PCIDT maps pass the same VA/PA offset. For the high PCIDT window, `mem64Va` and `PCIDT_HIGH_WINDOW` are page-aligned and `pcidt_mem64_va()` adds the same `cpu - mem64CpuBase` displacement to that base; the resulting virtual and physical page offsets match even for a non-page-aligned BAR. Thus no selected caller demonstrates the mapper's unsupported unequal-offset input, and no finding was promoted. Public external callers remain unverified. Rechecked pool-exhaustion/unmap behavior against existing EK9043; no additional reachable in-tree unmap caller. No mapping, unmapping, MMU, or hardware operation was run; source-only.

SysMon task-detail Status value follow-up (EK9455; 2026-10-24): read all 1,090 physical lines of `workbench/system/SysMon/tasks.c` in source order and reconciled the selected detail-window construction, timer refresh, list hooks, task.resource enumeration/removal paths, and MUI task-list class. AArch64 sparse CPU-ID API recheck (EK541; 2026-10-25): re-read `KrnGetCPUCount`, `KrnAllocCPUMask`, `KrnClearCPUMask`, `KrnGetCPUMask`, `SetTaskAffinity`, BCM27xx startup, idle-task assignment, and processor.resource query contracts. ARM/AArch64 CPU-load baseline race report reconciliation (EK8843 detailed; 2026-10-24): reread both selected SMP overrides and confirmed each has a single mutable per-CPU baseline shared by `KrnGetSystemAttr` callers, with no lock spanning the read/compute/write sequence. PC framebuffer mirror finding reconciliation (EK9456 added; prior EK344 candidate withdrawn, 2026-10-24): traced `AllocFB()` reservation, explicit `vesa=` dispatch, `setupVESAMode()` failure cleanup, subsequent bootstrap calls, and all `__bs_malloc()` call sites. A failed VESA mode set does reset the workspace allocator while leaving `fb_Mirror` at its old address, but after that failure the selected bootstrap path makes no further `__bs_malloc()` calls that can reuse/overwrite the mirror before handing off; the earlier reuse claim is therefore not substantiated and EK344 has no active detailed finding. Separately confirmed the i386 and x86-64 kernel startup `AllocMem()` results are passed unchecked to `fb_SetMirror()`, which assigns NULL, while selected framebuffer-console render/clear paths dereference it. Added EK9456 to the detailed report and master index. No allocation failure, mode set, or boot was run; source-only. No new file-body line credit.


PC bootconsole 15-bit pixel-width path (EK9457 added; 2026-10-24): traced all selected native bootconsole `fb_Init()` producers and the PC VBE explicit-mode route. `findMode()` accepts advertised direct-color modes without a 15-bit exclusion; `setupVESA()` forwards a requested depth of 15; `con_InitVESA()` passes `bits_per_pixel` to the framebuffer renderer. The renderer uses `depth >> 3`, making the pixel width one byte, while 15-bit pixels occupy two-byte storage according to the selected VBE mode/pitch contract. The clear loop and glyph offsets therefore under-address and misplace data. Added EK9457 to the detailed Exec/Kernel report and master index. Other architecture framebuffer renderers have separate implementations and are not covered by this PC finding. No mode selection or boot was run; source-only; no new body-line credit.


PC text bootconsole row-stride follow-up (EK9458 added; 2026-10-24): re-read the full `txt_Putc()` body against both selected Multiboot text initializers. They publish supplied widths into `scr_Width`; output wraps and destination loops use that width, while cursor indexing and scroll-source reads use the literal 80. For a reported width below 80, the scroll-copy maximum source index is `width * height + (79 - width)`, beyond the `width * height` cell array when scrolling at height >= 2; later-row output can also exceed the cell array. Wider widths misaddress rows. Added EK9458 to the Exec/Kernel report and master index, replacing the prior coverage-only EK9458 reference. No boot record or console output was exercised; source-only; no new body-line credit.

ARM/AArch64 spinlock caller local-IRQ contract follow-up (OD9573; no separate EK): extended the native spinlock caller census beyond Exec/kernel by tracing the shared SD-card bus lock. The AArch64 lock acquisition implementation provides inter-core exclusion and acquire ordering but does not mask local IRQs. The SDHCI task path takes the same lock as the IRQ callback; its non-SMP alternative pairs the lock region with `Disable()`/`Enable()`, while its SMP branch omits local masking. This is recorded as the selected device-side candidate OD9573, limited to the BCM2711/2712 AArch64 SMP SDHCI path; no second kernel finding was split out. The ARM32 SDHOST handler does not use that shared lock. The sampled ARM32 USB OTG task/soft-interrupt paths pair local interrupt masking with the SMP spinlock; remaining USB lock callers are not closed by this check. No interrupt, schedule or hardware was run; source-only.

ARM-native TLS layout and startup/user reconciliation (2026-10-24; no new EK): read the complete `tls.h` and traced every direct TLS helper use plus `exec_platform.h`'s per-CPU nest/scheduling macros. Matched boot CPU TPIDRURO installation and the explicitly assigned pointer/CPU fields (`kernel_startup.c:189-228`), later SysBase publication, secondary clear-allocation and field setup (`platform_bcm2708.c:125-132`), task publication/restore in `kernel_cpu.c` and `kernel_scheduler.c`, Exec nesting initialization before `Enable()` (`rom/exec/exec_init.c:263-275`), and per-core quantum/elapsed setup before heartbeat enable (`platform_bcm2708.c:299-315`). No layout, pointer-installation or selected task-switch mismatch was established. The boot TLS allocation sits after the bootstrap protected area and does not explicitly initialize `ScheduleFlags`; `core_Schedule()` clears only the switch bit before it may read the quantum bit (`kernel_scheduler.c:98-99,134`). That leaves a possible one-time stale-quantum scheduling decision, but no persistent or user-visible consequence is established, so it is retained as an initialization question rather than an EK. No CPU startup, interrupt or task switch was run; source-only.

x86-64 PC AP timeout cross-iteration consequence recheck (EK9454 expanded, 2026-10-24): verified the outer `for (cpuNo=1; cpuNo<apic_count; cpuNo++)` continues after the inner timeout sets `wakeresult=-1`; it does not cancel or join the timed-out AP. Each next iteration locks `apicReadyLocks[cpuNo]` and then publishes that lock pointer to the shared trampoline `Arg2` (`arch/all-pc/kernel/smp.c:234-245,266-305`). The trampoline reads `Arg2` separately from `Arg1`, `Arg3`, and `Arg4` (`arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/smpbootstrap.s:128-137`). A late earlier AP can therefore consume the next iteration's ready-lock pointer and unlock it from `smp_Entry()`, making the BSP's later readiness poll succeed on behalf of the wrong AP; its own lock remains held. Expanded EK9454 with this concrete bookkeeping failure in addition to the wrong/mixed CPU arguments and stack. No AP, IPI, or timeout was run; source-only.

PC AP wake syscall and APIC IPI completion pass (2026-10-25; no new EK): traced `smp_Wake()` through the `int $0xfe` CPU-wake wrapper, the registered ACPI syscall handler, `core_APIC_Wake()` and its `ia32_ipi_send()` INIT/STARTUP sequence (`arch/all-pc/kernel/smp.c:274-313`; `x86_syscalls.h:38-43`; `acpi_apic.c:80-101,257-260`; `apic_ia32.c:1179-1316`). The handler returns the APIC routine's status through the syscall register; `smp_Wake()` waits on the per-CPU ready lock only when that status is zero. IPI send/ESR errors therefore do not enter the ready wait, while a reported send success is followed by a bounded readiness wait. The timeout/continued-loop behavior and shared trampoline argument overwrite are already recorded in EK9400/EK9454; this pass found no separate APIC completion defect and does not add body credit because these files were already credited. No APIC, IPI, startup, or timeout was run; source-only. 

PC APIC IPI delivery-status helper recheck (no new EK; 2026-10-25): read the full `ia32_ipi_send()` loop and matched `ICR_DS` to the ICR low-register definition (`arch/all-pc/kernel/apic_ia32.c:271-310`; `apic_ia32.h:159-161,216`). After writing destination and command, the helper polls delivery status every 100 microseconds for at most 1,000 iterations and returns the still-set status bit on timeout. `core_APIC_Wake()` propagates that nonzero result, and its syscall caller returns it to `smp_Wake()`, which skips the AP-ready wait on send error. The wait is finite at the source level; no independent error-propagation or timeout defect established. This is caller-path reconciliation only, with no new body credit; the existing AP timeout and nonfatal partial-start findings remain. No IPI or hardware timing was exercised; source-only.


ARM32 call-IPI pool exhaustion guard recheck (2026-10-24; no EK added): checked the `core_ClaimCallIPI()` branch against ARM ID-nesting semantics (`arch/arm-native/kernel/kernel_ipi.c:98-134`; `exec_platform.h:190-196`; `rom/exec/disable.c:90-96`; `enable.c:83-100`). `Disable()` increments the per-core count, while `Enable()` decrements it and only enables interrupts after the count becomes negative. Therefore `IDNESTCOUNT_GET >= 0` is the disabled case, where Claim drains its own inbound hook queue inline while spinning; the condition is not reversed. In the negative/enabled case, local FIQ delivery can drain the queue asynchronously. This closes that apparent branch-condition concern only; pool-exhaustion liveness under real inter-core timing and hardware remains untested, as does the separate AArch64 TLS startup flag question. No IPI was sent and no pool was exhausted; source-only.

ARM32/AArch64 startup flag scope correction (2026-10-24; no EK): resolved the prior tail note's “separate AArch64 TLS startup flag question” wording. AArch64 `kernel_startup.c:268-287` clears the entire TLS block with `memset(__tls, 0, sizeof(tls_t))`, explicitly addressing potentially stale scheduler flags/nest counts; the unresolved initialization question is only in ARM32 `arch/arm-native/kernel/kernel_startup.c:219-227`, which assigns KernelBase, SysBase, ThisTask and CPUNumber but not ScheduleFlags. Tracing the ARM32 bootstrap and scheduler path shows `core_Schedule()` clears the switch flag before reading the quantum flag; the boot CPU timer setup later writes the quantum value and first heartbeat is armed during platform post-init. Source evidence does not establish that the reserved boot TLS memory contains nonzero stale flags at the relevant first schedule, or a resulting observable scheduling error. Keep it as a low-confidence initialization question, not an active finding. Secondary BCM2708 TLS uses clear allocation. No runtime start/reboot/timer was run; source-only.

AvailMem selected diagnostic/caller recheck (2026-10-24; no new EK): re-read the complete `AvailMem()` wrapper and traced its selected implementation `nommu_AvailMem()` across plain and managed headers, plus the ExecSMP list/per-header read locks (`rom/exec/availmem.c:64-78`; `memory_nommu.c:318-435`; `memory.h:14-27`). The wrapper computes availability first, then invokes `MungWall_Scan()` for `MEMF_CLEAR`; the command caller `C:CheckMem` intentionally discards the result (`workbench/c/CheckMem.c:37-45`; `debug.h:282`). Selected direct clients request TOTAL and LARGEST separately; no selected caller combined those modes. The shared MemList lock protects list traversal, and per-header read locks protect ordinary free-list traversal on SMP; semaphore-protected managed headers are excluded from the spinlock around their potentially blocking availability callback. This sample establishes no wrapper ordering, caller-result, or lock-order defect. Remaining memory accounting variants/providers and the wider AvailMem caller set are still open; no allocation, MungWall scan, alert or concurrent allocator was run; source-only.

ARM-native early CPU-count/processor initialization pass (2026-10-24; EK541 retained, no new finding): traced the boot CPU setup (`arch/arm-native/kernel/kernel_startup.c:189-228`) into `cpu_Init()` setting affinity bit 0 (`kernel_cpu.c:359-366`), kernel INITLIB ordering (`rom/kernel/kernel_init.c:131`), and platform post-init bringing up secondaries before Exec coldstart INITLIB (`platform_init.c:74-126`; `kernel_startup.c:366-367`; `rom/exec/exec_init.c:278`). `rom/processor/init.c:17-55` reads the online CPU population count at priority 0, and ARM `Processor_Init()` at priority 1 allocates/probes a dense `[0, count)` array (`arch/arm-native/processor/processor_init.c:28-95`). Exec ARM idle-task initialization likewise iterates the count as dense CPU IDs (`arch/arm-native/exec/platform_init.c:37-90`). The ordering makes the count available after platform secondary startup; no separate early-zero/count race was established. A sparse online logical-ID set still makes these dense loops address absent IDs, matching existing EK541; no duplicate finding added. No boot or CPU startup was run; source-only.

x86-64 AP timeout finding-ID reconciliation (EK9454 canonical; older EK8878 references are stale, 2026-10-24): rechecked the timeout loop, subsequent lock publication and trampoline argument loads (`arch/all-pc/kernel/smp.c:234-245,266-314`; `arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/smpbootstrap.s:128-137`) against the current detailed report and master index. m68k runner argument setup failure/overflow caller reconciliation (EK9162/EK9231 retained; 2026-10-25): re-read `setup_and_execute()` and both public entry points (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_run.c:35-89,138-181,191-232`), then traced the context fields through Moira's initial A0/D0 setup (`m68kemu_moira.cpp:345-346`) and the Process shadow's `pr_Arguments` publication (`m68kemu_shadow.c:288-289`; guest task shadow caller in `m68kemu_thunks.c:165-166`). EK9459 report recovery verification (2026-10-29; no path/LOC credit): rechecked the test's top-minus-one-pointer stack address against `AROS_WORSTALIGN` and the selected PPC/AArch64 16-byte alignment, then confirmed both StackSwap implementations install it unchanged. PPC/AArch64 StackSwap test alignment recheck (EK9459 retained; 2026-10-25): verified the test's 32,768-byte `AllocMem()` region and `stk_Upper - sizeof(IPTR)` pointer (`developer/debug/test/exec/stackswap.c:81-99`) against `MEMCHUNK_TOTAL`'s `AROS_WORSTALIGN` minimum (`compiler/include/exec/memory.h:44-47`) and each CPU's 16-byte `AROS_WORSTALIGN`/`AROS_STACKALIGN` (`arch/ppc-all/include/aros/cpu.h:36-43`; `arch/aarch64-all/include/aros/cpu.h:25-35`). Multiboot text boot-console stride recheck (EK9458 retained; 2026-10-25): confirmed both Multiboot1 and Multiboot2 text-framebuffer cases copy the bootloader's character width/height to `scr_Width`/`scr_Height` before calling the common text console (`arch/all-native/bootconsole/init_multiboot.c:19-31`; `init_multiboot2.c:64-72`). `txt_Clear()` initializes exactly `width * height` two-byte character cells (`screen_text.c:11-15,22-35`); `txt_Putc()` then uses that width for wrapping/destination clearing but the literal 80 for row indexing and scroll-source offsets (`:47-67`). The Multiboot text type explicitly reports dimensions in characters; graphical framebuffers use the separate `fb_Init()` path. ARM-native cold reboot and idle task caller/target pass (2026-10-25; no new EK): rechecked the `raspi-arm` and `raspi-armeb` manifest entries selecting `coldreboot.c` and `exec_idle.c` (`arch/arm-native/exec/mmakefile.src:33-58`). `ColdReboot()` dispatches warm-reset callbacks and branches to address zero; the selected kernel installs exception vectors there and its `SC_REBOOT` uses the same target (`kernel/intr.c:402-411`; `kernel/syscall.c:217-221`). This supports the reset-vector jump as intentional; actual platform restart behavior remains untested. `Exec_ARMCPUInit()` supplies the idle task entry at priority -127, pinned per CPU for SMP; the kernel bootstrap task uses -128. `IdleTask()` enters privileged mode, enables IRQs and waits with WFI, matching the secondary-core idle sequence in `kernel_cpu.c:245-253`. No source-level mismatch was established. This closes the selected local caller/setup slice for these two bodies, not the wider Exec/Kernel or hardware/runtime scope. No reboot, task scheduling or interrupt was run; source-only.

Exec AvailMem caller slice (no new EK; 2026-10-25): checked the selected `Avail` command and InstallAROS sizing caller. `Avail.c` uses `IPTR` arrays for all direct query results (`:145-203`), including separate TOTAL and LARGEST flags; no combined-flag ambiguity occurs there. InstallAROS stores `AvailMem()` results in `ULONG` for a buffer-size heuristic (`ia_stageclass.c:170-191`), but clamps the resulting I/O buffer to 64 MiB and enforces a minimum; the narrowing can choose a smaller buffer on very large-memory systems but does not establish a functional allocation error. AvailMem direct-call census reconciliation (2026-10-25; no new EK): reran a tracked-source C/C++ search for `AvailMem(` at the pinned commit: 38 paths match, including the implementation and comment/test/debug-only occurrences. The earlier “48-path” figure was a distinct broad textual ledger inventory; it is not the direct-call denominator. A broader `git grep` search finds 52 tracked C/C++/assembly/header paths mentioning `AvailMem`, including declarations, comments and assembler-facing references, and is not a call count. Reconciled the 11 paths absent by literal path name from this EK ledger: `workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm-compat/linux_mem.c` is body-reviewed in the Other Drivers ledger; `workbench/system/Wanderer/wandererprefs.c` is the already indexed GD6319 truncation finding; AmigaVideo's two queries are diagnostic failure logging on its m68k target; the graphics benchmark and Exec allocation/pool programs are diagnostics/test clients; JanoPrefs and Jed queries are debug diagnostics; `idalert.c` is only a comment; VMM `defs.h`/`protos.h` contain declarations rather than callsites. No query or allocation was run; source-only.

Sam440 EK872 startup reachability recheck (2026-10-25; finding retained with existing boot caveat): reread both PPC440/PPC460 bank-size decoders, `exec_GetMemory()`, `exec_main()`, selected Sam440 kernel manifest, `krnCreateMemHeader()`, `krnPrepareExecBase()`, and generic `AddMemList()`. Both decoders explicitly accept 16 MiB banks and sum the four bank sizes; for a decoded 16 MiB total, `exec_main()` passes `(16 - 16) * MiB == 0` to `AddMemList()` with base `0x01000000`. Generic `AddMemList()` writes `MemHeader` fields at that base before publishing the header, so the zero-size path is not rejected. The initial header covers `[memLowest, 16 MiB)` and is prepared before this second registration. Source confirms the arithmetic and post-ExecBase sequence, but does not establish actual board register values, installed RAM layout, or a successful boot reaching the call; EK872 remains explicitly conditional on that configuration/reachability. No hardware, memory probe, or boot was run; source-only.

Sam440 EK872 boundary and failure-gate recheck (2026-10-25; no new EK): verified the exact initial-region endpoint in `exec_main()`: its first header starts at the aligned `KRN_KernelHighest` and has size `0x01000000 - memLowest`, so its exclusive upper bound is 16 MiB. The later zero-sized `AddMemList()` therefore places the `MemHeader` exactly at the first byte beyond a 16 MiB physical map, and generic `AddMemList()` performs field writes there before list insertion. `krnPrepareExecBase()` can return NULL on setup failure, but the selected standalone `krnPanic()` path halts, so the later call requires successful preparation. This sharpens the consequence and execution gate for existing EK872; exact board registers and a successful 16 MiB boot remain unverified. No hardware or boot was used; source-only; no body-line credit.

OOP bulk attribute-base caller and rollback recheck (OD2399 retained; no new EK; 2026-10-25): followed the three-entry `Input_InitClass()` descriptor list through `OOP_ObtainAttrBases()` (`rom/hidds/input/input_init.c:20-44`; `rom/oop/obtainattrbases.c:52-65`). A zero result for a non-final descriptor enters the already reported non-advancing cleanup loop, so the API never returns to this caller; this is the shared OD2399 hang, not a separate Exec defect. The selected `kernel-hidd-input` module registers `Input_InitClass()` in INITLIB and `Input_ExpungeClass()` in EXPUNGELIB. For a failure on the final descriptor, the helper reaches `FALSE`; genmodule's `_set_libinit()` marks INITLIB rollback active before invoking that set and calls EXPUNGELIB on failure (`compiler/autoinit/functions.c:57-69`), so `Input_ExpungeClass()` releases any acquired bases and closes the previously opened utility.library (`input_init.c:47-63`). No separate utility-reference leak is established on that returning path. This closes this selected caller's outcome only; it adds no source-body credit and does not close other bulk-helper callers. No allocation failure or module init was induced; source-only.


Exec AllocTrap explicit-index recheck (EK9462 restored from coverage-only candidate; 2026-10-25): reread the complete allocator and paired `FreeTrap()`, checked Task/ETask allocation and enabled-mask widths, exported `exec.conf` signature, selected generic vector manifest, and exact native/generated caller census. Explicit values 16–30 shift into bits that truncate to zero in the `UWORD` mask, yet are returned as successful indices; 31 and larger encounter signed-shift undefined behavior on maintained 32-bit-int targets. The automatic branch is limited to representable indices 0–15. No ordinary native caller was found beyond the emulation thunk, whose `-1` conversion is separately tracked by EK10923. AArch64 BCM2711/2712 generic-timer initialization-order recheck (2026-10-25; no new EK): traced `platform_PostInit()` through `ARMI_Init`, `KrnAddSysTimerHandler`, the platform `ARMI_InitTimerCore` hook, and secondary `cpu_Register()`. BCM27xx startup wakes secondaries one at a time and waits on `startup_lock`; `cpu_Register()` calls the per-core timer initializer only after creating the bootstrap task and releases that lock afterward. Therefore the first secondary may initialize `gentimer_interval` before the boot CPU's later timer initialization, but later secondaries and the boot CPU observe the initialized interval after the serialized bring-up. The CNTP IRQ path rearms each core's timer, advances that core's scheduler quantum, and returns early on nonzero CPUs before the CPU-0-only VBlank and task-usage sweep (`platform_bcm2711.c:179-224`; corresponding BCM2712 path `:276-328`; `platform_bcm27xx.c:115-128`). No uninitialized-interval race or missing nonzero-core scheduler tick was established. Physical timer delivery and real hardware ordering remain untested; source-only.

all-PC SMP TaskRunning publication/transition caller trace (2026-10-25; no new EK): rechecked the all-PC override's `SET_THIS_TASK` against its only C call (`rom/exec/exec_init.c:198-204`) and the selected runtime scheduler state transitions (`arch/all-pc/exec/platform_init.c:207-255,269-338`). AUX handover representation recheck and finding reconciliation (EK867/EK8881 promoted to detailed report entries; 2026-10-25): re-read `aux_handler.c` and the selected `con_handler.c` parser and traced the resulting device name through Exec `OpenDevice()`/`FindName()`. Confirmed `AROS_FAST_BPTR` makes `MKBADDR`/`BADDR` identity conversions, while the handover unconditionally reserves and clears bit 30; if the actual `FileSysStartupMsg` address has that bit set, startup metadata is read from the wrong address (EK867; conditional on address placement). Separately confirmed `buildDefaultStartup()` always emits a length-prefixed `serial.device` BSTR, but `AROS_FAST_BSTR` consumers treat the first byte as the first C-string character, so the copied device name begins with byte `0x0d` and exact Exec device-name lookup fails (EK8881; selected ordinary AUX `Startup=0` path). These defects are recorded separately because either can break the same default startup path, and the BSTR failure remains after the pointer tag decodes correctly.

Taskless AttemptSemaphore report-detail recheck (EK9152 promoted to detailed entry; 2026-10-25): verified `InitSemaphore()` establishes `ss_QueueCount=-1`, `ss_Owner=NULL`, and `ss_NestCount=0`; `exec_init.c` invokes PREINITLIB before `SET_THIS_TASK`; both public Attempt wrappers can pass NULL owner to `InternalAttemptSemaphore`; the attempt helper lacks the taskless early return present in `InternalObtainSemaphore`; and `ReleaseSemaphore()` returns on NULL `ThisTask` without undoing the attempt's count. m68k emulator memory helper completion and guest-size overflow pass (EK9159 rechecked; EK9464 duplicate withdrawn; 2026-10-25): completed the remaining allocator/context, linked-segment loader, library-base, and AutoOpenLibs body review in `rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_memory.c`, then traced the `AllocMem`, `AllocVec`, and `AllocPooled` vectors directly into `M68KEmu_HeapAlloc()` (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks.c:100-105,394-399,416-420`). No guest allocation or write was run; source-only.

m68k emulator heap allocator guest/public caller census (EK9159 trigger qualification; 2026-10-25): searched all `M68KEmu_HeapAlloc()`/`HeapFree()` call sites and traced the public emulated `AllocMem`, `AllocVec`, and `AllocPooled` thunks; these forward guest-controlled D0 size values without clamping to the 32 MiB guest heap (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks.c:100-105,394-420`). No emulator or guest was run; source-only.


m68k emulator RunHunk/RunFile argument-size boundary pass (EK9231 rechecked; EK9465 duplicate withdrawn; 2026-10-25): traced the public `RunHunk()`/`RunFile()` vectors into `setup_and_execute()` and the DOS production caller chain (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_run.c:64-71,133-178,190-229`; `rom/dos/runcommand.c:103-113`; `rom/dos/createnewproc.c:851-866`). The helper allocates `argSize + 1` without overflow/capacity checks, ignores allocation failure for control flow, and copies `argSize` bytes whenever the resulting pointer is nonzero. At `ULONG_MAX`, the increment wraps to zero and the allocator can return a tiny block before the oversized host `CopyMem`; this is the existing EK9231 root cause; EK9465 duplicated it and is withdrawn. Correcting the allocator alone would not bound the separate call-site copy. Reachability requires a caller-valid very large argument buffer; no checked-in caller supplied such a length. No emulator or copy was run; source-only.

m68k emulator argument-allocation failure path (EK9162 rechecked; EK9466 duplicate withdrawn; 2026-10-25): traced `setup_and_execute()`'s argument allocation result through context publication, Process shadow, and the selected Moira entry-register setup (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_run.c:64-88`; `rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_shadow.c:288-289`; `rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_moira.cpp:343-346`). m68k emulator child-task versus guest-stack size recheck (EK9161 retained; no duplicate; 2026-10-25): re-read the remaining `setup_and_execute()` process branch and reconciled its `CreateNewProc()` tags with DOS `CreateNewProc()`'s default stack setup and Moira reset (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_run.c:91-127`; `rom/dos/createnewproc.c:119-120,452-468`; `rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_moira.cpp:315-320,343-346`). m68k fake-library map and region-capacity boundary recheck (EK9166 strengthened; no additional finding; 2026-10-25): reconciled the 16-entry `libmap`, 32-entry library records, 64 KiB base region, 512-vector allocation, and generated library table (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_intern.h:23-37,54`; `m68kemu_offsets.h:223`; `m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:8033-8053`). The generated table has 17 names including Exec and DOS; their 17 distinct fake bases require 17*(512*6+4)+628 = 52,920 bytes, within the 65,536-byte region (628 accounts for the 632-byte ExecBase data area instead of four bytes). Thus the 32-record/region-count mismatch does not independently block the current unique generated-library inventory. However, Exec and DOS consume two map entries, leaving one of the 17 generated names uncached; a second OpenLibrary of that name bypasses FindLibBase and creates a duplicate record/base, confirming EK9166's root cause and possible subsequent capacity pressure. No guest library was opened; source-only.

Native RISC-V Exec/TLS inline-assembly caller pass (EK9467 added; 2026-10-25): read all 229 physical lines / 208 `cloc 2.06` C code lines of `arch/riscv-native/exec/exec_platform.h`, and all of `arch/riscv-native/kernel/tls.h`. The selected SiFive U boot handoff remains non-running (`boot.c:36-43`; EK193/EK195), and OpenSBI uses a different override; the candidate is limited to any native-RISC-V route that reaches these macros. Native RISC-V context-frame layout comparison (EK9468 added; 2026-10-25): compared ExceptionContext.x[] and its omitted x0/x3/x4 entries (arch/riscv-all/include/aros/cpucontext.h:15-53) against every word saved by __int_handler (arch/riscv-native/kernel/intr.c:44-76) and each STORE_TASKSTATE/RESTORE_TASKSTATE access (arch/riscv-native/kernel/kernel_intern.h:51-115). The producer uses physical register-number slots, while the macros use compact array indices. With raw post-allocation SP, x1 is saved at word 1 but read from word 0; x5 is saved at word 3 but read from word 2; PC is saved at word 30 but read at word 29. A one-word pointer shift aligns x1 and x5-x31 but leaves x2 absent and PC at word 30 beyond the reserved frame; no conversion or reconstructed SP appears in the stub. Added EK9468, distinct from EK9028 frame capacity. The stub has no dispatch/return sequence and no in-tree stvec installation/reference, so exact frame-pointer use and a current running trigger remain unestablished. No trap or task context was exercised; source-only.

Semaphore reader-preference candidate disposition (EK875 withdrawn; 2026-10-25): rechecked public shared/exclusive contracts, immediate obtain and try-acquire branches, queued grants, selected DOS/POSIX callers, and the finite SMP semaphore test. The implementation permits readers to join an active shared group while an exclusive waiter is queued and may grant a queued shared request beyond an intervening writer. The public contract promises shared coexistence and exclusion by an active exclusive owner, but does not promise writer preference or bounded wait; selected callers/tests do not establish sustained reader arrivals that starve a writer. Withdraw the conditional EK875 candidate as unsupported rather than report reader-preference behavior as a correctness defect. No active EK875 heading or master-index link exists; historical ledger notes are superseded by this disposition. No contention was run. Source-only.


x86-64 PC early-trap flags formatter pass (EK9469 added, 2026-10-25): completed the pending local display-format audit in `arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/kernel_early.c` and matched `print_crash_info()`'s `uint32_to_hex()` call against the saved `stack[19]` RFLAGS word. `uint32_as_hex(uint32_t, ...)` shifts by 60 down to 32 for its eight nibbles, all outside the 32-bit operand width. Added EK9469 for C-level undefined shift behavior in the optional early-trap flags line; qualified visible corruption because x86 variable-shift instructions mask counts and may happen to emit the intended sequence on a particular compiler. Corrected the stale `EK250` row reference to the current register-label finding EK9062. `KERNEL_USE_EARLYTRAP` is unset in the checked-in x86-64 PC manifest by default and must be enabled to select this file. No build, trap or display operation was run; source-only.


x86-64 PC early-trap invalid-opcode dump caller/fault pass (EK9470 added, 2026-10-25): traced the vector-6 diagnostic's raw 32-byte RIP read against the early IDT table and vector-14 stub. The byte loop has no mapping or page-boundary check (`arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/kernel_early.c:319-332`), and the early IDT installs #PF back into the same `boot_crashhandler` (`:77-81,425-430`). A complete two-byte invalid instruction such as `UD2` in the final two mapped bytes can therefore raise #UD with a valid RIP, followed by #PF when the diagnostic reads its third byte; the nested page-fault screen replaces the original and also enters the reporter's permanent loop. Added EK9470, conditional on the specified code/page layout and `KERNEL_USE_EARLYTRAP`. This is a source-level diagnostic recursion candidate; no memory map or exception was induced.


OpenSBI no-Zicbom DMA candidate reconciliation (prior EK673 withdrawn from active findings; 2026-10-25): audited all checked-in `CachePreDMA()`/`CachePostDMA()` call sites against the selected `arch/riscv64-opensbi/boot/mmakefile.src` graph. EK9471 managed-pool usability cross-check (2026-10-25): completed the caller-side construction trace. After a successful managed `AllocMemHeader()`, `CreatePool()` allocates its `Pool` record through `Allocate()` and takes the managed-pool return path without requiring `mhe_AllocVec` (`rom/exec/createpool.c:159-192`; `rom/exec/allocate.c:96-106`). This validates the conditional API trigger; no current maintained backend has that callback combination with a successful ordinary allocator. Source-only; no runtime allocation.

CEBoot startup/namepart full-body and caller pass (EK9472 added; 2026-10-25): read all 154 `cloc 2.06` C code lines in `arch/arm-native/ceboot/bootstrap.c` and all 58 in `filesystem.c`, reconciled both with `mmakefile.src`, and traced every `namepart()` call. m68kemu initial guest privilege candidate disposition (EK9460 withdrawn; 2026-10-27): Moira reset sets supervisor mode and `M68KEmu_Execute()` intentionally preserves that state at guest entry (`rom/m68kemu/Moira/Moira/Moira.cpp:199-222`; `rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_moira.cpp:314-353`). DOS RunCommand/CreateNewProc callers establish the selected path but do not change this disposition. No guest or CPU exception was run; source-only.

EK419 dual-lookup exhaustion consequence qualification (2026-10-25): distinguished the two full-table behaviors. Manual `FindTask()` ignores failed `shadow_register()` and returns its still-allocated unregistered guest address, which later Task-pointer thunks resolve to raw arena bytes. Generated `FindTaskByPID()` uses `shadow_create_by_name()` and returns zero if new shadow allocation/registration fails. Both leak guest storage/table entries on each successful lookup before exhaustion; the native PID match remains present when its guest shadow creation fails. No guest lookup was run.


Exec pooled-vector selected caller trace (2026-10-25; no new Exec finding): rechecked the public `AllocVecPooled()`/`FreeVecPooled()` branches and selected NTFS pooled-vector callers. NTFS creates `glob->mempool` before entering its packet loop and only calls `_AllocVecPooled(glob->mempool, ...)` from the successful pool-initialization path (`workbench/fs/ntfs/main.c:68–80`; `support.c:131–141`). Its separate per-volume pool is checked before normal allocations (`disk.c:187–207`), and the allocation-failure path was found to publish incomplete volume state and enqueue a null volume packet; this cross-area filesystem defect is now FS-081 in `AROS-filesystems.md`. This caller trace does not establish a selected NULL-pool argument to the Exec vector API. Existing EK9278 size-wrap and EK9471 optional managed-callback candidates remain distinct. No allocation, disk insertion, or packet was run; source-only.

PC x86-64 AP idle-task affinity-mask allocation failure recheck (EK8835 expanded; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): traced `Exec_X86CreateIdleTask()`'s `KrnAllocCPUMask()` result through `KrnGetCPUMask()`, `TASKTAG_AFFINITY` adoption, the affinity-enabled PC scheduler predicate, `cpu_BootStrap()` and its bootstrap-task removal (`arch/all-pc/exec/platform_init.c:350-418`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/getcpumask.c:13-24`; `apic.c:115-149`; `arch/x86_64-all/exec/preparecontext.c:44-51`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/smp_exec.c:60,220-231`; `kernel_scheduler.c:308-405`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/smp.c:118-145`). `KrnGetCPUMask()`'s destination NULL check makes this a non-crashing path at mask construction; `PrepareContext()` nevertheless stores NULL, which the selected PC APIC predicate interprets as CPU 0 only. For an AP ID above zero, the idle task can be successfully created but cannot run on that AP; after bootstrap-task removal, EK8835's no-eligible-task recursion still applies. Expanded EK8835 to include this distinct low-memory trigger alongside task/name/context allocation failures, rather than opening a duplicate scheduler finding. No task, CPU mask or allocation failure was induced; source-only.

OpenSBI virtual-IRQ allocator and PCIDT failure cleanup recheck (OD1409 retained; no new EK; 2026-10-25): re-read the selected OpenSBI allocator/release implementation and its sole checked-in allocation caller (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/allocirq.c:22-95`; `hidd/pcidt/pcidt_driverclass.c:724-770,1080-1092`). The PCIDT caller halves its vector request to one and stops only when `KrnAllocIRQ` succeeds or no count remains. In the all-fail case, `PCIDT_MSIInit()` has already stored the allocated target and enabled/unmasked the DesignWare MSI block (`pcidt_access.c:363-388`); the caller clears only `msiReady`, losing its local page pointer, with no disable or free. This exactly matches Other Drivers OD1409, conditional on an FDT-described DesignWare bridge and exhaustion of every contiguous virtual range. Successful reservations are stored on the bridge and connected through `KrnModifyIRQA`; its failure path remains OD1411. The selected bridge registration loop is sequential; no in-tree overlapping OpenSBI allocation caller was found. No new kernel finding or line credit. No IRQ, bridge or hardware was exercised; source-only.

InitSemaphore field and static-pthread caller recheck (2026-10-25; no additional EK): re-read `initsemaphore.c`, `CheckSemaphore`, `InternalObtainSemaphore`, `ObtainSemaphoreList`, and the direct static-mutex initialization callers. The initializer sets the shared state and SMP lock; ordinary obtain uses a stack `SemaphoreRequest` whose links are set by `AddTail`, while `ObtainSemaphoreList` sets the embedded `sr_Waiter` and links `ss_MultipleLink` before queue use (`rom/exec/semaphores.c:120-137`; `obtainsemaphorelist.c:75-101`). A valid `PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER` caller does expose the already documented unsynchronized first-use race: lock and trylock independently test `SemaphoreIsInvalid()` and call `_pthread_mutex_init()`, which invokes this initializer on the same mutex (`compiler/pthread/pthread.h:285-305`; `compiler/pthread/pthread.c:51-59`; `pthread_mutex_lock.c:32-40`; `pthread_mutex_trylock.c:32-37`; `pthread_mutex_init.c:26-40`). The concurrent reinitialization candidate remains in the detailed Exec report; no pthread task interleaving was run. Broader `InitSemaphore` callers remain unclassified; source-only.

Expansion relocation / `AvailMem(MEMF_FAST)` caller recheck (2026-10-25; candidate boundary, no new confirmed EK): traced `expansion_init.c` through its BINCOMPAT relocation branch, `initExpBase()`, the m68k `ConfigChain()` implementation and all checked-in `ConfigBoard()` references. Relocation occurs after `ConfigChain()` and moves `BoardList` and `MountList`, but `initExpBase()` reinitializes `z2Slots` and `z3Slot`; if `ConfigBoard()` is called later, those allocation maps no longer reflect already configured boards. The only in-tree `ConfigBoard()` call is from `ConfigChain()`, before relocation, and no later maintained caller was found in this pass, so the state-loss consequence remains an external/later-call candidate rather than a confirmed maintained-path defect. The AvailMem threshold only gates a best-effort `MakeLibrary()` allocation; failure leaves the original base in use. No board configuration or allocation was run; source-only.

P96 bitmap migration rounds `bm->memsize` up to eight bytes before the two copies (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/p96gfx/p96gfx_bitmapclass.c:81,184,212`); the `Dir` pointer-table copy multiplies the count by `sizeof(char *)` (`workbench/c/Dir.c:275-276`).
