Exec `Enqueue()` task-scheduler caller follow-up (2026-10-25; no new EK): re-read the selected task ready/wait transitions at `rom/exec/newaddtask.c:31-43`, `rom/exec/wait.c:69-108`, `rom/exec/settaskpri.c:62-111`, `rom/exec/signal.c:360-400`, `rom/exec/service.c:88-113`, and `arch/all-pc/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:250-295,378-400`. Task launch initializes `tc_State` before insertion (SMP routes through `krnSysCallReschedTask`); Wait moves the running task while disabled and uses paired task/list helpers on SMP; SetTaskPri removes/reinserts only a ready task while holding the selected list lock; Signal's non-SMP wake removes from Wait and marks Ready before enqueue, while SMP uses the scheduler syscall; PC scheduler insertions take the corresponding Ready/Wait/Spinning write lock. ServiceTask's selected non-`EXEC_REMTASK_NEEDSSWITCH` fallback sets Ready and enqueues without an explicit list lock, but the checked-in producer is RemTask's self-removal message, sent after setting `TS_REMOVED`, and ServiceTask requeues that message until RemTask changes state to `TS_INVALID`; this pass found no maintained path that delivers a different live/listed task to that fallback, so no defect is established. Broader `Enqueue()` callers (including non-task lists), other platform scheduler implementations, node-membership preconditions and external callers remain open. No task state or scheduling operation was run; source-only.

The existing EK383 cleanup omission remains confirmed: both StrToDate failure and AnchorPath allocation failure return without `FreeArgs(rda)`. Shutdown command return-contract and selected caller pass (no new EK; 2026-10-25): traced the complete 31-line `workbench/c/Shutdown.c` body through each relevant selected `ShutdownA(SD_ACTION_POWEROFF)` implementation. Generic Exec runs reset callbacks and returns zero if the chain returns; Unix exits, MinGW calls `ExitProcess(0)`, CHRP attempts RTAS power-off and may return, Amiga returns `-1` when UAE poweroff is unavailable, and AArch64 invokes the poweroff syscall then returns if the kernel declines. In every returning path, the command reports `RETURN_FAIL`; nonreturning paths do not reach that status. AArch64 MMU partial-map failure caller refinement (EK8823 strengthened; no new ID; 2026-10-25): traced the maximum decoded xHCI scratchpad count through `xhci_controllerclass.c` to `pciAllocAligned()` and the selected RP1 `AllocPCIMem()` (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_controllerclass.c:418-453`; `rom/usb/pcixhci/pcixhci_arospci.c:474-484`; `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2712/rp1/rp1_pci.c:182-207`). At 1,023 4-KiB scratchpad pages, alignment overhead makes RP1 ask `KrnMapGlobal()` for 4 MiB, and the caller frees the backing allocation if mapping returns false. A 4-KiB-aligned but non-2-MiB-aligned range spans partial first/last 2-MiB blocks; `mmu_map_range()` can write the first partial PTEs and middle block before a later `mmu_next()` table allocation fails (`arch/aarch64-native/kernel/mmu.c:194-230`). The return skips `mmu_commit()` and there is no rollback; the RP1 caller frees the pages without an unmap. Updated EK8823 to state this conditional in-tree call path and its residual-attribute consequence. AArch64 manifest prerequisites remain absent under EK8902; no build, controller or allocation failure was exercised. Source-only.


AArch64 MMU partial-map caller refinement (EK8823 strengthened; existing full-body credit; 2026-10-25): the xHCI scratchpad path can request a multi-region RP1 mapping: 1,023 decoded pages at 4 KiB each require 4,190,208 bytes, and `pciAllocAligned()` requests one additional page for alignment (4 MiB total). Since RP1 aligns to 4 KiB rather than 2 MiB, an unaligned 4 MiB range has partial first and last 2 MiB regions. If the later L3-table allocation fails after the first partial PTEs and middle block have been written, `mmu_map_range()` returns FALSE before commit/rollback; `AllocPCIMem()` frees the backing allocation without an unmap. Updated EK8823 with this conditional selected-caller effect. The Raspberry Pi package's source selections are present, but missing AArch64 kernel prerequisites under EK8902 mean runtime/buildability is not established. No map, allocation failure or controller was run. No additional body credit; source-only.

Sashimi/Exec resource lifetime interleaving recheck (EK844 strengthened; 2026-10-25): reconstructed the exact cross-CPU order from OpenResource's read-lock release (rom/exec/openresource.c:55-64), Sashimi's post-return lib_OpenCnt++ (developer/debug/sashimi/sashimi.c:518-531), owner's local-Forbid zero-count check and RemResource (sashimi.c:403-423; rom/exec/remresource.c:48-54), and unconditional owner free after successful removal (sashimi.c:1200-1205). Cancelable ARM/AArch64 Signal IPI-claim lifetime recheck (EK9482 added, 2026-10-25): traced the off-affinity/running-target route in `rom/exec/signal.c:170-247` through `core_ClaimCallIPI()` in the selected ARM32/AArch64 implementations (`arch/arm-native/kernel/kernel_ipi.c:98-134`; `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/kernel_ipi.c:96-115`) and compared it with `RemTask()`'s cancellation and freeing sequence (`rom/exec/remtask.c:58-128,165-181`). Claim waits for a free pool entry before taking `tc_SpinLock`; cancellation only covers committed callbacks, so it cannot synchronize a sender waiting before commit. If another CPU frees the Task during that interval, Signal's lock and terminal-state check dereference reclaimed memory. Expanded the earlier raw-task-pointer lifetime concern (EK274) with this pre-lock window; kept it separate from PC's queued callback finding EK832. Timer AbortIO/list-lock reply-order follow-up (EK lock-order scope refined, 2026-10-25; no new EK): re-read the selected SMP `rom/timer/abortio.c` path and all `tb_ListLock` acquire/release sites in `rom/timer/lowlevel.c`, then compared their `ReplyMsg()` calls with Exec's `InternalPutMsg()` port-lock/signal order (`rom/exec/putmsg.c:68-111`; `replymsg.c:55-69`). Timer expiry and AbortIO can hold `tb_ListLock` while replying, so the observed order is timer-list lock -> reply-port spinlock; `InternalPutMsg()` releases the port spinlock before `Signal()`/`Cause()`. The checked in-tree GetMsg/WaitIO/PutMsg/ReplyMsg paths do not call back into timer list operations while retaining the port lock, and no in-tree reverse edge was established. No lock-order deadlock is promoted from this source slice. External clients, caller-held locks, pool-contention liveness and actual SMP schedules remain open; no timer request or lock was exercised. Source-only.

EK9482 task-lifetime concurrency recheck (2026-10-25): checked the platform teardown path against Forbid and IPI cancellation semantics. Exec documents that `Forbid()` is per-processor on ExecSMP (`rom/exec/forbid.c:42-55`), so `RemTask()`'s Forbid does not serialize a sender on another CPU. ARM32 and AArch64 both select `EXEC_REMTASK_NEEDSSWITCH` and `KERNEL_IPI_CALL_CANCELABLE` (`arch/{arm,aarch64}-native/exec/exec_platform.h`; `kernel_ipi.h`); their `Exec_ReschedTask()` acquires `tc_SpinLock` only during state/list transition, then `RemTask()` calls `CancelSignalIPIs()` and later frees the task's MemEntry chain. The cancellation sweep removes matching queued calls and waits for matching executing callbacks, but it has no registry for a sender holding a claimed, not-yet-committed `CallIPIEntry` (`kernel_ipi.c:186-217` ARM; `:153-184` AArch64). Thus a sender paused in `core_ClaimCallIPI()` is not waited out by either Forbid or cancellation; if it resumes after teardown, its later task-lock access remains reachable. Existing EK9482 remains qualified on simultaneous pool exhaustion and removal; no concurrency run or task operation was performed. Source-only.

Generic MMU allocator size-rounding overflow discriminator (2026-10-25; no new EK): traced the public `KrnAllocPages(addr, length, ...)` wrapper into `mm_AllocPages()` and `mm_Allocate()` (`rom/kernel/allocpages.c:17-85`; `kernel_mm.c:22-75`; `mm_linear.c:128-148`). ARM32 call-IPI pool local-drain guard discriminator (EK9482 retained; no new EK; 2026-10-25): checked `core_ClaimCallIPI()`'s `IDNESTCOUNT_GET >= 0` condition against the selected ARM32 nesting implementation (`arch/arm-native/kernel/kernel_ipi.c:122-139`; `arch/arm-native/exec/exec_platform.h:68-79,190-196`; `rom/exec/disable.c:83-90`; `enable.c:81-91`; `newaddtask.c:230-238`). New tasks start with `tc_IDNestCnt = -1`; each `Disable()` increments it and each `Enable()` decrements it. Thus the local queue drain runs in a disabled/nested context, where FIQ cannot drain the source CPU's inbound queue, and is skipped in the normal enabled state, where FIQ delivery remains available. The guard is consistent with the implementation comment; no independent polarity bug was established. EK9482's separate claim-to-commit task-lifetime race remains unchanged. No IPI or task interleaving was run; no body-line credit added. Source-only.

AArch64 call-IPI local-drain guard parity check (EK9482 retained; no new EK; 2026-10-25): traced the parallel `core_ClaimCallIPI()` and `core_HandleCallHookIPI()` implementations (`arch/aarch64-native/kernel/kernel_ipi.c:86-113,231-271`) against the shared Exec `Disable()`/`Enable()` nesting updates and task initial value (`rom/exec/disable.c:83-90`; `enable.c:81-91`; `newaddtask.c:230-238`). EfikaMX bootstrap allocator and ATAG allocation threshold recheck (EK9486 tightened; 2026-10-25): traced the complete selected `support.c` bump allocator and all checked-in callers. `boot()` reaches `parse_atags()` before any other explicit bootstrap `malloc()` (`boot.c:175-204`); each command-line tag requests `strlen()+1`, and `malloc()` rounds that size upward to 16 bytes before comparing with the remaining 524,288-byte arena (`support.c:9-11,46-60`; `boot.h:14-16`). AddBootNode long-BSTR narrowing and CopyMem size-contract recheck (EK9481 retained, 2026-10-25): traced the 255-byte standard BSTR case through the exact destination and copy signatures. `BYTE` is signed 8-bit (`exec/types.h:70-74`); on the selected two's-complement ABI it narrows 255 to -1, making `len + 2` one byte at `addbootnode.c:191-200`. `IPTR` is unsigned and pointer-sized (`types.h:82-86`), and CopyMem's generated signature accepts that unsigned length (`exec.conf:178`; `copymem.c:13-18`). The generic body returns only for zero and continues with the nonzero length (`copymem.c:60-72`); the selected m68k CopyMem assembly also processes D0 as an unsigned long count (`arch/m68k-all/exec/copymem_.S:18-50`). Thus the 255 case passes a maximum unsigned copy count into a one-byte destination, strengthening the source-level out-of-bounds read/write consequence in EK9481. `AddDosEntry()` publishes the node before this copy (`rom/dos/adddosentry.c:109-115`). No long BSTR or copy was executed; no body credit changed. Source-only.

RTL8029 task-port startup rendezvous recheck (EK620/FindPort caller slice; no new finding; 2026-10-25): reread `RunTask()` and `UnitTask()` around publication and message ownership (`workbench/devs/networks/rtl8029/driver.c:730-752,1740-1764`). POSIX `sysconf(_SC_PHYS_PAGES)` caller/width pass (2026-10-25; no new EK): read the selected POSIXC implementation and its public constants. `_SC_PAGESIZE` is 4096, matching `PAGESIZE`/`PAGE_SIZE` in the POSIXC limits header; `_SC_PHYS_PAGES` divides the `IPTR` total by 4096 before converting to signed `long`, so even a 32-bit address space's maximum page count fits in signed 32-bit `long` (`compiler/crt/posixc/sysconf.c:49-59`; `compiler/crt/posixc/include/aros/posixc/limits.h:36-37`). A source search found no in-tree `_SC_PHYS_PAGES` caller; Mesa's selected shim defines its own `sysconf()` and only handles `_SC_PAGE_SIZE` (`workbench/libs/mesa/aros_drm_shim.c:264-273`), so it does not exercise this implementation. No POSIX query or Mesa library was run; source-only.

Avail command FLUSH allocator-caller recheck (2026-10-25; no new EK): traced `FlushMem()`'s repeated `AllocMem(0x7ffffff0, MEMF_PUBLIC)` calls and reverse-order `FreeMem()` unwind (`workbench/c/Avail.c:91-107`) through `AllocMem()`'s failed-allocation loop (`rom/exec/allocmem.c:75-118`) into `checkMemHandlers()` (`rom/exec/memory.c:1313-1357`). The large request is the mechanism that invokes registered low-memory handlers; if a handler returns `MEM_TRY_AGAIN`, `AllocMem()` retries, and a successful allocation recurses to force another allocation/handler pass before freeing the reservations. Therefore failure to reserve a 2 GiB block on its own does not establish that FLUSH is a no-op: the low-memory-handler pass occurs first. No separate source defect was established. Handler-specific responses, very large recursive depth and runtime/overcommit behavior remain unverified. No memory pressure or FLUSH command was run; source-only.

EK8799 reply-publication recheck correction (2026-10-27; supersedes the 2026-10-25 SetPrefs reachability and CommandPort-corruption conclusion): `ReplyMsg` does publish `NT_REPLYMSG` before `InternalPutMsg` links the reply, and `GetMsg` leaves the removed node's link fields unchanged. However, Intuition `SetPrefs()` reaches `WaitIO()` through synchronous `DoIO()`; with the request still `NT_MESSAGE`, WaitIO sleeps for the private reply-port signal, which is sent only after insertion. That caller cannot observe the pre-enqueue state or establish the claimed CommandPort corruption. EK8799's selected early-observer evidence is instead `Exec_DoResetCallbacks()` and `C:Wait`'s independent Ctrl-C signal path, which can reach `CheckIO()`/`WaitIO()` while a VBlank timer interrupt on another ExecSMP CPU is between state publication and enqueue. Both callers proceed to request/port cleanup after WaitIO; the required overlap remains conditional and unrun. This is a scope correction to the existing EK8799, not a new ID or body credit. Source-only.

EK8875 RTL8139 trigger qualification (2026-10-25; no body-credit change): rechecked the checked-in x86 PC IRQ-affinity sources after the earlier RTL8139 caller-pair note. `IOAPICInt_EnableIRQ()` uses `IntrMapping.im_CPU` when present and otherwise uses `KrnGetCPUNumber()` (`arch/all-pc/kernel/acpi_ioapic.c:546-593`); initial ACPI I/O-APIC routing defaults to CPU0 (`:415-430`), and checked-in interrupt-override mappings are initialized on the parsing CPU (`:860-875,925-939`). The only maintained `KrnModifyIRQA()` callers adjust ACPI IRQ polarity/trigger or RISC-V MSI attributes; the PC implementation initializes a new mapping's CPU to the caller but exposes no CPU-affinity tag (`arch/all-pc/kernel/modifyirq.c:20-72`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/acpi.c:110,131`). Thus the RTL8139 timeout/TX-completion caller pair alone does not establish two concurrent CPUs on the selected PC setup; its report wording must be conditional and not presented as a demonstrated trigger. This does not disprove the generic ExecSMP race or rule out other task/interrupt caller combinations. No IRQ or interleaving was run; source-only.

Exec ETask cleanup caller closure (2026-10-25; no new EK): searched all checked-in C/assembly for `Exec_CleanupETask` and its `CleanupETask` macro. The only call sites are `NewAddTask()` failed CPU-launch cleanup and failed `PrepareContext()` cleanup (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:105-115,301-310`) and terminal `RemTask()` teardown (`rom/exec/remtask.c:109-128`). For selected x86-64/i386 PC `PrepareContext()`, failure follows `KrnCreateContext()` returning NULL after that NULL was stored in `et_RegFrame`; no allocated context is abandoned on this false return (`arch/x86_64-all/exec/preparecontext.c:37-40`; `arch/i386-all/exec/preparecontext.c:34-37`). `RemTask()` cancels pending signal IPIs and deletes a non-NULL context before calling cleanup (`remtask.c:109-128`). NewCreateTaskA frees its task MemList if NewAddTask returns NULL (`rom/exec/newcreatetaska.c:257-263`); the public DOS `NP_Affinity` contract states the affinity mask becomes system-owned and must not be reused/freed by the caller (`compiler/include/dos/dostags.h:92-97`), consistent with ETask cleanup freeing a real mask while preserving the `TASKAFFINITY_ANY` sentinel (`exec_util.c:252-257`). Optional x86-64 trap-backtrace frame validation pass (EK9511 added; 2026-10-26): traced `core_DumpExceptionState()`'s `TRAPDEBUG_UNWIND` call from the saved exception RBP (`arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/kernel_trapdebug.c:291-303`; context layout `arch/x86_64-all/include/aros/cpucontext.h:47-86`) into the selected x86-64 frame-chain walker (`arch/x86_64-all/kernel/backtracefromframe.c:23-39`). Confirmed boot TLS is not zeroed or assigned `ScheduleFlags`, whereas secondary TLS is `MEMF_CLEAR`; Exec enables multitasking before `platform_PostInit()` (priority 10) arms the boot CPU's per-core timer. `core_Schedule()` reads `TLSSF_Quantum` when a same/lower-priority ready task exists, and the bit is cleared when the scheduler dispatches a task. The actual boot-memory word and exact runnable-task ordering were not observed, so manifestation remains medium confidence. ARM32 boot TLS ScheduleFlags candidate withdrawn (2026-10-26): a follow-up of `NewAddTask()` and `core_Schedule()` showed that the first relevant boot-CPU dispatch is the priority-127 Exec housekeeper from the priority-0 bootstrap task. `NewAddTask()` calls `Reschedule()` immediately for this higher-priority task; `core_Schedule()` only consults `TLSSF_Quantum` when the next ready task is equal or lower priority and clears the quantum bit on the actual task dispatch. Thus the unset bit does not establish premature quantum preemption before the first timer tick. Withdrew EK9514 and removed its index link; the source initialization omission is retained as an observation, not an active finding. No scheduler was run; source-only.


ARM32 Raspberry Pi MMU descriptor-producer pass (no new EK; 2026-10-26): read the complete selected `arch/arm-native/kernel/mmu.h` and traced `core_SetupMMU()` through `cpu_Init()` into the boot-provided `bm_pde` table. The relocated-kernel sizes are rounded to 1 MiB and local interrupt areas smaller than a section are expanded to 1 MiB. RAM, firmware GPU and `/soc/ranges` extents are supplied at runtime; the helper rounds the end down and may map no descriptor for a sub-section extent, but the checked source does not establish such a selected runtime range, so no finding is added. `PAGE_SUPERSECTION` has no selected use. No boot, page-table update or MMU operation was performed; source-only; no LOC credit.

EK9515 zero-geometry rejection and selected scan recheck (2026-10-26; retained; no new ID or LOC credit): reread the active DOSBoot `FILES` selection and followed `CheckTables()`'s leaf fallback into `AddPartitionVolume()` (`rom/dosboot/mmakefile.src:19,37-38`; `bootscan.c:253-272`). A recognized RDB PART entry passes `PartitionRDBNewHandle()`'s identifier/checksum gate and copies the declared environment fields without validating `DE_NUMHEADS`/`DE_BLKSPERTRACK` (`rom/partition/partitionrdb.c:277-304,479-496`). The RDB/GPT attribute path does not replace those fields with device defaults; that fallback is limited to non-RDB metadata or the explicit legacy-default condition (`bootscan.c:84-98,130-197`). After only the DosType/table-size filter, AddPartitionVolume multiplies the geometry factors and immediately evaluates the remainder (`:204-212`), before filesystem lookup or BootNode creation. This confirms the prior trigger and narrows its order/consequence; no RDB or scan was run. Source-only.


MinGW bootstrap error-formatting failure follow-up (EK9516 added; 2026-10-26): traced the selected bootstrap manifest through `hostinterface.c` into `Host_HostLib_Open()`/`Host_HostLib_GetPointer()` and kernel `startup()` (`arch/all-mingw32/bootstrap/mmakefile.src:6-17`; `hostinterface.c:32-44`; `hostlib.c:12-20,28-36,50-57`; `kernel/kernel_startup.c:37,90-95,100-108`). On a loader failure, `GetErrorStr()` passes the caller's pointer to `FormatMessage(FORMAT_MESSAGE_ALLOCATE_BUFFER...)` but ignores the return value and does not initialize `*error`; if formatting also fails, startup's uninitialized `errstr` is consumed by `%s` and passed to `LocalFree`. Microsoft documents zero as FormatMessage's failure return and the allocated output-pointer contract, but does not promise a usable output on failure. Added conditional EK9516 at medium confidence. No Windows host or failure path was run; source-only.


MinGW restart shared-RAM environment follow-up (EK9517 added; 2026-10-26; no full-body or LOC credit for `memory.c`): traced `ColdReboot()`'s warm callback through `Host_Shutdown()` and its child bootstrap state (`arch/all-mingw32/exec/coldreboot.c:11-21`; `arch/all-mingw32/bootstrap/hostinterface.c:32-44`; `bootstrap/shutdown.c:25-61`). The callback ignores `putenv(var)`'s result, then calls `CreateProcess()` with a NULL environment block, so the child inherits the current environment. The selected RAM allocator reads `SHARED_RAM_VAR`; an absent/empty or malformed value leads to a new mapping, while a valid pointer pair is reused (`bootstrap/sharedmem.h:1-5`; `memory.c:46-93,96-145`). Thus a failed warm update can lose shared-RAM continuity when no prior variable exists, and a failed cold clear can reuse the previous RAM mapping. Added conditional EK9517 at medium confidence; CRT update failure and process creation were not induced. Source-only.


EK9517 environment-contract correction (2026-10-26; replaces the initial failure-only trigger): verified the selected MinGW bootstrap's `putenv()` call against MinGW/MS CRT's `_putenv` alias contract, which changes runtime-local environment structures rather than the OS process environment block, then traced `CreateProcess()` with a NULL environment pointer (`arch/all-mingw32/bootstrap/shutdown.c:38-49`). The child therefore inherits the preexisting OS environment, not the new/cleared CRT value. Followed both outcomes through `AllocateRAM32()` and x86-64 `AllocateRAM()`: warm restart from the normal marker-free launch creates a new mapping, while cold restart can reuse a valid preexisting marker (`bootstrap/memory.c:46-93,96-145`). Rewrote EK9517 from the narrower unchecked-return condition to the deterministic contract mismatch. No Windows process was run; source-only.

KrnMayGetChar selected-override and debug-consumer reconciliation (2026-10-26; no new EK, no body/LOC credit): revisited the generic `rom/kernel/maygetchar.c` fallback and every checked-in local override, then traced `RawMayGetChar()` and its maintained direct consumers. The generic `-1` matches the documented no-input result. All-PC delegates to `con_CanGetc()`/`con_Getc()`; the selected bootconsole returns no input unless serial debug is enabled, then delegates to the serial backend. MinGW32 wraps the nonblocking host `core_getc()` in a balanced Forbid/Permit pair; the host backend returns `-1` when no key event is available and filters non-key, key-up, and zero-character control events. Unix performs one nonblocking STDERR read and maps any result other than one byte to `-1`; its byte is held in `char`, so behavior for non-ASCII bytes depends on `char` signedness, while the public contract promises ASCII. ARM-native returns `-1` without a serial hook, Efika and Sam440 poll their selected UART status before reading, m68k delegates to its debug UART, and OpenSBI delegates to `krnSBIGetC()`. The maintained `GetK()` loop retries only the exact `-1` sentinel; no mismatch was established for the documented ASCII debug stream. AArch64-native's manifest/source discrepancy remains tracked under EK8902. Console hardware semantics, hosted descriptor behavior beyond the selected setup, and external API consumers remain outside this source pass; no console input or platform was run.

OpenSBI idle-task allocation-failure fallback and nested-interrupt pass (2026-10-26; no EK or body credit): traced the selected `riscv64Idle_Init()` unchecked `NewCreateTask()` result and unconditional successful init return (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/exec/exec_idle.c:44-59`) into `cpu_Dispatch()`'s empty-ready fallback (`kernel_cpu.c:161-188`). On a failed idle-task allocation, the fallback remains in its WFI loop, enables SIE before sleeping, and retries `core_Dispatch()` after each wake. The scheduler is entered from the outer trap with `__riscv64_trap_depth == 1`; a fallback-wake interrupt is nested and skips `core_ExitInterrupt()` (`kernel_traps.c:160-178`), but the IRQ body still runs. Before rechecking the ready list, `cpu_Dispatch()` explicitly invokes the Exec soft-interrupt vector when `SFF_SoftInt` is set and services a pending supervisor timer (`kernel_cpu.c:179-185`; `rom/kernel/kernel_intr.h:28-36`). This supports the earlier no-lost-softint conclusion and narrows the idle-task-creation gap: no dispatcher stall or lost softint is established by these local paths. It does not prove all hardware/firmware wake behavior or other degraded-startup contracts. No allocation failure, interrupt, or boot was induced; source-only.

ExecSMP Wait lock-release overlap and per-task accounting recheck (EK9451 strengthened; 2026-10-26; no full-body/LOC credit): re-read the task-state publication and scheduler handling on x86-64 PC, ARM32 and AArch64 (`rom/exec/wait.c:69-113`; `arch/{x86_64-pc,arm-native,aarch64-native}/kernel/kernel_cpu.c`; the selected `core_Switch()`/`core_Dispatch()` paths in `arch/{all-pc,arm-native,aarch64-native}/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c`). The saved register frame precedes `tc_SpinLock` release, but the original CPU has not yet run `core_Switch()`; a signaler and another dispatcher can therefore change the task from TS_WAIT to TS_RUN while the original switch is still active. The original scheduler then sees TS_RUN and performs its ordinary RUN-to-READY transition, allowing the task to be queued while the other CPU may be executing it. Additionally, ARM32/AArch64 update `iet_private2` and `iet_CpuTime` after the lock release and before `core_Switch()` (`kernel_cpu.c:414-444` and `:367-388`); a fast wake and second switch can overlap those per-task writes. Expanded EK9451's impact description; no separate ID because these are consequences of the same premature unlock. No signal or SMP schedule was run; source-only.

m68k CacheControl first-call dispatcher and generated guest thunk recheck (2026-10-26; no new finding; no full-body/LOC credit): re-read `arch/m68k-all/exec/cachecontrol.c:21-43`, its `FILES`/`AFILES` selection (`arch/m68k-all/exec/mmakefile.src:20-36`), and the three implementation vectors in `cachecontrol_.S:17-89`; then traced direct selected callers in Amiga startup and SetPatch plus the m68k emulator thunk (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:2281-2286,7445`). The initial vector disables interrupts while selecting by `AttnFlags` and publishing the CPU-specific vector through `SetFunction`, reenables interrupts, and retries with the original arguments. This is the deliberate one-time dispatcher; the concrete m68k target is single-CPU, and no checked source path here establishes a lost update or invalid cache-state result. Keep the generic unsupported fallback and broader non-m68k guest behavior as separate pending scope; do not credit the wrapper as a full architecture/cache-contract audit.

m68k AROSBootstrap resident-table boundary recheck (EK8932 retained, ROM feasibility unproven; 2026-10-26): reread `scanResidents()`'s starting-slot search and append loop against its repeated `scanMemLists()` callers and the `BootStruct.reslist` consumer. The search considers only indices 0–254; after 255 entries have filled those slots, slot 255 remains NULL and the next invocation finds no starting slot. A single scan nevertheless appends without checking remaining capacity. A scan begun at slot 254 can therefore store two entries within the array and a third into `FakeBase`; with an empty table, a single scan needs 257 matches to do so. After 255 entries have accumulated across prior scans, the next invocation returns without appending. `countres()` still traverses the list until NULL with no capacity argument. This refines per-invocation thresholds but does not establish a supported ROM image with the required resident density; EK8932 remains conditional and no concrete ROM count is claimed. No ROM or boot was used; source-only.

Confirmed i386-PC defaults to TLSF except with `notlsf` (`kernel_startup.c:175,320-321`) and that TLSF corruption reporting passes a frame and 16-slot buffer to the helper then prints its returned depth (`rom/kernel/tlsf.c:371-377`). SetFunction cross-area caller reconciliation (2026-10-26; OD9817 cross-reference): added the generic LowLevel library systemrequesters.c install/restore path to the caller notes for rom/exec/setfunction.c. SetFunction protects the vector mutation, but the LowLevel gate has already fetched its entry before its base lookup and does not hold an expunge-visible reference across subsequent field reads/call-through. LowLevel Expunge restores the vector but does not drain active gate calls; this is tracked once as OD9817 in Other Drivers. Existing wider caller and architecture-specific checks remain open. Source-only.

x86-64 PC protection split publication concurrency pass (EK9525 added; 2026-10-26): re-read the complete split path in core_ProtPage and its selected public vector/caller route. The public KrnSetProtection wrapper performs no serialization before invoking core_ProtKernelArea; when two callers concurrently reach the same still-large 2 MiB PDE, both can pass the unsplit test, allocate from the shared split-page counter without a lock, populate from the old PDE, and publish competing 4 KiB tables. The later PDE publication can discard the earlier call’s permission change, and the shared counter can lose an increment or allocate the same split slot. Startup callers are before AP bring-up; no checked-in post-SMP caller was established, so EK9525 is conditional on external concurrent kernel-resource clients. This is distinct from EK8889’s stale remote TLB after a completed mapping mutation and EK9024’s fixed split-pool exhaustion. No protection call or CPU interleaving was run; source-only.

x86-64 MMU boot-table lifetime and allocator failure route (2026-10-26; no new EK): traced the selected core_SetupMMU allocation branch to the generic all-native boot allocator. KernBootPrivate is boot-allocated/zeroed before core_SetupMMU; the allocator zeroes each returned range, advances its monotonic pointer, and calls krnPanic if an x86-64 request exceeds BootMemLimit instead of returning NULL (arch/all-native/kernel/kernel_bootmem.c:20-46; arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/kernel_startup.c:346,454). The live page-table arrays are retained in KernBootPrivate and no runtime teardown is expected before reboot. This closes the boot-allocation/lifetime source route for the selected target; allocator hardware limits, panic behavior and MMU semantics remain unexecuted. Source-only; no LOC credit.

OOP_DisposeObject null-guard candidate reconciliation (2026-10-26; no EK; no LOC credit): reread the full helper (`rom/oop/disposeobject.c:48-66`), its public precondition (an object previously allocated by `OOP_NewObject`), and the selected debug macros (`rom/oop/intern.h:44-45`; `compiler/arossupport/include/debug.h:57-60,108`). Although the source argument to `EnterFunc` contains `OOP_OCLASS(obj)`, this build forces `SDEBUG` to zero and expands `EnterFunc(x)` to `D(x)`, which is empty; the expression is not evaluated before the body-level NULL return. A repository-wide textual census found no literal `OOP_DisposeObject(NULL)`/`(0)` call among 206 matching expressions in 145 files (the count includes declarations, comments and docs). No selected NULL trigger or valid NULL-input contract was established, so this is not a bug candidate. The census does not prove every selected caller's lifetime path; broader selected caller ownership review remains open. No object was disposed; source-only.


DOSBoot child-registration result and detached BootNode follow-up (EK9526 added; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): rechecked `AddPartitionVolume()`/`CheckTables()`/`CheckPartitions()` as a unit against the pre-DOS `AddBootNode()` allocation and list semantics (`rom/dosboot/bootscan.c:245-316`; `rom/expansion/addbootnode.c:134-168`). `CheckTables()` reports successful table opening, not successful `MakeDosNode()`/`AddBootNode()` registration; `CheckPartitions()` consequently removes the original node even if every replacement fails. Named-object deferred-removal message caller census (EK9505 rechecked; 2026-10-26; no new finding or body credit): re-read `RemNamedObject()` and compared its `no_FreeMessage` lifetime with the documented single pending message/reply contract, `IntNamedObject` layout, and ExecSMP `Forbid()` contract (`rom/utility/remnamedobject.c:26-69,92-126`; `rom/utility/intern.h:98-108`; `rom/exec/forbid.c:33-60`). ExecSMP alert-buffer configuration recheck (EK9527 scope refined; 2026-10-26): `configure.in:1186-1194,1667-1670,2195-2198` enables `__AROSEXEC_SMP__` for the `smp` target variant on x86-64 PC and Raspberry Pi targets. The prior caller trace remains: traced the supervisor-mode alert caller through `Disable()` and `Exec_SystemAlert()` into `Alert_DisplayKrnAlert()` and `KrnDisplayAlert()` (`rom/exec/alert.c:168-186`; `systemalert.c:14-30,39-75`; `exec_intern.h:96`; `disable.c:56-61`). EK629 LowLevel public VBlank API caller extension (2026-10-26; no new EK or LOC credit): traced the packaged AArch64 Raspberry Pi `lowlevel.library` `AddVBlankInt()`/`RemVBlankInt()` client path through `AddIntServer(INTB_VERTB)`, `VBlankServer`, and the generic `IntServer()` walk. WaitPort EK276 BTSerial caller-trigger correction (2026-10-26; no code or LOC credit): re-read BTSerial `devOpen()` in exact order (`rom/bluetooth/classes/btserial/dev.c:120-127`) against `bSerialTask()` dequeue/reply (`btserial.class.c:656-658,694-697`). `devOpen()` calls `GetMsg(unit port)` before `WaitPort(unit port)`. If the worker consumes the initial SDCMD_SETPARAMS first, the opener then waits on the now-empty input port; that is the wrong-port wait already reported as OD3366, not WaitPort returning a stale head. BTSerial supplies a second consumer, but the checked trace does not establish another message queued during WaitPort's locked-nonempty/unlocked-return interval. Removed the unsupported EK276 caller-trigger wording from the report; the generic SMP race remains source-established, while this selected caller is not credited as reproducing its exact trigger. No device or port was used; source-only.

WaitPort EK276 withdrawal after caller/contract recheck (2026-10-26; no source or LOC credit): re-read `WaitPort()` and `GetMsg()` lock intervals, the public WaitPort result contract, the selected BTSerial open/worker ordering, and checked caller-family notes for private or serialized reply ports. PosixC CRT hook expunge/startup race (EK9528 added; 2026-10-26; focused caller/lifetime trace, no whole-file or LOC credit): traced `pthread_create()` from `CreateNewProcTags()` through `Signal()` and immediate return (`compiler/pthread/pthread_create.c:263-290`) into `StarterFunc()`'s `RunCRTThreadHooks(TRUE)` (`:63-89,132-134`). The dispatcher snapshots function pointers under `th_Sem`, releases the lock, and calls them later. PosixC registers `posixc_thread_enter()` in its generated library init and removes it in the expunge hook under the same registry lock (`compiler/crt/posixc/__threadhook.c:132-179`); the callback opens `posixc.library` only after it has begun executing (`:76-82`). Generated `LibClose` invokes expunge at zero open count only when `LIBF_DELEXP` is already set (`tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1506-1522`); a plain last close alone is insufficient. `RemLibrary()` sets the delayed-expunge flag when the library is still open (`rom/exec/remlibrary.c:54-67`; generated `LibExpunge`, `writestart.c:1550-1590`), after which the creator can close its last reference during worker startup and unload the callback code. No in-tree PosixC `RemLibrary()` caller was found, so EK9528 is retained as an external/public-API conditional trigger, with medium occurrence confidence; ordinary applications retaining PosixC and ordinary last close without `LIBF_DELEXP` are excluded. Other CRT hooks and library-expunge/callback contracts remain open. No library or worker was used; source-only.

X86-64 KrnSetProtection post-startup caller trace (EK9525 strengthened; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): closed the generic page-allocation caller question. Selected `KrnAllocPages()` calls `mm_AllocPages()` then `KrnSetProtection()` on each successful allocation (`rom/kernel/allocpages.c:75-82`); DOS `LoadSeg()` supplies an allocator that routes `MEMF_EXECUTABLE` hunks to `KrnAllocPages()` (`rom/dos/loadseg.c:61-79,152-170`), and the ELF loader sets that flag for `SHF_EXECINSTR` sections (`rom/dos/internalloadseg_elf.c:296-311`). Thus executable loads provide a maintained post-startup caller under the x86-64 PC kernel's MMU path. Two simultaneous loads still need protection ranges in the same not-yet-split 2 MiB PDE and overlapping table publication to trigger EK9525; no concurrent load or protection call was run. This replaces the prior external-caller-only qualification; source-only.

X86-64 KrnAllocPages path correction for EK9525 (2026-10-26; no new finding/LOC credit): rechecked the target's `kb_PageSize` state against `rom/kernel/allocpages.c:63-68`. The field has no assignment in selected x86-64 PC sources (`rg kb_PageSize arch/x86_64-pc arch/x86_64-all rom/kernel`), so the generic vector returns NULL before `mm_AllocPages()` or `KrnSetProtection()`. DOS `LoadSeg()` then takes its `AllocMem()` fallback (`rom/dos/loadseg.c:67-79`); executable ELF flags alone do not establish this runtime caller. Corrected the preceding EK9525 strengthening note and restored the external direct-API concurrency qualification. The race remains a valid public-vector condition; selected startup updates are before AP bring-up. Source-only.


ConClip synchronous request shutdown recheck (EK9529 added; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): reread `handleall()` and traced its one-time `Wait()` result through the port-drain conditional, Ctrl-C exit, port deletion, and each selected synchronous sender. KrnAllocPages x86-64 selected-caller census refinement (EK9525 scope checked; 2026-10-26; no new finding or LOC credit): enumerated all production C call expressions and preprocessor guards. RISC-V OpenSBI EFI retry snapshot reconciliation (EK8862 restored to detailed report/index; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): re-read `efi_stub_entry()` around both map reads and the ExitBootServices retry (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/efi_stub.c:840-869`), then traced the first-snapshot arrays to their consumers (`kernel_startup.c:581-600`; `kernel_mmu.c:435-445`). `efi_collect_memory()` and `efi_collect_firmware()` run only on the first successful map (`:852-853`); after a failed exit, a refreshed map is used for a second exit without rebuilding either array. Confirmed the candidate remained in the coverage narrative but had no detailed report heading or AROS.md index link; restored it as EK8862 with the trigger limited to a successful retry whose refreshed descriptor classification/ranges materially differ. ExecSMP RemDevice/OpenDevice lifetime recheck (EK9099 confirmed; 2026-10-26; no new finding or body/LOC credit): reread `RemDevice()` and `OpenDevice()` around their list/vector boundaries (`rom/exec/remdevice.c:57-85`; `opendevice.c:92-114`) and the selected ExecSMP lock macros (`exec_locks.h:34-64`). OpenDevice holds the DeviceList read lock only for `FindName()`, releases it before invoking the device Open vector, and increments a dynamic device's open count only after that vector has begun. RemDevice takes no DeviceList write lock and wraps the expunge vector only in `Forbid()`; Exec documents Forbid as processor-local on ExecSMP (`rom/exec/forbid.c:58-65`). A selected USB class expunge can remove/free its zero-open-count device base during the lookup-to-vector interval, confirming EK9099's race boundary. This recheck adds no independent issue and no caller beyond the previously inventoried dynamic-device families. No open/expunge overlap or device operation was run; source-only.

FindPort borrowed-pointer contract recheck (EK9094/EK820/EK8913 reconciliation; 2026-10-26; no new finding or LOC credit): reread `rom/exec/findport.c:23-28,54-69`, `rom/exec/forbid.c:40-50`, and `rom/exec/remport.c:49-75`. FindPort documents list arbitration by Forbid/Permit; on ExecSMP its internal PortListSpinLock protects only the FindName traversal and is released before the borrowed MsgPort pointer is returned. Forbid is explicitly processor-local, and RemPort's same list lock protects only unlinking; it does not pin the port after lookup. This confirms the primitive-level lifetime limit, while the concrete selected owner/sender races remain caller-specific: EK9094 (ConClip paste), EK820 (Break PORT route), and the graphics callers cross-referenced above. No separate generic primitive defect is credited because no stronger public owner/lifetime contract or distinct selected consumer was established. The report's ConClip, GfxControl, and Editor reconciliation notes remain as recorded in EK9094; broader caller census remains open. No port operation or interleaving was run; source-only.

The aggregate ReAction class parent edge is disabled; no default Workbench packaging claim is made. No library, class object or semaphore was used; source-only.

RawPutChar direct-caller census and early-kernel availability trace (2026-10-26; no new finding or LOC credit): searched checked-in C/assembly source for `RawPutChar()` and found textual references in 37 paths (61 matches, including declarations/comments). RawPutChar internal debugger caller pass (2026-10-26; no new EK or LOC credit): traced the generic Exec `Debug()` vector through `InternalDebug()` to `RawIOInit()`, `GetK()`/`RawMayGetChar()`, and the echo/backspace/newline `RawPutChar()` calls (`rom/exec/debug.c:54-58`; `debug_internal.c:27-62,405-418`; `rawioinit.c:44-48`; `rawmaygetchar.c:49-52`; `rawputchar.c:47-51`). `InternalDebug()` obtains the kernel debug-input provider before entering the loop and releases it on the explicit SAD quit command; the generic `RawIOInit()` is intentionally a no-op, while `RawMayGetChar()` delegates availability and blocking semantics to `KrnMayGetChar()`. i386-PC SAD scan-code bounds finding recheck (EK8942 strengthened, 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): counted the initializer entries in `arch/i386-pc/exec/debug_internal.c:43-47` (50 entries, indices 0-49) and traced the scancode producer/filter (`getkey()`/`GetK()`, `:388-411,452-462`) into both direct table subscripts (`InternalDebug()`, `:65-86`). Confirmed representative ordinary set-1 make codes F1 (`0x3b`), Caps Lock (`0x3a`), and Num Lock (`0x45`) exceed the table index range; space is separately translated only in the argument path, so it also indexes out of range in command collection. Reset-callback removal semantics and selected dynamic-owner pass (EK59 retained; no new EK or body credit; 2026-10-26): re-read `Exec_DoResetCallbacks()`'s safe-next traversal and support-task handoff against `RemResetCallback()`'s unlink-only implementation (`rom/exec/doresetcallbacks.c:115-160`; `remresetcallback.c:45-49`). Confirmed the two distinct consequences already tracked: removing/freeing the saved successor during the non-supervisor wait is EK59; freeing callback owner state while a dispatched callback is still running is caller-owned and is covered for selected PCI network units by OD3972 and HDAudio controllers by OD3973 in the Other Drivers report. Named-object removal/finder interleaving and AttemptRem contract pass (EK9506 expanded, EK9860 added; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): re-traced `FindNamedObject()`'s lock-protected lookup/count increment (`rom/utility/findnamedobject.c:79-110`), `ReleaseNamedObject()`'s zero transition (`releasenamedobject.c:71-81`), and `RemNamedObject()`'s count check before lock acquisition and unconditional unlink once the lock is acquired (`remnamedobject.c:115-126`). This confirms EK9506's check-to-unlink window: a concurrent finder can increment the still-linked object after the remover observes zero but before it obtains the namespace semaphore; the remover then unlinks and replies without rechecking. Named-object zero-count check versus namespace unlink recheck (EK9506 expanded; 2026-10-26; no body or LOC credit): traced `ReleaseNamedObject()`'s final decrement and deferred call into `RemNamedObject()` (`rom/utility/releasenamedobject.c:73-81`) against `FindNamedObject()`'s semaphore-protected list search and count increment (`findnamedobject.c:79-100`) and `RemNamedObject()`'s removal path (`remnamedobject.c:115-126`). When a deferred removal is pending, the final release can observe zero and enter `RemNamedObject()`. That function checks `no_UseCount == 0` before waiting for `ns_Lock`; a concurrent finder can then acquire the semaphore, find the still-linked object and increment the count, after which the remover acquires the semaphore and unlinks without rechecking. It replies to the removal message despite the new outstanding reference, so the owner may free the object returned by the finder. The race requires overlap on ExecSMP; no count or semaphore interleaving was run. No whole-file/LOC credit; all three bodies were already credited as full reads. Source-only.

RISC-V64 shell-command trampoline/cache-coherency pass (EK9873 added; 2026-10-26): checked the RISC-V `FullJumpVec` contract against the selected resource initializer and OpenSBI Exec cache hook. `__AROS_SET_FULLJMP()` writes executable instructions and its header requires an instruction-cache flush (`arch/riscv64-all/include/aros/cpu.h:85-98`), while `shellcommands_init.c:72` guards the only `CacheClearE()` call with `__AROS_USE_FULLJMP`, undefined by the RISC-V CPU headers. The OpenSBI Exec init installs a remote-fence `CacheClearE_SBI()` for instruction-cache clears (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/exec/cpu_init.c:196-205`; `:39-54`), but this caller never invokes it. Added EK9873 for RISC-V64 OpenSBI. AArch64 was not reconciled in this initial pass; the follow-up below resolves its selected cache-clear path. No boot or command invocation was run. Source-only.


AArch64 shell-command trampoline/cache path reconciliation (EK9873 expanded; 2026-10-26): followed the Raspberry Pi AArch64 target's `arch=raspi-aarch64` Exec source selection to the `arch/aarch64-native/exec/cachecleare.c` SVC wrapper and its kernel receiver. CLI synthesized-stream failure caller recheck (EK9875 trigger narrowed, 2026-10-26): traced selected `SystemTagList()` stream defaults and startup-packet construction. `sis`/`sos` begin from `Input()`/`Output()`, `ses` begins BNULL, caller tags can replace them, and the child packet forwards `sos` plus `ses` through `ExtArg` (`rom/dos/systemtaglist.c:133-155,402-415,443-446`). Thus EK9875 requires a streamless caller or explicit BNULL output/error, followed by successful stdout synthesis and failed stderr synthesis; it is not asserted for ordinary calls with inherited live streams. The process tags still set `NP_Output`/`NP_Error` BNULL, so the independent `DosEntry()` cleanup does not own the locally synthesized handle. No shell or failure was run; source-only.

Signal-bit sign-conversion reconciliation (EK8800 withdrawn; authoritative correction, 2026-10-26): all earlier references above that describe EK8800 as retained, confirmed, expanded or active are historical audit notes and are superseded by the corrections at the start of this ledger and the corrected Shell row. The source-level expressions remain inventoried, but positive signed shifts into bit 31 that are representable in the corresponding unsigned type have implementation-defined signed conversion under the applicable C rules. No selected compiler output or target behavior establishes an incorrect signal mask, so EK8800 is not an active finding and must not appear in the detailed report or master index. No signal operation or compiler execution was performed; source-only.

AArch64-native raw interrupt-mask pair and selected caller reconciliation (2026-10-26; no new EK): reread the complete `cli.c`/`sti.c` wrappers and traced their SVC numbers through `handle_syscall()` and the EL1/EL0 vector save/restore paths. `SC_CLI` sets both I/F in the saved PSTATE and `SC_STI` clears both; the vector restore masks only during frame restoration and `eret` installs the requested PSTATE (`syscall.c:180-196`; `vectors.S:117-145`). The selected Exec pair increments/decrements its per-task nesting count around these calls; Enable invokes STI only at the outer release and outside supervisor state (`rom/exec/disable.c:83-91`; `rom/exec/enable.c:94-106`). This masks the FIQ-delivered cross-CPU signal IPI as intended. The AArch64 idle-task STI call was checked; restricted FIQ callbacks use a separate raw IRQ/FIQ save-restore path because a CLI SVC would nest on the FIQ-handler SVC stack (`arch/arm-native/exec/exec_platform.h:285-302`). No independent source defect established. External direct kernel-library users and hardware interrupt timing remain open. No build, interrupt, or privilege transition was run; source-only.


x86-64 PC TLS header BSP setup and early-access caller pass (2026-10-26; no new EK): reread `tls_t` and its `TLS_GET`/`TLS_SET` macros (`arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/tls.h:12-49`), then traced the selected BSP allocation and installation: `kernel_startup()` obtains `BOOTTLS`, passes it to `core_SetupGDT()`, loads the resulting GDT with `core_CPUSetup()`, and only then reaches the first explicit `TLS_SET(ScheduleData)` and `TLS_SET(SysBase)` (`kernel_startup.c:381-397,425,557-566,589-590,672-744,764-797`). Every current TLS field is 4 or 8 bytes, matching the macro's implemented access widths. The TLS descriptor stores a 32-bit base, so this trace only establishes the selected boot-memory region used by the bootstrap; allocator placement above 4 GiB and secondary-CPU TLS/GDT installation remain open platform checks. No separate defect is established in the inspected header/BSP path. This adds targeted caller coverage only, not a new path or LOC credit. No build, boot, or TLS access was run; source-only.


CreatePool failure-path caller pass in selected MUI Window and List classes (2026-10-26; no new EK/GD): traced the selected `CreatePool()` failure branches in `Window__OM_NEW()` and `List__OM_NEW()` through `NewObjectA()` and each class's disposal path (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/window.c:2859-2872,3091-3100`; `list.c:1287-1307,1365-1388`; `rom/intuition/newobjecta.c:107-146`). `NewObjectA()` creates its per-class pool with `MEMF_CLEAR`, so zero-valued uninitialized pointers/counts used by the rollback disposers are established for these new instances. The Window class returns NULL on pool failure and `DeletePool(NULL)` is accepted; the List class also returns NULL and only deletes a non-NULL internally owned pool. Neither selected caller uses the object after construction failure. No independent issue established in these two paths. This is cross-subsystem caller coverage only, with no body/LOC credit; other pool callers remain open. No allocation failure or GUI was run; source-only.


x86-64 PC bootstrap TLS-base bound follow-up (2026-10-26; no EK; prior caveat narrowed): traced the selected Multiboot bootstrap's kickstart placement against the TLS GDT descriptor. `prepare_message()` publishes the loaded image end as `KRN_KernelHighest` (`arch/all-pc/bootstrap/bootstrap.c:522-537`); the 64-bit bootstrap computes the required region as image size plus 256 MiB and selects a RAM interval wholly below 4 GiB (`:669-731`, especially `:701-716`). The kernel's first boot allocator starts at that published image end and obtains `BOOTTLS` during early startup before the later MMU/page-table allocations (`arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/kernel_startup.c:278-297,378-397,801-807`). This removes the earlier suggestion that ordinary selected BSP placement can put this descriptor base above 4 GiB; no active BSP TLS truncation finding is established. The general boot allocator's published limit still extends to the end of the containing RAM map entry, and this pass does not bound pathological boot-tag relocation volume or prove a secondary-CPU TLS/GDT path, so those remain outside the conclusion. No boot or firmware map was used; source-only.

RISC-V64 per-core processor identification caller-contract pass (EK8906 detailed; 2026-10-26): re-read the complete OpenSBI SBI-ID helper and its generic initializer/query callers (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/processor/processor_sbi.c:20-40`; `arch/riscv64-all/processor/processor_init.c:412-425`; `processor_util.c:126-134`). RISC-V64 RVV first-use trap path recheck (EK198 strengthened; 2026-10-26): confirmed new task `sstatus` is initialized with FS_INITIAL and no VS bits (`arch/riscv64-all/exec/preparecontext.c:66-73`); the RISC-V Vector Extension specification makes a vector instruction with VS=Off an illegal-instruction exception. The selected trap map sends scause 2 through kernel exception handlers and then the Exec task trap handler (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_traps.c:60-66,242-258`; `rom/kernel/kernel_intr.h:38-55`); the default `Exec_TrapHandler` marks it AT_DeadEnd (`rom/exec/traphandler.c:63-77`). The OpenSBI CPU header states that lazy handler/save/restore protocol despite no implementation (`kernel_cpu.h:29-34`); folded this into EK198. The separate state-loss path remains when a task enables VS itself and later switches. No instruction or trap was executed; source-only, no new body/LOC credit.

OpenSBI shared FDT depth finding caller census and trigger refinement (EK285 retained; 2026-10-26): re-read the selected discovery loops and every in-tree `FDT_GetReg`/`FDT_GetRegNamed` call in OpenSBI PCI, DWI2C, DW UART and BattClock. The three hardware discovery loops pass nodes returned by whole-tree `FDT_FindCompatible()` directly into register decoding, with no caller-side nesting cap (`pcidt_driverclass.c:627-678`; `dwi2c_init.c:206-227,119-140`; `dwuart_init.c:79-97`). BattClock's tree-order scan chooses the preceding chip bus and queries its `reg`; it queries the RTC node's `reg` only as an optional address override (`battclock_init.c:59-112`). Refined the latter reachability: a deep RTC node alone does not imply `fdt_parent()` indexes past the stack; the bus queried for its base (or the RTC itself when it has `reg`) must be at depth 17 or greater. This supports the selected call chain while keeping EK285 conditional on firmware tree layout. No FDT, firmware, or device was run; source-only, no body/LOC credit.

x86-64 PC BSP APIC configuration caller pass (EK9130 rechecked; no new EK or body credit; 2026-10-26): traced `Platform_Init()`'s `core_APIC_GetBase()` → `core_APIC_Config(base, 0)` → `core_APIC_Enable(base, 0)` sequence (`arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/platform_init.c:277-279`) through the shared PC register routines (`arch/all-pc/kernel/apic.h:67-69,91-94`; `apic_ia32.c:968-1083`). Config writes the xAPIC MMIO DFR/LDR/SVR and default LINT/error-vector registers; ACPI's later per-CPU initialization reapplies its MADT LINT NMI settings (`acpi_apic.c:131-177,188-205`). Task.resource late-prelaunch stale-pointer report reconciliation (EK8866 detailed and indexed; 2026-10-26; no file/LOC credit): reconciled the existing finding evidence with the Exec report and master index. `TaskLaunch()` makes a task ready and re-enables local interrupts before the task.resource hook; the PC, ARM32 and AArch64 SMP schedulers can select it on another eligible CPU. If that task self-removes before the hook, the task.resource RemTask wrapper has no entry to remove, Exec cleanup frees its task memory, and the creator may then publish the stale pointer. `NextTaskEntry()` reads task state through that pointer. Added the standalone report entry and index link. This scheduling interleaving remains source-inferred and unrun; no file-body or LOC coverage changed. Source-only.

Repository-wide `NewAddTask()` caller census and failure-path reconciliation (2026-10-26; no new EK or LOC credit): searched the pinned checkout for every literal `NewAddTask()` call. Excluding declarations, comments, the task.resource forwarding wrapper, Exec's `AddTask`/`NewCreateTaskA` implementations, and the generated m68k thunk, callers are confined to DOS `CreateNewProcA` (checks the result), VMM's error-handler startup (checks NULL), Efika idle startup (EK9074), trackdisk (OD3566), USB MassStorage (OD9563/OD9564), USB HID keyboard/mouse (OD3564/OD3565/OD2247), USB stack/hub startup (OD2788/OD3357/OD3358), and the eight network `AddUnitTask` AROS implementations. x86-64 PC TLS descriptor selected AP caller recheck (no new EK or body/LOC credit; 2026-10-26): traced BSP TLS allocation/installation and AP-specific allocation through every selected direct `TLS_SET()` use (`arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/kernel_startup.c:382-397,565,590,672-746,801-807`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/platform_post.c:73-81`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/smp.c:87-114,247-250`). `core_SetupGDT()` encodes the GS base in a 32-bit descriptor; AP TLS is allocated with `MEMF_24BITDMA` and the selected x86-64 PC map confines that class to the first 16 MiB (`kernel_startup.c:59-60`), so the AP base fits. AP GDT setup precedes `TLS_SET(SysBase)` and `TLS_SET(KernelBase)`, and current TLS fields use widths implemented by the macros. BSP TLS is instead obtained from `krnAllocBootMem()` whose range follows the RAM region containing the kernel; this pass did not establish a <4-GiB ceiling for every selected bootloader placement. Retain that BSP physical-address caveat; it is not promoted to an active defect without a selected placement demonstrating truncation. AP allocation failure remains EK8830. No build, boot or GS access was run; source-only.

x86-64 PC `KrnSetProtection()` selected-caller census and EK9525 scope check (2026-10-26; no new finding or body/LOC credit): searched checked-in C/assembly for direct wrapper and lower-level protection calls, then resolved the x86-64 PC routes. Startup calls `core_ProtKernelArea()` directly for zero-page and kernel-image protection before AP launch (`arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/kernel_startup.c:587,601`). `rom/kernel/allocpages.c` is the selected generic wrapper that calls public `KrnSetProtection()` after page allocation; it returns NULL while `kb_PageSize` is zero, for which this target has no assignment (`allocpages.c:63-68`; `kernel_base.h:106`). DOS LoadSeg/UnLoadSeg and the developer allocator test reach `KrnFreePages()` only on page-allocation branches, with no successful selected x86-64 allocator path established here. `CreateSegList()`'s protection route is guarded by `__AROSPLATFORM_WXSEG__`, configured for Apple Silicon hosts, not x86-64 PC (`compiler/arossupport/createseglist.c:60-99`; `configure.in:1805-1809`). Remaining direct calls are other architecture implementations or boot code. Thus selected startup protection does not overlap AP execution and no checked-in post-SMP caller establishes concurrent edits to one unsplit PDE; EK9525 remains an external kernel-resource API condition. No protection call or interleaving was run; source-only.

x86-64 PC BSP TLS ceiling reconciliation (2026-10-26; no new EK or body/LOC credit): resolved the contradictory TLS caveats by separating the ordinary selected placement from an unbounded boot-payload edge. The Multiboot bootstrap reserves image size plus 256 MiB and clips its placement interval at 4 GiB (`arch/all-pc/bootstrap/bootstrap.c:673-716`); this keeps the ordinary BSP TLS address below 4 GiB when early allocations remain within the reserve. The x86-64 PC kernel instead sets `BootMemLimit` to the end of the original RAM-map entry containing `KRN_KernelHighest`, less the debug buffer, without a 4-GiB clamp (`kernel_startup.c:278-297`). Before allocating BSP TLS, it copies the complete tag list, memory map (`mmap_len`), BSS descriptors and command-line/bootloader strings (`:305-346,801-807`; `arch/all-native/kernel/boot_utils.c:28-99`). Consequently, a bootloader payload requiring more than the 256-MiB reserve could advance the allocator past 4 GiB if the containing RAM-map entry extends above that boundary; `core_SetupGDT()` would then truncate the GS base to 32 bits (`kernel_startup.c:735-742`). No ordinary checked-in bootloader payload or map establishes this extreme condition, and no runtime data was used, so this remains an external boot-data boundary rather than a confirmed finding. The coverage row now reflects this qualification and supersedes earlier blanket statements that the BSP base was either proven below 4 GiB or wholly unresolved. Source-only.

PC bootstrap framebuffer mirror capacity and initialization order (EK9876 added; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): re-traced all in-tree `AllocFB()` callers and the custom workspace allocator against selected bootconsole setup. The bootstrap first sets `fb_Mirror = __bs_malloc(0)` at workspace start (`bootstrap.c:595-598`); Multiboot1/2 initialize the framebuffer console before `AllocFB()` (`multiboot1.c:73-81`; `multiboot2.c:120-124`), and successful VESA mode setup also calls `con_InitVESA()` before `AllocFB()` (`vesa_setup.c:121-123`). `fb_Init()`/`fb_Resize()` call `fb_Clear()`, which `memset`s `scr_Width * scr_Height` through that pointer (`arch/all-native/bootconsole/screen_fb.c:91-129`); the selected font is 8×14 (`font8x14.c:5-6`). The 16-MiB `workspace` allocator returns NULL for a larger reserve (`support.c:64-92`), and `AllocFB()` ignores that result (`bootstrap.c:459-466`). Thus a graphical mode with over 16,777,216 text cells causes an out-of-workspace mirror clear before the later failed reservation; added EK9876. This is conditional on extraordinarily large but representable bootloader/VBE geometry; no boot or framebuffer was used. Source-only.
RISC-V scheduler affinity-field gate recheck (EK9131 scope; no new candidate or body credit; 2026-10-26): compared the two native-RISC-V scheduler expressions that treat `iet_CpuAffinity` as an integer with the public internal field type (`rom/exec/etask.h:67`) and the pointer-aware ARM/AArch64 helper implementations. The apparent pointer-versus-mask mismatch is inside `__AROSEXEC_SMP__`. In the OpenSBI configure branch, RV64 sets `PLATFORM_EXECSMP` but not `ENABLE_EXECSMP` (`configure.in:2202-2229`), so this branch is not compiled for that target. The native SiFive U boot path remains blocked before kernel entry: its boot function loops in WFI (`arch/riscv-native/sifive_u/boot/boot.c:38-44`), and the startup assembly handoff is disabled (`kernel_startup.c:50-66`); the boot aggregate labels the incomplete package `kernel-package-native-riscv-missing`. Thus no selected, runnable RISC-V SMP trigger is established, and no affinity finding is added. The existing latent dispatch wrong-node candidate EK9131 remains scoped as documented. Source-only.


Intuition default screen-notify child failure caller trace (2026-10-26; no new EK): traced `InitDefaultScreennotifyHandler()` through `NewCreateTask()`, the child startup handshake, and the failed-port path (`rom/intuition/screennotifytask.c:65-110`). The parent clears the handshake bit before task creation and waits for the child to signal after setting `success`; when `CreateMsgPort()` fails, the child signals and then parks in `Wait(0)`, so the parent’s `RemTask(task)` is an intentional cleanup of a live, non-running task. On success, the parent publishes the returned port only after the same handshake. This caller does not add a trigger beyond the already tracked remote `RemTask` lifetime issues; it is a bounded selected caller check, not evidence that all RemTask callers are closed. No task-creation failure or port allocation failure was induced; source-only.


EK9877 report recovery verification (2026-10-29; no path/LOC credit): re-read the Apple/AArch64 conditional branch in `kickstart.c`, its host pthread declarations, the ignored `pthread_create()` result, unconditional detach of local `tid`, and the only kernel entry in the new thread routine. Restored the detailed startup-hang path and kept thread-creation failure as the required trigger; no host failure or bootstrap was induced. Source-only.
Darwin/AArch64 kernel-thread creation caller pass (EK9877 added, 2026-10-26): checked the selected `arch/all-unix/bootstrap/mmakefile.src` object set, Apple/AArch64 preprocessor branch, local host `pthread_t_host` ABI declarations, `pthread_create` and `pthread_detach` sequence, and the Cocoa loop plus `kernel_thread()` entry path (`kickstart.c:12-20,35-91`). The creation return is ignored, `tid` is an uninitialized local, detach follows unconditionally, and the only kernel entry is in the new thread; if creation fails, the main thread stays in `cocoa_runloop_step()` forever. AHI database lookup-to-obtain lifetime cross-check (OD1442 expanded in Other Drivers; 2026-10-26; no new Exec finding or body/LOC credit): rechecked `FindSemaphore()` against `InternalObtainSemaphore()` and the AHI `LockDatabase()` callers. EK9873 trampoline/cache-visibility recheck (2026-10-26; retained, no new ID or body credit): re-read the selected shellcommands initializer, architecture trampoline definitions, and the two target-specific cache-clear providers. `__AROS_SET_FULLJMP()` writes the RISC-V instruction words and target pointer, while the architecture header explicitly requires a subsequent `fence.i`/`CacheClearE`; AArch64 writes its two-instruction literal-load/branch sequence and 64-bit target. Both target manifests select `kernel-shellcommands`. This confirms the source-level missing sync and affected target scope already reported by EK9873; stale instruction-fetch manifestation remains conditional. No build or command execution was performed; source-only.

EK19 hosted panic-buffer target expansion (2026-10-26; existing ID expanded, no body/LOC credit): re-read the generic Unix panic formatter and its `kernel_startup()` libc-open failure path, then reconciled Android's architecture-specific kernel manifest and `Alert_Init()` startup set. Pthread condition timed-wait caller extension to EK568 (2026-10-26; no new ID or LOC credit): traced `_pthread_cond_timedwait()`'s timer setup and error exits (`compiler/pthread/pthread_cond_timedwait.c:60-80`) through the shared `OpenTimerDevice()` and `CloseTimerDevice()` implementation (`pthread.c:129-195`). Failed OpenDevice calls cleanup before submission; after a successful open, `clock_gettime()` failure also closes before the timer request is initialized/sent. CloseTimerDevice checks/aborts based on the stack request's uninitialized `io_Flags` and message state. Extended the existing EK568 scope from timed locks to condition timed waits; same unsent-request cleanup root cause, no new finding. No clock/open failure or timer operation was induced; source-only.

Pthread barrier wait cancellation-point trace (EK9878 added; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): traced `pthread_barrier_wait()`'s internal `pthread_cond_wait()` through `_pthread_cond_timedwait()`'s `SIGBREAKF_CTRL_C` path to `pthread_testcancel()`/`pthread_exit()`. New pthreads are initialized with deferred cancellation enabled; the condition wait reacquires the barrier mutex before cancellation is acted upon, while the barrier wait has no cleanup for its locked mutex or incremented generation counter. Current POSIX.1-2024 cancellation-point rules list `pthread_cond_wait` but not `pthread_barrier_wait` and prohibit introducing cancellation points into other specified functions (Open Group 2.9.5.2). Added EK9878. Repository-wide C search found no direct barrier caller outside implementation/declaration; public clients remain the trigger surface. No thread, barrier, or cancellation was run; source-only.

Exec AllocSignal/FreeSignal vector and selected-caller recheck (EK8800 disposition reconfirmed; no new finding; 2026-10-26): reread both complete vector/helper bodies (`rom/exec/allocsignal.c`, 59 `cloc 2.06` C code lines; `rom/exec/freesignal.c`, 18 lines) and traced every checked-in `AllocTaskSignal()` caller. The public vector narrows its LONG argument to BYTE for the legacy D0.b ABI; `-1` and other negative values take the automatic-allocation branch, while nonnegative specific indices are checked against `tc_SigAlloc`. The only direct private helper use outside the vector is NewCreateTaskA's unpublished task-message-port setup, which initializes the new task's allocation mask before allocating the port bit (`newcreatetaska.c:218-235`). The ordinary current-task path is therefore the only published-task owner mutating allocation/wait/exception masks; received-bit changes are protected by Disable plus the per-task ExecSMP lock. FreeSignal's `-1` no-op and allocated-bit clearing match its documented caller contract; invalid bit numbers and freeing another subsystem's reserved bits require caller misuse and are not promoted. Rechecked bit-31 expressions against the signed/unsigned conversion disposition: no selected compiler result establishes a wrong mask, so withdrawn EK8800 remains withdrawn and no new finding is added. No signal allocation, free, wait or compiler execution was run; source-only.

Exec Signal/SetSignal/Wait received-mask and scheduling handoff recheck (existing EK811/EK9018/EK274 and cancelable-IPI findings retained; no new EK; 2026-10-26): reread the complete generic `signal.c` (310 `cloc 2.06` C code lines), `setsignal.c` (34), and `wait.c` (55), including local and cross-CPU branches, terminal-task handling, exceptions, affinity scheduling, and the SMP wait-lock transfer across `KrnSwitch()`. Confirmed `SetSignal()` and `Wait()` serialize received-mask updates with the same per-task spinlock on SMP; the already-documented ChildWait EK811 remains a predicate/list-check versus clear ordering race rather than a torn mask update. Rechecked the initial remote-CPU choice against hook delivery: restricted-context `signal_hook()` commits the signal bit under `tc_SpinLock`, handles a TS_WAIT target through `krnSysCallReschedTask()`, and sets task-exception state before arranging local scheduling attention. The source does not prove a distinct lost signal from an outdated initial CPU choice, so no additional finding is promoted; migration timing remains unexecuted and the existing EK9451/EK274/queued-IPI lifetime findings retain their exact interleaving scopes. SetSignal/SetExcept's absent automatic exception callback remains withdrawn as a defect under the prior API-semantics disposition. No signal, task switch, IPI or SMP schedule was run; source-only.

NewAllocEntry transaction and caller-settlement recheck (2026-10-26; no new finding or LOC credit): reread the complete `rom/exec/newallocentry.c`, `allocentry.c`, and `freeentry.c` bodies and compared `MemList`/`MemEntry` widths (`compiler/include/exec/memory.h:49-65`) with the `NewCreateTaskA`, Bluetooth and Poseidon direct C callers. The UWORD entry count times the selected 32/64-bit `MemEntry` width remains representable in `ULONG`; the copied-list allocation therefore has no count-product wrap at its API limit. On a nonzero entry allocation failure, prior entries have already had their address and length written before the rollback loop frees them; the failed entry is not freed, and the list allocation is released. Zero-length entries are deliberately returned with a NULL address, and `FreeEntry` safely passes that zero-size pair to `FreeMem`. The `me_Reqs`/`me_Addr` fields are a union, so the copied address overwriting request flags is the declared layout, not an omitted-field defect. Checked the maintained callers' initialized counts and their task/list rollback paths; existing NewCreateTaskA caller findings remain scoped as recorded. No allocator failure or task creation was induced; source-only.

EK198 task privilege and trap route recheck (2026-10-26; candidate retained, no new ID): confirmed `PrepareContext()` sets `SSTATUS_SPP`, so an ordinary new RISC-V task resumes in S-mode and can write supervisor status state; therefore the report's separate case of a task enabling VS itself is not blocked by U-mode privilege (`arch/riscv64-all/exec/preparecontext.c:68-73`). x86-64 PC `KrnMapGlobal` concurrency finding recheck (EK8887 retained, 2026-10-26; no new ID or LOC credit): re-read the complete x86-64 mapping loop and selected platform route (`arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/mapglobal.c:88-170`; `arch/x86_64-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:66-68`). `map_global_2m()` reads and writes the shared PML4 and nested PDPE entries, allocates missing tables, and publishes parent pointers without a lock or compare-and-swap; APs load `__KernBootPrivate->MMU` (`arch/all-pc/kernel/smp.c:91-108`) and the platform starts SMP before marking initialization primed (`platform_post.c:196-207`). Selected PCIPC calls this mapper for BARs extending beyond its 128-GiB identity window (`arch/all-pc/hidds/pcipc/pcipc_driverclass.c:230-258`). PCI enumeration holds `dev_lock` in shared mode while invoking callbacks (`rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:421-448`), which does not serialize independent enumerators. Thus two concurrent high-BAR MapPCI calls targeting the same previously absent PML4/PDPE entry can each allocate a child table and overwrite the other's parent entry; the losing caller may return success with its leaf installed in an unreachable table. The selected tree does not establish that two such calls actually overlap or that firmware supplies the needed BAR placement, so EK8887 remains explicitly conditional and no runtime manifestation is claimed. No allocation, enumeration, BAR or SMP interleaving was exercised; source-only.

Realtime SetPlayerAttrsA `PLAYER_ExtSync` input/caller reconciliation (EK9055 retained; 2026-10-26; no new finding or LOC credit): re-read the complete setter tag loop and `PLAYER_ExtSync` branch (`workbench/libs/realtime/setplayerattrsa.c:76-307,263-294`) against `CreatePlayerA()` defaults and its only in-tree direct call outside the setter (`createplayera.c:127-158`; `developer/demos/realtdemo.c:58-69`) and the public realtime tag/API documentation (`compiler/include/libraries/realtime.h`; `createplayera.c:47-108`).
