Rechecked adjacent tag branches and `CreatePlayerA()` failure cleanup against EK9056/EK9059; no distinct untracked return/cleanup defect established. Source and caller evidence only; no player/tag call was run.

Native-RISC-V SMP spin-wait helper reachability recheck (2026-10-26; no finding): read the complete `arch/riscv-native/exec/platform_init.c` spin-fail and `Exec_TaskSpinUnlock()` paths and traced `TS_SPIN` placement/requeue in `arch/riscv-native/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:219-228`. `Exec_TaskSpinUnlock()` moves matching tasks from `TaskSpinning` to `TaskReady` without changing `tc_State`; the scheduler tests `TS_SPIN` again and would return such a task to `TaskSpinning`. However, the native-RISC-V `EXECTASK_SPINLOCK_LOCK/UNLOCK` macros have no checked-in call sites, the only `TS_SPIN` assignment is the fail hook reached through that lock hook, and maintained native-RISC-V configure variants do not enable ExecSMP. The apparent wake-state defect therefore has no selected in-tree trigger and is not promoted as a current finding. This does not change EK9513's separate missing return in the manually enabled init hook. No spinlock wait or scheduler execution was run; source-only.

EK9471 managed MemHeader callback reachability recheck (2026-10-26; candidate retained with explicit API-only boundary, no new finding or LOC credit): re-read the `MemHeaderExt` callback layout and `AllocVecPooled()`/`FreeVecPooled()` dispatch, then searched all checked-in assignments of `mhe_Alloc` and `mhe_AllocVec`. The only ordinary allocator backends are TLSF, Radeon and VideoCore; TLSF sets both generic and vector callbacks, while Radeon and VideoCore set only `mhe_Alloc` and their callbacks return NULL, so they cannot provide the successful managed allocation needed to create a pool header. No checked-in code constructs a `CreatePool()` from a custom managed header. Thus EK9471 remains an implementation/API defect for a custom managed backend that supplies successful ordinary allocation without a vector callback; no current in-tree trigger is established. The `FreeVecPooled()` null-check supports the interpretation that this callback may be absent, but does not by itself define a full custom-backend contract. No pool or allocation operation was run; source-only.

EK9152 shared-attempt/release count recheck (2026-10-26; existing conditional candidate retained, no new finding or LOC credit): retraced both public wrappers through `InternalAttemptSemaphore()` and `ReleaseSemaphore()`. `AttemptSemaphore()` passes the current task (NULL before bootstrap publication); `AttemptSemaphoreShared()` passes NULL unconditionally. On an initialized free semaphore, either path can increment `ss_NestCount` and `ss_QueueCount` while leaving `ss_Owner == NULL`; the `ReleaseSemaphore()` NULL-`ThisTask` early return leaves that reference in place. A later ordinary shared acquisition/release pair increments then decrements the counters but preserves the pre-init reference, so an exclusive obtain remains blocked. The only maintained PREINITLIB registration is `Exec_X86PreInit()`, which registers the shutdown callback and makes no semaphore attempt; no selected in-tree PREINITLIB caller establishes reachability. The public API documentation does not state a task-context restriction, so EK9152 remains an external/future PREINITLIB contract issue, not a current default boot-path claim. No semaphore operation or startup was run; source-only.


EK8962 AArch64 Shell size-trigger refinement (2026-10-26; existing finding retained; no new ID or LOC credit): rechecked the complete selected chain from `workbench/c/shellcommands/Stack.c:43-84` through `Shell.c:514-555`, `rom/dos/runcommand.c:127-168`, and the AArch64 override (`arch/aarch64-all/exec/newstackswap.c:24-68`). `Stack` rounds a requested byte count to `sizeof(IPTR)` units (`dosextens.h:266-268`), while `RunCommand` sets `stk_Pointer = stack + stacksize` without ABI realignment; the AArch64 NewStackSwap installs it directly and calls `Enable()` before entering the command. For example, `Stack 2049` becomes 2056 bytes on LP64, an 8-mod-16 extent. AArch64's stack alignment constant is 16 (`arch/aarch64-all/include/aros/cpu.h:34-35`), and the AArch64 boot manifest selects `kernel-shell` (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:127-128`). This is an ordinary selected Shell trigger for existing EK8962, not a new issue. The RISC-V LP64 override likewise installs an unadjusted pointer and documents the psABI's 16-byte alignment requirement; its selected pthread custom-stack route is already covered by EK8962. No stack switch, build or command was run; source-only.

EK8962 AArch64 Shell clamp correction (2026-10-27): the 2026-10-26 `Stack 2049` example above is not a trigger because `RunCommand()` clamps its 2,056-byte extent to AArch64's 40,960-byte `AROS_STACKSIZE`, which is aligned. A valid selected Shell example is `Stack 40961`: the command rounds this to 40,968 bytes on LP64, which exceeds the clamp and leaves an 8-mod-16 top from the 16-byte-aligned allocation base. EK8962 remains confirmed by the accepted custom-pthread-stack paths on multiple architectures; this correction only replaces the smaller Shell example. No stack switch or command was run.

ARM/ARMeb NewStackSwap full-body and custom-stack alignment pass (EK8962 evidence strengthened; 2026-10-26; no new finding): read both complete 110-line architecture implementations (72 `cloc 2.06` C lines each) and confirmed they are byte-identical. Traced `pthread_attr_setstack()`'s positive-size acceptance through `pthread_create()`'s `stk_Upper = base + size` into the selected ARM-family stack swap. With a 16-byte-aligned base and size 40,961 (`PTHREAD_STACK_MIN + 1`), the upper bound is 1 modulo 16; the implementation's four 32-bit pushes subtract 16 bytes, preserving the misalignment at its `Enable()` and entry calls. Both ARM and ARMeb CPU headers set `AROS_STACKALIGN` to 16. Updated the two architecture rows from body-inspected/caller-pending to full-body read with the selected custom-stack caller traced; wider public callers and target build/runtime behavior remain open. No stack swap, build, or runtime operation was performed; source-only.


ARM-native MMIO accessor header and platform caller pass (2026-10-26; no new EK): read all 48 physical lines / 36 `cloc 2.06` C/header code lines of `arch/arm-native/kernel/io.h`. `platform_bcm2708.c` is the only selected translation unit that includes this header; its direct accessor census contains 17 `rd32le` and 25 `wr32le` uses, with no selected big-endian, 16-bit, or byte accessor use. Matched those sites to the BCM2835/BCM2836 register definitions, their four-byte alignment, and `ARMI_PeripheralBase`/boot-tag selection (`platform_bcm2708.c:30,34-37,654-705`; `hardware/bcm2708.h`; `hardware/pl011uart.h`). The build manifest selects this implementation for both `raspi-arm` and `raspi-armeb`; LE conversion is therefore intentional for the little-endian peripheral register interface on both CPU modes. The addresses remain 32-bit in this ARM32 target and are derived from the selected 32-bit peripheral physical base. No accessor width, alignment or endian mismatch established. Crediting this full header advances the latest Exec/Kernel represented checkpoint from 1,163/1,661 to **1,164/1,661 paths (70.1%)**, and from 236,224/364,673 to **236,260/364,673 C/header code lines (64.8%)**. No hardware access or build was run; source-only.

ARM processor frequency mailbox caller contract pass (EK9879 added; 2026-10-26): reread the full selected `processor_frequency.c` body and traced the only frequency-query route from `ARM_AnswerTag`/`GCIT_ProcessorSpeed` through maintained direct callers. Shell-command FullJumpVec synchronization recheck (EK9873 retained; no new ID or LOC credit; 2026-10-26): searched the complete pinned tree for `__AROS_USE_FULLJMP`; only the m68k and PowerPC CPU headers define it. The selected RISC-V64 and AArch64 CPU headers nevertheless define `FullJumpVec` and `__AROS_SET_FULLJMP()` as instruction-writing trampolines, and the RISC-V header explicitly requires a subsequent instruction-cache flush (`arch/riscv64-all/include/aros/cpu.h:80-98`; `arch/aarch64-all/include/aros/cpu.h:85-102`). `shellcommands_init()` performs the write at `workbench/c/shellcommands/shellcommands_init.c:71` but guards `CacheClearE(..., CACRF_ClearI | CACRF_ClearD)` with the absent macro (`:72-74`). The selected RISC-V OpenSBI provider sends a remote instruction fence for `CACRF_ClearI` (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/exec/cpu_init.c:39-54,196-205`); AArch64's selected `CacheClearE` reaches the kernel's cache-clear syscall (`arch/aarch64-native/exec/cachecleare.c:18-33`; `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/syscall.c:151-157`). No selected architecture definition or compiler option restores the guard, confirming EK9873's omitted post-write synchronization. No command, boot or cache operation was run; source-only.

CreateNewProc synthesized-entry ownership/error-path recheck (EK9874 retained; no new ID or LOC credit; 2026-10-26): followed `NP_Entry` without `NP_Seglist` through `CreateNewProc()` (`rom/dos/createnewproc.c:496-506,543-551`) and the generated segment allocator (`compiler/arossupport/createseglist.c:57-103`). If `CreateSegList(entry)` succeeds, `PRF_FREESEGLIST` is set, but the new segment is not stored in `process->pr_SegList` until after `segArray` allocation. A failed `segArray` allocation therefore reaches `enomem` with no segment reference; cleanup frees only `pr_SegList` when non-NULL (`createnewproc.c:593-650`). If task insertion fails after the segarray is published, cleanup frees the segarray but does not call `UnLoadSeg()` on element 3. The only nested-segment unload is in `DosEntry()` following successful task execution (`:943-952`). The selected pthread caller uses `CreateNewProcTags(NP_Entry, StarterFunc, ...)` and supplies no `NP_Seglist` (`compiler/pthread/pthread_create.c:263-278`), confirming an in-tree caller of the synthesized-entry path. On W^X targets the allocator uses `KrnAllocPages()` and documents `UnLoadSeg()` as the matching release path. No allocation/task-insertion failure or process creation was induced; source-only.

CLI synthesized-output failure-path ownership recheck (EK9875 retained; no new ID or LOC credit; 2026-10-26): followed `internal_CliInitAny()`'s stdout synthesis (`rom/dos/newcliproc.c:200-214`) to the subsequent stderr-open failure and `exit` path (`:216-239,334-341`). The new `cos` is held only in the local variable until both streams succeed and the function copies it into CLI/process state (`:238-245`); the failure branch neither closes it nor stores it in `pr_COS`. The selected `AROS_CLI` macro sees `IoErr() == me` and returns immediately (`compiler/include/dos/cliinit.h:161-165`), before its ordinary CLI stream cleanup. `DosEntry()` later closes only `pr_COS`/`pr_CES` according to flags, which remain the original `BNULL` process stream tags on the selected `SystemTagList()` path (`rom/dos/systemtaglist.c:402-415,443-446`; `rom/dos/createnewproc.c:436-438,920-934`). Thus this failed startup abandons the internally opened stdout handle/handler reference. No stream-open failure or shell startup was induced; source-only.

`CopyMemQuick()` selected SFS block-copy caller slice (2026-10-26; no new EK or LOC credit): followed the SFS `FS/deviceio.c`, `cachedio.c`, `nodes.c`, `btreenodes.c`, `transactions.c`, and `cachebuffers.c` copy sites through block geometry, cache-buffer allocation and block-offset construction. `changegeometry()` derives `bytes_sector` as `de_SizeBlock << 2` and `bytes_block` as that value times `de_SectorPerBlock` (`rom/filesys/SFS/FS/deviceio.c:268-276`), so the full-block copy lengths and shifted per-block spans are multiples of four. The node-container tail length subtracts `sizeof(struct fsNodeContainer)`, whose header fields are ULONG-sized and whose flexible array is `BLCKn`; the copied tail remains a multiple of four for the selected structure layout (`rom/filesys/SFS/FS/nodes.h:23-34`; `nodes.c:194`). The inspected copies use separate cache/block buffers; the overlapping-cache write path uses caller-provided `buffer` as source and switches to `CopyMem()` when that source is not ULONG-aligned (`cachedio.c:856-875`). This slice establishes no additional CopyMemQuick contract violation. It does not close the 133-reference repository census: in particular, ATA/SCSI `TD_GETGEOMETRY` have a 512-byte `CopyMemQuick()` branch to `io_Data` (`rom/devs/ata/ata.c:440-480`; `rom/devs/scsi/scsi.c:437-477`) whose arbitrary-buffer alignment contract and external callers remain unverified. No copy, disk request or filesystem operation was run; source-only.

`CopyMemQuick()` ATA/SCSI legacy geometry caller check (2026-10-27; no new EK): traced the two remaining geometry branches to the Exec vector contract. `rom/devs/ata/ata.c:478` and `rom/devs/scsi/scsi.c:475` copy 512 bytes from their unit's drive-identify buffer to caller-provided `io_Data` with `CopyMemQuick()` when `io_Length == 514`; neither callsite checks source/destination ULONG alignment. The public `TD_GETGEOMETRY` header documents a returned `DriveGeometry` (`compiler/include/devices/trackdisk.h:52`), and the checked-in callers located in partition, SFS, AFS and CDFS paths request `sizeof(struct DriveGeometry)`; no in-tree caller of the 514-byte branch was found. Thus the callsite is a potential violation for an external client supplying an unaligned destination, but this selected caller trace does not establish that trigger or a selected alignment-sensitive target, so no finding is promoted. This closes only these two source branches; Exec's 133-reference direct-call census and external caller contracts remain open. No request or copy was run; source-only.

EK71 selected resolver lifecycle and multi-frame dispatch recheck (2026-10-27; retained, no new ID or LOC credit): traced the saved callback through `KrnPrintBacktrace()`'s per-frame call loop (`rom/kernel/printbacktrace.c:110-117`) and checked the direct selected registration/removal paths again. `debug.library` registers `Debug_SymResolver` with its base (`rom/debug/debug_init.c:57-58`) and is configured `noexpunge` (`rom/debug/debug.conf:4`); the selected i386 hook attempts to register a different callback and later unregisters only that callback (`arch/i386-all/debug/debug_platform.c:55-70`), so no checked-in path unregisters the active generic resolver during a print. `CopyMemQuick()` sound datatype caller slice (2026-10-27; no new EK or LOC credit): traced the two selected `workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/dispatch.c` calls at `:3369` and `:3706` against the Exec vector preconditions in `rom/exec/copymemquick.c:24-43`. The M8S playback conversion path checks sample pointer, destination pointer and byte count for four-byte alignment and falls back to `CopyMem()` otherwise; the DMA output-buffer allocation comes from `AllocVec(..., MEMF_CHIP)` or the original chip sample is used as the source, and the playback destination is the separately allocated buffer. The next-buffer path similarly checks the sample pointer, destination pointer and computed transfer length before choosing `CopyMemQuick()`, with `dst` pointing into the AHI output buffer and `id->Sample` as the source. The checked quick-copy branches therefore satisfy the alignment and size contract; the two source/destination roles are distinct in these paths. No new candidate or body/LOC credit. This closes only the sound datatype slice of the 133-reference repository-wide census; unrelated callers, external API inputs and runtime behavior remain open. No playback was run; source-only.

`CopyMemQuick()` ReadArgs multiple-argument vector slice (2026-10-27; no new EK or LOC credit): traced all three `rom/dos/readargs.c` calls at `:678,773,829` against `CopyMemQuick()`'s ULONG alignment, multiple-of-ULONG size and nonoverlap preconditions (`rom/exec/copymemquick.c:24-43`). Both old and replacement arrays are `STRPTR *` buffers allocated with `AllocVec()`; the replacement is allocated while the old vector remains live, and the old vector is freed only after copying, so the allocations do not overlap. Each copied length is `multnum * sizeof(char *)`; selected supported targets have pointer width at least ULONG and therefore a multiple-of-ULONG copy length. The empty-vector case copies zero bytes, which the API permits. No defect or body/LOC credit. This closes only the ReadArgs vector-resize slice of the 133-reference census; broader caller review remains open. No argument parsing or allocation failure was run; source-only.

`CopyMemQuick()` Dir pointer-table growth slice (2026-10-27; no new EK or LOC credit): rechecked `workbench/c/Dir.c:AddEntry()` at `:258-293` against the Exec copy contract. `entries` and `new_entries` are `char **` arrays returned by `AllocVec()`, and the new allocation is live before the old one is freed, so the source and destination are distinct allocations. The byte count is `sizeof(char *) * table->num`, aligned to ULONG on supported 32/64-bit targets. A zero-entry growth does not issue a copy. No defect established; no line credit because the body was previously inventoried. This closes only the Dir table-growth call in the 133-reference census. No directory enumeration or allocation failure was run; source-only.

Sashimi resource reference-count SMP recheck (EK844 expanded; 2026-10-27; no body/LOC credit): verified the ledger's noted open-count race against `OpenSashimiResource()`, `CloseSashimiResource()` and owner removal (`developer/debug/sashimi/sashimi.c:403-423,506-531`). `sr_Library.lib_OpenCnt` is UWORD and `struct Library` has a separate SMP spinlock field (`compiler/include/exec/libraries.h:54-61`); Open and Close perform ordinary increment/decrement under `Forbid()`, and the zero check/removal uses the same local-only exclusion. Exec explicitly documents `Forbid()` as CPU-local on ExecSMP (`rom/exec/forbid.c:55-60`). Two CPUs can therefore lose one of two concurrent increments; after one corresponding close, the owner can observe zero and free the resource while the other client still retains it. Added this second independent trigger to EK844 alongside the OpenResource lookup-to-reference gap; no new finding ID or LOC credit. No Sashimi instance or SMP interleaving was run; source-only.


Exec/kernel AddIntServer kernel-route and selected null-token caller recheck (2026-10-27; no new EK or LOC credit): reread the complete `rom/exec/addintserver.c` and paired `remintserver.c`, then checked the generic `KrnAddIRQHandler()` allocation/return contract and `KrnRemIRQHandler()` removal ordering. On the kernel IRQ route, `AddIntServer()` stores the opaque return in `Interrupt.is_Node.ln_Succ` but has no status result; the generic add helper can return NULL on unsupported IRQ or interrupt-node allocation failure, while the generic remover reads `h->in_nr` before testing `h` (`rom/kernel/addirqhandler.c:79-115`; `remirqhandler.c:52-55`). This is an API/caller revalidation only; no new path or LOC credit. No IRQ registration, allocation failure or removal was run; source-only.


PC IRQ shared-cursor race route-selection and concurrent-dispatch recheck (EK821 restored to report; 2026-10-27; no new path/LOC credit): re-read the selected `arch/all-pc/kernel/addirqhandler.c` walker and followed the shared `PlatformData.kb_LastIntr` storage (`kernel_arch.h:82`) through `ForeachNodeSafe()`'s `current` parameter (`compiler/include/exec/lists.h:203-209`). With `in = &pdata->kb_LastIntr`, each loop condition/body dereferences the same global cursor rather than a stack-local current-node pointer (`addirqhandler.c:116-132`). Traced dispatch from the selected PC `cpu_intr()` path (`cpu_intr.c:499-519`) and route selection through `ictl_enable_irq()` to `IOAPICInt_EnableIRQ()` (`ictl.c:20-44`; `acpi_ioapic.c:546-593`): when an IRQ has no `IntrMapping`, enabling it chooses `KrnGetCPUNumber()` as its destination. The PC override is selected in `arch/all-pc/kernel/mmakefile.src:20-37` for PC targets. Thus distinct unmapped IRQ lines first enabled on different CPUs can be routed to separate CPUs; overlapping walks overwrite the single shared cursor. A walker can then read a node from the other IRQ's chain, skip its own handlers, or observe the list sentinel as though it were an `IntrNode`. Restored EK821 because this source-level candidate was present in surviving coverage notes but had no current report/index entry; no runtime or hardware behavior was exercised. ExecSMP/IOAPIC route manifestation remains conditional.

ARM-native `Exec_ReschedTask()` scheduler-list helper caller census (2026-10-27; no new EK or LOC credit): traced every checked-in `krnSysCallReschedTask` call under the selected ARM-native override (`signal.c`, `newaddtask.c`, `remtask.c`, `service.c`) through `Exec_ReschedTask()` and its `tc_SpinLock`/source-list/target-list ordering (`arch/arm-native/exec/platform_init.c:129-214`). Signal releases the task lock before migration; NewAddTask marks new tasks TS_INVALID before enqueue; RemTask and ServiceTask call under Disable/Enable, with the ReschedTask helper preserving the prior IRQ/FIQ state. Signal's direct cross-CPU and FIQ/IPI calls enter the same raw IRQ+FIQ-masked routine. Under the held task lock, the helper removes only from the list selected from current state, changes `tc_State`, then enqueues in the target list before unlock; READY wakeups reject already-running/ready/terminal tasks. AArch64's selected migration path uses the same helper lock order, and its direct caller set does not establish a mismatched lock-held entry. No selected caller was found holding `tc_SpinLock` on entry; no separate double-enqueue or wrong-list transition established. This closes the ARM-native helper's direct caller set only; the broader platform scheduler/API and lock-order census remains open. No scheduling, signal or SMP interleaving was run; source-only.

EK8835 PC AP bootstrap-dispatch state correction (2026-10-27; existing finding refined; no new EK or LOC credit): reread the selected PC `RemTask()` → `KrnDispatch()` handoff and scheduler retry (`arch/all-pc/exec/exec_platform.h:17`; `rom/exec/remtask.c:82-90,143-164`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:166-183,308-342,352-405`). The AP's self-removal path marks the bootstrap task `TS_INVALID` before dispatch; `core_Dispatch()`'s no-eligible-ready fallback excludes only `TS_WAIT`, so it selects that invalid current task, skips READY/RUN launch, and retries after `core_Switch()` declines the invalid task. AmigaGuide RemPort/reply-port caller lifecycle recheck (no new EK; 2026-10-27): re-read the selected process worker startup, ARexx reply loop, shutdown drain, `SendRexxCommand()` callers, and Exec `Forbid()` contract (`workbench/classes/datatypes/amigaguide/process.c:217-242,321-390`; `util.c:734-790`; `amigaguideclass.c:275,1141-1144`; `rom/exec/forbid.c:58-60`). Teardown clears `ag_RexxPort`, removes the public port, drains replies already counted in `ag_RexxOutstanding`, then deletes the reply port. `SendRexxCommand()` snapshots `ag_RexxPort` before entering Forbid; on ExecSMP, Forbid is processor-local and cannot pin that pointer against a concurrent teardown. If a caller can overlap object cleanup, it may create/send a Rexx message with the freed reply port. The maintained callers are class methods; this pass found no selected in-tree concurrent method/cleanup path or API contract proving such overlap is supported. Kept this as an external caller/object-lifetime question rather than a finding. No message, port, or concurrent object lifecycle was run; source-only.

AddResource kernel.resource publication-window RISC-V startup recheck (2026-10-27; no new EK or source/LOC credit): followed `Kernel_Init()`'s `AddResource(KernelBase)` before platform INITLIB dispatch (`rom/kernel/kernel_init.c:122-138`) into the selected OpenSBI startup path. The RISC-V kernel parses/records other harts for a future per-hart table but explicitly leaves secondary harts parked and marks HSM bring-up TODO (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/platform_init.c:6-8,23-59`; `kernel_startup.c:773`). Thus the early AddResource publication followed by KernelBase/PageSize initialization does not expose a concurrent secondary-hart reader on this target. This closes that platform branch only; remaining architecture startup concurrency and external AddResource clients are still open. No boot or concurrent resource lookup was run. Source-only.


AddResource kernel.resource publication-window ARM startup pass (2026-10-27; no new EK or source/LOC credit): rechecked both ARM generations. ARM32 and AArch64 register `platform_PostInit` as INITLIB routines; their SMP paths pin the boot task and call `ARMI_Init` to wake secondary cores there (`arch/arm-native/kernel/platform_init.c:74-107,126`; `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/platform_init.c:75-107,124`). Generic `Kernel_Init()` publishes kernel.resource with `AddResource()` before it runs platform INITLIBs and returns the KernelBase pointer (`rom/kernel/kernel_init.c:128-140`). Thus neither selected ARM startup can race secondary-core startup with the earlier ResourceList insertion/KernelBase/PageSize setup. Together with the checked PC post-Exec SMP start and the OpenSBI RISC-V single-hart path, this closes the selected architecture startup-order branches for this publication window; external AddResource callers remain open. No boot or concurrent lookup was run. Source-only.


AddResource kernel.resource publication-window selected-SMP matrix (2026-10-27; existing candidate not promoted): reconciled all source-selected AROS SMP startup routes against generic `Kernel_Init()` ordering. PC AP startup is in the post-Exec platform stage (`arch/all-pc/kernel/platform_post.c:97-104,174-204`); ARM32/AArch64 start secondaries from `platform_PostInit` after the kernel INITLIB sequence reaches `AddResource` (`arch/arm-native/kernel/platform_init.c:74-107,126`; `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/platform_init.c:75-107,124`; `rom/kernel/kernel_init.c:128-140`). OpenSBI RISC-V leaves other harts parked (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_startup.c:773`), and a repository search of other architecture kernel startup/platform files found no additional `__AROSEXEC_SMP__` implementations. Therefore the `kernel.resource` list-publication versus KernelBase/PageSize initialization window has no selected concurrent secondary-core reader on the architectures reviewed. External or future callers that themselves AddResource a node named `kernel.resource` remain outside this startup-order conclusion. No boot or concurrent lookup was run; source-only.

AArch64 GIC400 payload-slot and selected IPI caller closure (2026-10-27; no new EK or body/LOC credit): re-traced `gic400_send_ipi()`/`gic400_handle_ipi()` against both selected GICv2 platform receivers and every `ARMI_SendIPI` caller in the AArch64 target (`arch/aarch64-native/kernel/gic400.c:74-120`; `platform_bcm2711.c:139,266`; `platform_bcm2712.c:252,384`; `kernel_ipi.c:132-138`; `schedulecpu.c:23-39`). The GIC slot's `is_Data` field is a single per-target/per-source value and can be overwritten while message bits are pending, but every selected caller passes `ipi_data == 0`; `handle_ipi()` processes only message flags and does not consume payload data (`kernel_ipi.c:273-314`). Generic kernel page allocator initialization/caller reconciliation (2026-10-27; EK639/EK9156 qualification retained; no new finding or LOC credit): re-read `rom/kernel/{allocpages,freepages,initmemory,statmemory,kernel_init}.c`, `rom/exec/addresource.c`, and the generic kernel source manifest. Generic `KrnAllocPages()` and `KrnInitMemory()` both return without acting when `kb_PageSize` is zero; generic `KrnStatMemory(KMS_PageSize)` reports zero in that state. `Kernel_Init()` publishes the resource via `AddResource()`, and `AddResource()` then stores that queried value in Exec's `PageSize`, replacing zero with `MEMCHUNK_TOTAL`; this fallback does not set the kernel's `kb_PageSize`. A C/assembly source search across `arch/` and `rom/` found no assignment to `kb_PageSize` (only its declaration, zero checks, and the hosted Unix 4096-byte fallback read). The Unix hosted startup separately obtains its page size through `krnGetPageSize()` and its `allocpages.c` override supplies 4096 if the kernel field is zero. Thus generic page allocation and `KrnInitMemory()` findings remain conditional on external or target initialization; Exec's pool-granularity fallback is not evidence that generic kernel page allocation is enabled. Existing production `KrnAllocPages()` call sites and target-manifest boundaries remain as previously recorded; excluded allocator-test calls do not establish maintained startup reachability. No MMU, allocator, build or runtime operation was performed; source-only.

Exec library-reference ownership cross-check for Other Drivers OD9952 (2026-10-27; no new EK or path/LOC credit): compared OpenLibrary/CloseLibrary's selected vector behavior (`rom/exec/openlibrary.c:83-103`; `closelibrary.c:66-80`) with process Exit and task-removal cleanup (`rom/dos/exit.c:78-94`; `rom/exec/remtask.c:99-175`). AArch64 CachePreDMA selected xHCI request-lifetime follow-up (2026-10-27; no new EK or LOC credit): confirmed `pcixhci` is selected in the AArch64 Raspberry Pi package (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:217`) and traced `xhciPrepareDMABuffer()`/`xhciQueuePayloadTRBs()` into async, periodic and isochronous queues (`rom/usb/pcixhci/xhci_schedule.c:47-99,327-363`; `xhci_async.c:141-220`; `xhci_periodic.c:85-135`; `xhci_isoch.c:80-130`). AArch64 CachePreDMA selected NVMe caller follow-up (2026-10-27; no new EK or LOC credit): the Raspberry Pi package selects `nvme` (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:217`). Traced the selected PRP/SGL builders (`rom/devs/nvme/nvme_prp.c:48-232`; `nvme_sgl.c:61-193`) through `nvme_io.c:95-160`, DMA segment tracking/release (`nvme_intern.h:245-286`), and queue submission/completion (`nvme_queue_io.c:35-154`). These builders use the physical address returned by `CachePreDMA()` through the PCI driver's CPU-to-PCI conversion, split data at returned contiguous-length/page boundaries, and retain original CPU addresses/lengths/directions for matching PostDMA at completion. PRP construction checks second-page alignment and PRP-list alignment; failure unwinds recorded DMA segments and temporary list storage. SGL failure paths free descriptor storage and the caller releases recorded segments before PRP fallback; no double-post is indicated because `nvme_dma_release()` resets the map count. The actual buffer origin and AArch64 PCI translation implementation remain beyond this caller trace, so no selected non-identity/discontiguous mapping or incorrect caller behavior is established. EK8902 remains open as an API/build-source gap; no NVMe device, DMA transfer or build was exercised; source-only.

AArch64 CachePostDMA partial-edge ownership finding restoration (EK8816; 2026-10-27; no path/LOC credit): rechecked the native 64-byte line loop and instruction semantics against the selected Raspberry Pi 5 NVMe request path. `CachePostDMA()` applies `dc civac` on device-to-memory completion; the NVMe read path accepts arbitrary `io_Data` alignment, uses PREREAD, retains exact segment pointers, and applies POSTREAD before signaling the requester. RP1 source explicitly documents noncoherent DMA. A dirty cache line shared with adjacent data can therefore write stale DMA-region bytes back over a read result. Restored EK8816 to the detailed Exec report and index; kept its concrete trigger conditional on a public request buffer sharing an edge line and an adjacent CPU write during DMA. No DMA or cache operation was run; source-only.

The repository-wide source search found no direct checked-in NVMe data-I/O opener, so caller-owned buffer layout and the concurrent adjacent write remain conditional. Re-read the cache syscall's outward 64-byte range rounding and `dc civac`, plus the RP1 non-coherent DMA comment. The index link existed but a fresh heading search showed the detailed EK8816 section was absent; restored the detailed section and verified its anchor resolves. PowerPC CachePostDMA invalidation caller/target audit (EK9890 added; 2026-10-27; no path/LOC credit): followed the CHRP and Sam440 Exec post-DMA overrides into shared `arch/ppc-all/exec/cachecleare.c` and then the selected kernel syscall handlers. `ppcnative` enables the standalone invalidation branch; the maintained CHRP Efika and Sam440 handlers implement `SC_INVALIDATED` with `dcbi`, whose architecture reference says modified cache contents are discarded. The range is rounded outward to 32-byte lines, while CachePreDMA only flushes before device ownership begins. Thus a client-written neighbor sharing a DMA edge line can be lost at completion. Recorded this separately from EK8816: PPC uses invalidate-with-discard, so the concrete consequence is loss of adjacent CPU writes, not stale bytes overwriting the device result. CHRP Pegasos is not a configured standalone target here; no such handler path is claimed for it. The exact partial-buffer/neighbor-write overlap remains a conditional public-client trigger; no checked-in caller trace establishes it as a normal workload. No DMA/cache operation was run. Source-only. References: [IBM `dcbi` instruction reference](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/aix/7.1.0?topic=set-dcbi-data-cache-block-invalidate-instruction), [PowerPC Architecture manual](https://bitsavers.org/components/ibm/powerpc/SR28-5124-00_PowerPC_Architecture_First_Edition_May93.pdf).

The one-byte wrap example is `IPTR_MAX - MUNGWALL_TOTAL_SIZE + 2` at either pointer width, so the underlying arithmetic defect is not 32-bit-specific. `CreateProc(ULONG stackSize)` to `CreateNewProc()` establishes a caller-supplied route on 32-bit builds (`rom/dos/createproc.c:88-109`; `rom/dos/createnewproc.c:241-263`); no near-limit in-tree caller was found. On 64-bit builds, the public vector accepts the near-limit value but this pass did not establish an in-tree caller route. Corrected EK30's report scope accordingly; no allocation was attempted.
Cross-architecture Supervisor wrapper caller census (EK560/EK9050 retained and scoped; 2026-10-27; no path/LOC credit): rechecked the selected PowerPC `Supervisor()` implementations against all direct C callers. Sam440 `Processor_Init` is invoked from INITLIB after `Kernel_Init` sets `MSR_PR`, so its `Supervisor(getpvr)` call starts in user mode and does not trigger EK560 (`arch/ppc-sam440/processor/processor_init.c:26`; `rom/exec/exec_init.c:270-279`; `arch/ppc-sam440/kernel/kernel_startup.c:575-655`). The apparent Sam440 ATA call is in a source file/build edge commented out (`arch/ppc-sam440/ata/mmakefile.src:7-17`). The only other direct C caller found in the source tree is the optional `supertest`; PPC CHRP has no direct C caller. Thus the unconditional PPC `UserState()` in the paired wrapper remains a real API contract defect for an already-supervisor caller but no ordinary selected in-tree caller establishing that mode was found. Other architecture callers use their selected implementations and are not evidence for the PPC-specific result. No privilege transition was run; source-only.

m68k emulator CreateMsgPort/DeleteMsgPort shadow-lifetime pass (EK9891 added and reconciled; 2026-10-27; no path/LOC credit): compared the generated Exec lifecycle wrappers with the shared shadow allocator/destructor. `CreateMsgPort()` registers and returns a 34-byte guest shadow; `DeleteMsgPort()` resolves and frees the native port but omits `shadow_destroy()`, leaving both the guest allocation and fixed shadow-table entry live. Confirmed `shadow_destroy()` removes the entry and frees the guest block (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_shadow.c:101-107`), `M68KEMU_MAX_SHADOWS` is 256 (`m68kemu_intern.h:92-94`), and registration failure returns zero (`m68kemu_thunks.c:444-455`). This accumulates guest allocations and stale mappings until registry capacity is consumed. The constructor's failure to delete the native port after shadow registration fails is already covered under EK408; EK9891 is limited to the missing DeleteMsgPort shadow removal/free. Compared EK410's DeleteIORequest path, which removes but does not free its shadow, and EK419/EK9275's repeated borrowed-object shadow creation; those are distinct lifecycle/lookup paths. The emulator README describes CreateMsgPort/DeleteMsgPort as the device-I/O lifecycle (`rom/m68kemu/README.md:140-144`); the fake Exec base registers both generated vectors (`m68kemu_run.c:43-49`). The module is an explicit optional target (`mmakefile.src:14-17`). Existing source bodies were already inventoried; no path/LOC credit. No guest program or port lifecycle was run; source-only.

# AArch64 Raspberry Pi boot console cross-CPU caller follow-up (EK9897; 2026-10-27): traced public `KrnBug()` through `krnBug()`/`__vcformat()` into `krnPutC()` (`rom/kernel/bug.c:21-63`; `rom/kernel/_bug.c:18-20`; `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/kernel_debug.c:20-30`). Neither the public nor internal formatter serializes output; the early boot writes protected by the secondary-start handshake are only one caller window and do not serialize later concurrent `KrnBug()` calls before FBGfx sends the detach sentinel. Traced the callback to bootloader `fb_Putc()` and its global cursor/mirror/scroll mutations (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/boot.c:718-722`; `bc/screen_fb.c:135-213`). Added EK9897, scoped to corrupted/lost console output from concurrent diagnostics; no wider memory corruption claim. No boot or concurrent output was run. Source-only.

AArch64 FBGfx framebuffer-handoff recheck (EK9897 expanded; 2026-10-30): traced the selected `RawPutChar(0x03)` detach in `initFBGfxHW()` through `RawPutChar()`/`KrnPutChar()` to `krnPutC()` clearing `ARMI_PutChar` (`arch/aarch64-raspi/hidd/fbgfx/fbgfx_support.c:26-50`; `rom/exec/rawputchar.c:45-53`; `rom/kernel/putchar.c:44-55`; `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/kernel_debug.c:20-30`). The FBGfx init path then calls `ClearBuffer()`, which `memset`s the same framebuffer (`fbgfx_support.c:71,130-133`). `krnPutC()` has no cross-CPU lock or in-flight callback drain, and the callback pointer is read before invocation; a concurrent diagnostic that already entered the callback can therefore draw while FBGfx clears the surface. Expanded EK9897 to include this takeover window, with the consequence limited to lost/garbled display output. No report LOC credit: these files already have full-body coverage. No initialization, debug output or concurrent callback was run; source-only.

m68k GadTools context-backed message shadow lifecycle recheck (EK9891 expanded; 2026-10-27; no path/LOC credit): traced the normal context-gadget branch of `GT_FilterIMsg()` to its embedded reusable `contextgad->gtmsg`, and `GT_PostFilterIMsg()`'s reply path that clears `gtmsg_used` rather than freeing that wrapper. The generated `GT_GetIMsg()` thunk calls `shadow_create_by_name()` for every non-NULL return; `shadow_create()` always allocates/registers a fresh guest block, with no native-pointer deduplication, while `GT_ReplyIMsg()` performs no shadow cleanup. Repeated ordinary get/reply cycles therefore retain guest blocks and consume the bounded table even when the native wrapper is reused; destroying the gadget context can also leave those mappings pointing at its freed embedded wrapper. m68k graphics blit-queue node thunk/layout pass (EK9432 expanded; 2026-10-27; partial generated-file review, no path/LOC credit): traced `QBlit()`/`QBSBlit()`'s direct guest-node pointer to the native queue insertion branches. EK8845 ChildOrphan versus child-cleanup race recheck and report restoration (2026-10-27; no new path/LOC credit): re-read `ChildOrphan()`, `Exec_CleanupETask()`, `Remove()`, and all checked-in C call sites. Cleanup caches the parent before taking the child lock, then unconditionally removes the child node under the cached parent lock; `ChildOrphan(tid)` can clear the parent and remove that node under the same parent lock, while `ChildOrphan(0)` clears parent fields and resets the list head without unlinking nodes. `Remove()` leaves neighbor links intact. A concurrent cleanup can therefore repeat removal after detachment; visible child-list damage requires subsequent mutations through stale neighbor links, and stale former-parent notification is conditional. No maintained C caller was found; the public vector and generated emulator thunk remain exposed. Restored a detailed EK8845 section with ExecSMP/external-caller conditions and excluded any reproduced/runtime claim. The emulator thunk's discarded return remains separate EK813. No caller or schedule was run; source-only.

m68k baseline `CopyMem()` full body and public contract pass (candidate EK9903 opened then withdrawn; 2026-10-27): read all 51 assembly lines and reconciled the selected `CopyMem` symbol against the m68k Exec manifest, the architecture C stub, and the generic public contract. No source defect or in-tree caller trigger was established. EK9903 final disposition after nested-loop recheck (2026-10-27): the two DBF instructions share a loop body. Therefore the later large-unaligned-truncation claim was also false. EK9903 has been removed from the active report/index and no CopyMem defect is claimed from this body. AArch64 sparse CPU-ID processor.resource startup closure (EK541 strengthened; 2026-10-28): verified that BCM27xx skips a CPU after missing PSCI conduit or nonzero `CPU_ON`, then continues its CPU-ID loop; a later successful CPU retains its slot in TLS and registration, so IDs `{0,2}` produce `KrnGetCPUCount()==2` (`platform_bcm27xx.c:362-405`; `kernel_cpu.c:323-339`; `getcpucount.c:11-25`). The packaged processor.resource uses the ARM-native processor implementation (`arch/arm-native/processor/mmakefile.src:5-20`, selected by Raspberry Pi boot package `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:216`); its `Processor_Init()` iterates `i=0..cpucount-1`, creates a probe task pinned to mask bit 1, and waits for that task's signal (`processor_init.c:28-91,148`). `KrnGetCPUMask()` sets the requested bit without checking online membership; AArch64 scheduler affinity matching requires the current CPU's actual bit (`getcpumask.c:11-26`; `kernel_scheduler.c:40-48,115-120,247-251`), so no CPU can execute the CPU-1-only probe under `{0,2}` and the resource init wait cannot complete. This strengthens the existing conditional EK541 report; no boot/PSCI outcome was induced. Also corrected the old signal-hook claim as described above. The latest reproducible represented-body checkpoint remains 1,207/1,678 tracked paths (71.9%) and 237,152/365,058 C/header code lines (65.0%); this follow-up adds caller analysis but no body-line credit. Source-only.

Reset-callback SIGF_SINGLE fallback false-wake candidate recheck (2026-10-28; no new EK): traced signal-pool initialization and all direct `Signal(..., SIGF_SINGLE)` source occurrences against `Exec_DoResetCallbacks()`'s `AllocSignal()` failure branch. New tasks initialize `tc_SigAlloc` from `SysBase->TaskSigAlloc == 0xFFFF`, reserving bits 0-15, including SIGF_SINGLE; `AllocSignal(-1)` only allocates an unset bit, and `CreateMsgPort()` uses that allocator, so an ordinary message-port notification cannot alias the fallback bit. The caller-tree search found SIGF_SINGLE producers targeted at their own protocol peers, but no checked in-tree path that independently targets a task executing ShutdownA/ColdReboot during callback wait. Therefore the ordinary selected message-port collision suspicion is withdrawn; arbitrary external `Signal()` to the shutdown task remains a possible API-level interference but is not promoted without a concrete selected producer. No reset, signal-pool exhaustion or shutdown was run; source-only.

Each entry patches the caller return address and pre-vfork stack pointer into the expected buffer slots; each longjmp restores the saved callee state and passes the supplied result in the ABI return register. On ARM/ARM big-endian, the soft-float branch skips VFP restore only when the runtime reports no FPU; PPC and RISC-V offsets match their local setjmp layouts. m68kemu library first-open concurrency and DOS-reference cleanup pass (EK9914 detail restored after recheck; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-10-29): traced `M68KEmu_Open()` and `M68KEmu_Expunge()` through Exec `OpenLibrary()`, the generated standard library Open vector, ExecSMP `Forbid()` semantics, and the two checked-in hunk-module callers in DOS `RunCommand()` and process startup. The library-list read lock is released before the Open vector runs; OPENLIB callbacks precede the generated open-count increment and have no shared serialization. Two simultaneous first opens can each acquire DOS, overwrite the shared `dosBase` with the same library pointer, and leave one reference unbalanced when expunge closes it once. `dos.library` is `noexpunge`, so no unload blockage is claimed. The m68kemu target is optional; the trigger requires an explicitly included target, ExecSMP and concurrent hunk runs. ExecSMP per-task affinity-allocation failure recheck (EK8820 restored to detailed report and indexes, 2026-10-28; no path/LOC credit): reread `Exec_InitETask()` allocation, parent-mask copy, no-parent creator-CPU branch, selected ARM32/AArch64 and PC `KrnAllocCPUMask()`/`KrnGetCPUMask()`/`KrnCPUInMask()` behavior, and `NewAddTask()` failure handling. ARM32/AArch64 schedulers interpret NULL as unrestricted; PC/APIC interprets NULL as CPU 0 only. The parent-inheritance and creator-CPU placement contracts are therefore lost on the affected paths. m68kemu RawDoFmt pointer-width and VFWritef argument-layout continuation (EK9206 expanded; EK10164 added; 2026-10-28; no path/LOC credit): matched `%p`/`%P` in `m68k_to_native_fmt_stream()` against native RawDoFmt, which sets these conversions to IPTR width; the converter writes only four bytes and advances four, so a following packed argument is consumed as part of the pointer and subsequent offsets diverge. m68kemu pool-thunk semantic comparison (documented limitation; no EK added; 2026-10-28): compared the manual `CreatePool`/`AllocPooled`/`FreePooled`/`DeletePool` wrappers (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks.c:386-413`) against native Exec's all-at-once pool release (`rom/exec/createpool.c:35-66`; `rom/exec/deletepool.c:57-110`). EK9405 FASTREMAP allocation-failure qualification and report restoration (2026-10-28; no body/LOC credit): re-read the selected `mmuprotectregion()` path, the `KrnSetProtection`/`KrnMapGlobal` wrappers, `map_region2()` and `alloc_descriptor()`. Both protection operations can hide failure (`KrnSetProtection` returns void; FASTREMAP discards `KrnMapGlobal`'s BOOL), and `map_region2()` can stop at a missing page-table level after already writing earlier page descriptors, with no rollback. Refined EK9405: the boot-visible consequence requires a page-table allocation failure during the range updates; if initial invalidation fully creates all tables for the range, the same-range replacement normally needs no further table allocation, so a second-call-only failure is not asserted. Under allocation failure, invalidation and/or replacement may be partial and the helper proceeds as if complete; the newly allocated Fast buffer is not released on that path. FASTREMAP is enabled in the selected m68k Amiga source, while actual MMU setup remains gated by the boot option/A3000 detection. Replaced the report's summary-only EK9405 section with detailed trigger, partial-map consequence, configuration and confidence. No allocation failure or boot was induced; source-only.

EK9412 replacement insertion failure and DOS caller contract recheck (2026-10-28; no body/LOC credit): reread the two replacement constructors, their caller ordering and DOS `MakeDosEntry`/`AddDosEntry` contracts. `MakeDosEntry()` can return NULL when node/name allocation fails; `InterceptorProcess()` ignores both constructor results after removing the original node(s), then records the volume and begins servicing only the interceptor port. The device constructor additionally ignores `AddDosEntry()`'s false return: DOS rejects duplicate non-volume names, and the DOS-list lock protecting removal is released before this reinsert. The helper therefore reports success despite a failed device publication. Expanded EK9412 to cover both allocation failure and the conditional remove/reinsert name collision, with consequence limited to missing DOS aliases while interception proceeds. No allocation failure or concurrent DOS-list mutation was induced; source-only.

EK9413 DOS-list pointer lifetime and selected reload/unmount recheck (2026-10-28; no body/LOC credit): traced `FindVolumes()`'s handler-port/name snapshot through unlocked `ProbeNativeVolumes()`, `ProbeKeyFile()`'s packet to the saved port, and `AddNativeVolume()`'s subsequent BSTR read. Confirmed both `security_server.c` callers: initial startup and consistency-signal reload. DOS documents that `NextDosEntry()` traversal requires the list lock; `FreeDosEntry()` frees the BSTR and node, and selected RAM filesystem deletion removes/frees its volume node. Thus a concurrent removal after enumeration can invalidate the stored name and, if handler teardown completes, the saved port before probe use. Scoped EK9413 to this concurrent unmount window and left exact handler/task shutdown behavior filesystem-dependent. No scan, unmount or reload was run; source-only.

Historical EK9265 trace, superseded by the 2026-11-01 duplicate consolidation into EK9234 (2026-10-28; no path/LOC credit): followed the `bootiso-sam440-ppc` dependency, copied `boot/menu.lst`, parsed `default 0`, and the selected `testboot_aros()` loop. The default AROS entry loads the kernel plus 57 modules. Parthenope starts `ptr_ro` at `0x00800000`, advances it for each aligned read-only ELF section, and publishes the end as `KRN_KernelHighest`; therefore the threshold corresponds to at least 8 MiB of aggregate read-only section placement after the base, subject to per-section alignment. No checked-in build artifact supplies the default aggregate size, so the threshold remains conditional and default-image reachability unverified. At/above `0x01000000`, Sam440 rounds the cursor, underflows or zeroes the `0x01000000 - memLowest` size, and the kernel allocator writes a wrapped first chunk. Traced that state through resident-array allocation and `PrepareExecBase`, then into `AddMemList()` at `0x01000000`, which publishes the overlapping remainder as available Fast RAM without checking prior allocations. Restored the then-separate EK9265 detail with these callers; this candidate was subsequently merged into EK9234 as a duplicate of the same cursor threshold and startup arithmetic. No ISO, boot, or allocation was run; source-only.

EK8962 AArch64 NewStackSwap body/caller and trigger reconciliation (2026-10-29; existing finding strengthened; no path/LOC credit): reread all 100 physical lines / 61 `cloc 2.06` C lines of `arch/aarch64-all/exec/newstackswap.c` and reconciled the selected AArch64 Exec manifest, `Enable`/`Disable` vector stubs, DOS `RunCommand`, `Stack`, pthread and generated m68kemu thunk. Confirmed that AArch64 directly installs `stk_Pointer`; a valid aligned custom base plus `PTHREAD_STACK_MIN + 1` bytes is accepted and leaves the pointer one byte off the 16-byte AArch64 stack requirement. The guest thunk can forward NULL `StackSwapArgs`, but the fallback reads from the current stack's lower bound and the unused registers do not establish a wrong-result case for a zero-argument target. Corrected the historical small Shell example: `Stack 2049` is clamped by `RunCommand()` to 40,960 bytes and is aligned; `Stack 40961` rounds to 40,968 bytes (`sizeof(IPTR)` units), exceeds the clamp, and produces an 8-mod-16 top from an aligned allocation base. The existing 2026-10-27 correction already identified this larger example; this pass aligns the detailed EK8962 section with it and withdraws the conflicting 2026-10-26 example. The other supported `NewStackSwap` families preserve the custom top's misaligned remainder across their fixed argument/frame spans (i386, PPC, ARM/ARMeb, m68k, RV32/RV64); x86-64 explicitly rounds its pointer and hosted Unix uses `makecontext`, so those are excluded. No stack switch, command, guest call or target build was run; source-only.

EK8962 report restoration and direct-switch implementation recheck (2026-10-29; no path/LOC credit): restored the detailed finding after comparing the selected AArch64 implementation with i386, ARM, PPC, RISC-V and x86-64 implementations and the m68k assembly pair. The i386 pushes eight words, ARM pushes four, and PPC's copied frame span is alignment-multiple; these preserve a misaligned top's remainder. AArch64 and RISC-V directly set SP, m68k `StackSwap` installs the pointer verbatim, while x86-64 explicitly rounds down. m68k bus-error zero-page descriptor setup and caller pass (EK10190 added; no path/LOC credit; 2026-10-29): read all 235 physical lines / 174 `cloc 2.06` Assembly code lines of `arch/m68k-all/kernel/buserror.S` and traced its 040/060 address-4 recovery through `arch/m68k-all/kernel/mmu.c` and the selected Amiga MMU resident (`arch/m68k-amiga/boot/mmu.c`). The 040/060 recovery reads the zero-page descriptor pointer from VBR slot 253 and writes through it (`buserror.S:63-68`); `enable_mmu040()` stores the pointer unconditionally and installs this handler (`mmu.c:218-264,289-298`). `map_region2()` sets the pointer only after both lower descriptor allocations succeed (`mmu.c:389-405`), while allocation returns zero on memory/absolute-page allocation failure (`:54-67`) and mapping returns FALSE (`:391-399`). The selected `KrnSetProtection()` wrapper discards that result (`setprotection.c:15-31`), and Amiga boot continues through mapping calls to `enable_mmu()` (`boot/mmu.c:276-329`). Thus, on an MMU040/060 boot where all attempts to map page zero fail before the pointer is established, the handler still gets installed with a NULL saved pointer; a later long data read fault at address 4 takes the recovery branch and attempts a write through NULL, causing a secondary fault instead of the intended ExecBase recovery. This is a conditional allocation-failure startup defect; the normal successful page-zero mapping initializes the pointer, and the 68030 handler does not use slot 253. It is related to but has a distinct consumer/consequence from EK9405's FASTREMAP partial mapping and leaked-buffer path. No allocation failure, exception, boot, build or hardware was exercised; source-only.
x86-64 PC kernel internal header and ring-transition caller pass (EK10191 added; one previously uncredited selected header; 67 C/header code lines; 2026-10-29): read all 104 physical lines of `arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/kernel_intern.h`, reconciled its declarations with selected definitions/callers in x86-64 PC and all-PC kernel sources, and searched every use of its `KernBootPrivate` fields and `krnLeaveSupervisorRing()` macro. The three selected macro callers are boot startup, AP bootstrap, and the ACPI S5 transition (`kernel_startup.c:629`; `smp_exec.c:210`; `acpi_pm.c:84-89`). The macro pushes the supplied immediate as the IRETQ RFLAGS image (`kernel_intern.h:58-74`); `FLAGS_INTENABLED` is `0x3002`, so IF bit 9 is clear and IOPL bits 12-13 are both set. The ACPI S5 path immediately invokes `AcpiEnterSleepStatePrep()` after this transition despite the source comment requiring user mode with interrupts enabled. Added EK10191 for the selected ACPI path's IF mismatch, with the IOPL value recorded as an additional ring-transition effect. The normal BSP boot path next enters Exec `InitCode()`, whose caller comment says Exec enables interrupts, so no general boot-startup hang is claimed. AP bootstrap uses it before APIC setup, which has its own supervisor-state handling. No ACPI transition, interrupt state, or system was run. Crediting this selected header advances Exec/Kernel from 1,239/1,685 to **1,240/1,685 paths (73.6%)** and combined Graphics/Desktop, Exec/Kernel and Other Drivers from 4,175/4,813 to **4,176/4,813 paths (86.8%)**; C/header coverage advances from 1,414,576/1,899,293 to **1,414,643/1,899,293 code lines (74.5%)**. No project code changed; source-only.

PC alert-render nested-fault lock recheck (EK10193 detail restored; 2026-10-29; no body/path/LOC credit): re-read the PC debug lock, alert renderer, `krnPutC()` callbacks, and selected synchronous exception path (`kernel_debug.h:35-50`; `bug.c:18-44`; `_bug.c:31-80`; `_displayalert.c:72-112`; `x86_64-pc/kernel_debug.c:15-48`; `cpu_intr.c:413-470`). Corrected the earlier tentative note: the established route is a synchronous fault during a character-output callback, not an untraced nested interrupt caller. In PC ExecSMP, the alert renderer holds the shared lock; a fault in `con_Putc()`/framebuffer output reaches `cpu_intr.c`'s page-fault `bug()` before `cpu_Trap()`, and `krnBug()` spins trying to reacquire the same lock on that CPU. Restored EK10193 with the output fault retained as a conditional trigger; no ordinary workload is claimed to cause it. Header/source bodies were already credited, so coverage counts do not change. No alert, fault, interrupt, or build was run; source-only.


PC alert/debug lock nested-fault trace (EK10193 added; header body credited, 2026-10-29): re-read the complete 88-line / 58 `cloc 2.06` C/header-line `arch/all-pc/kernel/kernel_debug.h` and traced its lock wrappers through PC `bug.c`, `_bug.c`, `_displayalert.c`, architecture `krnPutC()`, and the common PC exception path. `DEBUG_USEATOMIC` is defined for ExecSMP and both selected PC architecture debug initializers set `_arosdebuglock = 1`. `krnDisplayAlert()` holds `KRNDEBUGLOCK` across rendering; each `krnPutC()` saves flags, disables interrupts for its console callback, then restores the prior flags. If that callback faults synchronously (for example, a page fault on the active output surface), selected `cpu_intr.c` logs the page-fault error code with `bug()` before calling `cpu_Trap()`. That wrapper disables local interrupts and enters `krnBug()`, whose `KRNDEBUGLOCK` spins on the bit still held by the interrupted alert frame. The interrupted frame cannot resume to clear it, so diagnostics and the alert/panic path stall on that CPU. Added EK10193, scoped to PC ExecSMP builds with atomic debug locking and a synchronous fault during alert rendering; high confidence in the lock sequence and consequence once triggered, low confidence that a maintained normal caller produces the secondary output fault. Distinct from EK9393's cross-CPU RawPutChar/cursor corruption. No fault, alert, or interrupt was run; source-only. PC SMP dispatch dequeue versus remote RemTask lifetime pass (EK10194 added; 2026-10-29; no file/LOC credit): re-read the full selected `arch/all-pc/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c` body and traced `core_Dispatch()` into PC `RemTask()` and `X86_HandleReschedTask()`. Dispatch removes an eligible task under `TaskReadySpinLock`, unlocks, and leaves `tc_State == TS_READY` through subsequent task-field reads; the x86-64 `RemTask()` syscall path sees that state, takes the ready lock, removes the already-detached node, marks it tombstoned, then synchronously cleans its ETask and frees its memory entries. This leaves a conditional remote TCB use-after-free in the dispatch continuation. Added EK10194, limited to PC ExecSMP with the 64-bit syscall-switch removal path. Compared with EK9451's wait/wakeup-before-switch-completion race and EK830's concurrent-remover cleanup race; the dequeue-to-dispatch reclamation path is distinct. The direct callers of `core_Dispatch`, `core_Switch`, `core_Schedule`, and `core_InitScheduleData` were checked in the selected PC CPU/IPI paths; remaining broader scheduler behavior and cross-architecture paths are open. No schedule, task removal, build or runtime test was run; source-only.

A trailing `%` leaves the data-stream prepass without an index or error; `InternalFormatString()`'s faulty-conversion fallback consumes the terminator, increments past it, and reads the format again on the next loop. For `%0$s`, unsigned `argpos - 1` underflows in the helper, index count remains zero, and the Locale parser later evaluates `indexStream[ULONG_MAX]` through `ARG(0)`. On 32-bit this is the preceding element; on 64-bit it is a huge positive out-of-bounds index. The source proves an out-of-bounds access on both widths, not a consistent negative index. The checked-in explicit-position unit example uses only positions 1 through 4, and repository search found no `%0$` format. Both remain conditional malformed-input candidates, not valid-format failures. Restored the exact conditions, caller chain and confidence limits in the report. No formatter call or malformed input was run; source-only.

Exec child-notification `Signal()` caller pass (EK277 retained; no new finding or body/LOC credit; 2026-10-29): re-read `Exec_CleanupETask()`'s notification branch and `Exec_InitETask()`'s task-message-port setup (`rom/exec/exec_util.c:171-177,302-337`). In ExecSMP, a notifying child is removed from its parent's child list and inserted into the parent's task-message queue under the parent-task and port spinlocks, then `Signal()` is called after releasing both locks. The message port's `mp_SigTask` is initialized to the owner task and `mp_SigBit` to `SIGB_CHILD`; a NULL signal task suppresses notification only, while `expunge` remains FALSE for the queued message. The non-SMP branch delegates queue insertion and signaling to `PutMsg()`. The cached-parent lifetime and reparenting race on the selected SMP cleanup path is already EK277 (`../AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek277`); this caller pass adds no independent root cause. Wider public `Signal()` callers and architecture-specific routing remain open. No task exit or interleaving was run; source-only.

The walk terminates only after hash-slot exhaustion, leaving successful earlier mappings in place; the PCI caller ignores failure and returns the requested address. No direct in-tree non-page-multiple Efika caller was established, so restored EK224 as conditional on an external/future caller and corrected the consequence to partial mapping/consumed PTE slots rather than claiming the entire hash table must be filled. EK348 BSS tracker capacity and bootstrap caller recovery (restored and width-qualified; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-10-29): traced the fixed `__bss_track[32768]`, PC `GetKernelSize()`/`LoadKernel()` calls, section append, and kernel-side terminator walk (`arch/all-pc/bootstrap/bootstrap.c:140,662,747`; `bootstrap/elfloader.c:45-50,73-103,573-590,612,735-737`; `rom/kernel/kernel_init.c:53-59`). The PC caller discards the loader's computed BSS size and provides no tracker capacity; each nonempty allocated `SHT_NOBITS` section appends a record, followed by an unchecked terminator. Record width is two loader-width `elf_uintptr_t` values, so the threshold is 2,048 sections for ELF64 and 4,096 for ELF32, with one additional slot needed for the terminator. Restored EK348 with the exact capacity condition and adjacent protected-table corruption consequence; no ELF image or boot was loaded. Source-only.

OpenSBI extended load-window arithmetic recheck (EK666 expanded; no new ID or body/LOC credit; 2026-10-29): traced `krnTimerTick()` from timer rearm through its elapsed-window gate and per-CPU scaling, then through both `krnTaskUsage()` walks and the current-task fold (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_timer.c:68-80,309-359`). The per-CPU and per-task fixed-point expressions left-shift an active-cycle numerator by 32 in `uint64_t`; each wraps when that numerator exceeds `UINT32_MAX` before division. `last_load_time` advances to `now` after a late sample rather than consuming one-second subwindows, so a prolonged gap in timer service can produce a window over `2^32` cycles and corrupt partial as well as full-scale values. At 100 MHz, the numerator threshold is about 42.95 seconds; this is conditional on a delayed timer service, which no checked-in caller or firmware behavior demonstrates at that duration. Expanded EK666 beyond the existing full-scale `uint32_t` narrowing case to include the guarded long-window overflow in both CPU and per-task load reporting. The selected frequency/timebase is `uint32_t`; no independent arithmetic issue was found in the task CPU-time nanosecond conversion after bounding its frequency remainder against that width. `kernel_cpu.c` and `kernel_timer.c` already have full-body credit; no path/LOC change. No timer delay, load query, task query or build was run; source-only.

Linux i386 signal-mask and dispatch caller closure (no new EK; 2026-10-29): re-read `arch/all-linux/kernel/cpu_i386.h` in full and traced `cpu_DispatchContext()` through the selected `SIGALRM`/`SIGIO` IRQ and trap signal setup, `sig_int_mask` construction, and `KrnCli()`/`KrnSti()`. The Linux i386 selection has `USE_SA_SIGINFO=0`; its one-argument handler reads the legacy `sigcontext` from the signal stack. The i386 legacy frame has a 32-bit `oldmask` plus a separately saved upper signal-mask word. The AROS macros write only `oldmask`; this does not change upper-word RT signal state when returning from the frame. However, the Unix kernel setup deliberately initializes the interrupt mask to all host signals then removes only handled trap signals, `SIGUSR1`, `SIGUSR2`, and `SIGINT`; the checked-in AROS Linux source has no realtime-signal registration/consumer requiring those upper bits to be unblocked. Thus the observed behavior is consistent with leaving unhandled host RT signals blocked, and no independent bug is asserted. `cloc 2.06` reports 106 C/C++ header code lines for this fully read file; crediting it advances Exec/Kernel from 1,273/1,685 to 1,274/1,685 paths and 247,653/365,733 to 247,759/365,733 code lines. This is source-only; no signal, host ABI, build, or runtime behavior was exercised.

i386-PC task-exception dispatch path recheck (EK10217 added; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-10-30): reread the selected pc-i386 cpu_Dispatch() and manifest, generic core_Schedule()/core_Dispatch(), SC_SCHEDULE and interrupt-exit paths, Exec SetExcept()/Signal()/Exception(), and maintained architecture dispatcher counterparts. m68kemu Locale DateStamp byte-order trace (EK9432 expanded; no new ID or body/LOC credit; 2026-10-30): traced generated `FormatDate()` and `ParseDate()` arguments through `THUNK_PTR()` to `m68k_to_host_or_shadow()` (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:6587-6595,6734-6742`; `m68kemu_thunks.h:34-38`; `m68kemu_intern.h:115-125`). For ordinary guest-owned storage with no exact registered shadow, the resolver returns the guest arena address; neither wrapper creates a `DateStamp` shadow. The 12-byte record has matching 32-bit field offsets in the checked-in guest/host map, but guest `LONG` byte order is big-endian while the supported x86-64/AArch64/RISC-V hosts are little-endian. Native `FormatDate()` reads the three fields (`workbench/libs/locale/formatdate.c:128-143`), and `ParseDate()` writes them (`parsedate.c:410-434`), without conversion. Expanded EK9432: formatting can interpret reversed day/minute/tick values; parsing can leave reversed fields in guest memory. This is separate from the callback bridge in EK9894/EK9208 and applies only to the optional explicitly built m68kemu little-endian host targets. No date API call, guest structure, or build was run; source-only.

m68k Locale `FormatString()` return-cursor finding detail restoration (EK9207; no new ID or body/LOC credit; 2026-10-30): re-read the generated wrapper, converter, and native return logic. `m68k_to_native_fmt_stream()` returns NULL for no conversions and otherwise allocates a separate stream; the thunk passes that pointer to native `FormatString()`, frees it immediately after return, then returns the result unchanged (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:6598-6608`; `m68kemu_thunks.c:255-282,303-322`). Native `InternalFormatString()` returns the input stream unchanged when no arguments were referenced, and otherwise returns a cursor computed inside that stream (`workbench/libs/locale/formatstring.c:560-575`). Therefore the no-conversion path returns NULL and the argument-bearing path returns a pointer into the just-freed temporary; neither returns a cursor into the guest's source argument stream. BOOPSI MakeClass nested shared-lock and duplicate-ID caller recheck (EK10218 retained/qualified; no path/LOC credit; 2026-10-30): traced `MakeClass()`'s `ClassListLock` shared acquisition into `FindClass()`'s nested shared acquisition, then through `InternalObtainSemaphore()` and `ReleaseSemaphore()` (`rom/intuition/makeclass.c:115-125,170-177`; `findclass.c:69-85`; `rom/exec/obtainsemaphoreshared.c:63-66`; `rom/exec/semaphores.c:96-113`; `rom/exec/releasesemaphore.c`). When the semaphore owner is NULL for shared mode, `InternalObtainSemaphore()` treats the nested acquisition as the same shared owner and increments `ss_NestCount`; nested release decrements it. Thus this call chain does not self-deadlock. The distinct EK10218 race remains: separate callers can both observe a public ID absent and later publish through unconditional `AddClass()`; the API documentation itself acknowledges duplicate IDs are unprotected/undefined. Repository-wide checked-in `MakeClass()`/`AddClass()` call-site review has not established an overlapping same-ID registration pair, so the report retains conditional external/future-caller reachability. No semaphore, class registration, scheduling interleaving or build was run; source-only.


Standard-pool `AllocPooled()` size-wrap free-link recheck (EK9124 detail restored; caller scope rechecked; no path/LOC credit; 2026-10-30): recomputed `IPTR_MAX - 15 + MEMPOOL_WORSTALIGN` for selected i386/x86-64 PC alignment (16), followed the wrapped zero through `stdAlloc()`'s zero-byte rounded chunk and first-bytes split, then through `InternalAllocPooled()`'s MemHeader write at the still-free chunk address. The write replaces `mc_Next`; a later free-list traversal can follow the MemHeader as a MemChunk. `notlsf` selects `ALLOCATOR_STD` on both PC targets; MungWall must be disabled because its subsequent size addition changes zero to nonzero. The public size is IPTR, but repository-wide checked-in direct `AllocPooled()` caller search found no near-limit request; occurrence remains conditional on external/future callers. Restored EK9124's complete report detail and added its missing master-index entry. No path/LOC credit: source bodies were already credited. EK9124 MungWall-enabled branch recheck (same finding expanded; 2026-11-01; no body/path/LOC credit): followed `IPTR_MAX - 15` through `InternalAllocPooled()` with MungWall enabled. The 16-byte `MEMPOOL_WORSTALIGN` addition wraps `memSize` to zero; `origSize` is captured at zero before MungWall overhead is added. A selected standard plain-pool puddle can satisfy that small nonzero overhead request. `MungWall_Build()` therefore lays down a zero-length allocation and post-wall; the subsequent `MemHeader *` prefix store overwrites the post-wall, and `AllocPooled()` returns a non-NULL pointer with no requested user payload. The paired free reports the damaged post-wall through `MungWall_Check()`; callers that access their requested extent can also exceed the backing allocation. This is a distinct consequence of the same overflow root cause from EK9124's MungWall-disabled free-list-link corruption. The route still requires the optional PC `notlsf` configuration, a plain pool and an external/future near-limit caller; no in-tree such request was found. No allocation/free or caller access was run; source-only.

TLSF 64-bit bucket-ceiling pooled-allocation trace (EK10221 added; 2026-10-30; no body/path/LOC credit): traced `MAX_FLI`/`REAL_FLI`, `MAPPING_SEARCH()` and unchecked `FIND_SUITABLE_BLOCK()` indexing (`rom/kernel/tlsf.c:35-49,111-125,166-209,489-513`), then followed managed pool creation through `AllocMemHeader()` callback inheritance (`rom/exec/createpool.c:134-143`; `rom/exec/memory.c:898-956`) and `AllocPooled()` direct `IPTR` forwarding (`rom/exec/allocpooled.c:32-33,72-83`). On 64-bit TLSF, requests rounded into the class at/above 2^37 bytes produce `fl == 31` although table indices end at 30; the mapping reaches that class beginning around 126 GiB because of TLSF search rounding. Added EK10221 for the conditional out-of-bounds bucket access, scoped to TLSF-backed managed pools; verified x86-64 PC (`kernel_startup.c:74,374`) and RISC-V64 OpenSBI (`kernel_startup.c:860-870`) default TLSF selection, with `notlsf` exclusions, and ran a source census of 503 `AllocPooled()`/`AllocVecPooled()` call expressions: no literal near-boundary size appeared in the search, but dynamic size expressions have not all been traced, so caller reachability remains open. The TLSF and pool bodies already have coverage credit, so no file/LOC totals change. No allocation, pool operation, build, or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only.


32-bit TLSF search-rounding overflow and managed-pool retry trace (EK10222 added; 2026-10-30; no body/path/LOC credit): re-read `tlsf_malloc()`/`MAPPING_SEARCH()` (`rom/kernel/tlsf.c:35-49,155-209,489-590`) against the 32-bit `IPTR` typedef (`compiler/include/exec/types.h:79-86`) and managed `CreatePool()`/`init_Pool()` setup (`rom/exec/createpool.c:129-143`; `tlsf.c:1419-1435`). For aligned request `0xfd000010`, `ROUNDUP()` preserves the value, but 32-bit `MAPPING_SEARCH()` adds `tmp=0x03ffffff`, wraps `tr` to `0x0100000f`, derives `fl=18, sl=0`, then stores `size=0`. If the first bucket search misses, managed-pool autogrowth asks only for a small puddle; after adding it, the retry maps zero and the normal allocator path can return a zero-size block. Added EK10222 with the autogrow/free-block condition and `notlsf` target exclusions; i386-PC and ARM-native startup selectors were verified at `kernel_startup.c:175,320-322` and `:279-293` respectively. A 503-call source census found no literal near-limit request; dynamic sizes remain open. TLSF and pool bodies already have coverage credit; totals unchanged. No allocation, build, or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only.


TLSF bucket-mask signed-shift audit (EK10223 added; 2026-10-30; no body/path/LOC credit): re-read `FIND_SUITABLE_BLOCK()` at `rom/kernel/tlsf.c:188-209` and both call sites in `tlsf_malloc()` (`:508,542`). `~0` is an unsuffixed signed-int expression; its left shift is evaluated before the unsigned bitmap operation and before assignment to `IPTR`, so a negative signed value is shifted and the C behavior is undefined for ordinary bucket searches. Added EK10223 as a distinct language-level issue from EK10221/EK10222 size-mapping boundaries. Scope is TLSF-backed configurations; selected i386-PC, x86-64 PC and ARM-native default paths were checked (`arch/i386-pc/kernel/kernel_startup.c:175,320-321`; `arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/kernel_startup.c:74,374-375`; `arch/arm-native/kernel/kernel_startup.c:279-293`). Runtime impact remains compiler/optimization dependent; no build or allocator call was run. The source body was already credited, so counts do not change.


EK10222 negative-index boundary subcase recheck (2026-10-30; no ID or LOC credit): recomputed the 32-bit `MAPPING_SEARCH()` arithmetic for aligned `0xfc000010` (`tlsf.c:178-184`). The addition wraps `tr` to `0x0000000f`; `MS(tr)==3`, making the second-level right-shift count `-2` and then `fl==-3`, which would index before `slbitmap` if execution continues. Because the shift count is negative, execution is already undefined at this subcase; narrowed EK10222 to report the invalid arithmetic/index without claiming deterministic runtime behavior. This is distinct from its `0xfd000010` zero-size retry case. No build or allocation was run.

Detached-startup duplicated-stream failure trace (EK10224 added; 2026-10-30; no new file/LOC credit): traced `detach.o` startup handle duplication and child creation (`compiler/startup/detach.c:83-118`) through `DupLockFromFH()` failure (`rom/dos/duplockfromfh.c:49-57`), `OpenFromLock()` null/error returns (`rom/dos/openfromlock.c:51-80`), and `CreateNewProc()` NIL-stream contract and conditional argument injection (`rom/dos/createnewproc.c:79-83,334-352,516-523`).
