EK10224 OpenFromLock failure-ownership follow-through (2026-10-30; finding strengthened; no body/path/LOC credit): checked the public OpenFromLock contract and implementation (`rom/dos/openfromlock.c:26-28,51-80`) against detach's nested expression (`compiler/startup/detach.c:83-84`). On a null lock, no lock exists to release; but when `DupLockFromFH()` succeeds and `OpenFromLock()` then fails to allocate a FileHandle or its ACTION_FH_FROM_LOCK packet fails, the contract leaves the lock for the caller to free. The detach caller has not retained that intermediate value, establishing an additional conditional duplicated-lock leak in EK10224. Rechecked successful child creation: the successfully converted other stream is passed to the child and closed by the detach handshake, so removed the earlier unsupported claim that it leaks when its partner is NIL. EK689 remains the distinct CreateNewProc-failure leak. No packet failure or stream handoff was induced; source-only.

EK9463 low-memory-list head representation recheck (2026-10-30; finding retained; no new body/LOC credit): verified the exact list layout to resolve whether `AllocMem()` snapshots a stable sentinel or the first handler. `struct MinList` stores `mlh_Head` as its first-node pointer; `NEWLIST()` sets that field to the address of `mlh_Tail` only when empty (`compiler/include/exec/lists.h:35-40,96-105`). Thus `allocmem.c:108` copies the current first handler pointer when Diskfont is the head, and `checkMemHandlers()` later dereferences the saved pointer only after acquiring `LowMemSem` (`memory.c:1318-1339`). Diskfont expunge removes the embedded node under that semaphore and generated expunge then frees its base (`remmemhandler.c:46-52`; `writestart.c:1557-1587`); ExecSMP `Forbid()` does not serialize that cross-CPU interval. The previously stated conditional use-after-free trigger remains supported. The separate cursor-staleness case still requires a handler returning `MEM_TRY_AGAIN` while self-removing (EK8818); it is not required for the Diskfont head-snapshot case. No allocation or expunge was run.

OpenSBI boot-module instruction-fetch synchronization pass (EK10226 added; 2026-10-30; no body/LOC credit): reconciled the explicit `boot-opensbi-riscv64` package staging (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/boot/mmakefile.src:114-120,136-165`; its parent aggregate edge is commented) and traced section copy and relocation stores in `arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_elf.c:258-405` through the selected package caller (`kernel_startup.c:813-829`), `krnMMUSetPerms()` (`kernel_mmu.c:264-279`), resident discovery followed by `InitCode(RTF_SINGLETASK)`/`InitCode(RTF_COLDSTART)` (`kernel_startup.c:928,1044-1048`; `rom/exec/initcode.c:68-96`). The permission change executes `sfence.vma` only; the loader-to-initializer path contains no `fence.i` or SBI remote-fence call. The SBI CacheClearE/CacheClearU override is installed later during Exec initialization (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/exec/cpu_init.c:40-64,196-223`; `kernel_sbi.h:142-160`); `SetFunction()` does not call it on selected RISC-V because its cache-clear block is guarded by `__AROS_USE_FULLJMP` (`rom/exec/setfunction.c:101-108`). Startup runs `RTF_SINGLETASK` and `RTF_COLDSTART` resident initializers at `kernel_startup.c:1044-1048`, with no preceding package synchronization. Added EK10226 for RISC-V systems whose instruction fetch is not coherent with stores; coherent targets are unaffected. The RISC-V ISA source states FENCE.I is required to guarantee subsequent same-hart fetch visibility ([Zifencei specification](https://docs.riscv.org/reference/isa/unpriv/zifencei.html)). No package, cache, boot, or build was used; source-only. Existing full-body credit for `kernel_elf.c` stands.

EK9473 selected Moira callback-path correction (2026-10-30; existing C++ body/path/LOC credit): corrected the earlier unreachable-trigger conclusion. `MOIRA_EMULATE_ADDRESS_ERROR=false` makes `misaligned<C, Word>()` return false for the selected M68040/C68020 execution path, and `addrMask<C68020>()` preserves all 32 address bits for M68040. Thus a guest word access at `0xFFFFFFFF` reaches `AROSMoira::read16()`/`write16()`; `addr + 1` wraps to zero in the callback guard, then the code indexes beyond the 32 MiB arena. A long access starting at `0xFFFFFFFD` can reach the same address on its second word. Expanded EK9473 to cover the Moira callbacks along with inline `m68k_read32()`/`m68k_write32()`; retained one finding for the shared wrap-prone bounds pattern. The callback body was already credited, so totals do not change. No guest access or build was run; source-only.

Moira DIVS.W overflow flag finding correction (EK10227 retargeted; body/path/LOC credit unchanged; 2026-10-30): checked the earlier `INT32_MIN / -1` report claim against the Motorola M68000 Family Programmer's Reference Manual. The manual says DIVS overflow sets V and leaves operands unchanged, while N/Z are undefined; therefore Moira's unchanged dividend and V=1 on this case are not a correctness defect, even though they differ from the bundled Musashi special case. Withdrew that claim and rechecked the same selected helper for architectural flag behavior: its quotient-overflow branch sets V but fails to clear C, unlike its success and special-case branches. The manual specifies C always cleared. Retargeted EK10227 to this independently supported omission; a prior C=1 plus any overflowing signed-word quotient leaves C incorrectly set. The selected `execDivsMusashi()` has no later flag modification. No instruction or build was run; source-only. Reference: [NXP-hosted Motorola M68000 Family Programmer's Reference Manual, pp. 194-195](https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/reference-manual/M68000PM.pdf).

Moira selected DIVL 32-bit quotient-overflow and carry-flag manual cross-check (EK10227 expanded; EK10231 added; no body/LOC credit; 2026-10-30): compared the selected `divlsMusashi()`/`divluMusashi()` branches and `execDivlMusashi()` writeback with the Motorola M68000 Family Programmer's Reference Manual. Expanded EK10227: signed/unsigned word-division overflow and 64-bit-dividend signed/unsigned DIVL overflow set V but leave a previously set C unchanged, although C is specified as always cleared. Added EK10231 for the distinct signed 32-bit-dividend DIVSL.L case: `divlsMusashi<Word>()` does not range-check the quotient; `INT32_MIN / -1` yields +2,147,483,648, clears V and returns a pair that the caller writes, although the manual requires overflow with operands unchanged. This restores the earlier 32-bit-dividend candidate on architectural grounds; matching bundled Musashi behavior does not satisfy the Motorola instruction contract. The safe selected 64-bit DIVL overflow case remains EK10159. Source bodies were already fully credited. No emulator instruction or build was run. Reference: [NXP-hosted Motorola M68000 Family Programmer's Reference Manual, pp. 194-201](https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/reference-manual/M68000PM.pdf).

EK9914 m68kemu first-open concurrency recheck (2026-10-30; no path/LOC credit): re-traced the unsynchronized `dosBase` check/open/store and expunge close against Exec's shared library-list read lock, lock release before the Open vector, and generated open-count ordering. On ExecSMP, two CPUs can enter the Open hook after concurrent read-locked lookups because `Forbid()` is local to each CPU. Each first open can acquire a DOS reference before either publishes `dosBase`; the common expunge closes only the final shared pointer once. `dos.library` is `noexpunge`, so the demonstrated resource effect is one retained open reference only. Confirmed checked-in DOS `RunCommand()` and process-startup hunk paths, but no actual overlapping run. Kept scope to explicitly built optional m68kemu plus ExecSMP. Moira selected M68040 Bcc/DBcc branch-semantics slice (2026-10-30; no new EK or body/LOC credit): traced all selected condition registrations for Bcc byte/word/long and DBcc word forms (`MoiraInit_cpp.h:418-479,825-862`) through `execBcc()` and the C68020-selected `execDbcc()` path (`MoiraExec_cpp.h:874-929,2140-2310`); confirmed `m68kemu_moira.cpp` fixes the guest model to M68040 (`:317`). In this path, byte displacement 0 selects the word form and 0xff selects long only on the C68020+ registration; Bcc consumes the long extension only when taken and consumes the required extension word(s) on fall-through. DBcc leaves Dn unchanged when its condition is true; otherwise it branches according to the pre-decrement low word and decrements only that word, including zero wrapping to 0xffff and terminating. `misaligned<C,S>()` deliberately suppresses the 68000/68010 address-error check for selected C68020. Compared the selected condition/decrement/PC structure with the bundled Musashi handlers; no separate mismatch was established. Exact cycle behavior and 68000/68010 address-error/loop-mode paths remain outside this slice; Musashi was used only as an implementation cross-check, not semantic authority. Moira CLR/NEG/NEGX/NOT/TST selected M68040 unary-operation pass (EK10234 added; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-10-30): traced the selected opcode masks, data-alterable destinations and TST's M68020+ additions (`MoiraInit_cpp.h:746-758,1350-1367,1863-1870`) through `execClr()`, `execNegRg/Ea()`, `execTst()` and `logic()`/`addsub()` (`MoiraExec_cpp.h:1745-1870,4694-4748,5549-5583`; `MoiraALU_cpp.h:356-410,557-610`). Checked NEG/NEGX carry, overflow and sticky-Z behavior, NOT/TST X preservation, CLR's fixed N/Z/V/C, word/long An legality for TST, immediate and PC-relative TST registration, and memory writeback through precomputed EA/postincrement handling. The selected M68040 CLR takes the C68020 branch, whose `readOp()` reads the memory destination before zero writeback. Motorola's manual says only MC68000/68008 CLR performs that read; M68020/030/040 clear without it ([NXP-hosted manual, pp. 4-73–4-74](https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/reference-manual/M68000PRM.pdf)). Traced this selected discrepancy into `AROSMoira`: `CLR.W $DFF02A` calls `customRead16(0x02A)`, which advances beam state by two clocks, before `customWrite16()` applies the VPOSW write (`m68kemu_moira.cpp:43-85,143-166`). Added EK10234 for the resulting later-VHPOSR shift, limited to explicit m68kemu M68040 runs. The independent sentinel termination on a word read remains EK10229 and is not duplicated. Other checked unary flags and destination paths matched their defined contracts; no extra candidate established. No guest instruction, custom-register access, or build was run; source-only.

Moira selected M68040 RTE frame-format compatibility pass (EK10235 added; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-10-30): retraced `RTE` registration and the selected M68040-to-C68020-core dispatch, then audited every branch in `execRte()`'s format loop (`MoiraInit_cpp.h:1546-1552`; `MoiraExec_cpp.h:4969-5180`; `m68kemu_moira.cpp:317`). Moira selected M68040 master-mode interrupt stack transition pass (EK10236 added; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-10-30): traced `checkForIrq()`/`execInterrupt()` and the C68020-selected interrupt branch (`Moira.cpp:417-440`; `MoiraExceptions_cpp.h:490-565`), then followed `setSupervisorMode()` through the stack-bank helper (`Moira.cpp:528-560`). `setSupervisorMode(true)` preserves `reg.sr.m`; the interrupt branch pushes format 0, tests the still-set M bit, and pushes format 1 without switching to ISP or updating the live M bit. Compared with NXP M68040 User's Manual §8.2.9: a master-mode interrupt creates format 0 on MSP, clears M, creates format 1 on ISP with supervisor state and new IPL, and enters the handler with M clear ([official manual](https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/reference-manual/MC68040UM.pdf)). Added EK10236 for the selected core's incorrect stack/SR transition. `setIPL()` is declared as a Moira API (`Moira.h:693-697`), but no selected AROS bridge caller was found; thus current bridge reachability is unestablished and the candidate is conditional on a client driving IPL during master mode. No body/LOC credit because the implementation body was already credited; no interrupt or build was run; source-only.

M68040 RTE format inventory reconciliation (EK10235 expanded; 2026-10-30; no body/path/LOC credit): compared every selected `execRte<Core::C68020>()` dispatch case with M68040 User's Manual §§8.4.4–8.4.6 (`MoiraExec_cpp.h:5060-5180`). The parser consumes formats 0, 1, 2 and B; format 3 is the valid M68040 floating-point post-instruction frame and format 7 is its valid access-error frame, but both fall through to FORMAT_ERROR. The M68000 Family Programmer's Reference Manual identifies format B as the MC68020/MC68030 long bus-cycle frame (Figure B-12), not an M68040 frame; the selected M68040 parser therefore accepts a foreign format and consumes/restores its SR/PC instead of raising FORMAT_ERROR. The base MC68040 manual explicitly says it does not generate or recognize format 4, so no format-4 defect is claimed. The selected bridge has no producer for the mismatched frames: address-error emulation is disabled, memory callbacks suppress out-of-range errors, FPU handlers throw unsupported-instruction exceptions, and no bus-error producer was found (`MoiraConfig.h:44`; `m68kemu_moira.cpp:130-168,317`; `MoiraExecFPU_cpp.h:121-187`). Expanded EK10235 to cover both rejected valid frames and the incorrectly accepted foreign frame, retaining the guest-supplied/restored-frame qualification. No frame or instruction was run; source-only.

CMPA sign-extends word sources and compares full 32-bit An; CMPI consumes a byte/word/long immediate and uses no destination writeback; CMPM reads and postincrements source An before destination An, including sequential increments when both fields encode the same An. Verified byte An exclusion for CMP, word/long An and all-source classes for CMPA, and the C68010+ PC-relative CMPI encodings against the selected C68020 registration and the manual's stated minimum processor. Cross-checked flags, comparison direction, sign extension, postincrement forms and supported addressing classes against the Motorola M68000 Family Programmer's Reference Manual ([CMP pp. 4-75–4-76](https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/reference-manual/M68000PRM.pdf); CMPA pp. 4-77–4-78; CMPI pp. 4-79–4-80; CMPM pp. 4-81–4-82). The selected bridge disables address-error emulation, so partial register updates on faulting memory accesses are not claimed as selected behavior. No additional compare mismatch established. CMP/CMPA/CMPI/CMPM form coverage only; broader Moira dispatch, timing and exception matrices remain open. No instruction or build was run; source-only.

Expanded EK10233 to cover CMP2's incorrect C/Z flags in addition to CHK2's missed trap for byte/word An truncation. Then traced byte bounds in `readM()` through the selected `MOIRA_MIMIC_MUSASHI` branch: only PC-displacement/indexed modes bypass `SEXT<Byte>()`, even though `readM<Byte>()` returns an unsigned byte. Compared those PC-relative handlers with bundled Musashi's signed `m68ki_read_pcrel_8()` and `(int8)` memory reads, and checked NXP's CHK2/CMP2 signed bound semantics plus its PC-relative EA allowance. Added EK10239 for PC-relative byte operands `0x80,0x81` with D0=`0x80`: selected Moira reports C=1/Z=0 and can take CHK2 instead of expected C=0/Z=1 and in-range. This applies to PC-displacement and PC-indexed CHK2/CMP2.B. This is a semantic/caller-dispatch recheck only; no instruction, emulator, guest, or build was run.

The memory path computes the effective address, applies predecrement before the read and postincrement after it through shared `readOp()` (`MoiraDataflow_cpp.h:207-221`), then writes the same byte location without recomputing the address; the write helpers preserve byte width. Both forms set N/Z from the original low byte, clear V/C, leave X unchanged, and set bit 7 only in the destination result. No instruction, guest, or build was run; source-only.

Moira EK10232 custom-register effect recheck (2026-10-30; finding retained, no new ID or body/LOC credit): re-read the selected CAS/CAS2 registrations and failed-compare branches (`MoiraInit_cpp.h:684-699`; `MoiraExec_cpp.h:1433-1549`), then checked the bridge's custom-chip dispatch (`m68kemu_moira.cpp:125-168`) and emulation notes (`rom/m68kemu/INTERNALS.md:438-458`). `CUSTOM_BASE=0x00DFF000` and `CUSTOM_MASK=0x00FFF000` route `$DFF02A` to `customRead16(0x02A)`, whose default result is zero; a failed word CAS therefore has a definite compare mismatch for a nonzero compare register. The omitted `write16(0xDFF02A, 0)` would reach `customWrite16(0x02A, 0)`, which clears `beam_lof` and `beam_v` bit 8, while the handler only updates the compare register and never invokes the write callback. This confirms a bridge-visible state difference beyond unchanged ordinary RAM contents. EK10232 remains limited to the explicitly built m68kemu M68040 execution path; no normal ROM aggregate inclusion or runtime guest execution is claimed. No additional CAS/CAS2 candidate established by this focused recheck. Source-only.

<a id="pc-execsmp-invalid-stack-dispatch-list-membership-pass"></a>
## PC ExecSMP invalid-stack dispatch list-membership pass

EK10240 added (2026-10-30; no file/body/LOC credit): traced the selected x86-64 PC `core_Dispatch()` from Ready removal through `SET_THIS_TASK()`'s Running insertion, saved-stack rejection, Wait insertion, and `core_Switch()` recovery (`arch/all-pc/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:205-215,273-287,304-405`; `arch/all-pc/exec/exec_platform.h:295-304`). Confirmed that the same intrusive `tc_Node` is queued on Wait before its Running membership is removed. `Enqueue()` rewrites the node and destination neighbors without unlinking prior neighbors (`rom/exec/enqueue.c:87-97`); `Remove()` uses the node's current links without identifying a list (`rom/exec/remove.c:55-62`). The later remove/requeue therefore operates through the rewritten Wait links and does not repair Running's neighbor links. Compared the ARM32/AArch64 dispatch recovery: their `SET_THIS_TASK()` does not insert into TaskRunning, and their `core_Switch()` only removes/requeues a task when its state is `TS_RUN`, so this specific list-membership defect is not extended to those targets. PC ExecSMP task-list Enqueue caller census for EK10240 (2026-10-30; finding scope strengthened; no body/path/LOC credit): searched direct `TaskReady`, `TaskWait`, and `TaskSpinning` Enqueue sites in `rom/exec` and the selected PC kernel/Exec code, then inspected each active PC transition. `core_Switch()` removes the current node from Running before its Ready/Wait/Spinning insertion (`arch/all-pc/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:205-287`); `SetTaskPri()` removes Ready nodes before priority reordering (`rom/exec/settaskpri.c:104-112`); `NewAddTask()` sets `TS_ADDED` before `TaskLaunch()` performs its first scheduler-list insertion (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:238,327`; `TaskLaunch()` at `:25-43`). QuickPart EK9355 matching-node and free-space-layout qualification (2026-10-30; no new finding or body/LOC credit): reconstructed a concrete ordered case through the full container child-list lifecycle. During FindParts() table-order enumeration (:428-451), a later disjoint partition is inserted at the first child when the child is the earlier nonmatching partition (:330-335), so the loop breaks before reaching the trailing free node. AArch64 idle-task physical wake source reconciliation (no new EK; 2026-10-30): traced the selected Pi 4/5 interrupt sources into the already-reviewed `IdleTask()` return path. BCM2711 and BCM2712 each dispatch the per-core CNTP timer PPI 30; their tick handler marks the local TLS quantum/switch flags when the slice expires (`platform_bcm2711.c:127-149,183-200`; `platform_bcm2712.c:238-260,286-307`; common `bcm27xx_sched_tick()` at `platform_bcm27xx.c:115-130`). Their GIC handlers also dispatch SGIs to `gic400_handle_ipi()` (`platform_bcm2711.c:127-149`; `platform_bcm2712.c:238-260`); the sender writes the target slot before sending the SGI (`gic400.c:74-99`), and `handle_ipi()` sets both quantum and switch flags for `IPI_SCHEDULE` (`kernel_ipi.c:273-296`). Current-EL/SP_EL0 IRQ and FIQ vectors both use the task-context save path and call `core_ExitInterrupt()` before restore (`vectors.S:203-218,304-325`); that exit checks the switch flag and schedules (`rom/kernel/kernel_intr.c:30-51`). Thus the selected source-level timer and inter-processor wake paths both reach rescheduling while the AArch64 idle task remains at EL1t. This closes the physical-source caller gap for these Pi 4/5 paths but does not prove board/GIC delivery timing, timer hardware behavior, or other AArch64 SoC integrations. No interrupt, timer, WFI or build was run; source-only.

Moira selected M68040 BKPT exception-dispatch cross-check (no new EK or body/LOC credit; 2026-10-30): traced the C68020-core BKPT registration (`rom/m68kemu/Moira/Moira/MoiraInit_cpp.h:574-583`) through `execBkpt()` and the selected `MOIRA_MIMIC_MUSASHI=true` branch to `execException(ILLEGAL)` (`MoiraExec_cpp.h:1321-1337`; `MoiraConfig.h:84`). The selected bridge fixes the model to M68040 (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_moira.cpp:317`). NXP's M68000 Family Programmer's Reference Manual states that MC68040 BKPT takes an illegal-instruction exception regardless of breakpoint-acknowledge cycle termination (4-53; [official NXP manual](https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/reference-manual/M68000PRM.pdf)). For this model, the selected Illegal path uses vector 4 and stacks the current instruction address through the same format-0 mechanism; no exception-vector or saved-PC discrepancy was established. Bus-cycle acknowledgement and external debug-monitor effects are not represented by the selected software bridge and remain outside this disposition. No instruction, guest, emulator, or build was run; source-only.

Moira selected M68040 CALLM/RTM opcode-table exclusion cross-check (no new EK or body/LOC credit; 2026-10-30): followed `M68KEmu_Execute()` setting the selected model to M68040 (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_moira.cpp:317`) through `Moira::setModel()` and both execute/disassembly jump-table construction (`rom/m68kemu/Moira/Moira/Moira.cpp:66-73`; `MoiraInit_cpp.h:157-185`). Although M68040 uses the C68020 core family, the CALLM and RTM registration blocks additionally require `model == Model::M68EC020 || model == Model::M68020` (`MoiraInit_cpp.h:653-668,1555-1565`), so neither opcode is installed in the selected M68040 execution or disassembly tables. NXP lists both CALLM and RTM as MC68020-only ([official M68000 Family Programmer's Reference Manual, CALLM p. 4-64 and RTM p. 4-167](https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/reference-manual/M68000PRM.pdf)). The apparent core/model mismatch therefore does not make these instructions executable on the selected M68040 path. No opcode, emulator, guest, or build was run; source-only.

Moira selected M68040 RESET instruction and bridge-side-effect boundary pass (no new EK or body/LOC credit; 2026-10-30): traced the selected RESET registration (`MoiraInit_cpp.h:1530-1537`) through `execReset()` (`MoiraExec_cpp.h:4919-4935`), confirming supervisor-only gating, the selected 68040 timing entry, prefetch, and no memory/device callback or reset delegate from the instruction handler. NXP's M68000 Family Programmer's Reference Manual, RESET entry (p. 6-83), specifies that M68040 asserts RSTO to reset external devices while leaving CPU state intact. Reconciled the AROS bridge: it models only a small custom-register subset and has no `cpuDidReset()` override or external-device reset hook; the base callback is only called by `cpu.reset()` during `M68KEmu_Execute()` startup, not by the RESET instruction. This leaves external reset side effects unsupported, but the selected bridge does not model resettable external peripherals and its exposed beam/custom-chip state has no established reset contract, so I did not promote the omission as a source-supported defect. Instruction-body coverage already exists; caller/device-model semantics remain a limitation to revisit if the bridge's peripheral scope expands. No guest instruction, peripheral, or build was run; source-only.

Moira full-index extension dispatch cross-check (no new EK or path/LOC credit; 2026-10-30): rechecked `computeEA()`'s selected C68020 full-extension dispatch and PC-relative counterpart against `computeEAfull()`, `baseDispWords()`, `outerDispWords()`, and `penaltyCycles()` (`rom/m68kemu/Moira/Moira/MoiraDataflow_cpp.h:9-203,695-736`). The selected bridge maps M68040 to the C68020 core; full-format extensions are therefore used for indexed address modes. The bit-8 selector distinguishes brief from full format; the base-displacement and indirect outer-displacement width fields map 00/01 to no words, 10 to one word, and 11 to two words; the indirect selector distinguishes preindexed and postindexed formulas, with index suppression applied before address formation. The penalty lookup is indexed only by the low six extension bits, so its 64-entry table index is bounded. No new discrepancy was established for these fields. Reserved extension encodings remain outside this pass's behavior claim, and the broad opcode-specific caller/extension matrix remains open; no body/LOC credit is added. No emulated instruction or build was run; source-only.

CDFS path-table parent-index bounds and selected lookup pass (EK10253 added; no body/LOC credit; 2026-10-30): traced `isoPathTable.ParentDirectory` (`iso9660.h:101-107`) from table ingestion into both consumers. `isoReadPathTables()` publishes the entries after only counting record lengths (`iso9660.c:492-529`); `isoParseDir()` reads `Entry[ParentDirectory-1]` without checking zero or the `Entries` upper bound (`:121-124`), and the `..` branch repeats it (`:708-713`). The path-table branch of `isoFindCmp()` reaches `isoParseDir()` for entries after locating the current directory by extent (`:361-375`), establishing a normal lookup path for a malformed, complete record. Added EK10253, distinct from EK10250's truncated-record extent case. No image, lookup, parent traversal, or build was run; source-only.


<a id="cdfs-path-table-child-lookup-follow-up"></a>
CDFS path-table child filtering and Locate caller pass (EK10254 added; no body/LOC credit; 2026-10-30): followed the table-backed branch of `isoFindCmp()` through its caller `isoFindName()` and `ISO9660_Locate()`. Once an entry matching the current directory extent is found, the inner loop visits every other path-table entry and compares its parsed name; no `ParentDirectory` relation is checked (`iso9660.c:361-375,429-437`). `ISO9660_Locate()` uses this lookup for path components (`:750-755,769-779`). On retained non-Rock-Ridge path tables, a matching directory elsewhere can therefore satisfy a component absent from the current directory. Added EK10254, distinct from EK10253's out-of-bounds parent-index case. No image, lookup, packet, or build was run; source-only.


<a id="cdfs-rock-ridge-extent-validation-follow-up"></a>
CDFS Rock Ridge extension minimum-length and block-extent pass (EK10255 added; no body/LOC credit; 2026-10-30): traced the single-block `BCache_Read()` result through `isoReadDir()` into `isoParseDir()` (`iso9660.c:316-329`). The input pointer has no accompanying remaining-block length, and the directory record length is not checked before parsing. Within the SUA loop, the only structural stop is a zero extension length; recognized AS/PX/CL/PL cases access fixed fields without verifying their declared extension length or remaining record extent (`:189-200,202-250,262-270,278-288`). A malformed cross-boundary directory record can therefore take reads past the sector buffer; short extension records can consume adjacent record bytes as metadata. Added EK10255, distinct from EK10246's use of an absolute offset within the selected buffer. No malformed image, block, parser or build was exercised; source-only.


CDFS Rock Ridge signed-length hypothesis rejected (no new finding or body/LOC credit; 2026-10-30): checked the proposed backward-cursor case in the system-use loop against the local type declarations. `iso9660.h:16` explicitly defines `int8` as `UBYTE`; consequently `rrSystemUse.Length` at `:134` is unsigned, and `i += rr->Length` cannot decrement the parser cursor for byte values 128–255. No signed-wrap candidate is retained. This does not change EK10255's independent missing bounds checks for extension and directory-record extents. Source-only.


<a id="cdfs-negative-read-length-follow-up"></a>
CDFS signed read-length packet and caller pass (EK10256 added; no body/LOC credit; 2026-10-30): confirmed public `Read()` takes signed `LONG length` and `rom/dos/read.c` sends it unchanged in `ACTION_READ`; CDFS then forwards `dp_Arg3` to `op_Read` and `ISO9660_Read()` (`read.c:59-73`; `cdfs.c:577-586`). `ISO9660_Read()` has no negative-length guard: with `il_Offset > 0` and `len == -1`, the clamp expression does not select a positive bounded read, `while (len)` executes, and the mixed signed/unsigned `tocopy` comparison leaves the initial block copy intact (`iso9660.c:869-887`). The DOS docs describe `length` as a byte count, so this is retained as a medium-confidence invalid-argument robustness candidate; no in-tree caller passing a negative length was found in this pass. Added EK10256. No packet, buffer, file, or build was used; source-only.

Followed a beyond-EOF cursor into `ISO9660_Read()`'s unsigned `size - il_Offset` clamp (`iso9660.c:869-887`), confirming a second consequence if a read follows. Added EK10257. No seek, read, file, or build was used; source-only.

Security task-owner restore allocation-failure pass (EK10274 added; no path/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): re-read `PopOwner()`/`SetNodeOwner()` and traced `secLogoutA()` into the selected `Logout` command (`rom/security/security_task.c:429-509`; `security_login.c:382-394,600-660`; `workbench/c/security/Logout.c:49-84`). `SetNodeOwner()` can fail while cloning a non-NULL saved owner; `PopOwner()` ignores that result, restores the real/saved UID/GID scalars, joins the old session, then frees the saved owner and stack entry while returning TRUE. `secLogoutA()` consequently regards logout as restored, skips the nobody/login path because `node->Owner` remains non-NULL, and returns that still-installed owner; `Logout` prints it and returns success. Checked `MAlloc()`/`CloneExtOwner()` failure propagation (`security_memory.c:45-59`; `security_task.c:35-51`) and the default current-task/non-global logout tags (`security_login.c:41-53`). Added EK10274, scoped to a saved non-NULL owner plus pool allocation failure. The complete `security_task.c` body and selected file path were already credited in the Exec ledger; no path/LOC change. The selected x86-64 PC `KLIBS` and RISC-V OpenSBI `BSP_LIBS` both include security.library (`arch/x86_64-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:62-65`; `arch/riscv64-opensbi/boot/mmakefile.src:97-101`). No login/logout, allocation failure, build or runtime operation was performed; source-only.

<a id="security-global-owner-stack-restore-pass-ek10275"></a>
Security global owner-stack recursion pass (EK10275 added; no path/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): traced `secT_Global` through `ApplyOwner()` and `RestoreOwner()` to the selected `Login`/`Logout` command tag construction (`rom/security/security_login.c:362-394,615-629`; `workbench/c/security/Login.c:132-135`; `Logout.c:43-71`). `ApplyOwner()` recurses through each descendant and calls `PushOwner()` at every level; `RestoreOwner()` pops the selected node and iterates only its direct children, calling non-recursive `PopOwner()` on each. Grandchildren and deeper nodes therefore keep the global login owner and their saved stack entries after `Logout GLOBAL`; `ALL` repeats this same one-level action and does not reach deeper nodes. Added EK10275 as distinct from EK10274's allocation-failure handling. Security task/login bodies were previously credited; no path/LOC change. x86-64 PC and RISC-V OpenSBI select security.library. No task hierarchy, login/logout, build or runtime operation was performed; source-only.

<a id="security-owner-stack-allocation-pass-ek10276"></a>
Security owner-stack allocation/caller pass (EK10276 added; no path/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): traced `ApplyOwner()`'s push/apply sequence into `PushOwner()` and `SetNodeOwner()`, then through `secLoginA()`, the selected `Login` command and later `secLogoutA()` (`rom/security/security_login.c:366-379,749-767,615-660`; `security_task.c:429-445,468-509`; `workbench/c/security/Login.c:154-187`). `PushOwner()` returns FALSE without a stack entry if the entry allocation or saved-owner clone fails; `ApplyOwner()` ignores that result and continues. If applying the new owner succeeds, `secLoginA()` returns the installed owner and the command reports success. Subsequent logout has no snapshot for that login: absent older entries it clears to nobody or prompts for a fresh login; with older entries it can pop the wrong, earlier login layer. Global login can leave different descendants with and without snapshots. Added EK10276, conditioned on prior non-NULL credentials and the split allocation outcome. The security task/login source bodies were already credited; no path/LOC change. Selected x86-64 PC and RISC-V OpenSBI package manifests include security.library. No login/logout, allocation failure, build or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only.

<a id="security-owner-application-failure-pass-ek10277"></a>
Security owner-application failure pass (EK10277 added; no path/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): traced `ApplyOwner()` through the `SetNodeOwner()` allocation check into `secLoginA()` return handling and the checked-in `Login` and `Login PARENT` callers (`rom/security/security_login.c:366-379,725-767`; `security_task.c:429-445`; `workbench/c/security/Login.c:154-187`). If cloning the requested owner fails, `SetNodeOwner()` returns FALSE before updating the node; `ApplyOwner()` ignores it, may still join the new session, and `secLoginA()` returns the previously installed owner. The command treats every non-`secOWNER_NOBODY` result as success, including the PARENT application check. Added EK10277 for a requested owner different from the current non-nobody owner when its clone fails. This is separate from EK10276's missing saved-owner snapshot and EK10274's failed restore; source bodies and LOC were previously credited. Selected x86-64 PC and RISC-V OpenSBI packages include security.library. No login, allocation failure, build or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only.

EK10277 trigger qualification (2026-10-31; no new ID or coverage credit): narrowed the report to an attempted owner change where the requested UID/GID differs from the currently installed non-nobody owner. The `Login PARENT` instance likewise requires the caller's owner to differ from the parent's; if the identities are already equal, failed cloning does not establish the reported false-success mismatch. No path/LOC or confidence change.

## Moira STOP model-specific manual reconciliation (EK10268 retained)

Moira STOP model-specific manual reconciliation (EK10268 retained at medium confidence; no path/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): reopened the STOP candidate against the selected M68040 rather than relying only on the family-level reference. The M68040 User’s Manual Table 1-4 (p. 1-19) states “If Supervisor State, Immediate Data → SR; STOP; Else TRAP”; §8.2.5 lists STOP as privileged and says privilege processing begins before instruction execution, while §8.2.6 describes loading SR before the stopped-state decision ([official M68040 User’s Manual](https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/reference-manual/MC68040UM.pdf)). This supports the interpretation that the initial S bit gates the instruction, followed by the specified full SR load. The archived fourth-edition M68000 Family Programmer’s Reference Manual STOP entry separately states that an immediate S bit of zero causes a privilege violation ([archived manual](https://gtts.ehu.es/WDW/German/68000/M68000%20Programmer%27s%20RefMan%204th%20Ed.pdf)). The selected Moira path checks pre-instruction privilege in `execStop()`, writes the immediate with `setSR()`, then `execute()` checks the changed S bit while `STOPPED` and can raise vector 8 (`MoiraExec_cpp.h:5353-5364`; `Moira.cpp:301-310`). The selected compatibility reference does not perform that second check: Musashi tests `FLAG_S`, sets `CPU_STOPPED`, then calls `m68ki_set_sr(new_sr)` (`Runner/Musashi/m68kops.c:30828-30842`), and its execute loop checks interrupts before skipping instruction execution while stopped (`Runner/Musashi/m68kcpu.c:952-968`). This agrees with the M68040-specific manual summary, but the reference source is not itself the hardware contract. Retained EK10268 at medium confidence because the archived family-manual S-bit rule remains in tension with the selected M68040 documentation. Existing source-body credit is unchanged; no instruction, exception, IPL, or build was run; source-only.

Moira selected M68040 RTD/RTR/RTS stack and return-state pass (no new EK or body/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): traced the selected RTD, RTR and RTS opcode entries (`rom/m68kemu/Moira/Moira/MoiraInit_cpp.h:1538-1544,1573-1587`) through their handlers (`MoiraExec_cpp.h:4938-4966,5218-5299`) and the common queued extension/prefetch and stack helpers. RTD pops the long PC and applies the sign-extended immediate displacement plus four to SP; RTR pops the low CCR byte, then PC, without restoring the supervisor part of SR; RTS pops PC and advances SP by four. These match the Motorola/NXP M68000 Family Programmer's Reference Manual operation definitions for RTD, RTR, and RTS ([official manual](https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/reference-manual/M68000PRM.pdf), pp. 4-165, 4-168-4-169). The AROS bridge selects M68040, where RTD is available; no selected valid-path SP, PC, or CCR mismatch was established. The shared odd-SP/odd-PC checks are inactive in this bridge because `MOIRA_EMULATE_ADDRESS_ERROR=false` (`MoiraConfig.h:44`); bus-fault behavior is not claimed because the selected memory callbacks do not raise those faults. No body/LOC credit because these handlers are within the already partially credited `MoiraExec_cpp.h`; no guest instruction or build was run; source-only.

Reconciled the ordinary ready-list fast path in `arch/m68k-all/exec/dispatch.S:17-45` with `m68k_DispatchFrame()` and `m68k_SwitchTail()` (`arch/m68k-all/kernel/kernel_cpu.c:30-45,68-76`). Moira selected M68040 branch-family and DBcc counter pass (no new EK; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): reviewed `execBra()`/`execBcc()`/`execBsr()` and both ordinary and 68010 loop forms of `execDbcc()` (`rom/m68kemu/Moira/Moira/MoiraExec_cpp.h:841-916,1342-1397,2140-2310`), their opcode registrations (`MoiraInit_cpp.h:418-466,825-862`), `readExt()` (`MoiraDataflow_cpp.h:610-620`), and the selected bridge/model/config (`m68kemu_moira.cpp:314-321`; `MoiraConfig.h:44,84`). Compared the selected M68040/C68020 dispatch with the Motorola/NXP M68000 Family Programmer's Reference Manual: branch base is the address after the opcode, 0 selects word displacement, 0xFF selects long displacement on 68020+, BSR stacks the following-instruction address, and DBcc decrements only when the condition is false and falls through when the low word reaches -1 ([Bcc](https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/reference-manual/M68000PM.pdf), [BRA/BSR](https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/reference-manual/M68000PM.pdf), [DBcc](https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/reference-manual/M68000PM.pdf)). The code's extension fetch updates `reg.pc` consistently with those bases and the BSR return address; DBcc's pre-decrement `takeBranch` test is equivalent to testing the decremented low word against -1, and the condition remains unmodified. The apparent validation of an odd DBcc target before checking loop exhaustion does not affect this selected build: `MOIRA_EMULATE_ADDRESS_ERROR` is false and `misaligned()` compiles to false for the selected configuration. No branch, stack, guest, emulator, build, or runtime operation was exercised. Broader opcode/timing/caller coverage of both generated Moira files remains open.

ARM32 CLI/STI interrupt-exit caller closure (updated 2026-11-07; no new EK or body/LOC credit): completed the direct-call census for the selected `arch/arm-native/kernel/cli.c` and `sti.c` wrappers. `Disable()` is the ordinary production `KrnCli()` caller; `Enable()` only calls `KrnSti()` after its nesting count becomes negative and when `KrnIsSuper()` is false. The generic `SoftIntDispatch()` also uses the wrappers directly: the ARM IRQ and FIQ vectors call `core_ExitInterrupt()` only when the saved return mode is User/System, and FIQ additionally defers when saved IRQs were masked (`arch/arm-native/kernel/intr.c:132-143,173-186`; `rom/kernel/kernel_intr.c:30-39`). In that path the dispatcher invokes `KrnCli()`/`KrnSti()`, whose syscall IDs are handled as mask-only cases before the generic scheduler syscall path; the latter runs only for User/System saved contexts (`syscall.c:169-191,237-246`). Thus this trace found no evidence that soft-int dispatch performs a task switch through the nested SVC while unwinding an interrupt, and the wrappers' documented purpose is consistent with their selected caller. Followed the common SWI frame in `VECTCOMMON_START/END` (`arch/arm-native/kernel/kernel_intern.h:83-111`): it saves SPSR in the frame at `regs[16]`, `handle_syscall()` changes the saved I/F bits for `SC_CLI`/`SC_STI`, and `rfefd` restores the modified return state. This closes the source-level saved-mask/exception-return path; physical interrupt delivery timing and FIQ stack-depth remain open. Existing full-body credits stand; no interrupt, SWI, task switch or build was run. Source-only.

Moira selected M68040 long-multiply pass (no new EK or body/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): traced the MULL opcode registration and extension-word dispatch (`MoiraInit_cpp.h:1321-1325`; `MoiraExec_cpp.h:4058-4135`) through the selected M68040 bridge/C68020 core and `MOIRA_MIMIC_MUSASHI=true` configuration (`m68kemu_moira.cpp:314-321`; `MoiraConfig.h:84`). The generated execution/initialization/ALU bodies remain partial; no file or LOC credit is claimed. No instruction, guest, emulator, or build was run; source-only.

Moira MULL/DIVL reserved-extension validation (EK10297 added; no body/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): followed the selected M68040 MULL and DIVL registrations (`MoiraInit_cpp.h:883-886,1321-1324`) through `Moira::execute()` dispatch (`Moira.cpp:251-263`) and the selected Musashi-compatible handlers (`MoiraExec_cpp.h:4058-4133,4436-4447,4568-4639`). Both handlers consume extension bits 11–10 but do not reject reserved bits 15 and 9–3. `isValidExt()` has the same mask for both instructions (`Moira.cpp:788-789`), but a complete call-site search shows it is used only in `MoiraDasm_cpp.h`, not instruction execution. The NXP M68000 Family Programmer's Reference Manual shows those reserved positions as zero for MULS/MULU (pp. 4-137–4-139) and DIVS/DIVU (pp. 4-94–4-99); the MC68040 User's Manual §8.2.4 defines invalid instruction patterns as illegal instructions. Added EK10297 as a medium-confidence candidate: malformed guest code can execute multiplication or division instead of taking the illegal-instruction exception. Scope is explicit M68040/Musashi-compatible `m68kemu.library` builds; parent ROM aggregate inclusion is not claimed (`rom/m68kemu/mmakefile.src:15-17`). Moira STOP state-transition recheck (EK10268 confirmed and narrowed; no path/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): revisited the selected STOP registration and `execStop()` pre-state guard/immediate-SR/STOPPED sequence (`rom/m68kemu/Moira/Moira/MoiraInit_cpp.h:1655`; `MoiraExec_cpp.h:5353-5364`), then followed `setSR()` stack-bank switching and the next `execute()` iteration's IRQ-before-stopped handling (`Moira.cpp:288-310,490-560`). The M68040 User's Manual Table 1-4 specifies the pre-instruction supervisor test followed by immediate-to-SR and STOP; §8.2.5 identifies privilege processing as beginning before execution, and §1-19 describes STOP as waiting for interrupts ([official NXP-hosted M68040 User's Manual](https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/reference-manual/MC68040UM.pdf)). The selected Musashi compatibility handler likewise checks the old S bit before loading the new SR and has no second privilege test (`Runner/Musashi/m68kops.c:30828-30842`; `MoiraConfig.h:84`). This resolves the prior family-manual ambiguity for the selected M68040 path: EK10268 is confirmed at high confidence, with the trigger narrowed to no interrupt eligible under the new mask. The optional `kernel-m68kemu-library` target remains the affected configuration; no maintained AROS IPL caller is claimed. No guest instruction, interrupt, exception, emulator, or build was run; source-only.

EK9883 WaitIO/AddTail concrete pointer-interleaving pass (2026-10-31; no new EK or path/LOC credit): re-read `WaitIO()`'s two ordered writes (`rom/exec/waitio.c:74-75`), `Remove()`'s direct neighbor updates (`remove.c:61-62`), and `AddTail()`'s four writes (`addtail.c:57-65`) against the AHI-Handler shared reply-port path. With A as the sole queued node, WaitIO first makes `head->next = tail`; before WaitIO's second write, concurrent AddTail for B writes `B->next = tail`, captures A as `B->prev`, and writes `A->next = B`. WaitIO then writes `tail->prev = head`, after which AddTail writes `tail->prev = B`. The final state has `head->next == tail` but `tail->prev == B`, with B unreachable from the port head. The missing shared lock allows the cross-CPU ordering despite WaitIO's local Disable. This makes EK9883's list-corruption consequence concrete; the required schedule remains conditional and was not run. No I/O, port operation, or build was performed; source-only.

Pthread detach-during-completion timing follow-up (EK569 expanded; no new ID or path/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): reread `StarterFunc()` completion and `pthread_detach()` (`compiler/pthread/pthread_create.c:203-209`; `pthread.c:942-960`) with `__pthread_Exit_Func()` (`pthread.c:1234-1255`). The worker branches on `inf->detached` without synchronization; a parent detach after the worker reads false sets the flag too late for the worker to take its slot-clearing path. The worker then signals completion while retaining `inf->task`, and the process exit hook waits on that pointer because it now sees `detached == TRUE`. This is an additional ExecSMP timing for EK569’s already-confirmed completed-unjoined trigger; both share the same missed completion cleanup. The library’s `__pthread_Init_Func()` itself always succeeds after initializing the semaphores and main-thread record (`pthread.c:1217-1231`), so this path is not dependent on generic EXIT-after-failed-INIT behavior. `compiler/pthread/mmakefile.src:15-48` selects `pthread.c` in the pthread link library. No concurrent detach, thread, or process exit was run; source-only.
ARM-native scheduler-list helper caller reconciliation (2026-10-31; no new EK or body/LOC credit): enumerated every in-tree `exec_TaskRemoveRunning()`/`exec_TaskEnqueue*()` call (`rom/exec/wait.c:99-100`; `arch/arm-native/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:201,214,229`; `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:180,193,208`; ARM bootstrap callers in `arch/arm-native/exec/platform_init.c:129-213`; AArch64 counterparts in `arch/aarch64-native/exec/platform_init.c:114-180`). Traced their generic `krnSysCallReschedTask()` callers in `signal.c:66-74,368-440`, `newaddtask.c:37-42,106-114`, `remtask.c:100-109`, and `service.c:106-112`. `Wait()` holds `tc_SpinLock` across the TS_RUN-to-TS_WAIT/list transition and the context switch; ARM/AArch64 `core_Switch()` holds it across TS_RUN-to-TS_READY, with IRQ/FIQ masking preventing local interrupt re-entry. The architecture `Exec_ReschedTask()` routines acquire `tc_SpinLock` before selecting/removing the source list and before publishing the new state/list, and their TS_READY wake path ignores tasks already READY/RUN or terminal, preventing duplicate enqueue after a competing wake. The per-architecture `EXEC_BLOCK_DISPATCH_*` operations update per-CPU TLS directly while the helper holds the relevant list lock, avoiding a Permit-triggered context switch in that critical section. No list/state ordering defect was established in these callers. The full API caller population outside checked-in AROS code and runtime SMP/IRQ schedules remain unverified; existing source bodies were already credited. No build or task/interrupt interleaving was run; source-only.


PC ExecSMP `SetTaskPri()` versus dispatch transition (EK10303 added; no source-path/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): traced the selected PC `core_Dispatch()` dequeue, `SET_THIS_TASK()` Running-list insertion and delayed TS_RUN store (`arch/all-pc/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:304-322,344-370`; `arch/all-pc/exec/exec_platform.h:295-303`) against `SetTaskPri()` task/list locking (`rom/exec/settaskpri.c:72-112`). The dispatcher does not take `tc_SpinLock`; the priority setter does and uses TS_READY to select `TaskReadySpinLock` and reinsert the node. A concurrent priority change can therefore requeue a dequeued node or unlink a Running node while holding the Ready lock, leaving duplicate/corrupt scheduler-list membership. Traced the maintained `ChangeTaskPri PROCESS` caller and confirmed `Forbid()` is CPU-local on ExecSMP (`workbench/c/ChangeTaskPri.c:86-104`; `rom/exec/forbid.c:58-61`). Compared the selected ARM32/AArch64 dispatch paths, which acquire `tc_SpinLock` before removing the ready node (`arm-native/kernel_scheduler.c:263-287`; `aarch64-native/kernel_scheduler.c:241-261`); they are excluded from EK10303. <a id="x86-64-page-protection-length-width-ek10312"></a>x86-64 page-protection length-width and caller pass (EK10312 added; 2026-10-31; no file/LOC credit): compared the generic page allocation/free signatures and protection calls (`rom/kernel/allocpages.c:27-44,61-83`; `freepages.c:23-37,45-52`) with the selected x86-64 `KrnSetProtection()` vector (`arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/setprotection.c:15-18,39-55`) and public map API types (`compiler/include/aros/kernel.h:28-39`). `KrnAllocPages`/`KrnFreePages` carry `uintptr_t` lengths, while the protection vector and its `protect_pages()` helper take `uint32_t`; lengths above `UINT32_MAX` are truncated before page rounding, so an exact 4-GiB range is a no-op and a larger range updates only its low-32-bit prefix. The free wrapper can then return the whole allocation while leaving tail-page attributes unchanged. Scoped EK10312 to x86-64 PC when the generic MMU allocator is enabled and `kb_PageSize` is nonzero. The checked x86-64 startup has no page-size assignment (EK639), and the maintained C-call census found no multi-gigabyte page request; no current default-path reachability is claimed. Both implementation bodies already have coverage credit; this adds no path/LOC count. No page allocation, permission update, free, or build was run; source-only.

EK10312 direct C-caller size-bound census (2026-10-31; finding qualification strengthened; no path/LOC credit): repeated a repository-wide direct-call search for `KrnAllocPages()` and `KrnFreePages()`. Apart from declarations/definitions/comments and the allocator debug test, the maintained allocation calls are `compiler/arossupport/createseglist.c:74` and `rom/dos/loadseg.c:73`; both pass `ULONG` lengths. Maintained free calls are the matching `rom/dos/loadseg.c:103` and `rom/dos/unloadseg.c:43`, also passed as `ULONG` segment lengths. Those call sites cannot request more than `UINT32_MAX` bytes, so the >32-bit truncation trigger is not established for direct in-tree C callers. This does not remove the API-width mismatch: the public page allocation/free vectors use `uintptr_t`, and external clients or other ABI callers can supply wider ranges when the x86-64 generic MMU allocator is enabled. EK10312 remains conditional on that path and a >32-bit request. No allocator, protection change, or build was run; source-only.

<a id="posixc-dup2-cross-process-target-reservation-ek10313"></a>POSIXC `dup2()` cross-process target ownership trace (EK10313 added; 2026-10-31; no path/LOC credit): re-read the complete `dup2()` target path, `__getfdslot()` reservation logic, `__setfdesc()` publication, `fd.library` `FD_SetData()`/`FD_Free()`, and `close()` lookup/cleanup (`compiler/crt/posixc/dup2.c:72-122`; `__fdesc.c:116-143,184-201,227-299`; `close.c:43-54,109-112`; `workbench/libs/fd/fd_alloc.c:146-196,414-445`). Confirmed ordinary processes have separate local descriptor arrays, but `fd.library` holds one system-wide owner/data entry per number. An empty local target in process A skips `FD_Reserve()` merely because process B's global owner class is already `FD_OWNER_POSIXC`; A then replaces global data. When either process closes, `FD_Free()` releases the shared entry despite the other local table's live descriptor; the survivor's next `__getfdesc()` rejects it and `close()` returns `EBADF`, leaving its local descriptor/FCB reference. The documented `dup2()` restriction prohibits shared-library and threaded use, not separate processes; no in-tree selected caller was found that deliberately collides targets, but the API contract establishes the caller scenario. Added EK10313 and master-index entry. Existing body/path/LOC credit is unchanged; no process, descriptor, `dup2()` call, or build was used; source-only.

<a id="unix-hosted-krnfreepages-width-ek21"></a>Unix-hosted `KrnFreePages()` public-width and caller recheck (EK21 detail restored; 2026-10-31; no new path/LOC credit): compared the public `uintptr_t` vector declaration (`rom/kernel/kernel.conf:66`) with the selected Unix override (`arch/all-unix/kernel/freepages.c:12-24`) and its `munmap()` call. The implementation parameter is `uint32_t`, so 64-bit callers lose all length bits above bit 31: exact 4 GiB becomes a zero-length unmap, and larger lengths unmap only the low-32-bit prefix. Console-handler input compaction versus all selected CopyMem implementations (EK706/EK710 rechecked; no new finding or coverage credit; 2026-10-31): `answer_read_request()` compacts at most `INPUTBUFFER_SIZE` (256) bytes from `inputbuffer + readlen` to the lower `inputbuffer` address (`rom/filesys/console_handler/support.c:1122-1132`; `con_handler_intern.h:40,89`). The generic Exec and x86-64 implementation copy forward; for this higher-source/lower-destination direction, each write stays below unread source bytes, including the x86-64 64-byte SSE blocks which load the full block before storing it (`rom/exec/copymem.c:67-152`; `arch/x86_64-all/exec/copymem.c:92-225`). The m68k 68000, 020, 040, 060 and AC68080 selections also advance source and destination together in increasing order (`arch/m68k-all/exec/copymem_.S`; `copymem_020.S`; `copymem_040.S`; `copymem_060.S`; `copymem_ac080.S`; selection in `exec_platform.c:32-52`). The i386 SSE replacement's threshold is 4096 bytes, so this 256-byte maximum takes the generic path (`arch/i386-all/exec/copymem_SSE.S:47-53`). Thus the call violates CopyMem's documented non-overlap precondition but the examined selected implementations preserve this specific compaction; no data-corruption finding is supported for these architectures. Other platform selection/implementation combinations were not exhaustively enumerated. Targeted caller/implementation pass only; no body, file, or C-LOC credit; no build or console operation.

Rechecked the close sequence: the process whose global entry has been freed subsequently gets `__getfdesc()==NULL` and has no POSIXC hook in `__getfdhooks()`, so its local slot is not cleared by `close()` and remains stranded (`__fdesc.c:116-170`; `close.c:43-54`). The documented `dup2()` threading prohibition does not cover this separate-process scenario. Retained EK10313 with no checked-in caller claiming the explicit collision; no process, descriptor, or build was used; source-only.

<a id="x86-64-standalone-xsave-context-size-and-switch-pair-reconciliation"></a>
x86-64 standalone XSAVE context sizing and task-switch pairing reconciliation (EK8958/EK9191/EK10209 rechecked; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): read the complete x86-64 `cpu_Init()` and `KrnCreateContext()` bodies, the saved-context layout, the x86-64 PC AP startup setup, and the selected dispatch save/restore paths. For standalone x86-64, CPUID leaf 1 gates XSAVE and AVX; the initializer enables CR4.OSXSAVE (`_CR4_OSXSBV`), sets XCR0 bits 0–2, then queries leaf D/subleaf 0 for the enabled XSAVE area size. The allocation reserves that size plus up to 63 bytes of alignment slack; context creation rounds the payload to 64-byte alignment and derives `FPUCtxSize` from the allocation, while task dispatch uses the same XSAVE mask for save and restore. The FXSAVE fallback reserves a 512-byte context plus 15 bytes of alignment slack and pairs `fxsave`/`fxrstor`. PC AP startup repeats the OSXSAVE/XCR0 enable before creating its bootstrap context. No size/alignment or save/restore mismatch was established in these paths. This does not close host CPU/firmware feature contracts, the x86-64 IRQ callback vector-preservation candidate EK9191, or Linux hosted extended-state omission EK10209; those have distinct configurations and evidence. The reviewed bodies were already credited, so this caller/contract reconciliation adds no file or LOC credit. No CPU probe, task switch, interrupt or build was run; source-only.

<a id="tasktrace-frame-record-extent-check-ek10320"></a>
TaskTrace frame-record extent check pass (EK10320 added; 2026-10-31; no file/LOC credit): traced x86-64 `GetFramePointer()` through `PrintStackTrace()` and `UnwindFrame()` (`developer/debug/shellcommands/TaskTrace.c:168-197,284-305`). CHK2/CMP2 address-register-width note correction (EK10233 retained; 2026-10-31; no body/path/LOC credit): rechecked the selected handler against `Moira::readR<S>()` (`rom/m68kemu/Moira/Moira.cpp:574-578`) and the selected `MOIRA_MIMIC_MUSASHI` branch (`MoiraExec_cpp.h:1693-1698`). `readR<S>()` always returns `CLIP<S>(reg.r[n])`; because the shared register array holds Dn and An, the byte/word read truncates An as well as Dn. This finding concerns the compare operand and is distinct from the PC-relative byte-bound issue EK10239. The report already states the trigger, consequence and selected configuration accurately. No new body/path/LOC credit; no instruction or build was run; source-only.

EK9052 AArch64 already-privileged entry reconciliation (2026-10-31; existing finding expanded; no new path/LOC credit): revisited the earlier cross-architecture disposition that excluded AArch64 based on the selected task-mode entry. The public `SuperState()` contract separately specifies an already-supervisor caller must receive NULL; AArch64's selected RasPi override has no mode check and always returns its saved stack token (`arch/aarch64-native/exec/superstate.c:13-31`; selected by `arch/aarch64-native/exec/mmakefile.src:18-39`). `SC_SUPERSTATE` unconditionally sets the saved return mode to EL1h, including for an EL1h entry (`arch/aarch64-native/kernel/syscall.c:198-205`); `SC_USERSTATE` unconditionally sets EL1t and clears IRQ masking (`:214-225`). The syscall's `SC_ISSUPERSTATE` semantics classify every saved mode other than EL1t as supervisor (`:228-233`; `kernel_cpu.h:28-37`). Thus a caller already in EL1h receives a non-NULL token, and documented `if (token) UserState(token)` returns it in EL1t task mode. This is the same documented token/mode-contract defect as ARM32 EK9052, with a port-specific consequence; it does not establish a default in-tree caller, since the checked SB128 AHI pair is task-only. Updated the detailed finding and master index to include AArch64 Raspberry Pi. The 2026-10-18 note saying no AArch64 mismatch for selected task-mode entry remains valid only for that entry and does not cover the public already-privileged case. No SVC, privilege transition, build or runtime operation was exercised; source-only.


<a id="ek9071-attemptsemaphore-counter-recheck"></a>
EK9071 semaphore counter arithmetic and AttemptSemaphore caller-path expansion (existing finding strengthened; 2026-10-31; no new ID or source-body credit): rechecked `InternalObtainSemaphore()`, `InternalAttemptSemaphore()`, both shared/exclusive vector wrappers, `Procure()`, and `ReleaseSemaphore()` (`rom/exec/semaphores.c:50-161,164-213`; `attemptsemaphore.c`; `attemptsemaphoreshared.c`; `obtainsemaphore.c`; `obtainsemaphoreshared.c`; `procure.c:68-92`; `releasesemaphore.c:83-114,188-196`). Both successful `AttemptSemaphore` variants retain the same signed `ss_QueueCount`/`ss_NestCount` increments as blocking obtains; a failed attempt against another owner rolls back its queue-count increment. Starting free at `ss_QueueCount=-1`, 65,536 successful recursive acquisitions leave the count at -1 and nesting at zero with the old owner pointer intact; a competing obtain or attempt then increments to zero and is treated as a free grant. With one exclusive owner at count zero, 32,769 queued task/message bids leave the signed count at -32767; the owner's release decrements to -32768, misses the `>= 0` waiter-service branch, sets the sentinel, and leaves the queue linked without replies. Expanded EK9071's detailed report and index to name the AttemptSemaphore path and exact thresholds. These are source arithmetic outcomes requiring extreme public-API workloads; this report does not claim a checked-in caller that produces either workload, and no semaphore operation was run.

<a id="sem-timedwait-timeout-with-available-permit-ek8910"></a>

EK8910 timed semaphore waiter and condition signal recheck (2026-10-31; detailed report/index entry restored; no new body or LOC credit): reread `sem_timedwait()` and `sem_post()` (`compiler/pthread/semaphore.c:226-294`) alongside `_pthread_cond_timedwait()` (`compiler/pthread/pthread_cond_timedwait.c:128-169`). `sem_post()` increments the protected count before signaling; if both timer and condition bits are returned by `Wait()`, the condition helper returns `ETIMEDOUT` first. `sem_timedwait()` then unlocks and returns without rechecking or consuming the positive count. Qualified the consequence to a false timeout for this waiter while the permit remains available to a later waiter, not permanent token loss. The only maintained direct `sem_wait()` caller passes a NULL deadline; timed-wait reachability therefore requires an application/external caller. No timer or semaphore operation was run; source-only.



x86-64 NewStackSwap NULL-argument and stack-boundary recheck (EK8837/EK8962 retained; no new finding or body/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): reread the complete selected `arch/x86_64-all/exec/newstackswap.c` body and reconciled its `args == NULL` path with the selected pthread caller and the public `StackSwapArgs` layout. The NULL path points the register-argument loads at the current task's `tc_SPLower`; those six loads are inside that stack's declared lower-to-upper region, and unspecified function argument registers do not establish a caller-visible defect for entries that do not consume them. The non-NULL path's final two stack arguments are the same writes below `stk_Lower` already recorded under EK8837 when the accepted custom-stack extent is undersized. Its insufficient-space/alignment checks only log and continue, as already recorded; no independent cause was established. The `TF_STACKCHK` fill loop writes only `[stk_Lower, newsp)` and does not itself cross the lower bound; for the undersized case `newsp` can equal the lower bound, after which EK8837's argument pushes remain the concrete below-bound writes. Existing stack alignment and `Enable()` alignment behavior remain under EK8962. No stack switch, memory access, pthread, or build was run; source-only.


Zune `NewStackSwap()` minimum-stack caller census (EK8837/EK8962 rechecked; no new finding or body/LOC credit; 2026-10-31): followed the selected `MIN_STACKSIZE` sites in NList and BetterString through the shared `stackswap_call()` in each `mccinit.c`. The maintained callsites allocate 8,192-byte or 16,384-byte stacks, assign only `swapargs.Args[0]` for the one-argument callback, pass a non-NULL args structure, and free the new stack only after `NewStackSwap()` returns. The allocator's `MEMCHUNK_TOTAL` is two `IPTR`s and `AllocMem()` rounds allocations to that boundary (`rom/exec/memory.c:565-566`), so the 64-bit selected allocation base and these size multiples preserve 16-byte alignment. They therefore do not reach EK8837's undersized-stack write or EK8962's misaligned-size condition on x86-64. The implementation still reads all eight `Args[]` entries (including the two stack-passed slots) when `args` is non-NULL, while these one-argument clients initialize only slot zero; the additional values are passed in unused argument positions and the callback signatures consume one argument, so this pass did not establish a caller-visible defect. The header does not spell out whether callers must initialize unused slots; external variadic or wider callbacks remain outside this caller census. No stack swap, callback, allocation, or build was run; source-only.

m68kemu EK9230 resident-name overflow candidate withdrawn after loop-order recheck (2026-10-31; no path/LOC change): reread `M68KEmu_LoadHunksFromMemory()`'s resident-name loop (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_memory.c:285-291`). POSIX `ftime()` and `gettimeofday()` selected time-path pass (EK10331/EK10332 added; 2026-10-31): read the full `ftime.c` (65 physical / 14 `cloc 2.06` C lines), public `sys/timeb.h` (29 / 15 C/header lines), POSIX `gettimeofday.c` (128 / 36), `__posixc_timer.c` (57 / 20), `__stdc_gmtoffset.c` (65 / 40), and `__optionallibs.c` (79 / 66), for six files and 191 C/header code lines. Confirmed `ftime` is selected in `POSIXC_LINKLIB` and declared in the public header; no checked-in caller beyond its implementation/header description was found. Added EK10331 because the microsecond `tv_usec` is multiplied by 1,000 and stored in the 16-bit millisecond field. Added EK10332 because `ftime()` ignores `gettimeofday()`'s -1 return, then reads both unwritten locals and reports success; the selected timer-open failure path leaves the per-task timer base null, and the close hook only closes a successful open. The selected timezone helper only obtains the optional locale library when already present and falls back to zero offset; no additional defect established in the checked helper/cleanup path. No clock, locale or timer operation was run; source-only.

Parthenope EK9216/EK9218 detailed-report restorations and caller reconciliation (2026-11-01; existing findings; no new IDs or body/path/LOC credit): restored the two missing report sections from the existing full `cdrom.c` audit and rechecked their distinct lifetimes. Parthenope EK9219 detailed-report restoration (2026-11-01; existing finding; no new ID or body/path/LOC credit): rechecked `get_dev()`'s CDROM scan branch (`arch/ppc-sam440/boot/parthenope/src/cdrom.c:469-475`). Parthenope EK9220 detailed-report restoration and zero-SUA caller recheck (2026-11-01; existing finding; no new ID or body/path/LOC credit): reread the root-record read and SUSP setup (`arch/ppc-sam440/boot/parthenope/src/cdrom.c:532-555`). The factory computes SUA size from on-media record length/name fields, does not check `malloc(sua_size)`, ignores `cdrom_read()`, and unconditionally reads `entry->sig`. A valid plain ISO root record without SUSP data yields a zero-length SUA; the zero-length read does not populate `sua` before the signature access. Positive-length allocation/read failures have the same unchecked consumer. Kept malformed signed-length/record-extent behavior separate under EK9228 and restored EK9220's detailed report and master-index entry. No media, allocation/read failure or boot was exercised; source-only.

Parthenope EK9221 detailed-report restoration and failed-scan caller qualification (2026-11-01; existing finding; no new ID or body/path/LOC credit): rechecked both read-error exits in `iterate_entries()` (`arch/ppc-sam440/boot/parthenope/src/cdrom.c:185-193,199-214`) and traced the return through `get_entry()` (`:254-270`) to the Rock Ridge/NM callers (`:332-340,562-568`). Each failed read returns without freeing its currently allocated SUA buffer; the helper ignores the iterator status and returns a NULL match, so callers conflate read failure with absence. Restored EK9221's detailed report and master-index entry, limiting repeated-scan exhaustion claims to unproven. No CD, media error or boot was exercised; source-only.

EK9266 timed pthread late-reply candidate withdrawn (2026-11-01; no new finding or coverage credit): rechecked `_obtain_sema_timed()` (`compiler/pthread/pthread.c:251-327`), `Vacate()` (`rom/exec/vacate.c:48-94`), `ReplyMsg()` (`rom/exec/replymsg.c:45-70`), `CloseTimerDevice()` (`compiler/pthread/pthread.c:173-196`), `FreeSignal()` (`rom/exec/freesignal.c:48-56`) and `WaitPort()` (`rom/exec/waitport.c:57-98`). A timer-first dequeue can be followed by `Vacate()` replying the semaphore request into the helper's stack-local port after its final `GetMsg()`, but the port and message remain confined to that stack frame, so no post-return consumer of the queued links is established. The pending signal is released with the port signal allocation; later `WaitPort()` rechecks its queue after wake. Withdrawn as no demonstrated defect; all three timed pthread callers share this helper. No timer, lock or interleaving was run; source-only.

EK9267 m68kemu generated `VNewRawDoFmt` thunk restored after re-review (2026-11-01; no new path/LOC credit): confirmed generated LVO 822 is installed through `m68kemu_thunks_exec_gen` and selected by `M68KEmu_SetupLibBase()` (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:2401-2408,7460`; `rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_run.c:40-49`). Its A1 translation resolves only to the host address of guest containment memory (`m68kemu_thunks.h:37`; `m68kemu_intern.h:108-122`), which is passed directly as native `va_list`; `InternalRawDoFmt()` uses host `va_arg` for non-NULL streams (`rom/exec/rawdofmt.c:43-74,101-118`). On the explicitly supported 64-bit m68kemu targets this does not translate the guest 32-bit big-endian argument stream into host varargs state. The manual RawDoFmt LVO 522 converter does not override generated LVO 822 (`m68kemu_thunks.c:319-365,699-735`). Restored EK9267 with external-client and optional-target scope; no in-tree guest caller found. No guest or formatter was run; source-only.

EK9268 m68kemu generated `VNewRawDoFmt` callback path restored after re-review (2026-11-01; no new path/LOC credit): traced generated A2 pointer translation (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:2401-2408`; `m68kemu_thunks.h:37`; `m68kemu_intern.h:108-122`) into `VNewRawDoFmt()` and `InternalRawDoFmt()` sentinel checks and callback dispatch (`rom/exec/rawdofmt.c:101-118`). Ordinary guest callback addresses become containment pointers and are invoked as native callbacks; guest `RAWFMTFUNC_SERIAL` and `RAWFMTFUNC_COUNT` values 1/2 also become containment pointers, missing the native sentinel values. A literal-only format isolates callback dispatch from EK9267 argument decoding. Scope is optional m68kemu targets and external guest clients; no maintained in-tree guest caller found. No guest callback or formatter was run; source-only.

EK9269 m68kemu `VNewRawDoFmt` return-pointer candidate restored after re-review (2026-11-01; no new path/LOC credit): traced the string sentinel and guest A3 translation through `InternalRawDoFmt()` pointer advancement/return (`compiler/include/exec/rawfmt.h:9-10`; `rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:2401-2408`; `rom/exec/rawdofmt.c:101-118,316-326`). Generated thunk returns the native pointer unchanged, and Moira truncates it to D0 without `host_to_m68k()` (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_moira.cpp:258-272`). ### Partition geometry-to-NSD command-selection recheck (EK9323 restored, 2026-11-01)

Pthread timed-condition waiter-list and semaphore caller recheck (EK604/EK8910/EK8979; no new finding or LOC credit; 2026-11-01): reread `_pthread_cond_timedwait()` and `_pthread_cond_broadcast()` in full and traced the direct barrier and semaphore callers (`compiler/pthread/pthread_cond_timedwait.c:29-181`; `pthread_cond_broadcast.c:26-57`; `pthread.c:477-519`; `semaphore.c:220-294`). ### Printer per-unit OpenDevice/expunge caller recheck (EK9099)

2026-11-01: traced the selected `workbench-devs-printer` manifest and per-unit construction/rollback in `workbench/devs/printer/driver.c`. `Printer_Unit()` sets the configured unit name and calls `AddDevice()` before `CreateNewProcTags()` and before waiting for the worker startup reply (`:783-812`). A failed worker handshake reaches `RemDevice((struct Device *)pd)` (`:850`); the per-unit expunge vector removes and frees the allocation if `lib_OpenCnt` is zero (`:144-166`). Generic `OpenDevice()` releases its DeviceList read lock after `FindName()` and before invoking the per-unit Open vector, where the open count would be acquired (`rom/exec/opendevice.c:92-114`; `driver.c:95-114`). Thus a direct open on another ExecSMP CPU can hold the raw pointer while this rollback removes/frees the target. The trigger requires worker-startup failure after publication and an overlapping direct `OpenDevice()`; no such overlap or failure was induced. No body/path/LOC credit; source-only.

`DeletePool()` protected-pool teardown synchronization boundary (2026-11-01; no new EK): re-read the complete `DeletePool()` body and compared its behavior with `InternalAllocPooled()` / `InternalFreePooled()` and the pool API comments. `MEMF_SEM_PROTECTED` serializes allocation and free operations, but `DeletePool()` does not obtain that semaphore; teardown therefore requires the owner to quiesce pool users. The API comments do not promise concurrent deletion safety. Checked selected protected-pool callers: USB stack expunge sends `evt_Cleanup` to its worker and waits for the reply before deleting the pool (`workbench/devs/USB/stack/usb_init.c:185-204`; worker cleanup/return at `usbprocess.c:255-261`); this orders the worker's pool use before deletion. HID and MassStorage pools are released during library expunge; Radeon teardown deletes after device unmapping/object disposal, and no selected overlapping operation was established in this pass. NVIDIA's `DeletePool()` is only in its failed-init path before successful use. Nouveau expunge deletes its global pool, but this pass did not establish a selected path where callers can operate after the owner expunges. Therefore the semaphore bypass is recorded as an API lifecycle boundary, not a project bug without a concrete concurrent caller. Broader device/class shutdown and external pool-owner contracts remain pending. No pool operation, expunge, or concurrency test was run; source-only.

EK30 `NewCreateTaskA()` MungWall-overflow caller path (existing finding strengthened; 2026-11-01; no new ID or body/LOC credit): rechecked `TASKTAG_TCBEXTRASIZE` through `NewCreateTaskA()` and `NewAllocEntry()` to `AllocMem()`. On 32-bit targets the public `ULONG` extra-size tag can make `sizeof(struct Task) + extra` equal `ULONG_MAX - MUNGWALL_TOTAL_SIZE + 2` without overflowing this task-size addition; `NewAllocEntry()` passes that length unchanged to `AllocMem()`, whose MungWall overhead addition wraps the reservation to one byte. If the small raw allocation succeeds, `MungWall_Build()` returns a user pointer and `NewCreateTaskA()` proceeds to initialize the task through it. This is a maintained API chain, though no checked-in caller sets the tag; MungWall must be enabled and the tiny allocation must succeed. It is distinct from EK10329, where the task-size addition itself wraps below `sizeof(struct Task)`. The tag is only 32-bit, so this particular `IPTR_MAX` caller route does not apply on 64-bit builds; direct `AllocMem()` remains the generic EK30 trigger there. The detailed EK30 configuration and caller wording was updated. No new whole-body or path credit: both implementation bodies were already credited. No allocation or task creation was attempted; source-only.

Plain `AllocMem()` alignment-rounding overflow discriminator (no new EK or coverage credit; 2026-11-01): checked whether `stdAlloc()`'s `AROS_ROUNDUP2(size, MEMCHUNK_TOTAL)` (`rom/exec/memory.c:565-566`; macro in `compiler/arossupport/include/macros.h:298`) independently returns a tiny block for a near-`IPTR_MAX` request when MungWall is disabled. In the selected standard allocator front end, `nommu_AllocMem()` first skips each MemHeader when `mh_Free < byteSize` (`rom/exec/memory_nommu.c:20-35`), before calling `stdAlloc()`. A near-limit request cannot pass this available-memory gate on a realizable MemHeader, so the rounding wrap alone does not establish an accepted small allocation. The separate EK30 case remains because MungWall wraps the request before this gate. No allocator call or memory operation was run; source-only.

<a id="hosted-bootstrap-memory-api-caller-pass"></a>Hosted bootstrap memory API caller pass (no new EK or body/path/LOC credit): searched all declarations, definitions and callsites of `AllocateRO`, `AllocateRW`, `AllocateRAM32`, `AllocateRAM` and `SetRO`. <a id="cause-smp-duplicate-enqueue-ek10363"></a>ExecSMP `Cause()` same-node concurrent enqueue pass (EK10363 added; no body/path/LOC credit): traced the pre-lock `ln_Type` check and protected `ADDTAIL` in `rom/exec/cause.c:84-100` against `Disable()`'s per-CPU-only SMP semantics (`rom/exec/disable.c:44-58`). Two CPUs can both pass the check for one `struct Interrupt`; if the second obtains the per-priority list lock before dispatch removes the first insertion, it appends the same node without rechecking. `ADDTAIL` then sets the node's predecessor to itself and its successor to itself (`compiler/include/exec/lists.h:122-134`). `SoftIntDispatch()` calls `RemHead()` while holding the list lock but invokes the node after unlocking (`cause.c:168-194`); on this self-linked head, `rom/exec/remhead.c:58-68` sets `lh_Head` to the same node again, so the dispatcher can repeatedly invoke the callback and cannot drain later nodes at that priority. Added EK10363 to the detailed report and master index. This is a public-API race requiring concurrent Cause calls on the same object; no selected in-tree caller pairing was established in this pass. Existing Exec body and LOC credit stand; no path or LOC increment. No concurrent Cause call, interrupt, callback, build or runtime operation was exercised; source-only.
