EK9071 signed semaphore-counter threshold and common-target recheck (2026-11-01; existing finding retained and scope clarified; no new ID or body/LOC credit): rechecked `WORD` as `signed AROS_16BIT_TYPE` (`compiler/include/exec/types.h:58-62`) and `ss_NestCount`/`ss_QueueCount` as `WORD` (`compiler/include/exec/semaphores.h:50-58`). In the common Exec implementation selected in `rom/exec/mmakefile.src:15-29,40`, an initially free semaphore starts at queue count -1; 65,536 successful nested same-owner acquisitions return both 16-bit counter representations to -1/0 while `ss_Owner` is still set. The next competing obtain or attempt sees the -1-to-0 free transition and replaces the owner (`rom/exec/semaphores.c:86-113,182-195`). Separately, an exclusive owner at queue count zero plus 32,769 queued task/message requests reaches -32767 on the usual two’s-complement 16-bit target; the owner's release decrements to -32768, fails the `>= 0` test, sets the queue count to free, and leaves the nonempty wait list unreplied (`rom/exec/procure.c:68-107`; `rom/exec/releasesemaphore.c:83-114,188-196`). These are source-derived extreme-count conditions; no workload or semaphore operation was run. No architecture-specific replacement for these common semaphore paths was found in the checked Exec manifests. Existing bodies and finding credit stand; no new path/LOC credit.

VMM's `PrepageIOStdReq()` selects the quick path only when `From` is longword aligned; its destination is a fresh `AllocVec()` buffer, page I/O requests are initialized to `PAGESIZE` (`workbench/system/VMM/pageio.c:518,581`), and allocation-failure splits are rounded down to `PagingDevParams.block_size`, defined as a count of ULONGs (`find_dev_params.c:32`; `prepager.c:75-95,111-129`). P96 bitmap migration allocates the destination separately and rounds `bm->memsize` up to eight bytes before either direction's copy (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/p96gfx/p96gfx_bitmapclass.c:81,174-185,200-213`). EK10292 withdrawal reconciliation (2026-11-01; no file/LOC credit): rechecked the public `KrnGetCPUNumber()` and `KrnGetCPUAttr()` contracts and all checked-in callsites. `KrnGetCPUAttr()` takes a documented `0..KrnGetCPUCount()-1` index; `KrnGetCPUNumber()` promises the current CPU number but does not promise an index in that range. OpenSBI CPU inventory status/count cross-check (EK9070 retained; 2026-11-01): re-read the early `/cpus` walker, per-hart initializer, and selected RISC-V processor resource (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_fdt.c:114-123,177-189`; `platform_init.c:23-49`; `arch/riscv64-all/processor/processor_init.c:400-456`; `getcpuinfo.c:26-45`). <a id="task-stacksize-align-overflow-ek10364"></a>NewCreateTaskA stack-size alignment overflow review (EK10364 added; no new body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): verified `rom/exec/newcreatetaska.c` is selected by `rom/exec/mmakefile.src:36`; re-read its stack-tag alignment and minimum clamp, `NewAllocEntry()`'s exact allocation length, and x86-64's `AROS_WORSTALIGN=16`/`AROS_STACKSIZE=40960` definitions (`arch/x86_64-all/include/aros/cpu.h:50,170,176`). With 32-bit unsigned `ULONG`, `0xfffffff1 + 15` wraps to zero, then the minimum clamp replaces it with 40,960; the allocator and task setup accept that smaller stack. Added EK10364 with the absent near-limit in-tree caller and conditional task-stack-use consequence qualified. Existing body/path credit for these sources remains unchanged. No allocation, task, build or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only.


EK10364 architecture-scope reconciliation (2026-11-01; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): inspected the checked-in architecture `cpu.h` definitions of `AROS_WORSTALIGN`: m68k uses 4; the legacy `ppc-morphos` header uses 8 but no AROS target selection was found; ARM/ARMeb, i386, x86-64, AArch64, PowerPC, and RISC-V use 16 (`arch/m68k-all/include/aros/cpu.h:26`; `arch/ppc-morphos/include/aros/cpu.h:25`; the selected architecture headers each define 16). Each value is a power of two and the shared `AROS_ALIGN(x)` adds `alignment - 1` before masking. On 32-bit `ULONG`, `0xfffffffd`, `0xfffffff9`, and `0xfffffff1` respectively round to zero. The m68k branch then clamps to 4,096 bytes; other architectures clamp to `AROS_STACKSIZE`. Updated EK10364's affected-configuration text and master-index summary to include the maintained 4- and 16-byte variants while excluding the unselected 8-byte header. Exact stack-use consequences remain conditional and no near-limit caller was found. No build or task was run; source-only.

<a id="ek10366-m68k-creatiorequest-shadow-rollback"></a>m68k Intuition lock-return thunk rollback sweep (EK10366 expanded; no new ID or path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): checked `thunk_intuition_LockPubScreen()` and `thunk_intuition_ObtainGIRPort()` (`m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:5578-5583,5641-5647`) against the present Screen/RastPort shadow layouts (`m68kemu_shadow_layouts.h:4618,4629`) and native lifetimes. `LockPubScreen()` increments/retains a public-screen visitor lock which must be released with `UnlockPubScreen()`; the thunk does not undo that lock when Screen shadow publication fails. `ObtainGIRPort()` clones a RastPort and, when it has a layer, locks that layer and updates shared backup context; `ReleaseGIRPort()` restores state, unlocks the layer and frees the clone (`rom/intuition/obtaingirport.c:55-104`; `releasegirport.c:46-75`). Failed shadow publication leaves those resources/locks live while returning zero to the guest. `GetScreenDrawInfo()` was excluded: this implementation returns the screen's embedded DInfo and `FreeScreenDrawInfo()` is a no-op. <a id="ek10367-gt-getimsg-shadow-failure"></a>m68k GadTools `GT_GetIMsg()` dequeue/shadow-failure pass (EK10367 added; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): traced the generated thunk (`m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:2769-2776`) through native `GT_GetIMsg()` (`workbench/libs/gadtools/gt_getimsg.c:27-28,57-74`) and its required `GT_ReplyIMsg()` path (`gt_replyimsg.c:25-45`). The native call removes UserPort messages with `GetMsg()` and returns only messages surviving `GT_FilterIMsg`; the thunk then returns NULL if `shadow_create_by_name()` cannot publish the returned `IntuiMessage`. It does not reply the already-dequeued message, so the guest cannot process or acknowledge it. The relevant `IntuiMessage` layout exists in `m68kemu_shadow_layouts.h`; the failure can arise from guest-heap exhaustion or the fixed shadow-registration cap already traced under EK10366. This is distinct from EK10366's leaks of native allocations/locks: this path loses a dequeued event and leaves its reply outstanding. No guest port, event, shadow allocation failure or build was exercised; source-only.

<a id="ek10368-gt-replyimsg-shadow-lifetime"></a>m68k GadTools reply-shadow lifetime pass (EK10368 added; EK10367 trigger strengthened; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): compared the generated `GT_GetIMsg()`/`GT_ReplyIMsg()` thunks (`m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:2769-2784`) with native reply/post-filter behavior (`workbench/libs/gadtools/gt_replyimsg.c:46-58`; `gt_postfilterimsg.c:52-83`) and generic Exec `ReplyMsg` shadow cleanup (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks.c:644-652`). `GT_GetIMsg()` adds a top-level IntuiMessage shadow; `GT_ReplyIMsg()` resolves it and calls the native reply routine, which frees or releases the GT wrapper, but the thunk never removes/frees the guest shadow. `shadow_create()` unconditionally allocates and registers another top-level mapping (`m68kemu_shadow.c:72-84`), while the context table is capped at 256 (`m68kemu_intern.h:92`). Therefore ordinary successful event cycles accumulate stale entries and guest heap blocks until later shadows fail. This supplies a normal-use route to EK10367's shadow-capacity trigger, with its exact limit dependent on other active shadows. No message loop or saturation was run; source-only.

<a id="ek10367-gt-getimsg-shadow-failure"></a>m68k GadTools `GT_PostFilterIMsg()` return-shadow failure follow-up (EK10367 expanded; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): traced the generated post-filter thunk (`m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:2821-2828`) through native `GT_PostFilterIMsg()` (`workbench/libs/gadtools/gt_postfilterimsg.c:52-90`). Native post-filtering restores/returns the original IntuiMessage and frees/releases the extended `GT_IntuiMessage`; only after that side effect does the thunk try to create the returned original-message shadow. On failure the guest receives NULL and has no output pointer to pass to ReplyMsg, leaving the original message unacknowledged. This is a second shadow-publication route to EK10367, distinct from `GT_GetIMsg()` dequeue-before-shadow. EK10368 remains the ordinary-use table-exhaustion route. No message or shadow failure was induced; source-only.

<a id="reset-timeout-callback-task-lifetime-ek8946"></a>## Reset timeout callback-task lifetime boundary (EK8946 restored and rechecked; 2026-11-01)

The callback can clear its shared pointer and begin teardown remotely after the launcher observes it; the task lock acquired by SetTaskPri cannot protect access before that first dereference. Kept this separate from EK873's late completion releasing a successor's wait, EK10252's overlapping reset-entry shared state, and EK10303's valid-task scheduler-list transition race. Affected builds are ExecSMP configurations (x86-64 PC and Raspberry Pi variants); no runtime path or LOC credit changes. `NewCreateTaskA()` immediate-start/early-exit return-lifetime candidate recheck (2026-11-01; no new EK or body/path/LOC credit): re-read the complete selected `NewAddTask()` launch path and its public-private contract (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:141-150,25-123,301-331`) against `NewCreateTaskA()`'s post-call use (`rom/exec/newcreatetaska.c:257-272`), the default finalizer (`rom/exec/prepareexecbase.c:51-56`), and `RemTask()`/service-task reclamation (`rom/exec/remtask.c:130-180`; `rom/exec/service.c:37-90`). A higher-priority task can run before `NewAddTask()` returns and can terminate; `NewCreateTaskA()` uses the return only as a success indicator and does not dereference the task after the call. A caller that retains the returned pointer across independent task termination needs a lifetime handshake; no API guarantee that the task remains live on return, nor a selected caller that dereferences the returned pointer after a termination race, was established. Do not promote the bare possibility of an already-dead returned task to a constructor defect. <a id="m68k-exec-getmsg-waitport-result-contract-ek9432-expanded-2026-11-01"></a>
## m68k Exec GetMsg and WaitPort result-contract recheck (EK9432 expanded; 2026-11-01; no new ID or body/path/LOC credit)

Compared both handwritten thunks in `rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks.c:609-653` with the public Exec prototypes and native implementations. `GetMsg()` returns generic `Message *` (`exec.conf:135`; `rom/exec/getmsg.c:40-55`), but the thunk casts every non-NULL result to `IntuiMessage *` and creates that larger shadow. A plain native Message on a native-backed guest port therefore receives the wrong guest type/layout, and shadow synchronization reads fields beyond the 48-byte native Message object (generic Message host size 48; IntuiMessage host size 96, descriptor ranges `m68kemu_shadow_layouts.h:2292-2308,2641-2652`; shadow field sync `m68kemu_shadow.c:72-84`). This is conditional on a generic Message being queued and returned; IntuiMessage is the intended case. `WaitPort()` is also declared to return the first generic Message without removing it (`exec.conf:137`; `rom/exec/waitport.c:40-57`), but its thunk returns the native pointer directly without creating or looking up a guest shadow. Guest code that consumes this documented result receives an untranslated/truncated host pointer; the usual pattern that ignores the return and follows with `GetMsg()` avoids this particular WaitPort result defect. Both are additional concrete instances of EK9432's guest/native API boundary. No in-tree emulated guest caller was established; no guest call, queue operation, or build was run. Existing generated and handwritten thunk bodies already have inventory credit; no path or LOC total changes.

<a id="riscv-legacy-isa-versioned-multiletter-feature-flags-ek10590-2026-11-01"></a>
## RISC-V legacy ISA versioned multi-letter feature-flag pass (EK10590; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01)

Re-read `ParseISA()`/`ExtensionFlags()` and traced a versioned multi-letter token through the public query path. For the legacy `riscv,isa` property, the parser retains the full original ISA string in `ParseCPUNode()`, but `ParseISA()` splits extension words at underscores and calls `ExtensionFlags()` with the entire token (`arch/riscv64-all/processor/processor_init.c:60-70,103-127,273-280`). The lookup table contains lowercase, unversioned names; consequently `Zba1p0`/`zba1p0` does not set `RVFEATB_ZBA`. `Processor_AnswerTag()` exposes that bit through `GCIT_SupportsZba` (`processor_util.c:80-82`), and ShowConfig queries both the ISA string and feature flag (`workbench/tools/ShowConfig/cpu_riscv.c:52-61,85-100`). The newer `riscv,isa-extensions` property takes a separate route and is not affected by this exact legacy-token issue. The RISC-V naming spec confirms case-insensitive ISA strings and extension version suffixes: [ISA Extension Naming Conventions](https://docs.riscv.org/reference/isa/v20260120/unpriv/naming.html). No in-tree firmware blob demonstrates the triggering spelling; scope is conditional on the documented accepted legacy form. Added EK10590 to the detailed report and index; no source body/path/LOC credit. No firmware tree, CPU query or build was used; source-only.

### Console-handler input-buffer and read-shift caller pass (2026-11-01; no new EK)

Reconciled the `process_input()`/`answer_read_request()` state transitions with the selected handler manifest (`rom/filesys/console_handler/mmakefile.src:4,21-23`) and the direct handler loop (`con_handler.c:1072-1104`). Paste and drag/drop insertion have separate capacity checks (`support.c:719-721,752-804`; `con_handler.c:770-810`). Read lengths are capped to buffered/can-read bytes before `answer_read_request()` (`support.c:1122-1135,1166-1189`), and the remaining-byte shift preserves the fixed array extent. That shift calls `CopyMem(inputbuffer + readlen, inputbuffer, inputsize - readlen)` with overlapping ranges when the unread suffix extends past the consumed prefix (`support.c:1129-1131`), despite Exec's CopyMem documentation stating that source and destination must not overlap (`rom/exec/copymem.c:28-38`). The selected implementation copies forward, which is safe for this particular higher-source-to-lower-destination move (`copymem.c:57-66,94-150`); the checked i386 SSE replacement delegates to the generic vector (`arch/i386-all/exec/copymem_SSE.S:49-54`). No current output corruption is established for those implementations, so this is recorded as a contract/portability concern rather than a new bug. The broader handler caller/state and architecture-implementation contracts remain open. Source-only; no DOS read, console input, or build was run.

<a id="console-shared-stream-stale-break-target-ek10594"></a>
Console shared-stream break-target lifetime pass (EK10594 added; 2026-11-01; no body/path/LOC credit): verified the distinct non-`ACTION_CHANGE_SIGNAL` path. The handler assigns `fh->breaktask` on FIND, READ, and WRITE packets, but ACTION_END does not clear it; Ctrl-C later signals the stored pointer. The boot console's `cis`/`cos` wrappers bind to the same handler state through OpenFromLock, and CreateNewProc accepts and retains a caller-supplied output handle; an explicitly buildable DOS test demonstrates sharing `Output()` with a child and disabling output close. A still-pending read from one task can therefore coexist with another shared-stream writer replacing the break target. Traced the child Process allocation through its `tc_MemEntry` list and Exec service-task reclamation, then through Signal's Task-field accesses. Added EK10594 for the conditional stale-target delivery/fault. This is separate from EK9345's out-of-order synchronous ACTION_CHANGE_SIGNAL restore race and EK699's `lastwritetask` completion dereference. No exact concurrent maintained caller sequence, process exit, Ctrl-C, or build was run; no source-body/path/LOC credit.

EK10594 pending-read interleaving caller recheck (no new ID or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): verified that the console handler can process another packet while the first task's read remains pending. `ACTION_READ` calls `con_read()` (`con_handler.c:1081-1090`); when no buffered input is available, `con_read()` appends that packet to `fh->pendingReads` and returns without replying (`support.c:1166-1189`). Device input is independently submitted through `SendIO()` by `startread()` (`con_handler.c:644-657`), so the packet loop can service later messages while that read waits. A later shared-stream `ACTION_WRITE` overwrites `fh->breaktask` with the writer task (`:1092-1102`); the checked `developer/debug/test/dos/clicreatenewproc.c:86-90` uses `NP_Output=Output()` and `NP_CloseOutput=FALSE`, so child completion does not close that shared output. Ctrl-C consumes the latest pointer through `Signal()` (`support.c:1069-1072`), while `ACTION_END` leaves it unchanged (`con_handler.c:1051-1068`). This confirms the stale-target ordering at the source level. Whether the child Task storage has already been reclaimed at signal time is still timing-dependent, so the report retains that qualification. No input, shared-stream process, signal, or build was run; source-only.

OpenSBI self-test signal-mask failure-path recheck (EK633 strengthened; no new ID or body/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): traced the two boot-task `AllocSignal(-1)` results through the selected Exec API and reconciled the FPU worker allocation with new-task initialization. `AllocSignal()` returns signed `BYTE` and returns -1 when no free bit remains (`rom/exec/allocsignal.c:45-68,89-96`); AROS `ULONG` and the Exec signal masks are 32-bit on this RV64 target (`compiler/include/exec/types.h:35-43`; `rom/exec/wait.c:24-30`; `rom/exec/signal.c:117-124`). The two boot-task `1UL << sigbit` expressions therefore shift a 64-bit value by a negative count on boot-task pool exhaustion, which is undefined in C. The FPU worker also shifts its result, but its fresh task receives `TaskSigAlloc=0xFFFF` in `NewAddTask()` and has free ordinary bits (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:249-251`; `prepareexecbase.c:319`), so that worker failure condition is not established. Under ordinary RV64 shift lowering, -1 becomes count 63, then assignment truncates the high bit to a zero `ULONG`; `Wait(0)` cannot observe a received bit and `Signal(..., 0)` cannot deliver one (`rom/exec/wait.c:75-80`; `rom/exec/signal.c:298-303`). Refined EK633 to state this concrete common-target failure mode without claiming defined C behavior. Separately confirmed both helpers return on `NewCreateTaskA()` failure without freeing their successfully allocated boot-task signal (`kernel_startup.c:146-151,205-210`). The checks occur after `InitCode(RTF_SINGLETASK/RTF_COLDSTART)`. A repository source search found no direct `AllocSignal()` use in the selected kernel/Exec/task startup trees before these helpers; generic `CreateMsgPort()` and reset-callback allocations have no direct caller in those selected startup trees. Ordinary boot-time exhaustion is therefore not established. The in-tree compound route for boot-task exhaustion is repeated bootarg substring matches plus repeated `NewCreateTaskA()` failures, which leak the boot-task bit until its 16 allocatable signals are consumed; this now bounds the practical trigger in EK633. The worker-side unchecked shift is not credited as an independently reachable failure. No signal exhaustion, task creation failure, self-test, or boot was induced; source-only.

# m68kemu display-driver notification callback caller trace (EK9894 expanded; 2026-11-01; no body/path/LOC credit)

Traced the generated `SetDisplayDriverCallback()` vector (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:3698-3705`): both callback and userdata are resolved with `THUNK_PTR()`, and the callback is stored unchanged by `rom/graphics/setdisplaydrivercallback.c:75-78`. The API contract says it is called using the C calling convention (`:29-49`). Graphics later calls the stored pointer directly on both display-driver removal and insertion (`rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:242-243,336-339`), with no m68k interpreter entry bridge or guest Hook conversion. Intuition itself installs `DisplayDriverNotify()` with its library base as userdata during initialization (`rom/intuition/intuition_init.c:300`; implementation `rom/intuition/monitorclass.c:50`). Thus an emulated guest using this private vector can replace the existing native notification callback; on a later driver event the native caller attempts to call the guest code address with the host C ABI. Added this selected Graphics caller path to EK9894, consolidating the same raw guest-callback/native-invocation root cause; no separate finding or source-body credit. The m68kemu module is optional and excluded from checked-in default package edges; no maintained emulated guest caller was found. No driver event, callback or build was run; source-only.

## DynModule RemoveModule reply-port result and Exec caller-contract recheck (EK8853 restored; 2026-11-01; no body/path/LOC credit)

Rechecked the existing `dynmodule_removemodule.c` candidate against the selected link-library recipe, public declaration, and Exec port APIs. `compiler/dynmodule/mmakefile.src:12-23` explicitly selects the implementation for `linklibs-dynmod`; its `core-linklibs` aggregate edge is commented. The public header declares `dynmoduleRemoveModule()` (`compiler/dynmodule/include/dynmodule.h:54`), but a repository-wide C/assembly caller search found no maintained in-tree call. Confirmed the success test is inverted: a non-NULL `CreateMsgPort()` result selects `DYNMODULE_Exit(0)` before `FindPort()`/`DMIFMSG_Dispose`, while allocation failure enters the request branch with `replyport == NULL`. If a module port exists, `GetMsg(NULL)` follows `PutMsg()`; Exec `GetMsg()` asserts/uses the supplied port and reads its message-list head (`rom/exec/getmsg.c:48-62`). `DeleteMsgPort(NULL)` is explicitly safe (`rom/exec/deletemsgport.c:24-33,47-56`), so that call is not cited as a fault. Restored EK8853 into the detailed Exec/Kernel report and master index; external callers remain the only established reachability. No module, port, allocation failure, or build was exercised; source-only.

Checked the direct `WaitPort()` callers in `workbench/c/Copy.c`, `GfxControl.c`, `ConClip.c`, and `Decoration/decoration.c` against port ownership and message completion. `Copy` waits on its own process startup port and immediately replies to the dequeued startup message (`Copy.c:568-576`). Sam440 kernel archspecific object-selection and boot-edge reconciliation (no new EK or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): traced `rom/kernel/mmakefile.src`'s `build_module(... archspecific=yes)` through `config/make.tmpl`'s generated module object selection (`:2260-2273,2408-2412,2500-2525`) and `build_archspecific` (`:3273-3312`), then reconciled the selected `arch/ppc-sam440/kernel/mmakefile.src` object list. No new defect or full-body/path/LOC credit; no build or image was generated. Source-only.

## OpenSBI long MICROHZ deadline conversion candidate withdrawn (2026-11-02; no EK or body/LOC credit)

The arithmetic overflow is real in `ticks.c:25-28,84-98`, but it is not reachable for a long user request in the selected OpenSBI configuration: `arch/riscv64-opensbi/timer/make.opts:2` enables `USE_VBLANK_EMU`; `timer_init.c:76-84` queues a recurring 20 ms request before device requests; `rom/timer/lowlevel.c:43-62,286-318` keeps requests sorted and requeues the internal request at the next VBlank deadline; and `Timer0Setup()` converts only the MICROHZ head (`ticks.c:83-97`). <a id="i386-pc-rdtsc-cpu-floor-ek8848"></a>
i386-PC RDTSC support-floor and dispatch trace (EK8848 restored to the detailed report/index; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): reconciled the existing ledger references to the missing finding. The explicit `pc-i386` compiler configuration uses `-march=i486` (`configure.in:1364-1382,1436-1448`); its selected `cpu_Dispatch()` writes `iet_private1` with raw `RDTSC()` for every dispatched task (`arch/i386-pc/kernel/kernel_cpu.c:25-72`), and the shared helper and timestamp vector add no CPUID TSC check (`arch/all-pc/kernel/kernel_arch.h:175-185`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/timestamp.c:14-20`). `KrnDispatch` is the startup/user-mode task dispatch route and `SC_SWITCH` reaches the same dispatcher (`rom/kernel/dispatch.c:17-40`; `rom/kernel/kernel_intr.c:74-80`). The PC interrupt-controller initializer falls back to 8259A when APIC probing returns no APIC (`arch/all-pc/kernel/apic.c:21-31`; `ictl.c:95-134`), so APIC presence is not established as a necessary TSC proxy. Intel's SDM states RDTSC was introduced with Pentium ([Intel SDM, Vol. 2B](https://www.intel.com/content/dam/www/public/us/en/documents/manuals/64-ia-32-architectures-software-developer-vol-2b-manual.pdf)); its CPUID documentation confirms later Intel486 models may expose CPUID ([Intel SDM, Vol. 2B](https://www.intel.com/content/dam/www/public/us/en/documents/manuals/64-ia-32-architectures-software-developer-vol-2b-manual.pdf)). Restored EK8848 with runtime hardware support qualified: the compiler baseline is evidence, not proof of the documented minimum system. No body/path/LOC credit changed. No CPU, dispatch, clock read, or build was run; source-only.

WaitX EK372 architecture timer-backend closure (2026-11-02; no new EK or body/path/LOC credit): traced `UNIT_WAITUNTIL` through the m68k-Amiga and Efika overrides, in addition to the generic implementation. m68k's selected timer manifest includes local `beginio.c`/`lowlevel.c` and its Amiga boot device list selects timer.device; its BeginIO queues future waits through `timer_addToWaitList()` and its interrupt removes then `ReplyMsg()`s expired requests (`arch/m68k-amiga/timer/mmakefile.src:4-9`; `beginio.c:105-119,192-246`; `lowlevel.c:214-221,275-286`; `arch/m68k-amiga/boot/mmakefile.src:154-159`). Efika's architecture module substitutes its timer sources and its Efika package selects timer.device; its future WAITUNTIL path likewise inserts the request into `TL_WAITVBL`, and completion removes and replies it (`arch/ppc-chrp/efika/timer/mmakefile.src:1-10`; `beginio.c:121-141,196-230`; `lowlevel.c:89-104`; boot package `:71-79`). In both backends, `ReplyMsg()` leaves the node on the reply port, while the next `WaitX` loop iteration calls `SendIO()` and the timer list insertion does not dequeue that old reply. Expanded EK372's affected-configuration wording and master-index summary from generic-only to generic plus these two confirmed architecture overrides. Existing WaitX, timer and SendIO bodies already have full-body credit. No timer request or list operation was run; source-only.

<a id="security-server-quit-packet-lifetime-caller-census-2026-11-02"></a>
## Security server quit-packet lifetime and maintained-caller census (no new EK or coverage credit; 2026-11-02)

Re-read the complete `rom/security/security_server.c` packet-send and server-loop bodies (`:33-76,471-649`) with `security_server.h` and the after-DOS startup caller (`security_afterdos.c:34-72`). A `SendServerPacket()` stack packet remains live until its exact reply is dequeued; after a quit packet, the server stops dispatching, replies to that packet, clears `ServerPort` under `Forbid()`, drains and replies to every packet already queued, then frees the ports and signals. A repository-wide C/header census finds no producer of `secSAction_Quit` outside the server's own case and no caller of the packet vector that requests quit. Thus the queue-drain path's behavior for a maintained quit sender is not established, and no dangling stack-packet or missed-reply defect is promoted. `ServerPort`/`secSPacket` are private implementation interfaces; external code reaching them is outside this in-tree caller check. No shutdown packet, concurrent request, server teardown or build was run; source-only. Existing body/path credit and coverage totals are unchanged.


<a id="remtask-exec-test-caller-census-ek473-2026-11-02"></a>
## RemTask optional Exec-test caller census (EK473 expanded; 2026-11-02; no default-denominator credit)

Read all three explicit caller bodies: `developer/debug/test/exec/tasktest.c` (74 `cloc 2.06` C lines), `tasktest2.c` (79), and `messagetest.c` (95). The manifest places `tasktest` and `messagetest` in `test-exec-public` and `tasktest2` in `test-exec-private` (`mmakefile.src:18-38,84-90`); their parent test aggregate is disabled by default. The first two signal the worker ten times although it waits nine times, then the worker enters a 10,000-iteration loop; the parent calls `RemTask()` and immediately frees the TCB/stack without waiting for completion. `messagetest` removes after a worker signal but has no handshake proving the worker reached its following `Wait(0)`. This gives EK473 additional explicit test-target caller paths when an ExecSMP worker is running remotely; the schedule remains conditional, and the code is not selected into the default image. No new root cause, finding ID, or default inventory/LOC credit is added. No test was run; source-only.


m68kemu Intuition SetPointer cursor-data byte-order trace (EK9432 expanded; no path/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): checked generated thunk `thunk_intuition_SetPointer()` (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:5265-5275`) against the public declaration, native SetPointer/MakePointerFromData/PointerClass route, and `AllocSpriteDataA()` old-format branch. The guest `const UWORD *` is mapped to raw arena memory; no per-word conversion occurs in the thunk. `AllocSpriteDataA()` loads native `UWORD`s, applies `AROS_WORD2BE()`, and writes planar words, while selected `BitMapScale()` reads plane bytes in left-to-right MSB-first order. On little-endian hosts an asymmetric guest row such as bytes `80 01` becomes `01 80`, rearranging its pixels within the row. BCM2837 AArch64 per-core generic-timer initialization ordering recheck (no EK or body/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): checked whether `bcm27xx_init_cntp_timer()`'s unsynchronized lazy write to shared `bcm27xx_cntp_interval` races across cores (`arch/aarch64-native/kernel/platform_bcm27xx.c:140-161`). For the selected SMP startup, `platform_PostInit()` calls the platform's `ARMI_Init` before its boot-core `ARMI_InitTimerCore` call (`platform_init.c:104-117`). BCM27xx `ARMI_Init` iterates secondary IDs serially, takes `startup_lock`, wakes one core and waits for `cpu_Register()` to release that lock before continuing to the next (`platform_bcm27xx.c:302-312,347-428`). Each secondary arms its own timer only after bootstrap task setup and before releasing the lock (`kernel_cpu.c:178-192`). Therefore the first timer callback initializes the shared interval before later secondary callbacks, and the boot core initializes after secondary startup completes. No selected concurrent first-write path established; no finding added. Other entry paths that bypass this startup sequence and hardware timer behavior remain unverified. OpenSBI FDT memory-tuple arithmetic recheck (EK769/EK772/EK10356 reconciled; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): reread `krnParseFDT()` from header parsing through memory `reg` tuple handling (`kernel_fdt.c:62-171`) against `kernel_cstart()` fallback ordering (`kernel_startup.c:515-568`). OpenSBI `dumpdt` deep-node cell-count recheck (EK10601 added; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): traced `krnDumpFDT()`'s depth-indexed `ac[]`/`sc[]` state and `reg` formatter (`kernel_fdt.c:300-422`) through the `dumpdt` bootargs caller (`kernel_startup.c:637-644`). At depth 24, `d` clamps to 23 and the `reg` branch reads parent counts from slot 22 instead of the depth-23 parent slot 23; a sufficiently deep node can therefore be rendered with the wrong address/size cell split. The FDT tree encoding imposes no 24-level cap (Devicetree Specification 5.4.2: https://devicetree-specification.readthedocs.io/en/stable/flattened-format.html#tree-structure). Added EK10601 as a diagnostic-only formatting defect, separate from malformed-blob parse bounds. No DTB was generated or dumped and no boot was run; source-only.


m68kemu IFFParse pointer-return round-trip recheck (EK9432 strengthened; 2026-11-02; no new ID or body/path/LOC credit): enumerated the pointer-returning signatures in `workbench/libs/iffparse/iffparse.conf:17-18,38-47` and matched them to the generated wrappers at `rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:4634-4638,4815-4867,4888-4897,4943-4948`. `AllocIFF`, property/collection/context/local-item lookup and data access, `AllocLocalItem`, and `OpenClipboard` return raw native pointers; their paired argument thunks resolve only guest-arena addresses or registered shadows (`m68kemu_thunks.h:37`; `m68kemu_intern.h:114-125`). The `AllocFileRequest()` implementation delegates to native `AllocAslRequest()` (`workbench/libs/asl/allocfilerequest.c:48`), and `AllocAslRequest()` allocates its public request and private state with native `AllocVec()` (`workbench/libs/asl/allocaslrequest.c:74-146`). m68kemu Graphics `FindDisplayInfo()` handle return recheck (EK9432 expanded; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): matched generated vector -726 (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:3812-3817`) to the `DisplayInfoHandle` pointer contract (`graphics.conf:163`; `compiler/include/graphics/displayinfo.h:28`) and confirmed `FindDisplayInfo()` returns a pointer into `mdd->modes` (`rom/graphics/finddisplayinfo.c:55-80`). m68kemu DataTypes `FindToolNodeA()` marshalling recheck (EK9432 expanded; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): traced generated LVO -246 (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:810-815`) to the public signature and native method. Both the guest `List *` and `TagItem *` are passed through `THUNK_PTR()` with no structure conversion; native `FindToolNodeA()` reads TOOLA tags via `GetTagData()` and walks list links/ToolNode fields (`workbench/libs/datatypes/findtoolnodea.c:73-105`). The returned native ToolNode pointer also has no guest mapping. m68kemu DOS `SetArgStr()` return-pointer reconciliation (EK9432 detailed report/index sync; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): re-read `GetArgStr()`/`SetArgStr()` implementations (`rom/dos/getargstr.c:47-54`; `setargstr.c:25-33,50-56`) and generated wrappers (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:1349-1359`). `GetArgStr()` returns native `Process.pr_Arguments`; `SetArgStr()` maps the guest input string to native arena memory, installs it, then returns the previous native argument pointer. m68k Amiga EK9453 producer-scope recheck (2026-11-02; existing finding refined; no body/path/LOC credit): traced both producers of `bootmsgptr` through the boot-memory ownership path. Ordinary `exec_boot()` initializes a local four-entry `bootmsg[]`, publishes its address into `PlatformData.BootMsg`, then switches off that temporary stack before attempting relocation (`arch/m68k-amiga/boot/start.c:674-682,176-234`). AROSBootstrap instead points `BootS->kerneltags` at `BootMemHeader.ktags` and its command string at `BootMemHeader.kcmd`; `initDataPool()` allocates the containing pool and adds it as an `NT_MEMORY` entry before loading/transferring to the ROM (`arch/m68k-amiga/c/AROSBootstrap.c:45-70,424-450,1350-1373,1467-1490`; `start.c:736`). The boot path builds a MemHeader for that memory, and `TypeOfMem()` checks address membership in a MemHeader (`start.c:344-364`; `rom/exec/typeofmem.c:48-54`), so AROSBootstrap's tag list is not expected to enter the unmanaged-stack relocation branch. Tightened EK9453's affected-path wording to ordinary stack-tag startup or another genuinely unmanaged list; the allocation-failure behavior remains confirmed. No reset or allocation failure was induced; source-only.


x86-64 AVX-512 wording versus enabled task state (no new EK; 2026-11-02): followed the apparent `AVX512` references in the selected x86-64 PC scheduler through the common x86-64 context initializer and per-CPU setup. Both set XCR0 only to bits 0–2 (x87/SSE/YMM), and task `XSAVE`/`XRSTOR` use the same `0b111` mask (`arch/x86_64-all/kernel/cpu_init.c:57-91`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/smp_exec.c:65-90`; `arch/x86_64-all/kernel/createcontext.c:34-47,78-84`; `arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/kernel_cpu.c:131-139,254-264`). The support query exposes AVX but no AVX-512 capability (`arch/all-pc/processor/getcpuinfo.c:222-227`). Thus AVX-512 state is not enabled for selected tasks, and the comment alone does not establish a missing context-save defect. The context sizing remains based on CPUID leaf D after enabling those same XCR0 bits. Hardware feature behavior and actual XSAVE execution were not tested; no body/path/LOC credit. Source-only.


CopyMemQuick ATA DMA bounce-buffer caller follow-up (no new EK or LOC credit; 2026-11-02): traced the selected ATA read/write request path through `cmd_Read32`/`cmd_Read64` and the high-address DMA bounce branch in `ata_exec_blk()` (`rom/devs/ata/ata.c:63-164,179-287`; `rom/devs/ata/lowlevel.c:1188-1245`). Sector-offset and length checks make the copy byte count a sector multiple, satisfying CopyMemQuick's multiple-of-ULONG size requirement. The bounce copy still forwards the caller-owned buffer without checking ULONG alignment; `SCSICmd.scsi_Data` is typed `UWORD *`, and the trackdisk I/O request uses generic `APTR` (`compiler/include/devices/scsidisk.h:21-30`; `exec/io.h:28-45`). The branch is reached only for a DMA request whose buffer range exceeds 32-bit address space; the checked-in selected x86-64 PC target provides the >32-bit case and uses the generic C CopyMemQuick body, while maintained 32-bit m68k targets cannot enter this address-range branch. No checked-in caller deliberately supplying a 2-mod-4 buffer was found, and the selected x86-64 implementation's concrete behavior for such a pointer was not established as an observable failure. Keep the generic caller/configuration census open; this source pass does not add an ATA finding or close the public alignment contract. No I/O, DMA, or build was run; source-only.


ReadArgs `/M` CopyMemQuick growth-path caller recheck (no new EK or LOC credit; 2026-11-02): traced all three variable-size `CopyMemQuick()` calls in `ReadArgs()` (`rom/dos/readargs.c:668-683,762-784,820-835`) against the public alignment, size and non-overlap contract (`rom/exec/copymemquick.c:24-43`). Each old and replacement vector is `STRPTR` storage allocated by `AllocVec()`; the requested copy size is `multnum * sizeof(char *)`, which is a multiple of `sizeof(ULONG)` on selected 32- and 64-bit targets. The replacement is a distinct allocation and the old vector is freed only after the copy. Initial growth can issue a zero-byte copy from the zero-initialized NULL vector; the selected generic body returns without dereferencing it, consistent with the documented zero-size allowance. No separate contract violation established for these three callers. This is a targeted caller slice; the wider CopyMemQuick census and EK8990's large-size API condition remain open. No argument parse or build was run; source-only.


TLSF realloc CopyMemQuick caller recheck (no new EK or LOC credit; 2026-11-02): traced the selected allocator's moving-reallocation branch (`rom/kernel/tlsf.c:869-978`) against the generic CopyMemQuick contract. TLSF rounds `new_size` to `AROS_WORSTALIGN`, and allocated payload addresses follow aligned block/header offsets (`:47-48,563-590,969-974`); `GET_SIZE(b)` masks flags from a block size maintained by the same aligned allocator (`:215-227`). The move branch is reached only when the adjacent block cannot extend the old allocation; the old block remains marked busy while `tlsf_malloc()` searches the free list for a distinct replacement, so the source and destination do not overlap. The copy length is the old payload size and therefore a multiple of ULONG on supported targets. This closes only the TLSF realloc copy call; the wider CopyMemQuick caller/configuration census and EK8990 remain open. No realloc or allocation was run; source-only.

SFS cache `CopyMemQuick()` caller pass (no new EK or LOC credit; 2026-11-02): completed the SFS `cachedio.c` direct-call slice, including the read-cache hit at `:790` missed by the prior inventory. The two `validateiocache()` copies (`:445,461`) use 16-byte-aligned cache data pointers (`:164-190`) and block-index offsets. The read-cache path checks the caller buffer's ULONG alignment before choosing the quick copy and advances that buffer only by copied block lengths; the write-through path checks its base caller buffer before deriving `src`, and cache destinations are 16-byte aligned. `changegeometry()` derives `shifts_block` from `bytes_sector * de_SectorPerBlock` (`deviceio.c:261-279`); for supported SFS block sizes (at least four bytes), these shifted block offsets and transfer lengths preserve ULONG alignment. Geometry is supplied from the DOS environment and this review did not establish validation of arbitrary malformed values, so the conclusion is limited to supported geometry; the wider CopyMemQuick caller/configuration census and EK8990 remain open. No filesystem operation or build was run; source-only.

SFS direct-caller `CopyMemQuick()` audit (FS-082 added to filesystem report; no EK or LOC credit; 2026-11-02): extended the SFS `cachedio.c` caller slice to `deviceio.c` and the `ACTION_READ` path. `transfer()` selects its bounce path when the request buffer violates `de_Mask`; `Mount.InitParams()` defaults that mask to `0xfffffffe`, so odd caller buffers reach `transfer_buffered()`. Its read and write branches use the original caller buffer in `CopyMemQuick()` without the alignment fallback that the cached-read path uses. The selected m68k implementation performs `move.l` through the pointer, establishing an address-error path for odd buffers on 68000-class CPUs. Recorded as FS-082 because the defect is in SFS; this cross-ledger caller trace does not close the wider Exec primitive census or EK8990. No I/O or build was run; source-only.

Task.resource `SaveTaskStorage()` CopyMemQuick caller closure (no new EK or LOC credit; 2026-11-02): traced `SaveTaskStorage()` (`rom/task/SaveTaskStorage.c:52-66`) through `SetTaskStorageSlot()` and the slot-array reallocation path (`rom/task/SetTaskStorageSlot.c:70-103`). The task slot array is `IPTR` storage from `AllocMem()`; the saved copy uses a separate `MEMF_PRIVATE` allocation sized `slots * sizeof(IPTR)`. That length is a multiple of ULONG on supported pointer widths, and both pointers are allocator-aligned, so this call satisfies the generic quick-copy alignment, size and non-overlap contract. This does not change EK10325, which remains a DEBUG-only undeclared `size` identifier in the diagnostic statement. No task storage was saved, allocation failure induced, or build run; source-only.

RISC-V Shell `NewStackSwap()` alignment caller recheck (EK8962 strengthened; no new ID or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): traced the selected Shell `Stack` command's `/N` size update (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Stack.c:69-82`) through `Shell.c:514-555`, `CLI_DEFAULTSTACK_UNIT = sizeof(IPTR)` (`compiler/include/dos/dosextens.h:266-268`), and DOS `RunCommand()`'s minimum clamp and direct upper-bound assignment (`rom/dos/runcommand.c:127-141,166`). `Stack 40961` becomes 40,964 bytes on RV32 and 40,968 on RV64; both exceed `AROS_STACKSIZE` 40,960. The 16-byte `MEMCHUNK_TOTAL`/`AROS_WORSTALIGN` allocator alignment plus those extents yields top pointers 4 or 8 modulo 16. Both RISC-V32/RV64 `NewStackSwap()` implementations set `sp` from that pointer and call `Enable()` and the function entry without alignment correction (`arch/riscv-all/exec/newstackswap.c:28,52-81`; `arch/riscv64-all/exec/newstackswap.c:28,52-81`). The standard RISC-V psABI requires 16-byte alignment at procedure entry and throughout standard-ABI execution ([§2.1](https://docs.riscv.org/reference/abi/v1.0/riscv-cc-procedure-calling-convention.html)); this confirms the violated boundary. This strengthens EK8962's ABI-misalignment cause. Scope is explicit Shell builds: `kernel-shell` and `kernel-shellcommands` are commented out in the RISC-V native and OpenSBI boot manifests, so no default RISC-V boot caller is claimed. The source and selected pthread cases are already credited; no body/path/LOC total changed. No stack command, swap, build, or runtime operation was run; source-only.


PPC Efika Shell `NewStackSwap()` alignment caller recheck (EK8962 strengthened; no new ID or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): followed the selected `AROS-chrp-ppc-efika` target through `workbench-complete` to `workbench-c` and the Shell/command set manifests (`arch/ppc-chrp/efika/boot/mmakefile.src`, `workbench/mmakefile.src`, `workbench/c/Shell/mmakefile.src`). PPC's four-byte `CLI_DEFAULTSTACK_UNIT` rounds `Stack 40961` to 40,964 bytes; DOS clamps only values below the 40,960-byte minimum and sets the stack pointer to allocation base plus this size (`rom/dos/runcommand.c:127-141`). With 16-byte allocator alignment, the upper bound is four modulo 16. PPC `NewStackSwap()` subtracts 16 bytes then copies the caller's ABI-framed stack before `StackSwap()` (`arch/ppc-all/exec/newstackswap.c:39-54`); PPC ABI frame sizing preserves the 16-byte remainder, leaving the replacement stack misaligned at the call. This extends EK8962 to a selected Efika workbench configuration. No command, stack switch, build or runtime operation was run; no body/path/LOC credit changed.


m68k Amiga `SetPatch.fastvbr()` CopyMemQuick caller trace (no new EK or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): traced `Supervisor(getvbr)` through the 68010+ VBR register read and the `fastvbr()` relocation branch (`arch/m68k-amiga/c/SetPatch.c:28-42,101-118`). VBR zero is a valid vector-table base, not a failed-read sentinel; the `if (!oldvbr)` branch allocates 1 KiB of cleared FAST memory and intentionally copies the original table from physical address zero before switching VBR. The source is 1 KiB aligned by architectural VBR semantics, the destination is `AllocMem()` storage, and the size is a multiple of ULONG. Thus the apparent NULL-source copy is intentional and satisfies this helper's extent/alignment requirements; allocation failure returns before the copy. No VBR, memory allocation, or build was exercised; source-only.

MinGW CPU-context `CopyMemQuick()` save/restore continuation pass (no new EK or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): traced the selected `SAVEREGS`/`RESTOREREGS` and `COPY_FPU` macros through `cpu_Switch()`, `cpu_Dispatch()`, `cpu_Exception()`, and `AROS_EXCEPTION_RESUME` (`arch/all-mingw32/kernel/{cpu_i386.h,cpu_x86_64.h,kernel_cpu.c,kernel_intr.c}`). The Win32 floating-save structure extent is composed of ULONG fields plus its 80-byte register array and is a multiple of four; extended state is 512 bytes; Win64 save/home/vector structures are fixed ULONG/IPTR multiples. `COPY_FPU()` allocates within `ContextSave[kb_ContextSize]`, places the FX area after rounding its address to 16 bytes, and `arch/i386-all/kernel/cpu_init.c` includes the legacy FPU extent, 512-byte FX area and 15-byte alignment slack in `kb_ContextSize`; i386 context construction uses the same layout. `cpu_Exception()` keeps the local context buffer alive through `core_raise(AROS_EXCEPTION_RESUME, ContextSave)`, whose trap handler restores it before the exception frame unwinds. The configured MinGW ARM CPU backend is not build-complete (EK10203), so no ARM alignment-sensitive selected configuration is claimed. This pass establishes valid extents and lifetime, but not exact compiler placement of the byte-typed local context buffer; x86/x64 scalar transfers are alignment-tolerant and no concrete failure was established. No context switch, exception, host process, or build was run; source-only.


MinGW host IRQ wait-set caller scope recheck (EK10175; no new finding or body/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): traced the socket IRQ allocation through `bsdsocket_Init()` and the native DLL's static `struct SocketController ctl`. The library init hook calls `sock_init()` once per library initialization under `Forbid()` (`arch/all-mingw32/bsdsocket/bsdsocket_init.c:32-66`); sockets do not allocate additional host IRQs. Thus the checked-in socket client contributes two IRQs per successful library initialization, not two per socket, and the current direct caller census remains three WingDI, two bsdsocket, and one emul.handler IRQ, in addition to the two static timer objects. Existing Network findings N12 and N13 cover the separate socket-init IRQ and Winsock failure leaks; N14 covers shutdown ordering. No checked-in path to the Windows 64-object wait-set limit was established, so EK10175 remains scoped to external/future callers that grow the host IRQ set past that API limit. No library initialization or wait failure was exercised; source-only.

Amiga-m68k KOBJ end-marker wildcard re-audit (EK555 restored; 2026-11-02; no body/path/LOC credit): re-read `arch/m68k-amiga/boot/kobj-romtag.ld:28-37`, `config/make.tmpl:2609,2763`, `tools/genmodule/writeend.c:21-30`, `arch/m68k-amiga/boot/mmakefile.src:225-264`, and `rom/kernel/kernel_romtags.c:263-278`. The earlier `*(.text .text.* .stub)` pattern matches `.text.moduleend` and consumes that input before the later dedicated rule; the KOBJ output then folds `.rodata` after it into `.text`. `rt_EndSkip` therefore points before folded module read-only data, and the scanner resumes there instead of skipping that data. Restored EK555 and its AROS.md entry with the certain extra-scan effect; a false Resident requires a matching record in module data and remains unobserved. This supersedes the 2026-10-30 withdrawal note, which overlooked the wildcard match. No link, ROM image, scan, or boot was produced; source-only.

Amiga-m68k EK9453 consumer null-safety recheck (2026-11-02; no new finding or source/path/LOC credit): read `LibFindTagItem`/`LibGetTagData`/`LibNextTagItem` and the selected consumers in `rom/bootloader/bootloader_init.c:119`, `rom/debug/debug_init.c:48-52`, `rom/exec/alertstrings.c:559-568`, and `arch/m68k-amiga/boot/mmu.c:196-208`. The tag helpers accept a null list and return no match; bootloader initialization consequently skips boot tags, debug initialization gets no module list, and MMU command parsing uses its default. This supports EK9453's scope as conditional loss of boot metadata/configuration after `AllocMem` failure, not an established crash or failed boot. The next cold startup republishes the producer's tag pointer as already recorded in EK9453. No allocation failure, boot, or reset was induced; source-only.

`KrnSetProtection()` target-selection matrix recheck (2026-11-02; no new candidate or LOC credit): repository-wide source/manifest search found five local architecture implementations (`arch/all-unix`, `all-mingw32`, `arm-native`, `m68k-all`, `x86_64-pc`) plus the generic stub. Relative-base task-slot publication failure (EK10602; 2026-11-02; no file/LOC credit): re-read the complete `compiler/startup/relbases.c` allocation and wrapper path against `SetTaskStorageSlot()`'s `FALSE` returns and all direct/generated relative-base callers (`rom/task/SetTaskStorageSlot.c:70-108`; `tools/genmodule/writegetlibbase.c:42-54`; `tools/genmodule/writeincproto.c:87-104`). When the table allocation succeeds but publishing it into task storage fails, `__aros_getoffsettable()` still opens PosixC and returns the unpublished table. <a id="ek473-intuition-failure-startup-callers"></a> EK473 Intuition worker-start failure caller recheck (EK473 expanded; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): corrected the prior assumption that `Wait(0)` had completed before the parent’s `RemTask()`. NewCreateTask affinity inherits the creator’s mask (`rom/exec/exec_util.c:129-164`), so when a caller eligible on multiple CPUs launches the worker under ExecSMP, the parent can resume on another CPU and remove the still-running child before its `Wait(0)`. Expanded EK473 with this maintained caller; no independent root cause or LOC credit. This is not an EK830 duplicate-cleanup path because only the parent calls RemTask. No allocation failure, task removal or interleaving was run; source-only.


<a id="ek473-ahi-and-network-caller-recheck"></a> EK473 optional caller and network-driver RemTask recheck (2026-11-02; no new root cause or body/LOC credit): searched checked-in C/header/assembly sources for direct `RemTask()` references and traced the optional hosted SDL HIDD expunge path plus the eight network-driver `DeleteUnit()` cleanup paths that call it. SDL publishes its task after a readiness signal; a later input/display initialization failure reaches expunge, which removes the event worker without a stop/join handshake (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/event.c:118-155`; `startup.c:275-307`). Its stack-backed VBlank server remains the independent Graphics/Desktop GD2620. For Atheros5000, Broadcom4400, EtherLink3, IntelPro100, NvidiaNet, Prism2, Realtek8180 and Rhine, `DeleteUnit()` is called only on `CreateUnit()` failure, and `UNITF_TASKADDED` is set only when `AddUnitTask()`/`NewAddTask()` succeeds; after successful task addition, no later operation in these creation paths sets `success` false. Thus these cleanup calls do not remove a successfully started worker on the checked creation paths. Also traced AHIRecord's optional level-meter process: its parent signals Ctrl-C, polls the task pointer for up to 50,000 delay ticks, then force-calls `RemTask()` if the pointer remains set (`workbench/tools/AHIRecord/AHIRecord.c:2179-2192`); the worker clears the pointer only at the end of its shutdown path (`:2644-2658`). A worker still executing remotely when the fallback expires is another conditional EK473 caller; no timeout or schedule was observed. No device, startup failure, task schedule, or build was exercised; source-only.

Exec WaitIO/ReplyMsg publication and shared-port recheck (EK8799/EK9883 retained; 2026-11-02; no new finding or LOC credit): reread `WaitIO()`, `ReplyMsg()`, `InternalPutMsg()`, `Remove()`, and `AddTail()`, then traced both maintained caller shapes. The VBlank timer removes an expired request from its timer queue before it calls `ReplyMsg()` (`rom/timer/lowlevel.c:354-379`); `ReplyMsg()` changes the node type before entering the reply-port insertion path, and `WaitIO()` checks that type without joining the in-progress publication. This confirms the narrow early-completion/lifetime window in EK8799. `Remove()` does not clear the node's predecessor/successor fields, but the selected timer path alone does not establish what stale neighbors will contain when a second removal occurs, so no queue-corruption claim is added to EK8799. Separately, on ExecSMP, `WaitIO()`'s `Disable()` is local while its `Remove()` writes the shared list links without the port spinlock; `InternalPutMsg()`'s `AddTail()` uses that lock. The exact concurrent append/unlink sequence and optional AHI-Handler shared reply-port caller remain as recorded in EK9883. No I/O request, timer, signal, port operation, or interleaving was run; source-only.

## TLSF `AllocAbs()` concrete caller census (EK10604; 2026-11-02; source-only)

Expanded the public-call inventory after confirming the full dispatch: `AllocAbs()` always enters `InternalAllocAbs()` and `nommu_AllocAbs()`; matching managed headers invoke `mhe_AllocAbs` after `mhe_InBounds`, and TLSF installs `tlsf_allocabs` (`rom/exec/allocabs.c:72-84`; `rom/exec/memory.c:879-883`; `rom/exec/memory_nommu.c:88-130`; `rom/kernel/tlsf.c:987-1129,1477-1478`). Their range sizes and aligned address calculations do not establish a near-address-space-sized or unmappable TLSF miss as a normal caller input. The finding therefore remains a conditional bug in the managed allocator API path: if `MAPPING_SEARCH()` maps a requested size to `fl >= REAL_FLI`, the first matrix access is out of bounds; if a valid search finds no containing free block, the loop advances up to `MAX_FLI`, also exceeding the `REAL_FLI` matrix dimension. It is not presented as a demonstrated failure of a selected in-tree call site. No allocation, build, or runtime was run; source-only.

Exec signal bit-31 standard recheck (EK8800 restored; no body/LOC credit): checked the exact language rule against the configured C-standard probes (`config/features.in:90-145`) and the signed expressions in `WaitPort`, `PutMsg`, `WaitIO` and `FreeSignal`. The 2026-10-26 withdrawal mistakenly used the proposed C23 “corresponding unsigned type” wording. The C17 ballot wording instead requires the positive signed shift result to be representable in the result type; `1 << 31` on 32-bit `int` is undefined ([WG14 C17 ballot N2176 §6.5.7p4](https://www.open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg14/www/docs/n2176.pdf); N1570 §6.5.7p4). Reconciled automatic signal allocation: the default task mask reserves bits 0–15, and the allocator selects the lowest free bit, so 31 is reached after bits 16–30 are occupied (`prepareexecbase.c:319`; `newaddtask.c:249-251`; `allocsignal.c:76-104,121`; `createmsgport.c:52-69`). Restored EK8800 in the report and index, updated the WaitPort/AllocSignal/pthread rows, and left compiler manifestation unverified. No compiler output, signal exhaustion, port, I/O request or runtime was used; source-only.

The failed idle-task creation can therefore leave the documented task absent without establishing a separate functional defect in this path. The target is selected by `arch/riscv64-opensbi/exec/mmakefile.src`; no allocation failure, scheduler, interrupt, boot or build was exercised. Firmware handoff and broader OpenSBI integration remain open. Source-only.


Partition geometry producer audit for EK10607 (2026-11-02; no new finding or body/LOC credit): traced selected `TD_GETGEOMETRY` producers against the root-handle and HDToolBox consumers. ATA's small-LBA path copies legacy IDENTIFY cylinders/heads/sectors without nonzero validation (`rom/devs/ata/lowlevel.c:1878-1926`), and AHCI copies IDENTIFY heads/sectors into the geometry response (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci_io.c:298-317`). NVMe and VirtIO instead synthesize geometry and guard zero heads/cylinders in their setup paths (`rom/devs/nvme/nvme_busclass.c:595-618`; `rom/devs/virtio/virtio_busclass.c:237-243`). Thus the zero divisor is not produced by those NVMe/VirtIO initialization paths; the candidate remains conditional on ATA/AHCI reporting zero legacy geometry. No checked-in hardware response establishes that trigger. Existing body/path/LOC credits stand. No device request, partition operation or build was run; source-only.

USB mass-storage geometry producer follow-up for EK10607 (2026-11-02; no new finding or body/LOC credit): traced `nGetGeometry()`'s MODE SENSE geometry flags into its final fake-geometry decision (`rom/usb/classes/massstorage/massstorage.class.c:2394-2402,2424-2433,2446-2454,2561-2565`). A nonzero cylinder field in mode page 04 marks both cylinder and head geometry present regardless of the head byte; page 05 similarly marks all three geometry flags when only its cylinder field is nonzero. With nonzero capacity, these flags suppress `nFakeGeometry()`, and the resulting zero head/track value is returned to `OpenRootPartition()`. This is a source-confirmed producer route conditional on a device returning such a mode page, not evidence that a particular supported device does so. Updated EK10607's trigger boundary; no separate root cause or line credit. No USB device, mode-page response, partition operation or build was used; source-only.

EK8800 allocator and core-consumer source recheck (2026-11-02; existing finding confirmed; no new ID or body/LOC credit): reread `AllocTaskSignal()`, `FreeSignal()`, `CreateMsgPort()`, `WaitPort()`, `PutMsg()` and `WaitIO()`. Fresh tasks reserve bits 0–15 (`newaddtask.c:249-252`; `prepareexecbase.c:319`); automatic allocation takes the least available bit and can select 31 once bits 16–30 are occupied (`allocsignal.c:76-121`). `CreateMsgPort()` accepts all allocated signal numbers and stores the byte bit without restricting it (`createmsgport.c:52-69`); core port, message, I/O and free paths form signed `1 << bit` masks at the previously reported sites. This reconfirms the valid-bit trigger and C-through-C17 undefined-shift basis. Also checked `input.device`'s `ResetSig = 1L << AllocSignal(-1)` (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:198`): its fresh worker consumes five signals for command/timer/key/game ports before ResetSig, leaving available user bits in the selected setup, so allocation exhaustion is not established on that path and no separate OD is added. Existing detailed scope remains compiler-dependent for the signed-shift consequences; no signal or message-port operation/build was run.

Read `m68k_to_native_taglist()` and the full generated wrapper bodies for `GetDTAttrsA`, `GT_GetGadgetAttrsA`, and `UnpackStructureTags` (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_shadow.c:139-163`; `m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:681-689,2863-2871,7031-7040`). Confirmed the converter creates a native TagItem array and resolves an in-range guest `ti_Data` address to the corresponding host address in the guest arena; wrappers pass that clone directly to the native API and free it after return, without a result-width or endian conversion. The native contracts and bodies write through `IPTR *`: DataTypes stores `opg_Storage` and zeros failed attributes (`workbench/libs/datatypes/getdtattrsa.c:72-88`); GadTools passes `ti_Data` to `GetAttr()` as the output address (`workbench/libs/gadtools/gt_getgadgetattrsa.c:58-67`); Utility documents `ti_Data` as an `IPTR *` and writes each unpacked value through it (`rom/utility/unpackstructuretags.c:35-43,100-153`). On a supported 64-bit host these stores are eight bytes into four-byte guest slots and use host byte order. Expanded EK9203 from `UnpackStructureTags()`/Graphics `GetRPAttrsA()` to include DataTypes `GetDTAttrsA()`, GadTools `GT_GetGadgetAttrsA()`, and DOS `GetSegListInfo()`. These share the direct native-width output-slot store; the separate `GetDrawInfoAttr()` result remains under EK10305. No maintained in-tree guest caller was found for the three generated vectors. The generated file remains partially reviewed and this targeted trace gives no path/LOC credit. No guest call, object, tag list, or build was run; source-only.

Utility Pack/UnpackStructureTags payload byte-order cross-check (EK10213 expanded; 2026-11-02; no body/path/LOC credit): re-read both native implementations (`rom/utility/packstructuretags.c:69-151`; `unpackstructuretags.c:71-148`) after confirming the generated thunks forward `pack` and `packTable` as raw guest pointers (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:7021-7038`). In addition to the already reported guest-endian pack-table decode error, PackStructureTags writes multi-byte ULONG/UWORD/WORD fields using native typed stores and UnpackStructureTags reads them using native typed loads. On a little-endian host, guest structures therefore receive reversed multi-byte fields or are interpreted as reversed values even if the table words were decoded. Added these consequences to EK10213 and the master index, keeping UnpackStructureTags' separate native-width output-slot issue under EK9203. Optional m68kemu guest API; no maintained guest caller identified. No guest operation or build was run; source-only.

`WaitPort()` core/message-queue caller inventory pass (2026-11-02; no new EK or body/LOC credit): re-read all 39 code lines of `rom/exec/waitport.c` and the selected queue primitives `GetMsg()`, `PutMsg()`/`InternalPutMsg()`, and `ReplyMsg()` (`rom/exec/getmsg.c:60-76`; `putmsg.c:66-111`; `replymsg.c:49-69`). On ExecSMP the wait loop checks list emptiness under the message-port read spinlock with local task switching disabled, releases both before `Wait()`, then reacquires and rechecks after any signal; after observing a nonempty list it releases the lock before returning the current head without removing it, consistent with the API contract. The matching enqueue/dequeue paths use local `Disable()` plus the port spinlock and release the lock before signaling or returning. A repository-wide fixed-string C/header search inventoried 308 `WaitPort()` references across 202 files. This establishes the caller inventory size, not a complete per-caller lifecycle audit; broad build-selected caller and port-destruction overlap review remains open. `WaitIO()` deliberately waits on the reply-port signal and rechecks its request rather than calling `WaitPort()` because other messages may share the port (`rom/exec/waitio.c:56-64`). No caller or concurrent queue operation was run; source-only.

`WaitPort()` direct-return caller lifetime recheck (no new EK or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): examined the checked-in callers that consume `WaitPort()`'s returned pointer without `GetMsg()`. LDDemon's waiter uses a zeroed `LDDMsg` and reply port embedded in its stack frame, reads the returned fields, then leaves scope (`rom/lddemon/lddemon.c:402-445`); its one-shot local message and port are not reused. RXLIB, RX, and FKey each create a private reply port and one Rexx message, wait until the returned message is their own, then immediately free that message and delete the private port (`workbench/rexxc/RXLIB.c:36-60,123-130`; `RX.c:59-87,186-205`; `workbench/tools/commodities/FKey.c:1053-1064,1077-1096`). `DeleteRexxMsg()` only frees the message allocation, while `DeletePort()` removes/frees the port and does not traverse its queue (`workbench/libs/rexxsyslib/deleterexxmsg.c:44-48`; `compiler/alib/deleteport.c:42-47`); these one-shot private-port paths therefore do not establish a surviving dangling queue or a `WaitPort()` API defect. This is a targeted resolution of the direct-return cases, not a full audit of the 308 inventoried references; broader build-selected caller and port-lifecycle review remains open. No message operation or build was run; source-only.

Exec/Kernel remaining selected `WaitPort()` caller pass (2026-11-02; EK10610 added; no body/path/LOC credit): checked the uncovered local source references in `rom/intuition/wbtasktalk.c`, `workbench/tools/Edit/Utility.c`, `workbench/libs/popupmenu/window.c`, `workbench/libs/asl/specialreq.c`, `workbench/libs/workbench/sendappwindowmessage.c`, `workbench/libs/gl/gl_init.c`, `workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/popasl.c`, `compiler/alib/getrexxvar.c`, `setrexxvar.c`, and `workbench/libs/rexxsupport/{waitpkt,openport,closeport,getpkt}.c`. Intuition's Workbench talker uses a private one-shot stack port/message and never retains either; the editor, popupmenu, and ASL requester drain their window ports and reply to messages; SendAppWindowMessage dequeues its private reply; GL drains queued notifications; Popasl consumes its startup message and its caller waits only for a one-shot completion before freeing its private objects. The Rexx variable helpers use one private request/reply and were already traced; no competing receiver was established. `WAITPKT` differs: `OPENPORT` creates a named port in the opener's task and stores it in the library-wide list, whereas any `WAITPKT` caller finding that name waits on its own task's signal mask. Exec routes the port signal to its stored creator task. Added conditional public-command candidate EK10610; no checked-in script exercises cross-task use and the command docs do not state a task-owner restriction, so that API-intent boundary remains explicit. `GETPKT`'s empty-queue behavior remains unclassified because no documented precondition or caller was established (existing coverage row). PC timer EClock update cross-CPU caller trace (EK10612 added; no new body/path/LOC credit beyond the timer bodies already in the reviewed set; 2026-11-02): read the selected all-PC implementation of `EClockAdd()`, `EClockUpdate()`, `EClockSet()`, `TimerInt()` and generic `common_BeginIO()` timer-request branches, then enumerated generic clock readers. `TimerInt()` calls `EClockUpdate()` from IRQ0; `ReadEClock()`, `GetSysTime()` and `GetUpTime()` call it from task/API context while using only `Disable()`. <a id="raspberry-pi-timer-compare-reprogramming-ek10613"></a>
Raspberry Pi AArch64 timer compare reprogramming pass (EK10613 added; 2026-11-02): read the complete selected `Timer_Reprogram()` body, its `common_BeginIO()` caller, timer initialization and interrupt re-arm path. The function takes `tb_ListLock` only while copying the current MICROHZ head and computing a delay; it releases the lock before reading CLO and writing the shared compare register. The BeginIO wrapper calls it when a request becomes the list head and uses only local `Disable()`. The Raspberry Pi configuration sets `__AROSEXEC_SMP__` for the `smp` variant (`configure.in:2197-2199`); the SoC system timer compare register is shared. Thus concurrent BeginIO callers can snapshot different heads and commit their compare writes in the opposite order, allowing an older longer delay to replace a newer shorter one. Recorded EK10613 as a conditional deadline-latency candidate; the precise delay depends on the interleaving and no hardware/IRQ-affinity behavior was exercised. No timer request, SMP schedule, or build was run; source-only.

The selected PC backend also resets `tb_ticks_total` and `tb_prev_tick` in `EClockSet()` with no cross-CPU serialization (`arch/all-pc/timer/ticks.c:115-126`). In-tree setters include `C:Date`, `C:SetClock`, DOS CLI initialization and Locale prefs (`workbench/c/Date.c:169`; `workbench/c/SetClock.c:144`; `rom/dos/cliinit.c:104`; `workbench/prefs/locale/registertab.c:295`; `workbench/prefs/time/prefs.c:35`). ## IFFParse pointer-return detail reconciliation for EK9432 (2026-11-03; no new EK or body/path/LOC credit)

Compared the IFFParse pointer-return coverage already in EK9432 with the thunk generator and IFFHandle layout (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunkgen.py:175-194,223-231`; `m68kemu_shadow_layouts.h:1881-1886`; generated `m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:4634-4638,4917-4932`). `IFFHandle` has a 12-byte guest / 16-byte native shadow layout and is accepted for input shadow lookup, but `AllocIFF()` is not in `SHADOW_RETURNS`, so its generated thunk returns the native allocation directly; subsequent `IFFHandle *` parameters only resolve a guest shadow or containment offset. `InitIFF()` then writes fields at native offsets. ## Housekeeper remote-tombstone queue progress review (EK10615; 2026-11-03)

<a id="housekeeper-remote-tombstone-queue-ek10615"></a>
Read `rom/exec/service.c`'s complete service loop and traced its queue operations, affinity state and selected x86-64 PC, ARM32, and AArch64 scheduling behavior. For `TS_TOMBSTONED`, a CPU mismatch leaves `taskRequeue` true; `InternalPutMsg()` requeues the node, and the loop's next `GetMsg()` can immediately consume that same node. This prevents reaching `WaitPort()` while the request remains at the head. `Exec_InitServices()` configures the housekeeper at priority 127 with `TASKAFFINITY_ANY`; each selected scheduler requires an affinity-eligible ready peer before quantum expiry can rotate the running task. `configure.in` enables ExecSMP in the x86-64 PC and Raspberry Pi SMP variants (`:1669,2197`), and the PC and ARM-native startup paths set `EXECF_CPUAffinity` (`arch/all-pc/kernel/smp_exec.c:60`; `arch/arm-native/exec/platform_init.c:258`; `arch/aarch64-native/exec/platform_init.c:207`). This substantiates EK10615 as a conditional queue-progress/busy-spin issue, separate from EK807's conditional reclamation race. ServicePort insertion and the existing self-removal message lifecycle were cross-checked; no claim is made about every producer's ordering. No task removal, affinity configuration, SMP schedule, build, or runtime behavior was exercised. Source-only; the `service.c` body already had review credit, so no new body/LOC credit.

RexxSupport `portcleanup()` tracked-message loop mechanics recheck (EK866 sharpened; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): reread `ForeachNode`'s macro (`compiler/include/exec/lists.h:195-201`), `ReplyMsg()` (`rom/exec/replymsg.c:54-64`) and `InternalPutMsg()`/`AddTail()` (`rom/exec/putmsg.c:75-89`; `rom/exec/addtail.c:53-65`) against `portcleanup.c:23-31`. The loop increment reads the current node's `ln_Succ` only after the body; ReplyMsg appends that same node to its reply port, and AddTail rewrites both links, including `ln_Succ` to the reply-port tail sentinel. `ForeachNode` then tests that sentinel's `ln_Succ` and exits, so the cleanup iteration stops after replying the first tracked message. Remaining nodes still linked in `data->msgs` are skipped before the parent `PortNode` is freed; this confirms the message-loss trigger and clarifies the exact link sequence in EK866. `ForeachNodeSafe` would save the successor before the body, but the selected implementation uses ordinary `ForeachNode`. EK8800 selected filesystem signal-mask caller extension (2026-11-03; no new ID/body/path/LOC credit): traced `workbench/fs/ntfs/main.c:191-208,163-173`. NTFS obtains `diskchgintbit` with `AllocSignal(-1)`, stores `1 << diskchgintbit` in the static interrupt data, and passes it to Exec `Signal()` from the disk-change interrupt. Thus valid bit 31 reaches the same signed `1 << 31` expression on 32-bit-`int` builds; a bad mask can leave `ProcessDiskChange()` asleep depending on compiler output. This is an additional selected caller for the existing EK8800 root cause, not an independent finding. No signal exhaustion or interrupt was induced; source-only.

**EK10615 queue-order qualification (2026-11-03; no new finding or body/LOC credit):** the mismatch path requeues the tombstone with `InternalPutMsg()` at the service-port tail. <a id="pc-timer-eclock-missed-wrap-ek10618"></a>
PC timer missed-wrap candidate (EK10618 added; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): rechecked the selected all-PC PIT mode, the programmed default/reload intervals, and the complete `EClockAdd()`/`EClockUpdate()`/`Timer0Setup()` path (`arch/all-pc/timer/ticks.c:81-112,127-190`; `timer_init.c:134-143,184-196`). The 16-bit value reveals only elapsed clocks modulo 65,536, while `EClockAdd()` compensates at most one rollover; an exact 65,536-clock gap leaves `time == tb_prev_tick` and adds zero. No timer, IRQ delay, hardware counter or build was exercised; source-only.

The intuition bodies already have coverage credit. No notification or reply was sent; source-only.

EK10615 tombstone CPU-origin and priority boundary recheck (finding retained; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): traced the producer's saved `iet_CpuNumber` from self-`RemTask()` through `tc_UserData` and the tombstoned service branch (`rom/exec/remtask.c:111-141`; `rom/exec/service.c:44-66`). Rechecked the priority-127 `TASKAFFINITY_ANY` housekeeper against selected PC and native scheduler scans: quantum rescheduling requires an affinity-eligible ready task whose numeric priority is less than or equal to the running task priority (`nexttask->tc_Node.ln_Pri <= task->tc_Node.ln_Pri`); with no such peer, the retry loop remains the only service-task work and does not yield to an arbitrary CPU. This confirms EK10615's trigger is conditional on the actual saved CPU and ready-list eligibility, not merely any remote tombstone. No self-removal, queue, scheduler, build or runtime operation was performed; source-only.

EK10615 scheduler handoff consequence correction (2026-11-05; finding retained; no body/path/LOC credit): reread the complete selected `core_Schedule()` and `core_Dispatch()` handoff on x86-64 PC, ARM-native, and AArch64-native. With no affinity-eligible peer, the schedule path can still enter dispatch; dispatch selects the `TASKAFFINITY_ANY` housekeeper again on that CPU if it remains the first eligible ready task (`arch/all-pc/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:63-150,308-342`; `arch/arm-native/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:55-105,269-307`; `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:55-105,247-298`). A different CPU may take it only if its dispatch wins while the housekeeper is on the shared ready list. Corrected the report's prior implication that an otherwise idle recorded CPU cannot move the housekeeper at all: it does not force migration, but later scheduling on that CPU can select it. Also clarified that an eligible peer only pauses the spin; when the housekeeper resumes on the wrong CPU it retries the same tombstone. This refines the scheduler and duration claim without withdrawing the immediate requeue/GetMsg loop or its conditional busy-spin and delayed-reclamation consequence. No schedule or build was run; source-only.

AArch64 Raspberry Pi EClock concurrent-update follow-up (EK10612 scope expanded; no new ID or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-04): traced `EClockUpdate()`'s CAS and both subsequent `ADDTIME()` calls (`arch/aarch64-raspi/timer/ticks.c:23-56`) against generic `ReadEClock()`, `GetSysTime()`, and `GetUpTime()` callers (`rom/timer/readeclock.c:56-62`; `getsystime.c:54-61`; `getuptime.c:54-61`). Each reader invokes the backend under local `Disable()` only, which does not exclude another CPU (`rom/exec/disable.c:58-61`); AArch64 Raspberry Pi ExecSMP is selected by `configure.in:2197-2199`. The CAS serializes which counter interval each caller books, but it publishes `tbp_EClockLast` before the non-atomic additions to shared `tb_CurrentTime` and `tb_Elapsed`. A later counter sample can therefore win a second CAS while the earlier caller is still applying its delta, allowing concurrent read-modify-write operations to lose or corrupt elapsed-time additions. Expanded EK10612, whose existing PC SMP baseline race and SetSysTime interaction remain separate manifestations of unsynchronized shared timer state. No EClock call, SMP schedule, or build was run; source-only.

Raspberry Pi timer compare IRQ-side caller closure (EK10613 retained; no new ID or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-04): traced the selected BCM2837 compare handler `Timer1Tick()` through `timer_ProcessTick()` and its final `Timer_Reprogram()` call (`arch/aarch64-raspi/timer/timer_init.c:56-74`) alongside the `BeginIO()` caller (`beginio.c:17-24`). On the Pi 3 compare-IRQ path, an interrupt on one CPU and a new MICROHZ request on another are independent writers of the shared compare register; either can snapshot a queue state, be delayed, and commit after the other has programmed a shorter deadline. This confirms the in-tree IRQ-side writer for EK10613's stale-compare interleaving. Pi 4/5 use the documented VBlank fallback and are excluded from the compare-IRQ deadline claim. The selected list-lock guard remains unset on this backend (EK10614), independently leaving queue-head access unprotected; this note does not treat that as a second root cause. No timer IRQ, request, SMP schedule or build was run; source-only.
