POSIXC `dup()` body and cross-process reservation race recheck (EK10313 expanded; 2026-11-03; one previously uncredited path, nine C code lines): read all 60 physical lines of `compiler/crt/posixc/dup.c` and traced its `__getfirstfd(0)` result directly into `dup2()`. `__getfirstfd()` checks the shared fd.library table but does not reserve its result (`__fdesc.c:199-224`); `dup2()` later calls `__getfdslot()`, which skips reservation for any existing `FD_OWNER_POSIXC` value without identifying the owning process (`:227-299`). A different ordinary process can claim the chosen number between the two calls, after which the local descriptor is published over the other process's global data pointer. Expanded canonical EK10313 and its master-index summary; no second ID. The `dup.c` implementation is selected by `compiler/crt/posixc/mmakefile.src:29`. No `dup()`, process, descriptor allocation or build was run; source-only.

ChildWait missed-wakeup recheck (EK05 confirmed; 2026-11-03; no finding or body/path/LOC credit): compared the complete `ChildWait()` empty-port scan and signal-clear sequence with `SetSignal()`, `Wait()`, `Signal()`, and the exit-notification publisher in `Exec_CleanupETask()`. `Wait()` correctly checks/enqueues under the task spinlock, but this cannot repair a child notification that `ChildWait()` clears after its queue scan and before entering `Wait()`. The publisher enqueues under the message-port lock and signals only after releasing it; Exec's `Forbid()` documentation explicitly says it is local to the calling CPU on EXECSMP builds. Another CPU can therefore publish and signal in that gap. This confirms existing EK05; no duplicate finding or coverage increment. No task was run; source-only.

Checked the `wcstoimax()`/`wcstoumax()` adapters; no additional width mismatch was promoted without a target-specific `intmax_t` width premise. No conversion or build was run; source-only. Also added EK10743 for the unchecked `wcstombs()` temporary allocation, EK10744 because the integer parsers stop at the first overflow digit when setting `endptr`, and EK10745 because the floating parsers do not implement their documented infinity/NaN inputs. <a id="ek8800-input-console-printer-mask-cross-check-2026-11-03"></a>
EK8800 input, console and printer caller pass (2026-11-03; no new ID or coverage credit): traced signal-mask setup and wait dispatch in `rom/devs/input/processevents.c:113-161,253-260`, `rom/devs/console/consoletask.c:191-193,235-240`, and `workbench/devs/printer/driver.c:80-88,286-293`. <a id="unsigned-string-overflow-recheck-ek10766"></a>
Unsigned string-conversion overflow/signedness recheck (EK10766; targeted source and test-corpus pass; 2026-11-04; no whole-file or LOC credit): traced `strtoul()` and `strtoull()` overflow handling from the cutoff loop through `any < 0`, saturation to the unsigned maximum, and the later `if (neg) val = -val` branch; confirmed `strtoumax()` forwards to one of those implementations. On a negative subject sequence whose magnitude overflows, the saturation sentinel is negated modulo the unsigned type (e.g. maximum becomes 1) while `ERANGE` remains set. The checked-in CUnit tests cover positive overflow and `-1`, but not negative magnitude overflow (`developer/debug/test/crt/stdc/cunit-crt-strto-c89.c:113-143`). POSIX documents the maximum return on overflow ([POSIX programmer reference](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man3/strtoul.3p.html)); the Austin Group/WG14 liaison statement also records the inherited C wording ambiguity and describes magnitude-first overflow detection as the intended interpretation ([WG14 N2723](https://www.open-std.org/JTC1/SC22/WG14/www/docs/n2723.pdf)). The candidate is retained with medium standards confidence; no runtime test was performed.

<a id="taskless-preinitlib-attemptsemaphore-ek9152"></a>Taskless PREINITLIB `AttemptSemaphore()` report/index restoration and final source-context recheck (EK9152; 2026-11-04; no new source-body or LOC credit): revalidated the pre-bootstrap ordering in `rom/exec/exec_init.c:61-66,143-200`, task-context behavior in `InternalAttemptSemaphore()`/`ReleaseSemaphore()`, and the complete `PREINITLIB` registration census. ## `SetTaskPri()` remote affinity-mask lifetime trace (EK10768; 2026-11-04)

Read the complete selected `rom/exec/settaskpri.c` body and traced its remote-running-task branch through `KrnScheduleCPU()` on all-PC, ARM32-native and AArch64-native kernels; also followed `SetTaskAffinity()`'s finite-mask update/kick path (`rom/task/SetTaskAffinity.c:98-142`) and all remote-kick paths in `rom/exec/signal.c:323-438`. Each releases the task lock before passing the task-owned affinity pointer to the kernel scheduler; `Signal()` can additionally publish a waiting target as ready before the later mask use. `RemTask()` can transition a task out of `TS_RUN` and call `CleanupETask()`; cleanup frees a non-sentinel affinity mask. On all-PC, `core_DoIPI()` copies the supplied mask; on ARM32/AArch64, the scheduler wrapper directly dereferences it to form the target IPI bits. Thus a target task that terminates in the unlock-to-call interval can invalidate the pointer before consumption. This establishes EK10768 for finite allocated affinity masks passed by these APIs; the `TASKAFFINITY_ANY` sentinel is not dereferenced by the selected wrappers. The task lock serializes the initial state/pointer read but does not extend mask lifetime beyond the unlock. No priority/affinity change, termination, IPI, or build was run; source-only. `settaskpri.c` already had body/path credit; no new body/LOC credit.


EK8866 TaskLaunch post-publication dereference follow-up (2026-11-04; finding expanded, no new ID or body/path/LOC credit): re-read the complete `TaskLaunch()` ordering in `rom/exec/newaddtask.c:25-123` against the task.resource prelaunch wrapper and self-removal/reclamation path (`rom/task/task_execfuncs.c:20-43,96-179`; `rom/exec/remtask.c:135-141`; `rom/exec/service.c:73-90`). After the SMP path publishes `TS_READY` and re-enables local interrupts, it continues reading `task` for affinity/priority decisions and later invokes `plHook`. A task eligible on another CPU may run and remove itself before those reads; if ServiceTask reclaims the TCB in that interval, the creator can directly dereference freed memory as well as leave the late stale task.resource entry already reported in EK8866. The direct `TaskLaunch()` use-after-free applies to ExecSMP regardless of task.resource; the stale tracked-entry consequence additionally requires task.resource wrappers. Both share the same premature-publication trigger, so no separate ID was added. No task launch, removal, list traversal or build was run; source-only.

ExecSMP `Wait()` signal-versus-sleep ordering recheck (2026-11-04; no new EK or body/path/LOC credit): re-read the complete `rom/exec/wait.c` body against `Signal()`'s target-task lock and ready/wait transitions (`rom/exec/signal.c:117-224,298-445`) and the ARM32/AArch64 locked state-migration helpers. `Wait()` holds `tc_SpinLock` while checking received signals, publishing `tc_SigWait`/`TS_WAIT`, and moving the node from Running to Wait; it retains the lock across `KrnSwitch()` until the saved register frame is safe. `Signal()` therefore either sets the signal before the check, or waits until the target is fully on Wait before making it ready. After wake, `Wait()` reacquires the lock and rechecks the mask before clearing received bits. No lost-wakeup window or state/list ordering defect was established in this path. Zero-mask waits and supervisor-mode use remain API/caller contract questions outside this ordering check. No signal, wait, task transition, or build was run; source-only.

X11 event-task VBlank server caller recheck against EK629 (2026-11-11; no new EK or body/path/LOC credit): traced `x11task_entry()`'s stack-local `struct Interrupt myint` through `AddIntServer(INTB_VERTB)`, `x11VBlank()`'s signal-only body, and `RemIntServer()` before the task returns (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/x11/x11.c:52-61,354-398,681-688`). The hosted Unix timer reaches `vblank_Cause()` from its SIGALRM `TimerTick()` path (`arch/all-unix/timer/timer_init.c:34-78,101-108`), and `KrnCli()` blocks the configured interrupt-signal mask on the current host thread (`arch/all-unix/kernel/cli.c:16-27`). `RemIntServer()` protects list mutation with `EXEC_LOCK_LIST_WRITE_AND_DISABLE`; when `__AROSEXEC_SMP__` is absent, that macro uses `Disable()` (`rom/exec/remintserver.c:53-63`; `rom/exec/exec_locks.h:40-44,145-151`). Hosted Unix configure sets platform SMP support but does not set `ENABLE_EXECSMP` for an Exec SMP build; that define is emitted for the explicit x86-64 PC and Raspberry Pi `smp` variants (`configure.in:1213-1215,1668-1670,2196-2198`). Thus this X11 caller does not establish EK629's cross-CPU interrupt-list race on the selected hosted Unix Exec configuration. Whether host signal delivery can run this VBlank walk on a non-AROS host thread remains an external threading question; no separate X11 or Exec finding is added. No task, VBlank interrupt, or build was run; source-only.


EK9482 PC asynchronous Signal-hook target lifetime pass (2026-11-04; existing finding expanded; no body/path/LOC credit): rechecked the selected PC ExecSMP `Signal()` fallback against `core_DoCallIPI()`, the receiver hook, and `RemTask()` cleanup (`rom/exec/signal.c:170-247,89-106`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/kernel_ipi.c:92-221,224-252`; `rom/exec/remtask.c:97-128,165-180`). The PC IPI header does not define `KERNEL_IPI_CALL_CANCELABLE`, so `Signal()` copies the target task pointer into an asynchronous hook, queues/sends it, and returns; `CancelSignalIPIs()` has no active PC sweep. A concurrent remover can free the standard `tc_MemEntry` task allocation before the queued receiver invokes `signal_hook`, which then calls `Signal()` on the stale pointer. This is distinct from ARM32/AArch64 EK9482's claimed-but-uncommitted entry gap: the PC interval is after asynchronous queue publication and teardown has no cancellation path. Expanded EK9482 to include the PC target; no separate ID. No signal, IPI, task removal or build was run; source-only.

EK714 PC SMP stale-affinity dispatch path expansion (2026-11-04; existing finding expanded; no new path/LOC credit): verified the PC scheduling window directly in `arch/all-pc/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c`. `core_Dispatch()` reads `iet_CpuAffinity` while holding `TaskReadySpinLock` and removes the candidate (`:304-322`), then sets the still-ready candidate to `TS_RUN` without acquiring `tc_SpinLock` or rechecking the mask (`:344-370`). `SetTaskAffinity()` rewrites the mask under only `tc_SpinLock` and kicks only when it observes `TS_RUN` (`rom/task/SetTaskAffinity.c:111-142`), so it can finish excluding the selected PC while the task still reports `TS_READY`; the PC dispatcher subsequently launches on its stale eligibility result. This extends EK714's prior ARM/AArch64 scope to the selected PC ExecSMP dispatcher. The prior PC note about a temporary empty mask only causing a skipped task was too narrow; stale selection also permits launch on an excluded CPU. No scheduling interleaving was run; source-only.

<a id="posix-stat-empty-path-mode-recheck-ek10800"></a>
POSIX empty-path wrapper and RAMFS caller expansion (EK10800 expanded; no new path/LOC credit; 2026-11-04): extended the stat-family shared-helper trace to `chdir()`, `opendir()`, and `fstatat()`; also checked `open()`/`openat()` as a negative case. `chdir()` and `opendir()` do not reject empty paths in either conversion mode; `opendir()` explicitly uses `Lock()` to allow an empty name. `open()` rejects empty input only when `doupath` is true, while `fstatat()` and `openat()` delegate relative paths through those wrappers. In native path mode the stat/open wrappers also pass the empty string through; in Unix path mode `__path_normalstuff_u2a()` emits an empty AROS path for empty input. Traced all selected routes through DOS `Lock()` and RAMFS `GetObject()`, which returns the starting directory object for an empty relative path. Thus the affected stat APIs can return current-directory metadata, `chdir("")` can succeed as a no-op, `opendir("")` can return a directory stream, and native-mode read-only `open("")`/`openat("")` can return a directory descriptor. POSIXC `__open()` detects directories from the DOS lock and bypasses RAMFS file-open, so the earlier wrong-type exclusion was incorrect. Added the exact per-API and mode scope to EK10800; separate empty-path `chown()` side effect remains EK10802. Rechecked EK10642 as an independent fallback-return issue. Existing full-body credit remains unchanged. No path, filesystem, build or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only.

POSIXC stat64 path-conversion ownership/concurrency closure check (EK10843 retained; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-04): traced the stat64/lstat64 `__path_u2a()` result into `Lock()` and, on the object-in-use/soft-link fallback, into `__stat64_from_path()` (`stat64.c:83-110`; `lstat64.c:66-99`; `__stat.c:375-489`). The conversion buffer belongs to the active `PosixCIntBase`; the base layout explicitly documents that each pthread worker has its own posixc.library base, while only descriptor-table state is shared with the creator (`__posixc_intbase.h:70-91`). Thus simultaneous worker conversions do not by themselves overwrite this buffer across task-local bases; no new stat-family concurrency finding is added. The existing DOS64 `fib_Size` to `off_t` narrowing in `__fill_stat64buffer()` remains EK10843. No pathname call, file query, thread, or build was run; source-only.

POSIXC `st_blocks`/AFS OFS accounting trace (EK10844 added; 2026-11-04; no body/path/LOC credit): compared both `__fill_statbuffer()` and `__fill_stat64buffer()` block-count formulas (`compiler/crt/posixc/__stat.c:851-856,945-950`) with AFS `getDiskInfo()` (`rom/filesys/afs/misc.c:76-82`). The OFS branch (`dosflags == 0`) reports `BLOCK_SIZE - 24`; AFS derives `BLOCK_SIZE` from DOS environment geometry (`afsblocks.h:16`; `volumes.c:186-188`). For 128-word blocks and one sector per block, this is 512 physical bytes but 488 reported bytes. Since both POSIXC helpers multiply the rounded file-block count by integer `st_blksize / 512`, a nonempty file gets `st_blocks == 0`. AFS `Examine` independently computes `fib_NumBlocks` from the same 488-byte OFS payload capacity and file-list blocks (`rom/filesys/afs/filehandles3.c:285-291`), confirming nonzero allocation. Added EK10844 to the detailed report and master index. AFS is selected in the active ARM/AArch64 Raspberry Pi boot dependency lists (`arch/arm-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:130`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:131`). No mounted volume, file query or build was run; source-only.

`arc4random` entropy/fallback and partial-result contract recheck (2026-11-04; no new EK or body/path/LOC credit): re-read `compiler/crt/stdc/__arc4random.c`, `arc4random.c`, and `arc4random_buf.c`, then traced `__entropy_available()` to `OpenResource()` and `GetEntropy()` to `rom/entropy/getentropy.c`. The selected entropy implementation returns exactly the requested `ULONG` length or `-1` for NULL, so the stdc chunk loop's `got <= 0` fallback and pointer/remaining-length updates do not admit a positive short or oversized result from this provider. The xorshift fallback's call counter is stored on `StdCIntBase`; stdc.conf selects `peropenerbase` and `rootbase_field StdCRootBase`, but I have not yet closed whether concurrently executing threads can share this particular opener base. Keep the existing counter-sharing concurrency question open; no concurrency defect promoted from this trace. No entropy call, thread or build was run; source-only.

`arc4random` fallback-counter task-base closure (no new EK or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-04): resolved the conditional sharing question from the prior entropy recheck. `pthread_create.c` documents that worker Tasks run registered CRT enter/leave hooks, and `posixc/__threadhook.c` opens a new `posixc.library` base in each worker, whose selected `peropenerbase,rellinklib` setup opens its own stdc rel-library base; `stdc.conf` also selects `peropenerbase`. Thus concurrent pthread workers use distinct `StdCIntBase.arc4_fallbackctr` fields, and this specific counter does not establish a shared-base race on the selected pthread path. With source length `L < n`, the NUL is written at index `L`, and the remaining count `n-L` pads indices `L` through `n-1`; the NUL at `L` was mistakenly counted twice in the earlier report. For source length at least `n`, the first loop writes at most indices `0..n-1`, and `n == 0` writes nothing. Thus `strncpy()` respects the stated byte bound, and `strxfrm()`/`strxfrm_l()` do not inherit an overrun. EK10820 hard-float RISC-V `feholdexcept()` direct-caller census closure (existing finding confirmed; no new body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-04): repository-wide source search confirms the only in-tree math callers of `feholdexcept()` are the shared `s_lrint.c` template (`:53`, which supplies `lrint`, `lrintf`, `llrint`, `llrintf` and selected long-double variants) and `e_sqrtl.c:94`. Both ignore the return and later restore through `feupdateenv()` or `fesetenv()` using the local environment. The RISC-V soft-float implementation stores zero and returns success (`arch/riscv-all/include/aros/fenv.h:102-106`); the hard-float implementation neither writes the output nor saves FCSR and returns -1 (`:204-210`), while `feupdateenv()` writes the supplied value back to FCSR (`:222-231`). `sqrtl()`'s exact-result return uses `fesetenv(&env)` (`e_sqrtl.c:135-139`); other positive finite cases reach `feupdateenv()` later. PC ExecSMP rejected-stack dispatch membership recheck (EK10240 retained; 2026-11-05; no body/path/LOC credit): traced `core_Dispatch()` through `SET_THIS_TASK(newtask)` and the stack-range failure into `TaskWait` insertion, then through recursive `core_Switch()` (`arch/all-pc/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:304-405,205-287`; `arch/all-pc/exec/exec_platform.h:295-304`). `SET_THIS_TASK()` adds the candidate to `TaskRunning`; the rejection path does not unlink it before `Enqueue(TaskWait, candidate)`. The subsequent `core_Switch()` `Remove()` follows the candidate's now-overwritten Wait links and cannot repair the old Running neighbors, confirming the intrusive cross-list corruption in EK10240. Exec `Enqueue()` writes the new neighbors without removing prior membership (`rom/exec/enqueue.c:87-97`), and `Remove()` has no source-list identity (`rom/exec/remove.c:55-62`). The selected configuration remains x86-64 PC ExecSMP; the trigger requires a ready task with invalid saved SP bounds. No invalid task, scheduler operation, or build was used; source-only.

OpenSBI FDT memory-node name classification and consumer trace (EK10861 added; 2026-11-05; no body/path/LOC credit): re-read `krnParseFDT()`'s root cell parsing and depth-two memory `reg` path, then traced each accepted `info->regions` record through `krnInitMMU()` and startup's later per-region `MemHeader` creation. The parser matches any name beginning `memory` and does not require `memory`/`memory@` or check `device_type`; the consumer maps all secondary parsed regions RWX and adds aligned ranges of at least 1 MiB above the kernel as system memory. OpenSBI FDT memory-node false-positive versus UEFI region override (EK10861/EK9042 scope reconciliation; 2026-11-05; no body/path/LOC credit): re-read the EFI override in `kernel_startup.c:575-596` against `krnParseFDT()` and both memory consumers. It can still establish `mem_base`/`mem_size` during FDT parsing; the EFI loop updates those scalars only when one individual EFI region is larger, and the primary heap later uses the retained scalar span (`:591-595,781-788,890-895`). StdC distinct-long-double complex exponential range continuation (EK10862 added; existing full-body credit retained; 2026-11-05): rechecked `s_cexpl.c` against the selected double/float implementations and their scaled helper after the prior precision-family pass. `cexpl()` evaluates `expl(x)` before applying `cosl(y)`/`sinl(y)`; when `expl(x)` overflows but one trig-scaled mathematical component is still within `LDBL_MAX`, the implementation returns infinity for that finite component. The double/float implementations explicitly scale in the analogous range. Added EK10862 with a component-wise range trigger, qualified to distinct-long-double targets; `rg` found no direct in-tree `cexpl()` caller, so this is a selected public-library API defect without a maintained local caller established. No additional file/LOC credit. No math operation or build was run; source-only.


StdC long-double complex hyperbolic pair full-body and range pass (EK10863 added; two selected paths, 24 `cloc 2.06` C code lines; 2026-11-05): read all of `math/s_ccoshl.c` and `math/s_csinhl.c`, confirmed both are in `STDC_LONGDB_MATH`, and compared their direct `coshl(x)`/`sinhl(x)` products against the selected double `ccosh`/`csinh` scaling branches. Added EK10863: for large finite `x` and `y` near pi/2, the source overflows both hyperbolic intermediates before multiplying by a small cosine, losing a component that remains within `LDBL_MAX`. The target selection adds these sources for the 80-bit x86/x86_64/m68k and binary128 AArch64/RISC-V configurations; unsupported targets alias the double implementations. `rg` found no direct in-tree calls to `ccoshl` or `csinhl`, so caller reachability is public-library only in this checkout. No separate exception/special-value finding is promoted from this two-file slice. No math call or build was run; source-only.


StdC long-double inverse-hyperbolic wrapper full-body confirmation (EK10846 caller impact retained; two selected paths, 18 `cloc 2.06` C code lines; 2026-11-05): read all of `math/s_cacoshl.c` and `math/s_casinhl.c`, verified both are selected by `STDC_LONGDB_MATH`, and traced their exact rotations into `cacosl()` and `casinl()`. `cacoshl(z)` computes `I*cacosl(z)`; `casinhl(z)` computes `-I*casinl(I*z)`. For `cacoshl(real x)` with `x > 1`, `cacosl()` calls the faulty real-axis `casinl()` branch; for `casinhl(+i*y)` with `y > 1`, the `I*z` rotation likewise feeds a real value below -1 to that branch. Both therefore inherit EK10846; this is downstream impact of the same root cause, not a new finding. No additional candidate was established in these wrappers. No math call or build was run; source-only.


StdC complex arctangent precision-family full-body and large-real-range pass (EK10864 added; three selected paths, 151 `cloc 2.06` C code lines; 2026-11-05): read all of `math/s_catan.c`, `s_catanf.c`, and `s_catanl.c`, confirmed selection in `compiler/crt/stdc/mmakefile.src:146-148,279-280`, and traced each component square, denominator guard, `atan2`/range reduction, logarithmic ratio and overflow fallback. This is distinct from EK10847's earlier pure-imaginary `y > 1` false overflow guard. `rg` found no direct in-tree catan/catanf/catanl callsites beyond the catanh rotation wrappers and tests; no additional maintained caller is claimed. These three bodies now have explicit full-body source-order evidence; no project-wide denominator is recalculated here. No math call or build was run; source-only.

RexxSupport named-port cross-task lifetime audit (EK10865 added; 2026-11-05; no body/path/LOC credit): re-read `openport.c`, `waitpkt.c`, `getpkt.c`, `closeport.c`, `closeportrsrc.c`, `portcleanup.c`, and the `PortNode` layout (`workbench/libs/rexxsupport: selected RexxSupport command table in `arexxdispatch.c:31-50`). `OPENPORT` links a node into the library-wide list and publishes its MsgPort; the wait/get/close commands use `FindName()` without synchronization; explicit close and script-end cleanup both call `portcleanup()`, which unlinks, deletes, and frees the referenced node and port. No lock, reference count, or active waiter tracking exists. A distinct Rexx task can therefore retain the raw lookup result while another closes the name; `GETPKT` then uses freed `data->port` in `GetMsg()`, and `WAITPKT` can call `WaitPort()` through the same stale pointer. Added EK10865, separate from EK10610's wrong-task signal bit. No checked-in cross-task script was found; no Rexx command, close, or build was run; source-only.

WaitPort direct-Remove reply-port caller pass (2026-11-05; no new finding or path/LOC credit): enumerated selected production callsites that pass `WaitPort()` directly to `Remove()` in the Zune BetterString, NList, NListTree and TextEditor clipboard servers. Traced their static reply message/port reuse and client-side semaphore serialization. The reply message is the sole node published by each serialized request; the server cannot reuse that same message until the client removes it, so the unlocked generic `Remove()` is not shown to race another producer on these selected flows. The startup handshake also has one published reply message. Existing caller pattern is atypical but no distinct correctness defect established. This does not complete WaitPort's broader caller audit: the repository has many unrelated production/test callers, and external shared-port/lifetime contracts remain open. No message or schedule was run.

Popasl private reply-port consumption boundary (WaitPort caller recheck; 2026-11-05; no new EK or body/path/LOC credit): corrected the exact message ownership description from the 2026-11-02 caller pass. `Asl_Entry()` removes the startup request from the child process port with `GetMsg()` and replies to the parent's private `msg_port` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/popasl.c:52-62`). The parent calls `WaitPort(msg_port)` but does not `GetMsg()` the reply; it then frees the one-shot `startup` message and immediately deletes the private port (`:191-195`). `WaitPort()` returns the borrowed head without removing it, while `DeleteMsgPort()` frees the port and does not reply remaining messages (`rom/exec/waitport.c:39-57`; `rom/exec/deletemsgport.c:38-57`). The reply node is therefore still linked during the brief free-before-port-delete interval, but no selected reader or later use of this private port/message list was established after WaitPort returns; this remains an unusual cleanup sequence, not a demonstrated Exec defect. No port or task was run.

Boot-info `BootMsg` producer lifetime slice (2026-11-05; no new EK or path/LOC credit): rechecked the retained boot-tag pointer in selected hosted and native startup producers. The hosted bootstrap owns its tag array in static `km[]` storage, and both Unix and MinGW kernel startup retain that pointer after clearing BSS; no bootstrap release or replacement is shown in the traced handoff (`arch/all-hosted/bootstrap/bootstrap.c:95-112`; `arch/all-hosted/bootstrap/kickstart.c:12-22`; `arch/all-unix/kernel/kernel_startup.c:58-120`; `arch/all-mingw32/kernel/kernel_startup.c:32-81`). ARM-native and AArch64-native preserve the incoming tag pointer through kernel startup and pass it to `krnPrepareExecBase()`; the checked startup code does not release or rewrite the list (`arch/arm-native/kernel/kernel_startup.c:132-140,306`; `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/kernel_startup.c:142-177,371`). RISC-V OpenSBI builds a fresh list with `krnPrepareBootTags()` and stores its boot-memory allocation in `BootMsg` before later consumers (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_startup.c:630-656`). This closes only these selected producer lifetime slices: firmware/bootloader ownership of ARM/AArch64 input tags, other `BootMsg` producers, mutable tag-data lifetimes, and consumer-specific assumptions remain open. No boot, tag mutation, or build was run; source-only.


Boot-info producer lifetime continuation (2026-11-05; no new EK or path/LOC credit): extended the `BootMsg` producer check to selected PPC and m68k paths. Sam440 and Efika use `tmp_struct.bootup_tags` in retained kernel data, then pass the same storage to `exec_main()`; Pegasos copies the incoming tags into the reserved `BootData` region after `KRN_KernelHighest` and uses that copy for relocation and later boot-info lookup (`arch/ppc-sam440/kernel/kernel_startup.c:92,230-355,363`; `arch/ppc-chrp/efika/kernel/kernel_init.c:160,180-295,370,387`; `arch/ppc-chrp/pegasos/kernel/kernel_startup.c:154-181`). The m68k Amiga startup copies a tag list from temporary supervisor-stack storage into public memory when `TypeOfMem()` reports that the original is not persistent; successful copy ownership is retained in `PrivExecBase(...).PlatformData.BootMsg` (`arch/m68k-amiga/boot/start.c:231,857-879`). The allocation-failure branch replaces that pointer with NULL; the selected `KrnGetBootInfo()` accessor then returns NULL, and no dereference consequence was established from this trace. These checks narrow the selected producers' array-storage lifetime; nested tag-data buffers, error-path consumer assumptions, and remaining platform producers/consumers stay open. No boot, allocation failure, or build was induced; source-only.

m68k Amiga boot-tag relocation allocation-failure consumer check (no new EK; 2026-11-05; no body/path/LOC credit): followed the `newbootmsg == NULL` branch in `arch/m68k-amiga/boot/start.c:863-879` through the selected early consumers. The command-line MMU parser passes a NULL list to `LibGetTagData()`, whose `LibFindTagItem()`/`LibNextTagItem()` chain returns NULL safely (`arch/m68k-amiga/boot/mmu.c:196`; `compiler/arossupport/libgettagdata.c:7-12`, `libfindtagitem.c:7-17`, `libnexttagitem.c:7-12`). `debug.library` also uses that safe lookup; `bootloader.library` iterates with `NextTagItem()`, whose selected helper returns NULL for a NULL list. Exec alert formatting checks `tags` before lookup (`rom/exec/alertstrings.c:559-566`). Thus the relocation failure leaves boot metadata unavailable but this checked early consumer set does not establish a null-list crash. Later and indirect consumers remain open. Narrator, Speech and printer-device `WaitPort()` caller continuation (no new EK; existing OD3210/OD1028 caller failures retained; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-05): traced the selected narrator worker's command-port wait/drain through `GetRequest()` and its semaphore-protected dequeue (`workbench/devs/narrator/narrator.c:79-92,461-465`); only `NarratorWorker()` consumes that port, and the command loop drains until empty. In `printer.device`, the worker removes its one startup message after waiting, then is the sole consumer of `pd_Unit`; per-open/close wrappers use private DoIO reply ports, and Printer_Unit consumes the startup reply before deleting that port (`workbench/devs/printer/driver.c:543-577,831-850`). Android-hosted and Raspberry Pi ARM/AArch64 `BootMsg` storage follow-up (no new EK or path/LOC credit; 2026-11-05): traced the Android `kick()` handoff to the common hosted bootstrap's static `km[]` tag array (`arch/all-android/bootstrap/kickstart.c:89-93,160-168`; `arch/all-hosted/bootstrap/bootstrap.c:95-112,415`). Android forks only after the loader has prepared and retained that tag list; the child inherits the mapped array, and the hosted memory cleanup is deferred until the child exits (`arch/all-android/bootstrap/kickstart.c:43-45,51-74,124-167`). The Raspberry Pi ARM32 bootloader places its tag records in `bm_boottags` inside the fixed low-memory `bcm2708bootmem` reservation, and sets `KRN_MEMLower` at or above the end of that reserved block (`arch/arm-raspi/boot/boot.c:96-100,226-231,248,710`; `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/include/hardware/bcm2708_boot.h:14-27`). AArch64 places them in the corresponding `__bootmem.bm_boottags`, with the same memory-lower reservation (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/boot.c:60-64,303-309,421,1088`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/include/bcm2708_boot.h:35-48`). Unsigned stdc conversion overflow/signed-input caller recheck (EK10766 retained; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-05): reread complete `strtoul()`, `strtoull()`, their signed wrappers and `strtoumax()` delegation. The overflow branches set the unsigned maximum and `ERANGE`, then the shared negative-sign step negates that sentinel; on 64-bit unsigned long long, `-18446744073709551616` therefore returns 1 while retaining `ERANGE`. `strtol()`/`strtoll()` deliberately depend on this sign step to detect signed overflow and saturate, so a correction must preserve those wrappers' behavior rather than simply suppressing all negative negation. Rechecked the selected C89/C99 tests: they cover `-1` and positive magnitude overflow, but not a negative magnitude overflow. The checked direct parser/caller set includes configuration and user-entered numeric fields; no specific maintained caller was found to feed a negative out-of-range number and rely on the returned unsigned value, so the direct product consequence remains conditional on API consumers. VMM library existing-manager `ReqMemHeader` WaitPort reachability correction (2026-11-06; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): rechecked the `vmm_init.c:42-75` `FindPort(VMPortName)` branch against publication and handling. `Init_VM_Manager()` publishes the public `VMPort` at `VM_Manager_Init.c:577-587` before `AllocAddressRange()` (`:606`) and later paging initialization; `VM_Manager()` does not enter its VMPort dispatch loop until after `Init_VM_Manager()` returns successfully (`VM_Manager.c:601-645`). USB mass-storage timer `WaitIO()` caller follow-up for EK8799 (2026-11-06; existing finding, no new ID or LOC credit): traced `StorageTask()`'s `TR_ADDREQUEST` submission and wait mask through normal unit-change handling and shutdown (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/MassStorage/storage_task.c:137-147,172-178,204-220,318-348`). The task waits on the timer reply signal together with unit-message, single, and Ctrl-C signals. When a non-timer event wins, it checks the timer request, aborts it if incomplete, calls `WaitIO()`, clears the timer reply signal, and later resubmits or tears down the request. Shutdown repeats CheckIO/AbortIO/WaitIO before deleting the reply port and request. Thus an unrelated wake can reach `WaitIO()` while timer-device completion is being published on another CPU; on ExecSMP this is another concrete caller route to EK8799's premature completion/lifetime window. This trace does not prove the exact interleaving or timer producer CPU, and does not add a separate bug. No timer, signal, I/O request, device, or build was run; source-only.

Shutdown aborts and waits on the same request before closing/freeing it (`:938-947`). The event-port wake and Ctrl-C cleanup provide independent control flow while the timer request may be completing. Bluetooth controller timer teardown exclusion check for EK8799 (2026-11-06; no finding or LOC credit): examined `rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c:3039-3045` with timer.device `AbortIO()` and VBlank completion (`rom/timer/abortio.c:63-86`; `rom/timer/lowlevel.c:348-370`). Controller shutdown calls `AbortIO()` before `WaitIO()`. The timer completion path removes the request and calls `ReplyMsg()` while holding the timer-list write lock; timer `AbortIO()` acquires the same lock before inspecting the request type, so this shutdown route cannot pass AbortIO while that completion's ReplyMsg publication is still in progress. The Bluetooth event-handler caller recorded above does not AbortIO on its event-port path before CheckIO/WaitIO, so that distinction remains relevant. No lock schedule or runtime operation was exercised; source-only.

EK8799 Bluetooth/USB caller precision correction (2026-11-06; supersedes the broader independent-wake wording in the two preceding caller notes): timer completion removes the request and calls `ReplyMsg()` while holding the timer-list lock (`rom/timer/lowlevel.c:275-326,354-376`); on ExecSMP, `timer.device` `AbortIO()` takes that same lock before inspecting `NT_REPLYMSG` (`rom/timer/abortio.c:63-86`). Therefore a caller that actually executes AbortIO before WaitIO cannot pass that abort while the timer reply publication is in progress. The affected selected branches are narrower: USB mass storage and the Bluetooth event handler call `CheckIO()` first and go directly to `WaitIO()` when it sees completion (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/MassStorage/storage_task.c:215-218`; `rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/classes.c:921-923`). Because `CheckIO()` reads only the message type (`rom/exec/checkio.c:48-59`), it may observe `NT_REPLYMSG` after the timer interrupt sets it but before the interrupt finishes `ReplyMsg()`; the lock does not protect that reader. `WaitIO()` then removes the not-yet-enqueued node without acquiring the reply-port lock (`rom/exec/waitio.c:66-82`). When CheckIO returns incomplete, these callers' AbortIO serializes with timer completion and that branch does not establish EK8799. Bluetooth event-handler Ctrl-C teardown unconditionally calls AbortIO before WaitIO and is excluded for the same lock reason (`classes.c:940-944`). This tightens the selected-trigger evidence; no interleaving was run.

<a id="ek10905-withdrawal-review"></a>
### EK10905 withdrawn — `LVF_IGNORE` does not prohibit global deletion

Re-read the `DeleteVar()` contract and implementation, `FindVar()` node-type comparison, `SetVar()` assignment to `ln_Type`, all checked-in `LVF_IGNORE` references, and every `DeleteVar()` caller (`rom/dos/deletevar.c:38-117`; `rom/dos/findvar.c:36-70`; `rom/dos/setvar.c:60-75,119-143`; `compiler/include/dos/var.h:45-72`). `LVF_IGNORE` is documented as a flag ORed into a local `LocalVar` node for private shell use; it is not an additional global environment-variable type. `GVF_GLOBAL_ONLY` deliberately skips the local `FindVar()`/deletion path. The subsequent `(flags & 0x7f) == 0` check admits the global `LV_VAR` case even when the private local-node flag bit 7 is also set, while rejecting `LV_ALIAS` (bit 0). Nothing in `DeleteVar()`'s documented contract says a local-node visibility flag should suppress an explicit global deletion. The DOS variable test exercises `LVF_IGNORE` only with `GVF_LOCAL_ONLY`; other selected callers use either aliases with `GVF_LOCAL_ONLY` or ordinary global flags. Therefore the earlier claim that `GVF_GLOBAL_ONLY | LVF_IGNORE` requests a distinct non-global type was unsupported, and deleting the matching global file is expected behavior for that combination. Removed EK10905 from the detailed findings and active master index; the already-read `deletevar.c` remains fully credited as source-body coverage. No new finding, file, or LOC credit. No variable or filesystem operation was run; source-only.

Shell executes each loaded command segment through `RunCommand()` on the same Process, supporting repeated NIX startup and restoration of the cloned local-variable list. Installer and POSIXC exec can also invoke command segments; the boot helpers invoke the fixed `AROSMonDrvs` command. `workbench/c/shellcommands/Execute.c:253` mentions `RunCommand()` only in a comment and is not another direct call. A manifest search found one selected explicit `nix=yes` command target, `network-dhcp-client`; its normal AROSTCP service launch uses a separate process. WaitIO premature-reply recheck correction (EK8799 retained at the lifetime-overlap scope; 2026-11-06; no body/path/LOC credit): rechecked the timer producer order (`rom/timer/lowlevel.c:365-375`) after tracing `CreateIORequest()` (`rom/exec/createiorequest.c:63-72`). Timer requests are linked in the timer's pending list and removed before `ReplyMsg()`; `REMOVE` leaves the node's predecessor/successor pointers unchanged (`compiler/include/exec/lists.h:136-145`). Thus on the pre-reply-port-insertion race, `WaitIO()` does not call `Remove()` on the initially zeroed links; it sees stale timer-list neighbor pointers. If that list is unchanged, the repeated neighbor writes may be idempotent. Retracted the direct null-link fault and any implied timer-list corruption. The remaining EK8799 consequence is the independently established early WaitIO return while `InternalPutMsg()` is still inserting/signaling, permitting request/reply-port cleanup or reuse to race the publisher. This is separate from EK9883's removal of a node already linked to its reply port racing another append. No signal or I/O was run; source-only.

x86-64 `PrepareContext()` direct-caller and ABI closeout (2026-11-06; no new EK or source-body/LOC credit): inventoried maintained `NewAddTask()` calls and the `AddTask()` compatibility wrapper, then compared the selected x86-64 `PrepareContext()` mapping (`arch/x86_64-all/exec/preparecontext.c:54-103`) with `TASKTAG_ARG1`–`TASKTAG_ARG8` and the caller tag lists. Arguments 1–6 map to the SysV integer argument registers; 7–8 map to the two reserved stack slots. Checked USB stack/classes, trackdisk, VMM, network-task wrappers, DOS `CreateNewProc`, `NewCreateTaskA`, and `AddTask` callers; no supplied argument exceeds the supported range or is assigned to the wrong slot. `NewAddTask()` aligns the initial stack to 16 bytes before `PrepareContext()` pushes five 8-byte words; the entry stack is 8 mod 16, and `TaskExitStub` removes the two reserved argument slots before returning to the fallback with the expected function-entry alignment. `NewCreateTaskA()` enforces the selected x86-64 minimum stack size of 40,960 bytes. This closes the checked x86-64 caller/ABI and minimum-stack slices; non-x86 architecture overrides and hardware/context-switch behavior remain open. No task, context, or build was run; source-only.

Sound datatype `WaitPort()` private-reply caller disposition (EK276; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-06): traced both waits in `workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/dispatch.c:864-901,1426-1445` into `PlayerProc()`'s message dispatch (`:2912-2923,2935-2947,3239-3244`). EK10615 scheduler priority/retry consequence recheck (2026-11-06; no body/path/LOC credit): re-read the PC, ARM32, and AArch64 `core_Schedule()` priority comparisons and `core_Dispatch()` ready-list selection, then traced ready requeue through `exec_TaskEnqueueReady()` to priority-sorted `Enqueue()`. A quantum-expired housekeeper can be rescheduled when a lower-priority eligible task exists, but because the housekeeper is priority 127 and is reinserted ahead of lower-priority nodes, dispatch selects it again; a lower-priority task does not time-slice it while it remains eligible. Equal-priority eligible peers already ahead can take a turn. Revised EK10615's trigger and impact language accordingly; other CPUs can select the ANY-affinity housekeeper while it is ready, so which CPU spins and how long remain schedule-dependent. No scheduling or tombstone cleanup was run.

EK8799 PPP/serial request-reuse interleaving recheck (2026-11-06; no body/path/LOC credit): traced the PPP unit task's `GetMsg(sd_Unit)` loop into `PerformIO()`/`WritePacket()` (`workbench/devs/networks/ppp/init.c:154-166`; `handler.c:47-58,147-164`) against its reused `SerTx` path through `SendPacket()`/`SendBYTES()` (`handler.c:184-204`; `ppp.c:937-957`; `serial.c:128-139`). Confirmed the serial `CMD_WRITE` branch keeps `STATUS_WRITES_PENDING` while a write is active and queues a reused request (`workbench/devs/serial/serial_init.c:453-545`); the write-empty interrupt calls `ReplyMsg()` before it dequeues the next queued write or clears pending status (`serial_interrupthandlers.c:143-184`). Thus, if PPP's independent SANA write runs after the old request is marked `NT_REPLYMSG` but before `InternalPutMsg()` adds it to the reply port, `WaitIO()` can return and `SendIO()` can link the same node onto the serial write queue before the old reply insertion links it onto the reply queue. The node can then be linked into two queues and the original `AddTail()` can overwrite its write-queue links. This strengthens the existing EK8799 caller consequence; no separate finding or LOC credit. No I/O, request, interrupt, or build was run.

Intuition synchronous screen-notification WaitPort caller ownership recheck (2026-11-07; no new EK or source-body/path/LOC credit): traced `FireScreenNotifyMessageCode()`'s `SNOTIFY_WAIT_REPLY` branch (`rom/intuition/intuition_misc.c:1130-1152`) against registration and the default asynchronous consumer (`startscreennotifytaglist.c:76-117`; `screennotifytask.c:28-69,76-126`). The synchronous branch creates a fresh reply port per notification, sends one message with that port, waits, dequeues the reply, frees the message and deletes the port; the registered recipient is the sole sender of the reply on this path. The default task instead services the separate persistent port used for non-waiting notifications. This selected caller adds no evidence of competing dequeue or stale borrowed-head use in `WaitPort()`. The broader public API caller inventory remains incomplete; no notification or reply interleaving was exercised; source-only.

m68k voluntary Wait switch Paula-mask semantics recheck (2026-11-07; no new EK or body/path/LOC credit): re-read the selected `arch/m68k-all/exec/wait.S` and `switch.S` against `compiler/include/hardware/intbits.h:43-44` and `rom/exec/chipset.h:14-26`. The raw `0x4000` write to INTENA clears `INTF_INTEN` because it omits `INTF_SETCLR`; `0xc000` sets master enable. Thus `m68k_VoluntarySwitch` disables Paula interrupts after constructing the prospective frame, then checks `tc_SigRecvd & tc_SigWait` and commits `TS_WAIT` plus `TaskWait` insertion before restoring master enable. An interrupt in that critical interval cannot publish a signal between the recheck and queue insertion; any signal in the earlier frame-build window is caught by this recheck. This corroborates the existing EK811/m68k no-finding disposition and closes the specific hardware-mask ambiguity, while physical interrupt latency/nesting and stack bounds remain unverified. No switch, signal, or build was run; source-only.

`spinlock_t.s_Owner` reader census for ARM/AArch64 init (2026-11-07; no new EK or path/LOC credit): searched all tracked C/header/assembly sources for `s_Owner` and separated spinlock owner uses from semaphore/library ownership fields. Only the selected PC spinlock implementation reads an existing `spinlock_t.s_Owner` while contending (`arch/all-pc/kernel/spinlock.c:50`), and PC `KrnSpinInit()` clears it (`spininit.c:22-25`). AArch64's selected lock/unlock/trylock and scheduler paths write the field after acquiring and clear it on unlock, with no in-tree read before initialization (`arch/aarch64-native/kernel/{spinlock,spintrylock,spinunlock,kernel_scheduler}.c`); ARM-native selected lock code has no `s_Owner` access. The ARM/AArch64 initializers' lock-word-only writes therefore do not establish an uninitialized-owner defect for selected in-tree callers. External consumers remain outside this census. No lock was acquired or build run; source-only.


PC SC_DISPATCH / RemTask return-path recheck (no new EK or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-07): traced the sole direct selected C caller `rom/exec/remtask.c:163` through the selected i386-PC and x86-64-PC syscall routes. `krnSysCall(SC_DISPATCH)` executes `int $0xfe`; the shared PC entry builds the exception frame and calls `core_IRQHandle`, which routes vector `0xfe` through `cpu_Trap` and the registered `core_SysCallHandler`. That handler dispatches the system syscall to `core_SysCall(SC_DISPATCH)`, which calls the selected `cpu_Dispatch`. `RemTask` has already marked the caller `TS_INVALID`; the dispatch path selects another ready task and leaves through its saved context with `core_LeaveInterrupt`, so no resumable caller frame is required and it does not return to `RemTask`. No mismatch established for these two PC targets. Other architecture handoffs remain open; no task removal or syscall was run; source-only.

StartNotify NetInfo selected-caller refinement (EK10912; 2026-11-07; no new ID or source-body/LOC credit): traced the NetInfo device path from OpenDevice startup to notification registration. Its server task is created without NP_CurrentDir (workbench/devs/netinfo/netinfo.c:172-179); CreateNewProc defaults to inheriting the opener's current-directory lock only for a Process whose pr_CurrentDir is non-null, and otherwise assigns BNULL (rom/dos/createnewproc.c:131,364-379,434-435). NetInfoStartup reads global SYS/userdb and SYS/groupdb variables without requiring a volume prefix (server.c:46-55), the passwd/group units retain those names as nim_Filename (passwdunit.c:48-59; groupunit.c:49-61), and entries.c passes that same name to StartNotify after opening/reading the database (entries.c:391-440). The workbench-devs-common target selects workbench-devs-netinfo through its active MetaMake edge, and workbench-complete includes workbench-devs (workbench/devs/netinfo/mmakefile.src:13,20-22; workbench/devs/mmakefile.src:4-13,21-27; workbench/mmakefile.src:4-13). This establishes an in-tree caller capable of supplying a relative name, but not a checked-in SYS/userdb/groupdb producer or a caller proven to have no current directory. EK10912 therefore remains conditional on both the relative configured name and opener state; the database file must also open before the notification call. No device, config variable, process, notification or build was used; source-only.

Exec ServiceTask WaitPort/drain caller closure (no new EK or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-07): traced its only `WaitPort(ServicePort)` call (`rom/exec/service.c:35-38,122`) with the task-port setup (`rom/exec/exec_init.c:318-327`) and self-removal producer (`rom/exec/remtask.c:130-163`). ServiceTask drains `GetMsg()` to NULL before waiting, then repeats the drain after wake; `WaitPort()` itself checks the queue before sleeping, so a request arriving between the last empty GetMsg and WaitPort is observed rather than lost. The service port is assigned to this one service task, and the producer enqueues the dying task only from self-removal. Since the return value is ignored and the queue is consumed with GetMsg, this caller does not rely on WaitPort's borrowed-head result. No separate lost-wakeup, multi-consumer or stale-message issue was established in this selected caller. The broader census remains open; no task removal, message or scheduling interleaving was run; source-only.

This narrows the normal configured path without withdrawing the source-level `StartNotify()` defect or claiming a checked-in trigger. No database, notification, device or build was used; source-only.

task.resource queued-hook registration and cleanup caller recheck (EK8803/EK9183 retained; 2026-11-07; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): re-read `AddTaskHook()`, `InitTaskHooks()`, `RunTaskHooks()`, `TaskListHookNode`, and the startup dispatcher. `InitTaskHooks(..., THF_IAR)` marks the late-init type queued (`tlhe_Node.ln_Pri = 1`); `RunTaskHooks()` walks `tlhe_Hooks` as `TaskListHookNode` and startup then changes the mode to `-1`, so later registrations use immediate dispatch. In queued mode, `AddTaskHook()` stores the supplied `Hook *` in a separately allocated wrapper but links the supplied hook's `h_MinNode`; the traversal consequently reads that list successor as `tln_Hook`, while the wrapper remains unlinked. This confirms EK8803's dispatch consequence and keeps the unchecked wrapper-allocation dereference separate as EK9183. An exact checked-in C-source search still finds no `AddTaskHook()` producer; startup's own late-init sequence calls only `InitTaskHooks()` and `RunTaskHooks()`. The broken queued interval therefore requires an external or future client registering between those calls. `TaskHooksDispose()` is empty, but no additional leak of client-owned Hook storage is established; the wrapper allocation already belongs to EK8803's consequence. No hook registration, dispatch, allocation failure, or build was run; source-only.

<a id="multiboot2-module-alignment-header-ek10927"></a>Multiboot2 module-alignment public-header layout and caller census (EK10927 added; 2026-11-08; no source-body/path/LOC credit): read the remaining Multiboot2 header definitions and traced all in-tree include and named-structure references. `struct mb2_header_tag_module_align` at `compiler/include/aros/multiboot2.h:104-110` contains the framebuffer width/height/depth payload, giving it a 20-byte size. The GNU Multiboot2 specification §3.1.11 defines type 6 as the 8-byte common tag header only and says the tag requests page alignment. <a id="multiboot-v1-public-layout-caller-reconciliation"></a>Multiboot v1 public-layout and selected-caller reconciliation (2026-11-08; no new EK or body/path/LOC credit): re-read `compiler/include/aros/multiboot.h` and traced direct structure consumers. The selected PC parser reads command line, map, basic memory, loader name, VBE/framebuffer and module fields (`arch/all-pc/bootstrap/multiboot1.c:66-277`); its bootconsole reads command-line and framebuffer fields (`arch/all-native/bootconsole/init_multiboot.c:14-61`); and the PC kernel consumes the normalized variable-size `mb_mmap` list (`arch/all-pc/kernel/kernel_mmap.c:102-185`). Hosted/MinGW/Unix kernel consumers accept `mb_mmap` through normalized boot tags and do not parse the v1 information structure. No additional selected declaration/caller mismatch established. Pointer validity and malformed-loader-record handling remain open; no boot record or build was used. Source-only.

<a id="arm-exidx-unwind-linker-symbols-ek10928"></a>ARM `.ARM.exidx` unwinder contract and link-selection trace (EK10928 added; 2026-11-08; no new body/path/LOC credit): re-read `compiler/startup/arm-exidx-unwind.c` and the startup makefile. The function computes `(__exidx_end - __exidx_start) / 8` and returns `__exidx_start` where both symbols are declared as unsigned objects; these linker-defined boundary symbols denote addresses. GCC's ARM unwinder contract returns the address of the first entry and computes the count as `&__exidx_end - &__exidx_start`; `.ARM.exidx` records are two words. All nine checked-in GNU GCC target patches inject the object into ARM links, with configure also listing it as an ARM no-startup object. The `__gnu_Unwind_Find_exidx` definition is strong; the weak attributes apply only to the separate `__cxa_*` fallback symbols, so uncertainty about their archive override does not change the table-lookup finding. Their independent C++ exception-runtime override behavior remains unverified. This trace corrects the earlier inference from generic specs alone; see the target-patch census below. No link, exception, boot, or build was run; source-only.

<a id="commandline-ek687-producer-census"></a>EK687 command-line producer recheck (no scope change; 2026-11-08): searched all checked-in C/C++ `RunCommand()` calls and inspected the selected producers most relevant to quoted trailing-star input. The Shell appends a newline before RunCommand (`workbench/c/Shell/convertLine.c:321-334`); POSIX `exec` serializes argv, escapes `*` and quotes when needed, then appends a newline (`compiler/crt/posixc/__exec.c:278-368,688-779`); the PC boot caller explicitly appends a newline (`rom/dos/boot.c:194-215`). The hosted boot caller passes unquoted `NOCOMPOSITION` without a newline (`arch/all-hosted/filesys/emul_handler/boot.c:85-95`), which does not trigger the quoted trailing-star parser path. Checked-in RunCommand debug calls pass empty or newline-only arguments. Installer is another direct caller (`workbench/utilities/Installer/execute.c:1247-1285`); its `collect_strings()` strips syntactic quotes before joining values (`:2449-2507`), so the checked path does not itself establish that exact quoted input. Exec `Wait()` implementation closeout (2026-11-08; no new EK or body/path/LOC credit): reread the complete signal wait body (`rom/exec/wait.c:24-144`) and checked the signal-mask and scheduling protocol against its documented `Forbid`/`Disable` behavior. It disables interrupts before taking the SMP task lock, checks received signals while locked, publishes `tc_SigWait`, saves and clears the task's forbid nesting before marking/enqueuing `TS_WAIT`, retains the lock through `KrnSwitch()` until the architecture saves context, then reacquires the lock on wake, restores nesting, consumes only matching received bits, unlocks, and reenables interrupts. The loop handles spurious/finished-task wakeups by rechecking the mask; `Wait(0)` remains an intentional indefinite wait. Exec `FindTask()` implementation closeout (2026-11-08; no new EK or body/path/LOC credit): reread the complete implementation (`rom/exec/findtask.c:20-128`) and reconciled its SMP lock transitions with EK799. The API documentation also explicitly warns that a returned task may be gone on return; caller lifetime cases are treated separately (including EK274/EK9482/EK10315). `FindTask(NULL)` returns the current task without list traversal, as expected. Exec `FindTaskByPID()` implementation closeout (2026-11-08; no new EK or body/path/LOC credit): reread the complete body (`rom/exec/findtaskbypid.c:18-149`) and compared its list-lock sequence with `FindTask()`. On SMP it scans Running, Spinning, Ready, then Wait, releasing each list lock before acquiring the next; each `et_UniqueID` read occurs while the containing-list lock is held. Exec `AllocSignal()`/`FreeSignal()` implementation closeout (2026-11-08; no new EK or body/path/LOC credit): read both complete vectors and `AllocTaskSignal()` (`rom/exec/allocsignal.c:24-144`; `rom/exec/freesignal.c:17-58`). Automatic allocation finds the lowest clear bit, returns `-1` when full, and updates allocation/exception/wait masks before clearing received state under the SMP task lock and interrupt disable. Explicit allocation constructs `1L << signalNum` without a range check; the valid bit-31 signed-shift issue is already EK8800, and invalid explicit values were not treated as an in-contract trigger. `FreeSignal(-1)` is a no-op; other values clear only the allocation bit using `1 << signalNum`, matching EK8800 for valid bit 31 and EK9261's unsigned-byte 255 sentinel path. Subsequent allocation clears stale per-bit state, so the asymmetric free does not alone establish stale signal delivery. No additional defect established for valid API inputs. No signal allocation/exhaustion or build was run; source-only.

Exec `SetSignal()`/`Signal()` implementation closeout (2026-11-08; no new EK or body/path/LOC credit): reread `SetSignal()` and the complete generic `Signal()` implementation (`rom/exec/setsignal.c:22-83`; `signal.c:114-462`) against the previously recorded `Wait()` pass. `SetSignal()` updates only current-task received bits while disabled and, on SMP, holding `tc_SpinLock`. Exec `SetExcept()`/`Exception()` implementation closeout (2026-11-08; no new EK or body/path/LOC credit): reread both complete bodies (`rom/exec/setexcept.c:23-91`; `exception.c:15-84`) and reconciled exception callback return semantics, pending-mask extraction, and dispatcher callers. `SetExcept()` serializes current-task mask changes with the SMP task lock, sets `TF_EXCEPT` when the new mask intersects received bits, and requests rescheduling while local interrupts remain disabled. `Exception()` clears the flag, temporarily clears interrupt-nesting state, extracts matching bits, enables interrupts around the callback, ORs the callback's returned mask back into the exception mask, and repeats for newly pending bits. The apparent unprotected XOR/read-modify-write race was already assessed under EK36 and withdrawn for the selected SMP routes because normal remote signals to a running task are delivered on that task's CPU and its interrupts stay disabled during extraction. Dispatcher omissions remain architecture-scoped (EK10217 and existing PC exception-dispatch findings); no new generic Exec exception-mask defect established. No callback, exception, or task switch was run; source-only.

Exec `WaitIO()`/`DoIO()` implementation closeout (2026-11-08; no new EK or body/path/LOC credit): reread both complete vectors (`rom/exec/waitio.c:15-83`; `doio.c:16-75`). `DoIO()` marks the request quick, validates the request and device pointers, calls the device's BeginIO, then delegates non-quick completion to `WaitIO()`. `WaitIO()` polls the request state rather than consuming an arbitrary port head, waits on the reply-port signal, rechecks after wake, and removes only its own node when marked replied. Exec `AttemptSemaphore()` / internal semaphore arbitration closeout (2026-11-08; no new EK or body/path/LOC credit): reread the public wrapper and both complete internal obtain/attempt helpers (`rom/exec/attemptsemaphore.c:18-58`; `semaphores.c:50-210`). Attempt acquires Forbid plus the SMP semaphore spinlock, speculatively increments `ss_QueueCount`, grants/increments nesting when free or recursively/shared-owned, and rolls the count back on contention before releasing locks and returning FALSE. Blocking obtain uses the same signed counters, queues a stack-local waiter request, drops the semaphore lock before Wait, and permits after wake. Exec `ObtainSemaphoreList()`/`ReleaseSemaphoreList()` implementation closeout (2026-11-08; no new EK or body/path/LOC credit): reread both complete list APIs (`rom/exec/obtainsemaphorelist.c:15-162`; `releasesemaphorelist.c:15-58`). Obtain forbids local task switches, walks the caller-protected intrusive list, arbitrates each semaphore with its own SMP lock, stores one waiter in each semaphore's embedded `ss_MultipleLink`, then waits/rechecks ownership before proceeding. Its `WORD failedObtain` narrowing and associated wait behavior are EK8781; forced removal while embedded waiter nodes remain queued is EK8880. The API's documented external list/ss_MultipleLink serialization contract remains necessary. Release simply walks the same list and invokes `ReleaseSemaphore()` once per entry; partial progress is inherent if callers violate ownership/lifetime assumptions and no independent defect was established. No semaphore list operation or build was run; source-only.

Exec `Procure()`/`Vacate()` implementation closeout (2026-11-08; no new EK or body/path/LOC credit): reread both complete asynchronous semaphore APIs (`rom/exec/procure.c:15-134`; `vacate.c:16-89`) and their shared `ReleaseSemaphore()` message conversion. Procure publishes the caller-owned bid under the semaphore lock, queues it with the shared/exclusive marker in the overlaid waiter field when contended, and replies immediately after direct grant; Vacate clears the public semaphore result, removes/replies a still-queued bid and reverses its queue count, or drops the lock and releases an already granted hold. ReleaseSemaphore removes queued bids and restores the semaphore pointer before ReplyMsg. Existing queue-counter boundary behavior is EK9071; timed-pthread extra nesting is EK567; task/message layout, stack lifetime and late-reply caller questions remain in EK9895/EK8880 and the withdrawn EK9266 analysis. No new ownership-transfer or cancellation defect established in these bodies. No semaphore message or build was used; source-only.

Plain-pool MungWall allocation route recheck (EK30 expanded; 2026-11-08; no body/LOC credit): traced the public `AllocPooled()` vector through non-managed `InternalAllocPooled()` and puddle growth (`rom/exec/allocpooled.c:70-87`; `rom/exec/memory.c:1038-1059,1071-1185,1217-1224`). On an N-bit `IPTR`, request `IPTR_MAX - MEMPOOL_WORSTALIGN - MUNGWALL_TOTAL_SIZE + 2`: the alignment addition is representable and saved as `origSize`, then the unchecked wall addition wraps the pool allocator request to one byte. A valid ordinary pool can grow a standard puddle for that small request and `stdAlloc()` can return a block; the subsequent MungWall builder writes a fixed pre-wall/header and original-size-based post-wall beyond the reservation. This route is restricted to non-managed pools; managed `AllocPooled()` uses the provider callback. It is distinct from EK9124, which wraps the alignment addition with MungWall disabled. No near-maximum request, allocation, build, or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only.

<a id="createpool-configured-size-arithmetic-reconciliation-ek10938"></a>
`CreatePool()` configured-size arithmetic reconciliation (EK10938 added; no body/LOC credit; 2026-11-08): re-read `CreatePool()`'s overhead additions and page rounding against both plain and managed allocation paths. The compact handle size for a plain pool is independently derived from the pool structure, and its small-growth path clamps the next puddle to a request-based minimum. The managed branch differs: a wrapped zero `puddleSize` is passed to `AllocMemHeader()`. `nommu_AllocMem()` accepts zero against any matching header with nonnegative free-byte count; TLSF rejects zero, but a subsequent plain header can reach `stdAlloc(0)`, which rounds the size to zero, returns an existing free-chunk address without consuming it, and leaves the parent free list in place. `AllocMemHeader()` then treats that pointer as a new plain region, subtracts `MEMHEADER_TOTAL` from zero, and writes a wrapped `mh_Free`/`mc_Bytes` extent into the parent chunk. EK10938 records this conditional corrupted-header path. Large-request alignment/addition overflow in ordinary pool allocation is separately covered by EK30/EK783 and was not counted again. No allocation or build was run; source-only.


`DeletePool()` teardown follow-up to EK10938 (2026-11-08; no separate finding or body/LOC credit): re-read the plain and managed teardown paths against the newly documented `CreatePool()` zero-size header case. The plain destructor reads `PoolMagic`, walks the puddle list, then frees the initial handle (`rom/exec/deletepool.c:62-110`). A forged handle/puddle produced by EK10938 can therefore carry corrupted bounds into the normal free path, but this is a continuation of the same failed construction invariant, not a separate teardown defect. For valid handles, the loop saves each successor before freeing non-handle puddles and frees the initial handle last. No independent `DeletePool()` issue was established; concurrent pool users remain pending. No pool was created or deleted; source-only.

`AllocMemHeader()` caller census after EK10938 (2026-11-08; no separate finding or body/LOC credit): a repository-wide C/header search confirmed two executable callers: `CreatePool()`'s managed first-puddle branch and `InternalAllocPooled()` growth (`rom/exec/createpool.c:142`; `rom/exec/memory.c:1150`). The latter supplies a size derived from the aligned allocation request; near-maximum request overflow there is already tracked by EK30/EK783/EK9124 depending on the adjustment and MungWall configuration, and no third independent zero-size producer was established. Existing `CreatePool()` checks for a NULL `AllocMemHeader()` result, but that does not protect against a non-NULL fabricated plain header returned by `nommu_AllocMem(0)`; this remains within EK10938. No external helper call exists in the checked-in tree. Source-only; no allocation or build was run.

`CreatePool()` configured-size caller census for EK10938 (2026-11-08; no new finding or body/LOC credit): searched all 167 textual `CreatePool()` matches and separated declarations/comments from calls. Two maintained configurable routes were traced. Standard MUI List stores its public `ULONG` `MUIA_List_PoolPuddleSize` tag in a signed `LONG` and passes it through to `CreatePool()` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/include/libraries/mui.h:2163`; `workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/list.c:91,1197-1199,1289-1294`), allowing a caller-selected high tag to become the negative overhead sum on 32- and 64-bit builds. NList reads its public puddle-size attribute into `ULONG` and forwards it unchanged on non-AmigaOS4 builds (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/include/mui/NList_mcc.h:128`; `docs/MCC_NList.doc:1492-1498`; `nlist_mcc/NList_mcc.c:621-634`); this route wraps on 32-bit builds. Defaults are 2,008 and 2,048 bytes; no in-tree caller supplies a near-maximum value. Other inspected calls pass fixed or bounded sizes; dynamic products and config values remain caller-specific and are not claimed exhaustive beyond the textual census. Both routes remain conditional on a caller supplying the boundary value and the required mixed-header allocation order. No pool or MUI object was created; source-only.

POSIX path-conversion whole-tree caller census (2026-11-09; `compiler/crt/posixc/__upath.c`): searched the full maintained source tree for both conversion vectors and traced all 33 call sites across 26 consumer files. Confirmed the unguarded result uses represented by EK10632, EK10634, EK10644, EK10664 and EK10856. Checked wrappers reject NULL before DOS/libc use; `symlink()` copies the first converted path before requesting the second from the shared per-task buffer. A state-by-state trace disproved EK10805: `..` converts to `/` within its requested three bytes, and `dir/..` converts to `dir//` within its seven-byte request. Consequently the second conversion in `rmdir("..")` requests a smaller buffer and `realloc_nocopy()` does not move/free the input; EK10860 is also withdrawn. No additional independent caller mismatch was established. External callers, allocation-failure manifestations and live filesystem behavior remain unverified; source-only.


POSIX parent-path conversion candidate withdrawals (2026-11-09; `compiler/crt/posixc/__upath.c`, `rmdir.c`, `remove.c`): replayed the converter states directly from source. Terminal `..` emits one slash and a NUL, not `../`; `dir/..` emits `dir//`, so neither exceeds the original input-sized allocation. This withdraws EK10805. For `rmdir("..")`, the first result is `/`; `remove()`'s second conversion requests two bytes after the first requested three, and `realloc_nocopy()` keeps the existing block for this small shrink, so the input is not freed before it is read. The second conversion maps `/` to `:`, but no distinct observable `rmdir()` defect was established because the requested ancestor contains the current directory. EK10860 is withdrawn without replacement. No path, handler, allocation or build was exercised; source-only.

This extends only the Exec/DOS core caller slice; the remaining wait-then-dequeue callers across devices, filesystems, GUI and networking are still open, as recorded in the primary `rom/exec/waitport.c` inventory row. AmigaGuide ARexx shutdown `WaitPort()` and `Forbid()` cross-check (EK276 caller slice; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-11): traced the support-process exit path in `workbench/classes/datatypes/amigaguide/process.c:352-389` against `SendRexxCommand()` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/amigaguide/util.c:734-781`) and Exec `Forbid()`/`Wait()`/`WaitPort()` (`rom/exec/forbid.c:31-62`; `rom/exec/wait.c:66-76`; `rom/exec/waitport.c:73-101`). CDC ACM `OpenDevice()` `WaitPort()` caller disposition (OD3366 cross-reference; no new EK or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-11): traced `devOpen()`'s initial `SDCMD_SETPARAMS` enqueue and same-unit-port `GetMsg()`/`WaitPort()` loop (`rom/usb/classes/cdcacm/dev.c:117-127`) through the selected class worker's command dequeue and `ReplyMsg()` (`cdcacm.class.c:789-849`, especially `:846-849`) and Exec `OpenDevice()`'s synchronous vector call under `Forbid()` (`rom/exec/opendevice.c:89-135`). On a uniprocessor, Open can dequeue its own setup request and return before the worker applies it. On ExecSMP, if the worker consumes it first, completion is sent to the IORequest's `mn_ReplyPort` while Open waits on the unit command port; if no unrelated command arrives there, Open remains blocked. This is the existing caller-level OD3366, not a `WaitPort()` implementation defect or borrowed-head race. No device, request, task schedule, or build was run; source-only.

SFS handler close-result cross-check for EK8840 (2026-11-11; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): reviewed the selected `rom/filesys/SFS/FS/filesystemmain.c` `ACTION_WRITE` and `ACTION_END` cases plus `locks.c` and the SFS source manifest. A failed `writetofile()` rolls back its transaction, restores the existing update lock's cursors/size/data, and returns `-1` without setting `EFL_MODIFIED`; `ACTION_END` skips its modified-object update and returns success when `freelock()` releases the valid lock. For a lock already marked modified, close-time metadata errors are also explicitly ignored before the same free/result path. Thus a final buffered SFS write failure such as exhausted disk-full recovery is independently hidden by DOS `Close()` when handler cleanup succeeds. FAT and NTFS `ACTION_END` validate the lock and can return an error; they are not counted as confirmed false-success paths here. Expanded EK8840's trigger and affected handlers; no second finding added. No disk I/O or build was run; source-only.

DOS close handler result comparison extension for EK8840 (2026-11-11; no new finding or source-body/path/LOC credit): extended the selected-handler check from RAMFS/SFS to FAT and optional SMBFS. FAT `OpWrite()` errors return -1, but `ACTION_END` returns `DOSTRUE` after `TestLock()` succeeds and the valid lock is freed. SMBFS `Action_Write()` returns -1 on its write-protect flag or `smba_write()` error, while `Action_End()` ignores `smba_close()` and unconditionally returns success; its write-protect action can set the flag while the volume is active. Thus both independently confirm the DOS `Close()` status overwrite. Recorded NTFS's separate readonly response behavior: `ACTION_WRITE` places positive `ERROR_DISK_WRITE_PROTECTED` in `dp_Res1`, so it is not counted as a normal negative-write trigger pending a distinct packet-result review. AFS, console, CDFS, pipe and other handler/client contracts remain open; no subsystem completion implied. No file, network share, volume state, write or build was exercised; source-only.
