DOS Write/NTFS readonly packet-result cross-check (FS-088; no EK or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-11): traced the full checked-in boundary from the `NTFS_READONLY` `ACTION_WRITE` branch through `ProcessPackets()` result publication, DOS `Write()` and `InternalFlush()`. NTFS publishes positive `ERROR_DISK_WRITE_PROTECTED` (214) in `dp_Res1` with `dp_Res2` left zero; DOS returns it unchanged although `Write()` documents -1 for failure, and `InternalFlush()` counts any nonnegative result as progress. The filesystem report records FS-088; this closes that specific DOS/handler result-contract question while other handler callers remain open. No write, NTFS volume, or build was used; source-only.

PC APIC duplicate-controller instance-count race recheck (no new EK; 2026-11-11): re-read `smp_Wake()`'s per-CPU launch/readiness loop and the AP bootstrap call order (`arch/all-pc/kernel/smp.c:233-314`; `smp_exec.c:193-231`; `smp.c:118-139`) against `krnAddInterruptController()` and every `ic_Count` use (`rom/kernel/kernel_interruptcontroller.c:33-70,137-150`; repository-wide `ic_Count` census). In the normal path BSP waits for each AP's ready lock before launching the next, and the AP releases that lock only after `cpu_BootStrap()` returns from `core_APIC_Init()`, so normal AP increments do not overlap. If one AP misses the bounded readiness wait, the loop continues and a late AP may overlap a later AP's `ic_Count++`; this remains an exceptional startup-time race. The full use census confirms `ic_Count` is otherwise read only by `krnInitInterruptControllers()`, which runs once before SMP wake, while the AP's returned instance value is consumed only by a debug print in `core_APIC_Init()`. Thus a lost increment can make the encoded/debug instance number inaccurate, but no current selected interrupt setup or dispatch consequence is established. Existing caller-row qualification is retained; no new finding or path/LOC credit. No AP startup, timeout, or race was induced; source-only.

EK10171 `OpenDevice()` immediate write-boundary refinement (2026-11-12; no source-body/path/LOC credit): re-read the m68k `CreateIORequest()` and `OpenDevice()` thunks, native constructor, `OpenDevice()` implementation, and generated `IORequest`/`IOStdReq` layouts (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:2070-2077,2289-2297`; `rom/exec/createiorequest.c:57-73`; `rom/exec/opendevice.c:98-103`; `m68kemu_shadow_layouts.h:2165-2200,4549-4550`). With the ordinary 48-byte m68k `IOStdReq` size, the thunk allocates 48 native bytes, while native `OpenDevice()` writes `io_Unit` at offset 56 and `io_Device` at offset 48. This is an immediate native out-of-allocation write before the later `DoIO()`/`CheckIO()`/`WaitIO()` `IOStdReq` synchronization mismatch. Expanded the canonical EK10171 detail with those exact stores and retained the 64-bit-host optional-m68kemu scope; neighboring-data consequences remain allocator-layout dependent. No guest request, device open, or build was performed; source-only.

EK9278 MungWall post-wall overwrite verification (2026-11-12; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): traced the near-maximum `AllocVec()` request through `AllocMem()` and `MungWall_Build()` (`rom/exec/allocvec.c:57-79`; `rom/exec/allocmem.c:99-110`; `rom/exec/mungwall.c:28-68`). For the one-byte wrapped request, MungWall's post-wall begins immediately after that one-byte user extent; the aligned hidden `IPTR` store therefore overwrites three guard bytes on 32-bit or seven on 64-bit targets (`compiler/arossupport/include/debug.h:224-235`). `FreeVec()` passes the stored wrapped size to `FreeMem()`, and `CheckHeader()` checks the damaged post-wall and raises the memory-insane alert (`rom/exec/freevec.c:48-56`; `rom/exec/mungwall.c:125-154`). The additional guard-corruption consequence requires the optional boot `mungwall` setting; the undersized successful allocation remains the general defect. No in-tree near-limit caller was identified in the existing census. No allocation, free, alert, or runtime path was exercised; source-only.

EK9278 unmanaged pooled-vector MungWall guard trace (2026-11-12; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): followed the wrapped one-byte `AllocVecPooled()` request through `AllocPooled()` to `InternalAllocPooled()` (`rom/exec/allocvecpooled.c:76-84`; `rom/exec/allocpooled.c:70-87`; `rom/exec/memory.c:1048-1064,1208-1224`). The pooled allocator reserves `MEMPOOL_WORSTALIGN` bytes for its own header/alignment and one byte for the requested payload before `MungWall_Build()` places the post-wall. `AllocVecPooled()` then writes its hidden `IPTR` size at the returned payload pointer, so the store overlaps the guard by `sizeof(IPTR)-1` bytes. `FreeVecPooled()` routes its stored wrapped size through `FreePooled()` to `InternalFreePooled()` and `MungWall_Check()`, which checks that post-wall (`freevecpooled.c:59-73`; `memory.c:1239-1257`; `mungwall.c:125-154,185-224`). This additional guard corruption requires an unmanaged pool and the optional MungWall setting; managed pools remain excluded. No pool allocation/free or MungWall alert was exercised; source-only.

m68kemu diskfont output-buffer and handle round-trip pass (EK9432 expanded; 2026-11-12; no new ID or body/path/LOC credit): compared all three registered diskfont thunk wrappers at `rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:914-936` against the public vector list (`workbench/libs/diskfont/diskfont.conf:13-19`), selected implementations and structures. `AvailFonts()` forwards its guest buffer unchanged; `BufferInfoCreate()`/`BufferInfoAdd()` write native `AvailFonts`/`TAvailFonts` records, native-width pointers and (for AFF_TAGGED) native `TagItem` arrays into that buffer (`workbench/libs/diskfont/availfonts.c:149-215`; `compiler/include/diskfont/diskfont.h:78-96`; `graphics/text.h:72-88`). The m68k records use 32-bit pointers, unlike the 64-bit host records, and little-endian hosts additionally retain host byte order; guest consumers cannot reliably parse the output. `NewFontContents()` returns a native `AllocVec()` allocation through D0, while `DisposeFontContents()` resolves A1 with `THUNK_PTR()` (`m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:923-936`; implementation `workbench/libs/diskfont/newfontcontents.c:249-266`; `disposefontcontents.c:41-63`), so the returned handle has no guest-address/shadow round trip. `FontContentsHeader` and its entries are fixed-width and pointer-free, so no structure-layout mismatch is claimed for that return object; the defect is the unmapped host allocation handle. The optional m68kemu library registers these vectors, but no maintained emulated diskfont caller was found. Bodies already have full-body credit; no guest call or build was run; source-only.

m68kemu DOS `Info()` output-layout trace (EK9432 expanded; 2026-11-12; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): checked the generated `Info()` wrapper's D2 pointer resolution (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:948-954`) against the public vector and native `Info()` packet forwarding (`rom/dos/dos.conf:72`; `rom/dos/info.c:44-63`). The optional `kernel-fs-ram` target provides a concrete selected `ACTION_INFO` producer: `CmdInfo()` writes each `InfoData` field through the supplied address (`rom/filesys/ram/handler.c:278-288`; `commands.c:1679-1700`; target `rom/filesys/ram/mmakefile.src`). The checked-in shadow-layout record gives `InfoData` as 36 bytes for m68k and 48 bytes for 64-bit AROS (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_shadow_layouts.h:2240-2253`), so a successful native write to a guest-sized 36-byte buffer can extend twelve bytes beyond the guest object and place `id_VolumeNode`/`id_InUse` at host offsets. Little-endian host writes also leave the multibyte guest fields in host order. Scoped this as an additional EK9432 structure-boundary case; `kernel-fs-ram` is an explicit target and is not claimed as default package inclusion, and no maintained emulated caller was found. Existing bodies already had credit; no guest call or build was run; source-only.

Ramdrive OFS formatter signed-bitmap-shift caller trace (EK8800 expanded; no new finding or source-body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-12): followed `unitentry()`'s successful startup through `FormatOFS()` (`workbench/devs/ramdrive_device.c:518-520,738-767`). The formatter initializes bitmap bits for sectors 2–1,759 with `FreeBitMapBlock()`, then marks the root and bitmap sectors allocated using `AllocBitMapBlock()`. Both helpers calculate `bit = (block - 2) % 32` and use signed `1L << bit` (`:706-733`); the selected loop includes bit index 31 repeatedly. `LONG`/`ULONG` are fixed 32-bit (`compiler/include/exec/types.h:34-39`), while the literal `1L` is 32-bit on 32-bit-long targets, making these bit-31 shifts undefined under the configured C standards through C17. If the compiler does not preserve the intended high bit, the initialized OFS bitmap can have incorrect allocation state. This is an additional selected caller of EK8800, not a separate root cause; runtime/compiler-output consequences remain conditional. No Ramdrive unit was started, formatted, or mounted; source-only.
Exec `ServiceTask()` ordinary WaitPort/GetMsg caller pass (2026-11-12; no new EK or body/path/LOC credit): re-read the only direct `WaitPort()` call in `rom/exec/*.c` (`service.c:37-38,122`) with `WaitPort()`, `GetMsg()`, and `InternalPutMsg()` synchronization (`waitport.c:62-97`; `getmsg.c:54-75`; `putmsg.c:72-107`). `ServiceTask()` drains the service queue with repeated `GetMsg()` before waiting; requeued task requests use `InternalPutMsg()` and the next `WaitPort()` rechecks queue non-emptiness before sleeping. The producer's queue insertion and waiter recheck therefore cover the empty-scan-to-wait interval, and the single service task is the only selected receiver of this private port. Exec initialization supplies that port to the service task (`exec_init.c:318-327`); the sole producer is `RemTask()` (`remtask.c:140`). No local WaitPort/GetMsg race or lifetime defect was established in this core caller. This closes only the Exec service-queue caller slice; the ordinary waiter/dequeue caller census elsewhere remains open. No task removal, message, or build was run; source-only.

<a id="intuition-dosyncaction-reply-publication-caller-ek8799"></a>

### Intuition `DoSyncAction()` independent-wake path into EK8799 (2026-11-12; no body/path/LOC credit)

Traced the selected synchronous action path through the reply-publication window. When called outside the input.device task, `DoSyncAction()` creates its stack-local `IOStdReq`, `MsgPort`, and `InputEvent`, queues the action, assigns the reply port the caller's `SIGB_INTUITION` bit, and sends `IND_WRITEEVENT` with `IECLASS_NULL` using `DoIO()` (`rom/intuition/inputhandler_actions.c:583-640`). `input.device` adds the event and calls `ForwardQueuedEvents()` before the common `ReplyMsg()` (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:400-415,433`); `ForwardQueuedEvents()` calls registered handlers synchronously (`:94-127`), and Intuition's selected handler invokes `HandleIntuiActions()` before processing the event (`rom/intuition/inputhandler.c:1929`). The action completes, sets `am->done`, and signals the caller (`inputhandler_actions.c:678-706`) before the input-device task enters `ReplyMsg()`. Because this is the same signal bit that DoIO's temporary port uses, on ExecSMP the caller can wake during `ReplyMsg()`'s `NT_REPLYMSG`-before-queue-insertion interval. If WaitIO observes that state, it returns early; `DoSyncAction()` sees `msg->done` and deletes the temporary port, while input.device still has to finish `InternalPutMsg()` using the request and reply port. This supplies a selected Intuition caller path and concrete stack-port lifetime consequence for EK8799; it is one caller trace of that finding, not a new root cause. `input.device` and Intuition are selected in the ROM dependency graph (`rom/mmakefile.src:17,21,98,103`). Rechecked `MH2Int_MakeMenusInactive()`'s separate stack reply port but found no independent signal source to its menu task during reply publication, so that case is not counted. Relevant function bodies already have coverage credit; no body/path/LOC totals change. No task schedule, event, I/O request, or build was run; source-only.

WaitPort hosted/native handler startup caller pass (2026-11-12; no new EK or body/path/LOC credit): traced the two additional selected direct `WaitPort()` callers in `arch/all-hosted/filesys/emul_handler/emul_handler.c:1398-1439` and `arch/all-native/econsole/econsole.c:217-233`. Each obtains the current Process's private `pr_MsgPort`, waits for the startup packet, immediately removes that packet with `GetMsg()`, then publishes that same port as `dn_Task`; each handler task is the sole selected consumer of its port. Emul subsequently drains its packet port with `GetMsg()` after `Wait()` reports the packet signal, while econsole serially replies to one packet before waiting for the next. The port queue remains authoritative across the WaitPort-to-GetMsg interval, and the checked handlers establish no competing consumer that could remove the head. No independent WaitPort race or null-GetMsg path is established for these callers. This closes only these two handler caller slices; tree-wide wait-then-dequeue ownership review remains open. No packet, handler, or build was run; source-only.

Hosted ROMTag range producer recheck for EK144 (2026-11-12; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): confirmed `arch/all-hosted/bootstrap/mmakefile.src:4,28-32` selects `bootstrap.c` for the hosted bootstrap. Its static `km[]` starts with zero-valued `KRN_KernelLowest`/`KRN_KernelHighest` entries (`bootstrap.c:102-106`), but the successful kernel-load path calls `GetKernelSize()`, allocates the RO image, requires `LoadKernel()` to succeed, then replaces those entries with `[ro_addr, ro_addr + ro_size - 1]` before `kick(kernel_entry, km)` (`:339-393,415`). Thus this zero initializer is not an empty range on the ordinary successful hosted boot path. This does not establish behavior for malformed ELF inputs, a failing/partial external loader contract, or other platform boot/firmware producers; EK144 remains conditional on a supplied range scan yielding no Residents, with no maintained hosted trigger established. The source bodies were already credited. No ELF, loader, or boot was run; source-only.

<a id="arm32-raspi-live-dtb-overlap-ek10944"></a>
ARM32 Raspberry Pi live DTB overlap recheck (EK10944 added; 2026-11-12; no body/path/LOC credit): compared the full DTB lifetime in `arch/arm-raspi/boot/boot.c` with the selected AArch64 sibling. ARM32 obtains `mem_upper` from `/memory/reg`, computes the kernel interval below it, clears that full interval, and only afterward copies the original DTB from `atags`; it later reparses and publishes that copy. AArch64 explicitly tests the DTB interval against the region before clearing and moves the kernel lower on overlap. This establishes corruption if the ARM32 DTB overlaps the cleared interval. AArch64 comments say Pi firmware may put the live DTB near the top of ARM memory, but no ARM32 firmware layout or DTB was inspected to prove the trigger. Added EK10944 as conditional, with the consequence qualified by overlap extent. No path or LOC credit changed; no build, boot or firmware image was used.

<a id="aarch64-raspi-live-dtb-overlap-guard-recheck"></a>
AArch64 Raspberry Pi live-DTB overlap guard recheck (no new EK; 2026-11-12): traced `dtb_addr` from the bootstrap entry through initial parse, interval calculation, zeroing, copy, tag publication and second parse (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/boot.c:416-438,895-940,1049`). For ordinary physical address ranges, if the source DTB intersects the exact kernel interval that will be cleared, the guard chooses a new kernel interval whose upper boundary is the 2 MiB-aligned DTB start; the subsequent clear therefore does not overwrite the DTB before `memcpy()`. This is the protection absent from ARM32 EK10944. No independent AArch64 overlap candidate established. Validation of malformed near-address-space-limit pointers, arithmetic wrap, and insufficient-RAM boot sizing remain outside this overlap-only disposition. No firmware, DTB or boot was used; source-only.

AHI driver request-list Enqueue caller slice (no EK finding or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-12): traced all six selected `Enqueue()` call expressions in `workbench/devs/AHI/Device/devcommands.c:1169,1268,1298-1304,1460` through `NewWriter()`, `AddWriter()`, `RethinkPlayers()` and `RemPlayers()`. DynModule glue `WaitPort()` receive-loop caller pass (EK276; 2026-11-12; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): traced the selected optional `dynmodule_glue.c` receive loop (`compiler/dynmodule/dynmodule_glue.c:52-59,126-177`) through the sole `__dynglue_GetIFMSg()` caller. While `inuse` is true, the one module task waits and immediately dequeues one message with `GetMsg()` before dispatch and `ReplyMsg()`; `Open`, `Close`, and `Dispose` state transitions are processed serially by that same consumer. When `inuse` becomes false, the loop exits and `__dynglue_DisposeIFPort()` drains remaining messages before port deletion. No second in-tree consumer of this interface port was found, so the caller does not establish a competing dequeue between WaitPort's nonempty check and the subsequent GetMsg. The optional `dynmodglue` link-library target is declared in `compiler/dynmodule/mmakefile.src:3-5,12-30`, but its aggregate dependency is commented; in-tree module clients and post-disposal external sender lifetime remain unestablished. Existing glue findings EK664, EK693, EK694 and loader findings are unchanged. No dynamic module, message or teardown was run; source-only.

USBHub and SiS900 `WaitPort()` cross-ledger caller closure (EK276; 2026-11-12; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): traced the two selected USBHub reply waits (`workbench/devs/USB/stack/usbhubclass.c:204-215,278-292`) and the SiS900 worker/creator startup handshakes (`workbench/devs/networks/sis900/unit.c:715-730,948-976`). On successful allocation, the hub task is the sole consumer and replies before the caller deletes its port; no EK276 competing consumer is established. Nouveau/VMware DRM timer-command `WaitPort()` caller closure (EK276; 2026-11-12; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): traced both selected `timer_send_cmd()` copies (`workbench/hidds/{nouveau,vmwaresvga}/drm-compat/linux_time.c:348-386`) through `timer_proc_main()` (`:288-325`). Each command uses a stack-local message and freshly initialized stack-local reply port; the single timer process dequeues commands from `timer_cmd_port`, sets `cmd.result`, and replies to the request. The caller waits on its private port, removes the response with `GetMsg()`, and frees its signal before returning, so the returned `WaitPort()` head is not concurrently consumed on this selected handshake. USB serial Open-vector same-port `WaitPort()` finding recheck (OD3366; 2026-11-12; no new EK, path or LOC credit): revalidated CDC ACM, CP210x, PL2303 and Palm PDA Open callsites against Exec `OpenDevice()` (`rom/exec/opendevice.c:92-114,130-135`), the `EXEC_LOCK_LIST_READ_AND_FORBID` macro (`rom/exec/exec_locks.h:46-50,58-62`), and the `Forbid()` UP/ExecSMP contract (`rom/exec/forbid.c:55-60`). The macro's system lock protects DeviceList lookup and is released before the vector; local Forbid remains active until OpenDevice returns. On UP, the worker cannot run during the synchronous vector, allowing the opener's GetMsg loop to remove its own queued setup request. On ExecSMP another CPU may run the worker; if it dequeues first, the completion goes to the IORequest's reply port while Open waits on the unit port. This confirms OD3366's split configuration consequences; the candidate and its detailed driver/caller scope remain in the Other Drivers report. No device open or task schedule was run; source-only.

DiskImage shared reply-port `WaitPort()` control/reload caller recheck (OD10428; 2026-11-12; no new EK, path or LOC credit): completed the separate `main_vectors.c` caller trace beyond the earlier startup-port slice. `Internal_UnitControl()` and `ReloadPlugins()` serialize the shared `DiskImageMsg` and reply port with `unit->MsgSemaphore`, set the reply port to `PA_SIGNAL` for the current task, enqueue one request to the unit worker, wait, dequeue the reply, then restore `PA_IGNORE` (`workbench/devs/diskimage/device/main_vectors.c:41-74,201-230`). The unit worker is the sole consumer of `unit->MsgPort` and replies to this request (`device/unit.c:152-181`). However, the shared reply port is made by `CreatePortNoSignal()`, which MEMF_CLEARs it and never allocates a signal bit (`support/ports.c:30-40`); these callers set action/task but leave `mp_SigBit == 0`. Exec `WaitPort()` therefore waits on bit zero (`rom/exec/waitport.c:73-80`), which is `SIGF_ABORT` (`compiler/include/exec/tasks.h:146`), and can consume a pending or arriving abort while waiting for the operation's reply. This is the existing caller-side OD10428 in the Other Drivers report; no separate Exec finding is added. The same signal-mode pattern appears in selected unit-startup code and is covered by OD10428. No signal, unit-control operation, task or build was run; source-only.

EK752 direct AllocAbs caller and aligned-helper bound recheck (2026-11-12; no body/path/LOC credit): repeated the repository-wide direct `AllocAbs()` census and re-read `compiler/alib/liballocaligned.c:57-77` with its sole maintained caller, CD32's fixed 1 KiB and 64 KiB allocations at alignment 1 KiB/4 KiB (`arch/m68k-amiga/devs/cd/cd32.c:1604-1612`; structure sizes at `:86-95`). Given the helper's checked nonzero power-of-two/aligned-size contract, the maximum representable valid `memSize` is `IPTR_MAX - alignMask`, so `memSize + alignMask` does not wrap. DOSBoot selected USB HIDD late-discovery path (EK9308 rechecked; 2026-11-12; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): confirmed both ARM and AArch64 Raspberry Pi boot manifests select `USB/massstorage` alongside DOSBoot (`arch/arm-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:182,187-193`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:215,226-232`). `Storage_Init()` registers the class with HIDD USB (`workbench/devs/USB/classes/MassStorage/storage_init.c:65-73`); the hub's separately created task processes connected ports and calls `HIDD_USB_NewDevice()` (`usbhubclass.c:183-193,583-590`), and the USB stack constructs the matched class object (`usbclass.c:351-363`). The storage class sets up its unit, then calls `USBMSS_AddVolume()` (`storageclass.c:315-322`); that helper starts an `NP_Synchronous` automounter which calls the partition scan and `AddBootNode()` (`storage_volumes.c:274-275,395-405,488-505`). DOS `CreateNewProc()` waits for this child to exit (`rom/dos/createnewproc.c:566-582,987-995`), but this waits only between the USB class task and its child, not against DOSBoot's count/allocation/menu phase. `AddBootNode()` takes `BootSemaphore` for the append, while DOSBoot acquires it only around final reorder (`dosboot_init.c:218-235,250-278`; `addbootnode.c:128-140,213-219`); DOS boot-up is not flagged until the chosen device passes the first bootability check (`rom/dos/cliinit.c:490-498`). A device enumerated during the intervening DOSBoot setup can therefore still be appended after the count snapshot. This confirms a second selected Raspberry Pi USB stack path for the existing conditional EK9308; it does not assert a deterministic timing or default trigger. No USB device, boot sequence, list mutation, or build was run; source-only.

P96 bitmap residency caller review for CopyMemQuick (2026-11-12; no finding or LOC credit): traced `P96GFXBitmap__ToFRAM()` and `P96GFXBitmap__BMToVRAM()` to bitmap-size construction, RAM allocation, and the P96 VRAM MemHeader (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/p96gfx/p96gfx_bitmapclass.c:67-85,180-216`; `p96gfx_hiddclass.c:1756-1772`; `rom/exec/allocate.c:51-70,116-144`). Selected AmigaVideo CopyMemQuick caller reconciliation (2026-11-12; no Exec finding or LOC credit): traced every `CopyMemQuick()` occurrence under `arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo`. `USE_UCOP_DIRECT` is defined as 1, excluding the user-copper copies in the compositor/chipset `#if !USE_UCOP_DIRECT` blocks. The compiled fixed PixFmt tag copies are 17 `TagItem`s (136 bytes on the 32-bit m68k target); their source/destination pointers are offsets in the AllocVec-backed tag table, each advanced by 136 bytes. `initvpicopper()` copies `MaxCount << 2` bytes between the `CopLStart`/`CopSStart` instruction buffers allocated with `AllocVec`; this meets the multiple-of-ULONG and allocation-alignment requirements when allocation succeeds. VMM library explicit initialization-failure reply ownership recheck (EK10945; 2026-11-12; no new body/path/LOC credit): followed the selected `vmm.library` startup request through `VM_Manager()`'s error reply branch and back to `VMM_InitLib()`. `Init_VM_Manager()` can return a normal error before consuming the request (for example, a required library open can fail); `VM_Manager()` then queues a separately allocated `VMCMD_InitFailed` with `ReplySignal == 0`, for which `ReceiveInitMsg()`'s ownership convention says the recipient frees the reply. `VMM_InitLib()` dequeues that reply into `VM_INIT_MSG`, checks only for `VMCMD_InitReady`, and falls through to port teardown / `FALSE` without freeing the failure reply. Added EK10945 for the lost reply allocation on this explicit-error path, separate from EK428's null-parameter startup fault and EK9488's failure to allocate/queue a reply. This rechecks already credited VMM source paths and adds no file or code-line credit. No VMM library open, startup error, allocation failure, or build was run; source-only.

VMM library `CreateNewProc()` failure cleanup recheck (EK10946; 2026-11-12; no new body/path/LOC credit): traced `VMM_InitLib()`'s checked `VM_INIT_MSG` allocation and `NewLoadSeg()` result into the `CreateNewProc()` NULL branch. The branch skips startup-message publication and falls through to common port/DOS cleanup, with no `FreeMem(VM_INIT_MSG)` or `UnLoadSeg(VM_HNDL_SEGLIST)`. The selected `NP_FreeSeglist` tag can transfer handler-segment cleanup only to a process that was successfully created; it does not cover this failure. Added EK10946 for the paired resource leak, conditional on `CreateNewProc()` failure after both earlier allocations succeed. Existing source-body credit unchanged; no process creation failure, load, or build was induced; source-only.

VMM EK10945 OpenLibs early-return ownership refinement (2026-11-12; no body/path/LOC credit): pinned the explicit-error trigger to Init_VM_Manager()'s first required-library opens (VM_Manager_Init.c:416-430), which return before the manager reaches its startup-port WaitPort()/GetMsg() (:433-438). On that path VM_Manager() still queues a separate VMCMD_InitFailed reply; VMM_InitLib() consumes but does not free that reply, and the original startup request remains on the exiting manager process's private message list. DOS process teardown frees its supplied handler segment when NP_FreeSeglist is set (rom/dos/createnewproc.c:943-953) but does not drain/free queued messages; the startup message's allocation therefore remains caller-owned and lost when VMM_InitLib() overwrites its pointer. Tightened EK10945 and its AROS.md summary to record both message allocations and the concrete OpenLibs() error condition. Existing VMM source paths were already body-credited; no coverage totals change. No library open, missing-library condition, process exit, or build was induced; source-only.

VMM manager result-message success-branch ownership follow-up (EK10945 expanded; 2026-11-12; no new body/path/LOC credit): followed the selected library's InitReady handling at vmm_init.c:55-66 in addition to the previously traced InitFailed path. VM_Manager sets ReplySignal to zero on both result messages and PutMsg() transfers each allocated result to the starter port; after InitReady the library reads the returned VM port but overwrites VM_INIT_MSG with a fresh ReqMemHeader allocation without freeing the result. Thus the result-message leak applies to both success and explicit error replies. Kept the additional original startup-request leak conditional on OpenLibs() failing before the manager dequeues its process-port request. Expanded EK10945 and its AROS.md summary; existing file/body totals do not change. No library open, error path, or build was run; source-only.

AArch64 TaskTag_CPUUsage interleaving and target-buildability recheck (EK9905 retained; 2026-11-13; no path/LOC credit): re-read `cpu_Switch()`'s elapsed-slice update (`arch/aarch64-native/kernel/kernel_cpu.c:364-392`), `core_Switch()`'s later acquisition of task/list write locks and `TaskRunning` removal (`kernel_scheduler.c:170-181,204-215`), and `core_TaskCPUUsage()`'s read-locked traversal and `core_TaskUsageWindow()` arithmetic (`kernel_scheduler.c:387-418,426-448`). The timer callbacks return on nonzero CPU IDs before invoking the sweep (`platform_bcm2711.c:184-198`; `platform_bcm2712.c:292-306`); a CPU-0 sweep can therefore read the updated cumulative value while a remote switch waits for the TaskRunning writer lock and the task still has `TS_RUN`, then add `now - iet_private1` for that committed interval. Scope qualification: the active Pi AArch64 boot target depends on `kernel-raspi-aarch64` (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:20-25`), whose selected architecture manifest has seven unresolved C prerequisites (EK8902); no buildable image or runtime reachability is established at this checkout. VMM required-library startup failure cleanup caller recheck (EK10945/EK10946; 2026-11-13; no body/path/LOC credit): read `OpenLibs()` and its `VM_Manager()` failure caller through `Cleanup_VM_Manager()` (`workbench/system/VMM/VM_Manager_Init.c:12-48,981-1130`; `VM_Manager.c:600-631`). EK10768 `NewAddTask()` inherited-affinity handoff recheck (2026-11-13; no new finding ID or body/path/LOC credit): traced `InitETask()` copying the creator mask under its task lock, the `TaskLaunch()` ready-list publication and later off-CPU affinity test, and the selected PC, ARM32 and AArch64 scheduler scans. A task can inherit a finite mask that excludes the CPU where its parent is still executing immediately after `SetTaskAffinity()` narrows that parent mask; the setter’s kick targets the new allowed mask and does not itself force the caller CPU to switch. If the child is dispatched remotely and exits before `TaskLaunch()` tests or passes its mask, `CleanupETask()` frees the child mask, grounding the additional `NewAddTask()` use in EK10768. The interleaving is conditional on the parent continuing on the excluded CPU and rapid child exit; no general same-mask launch failure is claimed. `newaddtask.c` already has full-body credit. No affinity change, task launch/exit, scheduler event, IPI or build was run; source-only.
